# 阿含部 (T01)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 98 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6a 阿含部 *Āhán bù* — Buddhist Canon — Āgama Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/): 98 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6a 阿含部 *Āhán bù* — Buddhist Canon — Āgama Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6a corresponds exactly to the 阿含部 *Āhán bù* of the Taishō canon (Vol. 1 and the first two-thirds of Vol. 2, T01n0001–T02n0151), the section in which the Chinese tradition collected its translations of the Indic *sūtra-piṭaka* — the discourse-collections common, in differing recensions, to all early Buddhist schools. Its spine is the four great Āgamas — *Dīrghāgama*, *Madhyamāgama*, *Saṃyuktāgama*, *Ekottarikāgama* — corresponding broadly to the Pāli *Dīgha-*, *Majjhima-*, *Saṃyutta-*, and *Aṅguttara-nikāya*. Around that spine the cataloguers gathered ~150 shorter translations: stand-alone parallels of individual sūtras, alternative translations of the long parinirvāṇa narrative, cosmological texts on the structure of the *lokadhātu*, biographical accounts of the seven past Buddhas, dialogues with brahmans, and a small group of Abhidharma-style treatises that frame the discourse material analytically. The CANWWW structural index  makes the architecture explicit: most of the parallel sūtras and parinirvāṇa variants are linked from inside the *Dīrghāgama* table of contents itself, marking the four Āgamas as the conceptual anchor against which the rest of the section is to be read.

The chronological range of KR6a is the largest of any subdivision of the Buddhist canon: from the second-century Later Hàn translations of Ān Shìgāo 安世高 down to the early eleventh-century court-translation projects of the Northern Sòng. Three school recensions are represented within the four Āgamas — the *Dīrghāgama* (Dharmaguptaka), *Madhyamāgama* and *Saṃyuktāgama* (Sarvāstivāda / Mūlasarvāstivāda), *Ekottarikāgama* (Mahāsāṃghika or a closely related school) — so that KR6a is not a single canonical *Sūtra-piṭaka* but a cross-sectarian composite assembled across eight centuries. Modern scholarship on this material is dominated by the comparative-Āgama project descended from Anesaki Masaharu and continued by Akanuma Chizen, with more recent contributions by Mizuno Kōgen, Tilmann Vetter, and especially Jan Nattier, whose redatings of attributed translators (notably stripping spurious Hàn-period attributions) the per-text notes follow throughout.

### Important texts and text clusters

The four Āgamas are the irreducible core of the division and account for close to half its total extent (183 of ~400 fascicles):

- *Cháng Āhán jīng* 長阿含經 [KR6a0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0001) — Dharmaguptaka *Dīrghāgama*, 22 fascicles, translated 413 by Buddhayaśas 佛陀耶舍 and Zhú Fóniàn 竺佛念 under the Later Qín. Thirty long discourses including the *Mahāpadāna*, *Mahāparinirvāṇa*, *Aggañña* and *Cakkavatti* sūtras.
- *Zhōng Āhán jīng* 中阿含經 [KR6a0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0026) — Sarvāstivāda *Madhyamāgama*, 60 fascicles, the largest single text in KR6a, retranslated 397–398 by Gōután Sēngjiātípó 瞿曇僧伽提婆 (Saṅghadeva) at Jiànkāng on the basis of an earlier Dào'ān 道安 / Saṅghadeva collaboration of 384.
- *Zá Āhán jīng* 雜阿含經 [KR6a0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0099) — Mūlasarvāstivāda *Saṃyuktāgama*, 50 fascicles, translated 435–443 by Qiúnàbátuóluó 求那跋陀羅 (Guṇabhadra) at Jiànkāng. Roughly 1,362 short connected sūtras, the principal Chinese witness to the *saṃyukta*-style sūtra collection. The textual order of the received recension is famously dislocated and was reconstructed in modern scholarship by Lǚ Chéng 呂澂 and Yìnshùn 印順.
- *Biéyì Zá Āhán jīng* 別譯雜阿含經 [KR6a0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0100) — anonymous "alternative-translation" *Saṃyuktāgama* in 16 fascicles, dated to the Sānqín period (c. 350–431); preserves a partial parallel recension of uncertain school affiliation, indispensable for comparative work on T99.
- *Zēngyī Āhán jīng* 增壹阿含經 [KR6a0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0126) — *Ekottarikāgama*, 51 fascicles, translated 384–398. The catalogue ascription oscillates between Dharmanandi 曇摩難提 (initial draft, 384) and Saṅghadeva (revision, 397); the received text shows clear Mahāsāṃghika or proto-Mahāyāna inflections and has been intensively studied for that reason.

Around this spine, several smaller clusters recur:

- **Parinirvāṇa cycle.** Three independent translations of the long *Mahāparinirvāṇa* narrative — *Fó bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0005) (Bái Fǎzǔ 白法祖, c. 290–305), *Bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0006) (anonymous, Eastern Jìn), and Fǎxiǎn 法顯's *Dà bānnièpán jīng* [KR6a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0007) (413–418) — sit in deliberate parallel to the *Yóuxíng jīng* 遊行經 inside the *Dīrghāgama*. The female parinirvāṇa narrative *Fó shuō Dà'àidào bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0148) and *Fómǔ bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0149) complete the cycle.
- **Past-Buddha biography.** *Qī fó jīng* [KR6a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0002), *Pípóshī fó jīng* [KR6a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0003) and *Qī fó fùmǔ xìngzì jīng* [KR6a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0004) expand the *Mahāpadāna* material from the *Dīrghāgama*'s opening; the first two are late tenth-century Sòng retranslations by Fǎtiān 法天.
- **Cosmology.** *Dà lóutàn jīng* [KR6a0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0023) (Fǎlì 法立 / Fǎjù 法炬, Western Jìn), *Qǐshì jīng* [KR6a0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0024) (Shénàjuéduō 闍那崛多 / Jñānagupta, Suí), and *Qǐshì yīnběn jīng* [KR6a0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0025) (Dámójíduō 達摩笈多 / Dharmagupta, Suí) are three successive renderings of the *Lokaprajñapti* / *Aggañña* cosmological material, each with substantive variants. They are the principal Chinese witnesses to early Buddhist cosmology and bear on later Chán and Tiāntái discussions of world-systems.
- **Brahman-dialogue group.** A cluster of Sòng-period retranslations by Shīhù 施護 (Dānapāla) — *Dà Jiāngù póluómén yuánqǐ jīng* [KR6a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0008), *Níjūtuó fànzhì jīng* [KR6a0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0011), among others — gives access to brahman-encounter discourses that are partial parallels to the *Mahāgovinda*, *Aggañña*, and *Udumbarīkasīhanāda* sūtras.
- **Late Sòng court-translation revival.** Roughly 25 KR6a texts dated 970–1017 stem from the Northern Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn* 譯經院 under Shīhù, Fǎtiān, Fǎxián 法賢 (Dharmadeva), and Fǎhù 法護 (Dharmapāla). These small-scale retranslations of *Āgama* parallels are systematically valuable as a fresh Indic vantage on material that had long since stabilized in earlier Chinese versions.
- **Mahāyāna-inflected outliers.** A handful of texts catalogued in KR6a are doctrinally Mahāyāna; the most important is *Yāngjuémóluó jīng* 央掘魔羅經 [KR6a0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0120), Guṇabhadra's *tathāgatagarbha* recension of the Aṅgulimāla legend — a key source for the early Chinese reception of buddha-nature teaching.
- **Analytic / Abhidharma annexes.** *Fēnbié gōngdé lùn* 分別功德論 [KR6a0159](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0159) (5 fascicles, anonymous Hàn–Jìn) is a commentarial treatise on the introductory section of the *Ekottarikāgama* and the principal indigenous bridge between *sūtra* and *abhidharma* in this division.

### Important persons

- [佛陀耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) (Buddhayaśas, fl. early 5c.) — Kashmiri reciter; translator of the *Dīrghāgama* and of the *Sìfēn lǜ* in the Vinaya division.
- [竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5) (Zhú Fóniàn, fl. late 4c.) — Liángzhōu-trained Chinese collaborator on the *Dīrghāgama* and many of Dào'ān's Cháng'ān projects; key oral interpreter for an entire generation.
- [瞿曇僧伽提婆](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9E%BF%E6%9B%87%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E6%8F%90%E5%A9%86) (Saṅghadeva, fl. 383–398) — Kashmiri Sarvāstivādin; sole authority for the standard recensions of both the *Madhyamāgama* and the *Ekottarikāgama*.
- [求那跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Guṇabhadra, 394–468) — central Indian master active at Jiànkāng under Liú Sòng; translator of the *Saṃyuktāgama* and of *Yāngjuémóluó jīng*; pivotal figure in the early Chinese reception of *tathāgatagarbha* doctrine.
- [法顯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%A1%AF) (Fǎxiǎn, c. 337–c. 422) — pilgrim-translator whose *Dà bānnièpán jīng* anchors the Hīnayāna parinirvāṇa cluster in KR6a; his Indic travels supplied the Sanskrit exemplars used here.
- [安世高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96%E9%AB%98) (Ān Shìgāo, fl. c. 148–170) — Parthian missionary, the earliest substantial translator into Chinese; ~20 short *Āgama*-parallel sūtras in KR6a are traditionally attributed to him, though many attributions have been narrowed by Nattier and others.
- [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) (Zhī Qiān, fl. c. 222–253) — Yuèzhī-descended Wú-court translator; produced numerous short *Āgama* sūtras, often in elegant literary register that contrasts with the more workmanlike Hàn versions.
- [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) (Zhú Fǎhù / Dharmarakṣa, c. 233–c. 311) — Western Jìn translator of the broadest range; supplied multiple individual sūtra parallels and (with Fǎlì) the cosmological *Dà lóutàn jīng*.
- [法炬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%82%AC) (Fǎjù, fl. c. 290–306) — prolific Western Jìn translator of short sūtras, frequently in collaboration with Fǎlì 法立; one of the largest individual contributors to KR6a by text count.
- [竺曇無蘭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%98%AD) (Zhú Tánwúlán, fl. c. 381–395) — Eastern Jìn translator of numerous short Āgama parallels.
- [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) (Jñānagupta, 523–c. 600) — Gandhāran translator at the Suí court; produced *Qǐshì jīng* and the parallel *Fó wèi Shǒujiā zhǎngzhě shuō yèbào chābié jīng* [KR6a0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0080) (with Gōután Fǎzhì 瞿曇法智).
- [達摩笈多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%94%E6%91%A9%E7%AC%88%E5%A4%9A) (Dharmagupta, d. 619) — Southern Indian translator at the Suí *Fānjīng guǎn*; produced the parallel *Qǐshì yīnběn jīng*.
- [施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7) (Dānapāla, fl. 980–1017) — Uḍḍiyāna monk and senior translator at the Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn*; the dominant figure in the late KR6a retranslation programme (~13 texts).
- [法天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E5%A4%A9) (Fǎtiān, d. 1001) — Magadhan translator at the Sòng court; rendered the past-Buddha biographies KR6a0002–0003 among others.
- [法賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%B3%A2) (Fǎxián / Dharmadeva, fl. late 10c.) — Sòng-period translator of Indic origin (distinct from the Eastern-Jìn pilgrim Fǎxiǎn 法顯, despite the homophone); ~10 short *Āgama* sūtras.
- [白法祖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%99%BD%E6%B3%95%E7%A5%96) (Bái Fǎzǔ, fl. 290–306) — Western Jìn translator of *Fó bānníhuán jīng* and *Dà'àidào bānníhuán jīng*.
- [慧簡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E7%B0%A1) (Huìjiǎn, fl. 457) — Liú Sòng translator of *Fómǔ bānníhuán jīng* and a small group of related short sūtras.

### Topics

The interpretive issues that recur across KR6a entries cluster around five problems:

1. **Sectarian recension.** Each of the four Āgamas was transmitted by a different school, and the comparative question — what does each Chinese Āgama tell us about the doctrinal commitments of its Indic *nikāya* — runs through nearly every per-text note. *Ekottarikāgama* in particular is read by some scholars as bearing proto-Mahāyāna features, by others as straightforwardly Mahāsāṃghika.

2. **Pāli–Chinese parallels.** The main scholarly use of the section since Anesaki and Akanuma has been comparative: matching Chinese Āgama sūtras to their Pāli *Nikāya* counterparts (or to Sanskrit fragments from Central Asia and Gilgit) and analysing the divergences. The CANWWW *Structural Division* index in `div01.xml` gives the parallel-text mapping at the level of individual sub-sūtras.

3. **Authenticity of Hàn-period attributions.** A large number of short sūtras are traditionally attributed to Ān Shìgāo, Zhī Qiān, or 失譯 ("translator unknown"). Modern scholarship — Zürcher, Nattier, Harrison, Karashima — has substantially redrawn the attribution map, often pushing texts forward by centuries. The per-text notes in this division reflect that revision (e.g., several "Hàn" attributions are bracketed to a Six-Dynasties or later notBefore).

4. **Parinirvāṇa narrative variants.** The multiple Chinese versions of the long parinirvāṇa story (KR6a0005, 0006, 0007, plus the *Yóuxíng jīng* embedded in the *Dīrghāgama*) provide one of the richest case-studies in early Buddhist textual history, with significant doctrinal divergences between the recensions on the Buddha's last instructions, the four guarantees, and the schismatic prediction.

5. **The cosmological tradition.** *Dà lóutàn jīng*, *Qǐshì jīng*, and *Qǐshì yīnběn jīng* descend from a single Indic *Lokaprajñapti* but show three increasingly detailed Chinese expansions; they are the indispensable backdrop for the cosmological material in later Chinese Buddhist scholasticism (Tiāntái, Huáyán, the *Cāntóngqì* tradition's Buddhist appropriation, and the popular cosmologies of the *Nièpán-jīng* commentaries in KR6c).

### Timeline

Composition / translation dates, oldest first; for translation literature the date is the date of the Chinese rendering (the underlying Indic material is in every case older).

- 25–220 — *Fēnbié gōngdé lùn* 分別功德論 [KR6a0159](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0159) — anonymous Hàn-attributed commentary on the *Ekottarikāgama* preface (later strata may be Three-Kingdoms / Jìn).
- c. 148–170 — Ān Shìgāo's short *Āgama* parallels (~20 texts), the earliest Chinese sūtra translations preserved in KR6a.
- c. 222–253 — Zhī Qiān's *Āgama* renderings (~12 texts) at the Wú court at Jiànyè.
- c. 290–311 — Western Jìn cluster: *Fó bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0005), *Dà lóutàn jīng* [KR6a0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0023), *Dà'àidào bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0148), and the bulk of Zhú Fǎhù 竺法護, Fǎlì 法立, and Fǎjù 法炬's translations.
- 384–385 — first draft of *Zēngyī Āhán jīng* 增壹阿含經 by Dharmanandi at Cháng'ān (later revised; see KR6a0126).
- 397–398 — Saṅghadeva's *Zhōng Āhán jīng* 中阿含經 [KR6a0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0026) and revised *Ekottarikāgama* 增壹阿含經 [KR6a0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0126) at Jiànkāng — the foundational Eastern-Jìn moment for the section.
- 413 — Buddhayaśas / Zhú Fóniàn's *Cháng Āhán jīng* 長阿含經 [KR6a0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0001) at Cháng'ān under the Later Qín.
- 413–418 — Fǎxiǎn's *Dà bānnièpán jīng* 大般涅槃經 [KR6a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0007), on his return from India.
- c. 350–431 — anonymous *Biéyì Zá Āhán jīng* 別譯雜阿含經 [KR6a0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0100), Sānqín period; window deliberately wide.
- 435–443 — Guṇabhadra's *Zá Āhán jīng* 雜阿含經 [KR6a0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0099) at Jiànkāng.
- 435–468 — Guṇabhadra's *Yāngjuémóluó jīng* 央掘魔羅經 [KR6a0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0120) and a substantial cluster of short sūtras.
- 457 — Huìjiǎn's *Fómǔ bānníhuán jīng* 佛母般泥洹經 [KR6a0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0149).
- 581–600 — Jñānagupta's *Qǐshì jīng* 起世經 [KR6a0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0024) under the Suí.
- 590–619 — Dharmagupta's *Qǐshì yīnběn jīng* 起世因本經 [KR6a0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0025), the parallel Suí cosmological recension.
- 973–1001 — opening phase of the Sòng court-translation programme: Fǎtiān's *Qī fó jīng* 七佛經 [KR6a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0002) and the past-Buddha cluster.
- 982–1017 — main Sòng programme under Shīhù: brahman-dialogue parallels (KR6a0008, KR6a0011, etc.) and a wide range of short sūtras; closes the Chinese translation history of the Āgama section.

- *Zhōng Āhán jīng* 中阿含經 [KR6a0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0026) — Sarvāstivāda *Madhyamāgama*, 60 fascicles, the largest single text in KR6a, retranslated 397–398 by Gōután Sēngjiātípó 瞿曇僧伽提婆 (Saṅghadeva) at Jiànkāng on the basis of an earlier Dào'ān 道安 / Saṅghadeva collaboration of 384.
- *Zá Āhán jīng* 雜阿含經 [KR6a0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0099) — Mūlasarvāstivāda *Saṃyuktāgama*, 50 fascicles, translated 435–443 by Qiúnàbátuóluó 求那跋陀羅 (Guṇabhadra) at Jiànkāng. Roughly 1,362 short connected sūtras, the principal Chinese witness to the *saṃyukta*-style sūtra collection. The textual order of the received recension is famously dislocated and was reconstructed in modern scholarship by Lǚ Chéng 呂澂 and Yìnshùn 印順.
- *Biéyì Zá Āhán jīng* 別譯雜阿含經 [KR6a0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0100) — anonymous "alternative-translation" *Saṃyuktāgama* in 16 fascicles, dated to the Sānqín period (c. 350–431); preserves a partial parallel recension of uncertain school affiliation, indispensable for comparative work on T99.
- *Zēngyī Āhán jīng* 增壹阿含經 [KR6a0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0126) — *Ekottarikāgama*, 51 fascicles, translated 384–398. The catalogue ascription oscillates between Dharmanandi 曇摩難提 (initial draft, 384) and Saṅghadeva (revision, 397); the received text shows clear Mahāsāṃghika or proto-Mahāyāna inflections and has been intensively studied for that reason.

Around this spine, several smaller clusters recur:

- **Parinirvāṇa cycle.** Three independent translations of the long *Mahāparinirvāṇa* narrative — *Fó bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0005) (Bái Fǎzǔ 白法祖, c. 290–305), *Bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0006) (anonymous, Eastern Jìn), and Fǎxiǎn 法顯's *Dà bānnièpán jīng* [KR6a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0007) (413–418) — sit in deliberate parallel to the *Yóuxíng jīng* 遊行經 inside the *Dīrghāgama*. The female parinirvāṇa narrative *Fó shuō Dà'àidào bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0148) and *Fómǔ bānníhuán jīng* [KR6a0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0149) complete the cycle.
- **Past-Buddha biography.** *Qī fó jīng* [KR6a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0002), *Pípóshī fó jīng* [KR6a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0003) and *Qī fó fùmǔ xìngzì jīng* [KR6a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0004) expand the *Mahāpadāna* material from the *Dīrghāgama*'s opening; the first two are late tenth-century Sòng retranslations by Fǎtiān 法天.
- **Cosmology.** *Dà lóutàn jīng* [KR6a0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0023) (Fǎlì 法立 / Fǎjù 法炬, Western Jìn), *Qǐshì jīng* [KR6a0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0024) (Shénàjuéduō 闍那崛多 / Jñānagupta, Suí), and *Qǐshì yīnběn jīng* [KR6a0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0025) (Dámójíduō 達摩笈多 / Dharmagupta, Suí) are three successive renderings of the *Lokaprajñapti* / *Aggañña* cosmological material, each with substantive variants. They are the principal Chinese witnesses to early Buddhist cosmology and bear on later Chán and Tiāntái discussions of world-systems.
- **Brahman-dialogue group.** A cluster of Sòng-period retranslations by Shīhù 施護 (Dānapāla) — *Dà Jiāngù póluómén yuánqǐ jīng* [KR6a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0008), *Níjūtuó fànzhì jīng* [KR6a0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0011), among others — gives access to brahman-encounter discourses that are partial parallels to the *Mahāgovinda*, *Aggañña*, and *Udumbarīkasīhanāda* sūtras.
- **Late Sòng court-translation revival.** Roughly 25 KR6a texts dated 970–1017 stem from the Northern Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn* 譯經院 under Shīhù, Fǎtiān, Fǎxián 法賢 (Dharmadeva), and Fǎhù 法護 (Dharmapāla). These small-scale retranslations of *Āgama* parallels are systematically valuable as a fresh Indic vantage on material that had long since stabilized in earlier Chinese versions.
- **Mahāyāna-inflected outliers.** A handful of texts catalogued in KR6a are doctrinally Mahāyāna; the most important is *Yāngjuémóluó jīng* 央掘魔羅經 [KR6a0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0120), Guṇabhadra's *tathāgatagarbha* recension of the Aṅgulimāla legend — a key source for the early Chinese reception of buddha-nature teaching.
- **Analytic / Abhidharma annexes.** *Fēnbié gōngdé lùn* 分別功德論 [KR6a0159](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0159) (5 fascicles, anonymous Hàn–Jìn) is a commentarial treatise on the introductory section of the *Ekottarikāgama* and the principal indigenous bridge between *sūtra* and *abhidharma* in this division.

### Topics

The interpretive issues that recur across KR6a entries cluster around five problems:

1. **Sectarian recension.** Each of the four Āgamas was transmitted by a different school, and the comparative question — what does each Chinese Āgama tell us about the doctrinal commitments of its Indic *nikāya* — runs through nearly every per-text note. *Ekottarikāgama* in particular is read by some scholars as bearing proto-Mahāyāna features, by others as straightforwardly Mahāsāṃghika.

2. **Pāli–Chinese parallels.** The main scholarly use of the section since Anesaki and Akanuma has been comparative: matching Chinese Āgama sūtras to their Pāli *Nikāya* counterparts (or to Sanskrit fragments from Central Asia and Gilgit) and analysing the divergences. The CANWWW *Structural Division* index in `div01.xml` gives the parallel-text mapping at the level of individual sub-sūtras.

3. **Authenticity of Hàn-period attributions.** A large number of short sūtras are traditionally attributed to Ān Shìgāo, Zhī Qiān, or 失譯 ("translator unknown"). Modern scholarship — Zürcher, Nattier, Harrison, Karashima — has substantially redrawn the attribution map, often pushing texts forward by centuries. The per-text notes in this division reflect that revision (e.g., several "Hàn" attributions are bracketed to a Six-Dynasties or later notBefore).

4. **Parinirvāṇa narrative variants.** The multiple Chinese versions of the long parinirvāṇa story (KR6a0005, 0006, 0007, plus the *Yóuxíng jīng* embedded in the *Dīrghāgama*) provide one of the richest case-studies in early Buddhist textual history, with significant doctrinal divergences between the recensions on the Buddha's last instructions, the four guarantees, and the schismatic prediction.

5. **The cosmological tradition.** *Dà lóutàn jīng*, *Qǐshì jīng*, and *Qǐshì yīnběn jīng* descend from a single Indic *Lokaprajñapti* but show three increasingly detailed Chinese expansions; they are the indispensable backdrop for the cosmological material in later Chinese Buddhist scholasticism (Tiāntái, Huáyán, the *Cāntóngqì* tradition's Buddhist appropriation, and the popular cosmologies of the *Nièpán-jīng* commentaries in KR6c).

# 本緣部 (T03)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 44 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6b 本緣部 *Běnyuán bù* — Buddhist Canon — Past-Life Narratives (Jātaka, Avadāna, Buddha-Biography, Parable, Dharmapada)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/): 44 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6b 本緣部 *Běnyuán bù* — Buddhist Canon — Past-Life Narratives (Jātaka, Avadāna, Buddha-Biography, Parable, Dharmapada)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6b corresponds to the 本緣部 *Běnyuán bù* ("Section on Original Conditions") of the Taishō canon, occupying Taishō volumes 3 and 4 (T152–T219). In the CANWWW structural division  this is the fourth division of the canon, sitting between the 寶積部 *Ratnakūṭa* collections (div03) and the 般若部 *Prajñāpāramitā* section (div05). The unifying generic category is **narrative scripture about prior lives or originary events** — *jātaka* tales of the *bodhisattva*'s past births, *avadāna* anthologies of edifying karmic biographies, full Buddha-biographies (*Buddhacarita* / *Lalitavistara*-class works and their Chinese variants), the *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* gnomic-verse traditions, and the various *pìyù* 譬喻 (parable) compilations. The Chinese title literally means "section on origins and conditioned causes," capturing the karmic-narrative logic that ties this generically heterogeneous material together.

Chronologically the division spans roughly thirteen centuries of Chinese translation and compilation, from Ān Shìgāo's mid-second-century *Tàizǐ Mùpò jīng* 太子慕魄經 ([KR6b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0019), c. 148–170) through the great Northern-Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn* 譯經院 translation programme of c. 980–1001 (the [Shīhù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0017) / [Fǎxián](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0048) / [Tiānxīzāi](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0070) cluster). A single late-imperial commentarial extension — Lái Zhōu's 來舟 Yōngzhèng-era *Qiǎnzhù* on the *Xīndì-guān jīng* ([KR6b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0009), [KR6b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0010), [KR6b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0011)) — carries the division into the eighteenth century. The principal transmissional traditions a reader must keep in mind are: (i) the Hàn–Wú southern translation lineage (Ān Shìgāo → Zhī Qiān → Kāng Sēnghuì), which produced the foundational Chinese *jātaka*-anthologies and the canonical *Dharmapada*; (ii) the Western-Jìn Dūnhuáng/Cháng'ān lineage of Zhú Fǎhù (Dharmarakṣa), responsible for an unusually large fraction of the division (at least seven works); (iii) the early-fifth-century Northern-Liáng (Dharmakṣema), Latter-Qín (Kumārajīva, Zhú Fóniàn), and Liú-Sòng (Guṇabhadra, Bǎoyún) translation programmes, which gave Chinese readers the *Buddhacarita*, the *Sūtrālaṃkāra*, and the *Udānavarga* with auto-commentary; and (iv) the Northern Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn*, which produced systematic re-translations of jātaka and parable material (T165, T173, T191, T213, T218, T219). One unusual feature of this division is the prominence of **Chinese editorial compilation** alongside translation: several of the most-influential works — *[Liù-dù jí jīng (T152)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001)*, *[Xiányú jīng (T202)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0059)*, the four *[Zá pìyù jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0061)* anthologies — are sinophone editorial assemblages of Indic narrative material rather than translations of single Indic recensions.

### Important texts and text clusters

**Mahāyāna jātaka-anthologies.** The principal Mahāyāna-inflected *bodhisattva*-jātaka anthologies of the Chinese canon: [KR6b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001) *Liù-dù jí jīng* 六度集經 (T152, Kāng Sēnghuì, c. 247–280), the foundational Wú-period anthology organising 91 *bodhisattva*-tales under the six *pāramitā*s; [KR6b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0002) *Púsà běnyuán jīng* 菩薩本緣經 (T153, Zhī Qiān); [KR6b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0003) *Shēng jīng* 生經 (T154, Zhú Fǎhù); and [KR6b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0012) *Púsà běnshēng mán lùn* 菩薩本生鬘論 (T160, Sòng), the Chinese version of Āryaśūra's *Jātakamālā*.

**Karuṇā-puṇḍarīka cluster.** [KR6b0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0006) *Bēihuā jīng* 悲華經 (T157, Dharmakṣema, 414–421) and its companion [KR6b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0007) *Dàshèng bēifēntuólì jīng* 大乘悲分陀利經 (T158, anonymous Northern-dynasties), two Chinese versions of the *Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra* — a Mahāyāna meta-jātaka in which Śākyamuni's vow-history is the principal narrative.

**Xīndì-guān cluster.** [KR6b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0008) *Dàshèng běnshēng xīndì-guān jīng* 大乘本生心地觀經 (T159, Prajña, 810–811) and its three Qing-Dynasty commentaries by Lái Zhōu — [KR6b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0009) *Xuánshì*, [KR6b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0010) *Kēwén*, and [KR6b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0011) *Qiǎnzhù*; the only post-Sòng works in the division.

**Royal-jātaka single sūtras.** A series of single-fascicle past-life narratives anchored on a virtuous king or prince, ranging from short Hàn-era survivals to Northern-Sòng re-translations: [KR6b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0013) *Chángshòu wáng jīng*, [KR6b0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0014) *Jīnsè wáng jīng*, [KR6b0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0015) *Miàosè wáng yīnyuán jīng*, [KR6b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0017) *Dǐngshēng wáng yīnyuán jīng*, [KR6b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0018) *Yuèguāng púsà jīng*, [KR6b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0023) *Tàizǐ Sūdánà jīng* (the Chinese Vessantara/Sudāna), [KR6b0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0025) *Fúlì tàizǐ yīnyuán jīng* (Puṇyabala). The 太子慕魄/墓魄 doublet — [KR6b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0019) (Ān Shìgāo, c. 148–170) and [KR6b0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0020) (Zhú Fǎhù) — is one of the earliest dated Chinese-Buddhist narrative pairs.

**Śyāmaka recensions.** A remarkable four-fold survival of the *Śyāmaka-jātaka* — [KR6b0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0026), [KR6b0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0027), [KR6b0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0028), [KR6b0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0029) — preserving multiple Chinese recensions (Yáo-Qín and Qǐfú-Qín attributions to Shèngjiān 聖堅, plus an anonymous one) of the same filial-piety jātaka, one of the very few cases in the canon where so many recensions of a single short narrative are preserved side by side. The pair of 九色鹿 (Nine-Coloured Deer, [KR6b0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0035) / [KR6b0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0036)) and 鹿母 (Mother-Deer, [KR6b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0037) / [KR6b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0038)) recensions show similar Wú/Western-Jìn doublet-preservation patterns.

**Lalitavistara pair.** [KR6b0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0042) *Pǔyào jīng* 普曜經 (T186, Zhú Fǎhù, 308) and [KR6b0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0043) *Fāngguǎng dàzhuāngyán jīng* 方廣大莊嚴經 (T187, Divākara, 685) — the early-Jìn and Táng Chinese versions of the Mahāyāna *Lalitavistara*-class Buddha-biography, separated by some 380 years and one of the principal test-cases in comparative Chinese Buddhist translation studies.

**Buddhacarita and verse-biographies.** [KR6b0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0049) *Fó suǒxíng zàn* 佛所行讚 (T192, Dharmakṣema, 414–421), Aśvaghoṣa's *Buddhacarita* — the Chinese version preserves chapters of the Sanskrit *kāvya* that are now lost in the original — and its companion [KR6b0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0050) *Fó běnxíng jīng* (T193, Bǎoyún, Liú-Sòng).

**Hàn-era Buddha-biography pair.** [KR6b0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0040) *Xiūxíng běnqǐ jīng* 修行本起經 (T184, Zhú Dàlì + Kāng Mèngxiáng, 197 CE) and [KR6b0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0053) *Zhōng běnqǐ jīng* 中本起經 (T196, Tánguǒ + Kāng Mèngxiáng, 207 CE) — together a complete Eastern-Hàn Chinese Buddha-biography cycle and one of the earliest dated translations after Ān Shìgāo's. [KR6b0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0041) *Tàizǐ ruìyìng běnqǐ jīng* (T185, Zhī Qiān) is the Wú-period parallel.

**Comprehensive Suí Buddha-biography.** [KR6b0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0047) *Fó běnxíng jí jīng* 佛本行集經 (T190, Jñānagupta, 587–591) — at 60 *juàn* the most extensive Mahāyāna Buddha-biography in Chinese and the most important pre-Tang biographical encyclopedia of the Buddha. [KR6b0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0048) *Zhòngxǔ móhēdì jīng* 眾許摩訶帝經 (T191, Fǎxián 法賢, 980–1001) is its Northern-Sòng re-translation.

**Avadāna anthologies.** Four of the most-cited Chinese *avadāna*-collections: [KR6b0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0057) *Zhuànjí bǎiyuán jīng* 撰集百緣經 (T200, Zhī Qiān) — the Chinese *Avadāna-śataka*; [KR6b0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0058) *Dàzhuāngyán lùn jīng* 大莊嚴論經 (T201, Aśvaghoṣa via Kumārajīva, 405–412) — the *Sūtrālaṃkāra* / *Kalpanāmaṇḍitikā*; [KR6b0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0059) *Xiányú jīng* 賢愚經 (T202, Huìjué et al., 445–459) — compiled at Khotan/Gāochāng directly from oral *avadāna*-recitations and the source of the Tibetan *mDzangs blun*; [KR6b0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0060) *Zábǎozàng jīng* 雜寶藏經 (T203, Jíjiāyè + Tányào, 472) — a Mūlasarvāstivādin compilation foundational for East-Asian popular literature.

**Parable (譬喻) anthologies.** Five anthologies of *pìyù*-narratives showcasing the genre's development from the late Hàn through the Suí: [KR6b0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0061) *Zá pìyù jīng* (T204, attributed Zhī Lóujiāchèn / Lokakṣema, c. 178–200); [KR6b0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0063) *Jiù zá pìyù jīng* 舊雜譬喻經 (T206, Kāng Sēnghuì); [KR6b0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0064) *Zá pìyù jīng* (T207, Dàoluè) and [KR6b0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0065) *Zhòngjīng zhuànzá pìyù* (T208, Dàoluè/Kumārajīva); and the masterpiece [KR6b0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0066) *Bǎiyú jīng* 百喻經 (T209, Saṃghasena via Guṇavṛddhi, 492) — Lú Xùn's 1914 edition made this one of the foundational texts for modern Chinese literary reception of the Buddhist canon.

**Dharmapada / Udānavarga cluster.** The four-text gnomic-verse complex of the Chinese canon: [KR6b0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0067) *Fǎjù jīng* 法句經 (T210, Wéi Qínán / Zhī Qiān, 224) — the canonical Chinese *Dharmapada* with the famous translator's preface; [KR6b0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0068) *Fǎjù pìyù jīng* (T211, Fǎjù + Fǎlì) — verse and avadāna-narrative combined; [KR6b0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0069) *Chūyào jīng* 出曜經 (T212, Zhú Fóniàn, 398–399) — the most extensive Chinese *Udānavarga* with full prose auto-commentary; [KR6b0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0070) *Fǎjí yàosòng jīng* (T213, Tiānxīzāi, 980–1000) — the Northern-Sòng re-translation.

### Important persons

- [安世高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96%E9%AB%98) (c. 148–170 CE active) — Parthian monk, the earliest dated translator in the division (T167 *Tàizǐ Mùpò jīng*); his rendering of a single princely jātaka inaugurates the Chinese reception of *běnyuán* literature.
- [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) (active c. 222–253) — Wú-period translator of more works in this division than any other figure: at least nine, including the canonical *Dharmapada* (T210), the *Avadāna-śataka* (T200), the *Aṭṭhakavagga* (T198), and the foundational royal-jātakas (T169, T181a/b, T185, T214); his preface to the *Dharmapada* is the foundational document of pre-modern Chinese Buddhist translation theory.
- [康僧會](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%B7%E5%83%A7%E6%9C%83) (d. 280) — Sogdian-Wú compiler of *[Liù-dù jí jīng (T152)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001)* and the *Jiù zá pìyù jīng* (T206), credited with naturalising *bodhisattva*-ethics in classical-Chinese ethical discourse.
- [竺大力](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E5%A4%A7%E5%8A%9B) and [康孟詳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%B7%E5%AD%9F%E8%A9%B3) — the Eastern-Hàn translation pair responsible for [T184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0040), [T196](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0053), and [T197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0054), the foundational Buddha-biography and karmic-aetiology corpus of the Hàn.
- [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) (Dharmarakṣa, c. 233–310) — Western-Jìn translator of at least seven works in this division (T154, T168, T170, T180, T182, T186, T199); the principal Western-Jìn conduit for *jātaka* and Buddha-biographical material.
- [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema, 385–433) — Northern-Liáng translator of the *Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka* ([T157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0006)) and the *Buddhacarita* ([T192](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0049)); the most consequential early-fifth-century translator of narrative material.
- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Kumārajīva, 344–413) — translator of the *Sūtrālaṃkāra* ([T201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0058)) and (with Dàoluè) of T208; the principal Latter-Qín influence on the division.
- [竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5) (active 365–410) — Latter-Qín translator of the *Udānavarga* with auto-commentary ([T212](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0069)), the most-extensive Chinese gnomic-verse compendium.

CE) — attributed author of the *Buddhacarita* ([T192](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0049)) and the *Sūtrālaṃkāra* ([T201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0058)); the most important Indic literary figure represented in the division.

### Topics

- **The 本緣 generic frame.** What unifies the division is the Indic karmic-narrative complex of *jātaka* (past-life of the *bodhisattva*), *avadāna* (karmically-conditioned biography of a virtuous being), *nidāna* (the conditioning narrative for a doctrinal point), and *upamā* / *dṛṣṭānta* (parable). The Chinese organising rubric 本緣 collapses these Indic distinctions; readers should treat them as a continuum rather than as sharply-bounded genres.
- **Translation vs. compilation.** Unlike the Āgamas (KR6a) or Prajñāpāramitā (KR6c), several of the most-influential works of KR6b are **Chinese editorial compilations** rather than translations of single Indic recensions: [T152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001) (Kāng Sēnghuì's compilation under six-*pāramitā* rubric), [T202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0059) (Huìjué et al. assembled from Khotanese oral recitations), the *[Zá pìyù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0061)* complex. The boundary between translation and Chinese authorship is unusually porous here.
- **Multiple-recension preservation.** The division contains an unusual density of multiple-recension survivals of single short jātakas: four *Śyāmaka*-jātakas ([KR6b0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0026)–[KR6b0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0029)), two *Tàizǐ Mùpò* ([KR6b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0019), [KR6b0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0020)), two *Jiǔsè lù* ([KR6b0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0035), [KR6b0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0036)), two *Lùmǔ* ([KR6b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0037), [KR6b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0038)). These doublet/triplet/quadruplet preservations are a key resource for the historical-linguistic study of pre-Tang Chinese Buddhist translation.
- **Buddha-biography textual problem.** Four parallel Buddha-biography traditions are preserved in Chinese — the Hàn 修行/中本起 cycle ([KR6b0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0040) + [KR6b0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0053)), the Wú *Tàizǐ ruìyìng* ([KR6b0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0041)), the *Lalitavistara* pair ([KR6b0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0042) / [KR6b0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0043)), the Mūlasarvāstivādin *Fó běnxíng jí* ([KR6b0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0047)), the *Buddhacarita* + *Fó běnxíng jīng* verse-pair ([KR6b0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0049) + [KR6b0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0050)), and the Sòng *Zhòngxǔ móhēdì jīng* ([KR6b0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0048)) — yielding a four-recension Chinese-canonical Buddha-biography problem whose comparative study is foundational for pre-modern Indic-Buddhist biographical reception.
- **The Dharmapada question.** The three-text Chinese *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* set ([KR6b0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0067), [KR6b0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0069), [KR6b0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0070)) preserves a Sarvāstivādin-tradition recension different from the Pāli *Dhammapada* in selection, ordering, and verse-count, and remains essential to comparative Buddhist gnomic-verse studies alongside the Gāndhārī (Brough), Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (Bernhard), and Pāli traditions.
- **Royal jātaka and ethical-political reading.** A substantial sub-set of the division ([KR6b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0013)–[KR6b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0018), [KR6b0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0022), [KR6b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0023), [KR6b0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0025)) places the *bodhisattva* as a royal protagonist whose *dāna* / *kṣānti* / *vīrya* paradigms are inscribed into models of just kingship; this material was particularly important in the Chinese ethical-political reception of Buddhism (the Vessantara-narrative of [KR6b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0023) is the most-cited example).
- **Vegetarianism / non-violence.** Several works ([KR6b0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0016) *Shīzǐ Sùtuósuō wáng duànròu jīng*; [KR6b0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0039) *Yīqièzhì guāngmíng xiānrén cíxīn yīnyuán bùshíròu jīng*) are textual ancestors of the Chinese-Buddhist meat-renunciation discourse that became central in the Liáng and afterwards.
- **Reception in popular literature.** The avadāna and parable anthologies — especially [T202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0059), [T203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0060), and [T209](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0066) — were the principal canonical source for the Dūnhuáng *biàn-wén* 變文 transformation-text tradition (Mair 1989) and for East-Asian Buddhist popular-narrative literature more broadly; T202 became the basis of the Tibetan *mDzangs blun*.

# 本緣部 (T04)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 28 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6b 本緣部 *Běnyuán bù* — Buddhist Canon — Past-Life Narratives (Jātaka, Avadāna, Buddha-Biography, Parable, Dharmapada)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/): 28 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6b 本緣部 *Běnyuán bù* — Buddhist Canon — Past-Life Narratives (Jātaka, Avadāna, Buddha-Biography, Parable, Dharmapada)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6b corresponds to the 本緣部 *Běnyuán bù* ("Section on Original Conditions") of the Taishō canon, occupying Taishō volumes 3 and 4 (T152–T219). In the CANWWW structural division  this is the fourth division of the canon, sitting between the 寶積部 *Ratnakūṭa* collections (div03) and the 般若部 *Prajñāpāramitā* section (div05). The unifying generic category is **narrative scripture about prior lives or originary events** — *jātaka* tales of the *bodhisattva*'s past births, *avadāna* anthologies of edifying karmic biographies, full Buddha-biographies (*Buddhacarita* / *Lalitavistara*-class works and their Chinese variants), the *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* gnomic-verse traditions, and the various *pìyù* 譬喻 (parable) compilations. The Chinese title literally means "section on origins and conditioned causes," capturing the karmic-narrative logic that ties this generically heterogeneous material together.

Chronologically the division spans roughly thirteen centuries of Chinese translation and compilation, from Ān Shìgāo's mid-second-century *Tàizǐ Mùpò jīng* 太子慕魄經 ([KR6b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0019), c. 148–170) through the great Northern-Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn* 譯經院 translation programme of c. 980–1001 (the [Shīhù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0017) / [Fǎxián](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0048) / [Tiānxīzāi](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0070) cluster). A single late-imperial commentarial extension — Lái Zhōu's 來舟 Yōngzhèng-era *Qiǎnzhù* on the *Xīndì-guān jīng* ([KR6b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0009), [KR6b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0010), [KR6b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0011)) — carries the division into the eighteenth century. The principal transmissional traditions a reader must keep in mind are: (i) the Hàn–Wú southern translation lineage (Ān Shìgāo → Zhī Qiān → Kāng Sēnghuì), which produced the foundational Chinese *jātaka*-anthologies and the canonical *Dharmapada*; (ii) the Western-Jìn Dūnhuáng/Cháng'ān lineage of Zhú Fǎhù (Dharmarakṣa), responsible for an unusually large fraction of the division (at least seven works); (iii) the early-fifth-century Northern-Liáng (Dharmakṣema), Latter-Qín (Kumārajīva, Zhú Fóniàn), and Liú-Sòng (Guṇabhadra, Bǎoyún) translation programmes, which gave Chinese readers the *Buddhacarita*, the *Sūtrālaṃkāra*, and the *Udānavarga* with auto-commentary; and (iv) the Northern Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn*, which produced systematic re-translations of jātaka and parable material (T165, T173, T191, T213, T218, T219). One unusual feature of this division is the prominence of **Chinese editorial compilation** alongside translation: several of the most-influential works — *[Liù-dù jí jīng (T152)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001)*, *[Xiányú jīng (T202)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0059)*, the four *[Zá pìyù jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0061)* anthologies — are sinophone editorial assemblages of Indic narrative material rather than translations of single Indic recensions.

### Important texts and text clusters

**Mahāyāna jātaka-anthologies.** The principal Mahāyāna-inflected *bodhisattva*-jātaka anthologies of the Chinese canon: [KR6b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001) *Liù-dù jí jīng* 六度集經 (T152, Kāng Sēnghuì, c. 247–280), the foundational Wú-period anthology organising 91 *bodhisattva*-tales under the six *pāramitā*s; [KR6b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0002) *Púsà běnyuán jīng* 菩薩本緣經 (T153, Zhī Qiān); [KR6b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0003) *Shēng jīng* 生經 (T154, Zhú Fǎhù); and [KR6b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0012) *Púsà běnshēng mán lùn* 菩薩本生鬘論 (T160, Sòng), the Chinese version of Āryaśūra's *Jātakamālā*.

**Karuṇā-puṇḍarīka cluster.** [KR6b0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0006) *Bēihuā jīng* 悲華經 (T157, Dharmakṣema, 414–421) and its companion [KR6b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0007) *Dàshèng bēifēntuólì jīng* 大乘悲分陀利經 (T158, anonymous Northern-dynasties), two Chinese versions of the *Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra* — a Mahāyāna meta-jātaka in which Śākyamuni's vow-history is the principal narrative.

**Xīndì-guān cluster.** [KR6b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0008) *Dàshèng běnshēng xīndì-guān jīng* 大乘本生心地觀經 (T159, Prajña, 810–811) and its three Qing-Dynasty commentaries by Lái Zhōu — [KR6b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0009) *Xuánshì*, [KR6b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0010) *Kēwén*, and [KR6b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0011) *Qiǎnzhù*; the only post-Sòng works in the division.

**Royal-jātaka single sūtras.** A series of single-fascicle past-life narratives anchored on a virtuous king or prince, ranging from short Hàn-era survivals to Northern-Sòng re-translations: [KR6b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0013) *Chángshòu wáng jīng*, [KR6b0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0014) *Jīnsè wáng jīng*, [KR6b0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0015) *Miàosè wáng yīnyuán jīng*, [KR6b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0017) *Dǐngshēng wáng yīnyuán jīng*, [KR6b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0018) *Yuèguāng púsà jīng*, [KR6b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0023) *Tàizǐ Sūdánà jīng* (the Chinese Vessantara/Sudāna), [KR6b0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0025) *Fúlì tàizǐ yīnyuán jīng* (Puṇyabala). The 太子慕魄/墓魄 doublet — [KR6b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0019) (Ān Shìgāo, c. 148–170) and [KR6b0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0020) (Zhú Fǎhù) — is one of the earliest dated Chinese-Buddhist narrative pairs.

**Śyāmaka recensions.** A remarkable four-fold survival of the *Śyāmaka-jātaka* — [KR6b0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0026), [KR6b0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0027), [KR6b0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0028), [KR6b0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0029) — preserving multiple Chinese recensions (Yáo-Qín and Qǐfú-Qín attributions to Shèngjiān 聖堅, plus an anonymous one) of the same filial-piety jātaka, one of the very few cases in the canon where so many recensions of a single short narrative are preserved side by side. The pair of 九色鹿 (Nine-Coloured Deer, [KR6b0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0035) / [KR6b0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0036)) and 鹿母 (Mother-Deer, [KR6b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0037) / [KR6b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0038)) recensions show similar Wú/Western-Jìn doublet-preservation patterns.

**Lalitavistara pair.** [KR6b0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0042) *Pǔyào jīng* 普曜經 (T186, Zhú Fǎhù, 308) and [KR6b0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0043) *Fāngguǎng dàzhuāngyán jīng* 方廣大莊嚴經 (T187, Divākara, 685) — the early-Jìn and Táng Chinese versions of the Mahāyāna *Lalitavistara*-class Buddha-biography, separated by some 380 years and one of the principal test-cases in comparative Chinese Buddhist translation studies.

**Buddhacarita and verse-biographies.** [KR6b0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0049) *Fó suǒxíng zàn* 佛所行讚 (T192, Dharmakṣema, 414–421), Aśvaghoṣa's *Buddhacarita* — the Chinese version preserves chapters of the Sanskrit *kāvya* that are now lost in the original — and its companion [KR6b0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0050) *Fó běnxíng jīng* (T193, Bǎoyún, Liú-Sòng).

**Hàn-era Buddha-biography pair.** [KR6b0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0040) *Xiūxíng běnqǐ jīng* 修行本起經 (T184, Zhú Dàlì + Kāng Mèngxiáng, 197 CE) and [KR6b0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0053) *Zhōng běnqǐ jīng* 中本起經 (T196, Tánguǒ + Kāng Mèngxiáng, 207 CE) — together a complete Eastern-Hàn Chinese Buddha-biography cycle and one of the earliest dated translations after Ān Shìgāo's. [KR6b0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0041) *Tàizǐ ruìyìng běnqǐ jīng* (T185, Zhī Qiān) is the Wú-period parallel.

**Comprehensive Suí Buddha-biography.** [KR6b0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0047) *Fó běnxíng jí jīng* 佛本行集經 (T190, Jñānagupta, 587–591) — at 60 *juàn* the most extensive Mahāyāna Buddha-biography in Chinese and the most important pre-Tang biographical encyclopedia of the Buddha. [KR6b0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0048) *Zhòngxǔ móhēdì jīng* 眾許摩訶帝經 (T191, Fǎxián 法賢, 980–1001) is its Northern-Sòng re-translation.

**Avadāna anthologies.** Four of the most-cited Chinese *avadāna*-collections: [KR6b0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0057) *Zhuànjí bǎiyuán jīng* 撰集百緣經 (T200, Zhī Qiān) — the Chinese *Avadāna-śataka*; [KR6b0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0058) *Dàzhuāngyán lùn jīng* 大莊嚴論經 (T201, Aśvaghoṣa via Kumārajīva, 405–412) — the *Sūtrālaṃkāra* / *Kalpanāmaṇḍitikā*; [KR6b0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0059) *Xiányú jīng* 賢愚經 (T202, Huìjué et al., 445–459) — compiled at Khotan/Gāochāng directly from oral *avadāna*-recitations and the source of the Tibetan *mDzangs blun*; [KR6b0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0060) *Zábǎozàng jīng* 雜寶藏經 (T203, Jíjiāyè + Tányào, 472) — a Mūlasarvāstivādin compilation foundational for East-Asian popular literature.

**Parable (譬喻) anthologies.** Five anthologies of *pìyù*-narratives showcasing the genre's development from the late Hàn through the Suí: [KR6b0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0061) *Zá pìyù jīng* (T204, attributed Zhī Lóujiāchèn / Lokakṣema, c. 178–200); [KR6b0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0063) *Jiù zá pìyù jīng* 舊雜譬喻經 (T206, Kāng Sēnghuì); [KR6b0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0064) *Zá pìyù jīng* (T207, Dàoluè) and [KR6b0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0065) *Zhòngjīng zhuànzá pìyù* (T208, Dàoluè/Kumārajīva); and the masterpiece [KR6b0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0066) *Bǎiyú jīng* 百喻經 (T209, Saṃghasena via Guṇavṛddhi, 492) — Lú Xùn's 1914 edition made this one of the foundational texts for modern Chinese literary reception of the Buddhist canon.

**Dharmapada / Udānavarga cluster.** The four-text gnomic-verse complex of the Chinese canon: [KR6b0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0067) *Fǎjù jīng* 法句經 (T210, Wéi Qínán / Zhī Qiān, 224) — the canonical Chinese *Dharmapada* with the famous translator's preface; [KR6b0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0068) *Fǎjù pìyù jīng* (T211, Fǎjù + Fǎlì) — verse and avadāna-narrative combined; [KR6b0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0069) *Chūyào jīng* 出曜經 (T212, Zhú Fóniàn, 398–399) — the most extensive Chinese *Udānavarga* with full prose auto-commentary; [KR6b0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0070) *Fǎjí yàosòng jīng* (T213, Tiānxīzāi, 980–1000) — the Northern-Sòng re-translation.

- [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) (active c. 222–253) — Wú-period translator of more works in this division than any other figure: at least nine, including the canonical *Dharmapada* (T210), the *Avadāna-śataka* (T200), the *Aṭṭhakavagga* (T198), and the foundational royal-jātakas (T169, T181a/b, T185, T214); his preface to the *Dharmapada* is the foundational document of pre-modern Chinese Buddhist translation theory.
- [康僧會](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%B7%E5%83%A7%E6%9C%83) (d. 280) — Sogdian-Wú compiler of *[Liù-dù jí jīng (T152)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001)* and the *Jiù zá pìyù jīng* (T206), credited with naturalising *bodhisattva*-ethics in classical-Chinese ethical discourse.

### Topics

- **The 本緣 generic frame.** What unifies the division is the Indic karmic-narrative complex of *jātaka* (past-life of the *bodhisattva*), *avadāna* (karmically-conditioned biography of a virtuous being), *nidāna* (the conditioning narrative for a doctrinal point), and *upamā* / *dṛṣṭānta* (parable). The Chinese organising rubric 本緣 collapses these Indic distinctions; readers should treat them as a continuum rather than as sharply-bounded genres.
- **Translation vs. compilation.** Unlike the Āgamas (KR6a) or Prajñāpāramitā (KR6c), several of the most-influential works of KR6b are **Chinese editorial compilations** rather than translations of single Indic recensions: [T152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001) (Kāng Sēnghuì's compilation under six-*pāramitā* rubric), [T202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0059) (Huìjué et al. assembled from Khotanese oral recitations), the *[Zá pìyù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0061)* complex. The boundary between translation and Chinese authorship is unusually porous here.
- **Multiple-recension preservation.** The division contains an unusual density of multiple-recension survivals of single short jātakas: four *Śyāmaka*-jātakas ([KR6b0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0026)–[KR6b0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0029)), two *Tàizǐ Mùpò* ([KR6b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0019), [KR6b0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0020)), two *Jiǔsè lù* ([KR6b0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0035), [KR6b0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0036)), two *Lùmǔ* ([KR6b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0037), [KR6b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0038)). These doublet/triplet/quadruplet preservations are a key resource for the historical-linguistic study of pre-Tang Chinese Buddhist translation.
- **Buddha-biography textual problem.** Four parallel Buddha-biography traditions are preserved in Chinese — the Hàn 修行/中本起 cycle ([KR6b0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0040) + [KR6b0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0053)), the Wú *Tàizǐ ruìyìng* ([KR6b0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0041)), the *Lalitavistara* pair ([KR6b0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0042) / [KR6b0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0043)), the Mūlasarvāstivādin *Fó běnxíng jí* ([KR6b0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0047)), the *Buddhacarita* + *Fó běnxíng jīng* verse-pair ([KR6b0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0049) + [KR6b0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0050)), and the Sòng *Zhòngxǔ móhēdì jīng* ([KR6b0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0048)) — yielding a four-recension Chinese-canonical Buddha-biography problem whose comparative study is foundational for pre-modern Indic-Buddhist biographical reception.
- **The Dharmapada question.** The three-text Chinese *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* set ([KR6b0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0067), [KR6b0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0069), [KR6b0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0070)) preserves a Sarvāstivādin-tradition recension different from the Pāli *Dhammapada* in selection, ordering, and verse-count, and remains essential to comparative Buddhist gnomic-verse studies alongside the Gāndhārī (Brough), Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (Bernhard), and Pāli traditions.
- **Royal jātaka and ethical-political reading.** A substantial sub-set of the division ([KR6b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0013)–[KR6b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0018), [KR6b0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0022), [KR6b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0023), [KR6b0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0025)) places the *bodhisattva* as a royal protagonist whose *dāna* / *kṣānti* / *vīrya* paradigms are inscribed into models of just kingship; this material was particularly important in the Chinese ethical-political reception of Buddhism (the Vessantara-narrative of [KR6b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0023) is the most-cited example).
- **Vegetarianism / non-violence.** Several works ([KR6b0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0016) *Shīzǐ Sùtuósuō wáng duànròu jīng*; [KR6b0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0039) *Yīqièzhì guāngmíng xiānrén cíxīn yīnyuán bùshíròu jīng*) are textual ancestors of the Chinese-Buddhist meat-renunciation discourse that became central in the Liáng and afterwards.
- **Reception in popular literature.** The avadāna and parable anthologies — especially [T202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0059), [T203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0060), and [T209](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0066) — were the principal canonical source for the Dūnhuáng *biàn-wén* 變文 transformation-text tradition (Mair 1989) and for East-Asian Buddhist popular-narrative literature more broadly; T202 became the basis of the Tibetan *mDzangs blun*.

# 般若部 (T05)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

- [KR6c 般若部 *Bōrě bù* — Buddhist canon — Prajñāpāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom) literature](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/): 1 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6c 般若部 *Bōrě bù* — Buddhist canon — Prajñāpāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom) literature](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6c` is the Kanripo mirror of the Taishō *Bōrě bù* 般若部 — the canonical Buddhist division gathering every Chinese translation of the Indic *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra-corpus together with the major Indic *śāstra*-commentaries on it and the bulk of the East-Asian exegetical literature it generated. In CANWWW the division is `div02` (般若部), running from `T05N0220` (Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle *Dà bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*) through `T08N0261` and the related *śāstra*-cluster in `T25`. The Kanripo `KR6c` directory expands the Taishō *Bōrě bù* by adding the very large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial corpus, so that 229 works are catalogued here in total — by some margin the largest single sūtra-class division in the entire Chinese Buddhist canon.

The chronological span is roughly 179 CE (Lokakṣema's *Dào-xíng bōrě* [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010), the earliest surviving Chinese rendering of an *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension and one of the earliest substantial Mahāyāna translations into Chinese) to the late nineteenth century (a long tail of Qīng-era *Jīngāng jīng* and *Xīnjīng* commentaries). The textual core is Indic: a small handful of Sanskrit *Prajñāpāramitā*-sūtras retranslated repeatedly across seven centuries, attended by an Indic *śāstra*-stratum (Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's Yogācāra commentaries on the *Vajracchedikā*) that mediates the sūtras to scholastic readers. Around this Indic core grew an enormous East-Asian commentarial superstructure — Suí-Táng Sānlùn and Yogācāra scholastic *shū* 疏, Tiāntái doctrinal classification, Sòng Tiāntái and Huáyán *jì* 記, Míng-Qīng Cáodòng and Chán philosophical readings, Japanese Shingon esoteric commentaries — making the division also the principal arena in which every major exegetical school of pre-modern East-Asian Buddhism articulated its reading of emptiness.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The large Prajñāpāramitā recensions

- *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* 大般若波羅蜜多經 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) — Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle integrated translation (660–663) of sixteen *huì* 會 (assemblies) covering the full Indic *prajñā*-corpus from the *Śatasāhasrikā* (100,000-verse) down to the *Vajracchedikā* and *Hṛdaya*. The single most extensive text in the Chinese Buddhist canon and the canonical reference-recension after the seventh century.
- *Móhē bōrě bōluómì jīng* 摩訶般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) — Kumārajīva's 27-fascicle rendering of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* (the "Larger Prajñāpāramitā", 25,000-verse). Up to Xuánzàng the standard Chinese form of the large *prajñā* and the base-text of Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*.
- *Fàngguāng bōrě jīng* 放光般若經 [KR6c0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0002) and *Guāngzàn jīng* 光讚經 [KR6c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0003) — the two Xī-Jìn (286 / 291) renderings of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* by Mokṣala 無羅叉 and Dharmarakṣa 竺法護 respectively; foundational documents of early Chinese Mahāyāna and the textual base for the *gé-yì* 格義 exegesis of the third and fourth centuries.
- *Dàoxíng bōrě jīng* 道行般若經 [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010) — Lokakṣema's 179 CE translation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* (8,000-verse Prajñāpāramitā), the earliest surviving Chinese Prajñāpāramitā text and a key witness for the linguistic state of Late-Hàn Buddhist Chinese.
- *Xiǎopǐn bōrě bōluómì jīng* 小品般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0013) — Kumārajīva's 408 retranslation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā*, the standard "Smaller Prajñāpāramitā" of the medieval Chinese tradition.
- *Dàmíngdù jīng* 大明度經 [KR6c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0011), *Móhē bōrě chāo jīng* 摩訶般若鈔經 [KR6c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0012), *Shèngtiānwáng bōrě bōluómì jīng* 勝天王般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0019) — further independent Wú, Qián-Qín, and Chén-era renderings of medium and large *prajñā* recensions, valued in subsequent tradition as comparative witnesses.

#### The Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra cluster

- *Dàzhìdù lùn* 大智度論 [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) — the 100-fascicle Mahāyāna *śāstra* attributed in the Chinese tradition to Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and translated by Kumārajīva in 402–405. Commentary on the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) but in practice an encyclopaedic compendium of pre-Yogācāra Mahāyāna doctrine; the principal Chinese source for the Sānlùn 三論 tradition and an irreplaceable doctrinal substrate for Tiāntái, Huáyán, and Chán.
- A small but doctrinally significant secondary commentarial cluster grew up around the *Dàzhìdù lùn*: [KR6c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0006) *Dàzhìdù lùn shū* by Huìyǐng 慧影 (the only surviving substantive Chinese commentary on the work), [KR6c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0007) *Dàpǐn jīng yóuyì* by Jízàng 吉藏, [KR6c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0008) *Dà huìdù jīng zōngyào* by the Silla master Wǒnhyo 元曉, and [KR6c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0009) *Dàpǐn jīng yìshū* (again Jízàng).

#### The Vajracchedikā (Diamond Sūtra) cluster

The single largest cluster in the division, comprising six translations, an Indic-śāstra layer, and an exegetical tradition running to the end of the Qīng dynasty:

- Six Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) (the canonical liturgical form), Bodhiruci's [KR6c0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0024), Paramārtha's [KR6c0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0026), Dharmagupta's *Jīngāng néngduàn* [KR6c0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0027), Xuánzàng's *Néngduàn jīngāng bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0029) (also embedded as the ninth *huì* of [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001)), and Yijing's *Fóshuō néngduàn jīngāng* [KR6c0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0028).
- Indic Yogācāra-school *śāstra*-tradition: Asaṅga's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn* [KR6c0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0030) (T1510), Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng lùn* in Bodhiruci's [KR6c0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0032) (T1511) and Yijing's [KR6c0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0031) translations, and the *Jīngāngxiān lùn* [KR6c0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0033) (T1512). Yijing also translated Vasubandhu's *Lùnshì* and *Lùnsòng* [KR6c0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0034) [KR6c0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0035), and the Mādhyamika-school *Pò qǔzhuó bùhuài jiǎmíng lùn* of Gunada 功德施 survives as [KR6c0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0036).
- Major Suí-Táng commentaries: Zhìyǐ 智顗's *Jīngāng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0037), Jízàng's *Jīngāng bōrě shū* [KR6c0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0038), Kuījī 窺基's *Zànshù* [KR6c0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0039) and *Luèshū* [KR6c0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0044), Tang Xuān-zōng's imperial preface-and-commentary [KR6c0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0100) with Dào-yīn 道氤's *Xuānyǎn* [KR6c0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0105), the Huáyán-school *Zuǎnyào* [KR6c0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0041) of Zōngmì 宗密 with Zǐxuán 子璿's *Kāndìng jì* [KR6c0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0042), and the prosimetric *Fù Dàshì sòng* [KR6c0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0104) traditionally attributed to Fù Xī 傅翕 (the *Liáng* Buddhist layman 497–569).
- A continuous Sòng–Yuán–Míng–Qīng Chinese-commentarial corpus of nearly seventy further works (KR6c0040–KR6c0099, KR6c0116) covering every major school: Tiāntái *cǎiwēi* studies of Zǐxuán-school inheritor Zōngjìng 宗鏡 [KR6c0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0052) [KR6c0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0053), Yuán-era *kēyí* ritual exegesis (the *Xiāoshì Jīngāng jīng kēyí* [KR6c0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0055)), late-Míng philosophical readings by Hānshān Déqīng 憨山德清 [KR6c0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0062), Zēng-fèng 曾鳳儀 [KR6c0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0059), and Zhìxù 智旭 [KR6c0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0067) [KR6c0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0068), and a still-larger Qīng commentary tradition.
- Japanese commentary: Kūkai 空海's *Jīngāng bānruò bōluómì jīng kāití* [KR6c0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0101) — the foundational Shingon reading of the *Vajracchedikā*.

#### The Heart Sūtra (Hṛdaya) cluster

The second great cluster — roughly seventy-five works (KR6c0127–KR6c0201) covering every Chinese translation of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya* and the major Chinese, Korean, and Japanese commentarial tradition:

- Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Móhē bānruò bōluómì dàmíng zhòu jīng* [KR6c0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0127) (T250, the earliest surviving form), Xuánzàng's canonical *Bānruò bōluómìduō xīnjīng* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128) (T251, 649 — the standard liturgical text of East-Asian Buddhism), Dharmacandra 法月's *Pǔbiàn zhìzàng* [KR6c0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0129), Prajñā 般若 and Lìyán 利言's long-recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the Sòng-era expansions by Fǎyuè 法月 (T254 / [KR6c0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0131)), Fǎchéng 法成 (T255 / [KR6c0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0132), translated from Tibetan), and Dānapāla 施護 (T257 / [KR6c0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0136)). Sanskrit-transliterated witnesses survive as [KR6c0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0133) (Bùkōng) and [KR6c0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0134) [KR6c0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0135).
- Major Tang commentaries: Kuījī 窺基's *Yōuzàn* [KR6c0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0137), Wǒnch'ǔk 圓測's *Zàn* [KR6c0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0138), Fǎzàng 法藏's *Lüèshū* [KR6c0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0139), Jìngmài 靖邁's *Shū* [KR6c0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0142), the *Huányuán shù* [KR6c0197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0197) and the *Xiézhù* [KR6c0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0198). Sòng *zhāng-shū* tradition: Shīhù 師護 [KR6c0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0140), Zhīyuán 智圓 [KR6c0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0148) [KR6c0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0150).
- A very large Míng–Qīng commentary stratum (KR6c0151–KR6c0195) representing every late-imperial school: Línjì-Chán, Tiāntái, Cáodòng (Hánshì 圅昰's philosophically substantial *Bōrě xīnjīng lùn* [KR6c0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0184); Yuánxián 元賢, Hónglì 弘麗, Hóngzàn 弘贊's *Tiānzú* and *Guànyì*), and gentry Confucian-Buddhist syncretists.
- Japanese commentary: Kūkai's *Bānruò xīnjīng mìjiàn* [KR6c0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0199) — foundational Shingon Heart-Sūtra reading — with two later sub-commentaries [KR6c0200](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0200) [KR6c0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0201).

#### The Renwáng-jīng (Humane King Sūtra) cluster

- Two translations: T245 [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) (canonically attributed to Kumārajīva but most likely a late-fifth- or sixth-century Chinese composition; see Orzech 1998) and Amoghavajra's revised T246 *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) (765–766) which became the canonical text used in the Tang and Heian *Rénwáng-huì* 仁王會 state-protective ritual programme.
- Principal commentaries: Tiāntái Zhìyǐ 智顗 (recorded by Guàndǐng 灌頂)'s *Hùguó bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0204](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0204) with the Sòng sub-commentary *Shénbǎo jì* [KR6c0205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0205); Jízàng's *Rénwáng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0206](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0206); Wǒnch'ǔk's *Rénwáng jīng shū* [KR6c0207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0207); and — most consequentially for state Buddhism — Liángbì 良賁's *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng shū* [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) (composed at Amoghavajra's request shortly after T246 and the canonical Tang esoteric reading of the sūtra). Ming-Qing recensions in [KR6c0209](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0209)–[KR6c0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0215) document the continuing imperial use of the work; Kūkai's *Rénwáng jīng kāití* [KR6c0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0218) is the Shingon counterpart.

#### The Adhyardhaśatikā / Lǐqù-jīng cluster

The *Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā* (the *Lǐqù-jīng* 理趣經) is the only *prajñā* sūtra whose canonical East-Asian reception is straightforwardly Tantric. Four Chinese renderings document its progressive Tantricisation: Bodhiruci II's *Shíxiāng bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0117) (Mahāyāna register), Vajrabodhi 金剛智's *Jīngāngdǐng yújiā lǐqù bānruò jīng* [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) (explicit *Vajraśekhara*-affiliation), Amoghavajra 不空's *Dàlè jīngāng bùkōng zhēnshí sānmóyē jīng* [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120) (the canonical Tang and Japanese *Lǐqù-jīng*, the doctrinal substrate of Shingon practice), and the Sòng *Biànzhào bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0119). The Sòng *Zuìshàng gēnběn dàlè* expansion is [KR6c0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0125). A small Shingon commentarial cluster — Kūkai's *Lǐqù jīng kāití* [KR6c0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0121) and *Zhēnshí jīng wénjù* [KR6c0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0122), Kakuban-circle *Zhǒngzǐ shì* [KR6c0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0123), the *Dàlè jīng xiǎnyì chāo* [KR6c0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0124) — preserves its Heian-Kamakura reception.

#### Wisdom-Mother (Fómǔ) and short-prajñā Sòng translations

A late-Northern-Sòng cluster (980–1018), produced under imperial patronage by the Indian translators Tiānxīzāi 天息災, Fǎxián 法賢, and especially Dānapāla 施護, brings into the canon the late-Indic Pāla-era *Prajñāpāramitā* short-recension and tantric-prajñā literature: the *Fómǔ chūshēng sānfǎzàng* [KR6c0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0014) (the Sòng *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension), the *Fómǔ bǎodézàng* [KR6c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0015) (= *Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā*), the late-Indic *śāstra*-pair [KR6c0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0017) [KR6c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0018) (*Triśatikāyāḥ Prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kārikāsaptati* of Asaṅga / Vasubandhu), the *Jiǔsòng jīngyì lùn* [KR6c0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0016), and a sequence of short Tantric-prajñā texts [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0225](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0225) (the *Yībǎibā míng tuóluóní jīng*, *Liǎoyì jīng*, *Wǔshísòng jīng*, *Dìshì bōrě xīn jīng*, *Xiǎozì bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*, *Guānxiǎng fómǔ púsà jīng*, *Kāijué zìxìng jīng*). Together they document the last continuous wave of Indic *prajñā* literature in Chinese.

#### Late synthetic and Mañjuśrī-related works

- *Wénshūshīlì suǒshuō Móhē bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0020) and *Wénshūshīlì suǒshuō bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0021) — Liáng-era translations of the *Saptaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā*, attaching the *prajñā*-tradition to the Mañjuśrī cult.
- *Dàshèng lǐqù liù bōluómìduō jīng* 大乘理趣六波羅蜜多經 [KR6c0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0226) — Prajñā 般若's late-Táng (788–798) translation of a *prajñā*-frame six-pāramitā synthesis, an important late-Tang doctrinal source.
- *Dà bōrě jīng guānfǎ* [KR6c0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0227), *Dà bōrě jīng gāngyào* [KR6c0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0228), *Dà bōrě guān* [KR6c0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0229) — Sòng and Qīng synthetic / structural guides to T220 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001), representing the long East-Asian project of making the 600-fascicle *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* navigable.
