### Topics

- **Śūnyatā 空 and prajñāpāramitā 般若波羅蜜多.** The division is the canonical home of the Mahāyāna doctrine of universal emptiness — every *dharma* is empty of an intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) — and of the *bodhisattva*-soteriology by which the realisation of emptiness through *prajñā* effects the perfection of all six *pāramitā*s. Every text in the division addresses this doctrine in some register, from the encyclopaedic exposition of the *Dàzhìdù lùn* [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) through the four-corner negation of the *Vajracchedikā* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) to the 260-character compression of the *Heart Sūtra* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128).
- **Form and emptiness (sè-kōng 色空).** The *Heart Sūtra* formula *sè jí shì kōng, kōng jí shì sè* — "form is itself emptiness, emptiness is itself form" — is the most-cited single sentence in East-Asian Buddhism and the focus of an enormous commentarial debate, with virtually every Heart-Sūtra commentary in KR6c0137–KR6c0201 staking a doctrinal position on the relation between the two terms (Yogācāra *vijñaptimātra*, Sānlùn two-truths, Huáyán *lǐ-shì*, Tiāntái *yī-niàn sān-qiān*, Chán *jiàn-xìng*, Cáodòng *substance-function*).
- **The relation of sūtra to śāstra.** The presence in the division of the Indic *śāstra*-stratum — Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn*-cluster — sets up a perennial East-Asian exegetical question about the proper relation between *prajñā*-sūtra and Mādhyamika or Yogācāra *śāstra*-commentary. Sānlùn 三論, Fǎxiàng 法相, and Huáyán 華嚴 commentaries each take a distinctive position; the disagreement runs through the Tang and recurs in Sòng-Míng.
- **Vinayana of the bodhisattva-path.** The *Dàzhìdù lùn* in particular provides the most extensive surviving Indic-source account of the *bodhisattva* career — six *pāramitā*s, ten *bhūmis*, the *anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi* — and is the textual base for medieval Chinese *bodhisattva*-doctrine.
- **State Buddhism.** The *Rénwáng-jīng* [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) is one of the three royal state-protective scriptures (with the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* and the *Mahāmāyūrī*) and the canonical text of an enormous Tang-Heian-Kamakura state-Buddhist political theology, with Liángbì's [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) as its principal scholastic commentary.
- **Tantricisation of the prajñā tradition.** The progressive Tantric reinterpretation of the *Adhyardhaśatikā* through Vajrabodhi [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) and Amoghavajra [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120), the embedding of *dhāraṇī* within the Heart Sūtra in Prajñā's recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the late-Indic Sòng cluster [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0224) together document the gradual incorporation of *prajñā* into the Indic and East-Asian Tantric programme. The Heian Shingon reception (Kūkai's commentaries) gives this tradition its definitive East-Asian articulation.
- **The Mahāprajñāpāramitā as canonical reference work.** The 600-fascicle *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) sits at the centre of the division as a single integrated witness to the Indic *prajñā*-corpus, but its sheer scale generates a continuing problem of accessibility: how does one read 600 fascicles? The Sòng-Qīng synthetic guides [KR6c0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0227) [KR6c0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0228) [KR6c0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0229) are the formal record of the East-Asian project of making the great sūtra usable.

# 般若部 (T06)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 1 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6c 般若部 *Bōrě bù* — Buddhist canon — Prajñāpāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom) literature](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/): 1 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6c 般若部 *Bōrě bù* — Buddhist canon — Prajñāpāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom) literature](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6c` is the Kanripo mirror of the Taishō *Bōrě bù* 般若部 — the canonical Buddhist division gathering every Chinese translation of the Indic *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra-corpus together with the major Indic *śāstra*-commentaries on it and the bulk of the East-Asian exegetical literature it generated. In CANWWW the division is `div02` (般若部), running from `T05N0220` (Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle *Dà bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*) through `T08N0261` and the related *śāstra*-cluster in `T25`. The Kanripo `KR6c` directory expands the Taishō *Bōrě bù* by adding the very large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial corpus, so that 229 works are catalogued here in total — by some margin the largest single sūtra-class division in the entire Chinese Buddhist canon.

The chronological span is roughly 179 CE (Lokakṣema's *Dào-xíng bōrě* [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010), the earliest surviving Chinese rendering of an *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension and one of the earliest substantial Mahāyāna translations into Chinese) to the late nineteenth century (a long tail of Qīng-era *Jīngāng jīng* and *Xīnjīng* commentaries). The textual core is Indic: a small handful of Sanskrit *Prajñāpāramitā*-sūtras retranslated repeatedly across seven centuries, attended by an Indic *śāstra*-stratum (Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's Yogācāra commentaries on the *Vajracchedikā*) that mediates the sūtras to scholastic readers. Around this Indic core grew an enormous East-Asian commentarial superstructure — Suí-Táng Sānlùn and Yogācāra scholastic *shū* 疏, Tiāntái doctrinal classification, Sòng Tiāntái and Huáyán *jì* 記, Míng-Qīng Cáodòng and Chán philosophical readings, Japanese Shingon esoteric commentaries — making the division also the principal arena in which every major exegetical school of pre-modern East-Asian Buddhism articulated its reading of emptiness.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The large Prajñāpāramitā recensions

- *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* 大般若波羅蜜多經 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) — Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle integrated translation (660–663) of sixteen *huì* 會 (assemblies) covering the full Indic *prajñā*-corpus from the *Śatasāhasrikā* (100,000-verse) down to the *Vajracchedikā* and *Hṛdaya*. The single most extensive text in the Chinese Buddhist canon and the canonical reference-recension after the seventh century.
- *Móhē bōrě bōluómì jīng* 摩訶般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) — Kumārajīva's 27-fascicle rendering of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* (the "Larger Prajñāpāramitā", 25,000-verse). Up to Xuánzàng the standard Chinese form of the large *prajñā* and the base-text of Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*.
- *Fàngguāng bōrě jīng* 放光般若經 [KR6c0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0002) and *Guāngzàn jīng* 光讚經 [KR6c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0003) — the two Xī-Jìn (286 / 291) renderings of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* by Mokṣala 無羅叉 and Dharmarakṣa 竺法護 respectively; foundational documents of early Chinese Mahāyāna and the textual base for the *gé-yì* 格義 exegesis of the third and fourth centuries.
- *Dàoxíng bōrě jīng* 道行般若經 [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010) — Lokakṣema's 179 CE translation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* (8,000-verse Prajñāpāramitā), the earliest surviving Chinese Prajñāpāramitā text and a key witness for the linguistic state of Late-Hàn Buddhist Chinese.
- *Xiǎopǐn bōrě bōluómì jīng* 小品般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0013) — Kumārajīva's 408 retranslation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā*, the standard "Smaller Prajñāpāramitā" of the medieval Chinese tradition.
- *Dàmíngdù jīng* 大明度經 [KR6c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0011), *Móhē bōrě chāo jīng* 摩訶般若鈔經 [KR6c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0012), *Shèngtiānwáng bōrě bōluómì jīng* 勝天王般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0019) — further independent Wú, Qián-Qín, and Chén-era renderings of medium and large *prajñā* recensions, valued in subsequent tradition as comparative witnesses.

#### The Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra cluster

- *Dàzhìdù lùn* 大智度論 [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) — the 100-fascicle Mahāyāna *śāstra* attributed in the Chinese tradition to Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and translated by Kumārajīva in 402–405. Commentary on the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) but in practice an encyclopaedic compendium of pre-Yogācāra Mahāyāna doctrine; the principal Chinese source for the Sānlùn 三論 tradition and an irreplaceable doctrinal substrate for Tiāntái, Huáyán, and Chán.
- A small but doctrinally significant secondary commentarial cluster grew up around the *Dàzhìdù lùn*: [KR6c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0006) *Dàzhìdù lùn shū* by Huìyǐng 慧影 (the only surviving substantive Chinese commentary on the work), [KR6c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0007) *Dàpǐn jīng yóuyì* by Jízàng 吉藏, [KR6c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0008) *Dà huìdù jīng zōngyào* by the Silla master Wǒnhyo 元曉, and [KR6c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0009) *Dàpǐn jīng yìshū* (again Jízàng).

#### The Vajracchedikā (Diamond Sūtra) cluster

The single largest cluster in the division, comprising six translations, an Indic-śāstra layer, and an exegetical tradition running to the end of the Qīng dynasty:

- Six Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) (the canonical liturgical form), Bodhiruci's [KR6c0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0024), Paramārtha's [KR6c0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0026), Dharmagupta's *Jīngāng néngduàn* [KR6c0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0027), Xuánzàng's *Néngduàn jīngāng bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0029) (also embedded as the ninth *huì* of [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001)), and Yijing's *Fóshuō néngduàn jīngāng* [KR6c0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0028).

#### The Heart Sūtra (Hṛdaya) cluster

The second great cluster — roughly seventy-five works (KR6c0127–KR6c0201) covering every Chinese translation of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya* and the major Chinese, Korean, and Japanese commentarial tradition:

- Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Móhē bānruò bōluómì dàmíng zhòu jīng* [KR6c0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0127) (T250, the earliest surviving form), Xuánzàng's canonical *Bānruò bōluómìduō xīnjīng* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128) (T251, 649 — the standard liturgical text of East-Asian Buddhism), Dharmacandra 法月's *Pǔbiàn zhìzàng* [KR6c0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0129), Prajñā 般若 and Lìyán 利言's long-recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the Sòng-era expansions by Fǎyuè 法月 (T254 / [KR6c0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0131)), Fǎchéng 法成 (T255 / [KR6c0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0132), translated from Tibetan), and Dānapāla 施護 (T257 / [KR6c0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0136)). Sanskrit-transliterated witnesses survive as [KR6c0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0133) (Bùkōng) and [KR6c0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0134) [KR6c0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0135).
- Major Tang commentaries: Kuījī 窺基's *Yōuzàn* [KR6c0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0137), Wǒnch'ǔk 圓測's *Zàn* [KR6c0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0138), Fǎzàng 法藏's *Lüèshū* [KR6c0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0139), Jìngmài 靖邁's *Shū* [KR6c0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0142), the *Huányuán shù* [KR6c0197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0197) and the *Xiézhù* [KR6c0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0198). Sòng *zhāng-shū* tradition: Shīhù 師護 [KR6c0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0140), Zhīyuán 智圓 [KR6c0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0148) [KR6c0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0150).

#### The Renwáng-jīng (Humane King Sūtra) cluster

- Two translations: T245 [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) (canonically attributed to Kumārajīva but most likely a late-fifth- or sixth-century Chinese composition; see Orzech 1998) and Amoghavajra's revised T246 *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) (765–766) which became the canonical text used in the Tang and Heian *Rénwáng-huì* 仁王會 state-protective ritual programme.
- Principal commentaries: Tiāntái Zhìyǐ 智顗 (recorded by Guàndǐng 灌頂)'s *Hùguó bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0204](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0204) with the Sòng sub-commentary *Shénbǎo jì* [KR6c0205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0205); Jízàng's *Rénwáng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0206](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0206); Wǒnch'ǔk's *Rénwáng jīng shū* [KR6c0207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0207); and — most consequentially for state Buddhism — Liángbì 良賁's *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng shū* [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) (composed at Amoghavajra's request shortly after T246 and the canonical Tang esoteric reading of the sūtra). Ming-Qing recensions in [KR6c0209](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0209)–[KR6c0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0215) document the continuing imperial use of the work; Kūkai's *Rénwáng jīng kāití* [KR6c0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0218) is the Shingon counterpart.

#### The Adhyardhaśatikā / Lǐqù-jīng cluster

The *Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā* (the *Lǐqù-jīng* 理趣經) is the only *prajñā* sūtra whose canonical East-Asian reception is straightforwardly Tantric. Four Chinese renderings document its progressive Tantricisation: Bodhiruci II's *Shíxiāng bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0117) (Mahāyāna register), Vajrabodhi 金剛智's *Jīngāngdǐng yújiā lǐqù bānruò jīng* [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) (explicit *Vajraśekhara*-affiliation), Amoghavajra 不空's *Dàlè jīngāng bùkōng zhēnshí sānmóyē jīng* [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120) (the canonical Tang and Japanese *Lǐqù-jīng*, the doctrinal substrate of Shingon practice), and the Sòng *Biànzhào bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0119). The Sòng *Zuìshàng gēnběn dàlè* expansion is [KR6c0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0125). A small Shingon commentarial cluster — Kūkai's *Lǐqù jīng kāití* [KR6c0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0121) and *Zhēnshí jīng wénjù* [KR6c0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0122), Kakuban-circle *Zhǒngzǐ shì* [KR6c0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0123), the *Dàlè jīng xiǎnyì chāo* [KR6c0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0124) — preserves its Heian-Kamakura reception.

#### Wisdom-Mother (Fómǔ) and short-prajñā Sòng translations

A late-Northern-Sòng cluster (980–1018), produced under imperial patronage by the Indian translators Tiānxīzāi 天息災, Fǎxián 法賢, and especially Dānapāla 施護, brings into the canon the late-Indic Pāla-era *Prajñāpāramitā* short-recension and tantric-prajñā literature: the *Fómǔ chūshēng sānfǎzàng* [KR6c0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0014) (the Sòng *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension), the *Fómǔ bǎodézàng* [KR6c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0015) (= *Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā*), the late-Indic *śāstra*-pair [KR6c0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0017) [KR6c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0018) (*Triśatikāyāḥ Prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kārikāsaptati* of Asaṅga / Vasubandhu), the *Jiǔsòng jīngyì lùn* [KR6c0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0016), and a sequence of short Tantric-prajñā texts [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0225](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0225) (the *Yībǎibā míng tuóluóní jīng*, *Liǎoyì jīng*, *Wǔshísòng jīng*, *Dìshì bōrě xīn jīng*, *Xiǎozì bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*, *Guānxiǎng fómǔ púsà jīng*, *Kāijué zìxìng jīng*). Together they document the last continuous wave of Indic *prajñā* literature in Chinese.

### Topics

- **Śūnyatā 空 and prajñāpāramitā 般若波羅蜜多.** The division is the canonical home of the Mahāyāna doctrine of universal emptiness — every *dharma* is empty of an intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) — and of the *bodhisattva*-soteriology by which the realisation of emptiness through *prajñā* effects the perfection of all six *pāramitā*s. Every text in the division addresses this doctrine in some register, from the encyclopaedic exposition of the *Dàzhìdù lùn* [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) through the four-corner negation of the *Vajracchedikā* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) to the 260-character compression of the *Heart Sūtra* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128).
- **Form and emptiness (sè-kōng 色空).** The *Heart Sūtra* formula *sè jí shì kōng, kōng jí shì sè* — "form is itself emptiness, emptiness is itself form" — is the most-cited single sentence in East-Asian Buddhism and the focus of an enormous commentarial debate, with virtually every Heart-Sūtra commentary in KR6c0137–KR6c0201 staking a doctrinal position on the relation between the two terms (Yogācāra *vijñaptimātra*, Sānlùn two-truths, Huáyán *lǐ-shì*, Tiāntái *yī-niàn sān-qiān*, Chán *jiàn-xìng*, Cáodòng *substance-function*).
- **The relation of sūtra to śāstra.** The presence in the division of the Indic *śāstra*-stratum — Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn*-cluster — sets up a perennial East-Asian exegetical question about the proper relation between *prajñā*-sūtra and Mādhyamika or Yogācāra *śāstra*-commentary. Sānlùn 三論, Fǎxiàng 法相, and Huáyán 華嚴 commentaries each take a distinctive position; the disagreement runs through the Tang and recurs in Sòng-Míng.
- **Vinayana of the bodhisattva-path.** The *Dàzhìdù lùn* in particular provides the most extensive surviving Indic-source account of the *bodhisattva* career — six *pāramitā*s, ten *bhūmis*, the *anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi* — and is the textual base for medieval Chinese *bodhisattva*-doctrine.
- **State Buddhism.** The *Rénwáng-jīng* [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) is one of the three royal state-protective scriptures (with the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* and the *Mahāmāyūrī*) and the canonical text of an enormous Tang-Heian-Kamakura state-Buddhist political theology, with Liángbì's [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) as its principal scholastic commentary.

# 般若部 (T07)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

## Division note: [KR6c 般若部 *Bōrě bù* — Buddhist canon — Prajñāpāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom) literature](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6c` is the Kanripo mirror of the Taishō *Bōrě bù* 般若部 — the canonical Buddhist division gathering every Chinese translation of the Indic *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra-corpus together with the major Indic *śāstra*-commentaries on it and the bulk of the East-Asian exegetical literature it generated. In CANWWW the division is `div02` (般若部), running from `T05N0220` (Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle *Dà bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*) through `T08N0261` and the related *śāstra*-cluster in `T25`. The Kanripo `KR6c` directory expands the Taishō *Bōrě bù* by adding the very large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial corpus, so that 229 works are catalogued here in total — by some margin the largest single sūtra-class division in the entire Chinese Buddhist canon.

The chronological span is roughly 179 CE (Lokakṣema's *Dào-xíng bōrě* [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010), the earliest surviving Chinese rendering of an *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension and one of the earliest substantial Mahāyāna translations into Chinese) to the late nineteenth century (a long tail of Qīng-era *Jīngāng jīng* and *Xīnjīng* commentaries). The textual core is Indic: a small handful of Sanskrit *Prajñāpāramitā*-sūtras retranslated repeatedly across seven centuries, attended by an Indic *śāstra*-stratum (Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's Yogācāra commentaries on the *Vajracchedikā*) that mediates the sūtras to scholastic readers. Around this Indic core grew an enormous East-Asian commentarial superstructure — Suí-Táng Sānlùn and Yogācāra scholastic *shū* 疏, Tiāntái doctrinal classification, Sòng Tiāntái and Huáyán *jì* 記, Míng-Qīng Cáodòng and Chán philosophical readings, Japanese Shingon esoteric commentaries — making the division also the principal arena in which every major exegetical school of pre-modern East-Asian Buddhism articulated its reading of emptiness.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The large Prajñāpāramitā recensions

- *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* 大般若波羅蜜多經 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) — Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle integrated translation (660–663) of sixteen *huì* 會 (assemblies) covering the full Indic *prajñā*-corpus from the *Śatasāhasrikā* (100,000-verse) down to the *Vajracchedikā* and *Hṛdaya*. The single most extensive text in the Chinese Buddhist canon and the canonical reference-recension after the seventh century.
- *Móhē bōrě bōluómì jīng* 摩訶般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) — Kumārajīva's 27-fascicle rendering of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* (the "Larger Prajñāpāramitā", 25,000-verse). Up to Xuánzàng the standard Chinese form of the large *prajñā* and the base-text of Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*.
- *Fàngguāng bōrě jīng* 放光般若經 [KR6c0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0002) and *Guāngzàn jīng* 光讚經 [KR6c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0003) — the two Xī-Jìn (286 / 291) renderings of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* by Mokṣala 無羅叉 and Dharmarakṣa 竺法護 respectively; foundational documents of early Chinese Mahāyāna and the textual base for the *gé-yì* 格義 exegesis of the third and fourth centuries.
- *Dàoxíng bōrě jīng* 道行般若經 [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010) — Lokakṣema's 179 CE translation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* (8,000-verse Prajñāpāramitā), the earliest surviving Chinese Prajñāpāramitā text and a key witness for the linguistic state of Late-Hàn Buddhist Chinese.
- *Xiǎopǐn bōrě bōluómì jīng* 小品般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0013) — Kumārajīva's 408 retranslation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā*, the standard "Smaller Prajñāpāramitā" of the medieval Chinese tradition.
- *Dàmíngdù jīng* 大明度經 [KR6c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0011), *Móhē bōrě chāo jīng* 摩訶般若鈔經 [KR6c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0012), *Shèngtiānwáng bōrě bōluómì jīng* 勝天王般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0019) — further independent Wú, Qián-Qín, and Chén-era renderings of medium and large *prajñā* recensions, valued in subsequent tradition as comparative witnesses.

#### The Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra cluster

- *Dàzhìdù lùn* 大智度論 [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) — the 100-fascicle Mahāyāna *śāstra* attributed in the Chinese tradition to Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and translated by Kumārajīva in 402–405. Commentary on the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) but in practice an encyclopaedic compendium of pre-Yogācāra Mahāyāna doctrine; the principal Chinese source for the Sānlùn 三論 tradition and an irreplaceable doctrinal substrate for Tiāntái, Huáyán, and Chán.
- A small but doctrinally significant secondary commentarial cluster grew up around the *Dàzhìdù lùn*: [KR6c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0006) *Dàzhìdù lùn shū* by Huìyǐng 慧影 (the only surviving substantive Chinese commentary on the work), [KR6c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0007) *Dàpǐn jīng yóuyì* by Jízàng 吉藏, [KR6c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0008) *Dà huìdù jīng zōngyào* by the Silla master Wǒnhyo 元曉, and [KR6c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0009) *Dàpǐn jīng yìshū* (again Jízàng).

#### The Vajracchedikā (Diamond Sūtra) cluster

The single largest cluster in the division, comprising six translations, an Indic-śāstra layer, and an exegetical tradition running to the end of the Qīng dynasty:

- Six Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) (the canonical liturgical form), Bodhiruci's [KR6c0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0024), Paramārtha's [KR6c0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0026), Dharmagupta's *Jīngāng néngduàn* [KR6c0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0027), Xuánzàng's *Néngduàn jīngāng bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0029) (also embedded as the ninth *huì* of [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001)), and Yijing's *Fóshuō néngduàn jīngāng* [KR6c0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0028).
- Indic Yogācāra-school *śāstra*-tradition: Asaṅga's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn* [KR6c0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0030) (T1510), Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng lùn* in Bodhiruci's [KR6c0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0032) (T1511) and Yijing's [KR6c0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0031) translations, and the *Jīngāngxiān lùn* [KR6c0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0033) (T1512). Yijing also translated Vasubandhu's *Lùnshì* and *Lùnsòng* [KR6c0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0034) [KR6c0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0035), and the Mādhyamika-school *Pò qǔzhuó bùhuài jiǎmíng lùn* of Gunada 功德施 survives as [KR6c0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0036).
- Major Suí-Táng commentaries: Zhìyǐ 智顗's *Jīngāng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0037), Jízàng's *Jīngāng bōrě shū* [KR6c0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0038), Kuījī 窺基's *Zànshù* [KR6c0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0039) and *Luèshū* [KR6c0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0044), Tang Xuān-zōng's imperial preface-and-commentary [KR6c0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0100) with Dào-yīn 道氤's *Xuānyǎn* [KR6c0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0105), the Huáyán-school *Zuǎnyào* [KR6c0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0041) of Zōngmì 宗密 with Zǐxuán 子璿's *Kāndìng jì* [KR6c0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0042), and the prosimetric *Fù Dàshì sòng* [KR6c0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0104) traditionally attributed to Fù Xī 傅翕 (the *Liáng* Buddhist layman 497–569).
- A continuous Sòng–Yuán–Míng–Qīng Chinese-commentarial corpus of nearly seventy further works (KR6c0040–KR6c0099, KR6c0116) covering every major school: Tiāntái *cǎiwēi* studies of Zǐxuán-school inheritor Zōngjìng 宗鏡 [KR6c0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0052) [KR6c0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0053), Yuán-era *kēyí* ritual exegesis (the *Xiāoshì Jīngāng jīng kēyí* [KR6c0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0055)), late-Míng philosophical readings by Hānshān Déqīng 憨山德清 [KR6c0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0062), Zēng-fèng 曾鳳儀 [KR6c0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0059), and Zhìxù 智旭 [KR6c0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0067) [KR6c0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0068), and a still-larger Qīng commentary tradition.
- Japanese commentary: Kūkai 空海's *Jīngāng bānruò bōluómì jīng kāití* [KR6c0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0101) — the foundational Shingon reading of the *Vajracchedikā*.

#### The Heart Sūtra (Hṛdaya) cluster

The second great cluster — roughly seventy-five works (KR6c0127–KR6c0201) covering every Chinese translation of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya* and the major Chinese, Korean, and Japanese commentarial tradition:

- Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Móhē bānruò bōluómì dàmíng zhòu jīng* [KR6c0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0127) (T250, the earliest surviving form), Xuánzàng's canonical *Bānruò bōluómìduō xīnjīng* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128) (T251, 649 — the standard liturgical text of East-Asian Buddhism), Dharmacandra 法月's *Pǔbiàn zhìzàng* [KR6c0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0129), Prajñā 般若 and Lìyán 利言's long-recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the Sòng-era expansions by Fǎyuè 法月 (T254 / [KR6c0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0131)), Fǎchéng 法成 (T255 / [KR6c0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0132), translated from Tibetan), and Dānapāla 施護 (T257 / [KR6c0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0136)). Sanskrit-transliterated witnesses survive as [KR6c0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0133) (Bùkōng) and [KR6c0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0134) [KR6c0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0135).
- Major Tang commentaries: Kuījī 窺基's *Yōuzàn* [KR6c0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0137), Wǒnch'ǔk 圓測's *Zàn* [KR6c0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0138), Fǎzàng 法藏's *Lüèshū* [KR6c0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0139), Jìngmài 靖邁's *Shū* [KR6c0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0142), the *Huányuán shù* [KR6c0197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0197) and the *Xiézhù* [KR6c0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0198). Sòng *zhāng-shū* tradition: Shīhù 師護 [KR6c0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0140), Zhīyuán 智圓 [KR6c0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0148) [KR6c0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0150).
- A very large Míng–Qīng commentary stratum (KR6c0151–KR6c0195) representing every late-imperial school: Línjì-Chán, Tiāntái, Cáodòng (Hánshì 圅昰's philosophically substantial *Bōrě xīnjīng lùn* [KR6c0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0184); Yuánxián 元賢, Hónglì 弘麗, Hóngzàn 弘贊's *Tiānzú* and *Guànyì*), and gentry Confucian-Buddhist syncretists.
- Japanese commentary: Kūkai's *Bānruò xīnjīng mìjiàn* [KR6c0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0199) — foundational Shingon Heart-Sūtra reading — with two later sub-commentaries [KR6c0200](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0200) [KR6c0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0201).

#### The Renwáng-jīng (Humane King Sūtra) cluster

- Two translations: T245 [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) (canonically attributed to Kumārajīva but most likely a late-fifth- or sixth-century Chinese composition; see Orzech 1998) and Amoghavajra's revised T246 *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) (765–766) which became the canonical text used in the Tang and Heian *Rénwáng-huì* 仁王會 state-protective ritual programme.
- Principal commentaries: Tiāntái Zhìyǐ 智顗 (recorded by Guàndǐng 灌頂)'s *Hùguó bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0204](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0204) with the Sòng sub-commentary *Shénbǎo jì* [KR6c0205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0205); Jízàng's *Rénwáng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0206](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0206); Wǒnch'ǔk's *Rénwáng jīng shū* [KR6c0207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0207); and — most consequentially for state Buddhism — Liángbì 良賁's *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng shū* [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) (composed at Amoghavajra's request shortly after T246 and the canonical Tang esoteric reading of the sūtra). Ming-Qing recensions in [KR6c0209](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0209)–[KR6c0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0215) document the continuing imperial use of the work; Kūkai's *Rénwáng jīng kāití* [KR6c0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0218) is the Shingon counterpart.

#### The Adhyardhaśatikā / Lǐqù-jīng cluster

The *Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā* (the *Lǐqù-jīng* 理趣經) is the only *prajñā* sūtra whose canonical East-Asian reception is straightforwardly Tantric. Four Chinese renderings document its progressive Tantricisation: Bodhiruci II's *Shíxiāng bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0117) (Mahāyāna register), Vajrabodhi 金剛智's *Jīngāngdǐng yújiā lǐqù bānruò jīng* [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) (explicit *Vajraśekhara*-affiliation), Amoghavajra 不空's *Dàlè jīngāng bùkōng zhēnshí sānmóyē jīng* [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120) (the canonical Tang and Japanese *Lǐqù-jīng*, the doctrinal substrate of Shingon practice), and the Sòng *Biànzhào bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0119). The Sòng *Zuìshàng gēnběn dàlè* expansion is [KR6c0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0125). A small Shingon commentarial cluster — Kūkai's *Lǐqù jīng kāití* [KR6c0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0121) and *Zhēnshí jīng wénjù* [KR6c0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0122), Kakuban-circle *Zhǒngzǐ shì* [KR6c0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0123), the *Dàlè jīng xiǎnyì chāo* [KR6c0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0124) — preserves its Heian-Kamakura reception.

#### Wisdom-Mother (Fómǔ) and short-prajñā Sòng translations

A late-Northern-Sòng cluster (980–1018), produced under imperial patronage by the Indian translators Tiānxīzāi 天息災, Fǎxián 法賢, and especially Dānapāla 施護, brings into the canon the late-Indic Pāla-era *Prajñāpāramitā* short-recension and tantric-prajñā literature: the *Fómǔ chūshēng sānfǎzàng* [KR6c0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0014) (the Sòng *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension), the *Fómǔ bǎodézàng* [KR6c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0015) (= *Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā*), the late-Indic *śāstra*-pair [KR6c0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0017) [KR6c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0018) (*Triśatikāyāḥ Prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kārikāsaptati* of Asaṅga / Vasubandhu), the *Jiǔsòng jīngyì lùn* [KR6c0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0016), and a sequence of short Tantric-prajñā texts [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0225](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0225) (the *Yībǎibā míng tuóluóní jīng*, *Liǎoyì jīng*, *Wǔshísòng jīng*, *Dìshì bōrě xīn jīng*, *Xiǎozì bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*, *Guānxiǎng fómǔ púsà jīng*, *Kāijué zìxìng jīng*). Together they document the last continuous wave of Indic *prajñā* literature in Chinese.

#### Late synthetic and Mañjuśrī-related works

- *Wénshūshīlì suǒshuō Móhē bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0020) and *Wénshūshīlì suǒshuō bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0021) — Liáng-era translations of the *Saptaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā*, attaching the *prajñā*-tradition to the Mañjuśrī cult.
- *Dàshèng lǐqù liù bōluómìduō jīng* 大乘理趣六波羅蜜多經 [KR6c0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0226) — Prajñā 般若's late-Táng (788–798) translation of a *prajñā*-frame six-pāramitā synthesis, an important late-Tang doctrinal source.
- *Dà bōrě jīng guānfǎ* [KR6c0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0227), *Dà bōrě jīng gāngyào* [KR6c0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0228), *Dà bōrě guān* [KR6c0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0229) — Sòng and Qīng synthetic / structural guides to T220 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001), representing the long East-Asian project of making the 600-fascicle *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* navigable.

### Topics

- **Śūnyatā 空 and prajñāpāramitā 般若波羅蜜多.** The division is the canonical home of the Mahāyāna doctrine of universal emptiness — every *dharma* is empty of an intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) — and of the *bodhisattva*-soteriology by which the realisation of emptiness through *prajñā* effects the perfection of all six *pāramitā*s. Every text in the division addresses this doctrine in some register, from the encyclopaedic exposition of the *Dàzhìdù lùn* [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) through the four-corner negation of the *Vajracchedikā* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) to the 260-character compression of the *Heart Sūtra* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128).
- **Form and emptiness (sè-kōng 色空).** The *Heart Sūtra* formula *sè jí shì kōng, kōng jí shì sè* — "form is itself emptiness, emptiness is itself form" — is the most-cited single sentence in East-Asian Buddhism and the focus of an enormous commentarial debate, with virtually every Heart-Sūtra commentary in KR6c0137–KR6c0201 staking a doctrinal position on the relation between the two terms (Yogācāra *vijñaptimātra*, Sānlùn two-truths, Huáyán *lǐ-shì*, Tiāntái *yī-niàn sān-qiān*, Chán *jiàn-xìng*, Cáodòng *substance-function*).
- **The relation of sūtra to śāstra.** The presence in the division of the Indic *śāstra*-stratum — Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn*-cluster — sets up a perennial East-Asian exegetical question about the proper relation between *prajñā*-sūtra and Mādhyamika or Yogācāra *śāstra*-commentary. Sānlùn 三論, Fǎxiàng 法相, and Huáyán 華嚴 commentaries each take a distinctive position; the disagreement runs through the Tang and recurs in Sòng-Míng.
- **Vinayana of the bodhisattva-path.** The *Dàzhìdù lùn* in particular provides the most extensive surviving Indic-source account of the *bodhisattva* career — six *pāramitā*s, ten *bhūmis*, the *anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi* — and is the textual base for medieval Chinese *bodhisattva*-doctrine.
- **State Buddhism.** The *Rénwáng-jīng* [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) is one of the three royal state-protective scriptures (with the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* and the *Mahāmāyūrī*) and the canonical text of an enormous Tang-Heian-Kamakura state-Buddhist political theology, with Liángbì's [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) as its principal scholastic commentary.
- **Tantricisation of the prajñā tradition.** The progressive Tantric reinterpretation of the *Adhyardhaśatikā* through Vajrabodhi [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) and Amoghavajra [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120), the embedding of *dhāraṇī* within the Heart Sūtra in Prajñā's recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the late-Indic Sòng cluster [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0224) together document the gradual incorporation of *prajñā* into the Indic and East-Asian Tantric programme. The Heian Shingon reception (Kūkai's commentaries) gives this tradition its definitive East-Asian articulation.
- **The Mahāprajñāpāramitā as canonical reference work.** The 600-fascicle *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) sits at the centre of the division as a single integrated witness to the Indic *prajñā*-corpus, but its sheer scale generates a continuing problem of accessibility: how does one read 600 fascicles? The Sòng-Qīng synthetic guides [KR6c0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0227) [KR6c0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0228) [KR6c0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0229) are the formal record of the East-Asian project of making the great sūtra usable.

# 般若部 (T08)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 42 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6c 般若部 *Bōrě bù* — Buddhist canon — Prajñāpāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom) literature](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/): 42 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6c 般若部 *Bōrě bù* — Buddhist canon — Prajñāpāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom) literature](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6c` is the Kanripo mirror of the Taishō *Bōrě bù* 般若部 — the canonical Buddhist division gathering every Chinese translation of the Indic *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra-corpus together with the major Indic *śāstra*-commentaries on it and the bulk of the East-Asian exegetical literature it generated. In CANWWW the division is `div02` (般若部), running from `T05N0220` (Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle *Dà bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*) through `T08N0261` and the related *śāstra*-cluster in `T25`. The Kanripo `KR6c` directory expands the Taishō *Bōrě bù* by adding the very large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial corpus, so that 229 works are catalogued here in total — by some margin the largest single sūtra-class division in the entire Chinese Buddhist canon.

The chronological span is roughly 179 CE (Lokakṣema's *Dào-xíng bōrě* [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010), the earliest surviving Chinese rendering of an *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension and one of the earliest substantial Mahāyāna translations into Chinese) to the late nineteenth century (a long tail of Qīng-era *Jīngāng jīng* and *Xīnjīng* commentaries). The textual core is Indic: a small handful of Sanskrit *Prajñāpāramitā*-sūtras retranslated repeatedly across seven centuries, attended by an Indic *śāstra*-stratum (Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's Yogācāra commentaries on the *Vajracchedikā*) that mediates the sūtras to scholastic readers. Around this Indic core grew an enormous East-Asian commentarial superstructure — Suí-Táng Sānlùn and Yogācāra scholastic *shū* 疏, Tiāntái doctrinal classification, Sòng Tiāntái and Huáyán *jì* 記, Míng-Qīng Cáodòng and Chán philosophical readings, Japanese Shingon esoteric commentaries — making the division also the principal arena in which every major exegetical school of pre-modern East-Asian Buddhism articulated its reading of emptiness.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The large Prajñāpāramitā recensions

- *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* 大般若波羅蜜多經 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) — Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle integrated translation (660–663) of sixteen *huì* 會 (assemblies) covering the full Indic *prajñā*-corpus from the *Śatasāhasrikā* (100,000-verse) down to the *Vajracchedikā* and *Hṛdaya*. The single most extensive text in the Chinese Buddhist canon and the canonical reference-recension after the seventh century.
- *Móhē bōrě bōluómì jīng* 摩訶般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) — Kumārajīva's 27-fascicle rendering of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* (the "Larger Prajñāpāramitā", 25,000-verse). Up to Xuánzàng the standard Chinese form of the large *prajñā* and the base-text of Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*.
- *Fàngguāng bōrě jīng* 放光般若經 [KR6c0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0002) and *Guāngzàn jīng* 光讚經 [KR6c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0003) — the two Xī-Jìn (286 / 291) renderings of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* by Mokṣala 無羅叉 and Dharmarakṣa 竺法護 respectively; foundational documents of early Chinese Mahāyāna and the textual base for the *gé-yì* 格義 exegesis of the third and fourth centuries.
- *Dàoxíng bōrě jīng* 道行般若經 [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010) — Lokakṣema's 179 CE translation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* (8,000-verse Prajñāpāramitā), the earliest surviving Chinese Prajñāpāramitā text and a key witness for the linguistic state of Late-Hàn Buddhist Chinese.
- *Xiǎopǐn bōrě bōluómì jīng* 小品般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0013) — Kumārajīva's 408 retranslation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā*, the standard "Smaller Prajñāpāramitā" of the medieval Chinese tradition.
- *Dàmíngdù jīng* 大明度經 [KR6c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0011), *Móhē bōrě chāo jīng* 摩訶般若鈔經 [KR6c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0012), *Shèngtiānwáng bōrě bōluómì jīng* 勝天王般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0019) — further independent Wú, Qián-Qín, and Chén-era renderings of medium and large *prajñā* recensions, valued in subsequent tradition as comparative witnesses.

#### The Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra cluster

- *Dàzhìdù lùn* 大智度論 [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) — the 100-fascicle Mahāyāna *śāstra* attributed in the Chinese tradition to Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and translated by Kumārajīva in 402–405. Commentary on the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) but in practice an encyclopaedic compendium of pre-Yogācāra Mahāyāna doctrine; the principal Chinese source for the Sānlùn 三論 tradition and an irreplaceable doctrinal substrate for Tiāntái, Huáyán, and Chán.
- A small but doctrinally significant secondary commentarial cluster grew up around the *Dàzhìdù lùn*: [KR6c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0006) *Dàzhìdù lùn shū* by Huìyǐng 慧影 (the only surviving substantive Chinese commentary on the work), [KR6c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0007) *Dàpǐn jīng yóuyì* by Jízàng 吉藏, [KR6c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0008) *Dà huìdù jīng zōngyào* by the Silla master Wǒnhyo 元曉, and [KR6c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0009) *Dàpǐn jīng yìshū* (again Jízàng).

#### The Vajracchedikā (Diamond Sūtra) cluster

The single largest cluster in the division, comprising six translations, an Indic-śāstra layer, and an exegetical tradition running to the end of the Qīng dynasty:

- Six Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) (the canonical liturgical form), Bodhiruci's [KR6c0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0024), Paramārtha's [KR6c0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0026), Dharmagupta's *Jīngāng néngduàn* [KR6c0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0027), Xuánzàng's *Néngduàn jīngāng bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0029) (also embedded as the ninth *huì* of [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001)), and Yijing's *Fóshuō néngduàn jīngāng* [KR6c0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0028).
- Indic Yogācāra-school *śāstra*-tradition: Asaṅga's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn* [KR6c0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0030) (T1510), Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng lùn* in Bodhiruci's [KR6c0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0032) (T1511) and Yijing's [KR6c0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0031) translations, and the *Jīngāngxiān lùn* [KR6c0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0033) (T1512). Yijing also translated Vasubandhu's *Lùnshì* and *Lùnsòng* [KR6c0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0034) [KR6c0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0035), and the Mādhyamika-school *Pò qǔzhuó bùhuài jiǎmíng lùn* of Gunada 功德施 survives as [KR6c0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0036).
- Major Suí-Táng commentaries: Zhìyǐ 智顗's *Jīngāng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0037), Jízàng's *Jīngāng bōrě shū* [KR6c0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0038), Kuījī 窺基's *Zànshù* [KR6c0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0039) and *Luèshū* [KR6c0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0044), Tang Xuān-zōng's imperial preface-and-commentary [KR6c0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0100) with Dào-yīn 道氤's *Xuānyǎn* [KR6c0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0105), the Huáyán-school *Zuǎnyào* [KR6c0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0041) of Zōngmì 宗密 with Zǐxuán 子璿's *Kāndìng jì* [KR6c0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0042), and the prosimetric *Fù Dàshì sòng* [KR6c0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0104) traditionally attributed to Fù Xī 傅翕 (the *Liáng* Buddhist layman 497–569).
- A continuous Sòng–Yuán–Míng–Qīng Chinese-commentarial corpus of nearly seventy further works (KR6c0040–KR6c0099, KR6c0116) covering every major school: Tiāntái *cǎiwēi* studies of Zǐxuán-school inheritor Zōngjìng 宗鏡 [KR6c0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0052) [KR6c0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0053), Yuán-era *kēyí* ritual exegesis (the *Xiāoshì Jīngāng jīng kēyí* [KR6c0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0055)), late-Míng philosophical readings by Hānshān Déqīng 憨山德清 [KR6c0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0062), Zēng-fèng 曾鳳儀 [KR6c0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0059), and Zhìxù 智旭 [KR6c0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0067) [KR6c0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0068), and a still-larger Qīng commentary tradition.
- Japanese commentary: Kūkai 空海's *Jīngāng bānruò bōluómì jīng kāití* [KR6c0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0101) — the foundational Shingon reading of the *Vajracchedikā*.

#### The Heart Sūtra (Hṛdaya) cluster

The second great cluster — roughly seventy-five works (KR6c0127–KR6c0201) covering every Chinese translation of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya* and the major Chinese, Korean, and Japanese commentarial tradition:

- Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Móhē bānruò bōluómì dàmíng zhòu jīng* [KR6c0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0127) (T250, the earliest surviving form), Xuánzàng's canonical *Bānruò bōluómìduō xīnjīng* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128) (T251, 649 — the standard liturgical text of East-Asian Buddhism), Dharmacandra 法月's *Pǔbiàn zhìzàng* [KR6c0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0129), Prajñā 般若 and Lìyán 利言's long-recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the Sòng-era expansions by Fǎyuè 法月 (T254 / [KR6c0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0131)), Fǎchéng 法成 (T255 / [KR6c0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0132), translated from Tibetan), and Dānapāla 施護 (T257 / [KR6c0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0136)). Sanskrit-transliterated witnesses survive as [KR6c0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0133) (Bùkōng) and [KR6c0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0134) [KR6c0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0135).
- Major Tang commentaries: Kuījī 窺基's *Yōuzàn* [KR6c0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0137), Wǒnch'ǔk 圓測's *Zàn* [KR6c0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0138), Fǎzàng 法藏's *Lüèshū* [KR6c0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0139), Jìngmài 靖邁's *Shū* [KR6c0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0142), the *Huányuán shù* [KR6c0197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0197) and the *Xiézhù* [KR6c0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0198). Sòng *zhāng-shū* tradition: Shīhù 師護 [KR6c0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0140), Zhīyuán 智圓 [KR6c0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0148) [KR6c0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0150).
- A very large Míng–Qīng commentary stratum (KR6c0151–KR6c0195) representing every late-imperial school: Línjì-Chán, Tiāntái, Cáodòng (Hánshì 圅昰's philosophically substantial *Bōrě xīnjīng lùn* [KR6c0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0184); Yuánxián 元賢, Hónglì 弘麗, Hóngzàn 弘贊's *Tiānzú* and *Guànyì*), and gentry Confucian-Buddhist syncretists.
- Japanese commentary: Kūkai's *Bānruò xīnjīng mìjiàn* [KR6c0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0199) — foundational Shingon Heart-Sūtra reading — with two later sub-commentaries [KR6c0200](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0200) [KR6c0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0201).

#### The Renwáng-jīng (Humane King Sūtra) cluster

- Two translations: T245 [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) (canonically attributed to Kumārajīva but most likely a late-fifth- or sixth-century Chinese composition; see Orzech 1998) and Amoghavajra's revised T246 *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) (765–766) which became the canonical text used in the Tang and Heian *Rénwáng-huì* 仁王會 state-protective ritual programme.
- Principal commentaries: Tiāntái Zhìyǐ 智顗 (recorded by Guàndǐng 灌頂)'s *Hùguó bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0204](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0204) with the Sòng sub-commentary *Shénbǎo jì* [KR6c0205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0205); Jízàng's *Rénwáng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0206](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0206); Wǒnch'ǔk's *Rénwáng jīng shū* [KR6c0207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0207); and — most consequentially for state Buddhism — Liángbì 良賁's *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng shū* [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) (composed at Amoghavajra's request shortly after T246 and the canonical Tang esoteric reading of the sūtra). Ming-Qing recensions in [KR6c0209](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0209)–[KR6c0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0215) document the continuing imperial use of the work; Kūkai's *Rénwáng jīng kāití* [KR6c0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0218) is the Shingon counterpart.

#### The Adhyardhaśatikā / Lǐqù-jīng cluster

The *Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā* (the *Lǐqù-jīng* 理趣經) is the only *prajñā* sūtra whose canonical East-Asian reception is straightforwardly Tantric. Four Chinese renderings document its progressive Tantricisation: Bodhiruci II's *Shíxiāng bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0117) (Mahāyāna register), Vajrabodhi 金剛智's *Jīngāngdǐng yújiā lǐqù bānruò jīng* [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) (explicit *Vajraśekhara*-affiliation), Amoghavajra 不空's *Dàlè jīngāng bùkōng zhēnshí sānmóyē jīng* [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120) (the canonical Tang and Japanese *Lǐqù-jīng*, the doctrinal substrate of Shingon practice), and the Sòng *Biànzhào bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0119). The Sòng *Zuìshàng gēnběn dàlè* expansion is [KR6c0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0125). A small Shingon commentarial cluster — Kūkai's *Lǐqù jīng kāití* [KR6c0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0121) and *Zhēnshí jīng wénjù* [KR6c0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0122), Kakuban-circle *Zhǒngzǐ shì* [KR6c0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0123), the *Dàlè jīng xiǎnyì chāo* [KR6c0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0124) — preserves its Heian-Kamakura reception.

#### Wisdom-Mother (Fómǔ) and short-prajñā Sòng translations

A late-Northern-Sòng cluster (980–1018), produced under imperial patronage by the Indian translators Tiānxīzāi 天息災, Fǎxián 法賢, and especially Dānapāla 施護, brings into the canon the late-Indic Pāla-era *Prajñāpāramitā* short-recension and tantric-prajñā literature: the *Fómǔ chūshēng sānfǎzàng* [KR6c0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0014) (the Sòng *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension), the *Fómǔ bǎodézàng* [KR6c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0015) (= *Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā*), the late-Indic *śāstra*-pair [KR6c0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0017) [KR6c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0018) (*Triśatikāyāḥ Prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kārikāsaptati* of Asaṅga / Vasubandhu), the *Jiǔsòng jīngyì lùn* [KR6c0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0016), and a sequence of short Tantric-prajñā texts [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0225](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0225) (the *Yībǎibā míng tuóluóní jīng*, *Liǎoyì jīng*, *Wǔshísòng jīng*, *Dìshì bōrě xīn jīng*, *Xiǎozì bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*, *Guānxiǎng fómǔ púsà jīng*, *Kāijué zìxìng jīng*). Together they document the last continuous wave of Indic *prajñā* literature in Chinese.

- *Dà bōrě jīng guānfǎ* [KR6c0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0227), *Dà bōrě jīng gāngyào* [KR6c0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0228), *Dà bōrě guān* [KR6c0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0229) — Sòng and Qīng synthetic / structural guides to T220 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001), representing the long East-Asian project of making the 600-fascicle *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* navigable.

### Topics

- **Śūnyatā 空 and prajñāpāramitā 般若波羅蜜多.** The division is the canonical home of the Mahāyāna doctrine of universal emptiness — every *dharma* is empty of an intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) — and of the *bodhisattva*-soteriology by which the realisation of emptiness through *prajñā* effects the perfection of all six *pāramitā*s. Every text in the division addresses this doctrine in some register, from the encyclopaedic exposition of the *Dàzhìdù lùn* [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) through the four-corner negation of the *Vajracchedikā* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) to the 260-character compression of the *Heart Sūtra* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128).
- **Form and emptiness (sè-kōng 色空).** The *Heart Sūtra* formula *sè jí shì kōng, kōng jí shì sè* — "form is itself emptiness, emptiness is itself form" — is the most-cited single sentence in East-Asian Buddhism and the focus of an enormous commentarial debate, with virtually every Heart-Sūtra commentary in KR6c0137–KR6c0201 staking a doctrinal position on the relation between the two terms (Yogācāra *vijñaptimātra*, Sānlùn two-truths, Huáyán *lǐ-shì*, Tiāntái *yī-niàn sān-qiān*, Chán *jiàn-xìng*, Cáodòng *substance-function*).
- **The relation of sūtra to śāstra.** The presence in the division of the Indic *śāstra*-stratum — Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn*-cluster — sets up a perennial East-Asian exegetical question about the proper relation between *prajñā*-sūtra and Mādhyamika or Yogācāra *śāstra*-commentary. Sānlùn 三論, Fǎxiàng 法相, and Huáyán 華嚴 commentaries each take a distinctive position; the disagreement runs through the Tang and recurs in Sòng-Míng.
- **Vinayana of the bodhisattva-path.** The *Dàzhìdù lùn* in particular provides the most extensive surviving Indic-source account of the *bodhisattva* career — six *pāramitā*s, ten *bhūmis*, the *anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi* — and is the textual base for medieval Chinese *bodhisattva*-doctrine.
- **State Buddhism.** The *Rénwáng-jīng* [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) is one of the three royal state-protective scriptures (with the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* and the *Mahāmāyūrī*) and the canonical text of an enormous Tang-Heian-Kamakura state-Buddhist political theology, with Liángbì's [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) as its principal scholastic commentary.
- **Tantricisation of the prajñā tradition.** The progressive Tantric reinterpretation of the *Adhyardhaśatikā* through Vajrabodhi [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) and Amoghavajra [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120), the embedding of *dhāraṇī* within the Heart Sūtra in Prajñā's recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the late-Indic Sòng cluster [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0224) together document the gradual incorporation of *prajñā* into the Indic and East-Asian Tantric programme. The Heian Shingon reception (Kūkai's commentaries) gives this tradition its definitive East-Asian articulation.
- **The Mahāprajñāpāramitā as canonical reference work.** The 600-fascicle *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) sits at the centre of the division as a single integrated witness to the Indic *prajñā*-corpus, but its sheer scale generates a continuing problem of accessibility: how does one read 600 fascicles? The Sòng-Qīng synthetic guides [KR6c0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0227) [KR6c0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0228) [KR6c0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0229) are the formal record of the East-Asian project of making the great sūtra usable.

## Division note: [KR6d 法華部 *Fǎhuá bù* — Buddhist Canon — Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Lotus) Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6d` corresponds to the *Fǎhuá bù* 法華部 of the Taishō structural ordering — the Lotus Sūtra and its satellite scriptures in Taishō volume 9, the Lotus sub-commentary tradition in Taishō volumes 26 and 33–34, the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal-and-meditation corpus in Taishō volume 46, the Lotus Dūnhuáng 敦煌 fragments in volume 85, and the very large Sòng–Qīng manuscript continuation of all these strands preserved in the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. In Wilkinson's outline of the Taishō (§29.5.8), volume 9 is identified as "*Fǎhuá bù* (Lotus and other Mahāyāna sūtras)"; Kanripo's `KR6d` extends that vol. 9 nucleus outward to absorb all Chinese-language Lotus commentary and the entire Tiāntái scholastic apparatus that grows out of it, because in East-Asian classification the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal tradition — including its meditation manuals, doctrinal-classification literature, and ritual / *chànyí* 懺儀 works — is canonically attached to the Lotus Sūtra rather than treated as an independent *zōng* 宗 section.

The principal scholarly tradition organising the division is therefore Tiāntái, whose founder Zhìyǐ 智顗 (538–597) was traditionally regarded as the patriarch and whose 593–597 lectures at Yùquánsì 玉泉寺, redacted by Guàndǐng 灌頂 (561–632), produced the *Tiāntái sāndàbù* 天台三大部 ("Three Great Treatises of Tiāntái") — *Fǎhuá xuányì* [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006), *Fǎhuá wénjù* [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014), and *Móhē zhǐguān* [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) — around which most of the division is structured (Wilkinson §29.5.7.1 on Tiāntái; Hurvitz 1963 on Zhìyǐ; Lopez 2016 and Teiser & Stone 2009 on the Lotus Sūtra). Pre-Tiāntái Liáng exegesis (Fǎyún 法雲), the early Suí Sānlùn 三論 reading by Jízàng 吉藏, and the Táng Faxiang 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 reading by Kuījī 窺基 are also represented; from the 8th century onward the division is dominated by Zhànrán 湛然 (711–782) and his Sòng-period successors of the Tiāntái revival, and from the 11th century by the long *shānjiā* / *shānwài* 山家／山外 controversy and its literature. The division extends through Yuán, Míng (with the Tiāntái revival under Zhìxù 智旭 1599–1655), and Qīng (under Língyào 靈耀 and Tōnglǐ 通理) to roughly the mid-18th century.

### Important texts and text clusters

The 249 per-text notes in `kb/KR6d/` organise into five recognisable clusters.

#### The Lotus Sūtra itself and its parallel translations

- *Zhèng fǎhuá jīng* 正法華經 [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002) — Dharmarakṣa's 竺法護 translation of 286 CE, the earliest complete Chinese Lotus, surviving in 10 *juan*.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001) — Kumārajīva's 鳩摩羅什 translation of 406 CE, the dominant East-Asian recension in 7 *juan* and 28 chapters; the literary base for virtually all subsequent Lotus exegesis in Chinese.
- *Tiānpǐn miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 添品妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003) — the Suí (601) collation by Jñānagupta 闍那崛多 and Dharmagupta 笈多, incorporating the *Devadatta* chapter and the *Pǔmén pǐn* 普門品 verses.
- *Sàtán fēntuólì jīng* 薩曇分陀利經 [KR6d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0004) — a Western Jìn anonymous partial translation of the *Devadatta* episode, preserving a textual stratum independent of the three full versions.

#### Satellite Lotus-cycle sūtras (vol. 9)

- *Wúliàng yì jīng* 無量義經 [KR6d0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0118) — the Liáng-period "Sūtra of Innumerable Meanings," traditionally the prologue of the East-Asian "Threefold Lotus" 法華三部經.
- *Fóshuō Guān Pǔxián púsà xíngfǎ jīng* 佛說觀普賢菩薩行法經 [KR6d0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0120) — the Liú-Sòng-period "Sūtra of the Contemplation of Samantabhadra's Practice," the epilogue of the same triad.
- *Fóshuō fǎhuá sānmèi jīng* 佛說法華三昧經 [KR6d0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0108), *Bùtuìzhuǎn fǎlún jīng* 不退轉法輪經 [KR6d0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0106), *Dà fǎgǔ jīng* 大法鼓經 [KR6d0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0109), *Dà sàzhē Nígānzǐ suǒshuō jīng* 大薩遮尼乾子所說經 [KR6d0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0111) — Mahāyāna sūtras grouped with the Lotus on doctrinal and thematic grounds (one-vehicle teaching, irreversibility, the Tathāgata's hidden lifespan).

#### The *Tiāntái sāndàbù* 天台三大部 and their commentaries

- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuányì* 妙法蓮華經玄義 [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006) — Zhìyǐ's 593 Yùquánsì lectures on the doctrinal meaning of the Lotus, recorded by Guàndǐng; the foundational systematic theology of Tiāntái, source for the *wǔshí bājiào* 五時八教 classification.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng wénjù* 妙法蓮華經文句 [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014) — Zhìyǐ's 587 phrase-by-phrase commentary on Kumārajīva's Lotus, recorded by Guàndǐng; pairs with the *Xuányì* as the doctrinal-plus-textual exegetical core.
- *Móhē zhǐguān* 摩訶止觀 [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) — Zhìyǐ's 594 lectures on Tiāntái meditation, recorded by Guàndǐng; the most systematic *śamatha-vipaśyanā* manual in Chinese, organised on the *shíjìng × shíchéng* 十境十乘 matrix.
- *Fǎhuá xuányì shìqiān* 法華玄義釋籤 [KR6d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0007), *Fǎhuá wénjù jì* 法華文句記 [KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015), and *Zhǐguān fǔxíng zhuànhóngjué* 止觀輔行傳弘決 [KR6d0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0131) — Zhànrán's 湛然 (711–782) standard sub-commentaries on each member of the *sāndàbù*; the principal textual base of the Sòng Tiāntái revival.

#### Alternative Lotus-commentary traditions

- *Fǎhuá jīng yìjì* 法華經義記 [KR6d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0005) — Fǎyún's 法雲 Liáng-period exegesis, the principal southern pre-Tiāntái reading and the polemical target of Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì*.
- *Fǎhuá xuánlùn* 法華玄論 [KR6d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0023), *Fǎhuá yìshū* 法華義疏 [KR6d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0024), *Fǎhuá yóuyì* 法華遊意 [KR6d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0025) — Jízàng's 吉藏 (549–623) Sānlùn 三論-school readings, doctrinally distinct from Tiāntái.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuánzàn* 妙法蓮華經玄贊 [KR6d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0026) — Kuījī's 窺基 (632–682) Cí'ēn 慈恩 / Yogācāra reading of the Lotus, the principal Faxiang interpretation.
- *Fǎhuá zōngyào* 法華宗要 [KR6d0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0032) — the Sillan master Wǒnhyo's 元曉 short doctrinal synthesis, an important East-Asian non-Chinese voice.

#### Tiāntái doctrinal, meditation, and ritual literature (vol. 46)

- *Sìjiào yì* 四教義 [KR6d0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0166) and *Tiāntái sìjiào yí* 天台四教儀 [KR6d0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0168) — Zhìyǐ's and the late-Táng / Korean Chégwan 諦觀's expositions of the four doctrinal teachings, the most-studied Tiāntái catechetical works.
- *Shí bùèr mén* 十不二門 [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and the very large body of commentary it provoked (e.g. *Shí bùèr mén zhǐyào chāo* [KR6d0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0158) by Zhīlǐ 知禮) — Zhànrán's 10-fold non-duality scheme, the textual flashpoint of the *shānjiā / shānwài* controversy.
- *Jīngāngbēi* 金剛錍 [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175) — Zhànrán's polemical defense of *wúqíng yǒu xìng* 無情有性 (Buddha-nature in insentient things), generative of a sub-commentary tradition into the Sòng.
- *Fǎhuá sānmèi chànyí* 法華三昧懺儀 [KR6d0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0191) and the related *chànyí* / *xíngfǎ* corpus — Zhìyǐ's Lotus-Samādhi liturgy and its Sòng elaborations (Zūnshì 遵式, Zhīlǐ 知禮), the principal Tiāntái ritual texts.
- *Sìmíng zūnzhě jiàoxíng lù* 四明尊者教行錄 [KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186) — Zōngxiǎo's 宗曉 collected works of Zhīlǐ, the textual monument of the Sòng *shānjiā* school.
- *Jiàoguān gāngzōng* 教觀綱宗 [KR6d0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0188) — Zhìxù's 智旭 (1599–1655) Míng-period summary of Tiāntái doctrine, the principal late-imperial textbook.

### Important persons

- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) — translator of the standard Lotus recension (T262 = [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001)); the literary register of his translation supplied the canonical Sinitic vocabulary of all subsequent Lotus exegesis in this division.
- [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) — translator of the earliest complete Chinese Lotus (T263 = [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002), 286) and of several satellite vol. 9 sūtras; his Lotus survives as the principal philological witness independent of Kumārajīva.
- [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) — co-translator with Dharmagupta 笈多 of the Suí Lotus recension (T264 = [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003), 601), source of the textual additions to the received Kumārajīva Lotus.
- [法雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%9B%B2) — Liáng-period exegete of the Lotus ([KR6d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0005)); the standard pre-Tiāntái southern reading, against which Zhìyǐ defined his own system.
- [慧思](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%80%9D) — Tiāntái second patriarch and Zhìyǐ's teacher; author of the *Fǎhuá jīng ānlèxíng yì* [KR6d0156](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0156) and other proto-Tiāntái Lotus-meditation works.
- [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) — third Tiāntái patriarch and de facto founder of Chinese Tiāntái doctrine; lecturer of the *sāndàbù* and dozens of other works in this division (the most-cited person in `KR6d`, named in ≈ 25 per-text notes).
- [灌頂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%81%8C%E9%A0%82) — Zhìyǐ's principal disciple and the redactor / co-author of nearly the entire Zhìyǐ corpus; also author of the *Guóqīng bǎilù* [KR6d0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0183), the documentary record of the early Tiāntái community.
- [吉藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%97%8F) — Sānlùn master whose Lotus commentaries ([KR6d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0023)–[KR6d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0025), [KR6d0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0128)) represent the principal alternative early-Suí exegetical line.
- [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) — Cí'ēn / Faxiang master who gave the Lotus a Yogācāra reading ([KR6d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0026)); the source of the *xuánzàn* sub-commentary tradition.
- [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) — sixth Tiāntái patriarch and reviver of the school in the mid-Táng; author of the canonical sub-commentaries on the *sāndàbù* ([KR6d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0007), [KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015), [KR6d0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0131)) and of the doctrinally generative *Shí bùèr mén* [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and *Jīngāngbēi* [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175).
- [空海](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A9%BA%E6%B5%B7) — founder of Japanese Shingon and author of seven Lotus-related Heian works in this division (e.g. [KR6d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0036)–[KR6d0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0042)), giving the Lotus its esoteric / *mìjiào* 密教 reading.
- [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) — leader of the Sòng *shānjiā* 山家 branch of Tiāntái and the dominant figure of the 11th-century revival; the second-most-cited person in `KR6d` (≈ 11 notes), with the *Shí bùèr mén zhǐyào chāo* [KR6d0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0158) and his liturgical *xíngfǎ* corpus.
- [遵式](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%B5%E5%BC%8F) — Zhīlǐ's contemporary and the principal Sòng ritual compiler; author of Tiāntái *chànyí* and devotional works (e.g. [KR6d0195](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0195), [KR6d0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0199)).
- [仁岳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BB%81%E5%B2%B3) — Zhīlǐ's disciple who later turned to the *shānwài* 山外 position; author of the *Sìmíng Rényuè yìshuō cóngshū* [KR6d0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0224), the principal *shānwài* counter-statement.
- [從義](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%9E%E7%BE%A9) — late-Sòng commentator on the *Móhē zhǐguān* and *Shí bùèr mén* whose works ([KR6d0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0139)–[KR6d0141](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0141)) preserve the post-Zhīlǐ scholastic apparatus.
- [宗曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E6%9B%89) — Sòng compiler of the *Sìmíng zūnzhě jiàoxíng lù* [KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186), the corpus of Zhīlǐ's writings; principal documentary editor of *shānjiā* Tiāntái.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) — Míng-period reviver of Tiāntái and author of the *Jiàoguān gāngzōng* [KR6d0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0188); the principal late-imperial systematiser whose works re-frame Tiāntái for the Míng-Qīng setting.
- [靈耀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9D%88%E8%80%80) — Qīng-period Tiāntái commentator on the *Móhē zhǐguān* and the *sāndàbù* ([KR6d0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0142) and related); his work is the principal Qīng Tiāntái scholastic continuation.

### Topics

- **The ekayāna 一乘 doctrine and *kāiquán xiǎnshí* 開權顯實.** The proclamation in chapters 2–9 of the Lotus that the *śrāvaka* / *pratyekabuddha* / *bodhisattva* three vehicles are provisional (*quán* 權) and the Buddha-vehicle alone is real (*shí* 實) is the central scriptural commitment around which the entire Tiāntái doctrinal apparatus is built, and almost every Sinitic Lotus exegete from Fǎyún onward addresses its hermeneutic status.
- **The *jìmén* / *běnmén* 跡門／本門 division.** The split of the Lotus into a "trace-gate" (chapters 1–14) and an "origin-gate" (15–28) is associated with Dàoxuān's preface to Kumārajīva ([KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001)) and given systematic articulation in Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì* [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006); it remains the standard Sinitic exegetical schema through the entire division.
- **The *wǔshí bājiào* 五時八教 classification.** Zhìyǐ's chronological-and-modal organisation of the Buddha's *kerygma* into five periods (*Huāyán*, *Lùyuàn / Āhán*, *Fāngděng*, *Bōrě*, *Fǎhuá-Nièpán*) and eight modes is developed in the *Xuányì*, summarised in [KR6d0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0166) and [KR6d0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0167), and given canonical compact form in Chégwan's *Tiāntái sìjiào yí* [KR6d0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0168); it is the basic doctrinal-classification apparatus of the division.
- **Tiāntái meditation: *yīxīn sānguān* 一心三觀, *yīniàn sānqiān* 一念三千, *zhǐguān bùèr* 止觀不二.** Articulated principally in the *Móhē zhǐguān* [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) and its commentaries; the most systematic Mahāyāna meditation theory in Chinese, organised on the *shíjìng × shíchéng* 十境十乘 matrix.
- **The *shānjiā / shānwài* 山家／山外 controversy.** The 11th-century Sòng-period split between Zhīlǐ's [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) "mountain-house" *shānjiā* — defending the Tiāntái doctrine of evil in the Buddha-nature (*xìng-è* 性惡) and Guàndǐng's role in the early canon — and the *shānwài* counter-position of Yuánqīng 源清, Zhìyuán 智圓, and (later) Rényuè 仁岳, particularly over the interpretation of Zhànrán's *Shí bùèr mén* [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and the status of Guàndǐng's *Guānyīn xuányì* commentary [KR6d0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0046). The dispute generated the large mid-Sòng polemical literature visible in [KR6d0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0184)–[KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186) and [KR6d0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0220)–[KR6d0235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0235).
- **Buddha-nature in the insentient (*wúqíng yǒu xìng* 無情有性).** Zhànrán's claim in the *Jīngāngbēi* [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175) that even insentient things possess Buddha-nature; the Tiāntái counter-position to the Chán and Huāyán readings on the same question, generating the *Jīngāngbēi*-commentary sub-tradition ([KR6d0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0176)–[KR6d0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0181)).
- **The Lotus liturgy: *Fǎhuá sānmèi* 法華三昧 and the *chànyí* tradition.** Zhìyǐ's Lotus-Samādhi practice from the *Móhē zhǐguān* and the *Fǎhuá sānmèi chànyí* [KR6d0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0191) is the textual base for a Sòng-period ritual literature, principally elaborated by Zūnshì and Zhīlǐ, that fed back into ordinary monastic and lay practice and shaped the late-imperial Tiāntái devotional landscape.
- **The Guānyīn 觀音 sub-cult.** The detachment of the *Pǔmén pǐn* 普門品 (Lotus chapter 25) as an independent devotional unit, with its own commentarial corpus ([KR6d0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0046)–[KR6d0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0057)) — Zhìyǐ's *Guānyīn xuányì* and *yìshū* and their Sòng / Míng / Qīng commentaries — is one of the principal vehicles by which the Lotus's textual presence extended into popular ritual practice.
- **Japanese Lotus reception: Tendai 天台 and Shingon 真言 readings.** The Heian-period esoteric / *mìjiào* interpretations of the Lotus by Kūkai 空海 ([KR6d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0036)–[KR6d0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0044)) and the early Japanese Tendai materials (e.g. [KR6d0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0220)) constitute a distinct Lotus reading transmitted within the same division.
- **The Míng–Qīng Tiāntái revival.** Zhìxù's [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) 17th-century systematisation, the Qīng-period Tiāntái commentaries by Língyào, Tōnglǐ, and others ([KR6d0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0084)–[KR6d0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0098), [KR6d0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0142)), and the late-imperial *Sìjiào yí* sub-commentaries ([KR6d0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0169)–[KR6d0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0174)) constitute the final phase of pre-modern Lotus scholarship represented in the division.
