# 律部 (T22)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 15 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6k 律部 *Lǜ bù* — Buddhist canon — Vinaya (monastic discipline)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/): 15 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6k 律部 *Lǜ bù* — Buddhist canon — Vinaya (monastic discipline)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6k` 律部 (*Lǜ bù*, "Vinaya section") is the Kanripo mirror of the Vinaya division of the Chinese Buddhist canon — the canonical *Vinaya-piṭaka* together with its Indic and East-Asian exegetical and ritual-procedural literature. In CANWWW  the material is distributed across three divisions: `div13` 律部 holds the Vinayas proper and their *prātimokṣa-*, *karman-* and *paripṛcchā-*satellites (T22 No. 1421 — T24 No. 1504); `div14` 律疏部 holds the principal Suí–Tang exegetical layer (T40 Nos. 1804–1815, plus T45 Nos. 1892–1910); `div27` 續律疏部 holds the later Sòng–Míng–Qīng Chinese sub-commentaries together with the Japanese scholastic apparatus. Kanripo `KR6k` integrates these three CANWWW divisions and supplements them with a large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial tail, so that 263 works are catalogued here in total — roughly the same order of magnitude as the *Prajñāpāramitā* division [KR6c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/) but with a quite different shape: where the *Bōrě bù* is anchored by a small handful of recurrently retranslated Indic sūtras, the Vinaya division is anchored by five Indic disciplinary corpora belonging to five different *nikāya* schools, all surviving only in their Chinese form, together with a much larger East-Asian scholastic and ritual-procedural superstructure.

The corpus falls into six historically and doctrinally distinct strata. (1) The **early-fifth-century translation wave** (404–431) at Chángān and Jiànyè brought into Chinese the full disciplinary literature of four Indic *nikāya* schools — the *Shísòng lǜ* 十誦律 of the Sarvāstivāda, the *Sìfēn lǜ* 四分律 of the Dharmaguptaka, the *Móhēsēngqí lǜ* 摩訶僧祇律 of the Mahāsāṃghika, and the *Wǔfēn lǜ* 五分律 of the Mahīśāsaka — together with supplementary texts of the Kāśyapīya and Sammitīya. The Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas survive in no other language, so this stratum is the principal evidentiary base for *all* modern comparative-Vinaya scholarship (Clarke 2015; *cf.* Wilkinson §29.5.7.6). (2) The **Tang *Sìfēnlǜ* scholastic synthesis** at Chángān (620–697) saw the *Sìfēn lǜ* gradually displace the *Shísòng lǜ* as the practical Vinaya of Chinese monasticism, under three competing exegetical schools — Fǎlì's 法礪 ([法礪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%A4%AA)) Xiāngbù 相部, Dàoxuān's 道宣 ([道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3)) Nánshān 南山, and Huáisù's 懷素 ([懷素](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E7%B4%A0)) Dōngtǎ 東塔 — of which the Nánshān school's victory under the imperial decree of Dàizōng (777) made Dàoxuān's *San dàbù* 三大部 the canonical Chinese Vinaya curriculum thereafter. (3) The **Yìjìng Mūlasarvāstivāda programme** (700–714) translated the disciplinary corpus of the late-Indic Mūlasarvāstivāda — by then the dominant Vinaya school of Indian Buddhism and (still later) the canonical Vinaya of the Tibetan, Mongolian, and Bhutanese traditions — into Chinese as a single eighteen-text *vastu*-by-*vastu* programme, but this Vinaya never displaced the *Sìfēn* in Chinese practice. (4) The **Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* stream** is anchored by the apocryphal *Fànwǎng jīng* 梵網經 ([KR6k0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0076), attributed to Kumārajīva but Chinese in origin) and runs in parallel to the school-Vinaya tradition, generating its own large commentarial corpus (Zhìyǐ 智顗, Fǎzàng 法藏, Wǒnhyo 元曉, Tàixián 太賢, Yúnqī Zhūhóng 雲棲袾宏, Ǒuyì Zhìxù 蕅益智旭); the alternative *Yogācāra*-school *bodhisattva-precepts* (Maitreya / Asaṅga, translated by Dharmakṣema and re-translated by Xuánzàng) provided the Mahāyāna stream with a second textual base. (5) The **Sòng *Língzhī*-school revival** (Yǔnkān 允堪 1005–1061; Yuánzhào 元照 1048–1116; Shǒuyī 守一 / Miàolián 妙蓮 in the Southern Sòng) produced an extensive sub-commentarial apparatus on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù*, recovered the doctrine of the precept-body (戒體 *jiètǐ*), and re-anchored Vinaya practice in the Tiāntái doctrinal system. (6) The **late-Míng / Qīng Vinaya revival** (Yúnqī Zhūhóng, Zhìxù, Dúté 讀體 1601–1679 at Bǎohuáshān 寶華山, Hóngzàn 弘贊 1611–1685 at Dǐnghú-shān 鼎湖山, the *Sānfēng* line of Fǎzàng 法藏 1573–1635) re-standardised Chinese ordination practice through the new *sāntán* 三壇 (three-platform) ordination system, generated the daily-use Vinaya manual that has remained in use to the present (*Píní rìyòng qièyào* [KR6k0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0224)), and produced the most thorough Qīng-period commentaries on every layer of the disciplinary tradition.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The four (then five) school-Vinayas

- *Sìfēn lǜ* 四分律 [KR6k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0009) — the **Dharmaguptaka** Vinaya translated 410–412 by [佛陀耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) (Buddhayaśas) and [竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5) (Zhú Fóniàn). After the Tang imperial decree of 777 the canonical Chinese Vinaya and the operational basis of Chinese, Korean, Japanese, and Vietnamese monasticism to the present. Its *bhikṣu-prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0010) / [KR6k0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0011); the *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0012); the early *karmavācanā* compendia [KR6k0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0013) [KR6k0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0014) [KR6k0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0015).
- *Shísòng lǜ* 十誦律 [KR6k0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0016) — the **Sarvāstivāda** Vinaya translated 404–409 by [弗若多羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%97%E8%8B%A5%E5%A4%9A%E7%BE%85) (Puṇyatāra) and [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Kumārajīva). The first complete Indian Vinaya translated into Chinese and the dominant Vinaya of southern-Chinese monasticism through the Liú-Sòng and Qí–Liáng. Its *prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0017) / [KR6k0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0018); the *karmavācanā* manuals [KR6k0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0019) [KR6k0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0020); the principal Indic commentary [KR6k0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0021) *Sàpóduō pínì pípóshā* and the *mātṛkā* [KR6k0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0022).
- *Móhēsēngqí lǜ* 摩訶僧祇律 [KR6k0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0006) — the **Mahāsāṃghika** Vinaya translated 416–418 by [法顯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%A1%AF) (Fǎxiǎn) and [佛陀跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Buddhabhadra), based on the manuscript Fǎxiǎn brought back from Pāṭaliputra. Surviving in no other language; the principal evidentiary witness to the disciplinary tradition of the *Mahāsāṃghika* — the lineage whose schism in the second post-Nirvāṇa century is conventionally regarded as the institutional ancestry of Mahāyāna Buddhism. Its *prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0007) / [KR6k0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0008).
- *Wǔfēn lǜ* 五分律 [KR6k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0001) — the **Mahīśāsaka** Vinaya translated 422–423 by [佛陀什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E4%BB%80) (Buddhajīva) and [竺道生](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E9%81%93%E7%94%9F) (Zhú Dàoshēng). Surviving in no other language; the only complete Mahīśāsaka disciplinary text in any tradition. Its *prātimokṣa* (in two recensions [KR6k0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0002) [KR6k0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0003)), *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* [KR6k0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0004), and *karmavācanā* [KR6k0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0005).
- *Gēnběn shuōyīqièyǒubù pínàiyé* 根本說一切有部毘奈耶 [KR6k0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0023) — the **Mūlasarvāstivāda** Vinaya, translated 700–714 by [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) (Yìjìng) after his Indian sojourn 671–695. Translated as a single eighteen-text *vastu*-by-*vastu* programme: the *Pravrajyā-vastu* [KR6k0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0025), *Varṣā-vastu* [KR6k0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0026), *Pravāraṇā-vastu* [KR6k0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0027), *Carma-vastu* [KR6k0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0028), *Bhaiṣajya-vastu* [KR6k0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0029), *Kaṭhina-vastu* [KR6k0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0030), *Saṃghabhedavastu* [KR6k0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0031), *Kṣudraka-vastu* [KR6k0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0032), *Nidāna-mātṛkā* [KR6k0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0033), the *prātimokṣas* [KR6k0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0035) / [KR6k0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0036), the *karmavācanā* [KR6k0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0034), the *uddāna* summaries [KR6k0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0037) [KR6k0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0038), the *Vinaya-saṃgraha* digest [KR6k0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0039), and Viśākhā's versified Vinaya [KR6k0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0040). Although this is the Vinaya of the Indo-Tibetan tradition to the present, it never displaced the *Sìfēn* in Chinese practice.
- The minor-school witnesses: *Jiětuō jièjīng* 解脫戒經 [KR6k0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0041) (Kāśyopadyā translated by [般若流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) in 543); *Lǜ èrshíèr míngliǎo lùn* 律二十二明了論 [KR6k0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0042) (the only extant Sammitīya Vinaya in any language, translated by [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) Paramārtha in 568); *Shànjiàn lǜ pípóshā* 善見律毘婆沙 [KR6k0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0043) (the *Samantapāsādikā*, Buddhaghosa's Pāli Vinaya commentary, translated by [僧伽跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) in 489 — the only Theravāda Vinaya document in Chinese); *Pínìmǔ jīng* 毘尼母經 [KR6k0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0044) (an unattributed *mātṛkā*-style Vinaya commentary, 4th–5th c.); and *Bínàiyē* 鼻奈耶 [KR6k0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0045) ([竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5), 383 — the **earliest extant Chinese Vinaya translation**, predating the four-school programme by twenty-one years).

#### Dàoxuān's *Three Great Works* of the Nánshān school

The institutional triad of the Tang *Sìfēnlǜ* curriculum, codified at Zhōngnánshān 終南山 by Dàoxuān between 626 and 667:

- *Sìfēn lǜ shānfán bǔquē xíngshì chāo* 四分律刪繁補闕行事鈔 [KR6k0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0128) (T1804) — the procedural manual of monastic practice; the most-studied Vinaya book in pre-modern East Asia.
- *Sìfēn lǜ shānbǔ suíjī jiémó* 四分律刪補隨機羯磨 [KR6k0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0046) (T1808) — the codified *karmavācanā* compendium for all monastic legal acts.
- *Sìfēn lǜ bǐqiū hánzhù jièběn* 四分律比丘含注戒本 [KR6k0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0131) (T1806) — Dàoxuān's annotated *prātimokṣa* recension; with the parallel *Sìfēn bǐqiūnī chāo* 四分比丘尼鈔 [KR6k0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0155) for the women's saṅgha.

Around the *San dàbù* runs the principal Tang *Nánshān* sub-commentarial cluster — Dàoxuān's own *Yìchāo* 義鈔 [KR6k0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0176), the Five-Dynasties *Jiǎnzhèng jì* [KR6k0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0167) of Jǐng Xiāo 景霄, and the eighth-century *Sōuxuán lù* [KR6k0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0162) of Zhì Hóng 志鴻; the Tang Xiāngbù tradition is represented by Fǎlì's *Shū* [KR6k0161](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0161) with Dìngbīn's *Shìzōng yìjì* [KR6k0163](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0163) and Dìngbīn's *Bǐqiū jièběn shū* [KR6k0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0132); the Tang Dōngtǎ tradition by Huáisù's *Kāizōng jì* [KR6k0165](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0165) and his alternative *karmavācanā* recensions [KR6k0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0047) [KR6k0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0048).

The principal Sòng *jì* — running line-by-line sub-commentaries on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù* by Yǔnkān 允堪 and Yuánzhào 元照, the two pillars of the *Língzhī* 靈芝 revival — fill out the Vinaya scholastic apparatus: Yuánzhào's *Zīchí jì* [KR6k0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0129) on the *Xíngshì chāo*; his *Xíngzōng jì* [KR6k0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0146) on the *Hánzhù jièběn shū*; his *Jìyuán jì* [KR6k0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0158) on the *Suíjī jiémó shū*; Yǔnkān's *Fāhuī jì* [KR6k0144](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0144) on the same; the *Fǔyào jì* [KR6k0177](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0177) on the *Yìchāo*; the Japanese *Zīxíng chāo* [KR6k0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0130) by Shōen 照遠 (14th c., Tō-ji Vinaya scholar). Yuánzhào's wider Vinaya prose — the *Zhīyuán jí* [KR6k0217](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0217), *Bǔxù Zhīyuán jí* [KR6k0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0218), *Zhīyuán yíbiān* [KR6k0216](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0216) — preserves the doctrinal foundations of the *Língzhī* revival.

#### Dàoxuān's wider Vinaya treatises

A distinct cluster of nine Dàoxuān works on institutional and ritual aspects of monastic discipline that fall outside the *San dàbù* proper:

- *Jiètán tújīng* 戒壇圖經 [KR6k0178](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0178) — the canonical Tang manual on the architectural form of the ordination platform; the foundational document for every East-Asian Vinaya-school ordination hall.
- *Jìngxīn jièguān fǎ* 淨心戒觀法 [KR6k0179](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0179) — Vinaya observance integrated with meditative practice.
- *Zhāngfú yí* 釋門章服儀 [KR6k0180](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0180) — the canonical regulation of monastic vestments.
- *Liàngchù qīngzhòng yí* 量處輕重儀 [KR6k0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0181) — the disposition of a deceased monk's property.
- *Guījìng yí* 釋門歸敬儀 [KR6k0182](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0182) — refuge-taking.
- *Xínghù lǜyí* 教誡新學比丘行護律儀 [KR6k0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0183) — novice instruction.
- *Lǜxiàng gǎntōng zhuàn* 律相感通傳 [KR6k0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0184) — the hagiographic Wèituó 韋陀 tradition.
- *Qíhuánsì tújīng* 中天竺舍衛國祇洹寺圖經 [KR6k0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0185) — the cosmographic blueprint of the standard Buddhist monastery.

The cluster's Sòng running commentaries — Yuánzhào and Liángxìn's *Yìngfǎ jì* [KR6k0214](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0214) on the *Zhāngfú yí*; Yuánzhào's *Liùwù tú* [KR6k0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0186) (the *Pratītyasamutpāda* of robes and bowl); Miàoshēng's *Sānyī xiǎnzhèng tú* [KR6k0254](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0254) and *Liùwù tú biàné* [KR6k0187](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0187) — together with the Tiāntái-line subcommentary *Tōngzhēn jì* [KR6k0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0253) and *Hùfǎ jì* [KR6k0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0252) on the *Guījìng yí* — preserve the most extensive Sòng-period institutional-Vinaya scholarship.

#### The *Fànwǎng jīng* + Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* cluster

The Mahāyāna disciplinary stream is anchored by the *Brahma-net Sūtra*, the foundational scripture of East-Asian *bodhisattva-precepts*, generating one of the densest commentarial clusters in the entire Buddhist canon:

- *Fànwǎng jīng* 梵網經 [KR6k0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0076) (T1484) — canonically ascribed to Kumārajīva but widely recognised as a Chinese apocryphon composed c. 440–480; the canonical scripture of the Mahāyāna ten-major-precepts and forty-eight-minor-precepts system. With Kūkai's [空海](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A9%BA%E6%B5%B7) Shingon *Fànwǎngjīng kāití* [KR6k0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0077).
- The **Tang scholastic commentarial cluster** spans every major doctrinal school. Tiāntái: Zhìyǐ–Guàndǐng *Púsàjiè yìshū* [KR6k0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0078) and its Tang revision by Míngkuàng [KR6k0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0079) and Guàndǐng's independent *Yìshū* [KR6k0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0084). Huáyán: Fǎzàng *Púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0080). The Silla/Korean cluster: Wǒnhyo *Sījì* [KR6k0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0090) (the Korean scholastic foundation), Ŭijŏk *Púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0082) (Silla Yogācāra), Tàixián *Gǔjì jì* [KR6k0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0083), Sŭngjang *Shùjì* [KR6k0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0091), and the Cí'ēn Yogācāra readings of Zhī Zhōu [KR6k0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0092) and Fǎ Xiǎn [KR6k0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0093). The Japanese sub-commentary stratum is anchored by Gyōnen's 凝然 *Rìzhū chāo* 梵網戒本疏日珠鈔 [KR6k0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0081) (1276–1321) — the largest single commentary on the *Fànwǎng jīng* in any language.
- The **late-Míng commentarial flowering** under Yúnqī Zhūhóng and his successors: Zhūhóng's three-part synthesis [KR6k0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0086) *Yìshū fāyǐn* with its *Shìyì* [KR6k0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0087) and *Wènbiàn* [KR6k0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0088); Zhìxù's *Xuányì* [KR6k0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0096) and *Hézhù* [KR6k0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0097), the principal Tiāntái-school late-imperial commentary; Hóngzàn's *Lüèshū* [KR6k0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0098) and *Bànyuè sòng púsà jiè yíshì zhù* [KR6k0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0099); Jìguāng's *Zhíjiě* [KR6k0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0100) with its *Shìyì* [KR6k0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0101), the principal Bǎohuáshān commentary; Déyù's red-ink *Shùnzhū* [KR6k0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0102); Shūyù's *Chūjīn* [KR6k0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0103). Dunhuang fragments [KR6k0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0104) preserve the lost middle-Tang commentarial layer.

#### Repentance (懺) liturgies

- *Cíbēi dàochǎng chànfǎ* 慈悲道場懺法 [KR6k0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0198) (T1909) — the *Liánghuáng bǎochàn* 梁皇寶懺, codified at the Liáng court 502–549 under imperial sponsorship; the principal court-Buddhist repentance liturgy of medieval China and the foundational document of all subsequent East-Asian *chànfǎ*. Still performed continuously to the present.
- *Cíbēi shuǐchàn fǎ* 慈悲水懺法 [KR6k0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0199) (T1910) — Zhìxuán's 知玄 *Water Repentance* (850–883). With the late-Míng / Qīng commentaries [KR6k0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0202) (Zhìzhèng, Tiāntái) and [KR6k0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0203) (Xīzōng).
- The *Shuǐlù* 水陸 mass — the most elaborate East-Asian Buddhist ritual programme: the foundational Sòng liturgy *Fǎjiè shèngfán shuǐlù shènghuì xiūzhāi yíguǐ* [KR6k0204](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0204) of Zhìpán 志磐, in the Míng redaction of Zhūhóng; the late-Qīng doctrinal synthesis *Xìngxiàng tōnglùn* [KR6k0205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0205) and the new *Fǎlún bǎochàn* [KR6k0206](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0206) of Zhǐguàn 咫觀 (1850–1880), the first systematic adaptation of the *Shuǐlù* under the late-Qīng *Lóngzàng* canon.
- The *zànyí* tradition: Sòng patriarch-veneration verses for Dàoxuān [KR6k0207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0207) (Zhìyuán) [KR6k0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0208) (Rényuè) [KR6k0209](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0209) (Yǔnkān) and for Yuánzhào [KR6k0210](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0210) (Zé'ān) — the foundational lineage-veneration texts of the *Nánshānlǜ* school.
- The late-imperial repentance cluster: *Fànwǎng jīng chànhuǐ xíngfǎ* [KR6k0245](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0245) (Zhìxù); *Wúzhōng shífó xiànghǎo chànyí* [KR6k0200](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0200) (Chuándēng); *Shèlì chànfǎ* [KR6k0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0201) (Jìsēng, 1718); Hóngzàn's three-part liturgical sequence [KR6k0238](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0238) [KR6k0239](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0239) [KR6k0240](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0240) for relic-veneration, buddha-veneration, and the *gòngtiān* 供天 deva-offering.

#### The Sòng *Língzhī*-school revival

Beyond the *jì* on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù*, the Sòng *Língzhī* school produced a substantial body of independent Vinaya scholarship: Yǔnkān's *Yībō míngyì zhāng* [KR6k0212](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0212) (the canonical Sòng pedagogical handbook on robes and bowl), his *Xīnshòujiè bǐqiū liùniàn wǔguān fǎ* [KR6k0213](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0213) (the *liùniàn / wǔguān* daily reflections), his *Jìngxīn jièguān fǎ fāzhēn chāo* [KR6k0211](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0211) (sub-commentary on Dàoxuān's *Jìngxīn jièguān fǎ*); Yuánzhào's *Dàojù fù* [KR6k0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0215) (the *rhapsody on monastic equipment*); the Southern Sòng compendia of Shǒuyī and Xíngzhī — *Zhōngnán jiāyè* [KR6k0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0219) (the principal Southern-Sòng *Nánshānlǜ* doctrinal compendium) and *Lǜzōng huìyuán* [KR6k0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0220); Miàolián's two polemics *Péngzhé zhíbiàn* [KR6k0221](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0221) and *Péngzhé zhēn* [KR6k0222](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0222) defending the *Nánshān* doctrine; Huáixiǎn's terminological dictionary *Lǜzōng xīnxué míngjù* [KR6k0255](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0255); the early-Kamakura Sino-Japanese exchange *Lǜzōng wèndá* [KR6k0256](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0256) (1209, Shunjō et al.); and Shěngwù's Yuán-period monastic code *Lǜyuàn shìguī* [KR6k0257](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0257) — the only Yuán-dynasty Vinaya monastic code.

#### Late-Míng / Qīng Vinaya revival

The two dominant late-imperial Vinaya centres — Bǎohuáshān 寶華山 and Dǐnghú-shān 鼎湖山 — together with the related Yúnqī, Tiāntái and Sānfēng lineages produced the working Vinaya literature of the late Míng and the entire Qīng:

- The **Bǎohuáshān corpus** of Dúté (1601–1679) and his successor Shūyù 書玉: *Píní zhǐchí huìjí* [KR6k0223](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0223) (the foundational study handbook), *Píní rìyòng qièyào* [KR6k0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0224) (the daily-use Vinaya manual still in continuous monastic use), *Shāmíní lǜyí yàolüè* [KR6k0225](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0225) (the women's novitiate manual), *Chuánjiè zhèngfàn* [KR6k0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0226) (the canonical Chinese ordination handbook that codified the *sāntán* 三壇 system), and *Píní zuòchí xùshì* [KR6k0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0160) for the karman procedures. Shūyù's supplementary apparatus: *Xiāngrǔ jì* [KR6k0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0227) (commentary on the *Píní rìyòng*), *Shùyì* [KR6k0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0228), *Èrbù sēng shòujiè yíshì* [KR6k0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0229), *Jiémó yíshì* [KR6k0230](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0230). The *Sìfēn lǜ míngyì biāoshì* [KR6k0173](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0173) of Hóngzàn is the indispensable late-imperial Vinaya lexicon for this body of work.
- The **Dǐnghú-shān corpus** of Hóngzàn (1611–1685): *Sìfēn jièběn rúshì* [KR6k0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0149) (the principal late-Míng commentary on the *Sìfēn-prātimokṣa*), the lay manuals [KR6k0233](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0233) [KR6k0234](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0234), the *Bǐqiū shòujiè lù* [KR6k0235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0235) / *Bǐqiūnī shòujiè lù* [KR6k0236](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0236) (historical-procedural witnesses to the *bhikṣuṇī*-ordination question), and the comprehensive *Míyú biāoshì* glossary [KR6k0173](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0173). Hóngzàn's *Píní rìyòng* alternative *Shāmén rìyòng* [KR6k0231](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0231) was the principal early-Qīng competitor to Dúté's manual.
- **Cáodòng-Chán Vinaya synthesis**: Yuánxián 元賢 (1578–1657)'s *Sìfēn jièběn yuēyì* [KR6k0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0150), *Lǜxué fārèn* [KR6k0260](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0260) (the late-Míng pedagogical introduction to Vinaya study); Hánshì 函昰 and the Lǐngnán Cáodòng school; Jīnshì 今釋's *Púsà jièshū suíjiàn lù* [KR6k0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0095).
- **Tiāntái-Chán synthesis under Ǒuyì Zhìxù** (1599–1655): *Píní jíyào* [KR6k0151](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0151) (Zhìxù's restructured *Sìfēn* digest); the *Píní zhēnjìng lù* [KR6k0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0143) anthology; the *bodhisattva-precept* trio [KR6k0195](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0195) [KR6k0196](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0196) [KR6k0245](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0245); the lay-precept compendium [KR6k0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0244); the *Sìfēn lǜ chíjiè jiēdù lüèshì* [KR6k0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0174); the *Shāmí shíjiè wēiyí lùyào* [KR6k0242](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0242).
- **The Tang/Sòng Tiāntái-line subcommentaries on Dàoxuān's wider works** — *Tōngzhēn jì* [KR6k0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0253) (Liǎorán); *Hùfǎ jì* [KR6k0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0252) (Yànqǐ).
- **The Sānfēng line of Fǎzàng** 法藏 (1573–1635): the early-imperial Chán-school ordination manual *Hóngjiè fǎyí* [KR6k0246](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0246) and its full *sāntán* successor [KR6k0247](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0247) — texts whose later imperial suppression (the *Sānfēng* faction was banned under the Yōngzhèng emperor in 1733) makes them important historical witnesses.
- **Yuán imperial Mongolian Vinaya manuals**: ʼPhags-pa's 拔合思巴 *Mūlasarvāstivāda* karman manual [KR6k0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0191) and *bhikṣu* training manual [KR6k0192](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0192) — Beijing court productions for the Mongol-Tibetan Buddhist community.

#### Dunhuang Vinaya fragments

T85 preserves a distinctive Tang-period Vinaya manuscript-fragment cluster recovered from the Mogao library cave: working *Sìfēn* commentary fragments [KR6k0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0104) [KR6k0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0133) [KR6k0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0134) [KR6k0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0135) [KR6k0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0106), a working selection [KR6k0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0136), a *wēiyí* decorum manual [KR6k0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0137), a *Pínìxīn* doctrinal distillation [KR6k0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0138), comparative Vinaya selections [KR6k0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0139) [KR6k0141](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0141), a working anthology [KR6k0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0140), and the *shǒujué* oral-pedagogical record [KR6k0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0142). The cluster is the principal evidentiary witness to the operational, practical Vinaya scholarship of Dunhuang monasticism — distinct from the Chángān scholastic tradition preserved in the canonical Suí-Tang commentaries.

### Important persons

#### Vinaya translators

- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Kumārajīva, 344–413) — translated the **Sarvāstivāda** *Shísòng lǜ* [KR6k0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0016) with [弗若多羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%97%E8%8B%A5%E5%A4%9A%E7%BE%85) 404–409; the foundational document of southern-Chinese Vinaya practice. Also translated the apocryphal-Mahāyāna *Qīngjìng pínì fāngguǎng jīng* [KR6k0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0111) and the *Fànwǎng jīng* [KR6k0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0076) is canonically attributed to him.
- [佛陀耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) (Buddhayaśas) and [竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5) (Zhú Fóniàn) — translated the **Dharmaguptaka** *Sìfēn lǜ* [KR6k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0009) at Chángān 410–412. The Vinaya that became canonical for all subsequent Chinese, Korean, Japanese, and Vietnamese monasticism. Zhú Fóniàn alone is also the translator of the *Bínàiyē* [KR6k0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0045) (383) — the earliest extant Chinese Vinaya — and of *Yīngluò běnyè jīng* [KR6k0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0105).
- [法顯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%A1%AF) (Fǎxiǎn, 337–422) — translated the **Mahāsāṃghika** *Móhēsēngqí lǜ* [KR6k0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0006) (416–418) with [佛陀跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) Buddhabhadra from the Sanskrit manuscript he brought back from Pāṭaliputra; also translated the Sarvāstivāda *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* [KR6k0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0018) and the Mahāsāṃghika *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* [KR6k0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0008).
- [佛陀什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E4%BB%80) (Buddhajīva) and 竺道生 [竺道生](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E9%81%93%E7%94%9F) — translated the **Mahīśāsaka** *Wǔfēn lǜ* [KR6k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0001) (423–424). Buddhajīva is the principal translator of the entire Mahīśāsaka tradition.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) (Yìjìng, 635–713) — the **Mūlasarvāstivāda** translator. After his Indian sojourn 671–695, executed at Chángān 700–714 the most ambitious single Vinaya programme in Chinese: the eighteen-text *vastu*-by-*vastu* translation of the entire Mūlasarvāstivāda corpus ([KR6k0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0023)–[KR6k0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0040)) plus three short standalone Vinaya manuals [KR6k0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0188) [KR6k0189](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0189) [KR6k0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0190) based on his observation of Indian monastic practice.
- [求那跋摩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E6%91%A9) (Guṇavarman, 367–431) — Kashmiri master at Jiànkāng; translated the *Sìfēn bǐqiūnī jiémófǎ* [KR6k0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0015) (the procedural-textual foundation of the historical *bhikṣuṇī*-saṅgha in China, 431), the parallel *Bǐqiūnī jiémójīng* [KR6k0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0052), and the principal Chinese lay-precept *sūtra* [KR6k0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0065). The principal Indian author of the early Chinese *bhikṣuṇī* tradition.
- [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema, 385–433) — translated the *Yōupósè jièjīng* [KR6k0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0110) (the foundational lay-bodhisattva precept scripture) and the **Yogācāra** bodhisattva-precept material [KR6k0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0122) *Púsà jièběn* (414–421).
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — re-translated the **Yogācāra** bodhisattva-precept text [KR6k0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0123) and its procedural *Jiémówén* [KR6k0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0121) from the Sanskrit (645–664), supplying the Mahāyāna stream with its philologically definitive base.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha, 499–569) — translated the **Sammitīya** *Lǜ èrshíèr míngliǎo lùn* [KR6k0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0042) (568) with Buddhatrāta — the only extant Sammitīya Vinaya in any language.

#### The Tang Sìfēnlǜ scholastic founders

- [道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3) (Dàoxuān, 596–667) — founder of the **Nánshān** 南山 school at Zhōngnánshān 終南山; the single most consequential Vinaya master in Chinese history. Author of the *San dàbù* [KR6k0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0046) [KR6k0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0128) [KR6k0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0131), the institutional manuals [KR6k0178](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0178)–[KR6k0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0185), the *Píní zuòchí xùshì* [KR6k0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0160), the women's-saṅgha manual [KR6k0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0155), the *Yìchāo* [KR6k0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0176), and the *Xīnshāndìng* prātimokṣa [KR6k0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0049). After the imperial decree of 777 the canonical Chinese Vinaya master.
- [法礪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%A4%AA) (Fǎlì, 569–635) — founder of the **Xiāngbù** 相部 school of *Sìfēnlǜ* exegesis at Yè 鄴 in northern China. His *Shū* [KR6k0161](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0161) and the Tang sub-commentary by Dìngbīn [KR6k0163](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0163) are the principal documents of the older Xiāngbù tradition that the Nánshān eventually superseded.
- [懷素](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E7%B4%A0) (Huáisù, 625–698) — founder of the **Dōngtǎ** 東塔 school at the East Pagoda of the Xī-Míng-sì 西明寺. The *Kāizōng jì* [KR6k0165](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0165) is the principal surviving Dōngtǎ commentary; the alternative *karmavācanā* manuals [KR6k0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0047) [KR6k0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0048) codify the Dōngtǎ procedural tradition for both *bhikṣus* and *bhikṣuṇīs*.
- 智首 (Zhìshǒu, 567–635) — Dàoxuān's teacher; conventionally the eighth patriarch of the Chinese *Sìfēnlǜ* tradition. The *Shū* [KR6k0164](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0164) survives in fragmentary form.
- 定賓 (Dìngbīn, fl. 700–740) — Xiāngbù scholastic; authored the *Bǐqiū jièběn shū* [KR6k0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0132) (the principal alternative to Dàoxuān's Hánzhù jièběn) and the great Tang sub-commentary on Fǎlì's *Shū* [KR6k0163](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0163).
- 道世 (Dàoshì, d. 683) — Dàoxuān's collaborator at the West Pagoda; author of the *Píní tǎoyào* [KR6k0172](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0172) and of the encyclopaedic *Fǎyuàn zhūlín*.
- 大覺 (Dàjué, fl. 700–800) — author of the substantial *Xíngshì chāo pī* [KR6k0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0166) commentary.
- 志鴻 (Zhìhóng, fl. 766–779) — *Sōuxuán lù* [KR6k0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0162), mid-Tang *Nánshān* sub-commentary.
- 景霄 (Jǐngxiāo, fl. 920–940) — Five-Dynasties *Nánshān* sub-commentator; *Jiǎnzhèng jì* [KR6k0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0167).

#### The Sòng Língzhī-school masters

- [元照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E7%85%A7) (Yuánzhào, 1048–1116) — the pivotal **Sòng *Língzhī* 靈芝** master at Língzhīsì 靈芝寺 (Hángzhōu); the single most prolific Sòng Vinaya author. His running *jì* commentaries [KR6k0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0129) [KR6k0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0146) [KR6k0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0158) [KR6k0177](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0177) on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù* and *Yìchāo*; his independent Vinaya theology in [KR6k0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0186) *Liùwù tú*, [KR6k0214](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0214) *Yìngfǎ jì*, [KR6k0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0215) *Dàojù fù*, [KR6k0216](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0216) *Zhīyuán yíbiān*, [KR6k0217](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0217) *Zhīyuán jí*, [KR6k0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0218) *Bǔxù Zhīyuán jí*. The principal architect of the Sòng *Língzhī* doctrinal synthesis of Vinaya, Tiāntái, and Huáyán.
- 允堪 (Yǔnkān, 1005–1061) — the founder of the *Língzhī* revival at Qiántáng. His *Fāhuī jì* [KR6k0144](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0144) on the *Hánzhù jièběn shū*, *Zhèngyuán jì* [KR6k0156](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0156) on the *Suíjī jiémó shū*, *Fǔyào jì* [KR6k0177](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0177), *Yībō míngyì zhāng* [KR6k0212](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0212), *Liùniàn wǔguān fǎ* [KR6k0213](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0213), *Fāzhēn chāo* [KR6k0211](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0211) on the *Jìngxīn jièguān fǎ*. The institutional teacher whose pupils trained Yuánzhào's generation.
- 守一 (Shǒuyī, fl. 1239–1260) — Southern-Sòng *Nánshānlǜ* master; *Zhōngnán jiāyè* [KR6k0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0219) and *Lǜzōng huìyuán* [KR6k0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0220), the foundational Southern-Sòng doctrinal compendia.
- 妙蓮 (Miàolián, fl. 1241–1254) — Sòng *Língzhī*-school polemicist; the two *Péngzhé* texts [KR6k0221](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0221) [KR6k0222](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0222).
- 妙生 (Miàoshēng, fl. 1080–1146) — Yuánzhào-line Vinaya disputant; *Biàné* [KR6k0187](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0187) and *Sānyī xiǎnzhèng tú* [KR6k0254](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0254).
- 則安 (Zéān, fl. 1116–1140) — Yuánzhào successor; *Zīchí jì xùjiě bìng wǔlì jiǎngyì* [KR6k0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0169), *Jiémójīng xùjiě* [KR6k0159](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0159), *Dàzhì lǜshī lǐzàn wén* [KR6k0210](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0210).

#### The Korean / Silla Vinaya commentators

- [元曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E6%9B%89) (Wǒnhyo 元曉, 617–686) — Silla philosopher; the foundational scholastic of Korean Buddhism. His *Fànwǎng púsà jièběn sījì* [KR6k0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0090), the *bodhisattva*-precept performative manual *Púsà jièběn chífàn yàojì* [KR6k0194](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0194), the *Yīngluò běnyè jīng shū* [KR6k0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0107), and the *Mahāyāna-six-senses repentance* [KR6k0197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0197). The principal Silla witness to the Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* synthesis.
- 義寂 (Ŭijŏk, fl. 660–690) — Silla Yogācāra scholastic; *Púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0082) — the canonical Silla-Yogācāra reading of the *Fànwǎng*.
- 太賢 (Tàixián / Taehyŏn, fl. 700–770) — Silla Yogācāra scholastic; *Fànwǎng jīng gǔjì jì* [KR6k0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0083) (the most thorough Silla commentary on the *Fànwǎng*) and the *Púsà jièběn zōngyào* [KR6k0193](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0193).
- 勝莊 (Sŭngjang, fl. 700–720) — Silla Yogācāra; *Púsà jièběn shùjì* [KR6k0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0091).

#### Tang and Sòng Tiāntái / Huáyán commentators on the Fànwǎng

- [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) (Zhìyǐ, 538–597) — Tiāntái founder; *Púsàjiè yìshū* [KR6k0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0078) (recorded by Guàndǐng) — the foundational Tiāntái commentary on the *Fànwǎng*.
- 灌頂 (Guàndǐng, 561–632) — Zhìyǐ's recorder and his independent *Yìshū* [KR6k0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0084).
- 明曠 (Míngkuàng, fl. 712–779) — Tang Tiāntái redactor of Zhìyǐ's commentary [KR6k0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0079).
- [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) (Fǎzàng, 643–712) — Huáyán founder; *Fànwǎng púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0080), the foundational Huáyán reading of the *bodhisattva-precepts*.
- 知周 (Zhī Zhōu, fl. 668–723) — Cí'ēn Yogācāra; *Púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0092).
- 法銑 (Fǎ Xiǎn, fl. 700–800) — *Fànwǎng púsà jiè shū* [KR6k0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0093).
- 與咸 (Yǔxián, fl. 960–1127) — Sòng commentator; *Fànwǎng púsà jiè jīng shū zhù* [KR6k0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0085).
- 智圓 (Zhìyuán, 976–1022) — Northern-Sòng Tiāntái; *Nánshān zǔshī lǐzàn wén* [KR6k0207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0207) — the earliest Sòng patriarch-veneration verse for Dàoxuān.
- [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) (Zhànrán, 711–782) — Tiāntái sixth patriarch; *Shòu púsà jiè yí* [KR6k0249](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0249) — the principal Tang Tiāntái *bodhisattva-precept* conferral manual.

#### Late-Míng and Qīng Vinaya revival masters

- [袾宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%BE%E5%AE%8F) (Yúnqī Zhūhóng, 1535–1615) — the inaugural figure of the **late-Míng Vinaya revival** at Yúnqīsì 雲棲寺. The three-part commentary *Yìshū fāyǐn* [KR6k0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0086) *Shìyì* [KR6k0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0087) *Wènbiàn* [KR6k0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0088); the foundational *Shāmí lǜyí yàolüè* (preserved here in its commentarial transmission [KR6k0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0228) [KR6k0232](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0232)). The teacher whose influence ramifies through Zhìxù, Dúté, and Hóngzàn.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) (Ǒuyì Zhìxù, 1599–1655) — Tiāntái-Chán late-Míng systematiser; *Píní jíyào* [KR6k0151](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0151), *Sìfēn lǜ chíjiè jiēdù lüèshì* [KR6k0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0174), *Púsà jièběn jīng jiānyào* [KR6k0195](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0195), *Jiémówén shì* [KR6k0196](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0196), the *Fànwǎng* commentaries [KR6k0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0096) [KR6k0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0097), the lay-precept compendium [KR6k0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0244), the *Shāmí shíjiè wēiyí lùyào* [KR6k0242](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0242), the repentance manual [KR6k0245](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0245). The principal late-Míng Tiāntái Vinaya scholar.
- [讀體](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AE%80%E9%AB%94) (Dúté, 1601–1679) — founder of the **Bǎohuáshān** Vinaya revival; the canonical authority on Chinese ordination practice. *Píní zhǐchí huìjí* [KR6k0223](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0223), *Píní rìyòng qièyào* [KR6k0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0224) (in continuous monastic use to the present), *Shāmíní lǜyí yàolüè* [KR6k0225](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0225), *Chuánjiè zhèngfàn* [KR6k0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0226) (the canonical *sāntán* ordination manual), *Píní zuòchí xùshì* [KR6k0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0160).

- [弘贊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%98%E8%B4%8A) (Hóngzàn, 1611–1685) — founder of the **Dǐnghú-shān** Vinaya revival; the most prolific Vinaya author of the early Qīng. ### Topics

- **The four Chinese Vinayas in conflict and synthesis.** The five-school disciplinary corpora translated 383–714 made China the first culture in which all Indic Vinaya traditions were systematically available in a single language. The fifth-century period saw active competition between the Sarvāstivāda (*Shísòng*, southern preference) and Dharmaguptaka (*Sìfēn*, northern preference), eventually resolved by the imperial decree of Dàizōng (777) mandating exclusive use of the *Sìfēn lǜ* — the decision that shaped all subsequent East-Asian monastic discipline.
- **The Sìfēnlǜ scholastic schools.** The Tang produced three competing schools of *Sìfēnlǜ* exegesis — the *Xiāngbù* of Fǎlì at Yè, the *Nánshān* of Dàoxuān at Zhōngnánshān, and the *Dōngtǎ* of Huáisù at the Xīmíngsì. Each developed its own karman-formulary [KR6k0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0046) vs. [KR6k0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0047) and its own *prātimokṣa* recension [KR6k0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0131) vs. [KR6k0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0132) vs. [KR6k0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0049); the *Nánshān* eventually displaced both rivals after the eighth century.
- **The Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* problem.** The presence in the Mahāyāna canon of two parallel disciplinary traditions — the *Fànwǎng jīng* tradition (Chinese-apocryphal, ten major + forty-eight minor precepts, conferred on monks and laity alike) and the Yogācāra tradition (Indian-canonical, derived from the *Yogācārabhūmi*, framed as supplementary to the school-Vinaya) — generated one of the central exegetical debates of East-Asian Buddhism. The Tiāntái and Huáyán schools generally favoured the *Fànwǎng* reading; the Cí'ēn / Fǎxiàng school favoured the Yogācāra reading; the Silla scholastics produced a distinctive synthetic interpretation.
- **The precept-body (戒體 jiètǐ).** The doctrinal-metaphysical question: what is the ontological status of the discipline conferred by ordination? Is it a physical *rūpa*-dharma (the Sarvāstivāda position), a *citta-viprayukta* unconditioned dharma (the early *Sìfēn* / *Dharmaguptaka* position), or a *citta-saṃprayukta* mental state (the Mahāyāna / *Língzhī*-school position)? Yuánzhào's *jiètǐ* theology in his *Zhīyuán jí* [KR6k0217](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0217) is the canonical Sòng synthesis, integrating Vinaya, Tiāntái doctrinal classification, and Huáyán *fǎjiè* metaphysics.
- **The dual-saṅgha (二部僧) ordination of nuns.** The canonical requirement that *bhikṣuṇī* ordination be conferred by both the male and female saṅghas — and the historical question of when, and through what lineage, this had first been achieved in China — runs from Guṇavarman's foundational 433 ordination texts [KR6k0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0015) [KR6k0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0052) through Dúté's *Chuánjiè zhèngfàn* [KR6k0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0226) and Hóngzàn's *Bǐqiūní shòujiè lù* [KR6k0236](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0236). The historical accuracy of Hóngzàn's narrative was disputed in 17th-century Qīng scholarship and remains a live issue in contemporary East-Asian Buddhism.
- **The ordination platform and the architecture of monastic discipline.** Dàoxuān's *Jiètán tújīng* [KR6k0178](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0178) and *Qíhuánsì tújīng* [KR6k0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0185) are the foundational documents for the institutional vision in which the architecture of the monastery itself enacts the discipline. The *sāntán* 三壇 (three-platform) ordination of the late-Míng Bǎohuáshān revival [KR6k0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0226) is the operative codification of this vision for the late-imperial and modern periods.
- **Vinaya casuistry.** The casuistic genre — Q&A on points of discipline — runs from the early *paripṛcchā* sūtras (*Shèlìfú wèn jīng* [KR6k0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0053), *Yōubālí wèn fó jīng* [KR6k0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0054), *Mùlián suǒwèn jīng* [KR6k0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0057)) through the apocryphal *Mùlián wǔbǎiwèn* [KR6k0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0072) [KR6k0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0073) and its late-Míng commentaries [KR6k0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0074) [KR6k0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0075), down to the popular *Jièshā sìshíbā wèn* [KR6k0262](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0262) of 1700–1739. The genre is the principal vehicle for practical-pastoral monastic instruction.
- **Repentance liturgy.** The *chànfǎ* corpus — anchored by the Liáng-court *Liánghuáng bǎochàn* [KR6k0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0198) (502–549) — is the principal liturgical interface between Vinaya and lay-Buddhist devotion. The *Shuǐlù* mass [KR6k0204](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0204) and the *Cíbēi shuǐchàn* [KR6k0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0199) generated the most elaborate East-Asian Buddhist ritual programmes; the late-Qīng adaptations [KR6k0205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0205) [KR6k0206](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0206) document the continuing imperial-court adaptation of the genre.
- **The Vinaya as institutional history.** Dàoxuān's hagiographic *Lǜxiàng gǎntōng zhuàn* [KR6k0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0184) and the lineage-veneration *zànyí* tradition for the Nánshān masters [KR6k0207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0207)–[KR6k0210](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0210) document the way the Vinaya tradition wrote itself as an institutional history of patriarchal succession — a function paralleling the lineage-claims of the Chán school but anchored in scriptural-procedural rather than mind-to-mind transmission.
- **East-Asian transmission.** The transmission of the *Sìfēn lǜ* to Korea (foundational for the Silla scholastic tradition documented by Wǒnhyo, Ŭijŏk, and Tàixián), to Japan (where Ganjin's 鑑真 establishment of the Tang Vinaya at Nara — outside KR6k proper — drew on this body of literature, and where the Kamakura *Lǜzōng wèndá* [KR6k0256](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0256) documents the Sino-Japanese exchange), and to Vietnam are the principal continuing transmission histories of the division.
- **The late-Indian Mūlasarvāstivāda detour.** Yìjìng's ambitious 700–714 programme to make the late-Indian Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya available in Chinese, even as the Chinese practice itself was decisively shifting to the Dharmaguptaka *Sìfēn*, is one of the great translational paradoxes of Tang Buddhism. The Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya as preserved here remains the most thorough Chinese-language witness to a Vinaya tradition that has nowhere been the operational discipline of Chinese monasticism — but is the canonical Vinaya of the entire Tibetan Buddhist world.

# 律部 (T23)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 13 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6k 律部 *Lǜ bù* — Buddhist canon — Vinaya (monastic discipline)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/): 13 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6k 律部 *Lǜ bù* — Buddhist canon — Vinaya (monastic discipline)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6k` 律部 (*Lǜ bù*, "Vinaya section") is the Kanripo mirror of the Vinaya division of the Chinese Buddhist canon — the canonical *Vinaya-piṭaka* together with its Indic and East-Asian exegetical and ritual-procedural literature. In CANWWW  the material is distributed across three divisions: `div13` 律部 holds the Vinayas proper and their *prātimokṣa-*, *karman-* and *paripṛcchā-*satellites (T22 No. 1421 — T24 No. 1504); `div14` 律疏部 holds the principal Suí–Tang exegetical layer (T40 Nos. 1804–1815, plus T45 Nos. 1892–1910); `div27` 續律疏部 holds the later Sòng–Míng–Qīng Chinese sub-commentaries together with the Japanese scholastic apparatus. Kanripo `KR6k` integrates these three CANWWW divisions and supplements them with a large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial tail, so that 263 works are catalogued here in total — roughly the same order of magnitude as the *Prajñāpāramitā* division [KR6c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/) but with a quite different shape: where the *Bōrě bù* is anchored by a small handful of recurrently retranslated Indic sūtras, the Vinaya division is anchored by five Indic disciplinary corpora belonging to five different *nikāya* schools, all surviving only in their Chinese form, together with a much larger East-Asian scholastic and ritual-procedural superstructure.

The corpus falls into six historically and doctrinally distinct strata. (1) The **early-fifth-century translation wave** (404–431) at Chángān and Jiànyè brought into Chinese the full disciplinary literature of four Indic *nikāya* schools — the *Shísòng lǜ* 十誦律 of the Sarvāstivāda, the *Sìfēn lǜ* 四分律 of the Dharmaguptaka, the *Móhēsēngqí lǜ* 摩訶僧祇律 of the Mahāsāṃghika, and the *Wǔfēn lǜ* 五分律 of the Mahīśāsaka — together with supplementary texts of the Kāśyapīya and Sammitīya. The Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas survive in no other language, so this stratum is the principal evidentiary base for *all* modern comparative-Vinaya scholarship (Clarke 2015; *cf.* Wilkinson §29.5.7.6). (2) The **Tang *Sìfēnlǜ* scholastic synthesis** at Chángān (620–697) saw the *Sìfēn lǜ* gradually displace the *Shísòng lǜ* as the practical Vinaya of Chinese monasticism, under three competing exegetical schools — Fǎlì's 法礪 ([法礪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%A4%AA)) Xiāngbù 相部, Dàoxuān's 道宣 ([道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3)) Nánshān 南山, and Huáisù's 懷素 ([懷素](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E7%B4%A0)) Dōngtǎ 東塔 — of which the Nánshān school's victory under the imperial decree of Dàizōng (777) made Dàoxuān's *San dàbù* 三大部 the canonical Chinese Vinaya curriculum thereafter. (3) The **Yìjìng Mūlasarvāstivāda programme** (700–714) translated the disciplinary corpus of the late-Indic Mūlasarvāstivāda — by then the dominant Vinaya school of Indian Buddhism and (still later) the canonical Vinaya of the Tibetan, Mongolian, and Bhutanese traditions — into Chinese as a single eighteen-text *vastu*-by-*vastu* programme, but this Vinaya never displaced the *Sìfēn* in Chinese practice. (4) The **Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* stream** is anchored by the apocryphal *Fànwǎng jīng* 梵網經 ([KR6k0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0076), attributed to Kumārajīva but Chinese in origin) and runs in parallel to the school-Vinaya tradition, generating its own large commentarial corpus (Zhìyǐ 智顗, Fǎzàng 法藏, Wǒnhyo 元曉, Tàixián 太賢, Yúnqī Zhūhóng 雲棲袾宏, Ǒuyì Zhìxù 蕅益智旭); the alternative *Yogācāra*-school *bodhisattva-precepts* (Maitreya / Asaṅga, translated by Dharmakṣema and re-translated by Xuánzàng) provided the Mahāyāna stream with a second textual base. (5) The **Sòng *Língzhī*-school revival** (Yǔnkān 允堪 1005–1061; Yuánzhào 元照 1048–1116; Shǒuyī 守一 / Miàolián 妙蓮 in the Southern Sòng) produced an extensive sub-commentarial apparatus on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù*, recovered the doctrine of the precept-body (戒體 *jiètǐ*), and re-anchored Vinaya practice in the Tiāntái doctrinal system. (6) The **late-Míng / Qīng Vinaya revival** (Yúnqī Zhūhóng, Zhìxù, Dúté 讀體 1601–1679 at Bǎohuáshān 寶華山, Hóngzàn 弘贊 1611–1685 at Dǐnghú-shān 鼎湖山, the *Sānfēng* line of Fǎzàng 法藏 1573–1635) re-standardised Chinese ordination practice through the new *sāntán* 三壇 (three-platform) ordination system, generated the daily-use Vinaya manual that has remained in use to the present (*Píní rìyòng qièyào* [KR6k0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0224)), and produced the most thorough Qīng-period commentaries on every layer of the disciplinary tradition.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The four (then five) school-Vinayas

- *Sìfēn lǜ* 四分律 [KR6k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0009) — the **Dharmaguptaka** Vinaya translated 410–412 by [佛陀耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) (Buddhayaśas) and [竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5) (Zhú Fóniàn). After the Tang imperial decree of 777 the canonical Chinese Vinaya and the operational basis of Chinese, Korean, Japanese, and Vietnamese monasticism to the present. Its *bhikṣu-prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0010) / [KR6k0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0011); the *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0012); the early *karmavācanā* compendia [KR6k0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0013) [KR6k0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0014) [KR6k0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0015).
- *Shísòng lǜ* 十誦律 [KR6k0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0016) — the **Sarvāstivāda** Vinaya translated 404–409 by [弗若多羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%97%E8%8B%A5%E5%A4%9A%E7%BE%85) (Puṇyatāra) and [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Kumārajīva). The first complete Indian Vinaya translated into Chinese and the dominant Vinaya of southern-Chinese monasticism through the Liú-Sòng and Qí–Liáng. Its *prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0017) / [KR6k0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0018); the *karmavācanā* manuals [KR6k0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0019) [KR6k0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0020); the principal Indic commentary [KR6k0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0021) *Sàpóduō pínì pípóshā* and the *mātṛkā* [KR6k0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0022).
- *Móhēsēngqí lǜ* 摩訶僧祇律 [KR6k0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0006) — the **Mahāsāṃghika** Vinaya translated 416–418 by [法顯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%A1%AF) (Fǎxiǎn) and [佛陀跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Buddhabhadra), based on the manuscript Fǎxiǎn brought back from Pāṭaliputra. Surviving in no other language; the principal evidentiary witness to the disciplinary tradition of the *Mahāsāṃghika* — the lineage whose schism in the second post-Nirvāṇa century is conventionally regarded as the institutional ancestry of Mahāyāna Buddhism. Its *prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0007) / [KR6k0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0008).
- *Wǔfēn lǜ* 五分律 [KR6k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0001) — the **Mahīśāsaka** Vinaya translated 422–423 by [佛陀什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E4%BB%80) (Buddhajīva) and [竺道生](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E9%81%93%E7%94%9F) (Zhú Dàoshēng). #### Dàoxuān's *Three Great Works* of the Nánshān school

The institutional triad of the Tang *Sìfēnlǜ* curriculum, codified at Zhōngnánshān 終南山 by Dàoxuān between 626 and 667:

- *Sìfēn lǜ shānfán bǔquē xíngshì chāo* 四分律刪繁補闕行事鈔 [KR6k0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0128) (T1804) — the procedural manual of monastic practice; the most-studied Vinaya book in pre-modern East Asia.
- *Sìfēn lǜ shānbǔ suíjī jiémó* 四分律刪補隨機羯磨 [KR6k0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0046) (T1808) — the codified *karmavācanā* compendium for all monastic legal acts.
- *Sìfēn lǜ bǐqiū hánzhù jièběn* 四分律比丘含注戒本 [KR6k0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0131) (T1806) — Dàoxuān's annotated *prātimokṣa* recension; with the parallel *Sìfēn bǐqiūnī chāo* 四分比丘尼鈔 [KR6k0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0155) for the women's saṅgha.

Around the *San dàbù* runs the principal Tang *Nánshān* sub-commentarial cluster — Dàoxuān's own *Yìchāo* 義鈔 [KR6k0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0176), the Five-Dynasties *Jiǎnzhèng jì* [KR6k0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0167) of Jǐng Xiāo 景霄, and the eighth-century *Sōuxuán lù* [KR6k0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0162) of Zhì Hóng 志鴻; the Tang Xiāngbù tradition is represented by Fǎlì's *Shū* [KR6k0161](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0161) with Dìngbīn's *Shìzōng yìjì* [KR6k0163](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0163) and Dìngbīn's *Bǐqiū jièběn shū* [KR6k0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0132); the Tang Dōngtǎ tradition by Huáisù's *Kāizōng jì* [KR6k0165](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0165) and his alternative *karmavācanā* recensions [KR6k0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0047) [KR6k0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0048).

The principal Sòng *jì* — running line-by-line sub-commentaries on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù* by Yǔnkān 允堪 and Yuánzhào 元照, the two pillars of the *Língzhī* 靈芝 revival — fill out the Vinaya scholastic apparatus: Yuánzhào's *Zīchí jì* [KR6k0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0129) on the *Xíngshì chāo*; his *Xíngzōng jì* [KR6k0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0146) on the *Hánzhù jièběn shū*; his *Jìyuán jì* [KR6k0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0158) on the *Suíjī jiémó shū*; Yǔnkān's *Fāhuī jì* [KR6k0144](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0144) on the same; the *Fǔyào jì* [KR6k0177](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0177) on the *Yìchāo*; the Japanese *Zīxíng chāo* [KR6k0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0130) by Shōen 照遠 (14th c., Tō-ji Vinaya scholar). Yuánzhào's wider Vinaya prose — the *Zhīyuán jí* [KR6k0217](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0217), *Bǔxù Zhīyuán jí* [KR6k0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0218), *Zhīyuán yíbiān* [KR6k0216](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0216) — preserves the doctrinal foundations of the *Língzhī* revival.

#### Dàoxuān's wider Vinaya treatises

A distinct cluster of nine Dàoxuān works on institutional and ritual aspects of monastic discipline that fall outside the *San dàbù* proper:

- *Jiètán tújīng* 戒壇圖經 [KR6k0178](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0178) — the canonical Tang manual on the architectural form of the ordination platform; the foundational document for every East-Asian Vinaya-school ordination hall.
- *Jìngxīn jièguān fǎ* 淨心戒觀法 [KR6k0179](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0179) — Vinaya observance integrated with meditative practice.
- *Zhāngfú yí* 釋門章服儀 [KR6k0180](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0180) — the canonical regulation of monastic vestments.
- *Liàngchù qīngzhòng yí* 量處輕重儀 [KR6k0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0181) — the disposition of a deceased monk's property.
- *Guījìng yí* 釋門歸敬儀 [KR6k0182](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0182) — refuge-taking.
- *Xínghù lǜyí* 教誡新學比丘行護律儀 [KR6k0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0183) — novice instruction.
- *Lǜxiàng gǎntōng zhuàn* 律相感通傳 [KR6k0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0184) — the hagiographic Wèituó 韋陀 tradition.
- *Qíhuánsì tújīng* 中天竺舍衛國祇洹寺圖經 [KR6k0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0185) — the cosmographic blueprint of the standard Buddhist monastery.

The cluster's Sòng running commentaries — Yuánzhào and Liángxìn's *Yìngfǎ jì* [KR6k0214](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0214) on the *Zhāngfú yí*; Yuánzhào's *Liùwù tú* [KR6k0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0186) (the *Pratītyasamutpāda* of robes and bowl); Miàoshēng's *Sānyī xiǎnzhèng tú* [KR6k0254](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0254) and *Liùwù tú biàné* [KR6k0187](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0187) — together with the Tiāntái-line subcommentary *Tōngzhēn jì* [KR6k0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0253) and *Hùfǎ jì* [KR6k0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0252) on the *Guījìng yí* — preserve the most extensive Sòng-period institutional-Vinaya scholarship.

#### The *Fànwǎng jīng* + Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* cluster

The Mahāyāna disciplinary stream is anchored by the *Brahma-net Sūtra*, the foundational scripture of East-Asian *bodhisattva-precepts*, generating one of the densest commentarial clusters in the entire Buddhist canon:

- *Fànwǎng jīng* 梵網經 [KR6k0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0076) (T1484) — canonically ascribed to Kumārajīva but widely recognised as a Chinese apocryphon composed c. 440–480; the canonical scripture of the Mahāyāna ten-major-precepts and forty-eight-minor-precepts system. With Kūkai's [空海](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A9%BA%E6%B5%B7) Shingon *Fànwǎngjīng kāití* [KR6k0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0077).
- The **Tang scholastic commentarial cluster** spans every major doctrinal school. Tiāntái: Zhìyǐ–Guàndǐng *Púsàjiè yìshū* [KR6k0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0078) and its Tang revision by Míngkuàng [KR6k0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0079) and Guàndǐng's independent *Yìshū* [KR6k0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0084). Huáyán: Fǎzàng *Púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0080). The Silla/Korean cluster: Wǒnhyo *Sījì* [KR6k0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0090) (the Korean scholastic foundation), Ŭijŏk *Púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0082) (Silla Yogācāra), Tàixián *Gǔjì jì* [KR6k0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0083), Sŭngjang *Shùjì* [KR6k0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0091), and the Cí'ēn Yogācāra readings of Zhī Zhōu [KR6k0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0092) and Fǎ Xiǎn [KR6k0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0093). The Japanese sub-commentary stratum is anchored by Gyōnen's 凝然 *Rìzhū chāo* 梵網戒本疏日珠鈔 [KR6k0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0081) (1276–1321) — the largest single commentary on the *Fànwǎng jīng* in any language.
- The **late-Míng commentarial flowering** under Yúnqī Zhūhóng and his successors: Zhūhóng's three-part synthesis [KR6k0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0086) *Yìshū fāyǐn* with its *Shìyì* [KR6k0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0087) and *Wènbiàn* [KR6k0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0088); Zhìxù's *Xuányì* [KR6k0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0096) and *Hézhù* [KR6k0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0097), the principal Tiāntái-school late-imperial commentary; Hóngzàn's *Lüèshū* [KR6k0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0098) and *Bànyuè sòng púsà jiè yíshì zhù* [KR6k0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0099); Jìguāng's *Zhíjiě* [KR6k0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0100) with its *Shìyì* [KR6k0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0101), the principal Bǎohuáshān commentary; Déyù's red-ink *Shùnzhū* [KR6k0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0102); Shūyù's *Chūjīn* [KR6k0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0103). Dunhuang fragments [KR6k0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0104) preserve the lost middle-Tang commentarial layer.
- The **Yogācāra alternative**: the bodhisattva-precept section of the *Yogācārabhūmi* translated twice by [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) Dharmakṣema as [KR6k0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0122) *Púsà jièběn* (414–421) and re-translated by [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) Xuánzàng as [KR6k0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0123) (645–664); the procedural *Jiémówén* [KR6k0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0121) of Xuánzàng, with Zhìxù's late-Míng commentary [KR6k0195](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0195) *Jiānyào* and [KR6k0196](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0196) *Jiémówén shì*.
- The **bodhisattva-precept conferral manuals**: the Tang Tiāntái *Shòu púsà jiè yí* by Zhànrán [KR6k0249](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0249), the doubtfully-attributed parallel work by Huìsī [KR6k0248](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0248), the combined-rite *Lüè shòu sānguī wǔbājiè bìng púsàjiè* [KR6k0250](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0250) by Chéngzhào, Yánshòu's *Shòu púsà jiè fǎ* [KR6k0251](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0251), and the foundational late-Míng Chán-school *Hóngjiè fǎyí* [KR6k0246](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0246) of Sānfēng Fǎzàng with its successor *San-tán* manual [KR6k0247](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0247).
- The **bodhisattva-vinaya sūtra cluster** in T24: *Yīngluò běnyè jīng* [KR6k0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0105) (a Chinese apocryphon, with Wǒnhyo's commentary [KR6k0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0107) and a Dunhuang fragment [KR6k0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0106)); *Shòu shíshànjiè jīng* [KR6k0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0108); *Yōupósè jièjīng* [KR6k0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0110) (Dharmakṣema's lay-bodhisattva precept *sūtra*); *Qīngjìng pínì fāngguǎng jīng* [KR6k0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0111) (Kumārajīva, c. 405); *Cíngjìng pínì jīng* [KR6k0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0112); the Sòng late-Indic *Dàshèng jiè jīng* [KR6k0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0119) and *Bāzhǒng chángyǎng gōngdé jīng* [KR6k0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0120); the Sòng *Qīngjìng pínàiyé zuìshàng dàshèng jīng* [KR6k0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0127); together with the apocryphal-historical *Shèlìfú wèn jīng* [KR6k0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0053) and the *paripṛcchā*-genre satellites [KR6k0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0054) [KR6k0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0057).

- The *Mùlián wǔbǎiwèn* 目連五百問 cluster — the Buddhist Vinaya casuistic catechism: [KR6k0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0072) [KR6k0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0073) (Buddhist apocrypha, c. 350–600) with their late-Míng commentaries [KR6k0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0074) (Xìngqí) and [KR6k0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0075) (Yǒnghǎi).
