### Topics

- **Vijñaptimātra / cittamātra** (唯識 *wéishí*). The thesis that what appears as an external object is a transformation of consciousness; argued textually through Vasubandhu's *Viṃśatikā* and *Triṃśikā* and exegetically through the entire *Chéng wéishí lùn* commentarial pyramid.
- **The eight consciousnesses** (八識 *bā shí*), with particular attention to the *ālayavijñāna* (阿賴耶識) as substrate and *kliṣṭamanas* (染汚意) as the sixth-to-seventh-consciousness link. Paramārtha's idiosyncratic positing of a ninth, *amalavijñāna* 阿摩羅識, is one of the principal Old-Yogācāra peculiarities. The *Bā shí guījǔ* tradition turns the eight-consciousness schema into a Ming pedagogical genre.
- **The three natures** (三性 *sān xìng*, *trisvabhāva*): *parikalpita* (遍計所執), *paratantra* (依他起), *pariniṣpanna* (圓成實). The cross-cutting **three non-natures** (三無性) doctrine is foregrounded in Paramārtha's *Sān wúxìng lùn* [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) and is the principal hermeneutic key for reconciling the Yogācāra ontology with the Prajñāpāramitā emptiness teaching.
- **Five gotras / five natures** (五姓各別 *wǔxìng gèbié*). The Yogācārabhūmi taxonomy of five fixed spiritual lineages, against which Wǒnch'ǔk and the East Asian one-vehicle traditions argue. The Cí'ēn defence of the five-gotras position is the principal polemical thread of Huìzhāo's *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- **The Hundred Dharmas** (百法 *bǎifǎ*). Vasubandhu's 5-category × 100-item taxonomy of dharmas (T1614); becomes the standard East Asian Buddhist abhidharmic primer and generates a long commentarial chain from Kuījī's *Dàshèng bǎifǎ míngmén lùn shū* [KR6n0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0098) through the Dūnhuáng *Kāizōng yìjì* [KR6n0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0107) to the Wànlì-era revivalist commentaries [KR6n0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0103)–[KR6n0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0106).
- **Stages of the Yoga practitioner** (瑜伽師地 *yúqié shī dì*) — the seventeen-bhūmi structure of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, organising the entire division.
- **Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha synthesis**. T1610 *Fóxìng lùn*, T1611 *Bǎoxìng lùn*, T1626–1627 *Fǎjiè wú chābié lùn*, and T1612 *Wǔyùn lùn* sit at the seam between Yogācāra and the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q; the question of whether the *tathāgatagarbha* is reducible to the *ālayavijñāna* shapes both the Old-Yogācāra reception in China and the *Awakening of Faith* tradition.
- **Epistemology of perception (所緣緣)**. Through Dignāga's *Ālambanaparīkṣā* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and its commentaries, the question of what constitutes a valid object of perception becomes a Yogācāra theme; it is taken up again in the Wànlì–early Qīng commentary wave of [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117).
- **Old- vs. New-Yogācāra** (舊譯 *jiùyì* / 新譯 *xīnyì*). The Paramārtha-line readings of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* and *Triṃśikā* differ systematically from Xuánzàng's: on *amalavijñāna*, on the status of the *paratantra*, and on the relation between *vāsanā* and the *ālaya*. The division as a whole preserves both layers in parallel — the cataloguing principle is doctrinal subject matter, not translatorial school.
- **Cí'ēn school polemics**. Internal to the Táng layer: Kuījī vs. Wǒnch'ǔk on the reading of T1585; Huìzhāo's continuation of that polemic; Zhìzhōu's consolidation. These polemics define the canonical shape of the Fǎxiàng curriculum.
- **East Asian transmission and revival**. The division is the textual basis for three successive scholastic traditions: Táng Cí'ēn (mid-7th to early 8th c., centred at Cháng'ān, with Silla and Goguryeo participation), Heian–Kamakura Hossō (Vols. 65–70 of the Taishō, c. 800–1500), and late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng revival (c. 1530–1660, *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 46–55).

# 論集部 (T32)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 66 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6o 論集部 *Lùnjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Treatise Collection](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/): 66 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6o 論集部 *Lùnjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Treatise Collection](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6o corresponds to the *Lùnjí bù* 論集部 of the Taishō canon (vol. 32, nos. 1628–1692), together with the commentarial overflow in vol. 44 (nos. 1839–1850) and a small group of Dūnhuáng-recovered manuscripts in vol. 85 (nos. 2813–2816). The division is the canon's general miscellany of doctrinal treatises (*lùn* 論, śāstra) and the verse-collections (*sòng* 頌, *zàn* 讚, *gāthā* 伽他) attached to them. Unlike the dedicated divisions for Mādhyamaka and Yogācāra commentary on specific sūtras (`KR6m` 釋經論部, `KR6n` 毘曇部, 瑜伽部), KR6o gathers freestanding śāstras that do not belong to a single school or sūtra-commentary lineage: hetuvidyā (yīnmíng 因明) logic, Madhyamaka and Sautrāntika doctrinal works, the *Satyasiddhi-śāstra* of the 成實宗 school, *pratītyasamutpāda* tracts, *bodhicitta* literature, the *Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda* (*Awakening of Faith*) corpus, the Sino-Buddhist *Milindapañha* (*Nā xiān bǐqiū jīng*), and an extensive stotra/*gāthā* section. 

Chronologically the division spans c. 150 CE (the Indian source-strata of treatises by Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva, Dignāga) through 1911 (a late-Qīng vernacular gloss on *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn*), with the densest layers in (i) the fifth-/sixth-century translation projects of Kumārajīva, Paramārtha and Bodhiruci, (ii) the Táng Xuánzàng–Yìjìng era, (iii) the Northern Sòng translation bureau under Tiānxīsāi 天息災, Dānapāla 施護 and Dharmadeva 法天 (c. 982–1000), and (iv) the Heian–Kamakura and late-Míng waves of native East-Asian commentary on *yīnmíng* and *Qǐxìnlùn*. The principal transmissional issue throughout is the apocryphal or pseudepigraphic status of several of its most influential texts — *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn*, *Shì móhēyǎn lùn*, *Zhāng suǒzhī lùn*, the Sino-Tibetan-Mongol *Bāsībā* tract — for which East-Asian and modern scholarship has reached very different conclusions.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **Yīnmíng 因明 (Buddhist logic) cluster** — *Yīnmíng zhènglǐmén lùn běn* 因明正理門論本 [KR6o0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0001) (Dignāga 大域龍, tr. Xuánzàng), *Yīnmíng rù zhènglǐ lùn* 因明入正理論 [KR6o0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0003) (Śaṅkarasvāmin 商羯羅主, tr. Xuánzàng), and a parallel re-translation by Yìjìng [KR6o0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0002) form the doctrinal core of East-Asian Buddhist logic; the commentarial chain runs through Shéntài 神泰 [KR6o0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0007), Kuījī 窺基's *Yīnmíng dàshū* 因明大疏 [KR6o0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0008), Wǒnhyo's *Pànbǐliàng lùn* 判比量論 [KR6o0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0034), the Heian *Yīnmíng lùnshū míngdēng chāo* 因明論疏明燈抄 [KR6o0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0009) of Zenju 善珠, and the Edo *Yīnmíng dàshū róngguàn chāo* [KR6o0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0011) of Hōtan 鳳潭.
- **Nāgārjuna's logical-Madhyamaka treatises** — *Huízhèng lùn* 迴諍論 [KR6o0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0004) (*Vigrahavyāvartanī*), *Fāngbiàn xīn lùn* 方便心論 [KR6o0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0005) (*Upāyahṛdaya*), and *Rúshí lùn* 如實論 [KR6o0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0006) (*Tarkaśāstra*, tr. Paramārtha) preserve the earliest layer of Indian Buddhist epistemology.
- **Satyasiddhi-śāstra** — *Chéngshí lùn* 成實論 [KR6o0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0050) (Harivarman 訶梨跋摩, tr. Kumārajīva 411–412); the foundational text of the short-lived Chinese 成實宗 school and a major bridge between Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma and emerging Mahāyāna.
- **Doctrinal tracts of the Paramārtha and Bodhiruci circles** — *Suíxiāng lùn* 隨相論 [KR6o0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0045), *Sìdì lùn* 四諦論 [KR6o0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0051), *Lìshì āpítán lùn* 立世阿毘曇論 [KR6o0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0048), *Shíèr yīnyuán lùn* 十二因緣論 [KR6o0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0055), *Típó púsà pò lèngqié jīng zhōng wàidào xiǎochéng sìzōng lùn* 提婆菩薩破楞伽經中外道小乘四宗論 [KR6o0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0043) and its companion 涅槃論 [KR6o0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0044); together they constitute the sixth-century North Indian doxographic and ontological strata in Chinese translation.
- **Bodhicitta cluster** — Centred on the *Pútí xíng jīng* 菩提行經 [KR6o0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0067) (Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatāra* in Tiānxīzāi's Sòng-period rendering), with *Pútí zīliáng lùn* 菩提資糧論 [KR6o0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0065), *Guǎng shì pútíxīn lùn* 廣釋菩提心論 [KR6o0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0069), and the Vajrayāna *Jīngāngdǐng yújiā zhōng fā ānòuduōluó sānmiǎo sānpútí xīn lùn* 金剛頂瑜伽中發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心論 [KR6o0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0070) (attr. Nāgārjuna, tr. Amoghavajra 不空), which became the principal *bodhicitta* text of Shingon and attracted a dense Heian–Kamakura commentarial layer ([KR6o0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0071)–[KR6o0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0075)).
- **Awakening of Faith corpus** — *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn* 大乘起信論 attr. Aśvaghoṣa 馬鳴菩薩, in the Paramārtha [KR6o0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0078) and Śikṣānanda 實叉難陀 [KR6o0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0079) recensions; the single most consequential text of the division and arguably of East-Asian Buddhism, generating an enormous commentarial tradition represented here by Huìyuǎn 慧遠 of Jìngyǐng [KR6o0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0100), Wǒnhyo 元曉 [KR6o0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0103)/[KR6o0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0104), Fǎzàng 法藏 [KR6o0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0105)/[KR6o0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0106), Zǐxuán 子璿 [KR6o0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0107), Taehyŏn 太賢 [KR6o0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0108), Zhìxù 智旭 [KR6o0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0109), and late-Míng/Qīng glosses [KR6o0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0114)–[KR6o0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0120); plus the Dūnhuáng-recovered Tánkuàng 曇曠 layer [KR6o0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0121)/[KR6o0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0122) and an anonymous *Qǐxìnlùn zhù* [KR6o0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0123) preserved as T2814.
- **Shì móhēyǎn lùn 釋摩訶衍論 sub-cluster** — *Shì móhēyǎn lùn* [KR6o0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0084), attributed to Nāgārjuna and a translator (Vṛddhimati 筏提摩多) for whom no other works survive; almost certainly a late-eighth-century Sino-Korean apocryphon, but enormously influential in Japanese Shingon and Tendai exegesis, with thirteen commentaries here ([KR6o0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0085)–[KR6o0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0097)).
- **Apocryphal and pseudepigraphic foundational treatises** — *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn* 大宗地玄文本論 [KR6o0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0098) attr. Mǎmíng / tr. Paramārtha (very probably a Sui-Tang Chinese composition); *Zhāng suǒzhī lùn* 彰所知論 [KR6o0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0049) composed in Chinese by ʼPhags-pa Blo-gros rgyal-mtshan 八思巴 in 1278 for Qubilai's heir Zhēnjīn 真金.
- **Nā xiān bǐqiū jīng 那先比丘經 (Milindapañha)** — Two parallel early Chinese recensions [KR6o0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0124) and [KR6o0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0125), the principal Chinese witness to the Theravāda *Milindapañha* tradition.
- **Stotra / verse-praise (zàn 讚 / sòng 頌 / gāthā 伽他) cluster** — Three Chinese translations of Nāgārjuna's *Suhṛllekha* (Letter to King Gautamīputra): *Lóngshù púsà wèi Chántuójiā wáng shuō fǎyào jì* 龍樹菩薩為禪陀迦王說法要偈 [KR6o0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0127), *Quànfā zhū wáng yào jì* 勸發諸王要偈 [KR6o0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0128), and *Lóngshù púsà quànjiè wáng sòng* 龍樹菩薩勸誡王頌 [KR6o0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0129); plus *Yī bǎi wǔshí zàn fó sòng* 一百五十讚佛頌 [KR6o0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0135) (Mātṛceṭa, tr. ### Important persons

- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) — translator of *Chéngshí lùn* (411–412); single most influential Latter-Qín translator represented in the division.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha) — chief translator of the sixth-century South Indian doctrinal layer: *Rúshí lùn*, *Suíxiāng lùn*, *Sìdì lùn*, *Lìshì āpítán lùn*, *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn* (KR6o0078), *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn*.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) — translator of the *yīnmíng* core (Dignāga's *Nyāyamukha*, Śaṅkarasvāmin's *Nyāyapraveśa*) and of doctrinal compendia (*Yuánshēng lùn*, *Pútí zīliáng lùn*), founder of the East-Asian *yīnmíng* tradition.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) — re-translator of the *Nyāyamukha* [KR6o0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0002), the *Suhṛllekha* [KR6o0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0129), the *Bǎo xíng wáng zhèng lùn* [KR6o0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0061), and of several treatises (*Shǒuzhàng lùn* [KR6o0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0062), *Zhǐguān mén lùn sòng* [KR6o0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0060)) reflecting late-seventh-century Indian doctrinal style.

- [大域龍菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A7%E5%9F%9F%E9%BE%8D%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dignāga) and [商羯羅主菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%95%86%E7%BE%AF%E7%BE%85%E4%B8%BB%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Śaṅkarasvāmin) — Indian founders of Buddhist *pramāṇa* logic, whose texts head the division.
- [馬鳴菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%B3%B4%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Aśvaghoṣa, attributed) — pseudepigraphic author of the *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn* and *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn*.

### Topics

- **Buddhist logic (yīnmíng 因明 / hetuvidyā)** — the structure of the three-membered syllogism (三支比量), the analysis of the nine reasons (九句因) and the four kinds of pseudo-reason (四相違), the boundary between perception (現量) and inference (比量); a topic that runs from Dignāga's *Nyāyamukha* [KR6o0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0001) through Kuījī's *Dàshū* [KR6o0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0008) and the Japanese *Sìxiāngwéi* sub-commentaries [KR6o0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0014)–[KR6o0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0017) to late-Míng synthetic restatements [KR6o0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0026)–[KR6o0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0029).
- **The status of the *Awakening of Faith* and the *Shì móhēyǎn lùn*** — whether they are translations of lost Indian originals or East-Asian (Chinese, Korean, or possibly Central-Asian) compositions; the textual history of the doubled *Qǐxìnlùn* translation under Paramārtha and Śikṣānanda; the philological independence (or not) of the *Shì móhēyǎn lùn* from the *Qǐxìnlùn* itself. This is the principal modern philological debate in the division.
- **Pseudepigraphy and translator-attribution forgery** — *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn* and *Shì móhēyǎn lùn* travel in the canon under unverifiable translator names (Paramārtha, Vṛddhimati 筏提摩多), allowing comparison of the formal traits by which East-Asian apocrypha were inserted into a canon of putative Indian śāstras.
- **The *bodhicitta* tradition's bifurcation** — between the exoteric, ethical reading represented by Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatāra* [KR6o0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0067) and the esoteric, ritual reading represented by the Vajraśekhara *Pútíxīn lùn* [KR6o0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0070); the latter's commentarial chain in Heian Japan is the densest sub-cluster in the division.
- **The 成實宗 question** — whether Harivarman's *Chéngshí lùn* belongs to Sautrāntika, to a transitional position between Sthaviravāda and Mahāyāna, or constitutes an independent doctrinal lineage; the disappearance of the Chinese 成實宗 school in the early Táng.
- **The fivefold Pratītyasamutpāda corpus** — five short treatises ([KR6o0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0055)–[KR6o0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0059)) translating overlapping Indian materials on dependent origination, of unusual value for comparative study because they preserve parallel Chinese renderings of related Sanskrit verse-cores.
- **The transmission of Buddhist verse genres into Chinese** — how *gāthā* / *stotra* / *sòng* forms were rendered, including the three-translation problem of Nāgārjuna's *Suhṛllekha* [KR6o0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0127)–[KR6o0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0129) and the metrical conventions of the Sòng translation bureau ([KR6o0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0130)–[KR6o0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0143)).
- **The Dūnhuáng *Qǐxìnlùn* layer** — the unique witness of Tánkuàng's mid-eighth-century *Qǐxìnlùn* lectures preserved only at Dunhuang (T2813–T2814 = [KR6o0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0121)/[KR6o0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0122)/[KR6o0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0123)), evidence for a North-West-Chinese reading tradition independent of the central Táng commentaries.

## Division note: [KR6c 般若部 *Bōrě bù* — Buddhist canon — Prajñāpāramitā (Perfection of Wisdom) literature](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6c` is the Kanripo mirror of the Taishō *Bōrě bù* 般若部 — the canonical Buddhist division gathering every Chinese translation of the Indic *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtra-corpus together with the major Indic *śāstra*-commentaries on it and the bulk of the East-Asian exegetical literature it generated. In CANWWW the division is `div02` (般若部), running from `T05N0220` (Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle *Dà bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*) through `T08N0261` and the related *śāstra*-cluster in `T25`. The Kanripo `KR6c` directory expands the Taishō *Bōrě bù* by adding the very large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial corpus, so that 229 works are catalogued here in total — by some margin the largest single sūtra-class division in the entire Chinese Buddhist canon.

The chronological span is roughly 179 CE (Lokakṣema's *Dào-xíng bōrě* [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010), the earliest surviving Chinese rendering of an *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension and one of the earliest substantial Mahāyāna translations into Chinese) to the late nineteenth century (a long tail of Qīng-era *Jīngāng jīng* and *Xīnjīng* commentaries). The textual core is Indic: a small handful of Sanskrit *Prajñāpāramitā*-sūtras retranslated repeatedly across seven centuries, attended by an Indic *śāstra*-stratum (Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's Yogācāra commentaries on the *Vajracchedikā*) that mediates the sūtras to scholastic readers. Around this Indic core grew an enormous East-Asian commentarial superstructure — Suí-Táng Sānlùn and Yogācāra scholastic *shū* 疏, Tiāntái doctrinal classification, Sòng Tiāntái and Huáyán *jì* 記, Míng-Qīng Cáodòng and Chán philosophical readings, Japanese Shingon esoteric commentaries — making the division also the principal arena in which every major exegetical school of pre-modern East-Asian Buddhism articulated its reading of emptiness.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The large Prajñāpāramitā recensions

- *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* 大般若波羅蜜多經 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) — Xuánzàng's 600-fascicle integrated translation (660–663) of sixteen *huì* 會 (assemblies) covering the full Indic *prajñā*-corpus from the *Śatasāhasrikā* (100,000-verse) down to the *Vajracchedikā* and *Hṛdaya*. The single most extensive text in the Chinese Buddhist canon and the canonical reference-recension after the seventh century.
- *Móhē bōrě bōluómì jīng* 摩訶般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) — Kumārajīva's 27-fascicle rendering of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* (the "Larger Prajñāpāramitā", 25,000-verse). Up to Xuánzàng the standard Chinese form of the large *prajñā* and the base-text of Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*.
- *Fàngguāng bōrě jīng* 放光般若經 [KR6c0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0002) and *Guāngzàn jīng* 光讚經 [KR6c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0003) — the two Xī-Jìn (286 / 291) renderings of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* by Mokṣala 無羅叉 and Dharmarakṣa 竺法護 respectively; foundational documents of early Chinese Mahāyāna and the textual base for the *gé-yì* 格義 exegesis of the third and fourth centuries.
- *Dàoxíng bōrě jīng* 道行般若經 [KR6c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0010) — Lokakṣema's 179 CE translation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* (8,000-verse Prajñāpāramitā), the earliest surviving Chinese Prajñāpāramitā text and a key witness for the linguistic state of Late-Hàn Buddhist Chinese.
- *Xiǎopǐn bōrě bōluómì jīng* 小品般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0013) — Kumārajīva's 408 retranslation of the *Aṣṭasāhasrikā*, the standard "Smaller Prajñāpāramitā" of the medieval Chinese tradition.
- *Dàmíngdù jīng* 大明度經 [KR6c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0011), *Móhē bōrě chāo jīng* 摩訶般若鈔經 [KR6c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0012), *Shèngtiānwáng bōrě bōluómì jīng* 勝天王般若波羅蜜經 [KR6c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0019) — further independent Wú, Qián-Qín, and Chén-era renderings of medium and large *prajñā* recensions, valued in subsequent tradition as comparative witnesses.

#### The Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra cluster

- *Dàzhìdù lùn* 大智度論 [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) — the 100-fascicle Mahāyāna *śāstra* attributed in the Chinese tradition to Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and translated by Kumārajīva in 402–405. Commentary on the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* [KR6c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0004) but in practice an encyclopaedic compendium of pre-Yogācāra Mahāyāna doctrine; the principal Chinese source for the Sānlùn 三論 tradition and an irreplaceable doctrinal substrate for Tiāntái, Huáyán, and Chán.
- A small but doctrinally significant secondary commentarial cluster grew up around the *Dàzhìdù lùn*: [KR6c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0006) *Dàzhìdù lùn shū* by Huìyǐng 慧影 (the only surviving substantive Chinese commentary on the work), [KR6c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0007) *Dàpǐn jīng yóuyì* by Jízàng 吉藏, [KR6c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0008) *Dà huìdù jīng zōngyào* by the Silla master Wǒnhyo 元曉, and [KR6c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0009) *Dàpǐn jīng yìshū* (again Jízàng).

#### The Vajracchedikā (Diamond Sūtra) cluster

The single largest cluster in the division, comprising six translations, an Indic-śāstra layer, and an exegetical tradition running to the end of the Qīng dynasty:

- Six Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) (the canonical liturgical form), Bodhiruci's [KR6c0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0024), Paramārtha's [KR6c0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0026), Dharmagupta's *Jīngāng néngduàn* [KR6c0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0027), Xuánzàng's *Néngduàn jīngāng bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0029) (also embedded as the ninth *huì* of [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001)), and Yijing's *Fóshuō néngduàn jīngāng* [KR6c0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0028).
- Indic Yogācāra-school *śāstra*-tradition: Asaṅga's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn* [KR6c0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0030) (T1510), Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě bōluómì jīng lùn* in Bodhiruci's [KR6c0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0032) (T1511) and Yijing's [KR6c0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0031) translations, and the *Jīngāngxiān lùn* [KR6c0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0033) (T1512). Yijing also translated Vasubandhu's *Lùnshì* and *Lùnsòng* [KR6c0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0034) [KR6c0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0035), and the Mādhyamika-school *Pò qǔzhuó bùhuài jiǎmíng lùn* of Gunada 功德施 survives as [KR6c0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0036).
- Major Suí-Táng commentaries: Zhìyǐ 智顗's *Jīngāng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0037), Jízàng's *Jīngāng bōrě shū* [KR6c0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0038), Kuījī 窺基's *Zànshù* [KR6c0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0039) and *Luèshū* [KR6c0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0044), Tang Xuān-zōng's imperial preface-and-commentary [KR6c0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0100) with Dào-yīn 道氤's *Xuānyǎn* [KR6c0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0105), the Huáyán-school *Zuǎnyào* [KR6c0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0041) of Zōngmì 宗密 with Zǐxuán 子璿's *Kāndìng jì* [KR6c0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0042), and the prosimetric *Fù Dàshì sòng* [KR6c0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0104) traditionally attributed to Fù Xī 傅翕 (the *Liáng* Buddhist layman 497–569).
- A continuous Sòng–Yuán–Míng–Qīng Chinese-commentarial corpus of nearly seventy further works (KR6c0040–KR6c0099, KR6c0116) covering every major school: Tiāntái *cǎiwēi* studies of Zǐxuán-school inheritor Zōngjìng 宗鏡 [KR6c0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0052) [KR6c0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0053), Yuán-era *kēyí* ritual exegesis (the *Xiāoshì Jīngāng jīng kēyí* [KR6c0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0055)), late-Míng philosophical readings by Hānshān Déqīng 憨山德清 [KR6c0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0062), Zēng-fèng 曾鳳儀 [KR6c0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0059), and Zhìxù 智旭 [KR6c0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0067) [KR6c0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0068), and a still-larger Qīng commentary tradition.
- Japanese commentary: Kūkai 空海's *Jīngāng bānruò bōluómì jīng kāití* [KR6c0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0101) — the foundational Shingon reading of the *Vajracchedikā*.

#### The Heart Sūtra (Hṛdaya) cluster

The second great cluster — roughly seventy-five works (KR6c0127–KR6c0201) covering every Chinese translation of the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya* and the major Chinese, Korean, and Japanese commentarial tradition:

- Chinese translations: Kumārajīva's *Móhē bānruò bōluómì dàmíng zhòu jīng* [KR6c0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0127) (T250, the earliest surviving form), Xuánzàng's canonical *Bānruò bōluómìduō xīnjīng* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128) (T251, 649 — the standard liturgical text of East-Asian Buddhism), Dharmacandra 法月's *Pǔbiàn zhìzàng* [KR6c0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0129), Prajñā 般若 and Lìyán 利言's long-recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the Sòng-era expansions by Fǎyuè 法月 (T254 / [KR6c0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0131)), Fǎchéng 法成 (T255 / [KR6c0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0132), translated from Tibetan), and Dānapāla 施護 (T257 / [KR6c0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0136)). Sanskrit-transliterated witnesses survive as [KR6c0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0133) (Bùkōng) and [KR6c0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0134) [KR6c0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0135).
- Major Tang commentaries: Kuījī 窺基's *Yōuzàn* [KR6c0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0137), Wǒnch'ǔk 圓測's *Zàn* [KR6c0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0138), Fǎzàng 法藏's *Lüèshū* [KR6c0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0139), Jìngmài 靖邁's *Shū* [KR6c0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0142), the *Huányuán shù* [KR6c0197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0197) and the *Xiézhù* [KR6c0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0198). Sòng *zhāng-shū* tradition: Shīhù 師護 [KR6c0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0140), Zhīyuán 智圓 [KR6c0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0148) [KR6c0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0150).
- A very large Míng–Qīng commentary stratum (KR6c0151–KR6c0195) representing every late-imperial school: Línjì-Chán, Tiāntái, Cáodòng (Hánshì 圅昰's philosophically substantial *Bōrě xīnjīng lùn* [KR6c0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0184); Yuánxián 元賢, Hónglì 弘麗, Hóngzàn 弘贊's *Tiānzú* and *Guànyì*), and gentry Confucian-Buddhist syncretists.
- Japanese commentary: Kūkai's *Bānruò xīnjīng mìjiàn* [KR6c0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0199) — foundational Shingon Heart-Sūtra reading — with two later sub-commentaries [KR6c0200](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0200) [KR6c0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0201).

#### The Renwáng-jīng (Humane King Sūtra) cluster

- Two translations: T245 [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) (canonically attributed to Kumārajīva but most likely a late-fifth- or sixth-century Chinese composition; see Orzech 1998) and Amoghavajra's revised T246 *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) (765–766) which became the canonical text used in the Tang and Heian *Rénwáng-huì* 仁王會 state-protective ritual programme.
- Principal commentaries: Tiāntái Zhìyǐ 智顗 (recorded by Guàndǐng 灌頂)'s *Hùguó bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0204](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0204) with the Sòng sub-commentary *Shénbǎo jì* [KR6c0205](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0205); Jízàng's *Rénwáng bōrě jīng shū* [KR6c0206](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0206); Wǒnch'ǔk's *Rénwáng jīng shū* [KR6c0207](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0207); and — most consequentially for state Buddhism — Liángbì 良賁's *Rénwáng hùguó bōrě bōluómìduō jīng shū* [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) (composed at Amoghavajra's request shortly after T246 and the canonical Tang esoteric reading of the sūtra). Ming-Qing recensions in [KR6c0209](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0209)–[KR6c0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0215) document the continuing imperial use of the work; Kūkai's *Rénwáng jīng kāití* [KR6c0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0218) is the Shingon counterpart.

#### The Adhyardhaśatikā / Lǐqù-jīng cluster

The *Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā* (the *Lǐqù-jīng* 理趣經) is the only *prajñā* sūtra whose canonical East-Asian reception is straightforwardly Tantric. Four Chinese renderings document its progressive Tantricisation: Bodhiruci II's *Shíxiāng bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0117) (Mahāyāna register), Vajrabodhi 金剛智's *Jīngāngdǐng yújiā lǐqù bānruò jīng* [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) (explicit *Vajraśekhara*-affiliation), Amoghavajra 不空's *Dàlè jīngāng bùkōng zhēnshí sānmóyē jīng* [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120) (the canonical Tang and Japanese *Lǐqù-jīng*, the doctrinal substrate of Shingon practice), and the Sòng *Biànzhào bānruò bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0119). The Sòng *Zuìshàng gēnběn dàlè* expansion is [KR6c0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0125). A small Shingon commentarial cluster — Kūkai's *Lǐqù jīng kāití* [KR6c0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0121) and *Zhēnshí jīng wénjù* [KR6c0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0122), Kakuban-circle *Zhǒngzǐ shì* [KR6c0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0123), the *Dàlè jīng xiǎnyì chāo* [KR6c0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0124) — preserves its Heian-Kamakura reception.

#### Wisdom-Mother (Fómǔ) and short-prajñā Sòng translations

A late-Northern-Sòng cluster (980–1018), produced under imperial patronage by the Indian translators Tiānxīzāi 天息災, Fǎxián 法賢, and especially Dānapāla 施護, brings into the canon the late-Indic Pāla-era *Prajñāpāramitā* short-recension and tantric-prajñā literature: the *Fómǔ chūshēng sānfǎzàng* [KR6c0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0014) (the Sòng *Aṣṭasāhasrikā* recension), the *Fómǔ bǎodézàng* [KR6c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0015) (= *Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā*), the late-Indic *śāstra*-pair [KR6c0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0017) [KR6c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0018) (*Triśatikāyāḥ Prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kārikāsaptati* of Asaṅga / Vasubandhu), the *Jiǔsòng jīngyì lùn* [KR6c0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0016), and a sequence of short Tantric-prajñā texts [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0225](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0225) (the *Yībǎibā míng tuóluóní jīng*, *Liǎoyì jīng*, *Wǔshísòng jīng*, *Dìshì bōrě xīn jīng*, *Xiǎozì bōrě bōluómìduō jīng*, *Guānxiǎng fómǔ púsà jīng*, *Kāijué zìxìng jīng*). Together they document the last continuous wave of Indic *prajñā* literature in Chinese.

#### Late synthetic and Mañjuśrī-related works

- *Wénshūshīlì suǒshuō Móhē bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0020) and *Wénshūshīlì suǒshuō bōrě bōluómì jīng* [KR6c0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0021) — Liáng-era translations of the *Saptaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā*, attaching the *prajñā*-tradition to the Mañjuśrī cult.
- *Dàshèng lǐqù liù bōluómìduō jīng* 大乘理趣六波羅蜜多經 [KR6c0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0226) — Prajñā 般若's late-Táng (788–798) translation of a *prajñā*-frame six-pāramitā synthesis, an important late-Tang doctrinal source.
- *Dà bōrě jīng guānfǎ* [KR6c0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0227), *Dà bōrě jīng gāngyào* [KR6c0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0228), *Dà bōrě guān* [KR6c0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0229) — Sòng and Qīng synthetic / structural guides to T220 [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001), representing the long East-Asian project of making the 600-fascicle *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* navigable.

### Topics

- **Śūnyatā 空 and prajñāpāramitā 般若波羅蜜多.** The division is the canonical home of the Mahāyāna doctrine of universal emptiness — every *dharma* is empty of an intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) — and of the *bodhisattva*-soteriology by which the realisation of emptiness through *prajñā* effects the perfection of all six *pāramitā*s. Every text in the division addresses this doctrine in some register, from the encyclopaedic exposition of the *Dàzhìdù lùn* [KR6c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0005) through the four-corner negation of the *Vajracchedikā* [KR6c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023) to the 260-character compression of the *Heart Sūtra* [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128).
- **Form and emptiness (sè-kōng 色空).** The *Heart Sūtra* formula *sè jí shì kōng, kōng jí shì sè* — "form is itself emptiness, emptiness is itself form" — is the most-cited single sentence in East-Asian Buddhism and the focus of an enormous commentarial debate, with virtually every Heart-Sūtra commentary in KR6c0137–KR6c0201 staking a doctrinal position on the relation between the two terms (Yogācāra *vijñaptimātra*, Sānlùn two-truths, Huáyán *lǐ-shì*, Tiāntái *yī-niàn sān-qiān*, Chán *jiàn-xìng*, Cáodòng *substance-function*).
- **The relation of sūtra to śāstra.** The presence in the division of the Indic *śāstra*-stratum — Nāgārjuna's *Dàzhìdù lùn*, Asaṅga's and Vasubandhu's *Jīngāng bōrě lùn*-cluster — sets up a perennial East-Asian exegetical question about the proper relation between *prajñā*-sūtra and Mādhyamika or Yogācāra *śāstra*-commentary. Sānlùn 三論, Fǎxiàng 法相, and Huáyán 華嚴 commentaries each take a distinctive position; the disagreement runs through the Tang and recurs in Sòng-Míng.
- **Vinayana of the bodhisattva-path.** The *Dàzhìdù lùn* in particular provides the most extensive surviving Indic-source account of the *bodhisattva* career — six *pāramitā*s, ten *bhūmis*, the *anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi* — and is the textual base for medieval Chinese *bodhisattva*-doctrine.
- **State Buddhism.** The *Rénwáng-jīng* [KR6c0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0202) [KR6c0203](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0203) is one of the three royal state-protective scriptures (with the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* and the *Mahāmāyūrī*) and the canonical text of an enormous Tang-Heian-Kamakura state-Buddhist political theology, with Liángbì's [KR6c0208](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0208) as its principal scholastic commentary.
- **Tantricisation of the prajñā tradition.** The progressive Tantric reinterpretation of the *Adhyardhaśatikā* through Vajrabodhi [KR6c0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0118) and Amoghavajra [KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120), the embedding of *dhāraṇī* within the Heart Sūtra in Prajñā's recension [KR6c0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0130), and the late-Indic Sòng cluster [KR6c0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0219)–[KR6c0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0224) together document the gradual incorporation of *prajñā* into the Indic and East-Asian Tantric programme. The Heian Shingon reception (Kūkai's commentaries) gives this tradition its definitive East-Asian articulation.
- **The Mahāprajñāpāramitā as canonical reference work.** The 600-fascicle *Dàbōrě bōluómìduō jīng* [KR6c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001) sits at the centre of the division as a single integrated witness to the Indic *prajñā*-corpus, but its sheer scale generates a continuing problem of accessibility: how does one read 600 fascicles? The Sòng-Qīng synthetic guides [KR6c0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0227) [KR6c0228](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0228) [KR6c0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0229) are the formal record of the East-Asian project of making the great sūtra usable.

# 經疏部 (T34)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 13 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6d 法華部 *Fǎhuá bù* — Buddhist Canon — Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Lotus) Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/): 13 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6d 法華部 *Fǎhuá bù* — Buddhist Canon — Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Lotus) Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6d` corresponds to the *Fǎhuá bù* 法華部 of the Taishō structural ordering — the Lotus Sūtra and its satellite scriptures in Taishō volume 9, the Lotus sub-commentary tradition in Taishō volumes 26 and 33–34, the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal-and-meditation corpus in Taishō volume 46, the Lotus Dūnhuáng 敦煌 fragments in volume 85, and the very large Sòng–Qīng manuscript continuation of all these strands preserved in the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. In Wilkinson's outline of the Taishō (§29.5.8), volume 9 is identified as "*Fǎhuá bù* (Lotus and other Mahāyāna sūtras)"; Kanripo's `KR6d` extends that vol. 9 nucleus outward to absorb all Chinese-language Lotus commentary and the entire Tiāntái scholastic apparatus that grows out of it, because in East-Asian classification the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal tradition — including its meditation manuals, doctrinal-classification literature, and ritual / *chànyí* 懺儀 works — is canonically attached to the Lotus Sūtra rather than treated as an independent *zōng* 宗 section.

The principal scholarly tradition organising the division is therefore Tiāntái, whose founder Zhìyǐ 智顗 (538–597) was traditionally regarded as the patriarch and whose 593–597 lectures at Yùquánsì 玉泉寺, redacted by Guàndǐng 灌頂 (561–632), produced the *Tiāntái sāndàbù* 天台三大部 ("Three Great Treatises of Tiāntái") — *Fǎhuá xuányì* [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006), *Fǎhuá wénjù* [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014), and *Móhē zhǐguān* [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) — around which most of the division is structured (Wilkinson §29.5.7.1 on Tiāntái; Hurvitz 1963 on Zhìyǐ; Lopez 2016 and Teiser & Stone 2009 on the Lotus Sūtra). Pre-Tiāntái Liáng exegesis (Fǎyún 法雲), the early Suí Sānlùn 三論 reading by Jízàng 吉藏, and the Táng Faxiang 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 reading by Kuījī 窺基 are also represented; from the 8th century onward the division is dominated by Zhànrán 湛然 (711–782) and his Sòng-period successors of the Tiāntái revival, and from the 11th century by the long *shānjiā* / *shānwài* 山家／山外 controversy and its literature. The division extends through Yuán, Míng (with the Tiāntái revival under Zhìxù 智旭 1599–1655), and Qīng (under Língyào 靈耀 and Tōnglǐ 通理) to roughly the mid-18th century.

### Important texts and text clusters

The 249 per-text notes in `kb/KR6d/` organise into five recognisable clusters.

#### The Lotus Sūtra itself and its parallel translations

- *Zhèng fǎhuá jīng* 正法華經 [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002) — Dharmarakṣa's 竺法護 translation of 286 CE, the earliest complete Chinese Lotus, surviving in 10 *juan*.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001) — Kumārajīva's 鳩摩羅什 translation of 406 CE, the dominant East-Asian recension in 7 *juan* and 28 chapters; the literary base for virtually all subsequent Lotus exegesis in Chinese.
- *Tiānpǐn miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 添品妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003) — the Suí (601) collation by Jñānagupta 闍那崛多 and Dharmagupta 笈多, incorporating the *Devadatta* chapter and the *Pǔmén pǐn* 普門品 verses.
- *Sàtán fēntuólì jīng* 薩曇分陀利經 [KR6d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0004) — a Western Jìn anonymous partial translation of the *Devadatta* episode, preserving a textual stratum independent of the three full versions.

#### Satellite Lotus-cycle sūtras (vol. 9)

- *Wúliàng yì jīng* 無量義經 [KR6d0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0118) — the Liáng-period "Sūtra of Innumerable Meanings," traditionally the prologue of the East-Asian "Threefold Lotus" 法華三部經.
- *Fóshuō Guān Pǔxián púsà xíngfǎ jīng* 佛說觀普賢菩薩行法經 [KR6d0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0120) — the Liú-Sòng-period "Sūtra of the Contemplation of Samantabhadra's Practice," the epilogue of the same triad.
- *Fóshuō fǎhuá sānmèi jīng* 佛說法華三昧經 [KR6d0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0108), *Bùtuìzhuǎn fǎlún jīng* 不退轉法輪經 [KR6d0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0106), *Dà fǎgǔ jīng* 大法鼓經 [KR6d0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0109), *Dà sàzhē Nígānzǐ suǒshuō jīng* 大薩遮尼乾子所說經 [KR6d0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0111) — Mahāyāna sūtras grouped with the Lotus on doctrinal and thematic grounds (one-vehicle teaching, irreversibility, the Tathāgata's hidden lifespan).

#### The *Tiāntái sāndàbù* 天台三大部 and their commentaries

- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuányì* 妙法蓮華經玄義 [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006) — Zhìyǐ's 593 Yùquánsì lectures on the doctrinal meaning of the Lotus, recorded by Guàndǐng; the foundational systematic theology of Tiāntái, source for the *wǔshí bājiào* 五時八教 classification.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng wénjù* 妙法蓮華經文句 [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014) — Zhìyǐ's 587 phrase-by-phrase commentary on Kumārajīva's Lotus, recorded by Guàndǐng; pairs with the *Xuányì* as the doctrinal-plus-textual exegetical core.
- *Móhē zhǐguān* 摩訶止觀 [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) — Zhìyǐ's 594 lectures on Tiāntái meditation, recorded by Guàndǐng; the most systematic *śamatha-vipaśyanā* manual in Chinese, organised on the *shíjìng × shíchéng* 十境十乘 matrix.
- *Fǎhuá xuányì shìqiān* 法華玄義釋籤 [KR6d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0007), *Fǎhuá wénjù jì* 法華文句記 [KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015), and *Zhǐguān fǔxíng zhuànhóngjué* 止觀輔行傳弘決 [KR6d0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0131) — Zhànrán's 湛然 (711–782) standard sub-commentaries on each member of the *sāndàbù*; the principal textual base of the Sòng Tiāntái revival.

#### Alternative Lotus-commentary traditions

- *Fǎhuá jīng yìjì* 法華經義記 [KR6d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0005) — Fǎyún's 法雲 Liáng-period exegesis, the principal southern pre-Tiāntái reading and the polemical target of Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì*.
- *Fǎhuá xuánlùn* 法華玄論 [KR6d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0023), *Fǎhuá yìshū* 法華義疏 [KR6d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0024), *Fǎhuá yóuyì* 法華遊意 [KR6d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0025) — Jízàng's 吉藏 (549–623) Sānlùn 三論-school readings, doctrinally distinct from Tiāntái.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuánzàn* 妙法蓮華經玄贊 [KR6d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0026) — Kuījī's 窺基 (632–682) Cí'ēn 慈恩 / Yogācāra reading of the Lotus, the principal Faxiang interpretation.
- *Fǎhuá zōngyào* 法華宗要 [KR6d0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0032) — the Sillan master Wǒnhyo's 元曉 short doctrinal synthesis, an important East-Asian non-Chinese voice.

#### Tiāntái doctrinal, meditation, and ritual literature (vol. 46)

- *Sìjiào yì* 四教義 [KR6d0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0166) and *Tiāntái sìjiào yí* 天台四教儀 [KR6d0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0168) — Zhìyǐ's and the late-Táng / Korean Chégwan 諦觀's expositions of the four doctrinal teachings, the most-studied Tiāntái catechetical works.
- *Shí bùèr mén* 十不二門 [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and the very large body of commentary it provoked (e.g. *Shí bùèr mén zhǐyào chāo* [KR6d0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0158) by Zhīlǐ 知禮) — Zhànrán's 10-fold non-duality scheme, the textual flashpoint of the *shānjiā / shānwài* controversy.
- *Jīngāngbēi* 金剛錍 [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175) — Zhànrán's polemical defense of *wúqíng yǒu xìng* 無情有性 (Buddha-nature in insentient things), generative of a sub-commentary tradition into the Sòng.
- *Fǎhuá sānmèi chànyí* 法華三昧懺儀 [KR6d0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0191) and the related *chànyí* / *xíngfǎ* corpus — Zhìyǐ's Lotus-Samādhi liturgy and its Sòng elaborations (Zūnshì 遵式, Zhīlǐ 知禮), the principal Tiāntái ritual texts.
- *Sìmíng zūnzhě jiàoxíng lù* 四明尊者教行錄 [KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186) — Zōngxiǎo's 宗曉 collected works of Zhīlǐ, the textual monument of the Sòng *shānjiā* school.
- *Jiàoguān gāngzōng* 教觀綱宗 [KR6d0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0188) — Zhìxù's 智旭 (1599–1655) Míng-period summary of Tiāntái doctrine, the principal late-imperial textbook.

### Important persons

- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) — translator of the standard Lotus recension (T262 = [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001)); the literary register of his translation supplied the canonical Sinitic vocabulary of all subsequent Lotus exegesis in this division.
- [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) — translator of the earliest complete Chinese Lotus (T263 = [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002), 286) and of several satellite vol. 9 sūtras; his Lotus survives as the principal philological witness independent of Kumārajīva.
- [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) — co-translator with Dharmagupta 笈多 of the Suí Lotus recension (T264 = [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003), 601), source of the textual additions to the received Kumārajīva Lotus.

### Topics

- **The ekayāna 一乘 doctrine and *kāiquán xiǎnshí* 開權顯實.** The proclamation in chapters 2–9 of the Lotus that the *śrāvaka* / *pratyekabuddha* / *bodhisattva* three vehicles are provisional (*quán* 權) and the Buddha-vehicle alone is real (*shí* 實) is the central scriptural commitment around which the entire Tiāntái doctrinal apparatus is built, and almost every Sinitic Lotus exegete from Fǎyún onward addresses its hermeneutic status.
- **The *jìmén* / *běnmén* 跡門／本門 division.** The split of the Lotus into a "trace-gate" (chapters 1–14) and an "origin-gate" (15–28) is associated with Dàoxuān's preface to Kumārajīva ([KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001)) and given systematic articulation in Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì* [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006); it remains the standard Sinitic exegetical schema through the entire division.
- **The *wǔshí bājiào* 五時八教 classification.** Zhìyǐ's chronological-and-modal organisation of the Buddha's *kerygma* into five periods (*Huāyán*, *Lùyuàn / Āhán*, *Fāngděng*, *Bōrě*, *Fǎhuá-Nièpán*) and eight modes is developed in the *Xuányì*, summarised in [KR6d0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0166) and [KR6d0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0167), and given canonical compact form in Chégwan's *Tiāntái sìjiào yí* [KR6d0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0168); it is the basic doctrinal-classification apparatus of the division.
- **Tiāntái meditation: *yīxīn sānguān* 一心三觀, *yīniàn sānqiān* 一念三千, *zhǐguān bùèr* 止觀不二.** Articulated principally in the *Móhē zhǐguān* [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) and its commentaries; the most systematic Mahāyāna meditation theory in Chinese, organised on the *shíjìng × shíchéng* 十境十乘 matrix.
- **The *shānjiā / shānwài* 山家／山外 controversy.** The 11th-century Sòng-period split between Zhīlǐ's [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) "mountain-house" *shānjiā* — defending the Tiāntái doctrine of evil in the Buddha-nature (*xìng-è* 性惡) and Guàndǐng's role in the early canon — and the *shānwài* counter-position of Yuánqīng 源清, Zhìyuán 智圓, and (later) Rényuè 仁岳, particularly over the interpretation of Zhànrán's *Shí bùèr mén* [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and the status of Guàndǐng's *Guānyīn xuányì* commentary [KR6d0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0046). The dispute generated the large mid-Sòng polemical literature visible in [KR6d0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0184)–[KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186) and [KR6d0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0220)–[KR6d0235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0235).
- **Buddha-nature in the insentient (*wúqíng yǒu xìng* 無情有性).** Zhànrán's claim in the *Jīngāngbēi* [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175) that even insentient things possess Buddha-nature; the Tiāntái counter-position to the Chán and Huāyán readings on the same question, generating the *Jīngāngbēi*-commentary sub-tradition ([KR6d0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0176)–[KR6d0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0181)).
- **The Lotus liturgy: *Fǎhuá sānmèi* 法華三昧 and the *chànyí* tradition.** Zhìyǐ's Lotus-Samādhi practice from the *Móhē zhǐguān* and the *Fǎhuá sānmèi chànyí* [KR6d0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0191) is the textual base for a Sòng-period ritual literature, principally elaborated by Zūnshì and Zhīlǐ, that fed back into ordinary monastic and lay practice and shaped the late-imperial Tiāntái devotional landscape.
- **The Guānyīn 觀音 sub-cult.** The detachment of the *Pǔmén pǐn* 普門品 (Lotus chapter 25) as an independent devotional unit, with its own commentarial corpus ([KR6d0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0046)–[KR6d0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0057)) — Zhìyǐ's *Guānyīn xuányì* and *yìshū* and their Sòng / Míng / Qīng commentaries — is one of the principal vehicles by which the Lotus's textual presence extended into popular ritual practice.
- **Japanese Lotus reception: Tendai 天台 and Shingon 真言 readings.** The Heian-period esoteric / *mìjiào* interpretations of the Lotus by Kūkai 空海 ([KR6d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0036)–[KR6d0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0044)) and the early Japanese Tendai materials (e.g. [KR6d0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0220)) constitute a distinct Lotus reading transmitted within the same division.
- **The Míng–Qīng Tiāntái revival.** Zhìxù's [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) 17th-century systematisation, the Qīng-period Tiāntái commentaries by Língyào, Tōnglǐ, and others ([KR6d0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0084)–[KR6d0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0098), [KR6d0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0142)), and the late-imperial *Sìjiào yí* sub-commentaries ([KR6d0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0169)–[KR6d0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0174)) constitute the final phase of pre-modern Lotus scholarship represented in the division.

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6e gathers the Chinese-language literature of the *Huáyánjīng* 華嚴經 / *Buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra* tradition: the three full Chinese translations of the sūtra, the early Hàn-through-Jìn partial translations and parallel texts (兜沙經, 菩薩本業經, 漸備一切智德經 etc.), the *Daśabhūmika* and *Gaṇḍavyūha* clusters that circulated independently, the foundational śāstras of Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and Vasubandhu 天親, the writings of the Táng "five patriarchs" (Dùshùn 杜順, Zhìyǎn 智儼, Fǎzàng 法藏, Chéngguān 澄觀, Zōngmì 宗密) and of the parallel layman-exegete Lǐ Tōngxuán 李通玄, the Sillan Huāǒm 華嚴 contributions of Wǒnhyo 元曉 and Ǔisang 義湘, the Northern-Sòng "restoration" centred on Jìngyuán 淨源 and the Liáo-Sòng *Wǔjiào zhāng* subcommentarial tradition, and the Yuán-Míng-Qīng synthetic and ritual works that close the corpus. The division spans roughly seventeen centuries, from Lokakṣema's 支婁迦讖 *Dōushā jīng* in the Later Hàn (c. 178–189) to Péng Jìqīng's 彭際清 *Huáyán niànfó sānmèi lùn* (c. 1770–1796).

In Taishō organisation, the heart of the corpus is the *Huáyánbù* 華嚴部, running from T277 to T309. KR6e is broader than that division: it pulls in the *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā* 十住毘婆沙論 and the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra* 十地經論 from the Taishō treatise sections (T1521, T1522), Fǎzàng's and Chéngguān's exegetical works from the *Jīngshūbù* 經疏部 (T1731–T1740), the patriarchal essays from the *Zhūzōngbù* 諸宗部 (T1866–T1899), and Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng material from the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. The Kanripo grouping thus reflects sectarian rather than strictly bibliographic logic: it is the textual archive of the Huáyán *school* (Huáyánzōng 華嚴宗, also known as Xiánshǒuzōng 賢首宗 after Fǎzàng's posthumous title) read as a continuous tradition.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The three full translations of the *Huáyánjīng***.
  - *Liùshí Huáyán* 六十華嚴, [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001) — Buddhabhadra 佛馱跋陀羅's sixty-fascicle rendering completed at Yángzhōu in 418–420; the base text for Dùshùn, Zhìyǎn, Wǒnhyo and the early Huáyán synthesis.
  - *Bāshí Huáyán* 八十華嚴, [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010) — Śikṣānanda 實叉難陀's eighty-fascicle "new translation" of 695–699, sponsored by Wǔ Zétiān 武則天; supersedes the Liùshí Huáyán in Táng and later exegesis and is the version Fǎzàng (after revision), Chéngguān, and Lǐ Tōngxuán comment on.
  - *Sìshí Huáyán* 四十華嚴, [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) — Prajñā 般若's forty-fascicle translation of 796–798, which renders only the *Gaṇḍavyūha* 入法界品 but adds the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* / Pǔxián xíngyuàn 普賢行願 hymn that became the principal Huáyán liturgical text.
- **Early partial and parallel translations**. [KR6e0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0028) 兜沙經 (Lokakṣema, c. 178–189) is the oldest extant Chinese fragment of the corpus; [KR6e0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0029) 菩薩本業經 (Zhī Qiān 支謙, 222–253), [KR6e0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0030) 諸菩薩求佛本業經 (Niè Dàozhēn 聶道真), and [KR6e0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0031) 菩薩十住行道品 / [KR6e0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0032) 佛說菩薩十住經 form the Hàn-through-Jìn pre-history of the *Huáyán*'s reception in China.
- **The *Daśabhūmika* / 十地 cluster**. [KR6e0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0033) 漸備一切智德經 (Zhú Fǎhù 竺法護, 297), [KR6e0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0034) 十住經 (Kumārajīva 鳩摩羅什, c. 405), and [KR6e0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0035) 佛說十地經 (Śīladharma 尸羅達摩, 789–798) translate the same sūtra at three points; together with [KR6e0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0059) 十住毘婆沙論 (Nāgārjuna 龍樹 / Kumārajīva tr.) and [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060) 十地經論 (Vasubandhu / Bodhiruci 菩提流支, 508–511), they constitute the Indian doctrinal core that anchored the Northern Wèi Dìlùn 地論 school and through it the later Huáyán synthesis.
- **The *Gaṇḍavyūha* / 入法界品 cluster**. [KR6e0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0043) 羅摩伽經 (Shèngjiān 聖堅), [KR6e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0044) 大方廣佛華嚴經入法界品 (Divākara 地婆訶羅), and the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) all transmit Sudhana's 善財 pilgrimage; this cluster underlies [KR6e0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0115) 文殊指南圖讚 (Wéibái 惟白) and the standard iconographic programme of the fifty-three teachers.
- **Tathāgata-realm sūtras** (Wǔ-Zhōu-era expansions of the corpus). [KR6e0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0049) 不思議佛境界分, [KR6e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0050) 大方廣如來不思議境界經, [KR6e0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0052) 佛華嚴入如來德智不思議境界經, and [KR6e0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0053) 大方廣入如來智德不思議經 round out the Avataṃsaka literary horizon as it was received in early Táng.
- **The Táng patriarchal corpus**. Zhìyǎn's *Sōuxuán jì* 搜玄記 [KR6e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0003) and *Wǔshí yào wèndá* [KR6e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0083); Fǎzàng's *Tànxuán jì* 探玄記 [KR6e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0004), *Wénjì gāngmù* [KR6e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0005), the *Wǔjiào zhāng* 五教章 (Huáyán yīchéng jiàoyì fēnqí zhāng) [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074), the *Zhǐguī* [KR6e0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0085), *Yìhǎi bǎimén* [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089), *Wàngjìn huányuán guān* [KR6e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0090) and the *Jīnshīzǐ zhāng* 金獅子章 commentarial tradition [KR6e0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0097)–[KR6e0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0098); Chéngguān's massive *Dàshū* [KR6e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0011) and *Yǎnyìchāo* [KR6e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0012) together with the *Fǎjiè xuánjìng* [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and *Sānshèng yuánróng guānmén* [KR6e0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0099); and Zōngmì's *Zhù Fǎjiè guānmén* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) and *Yuánrén lùn* 原人論 [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105), the latter widely read as the school's most concise doctrinal statement.
- **Lǐ Tōngxuán's parallel tradition**. The *Xīn Huáyán jīng lùn* 新華嚴經論 [KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022), the *Juéyí lùn* [KR6e0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0024) and *Shímíng lùn* [KR6e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0112), later edited together with the sūtra as the *Huáyánjīng hélùn* 華嚴經合論 [KR6e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0066), offered an alternative reading of the *Bāshí Huáyán* outside the patriarchal lineage and exerted strong influence on Sòng Chán reception.
- **Sillan Huāǒm**. Wǒnhyo 元曉's surviving *Huáyán jīng shū* fascicle [KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009), Ǔisang 義湘's *Yīchéng fǎjiè tú* 一乘法界圖 [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109) with its later anthology [KR6e0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0110), Pyowǒn 表員's *Wényì yàojué wèndá* [KR6e0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0121), Gyǒndǔng 見登之's *Yīchéng chéngfó miàoyì* [KR6e0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0114) and Myǒnghyo 明皛's *Hǎiyìn sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0113) are the principal Korean contributions retained in the Chinese canon.
- **The *Wǔjiào zhāng* subcommentarial tradition**. Dàotíng 道亭's *Yìyuàn shū* [KR6e0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0075), Shīhuì 師會's *Fénxīn* [KR6e0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0076) and *Fùgǔ jì* [KR6e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0078), and Xīdí 希迪's *Jíchéng jì* [KR6e0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0079) and *Píngfùgǔjì* [KR6e0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0080) form the Sòng debate over Fǎzàng's foundational five-teachings classification.
- **Sòng-Liáo-Yuán exegesis**. Jìngyuán 淨源's *Huányuánguān kē* [KR6e0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0091) and related ritual reconstructions of the school in the Northern Sòng; the Liáo monk Xiānyǎn 鮮演's *Tánxuán juézé* [KR6e0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0119); the Yuán *Xuántán huìxuán jì* [KR6e0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0120) of Pǔruì 普瑞; Jièhuán 戒環's *Yàojiě* [KR6e0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0122) and Dàotōng 道通's *Tūnhǎi jí* [KR6e0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0123).
- **Late synthesis (Míng-Qīng)**. Chéngguān's *Gāngyào* (with Míng reorganisation) [KR6e0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0124), Xùfǎ 續法's *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí* [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) and *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí kāiméng* [KR6e0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0143) codifying the Qīng-dynasty school curriculum, and Péng Jìqīng 彭際清's lay-Buddhist *Yīchéng juéyí lùn* [KR6e0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0147) and *Huáyán niànfó sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) integrating Huáyán with Pure-Land practice.
- **Ritual and contemplative material**. The *Fǎjiè guānmén* 法界觀門 attributed to Dùshùn (preserved only via [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101)), [KR6e0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0081) 華嚴五教止觀, [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082) 華嚴一乘十玄門 (whose authenticity as Dùshùn's own work is contested), and the great repentance and offering manuals — [KR6e0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0149) 海印道場九會請佛儀, [KR6e0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0150) 海印道場懺儀, [KR6e0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0152)–[KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153) 普賢行願修證儀, and Zōngmì's [KR6e0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0155) 圓覺經道場修證儀 — establish Huáyán as a practice-tradition, not only an exegetical one.

### Important persons

- [佛馱跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%A6%B1%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Buddhabhadra, 359–429) — translator of the *Liùshí Huáyán* [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001) and of the early *Wénshū shīlì fāyuàn jīng* [KR6e0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0045); the figure through whom the *Avataṃsaka* first entered Chinese in its full form.
- [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) (Śikṣānanda, 652–710) — Khotanese monk recruited by Wǔ Zétiān to retranslate the sūtra; produced the *Bāshí Huáyán* [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010) and the parallel inconceivable-realm sūtras [KR6e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0050), [KR6e0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0053), [KR6e0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0047).
- [般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) (Prajñā, 744–810) — Kashmiri translator of the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) at the request of Emperor Dézōng 德宗; brought the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* into the corpus.
- [杜順](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E9%A0%86) (Dùshùn, 557–640) — traditional first patriarch; lifetime work survives only in attributions ([KR6e0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0081), [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082), [KR6e0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0160)) and through Chéngguān and Zōngmì's transmission of the *Fǎjiè guānmén* in [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100)–[KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101).
- [智儼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%84%BC) (Zhìyǎn, 602–668) — second patriarch; in the *Sōuxuán jì* [KR6e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0003) and the *Kǒngmù zhāng* [KR6e0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0084) he organised the *Liùshí Huáyán* into the analytical framework Fǎzàng would inherit.
- [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) (Fǎzàng, 643–712) — third patriarch and the systematiser of the school; sixteen distinct works in the division, anchoring the doctrinal core in the *Wǔjiào zhāng* [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074) and the meditative-metaphysical core in the *Wàngjìn huányuán guān* [KR6e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0090) and *Yìhǎi bǎimén* [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089).
- [澄觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BE%84%E8%A7%80) (Chéngguān, 738–839) — fourth patriarch; author of the largest single body of writing in the division (seventeen works), centred on the *Dàshū* and *Yǎnyìchāo* commentaries on the *Bāshí Huáyán* [KR6e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0011)–[KR6e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0012). The exegetical horizon of every later author rests on his work.
- [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) (Zōngmì, 780–841) — fifth patriarch and the bridge to Chán; his *Yuánrén lùn* [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105) is the most widely read short Huáyán text outside the school proper.
- [李通玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%80%9A%E7%8E%84) (Lǐ Tōngxuán, 645–740) — Táng layman; his *Xīn Huáyán jīng lùn* [KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022) and successor works developed a reading of the *Bāshí Huáyán* organised around the Wǔtáishān cosmology and the Sudhana pilgrimage, parallel and partly counter to the patriarchal tradition.
- [元曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E6%9B%89) (Wǒnhyo, 617–686) — Sillan exegete; his *Huáyán jīng shū* [KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009) survives only in fragments but is the earliest extant Korean Huáyán commentary.
- [義湘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B9%98) (Ǔisang, 625–702) — Sillan founder of Huāǒm; the *Yīchéng fǎjiè tú* [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109) is one of the school's iconic short doctrinal works.
- [慧苑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E8%8B%91) (Huìyuàn, fl. early 8th c.) — Fǎzàng's disciple; the *Xù-Huáyán-jīng lüèshū kāndìng jì* [KR6e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0065) reorganised his master's commentarial scheme on the new translation and was sharply contested in later transmission.
- [淨源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B7%A8%E6%BA%90) (Jìngyuán, 1011–1088) — the Northern-Sòng "restorer of the Huáyán teaching" (中興教主); a cluster of his works ([KR6e0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0091), [KR6e0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0092), [KR6e0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0152), [KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153), [KR6e0156](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0156), [KR6e0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0157)) reassembled the school's curriculum after the loss of major Táng texts.
- [師會](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B8%AB%E6%9C%83) (Shīhuì, fl. mid-12th c.) — central voice in the Sòng *Wǔjiào zhāng* debate; [KR6e0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0076)–[KR6e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0078) defend Fǎzàng's text against Huìyuàn's emendations and frame the later orthodox reading.
- [續法](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BA%8C%E6%B3%95) (Xùfǎ, 1641–1728) — Qīng compiler and self-styled twenty-eighth Huáyán patriarch; his *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí* [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) became the standard pedagogical entry into the school.
- [彭際清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E9%9A%9B%E6%B8%85) (Péng Jìqīng / Péng Shàoshēng 彭紹昇, 1740–1796) — Qing lay scholar; his integration of Huáyán with Pure-Land practice in [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) marks the final major intellectual moment of the corpus.

### Topics

- **The classification of teachings (*pànjiào* 判教)**. The school's signature project is the ranking of all Buddhist teachings into the *Wǔjiào* 五教 (Hīnayāna 小乘 / Elementary Mahāyāna 大乘始 / Final Mahāyāna 大乘終 / Sudden 頓 / Perfect 圓) and *Shízōng* 十宗 schemes laid out in Fǎzàng's *Wǔjiào zhāng* [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074). The contested Sòng-era reception of that text ([KR6e0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0075)–[KR6e0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0080)) and Xùfǎ's Qīng codification [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) map the boundaries of school orthodoxy across a millennium.
- **The Dharma-realm (*fǎjiè* 法界) and its four divisions**. Dùshùn's *Fǎjiè guānmén* — surviving only in Chéngguān's *Xuánjìng* [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and Zōngmì's *Zhù* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) — articulates the canonical fourfold scheme (*shìfǎjiè* 事法界 / *lǐfǎjiè* 理法界 / *lǐshì wúài fǎjiè* 理事無礙法界 / *shìshì wúài fǎjiè* 事事無礙法界). This is the doctrinal kernel from which all later Huáyán metaphysics is unfolded.
- **The Ten Mysterious Gates (*shíxuánmén* 十玄門) and the Six Marks (*liùxiàng* 六相)**. The cosmological apparatus that converts *fǎjiè* doctrine into the school's signature mereology of mutual interpenetration; older redaction in [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082), systematised by Zhìyǎn ([KR6e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0083), [KR6e0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0084)) and given its definitive form by Fǎzàng (notably in [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074) and [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089)).
- **The *Daśabhūmika* and the legacy of the Dìlùn school**. Vasubandhu's *Shídì jīng lùn* [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060), translated in the Northern Wèi, was the doctrinal core of the Dìlùn 地論 school and a direct ancestor of Huáyán; the school's debates over *ālayavijñāna* and the relation of the *tathāgatagarbha* to the bodhisattva path enter Huáyán through Zhìyǎn's reading of [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060) together with [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001).
- **Patriarchal lineage versus layman exegesis**. The five-patriarch line (Dùshùn → Zhìyǎn → Fǎzàng → Chéngguān → Zōngmì) is itself a Sòng-era retrospective construction; the parallel and historically prior reading of Lǐ Tōngxuán ([KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022), [KR6e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0066), [KR6e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0112)) provides a check on its self-presentation and exerted independent influence on Chán.
- **Cross-cultural transmission**. The Sillan contributions ([KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009), [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109), [KR6e0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0110), [KR6e0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0113), [KR6e0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0114), [KR6e0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0121)) — produced under and after the Korean monks who studied with Zhìyǎn and Fǎzàng — and the Khotanese, Kashmiri, and Sogdian translators ([KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001), [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010), [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041), [KR6e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0044), [KR6e0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0046)) make the *Huáyán* the most internationally produced corpus in the Chinese canon outside the Vinaya.
- **Huáyán as Chán and as Pure Land**. Zōngmì's *Yuánrén lùn* [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105) and *Zhù Fǎjiè guānmén* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) frame Huáyán doctrine for a Chán readership; Péng Jìqīng's *Niànfó sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) reframes it for a Pure-Land one. These two ends of the doctrinal afterlife are essential to reading Sòng-Qīng intellectual history.
- **The *Pǔxián xíngyuàn* 普賢行願 cult**. The hymn appended to the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) generated its own commentarial micro-corpus ([KR6e0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0069), [KR6e0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0070), [KR6e0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0071), [KR6e0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0072), [KR6e0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0073)) and the ritual structures of [KR6e0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0149)–[KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153); the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* is the daily liturgical text of East Asian Mahāyāna and originates here.
- **Pseudepigrapha and apocrypha**. Several works ascribed to Dùshùn (notably [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082)) are now thought to be Zhìyǎn's or later; the *Xíngyuàn pǐn biéxíng shūchāo* [KR6e0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0073) survives only in selection. Authenticity is a live problem across the early-Táng layer.
