### Important texts and text clusters

- *Yúqié shī dì lùn* 瑜伽師地論 [KR6n0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0001) — Xuánzàng's 646–648 translation of the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* in 100 *juǎn*; the encyclopaedic root text of the entire division, conventionally attributed to Maitreya 彌勒菩薩 but in fact a multi-author stratified compilation of the Asaṅga circle. The exegetical aid *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* 瑜伽師地論釋 [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002) of Jinaputra 最勝子 accompanies it.
- *Chéng wéishí lùn* 成唯識論 [KR6n0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0016) — Xuánzàng and Kuījī's 659 redaction of the ten Indian *Triṃśikā*-bhāṣyas around Dharmapāla's reading; the doctrinal charter of the Cí'ēn school. The commentarial pyramid stacked over it — Kuījī's *Shùjì* 述記 [KR6n0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0026), *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào* 掌中樞要 [KR6n0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0029), Huìzhāo's *Liǎoyì dēng* 了義燈 [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030), Zhìzhōu's *Yǎnmì* 演祕 [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032), and Taehyŏn's 太賢 *Xuéjì* 學記 [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041) — defines Táng-period Fǎxiàng orthodoxy.
- *Wéishí sānshí lùn sòng* 唯識三十論頌 [KR6n0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0022) and *Wéishí èrshí lùn* 唯識二十論 [KR6n0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0055) — Vasubandhu's *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā*, translated by Xuánzàng in 648 and 661; the textual nucleus around which both Indian and Chinese consciousness-only argumentation organises itself. Paramārtha's earlier renderings as *Zhuǎn shí lùn* 轉識論 [KR6n0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0024), *Wéishí lùn* 唯識論 [KR6n0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0053), and *Dàshèng wéishí lùn* 大乘唯識論 [KR6n0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0054) preserve the Old-Yogācāra reception.
- The *Shè dàshèng lùn* 攝大乘論 cluster — Asaṅga's *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, surviving in three Chinese translations (Buddhaśānta 531–534 [KR6n0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0058), Paramārtha 563–564 [KR6n0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0059), Xuánzàng 648–649 [KR6n0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0060)) plus the *Bhāṣya* in three further versions [KR6n0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0061) [KR6n0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0063) [KR6n0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0064) [KR6n0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0065) and a thicket of Sui–Táng commentaries and Dūnhuáng *zhāng* fragments [KR6n0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0066)–[KR6n0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0070). The cluster is the principal vehicle by which the *ālayavijñāna* doctrine enters China, and the Paramārtha line generates the Shèlùn 攝論 lineage that the Cí'ēn school then displaces.
- The *Madhyāntavibhāga* cluster — Paramārtha's *Zhōngbiān fēnbié lùn* 中邊分別論 [KR6n0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0071) and Xuánzàng's *Biàn zhōngbiān lùn* 辯中邊論 [KR6n0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0072) plus its verse [KR6n0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0073) and Kuījī's *Shùjì* [KR6n0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0075); with the closely related *Shíbā kōng lùn* 十八空論 [KR6n0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0074) and *Sān wúxìng lùn* 三無性論 [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) of the Paramārtha corpus.
- *Dàshèng zhuāngyán jīng lùn* 大乘莊嚴經論 [KR6n0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0080) — the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* with Vasubandhu-circle commentary, Prabhākaramitra 630–633; together with *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn* 顯揚聖教論 [KR6n0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0077), Asaṅga's digest of the *Yogācārabhūmi* in Xuánzàng's 645–646 rendering.
- *Dàshèng āpídámó jí lùn* 大乘阿毘達磨集論 [KR6n0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0081) and its expanded *Zájí lùn* 雜集論 [KR6n0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0082) — Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya* and Sthiramati's bhāṣya; the Yogācāra abhidharma proper. Read in China together with the *Dàshèng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘五蘊論 [KR6n0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0094), the *Guǎng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘廣五蘊論 [KR6n0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0095), and the *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn* 大乘百法明門論 [KR6n0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0096) of Vasubandhu, the four works form the standard East Asian curriculum in Yogācāra dharma-taxonomy.
- The tathāgatagarbha-Yogācāra hybrids — *Fóxìng lùn* 佛性論 [KR6n0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0087), the *Ratnagotravibhāga* (*Jiūjìng yīshèng bǎoxìng lùn* 究竟一乘寶性論) [KR6n0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0088), and the two recensions of *Dàshèng fǎjiè wú chābié lùn* 大乘法界無差別論 [KR6n0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0089) [KR6n0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0090) — bridge the division to the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q and were a central battleground in the East Asian one-vehicle / five-natures controversy.
- The *Ālambanaparīkṣā* cluster — Dignāga's *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* 觀所緣緣論 [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) with Dharmapāla's commentary [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113), and a late-Míng wave of revival commentaries [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117) — anchors the epistemological side of the division.
- The Cí'ēn doctrinal compendia — Kuījī's *Dàshèng fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* 大乘法苑義林章 [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), Huìzhāo's *Quànfā pútí xīn jí* 勸發菩提心集 [KR6n0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0127) and *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* 能顯中邊慧日論 [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128), Zhìzhōu's *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* 大乘入道次第 [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129) — codify the Cí'ēn school's doctrinal positions, including the five-gotras doctrine and the polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk's 圓測 readings.
- The *Bā shí guījǔ* 八識規矩 cluster ([KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131)–[KR6n0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0140)) — Xuánzàng's (apocryphally attributed) verses on the eight consciousnesses, with Putai's 普泰 1530s Yuán-Míng-transition commentary [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) and a dense Wànlì-Chongzhen-era stratum from Mingyu 明昱, Zhixu 智旭, Deqing 德清, and others. These short verse cycles, together with the *Xiàngzōng bā yào* 相宗八要 anthology [KR6n0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0143)–[KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145), are the late-Míng Fǎxiàng revival's basic curriculum and the principal channel by which Cí'ēn doctrine survives into the Qīng.
- *Dàshèng yìzhāng* 大乘義章 [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) — Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn's 慧遠 580–592 doctrinal encyclopaedia: not a pure Yogācāra work, but a Sui-era Shèlùn-tradition synthesis included here because it remains the most systematic pre-Xuánzàng treatment of the Yogācāra dharma-list in Chinese.

### Important persons

- [彌勒菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%8C%E5%8B%92%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) — the traditional speaker of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and the so-called Maitreya corpus (*Madhyāntavibhāga*, *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra*, etc.); historicity disputed in modern scholarship, but the canonical attribution shapes every East Asian reading of the division.
- [無著菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%84%A1%E8%91%97%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Asaṅga, c. 4th c.) — author of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, the *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn*, and the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*; the architect of the systematic Yogācāra in this division.
- [世親菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%96%E8%A6%AA%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Vasubandhu, c. 4th–5th c.; also rendered 天親菩薩) — author of the *Triṃśikā*, *Viṃśatikā*, *Pañcaskandhaka*, *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn*, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, and *Dàshèng chéngyè lùn* [KR6n0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0086); the most heavily commented author in the division.
- [安慧菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E6%85%A7%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Sthiramati, 6th c.) — author of the *Abhidharmasamuccaya-vyākhyā* underlying T1606 and of the *Madhyāntavibhāga-ṭīkā* underlying parts of T1599; the principal "Old-Yogācāra" exegete reaching China through Paramārtha.
- [護法菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%B7%E6%B3%95%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dharmapāla, c. 530–561) — Nālandā commentator whose reading of the *Triṃśikā* is the spine of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* and whose *Ālambanaparīkṣā-vṛtti* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113) founds the Cí'ēn epistemological tradition.
- [陳那菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%82%A3%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dignāga, c. 480–540) — author of *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and, by implication, of the epistemological reorientation that drives the *Ālambanaparīkṣā* and *Buddhabhūmi-vyākhyāna* portions of the corpus.
- [親光菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%AA%E5%85%89%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Bandhuprabha) — credited author of the *Buddhabhūmi-śāstra* materials underlying the *Chéng wéishí lùn* synthesis.
- [最勝子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%80%E5%8B%9D%E5%AD%90) (Jinaputra) — Indian compiler of *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002), the canonical exegetical key to the *Yogācārabhūmi*.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha, 499–569) — translator of the bulk of the Old-Yogācāra layer (T1584, T1587, T1589, T1593, T1595, T1599, T1610, T1616–1620); the rival transmissional lineage that the Xuánzàng school later partly supersedes.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — translator of the New-Yogācāra core (T1579, T1585, T1586, T1590, T1594, T1597, T1600–1606, T1612, T1614 and many others); the single most important figure for the division and the founder of its Chinese school.

- [通潤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%9A%E6%BD%A4) (Tōngrùn, 1565–1624) — Yúfēng 玉峯 master; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn jíjiě* [KR6n0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0044) and one of the leading Fǎxiàng-revivalist preachers of the Wànlì–Tianqi period.

- [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) (Hānshān Déqīng, 1546–1623) — one of the "four great masters of the late Míng"; his *Bā shí guījǔ tōngshuō* [KR6n0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0135) gives the eight-consciousnesses schema its Chán-inflected late-Míng reading.

### Topics

- **Vijñaptimātra / cittamātra** (唯識 *wéishí*). The thesis that what appears as an external object is a transformation of consciousness; argued textually through Vasubandhu's *Viṃśatikā* and *Triṃśikā* and exegetically through the entire *Chéng wéishí lùn* commentarial pyramid.
- **The eight consciousnesses** (八識 *bā shí*), with particular attention to the *ālayavijñāna* (阿賴耶識) as substrate and *kliṣṭamanas* (染汚意) as the sixth-to-seventh-consciousness link. Paramārtha's idiosyncratic positing of a ninth, *amalavijñāna* 阿摩羅識, is one of the principal Old-Yogācāra peculiarities. The *Bā shí guījǔ* tradition turns the eight-consciousness schema into a Ming pedagogical genre.
- **The three natures** (三性 *sān xìng*, *trisvabhāva*): *parikalpita* (遍計所執), *paratantra* (依他起), *pariniṣpanna* (圓成實). The cross-cutting **three non-natures** (三無性) doctrine is foregrounded in Paramārtha's *Sān wúxìng lùn* [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) and is the principal hermeneutic key for reconciling the Yogācāra ontology with the Prajñāpāramitā emptiness teaching.
- **Five gotras / five natures** (五姓各別 *wǔxìng gèbié*). The Yogācārabhūmi taxonomy of five fixed spiritual lineages, against which Wǒnch'ǔk and the East Asian one-vehicle traditions argue. The Cí'ēn defence of the five-gotras position is the principal polemical thread of Huìzhāo's *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- **The Hundred Dharmas** (百法 *bǎifǎ*). Vasubandhu's 5-category × 100-item taxonomy of dharmas (T1614); becomes the standard East Asian Buddhist abhidharmic primer and generates a long commentarial chain from Kuījī's *Dàshèng bǎifǎ míngmén lùn shū* [KR6n0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0098) through the Dūnhuáng *Kāizōng yìjì* [KR6n0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0107) to the Wànlì-era revivalist commentaries [KR6n0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0103)–[KR6n0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0106).
- **Stages of the Yoga practitioner** (瑜伽師地 *yúqié shī dì*) — the seventeen-bhūmi structure of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, organising the entire division.
- **Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha synthesis**. T1610 *Fóxìng lùn*, T1611 *Bǎoxìng lùn*, T1626–1627 *Fǎjiè wú chābié lùn*, and T1612 *Wǔyùn lùn* sit at the seam between Yogācāra and the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q; the question of whether the *tathāgatagarbha* is reducible to the *ālayavijñāna* shapes both the Old-Yogācāra reception in China and the *Awakening of Faith* tradition.
- **Epistemology of perception (所緣緣)**. Through Dignāga's *Ālambanaparīkṣā* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and its commentaries, the question of what constitutes a valid object of perception becomes a Yogācāra theme; it is taken up again in the Wànlì–early Qīng commentary wave of [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117).
- **Old- vs. New-Yogācāra** (舊譯 *jiùyì* / 新譯 *xīnyì*). The Paramārtha-line readings of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* and *Triṃśikā* differ systematically from Xuánzàng's: on *amalavijñāna*, on the status of the *paratantra*, and on the relation between *vāsanā* and the *ālaya*. The division as a whole preserves both layers in parallel — the cataloguing principle is doctrinal subject matter, not translatorial school.
- **Cí'ēn school polemics**. Internal to the Táng layer: Kuījī vs. Wǒnch'ǔk on the reading of T1585; Huìzhāo's continuation of that polemic; Zhìzhōu's consolidation. These polemics define the canonical shape of the Fǎxiàng curriculum.
- **East Asian transmission and revival**. The division is the textual basis for three successive scholastic traditions: Táng Cí'ēn (mid-7th to early 8th c., centred at Cháng'ān, with Silla and Goguryeo participation), Heian–Kamakura Hossō (Vols. 65–70 of the Taishō, c. 800–1500), and late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng revival (c. 1530–1660, *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 46–55).

# 論疏部 (T44)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 17 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6o 論集部 *Lùnjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Treatise Collection](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/): 12 texts (71%)
- [KR6n 瑜伽部 *Yújiā bù* — Yogācāra works](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/): 5 texts (29%)

## Division note: [KR6o 論集部 *Lùnjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Treatise Collection](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6o corresponds to the *Lùnjí bù* 論集部 of the Taishō canon (vol. 32, nos. 1628–1692), together with the commentarial overflow in vol. 44 (nos. 1839–1850) and a small group of Dūnhuáng-recovered manuscripts in vol. 85 (nos. 2813–2816). The division is the canon's general miscellany of doctrinal treatises (*lùn* 論, śāstra) and the verse-collections (*sòng* 頌, *zàn* 讚, *gāthā* 伽他) attached to them. Unlike the dedicated divisions for Mādhyamaka and Yogācāra commentary on specific sūtras (`KR6m` 釋經論部, `KR6n` 毘曇部, 瑜伽部), KR6o gathers freestanding śāstras that do not belong to a single school or sūtra-commentary lineage: hetuvidyā (yīnmíng 因明) logic, Madhyamaka and Sautrāntika doctrinal works, the *Satyasiddhi-śāstra* of the 成實宗 school, *pratītyasamutpāda* tracts, *bodhicitta* literature, the *Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda* (*Awakening of Faith*) corpus, the Sino-Buddhist *Milindapañha* (*Nā xiān bǐqiū jīng*), and an extensive stotra/*gāthā* section. 

Chronologically the division spans c. 150 CE (the Indian source-strata of treatises by Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva, Dignāga) through 1911 (a late-Qīng vernacular gloss on *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn*), with the densest layers in (i) the fifth-/sixth-century translation projects of Kumārajīva, Paramārtha and Bodhiruci, (ii) the Táng Xuánzàng–Yìjìng era, (iii) the Northern Sòng translation bureau under Tiānxīsāi 天息災, Dānapāla 施護 and Dharmadeva 法天 (c. 982–1000), and (iv) the Heian–Kamakura and late-Míng waves of native East-Asian commentary on *yīnmíng* and *Qǐxìnlùn*. The principal transmissional issue throughout is the apocryphal or pseudepigraphic status of several of its most influential texts — *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn*, *Shì móhēyǎn lùn*, *Zhāng suǒzhī lùn*, the Sino-Tibetan-Mongol *Bāsībā* tract — for which East-Asian and modern scholarship has reached very different conclusions.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **Yīnmíng 因明 (Buddhist logic) cluster** — *Yīnmíng zhènglǐmén lùn běn* 因明正理門論本 [KR6o0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0001) (Dignāga 大域龍, tr. Xuánzàng), *Yīnmíng rù zhènglǐ lùn* 因明入正理論 [KR6o0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0003) (Śaṅkarasvāmin 商羯羅主, tr. Xuánzàng), and a parallel re-translation by Yìjìng [KR6o0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0002) form the doctrinal core of East-Asian Buddhist logic; the commentarial chain runs through Shéntài 神泰 [KR6o0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0007), Kuījī 窺基's *Yīnmíng dàshū* 因明大疏 [KR6o0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0008), Wǒnhyo's *Pànbǐliàng lùn* 判比量論 [KR6o0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0034), the Heian *Yīnmíng lùnshū míngdēng chāo* 因明論疏明燈抄 [KR6o0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0009) of Zenju 善珠, and the Edo *Yīnmíng dàshū róngguàn chāo* [KR6o0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0011) of Hōtan 鳳潭.
- **Nāgārjuna's logical-Madhyamaka treatises** — *Huízhèng lùn* 迴諍論 [KR6o0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0004) (*Vigrahavyāvartanī*), *Fāngbiàn xīn lùn* 方便心論 [KR6o0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0005) (*Upāyahṛdaya*), and *Rúshí lùn* 如實論 [KR6o0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0006) (*Tarkaśāstra*, tr. Paramārtha) preserve the earliest layer of Indian Buddhist epistemology.
- **Satyasiddhi-śāstra** — *Chéngshí lùn* 成實論 [KR6o0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0050) (Harivarman 訶梨跋摩, tr. Kumārajīva 411–412); the foundational text of the short-lived Chinese 成實宗 school and a major bridge between Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma and emerging Mahāyāna.
- **Doctrinal tracts of the Paramārtha and Bodhiruci circles** — *Suíxiāng lùn* 隨相論 [KR6o0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0045), *Sìdì lùn* 四諦論 [KR6o0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0051), *Lìshì āpítán lùn* 立世阿毘曇論 [KR6o0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0048), *Shíèr yīnyuán lùn* 十二因緣論 [KR6o0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0055), *Típó púsà pò lèngqié jīng zhōng wàidào xiǎochéng sìzōng lùn* 提婆菩薩破楞伽經中外道小乘四宗論 [KR6o0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0043) and its companion 涅槃論 [KR6o0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0044); together they constitute the sixth-century North Indian doxographic and ontological strata in Chinese translation.
- **Bodhicitta cluster** — Centred on the *Pútí xíng jīng* 菩提行經 [KR6o0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0067) (Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatāra* in Tiānxīzāi's Sòng-period rendering), with *Pútí zīliáng lùn* 菩提資糧論 [KR6o0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0065), *Guǎng shì pútíxīn lùn* 廣釋菩提心論 [KR6o0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0069), and the Vajrayāna *Jīngāngdǐng yújiā zhōng fā ānòuduōluó sānmiǎo sānpútí xīn lùn* 金剛頂瑜伽中發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心論 [KR6o0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0070) (attr. Nāgārjuna, tr. Amoghavajra 不空), which became the principal *bodhicitta* text of Shingon and attracted a dense Heian–Kamakura commentarial layer ([KR6o0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0071)–[KR6o0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0075)).
- **Awakening of Faith corpus** — *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn* 大乘起信論 attr. Aśvaghoṣa 馬鳴菩薩, in the Paramārtha [KR6o0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0078) and Śikṣānanda 實叉難陀 [KR6o0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0079) recensions; the single most consequential text of the division and arguably of East-Asian Buddhism, generating an enormous commentarial tradition represented here by Huìyuǎn 慧遠 of Jìngyǐng [KR6o0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0100), Wǒnhyo 元曉 [KR6o0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0103)/[KR6o0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0104), Fǎzàng 法藏 [KR6o0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0105)/[KR6o0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0106), Zǐxuán 子璿 [KR6o0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0107), Taehyŏn 太賢 [KR6o0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0108), Zhìxù 智旭 [KR6o0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0109), and late-Míng/Qīng glosses [KR6o0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0114)–[KR6o0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0120); plus the Dūnhuáng-recovered Tánkuàng 曇曠 layer [KR6o0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0121)/[KR6o0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0122) and an anonymous *Qǐxìnlùn zhù* [KR6o0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0123) preserved as T2814.

### Important persons

- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) — translator of *Chéngshí lùn* (411–412); single most influential Latter-Qín translator represented in the division.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha) — chief translator of the sixth-century South Indian doctrinal layer: *Rúshí lùn*, *Suíxiāng lùn*, *Sìdì lùn*, *Lìshì āpítán lùn*, *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn* (KR6o0078), *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn*.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) — translator of the *yīnmíng* core (Dignāga's *Nyāyamukha*, Śaṅkarasvāmin's *Nyāyapraveśa*) and of doctrinal compendia (*Yuánshēng lùn*, *Pútí zīliáng lùn*), founder of the East-Asian *yīnmíng* tradition.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) — re-translator of the *Nyāyamukha* [KR6o0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0002), the *Suhṛllekha* [KR6o0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0129), the *Bǎo xíng wáng zhèng lùn* [KR6o0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0061), and of several treatises (*Shǒuzhàng lùn* [KR6o0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0062), *Zhǐguān mén lùn sòng* [KR6o0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0060)) reflecting late-seventh-century Indian doctrinal style.

### Topics

- **Buddhist logic (yīnmíng 因明 / hetuvidyā)** — the structure of the three-membered syllogism (三支比量), the analysis of the nine reasons (九句因) and the four kinds of pseudo-reason (四相違), the boundary between perception (現量) and inference (比量); a topic that runs from Dignāga's *Nyāyamukha* [KR6o0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0001) through Kuījī's *Dàshū* [KR6o0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0008) and the Japanese *Sìxiāngwéi* sub-commentaries [KR6o0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0014)–[KR6o0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0017) to late-Míng synthetic restatements [KR6o0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0026)–[KR6o0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0029).
- **The status of the *Awakening of Faith* and the *Shì móhēyǎn lùn*** — whether they are translations of lost Indian originals or East-Asian (Chinese, Korean, or possibly Central-Asian) compositions; the textual history of the doubled *Qǐxìnlùn* translation under Paramārtha and Śikṣānanda; the philological independence (or not) of the *Shì móhēyǎn lùn* from the *Qǐxìnlùn* itself. This is the principal modern philological debate in the division.
- **Pseudepigraphy and translator-attribution forgery** — *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn* and *Shì móhēyǎn lùn* travel in the canon under unverifiable translator names (Paramārtha, Vṛddhimati 筏提摩多), allowing comparison of the formal traits by which East-Asian apocrypha were inserted into a canon of putative Indian śāstras.
- **The *bodhicitta* tradition's bifurcation** — between the exoteric, ethical reading represented by Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatāra* [KR6o0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0067) and the esoteric, ritual reading represented by the Vajraśekhara *Pútíxīn lùn* [KR6o0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0070); the latter's commentarial chain in Heian Japan is the densest sub-cluster in the division.
- **The 成實宗 question** — whether Harivarman's *Chéngshí lùn* belongs to Sautrāntika, to a transitional position between Sthaviravāda and Mahāyāna, or constitutes an independent doctrinal lineage; the disappearance of the Chinese 成實宗 school in the early Táng.
- **The fivefold Pratītyasamutpāda corpus** — five short treatises ([KR6o0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0055)–[KR6o0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0059)) translating overlapping Indian materials on dependent origination, of unusual value for comparative study because they preserve parallel Chinese renderings of related Sanskrit verse-cores.
- **The transmission of Buddhist verse genres into Chinese** — how *gāthā* / *stotra* / *sòng* forms were rendered, including the three-translation problem of Nāgārjuna's *Suhṛllekha* [KR6o0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0127)–[KR6o0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0129) and the metrical conventions of the Sòng translation bureau ([KR6o0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0130)–[KR6o0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0143)).
- **The Dūnhuáng *Qǐxìnlùn* layer** — the unique witness of Tánkuàng's mid-eighth-century *Qǐxìnlùn* lectures preserved only at Dunhuang (T2813–T2814 = [KR6o0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0121)/[KR6o0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0122)/[KR6o0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0123)), evidence for a North-West-Chinese reading tradition independent of the central Táng commentaries.

## Division note (scope only): [KR6n 瑜伽部 *Yújiā bù* — Yogācāra works](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6n collects the Chinese canon's holdings for the Yogācāra (瑜伽 *yújiā*) doctrinal stream — the abhidharmic-idealist tradition that descends from the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* and the works of Asaṅga 無著菩薩 and Vasubandhu 世親菩薩 in fourth- and fifth-century North India, and that becomes the East Asian Fǎxiàng 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 school after Xuánzàng 玄奘 reimports it in the mid-seventh century. The doctrinal core is established by the CANWWW Taishō *Yújiā bù* (`div30`, Taishō Vol. 30–31, Nos. 1579–1627): the *Yogācārabhūmi* and its summaries, the *Madhyāntavibhāga* and *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* of the so-called Maitreya corpus, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* of Asaṅga, the *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā* of Vasubandhu, the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the *Ratnagotravibhāga*, the Hundred-Dharmas list, Dignāga's 陳那菩薩 *Ālambanaparīkṣā*, and the Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha hybrids preserved at T1610–1611 and T1626–1627.

The division as catalogued in Kanripo, however, extends well beyond the Taishō *Yújiā bù* proper: it folds in the Cí'ēn-school commentarial canon of Vols. 42–45 (Kuījī's 窺基 *Chéng wéishí lùn shùjì* and *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng*; Huìzhāo 慧沼 and Zhìzhōu 智周 sub-commentaries), the late-Táng to Wǔdài Dūnhuáng Yogācāra fragments of Taishō Vol. 85, the Japanese Hossō 法相 scholastic apparatus of Vols. 65–70, and a sizeable late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng-revival corpus in *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 39 and 46–55. Three transmissional layers must therefore be kept distinct when reading the division: the **Old-Yogācāra** layer of Paramārtha 真諦 (c. 546–569), which is closer to a Valabhī recension and preserves the *trisvabhāva* and *amalavijñāna* in idiosyncratic form; the **New-Yogācāra** layer of Xuánzàng (646–664), based on Nālandā materials and Dharmapāla's 護法菩薩 reading; and the **East Asian scholastic** layer (Táng Cí'ēn school, Korean Hyŏnyu monks at Cháng'ān, Heian/Kamakura Hossō, Ming Cíbēi-Cí'ēn revivalists), in which the imported Indian texts become objects of an autonomous and very long-lived commentarial industry. The chronological span runs from c. 414 (Dharmakṣema's 曇無讖 *Bodhisattvabhūmi* [KR6n0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0003)) to the late seventeenth century (Ouyi Zhixu's 智旭 *Xiàngzōng bā yào zhíjiě* [KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145)) — roughly twelve centuries of continuous Yogācāra scholasticism in Chinese.

## Division note (scope only): [KR6e 華嚴部類 *Huáyán bùlèi* — Buddhist Canon — Huáyán (Avataṃsaka) Corpus](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6e gathers the Chinese-language literature of the *Huáyánjīng* 華嚴經 / *Buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra* tradition: the three full Chinese translations of the sūtra, the early Hàn-through-Jìn partial translations and parallel texts (兜沙經, 菩薩本業經, 漸備一切智德經 etc.), the *Daśabhūmika* and *Gaṇḍavyūha* clusters that circulated independently, the foundational śāstras of Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and Vasubandhu 天親, the writings of the Táng "five patriarchs" (Dùshùn 杜順, Zhìyǎn 智儼, Fǎzàng 法藏, Chéngguān 澄觀, Zōngmì 宗密) and of the parallel layman-exegete Lǐ Tōngxuán 李通玄, the Sillan Huāǒm 華嚴 contributions of Wǒnhyo 元曉 and Ǔisang 義湘, the Northern-Sòng "restoration" centred on Jìngyuán 淨源 and the Liáo-Sòng *Wǔjiào zhāng* subcommentarial tradition, and the Yuán-Míng-Qīng synthetic and ritual works that close the corpus. The division spans roughly seventeen centuries, from Lokakṣema's 支婁迦讖 *Dōushā jīng* in the Later Hàn (c. 178–189) to Péng Jìqīng's 彭際清 *Huáyán niànfó sānmèi lùn* (c. 1770–1796).

In Taishō organisation, the heart of the corpus is the *Huáyánbù* 華嚴部, running from T277 to T309. KR6e is broader than that division: it pulls in the *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā* 十住毘婆沙論 and the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra* 十地經論 from the Taishō treatise sections (T1521, T1522), Fǎzàng's and Chéngguān's exegetical works from the *Jīngshūbù* 經疏部 (T1731–T1740), the patriarchal essays from the *Zhūzōngbù* 諸宗部 (T1866–T1899), and Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng material from the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. The Kanripo grouping thus reflects sectarian rather than strictly bibliographic logic: it is the textual archive of the Huáyán *school* (Huáyánzōng 華嚴宗, also known as Xiánshǒuzōng 賢首宗 after Fǎzàng's posthumous title) read as a continuous tradition.

## Division note (scope only): [KR6k 律部 *Lǜ bù* — Buddhist canon — Vinaya (monastic discipline)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6k` 律部 (*Lǜ bù*, "Vinaya section") is the Kanripo mirror of the Vinaya division of the Chinese Buddhist canon — the canonical *Vinaya-piṭaka* together with its Indic and East-Asian exegetical and ritual-procedural literature. In CANWWW  the material is distributed across three divisions: `div13` 律部 holds the Vinayas proper and their *prātimokṣa-*, *karman-* and *paripṛcchā-*satellites (T22 No. 1421 — T24 No. 1504); `div14` 律疏部 holds the principal Suí–Tang exegetical layer (T40 Nos. 1804–1815, plus T45 Nos. 1892–1910); `div27` 續律疏部 holds the later Sòng–Míng–Qīng Chinese sub-commentaries together with the Japanese scholastic apparatus. Kanripo `KR6k` integrates these three CANWWW divisions and supplements them with a large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial tail, so that 263 works are catalogued here in total — roughly the same order of magnitude as the *Prajñāpāramitā* division [KR6c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/) but with a quite different shape: where the *Bōrě bù* is anchored by a small handful of recurrently retranslated Indic sūtras, the Vinaya division is anchored by five Indic disciplinary corpora belonging to five different *nikāya* schools, all surviving only in their Chinese form, together with a much larger East-Asian scholastic and ritual-procedural superstructure.

The corpus falls into six historically and doctrinally distinct strata. (1) The **early-fifth-century translation wave** (404–431) at Chángān and Jiànyè brought into Chinese the full disciplinary literature of four Indic *nikāya* schools — the *Shísòng lǜ* 十誦律 of the Sarvāstivāda, the *Sìfēn lǜ* 四分律 of the Dharmaguptaka, the *Móhēsēngqí lǜ* 摩訶僧祇律 of the Mahāsāṃghika, and the *Wǔfēn lǜ* 五分律 of the Mahīśāsaka — together with supplementary texts of the Kāśyapīya and Sammitīya. The Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas survive in no other language, so this stratum is the principal evidentiary base for *all* modern comparative-Vinaya scholarship (Clarke 2015; *cf.* Wilkinson §29.5.7.6). (2) The **Tang *Sìfēnlǜ* scholastic synthesis** at Chángān (620–697) saw the *Sìfēn lǜ* gradually displace the *Shísòng lǜ* as the practical Vinaya of Chinese monasticism, under three competing exegetical schools — Fǎlì's 法礪 ([法礪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%A4%AA)) Xiāngbù 相部, Dàoxuān's 道宣 ([道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3)) Nánshān 南山, and Huáisù's 懷素 ([懷素](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E7%B4%A0)) Dōngtǎ 東塔 — of which the Nánshān school's victory under the imperial decree of Dàizōng (777) made Dàoxuān's *San dàbù* 三大部 the canonical Chinese Vinaya curriculum thereafter. (3) The **Yìjìng Mūlasarvāstivāda programme** (700–714) translated the disciplinary corpus of the late-Indic Mūlasarvāstivāda — by then the dominant Vinaya school of Indian Buddhism and (still later) the canonical Vinaya of the Tibetan, Mongolian, and Bhutanese traditions — into Chinese as a single eighteen-text *vastu*-by-*vastu* programme, but this Vinaya never displaced the *Sìfēn* in Chinese practice. (4) The **Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* stream** is anchored by the apocryphal *Fànwǎng jīng* 梵網經 ([KR6k0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0076), attributed to Kumārajīva but Chinese in origin) and runs in parallel to the school-Vinaya tradition, generating its own large commentarial corpus (Zhìyǐ 智顗, Fǎzàng 法藏, Wǒnhyo 元曉, Tàixián 太賢, Yúnqī Zhūhóng 雲棲袾宏, Ǒuyì Zhìxù 蕅益智旭); the alternative *Yogācāra*-school *bodhisattva-precepts* (Maitreya / Asaṅga, translated by Dharmakṣema and re-translated by Xuánzàng) provided the Mahāyāna stream with a second textual base. (5) The **Sòng *Língzhī*-school revival** (Yǔnkān 允堪 1005–1061; Yuánzhào 元照 1048–1116; Shǒuyī 守一 / Miàolián 妙蓮 in the Southern Sòng) produced an extensive sub-commentarial apparatus on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù*, recovered the doctrine of the precept-body (戒體 *jiètǐ*), and re-anchored Vinaya practice in the Tiāntái doctrinal system. (6) The **late-Míng / Qīng Vinaya revival** (Yúnqī Zhūhóng, Zhìxù, Dúté 讀體 1601–1679 at Bǎohuáshān 寶華山, Hóngzàn 弘贊 1611–1685 at Dǐnghú-shān 鼎湖山, the *Sānfēng* line of Fǎzàng 法藏 1573–1635) re-standardised Chinese ordination practice through the new *sāntán* 三壇 (three-platform) ordination system, generated the daily-use Vinaya manual that has remained in use to the present (*Píní rìyòng qièyào* [KR6k0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0224)), and produced the most thorough Qīng-period commentaries on every layer of the disciplinary tradition.

## Division note: [KR6d 法華部 *Fǎhuá bù* — Buddhist Canon — Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Lotus) Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6d` corresponds to the *Fǎhuá bù* 法華部 of the Taishō structural ordering — the Lotus Sūtra and its satellite scriptures in Taishō volume 9, the Lotus sub-commentary tradition in Taishō volumes 26 and 33–34, the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal-and-meditation corpus in Taishō volume 46, the Lotus Dūnhuáng 敦煌 fragments in volume 85, and the very large Sòng–Qīng manuscript continuation of all these strands preserved in the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. In Wilkinson's outline of the Taishō (§29.5.8), volume 9 is identified as "*Fǎhuá bù* (Lotus and other Mahāyāna sūtras)"; Kanripo's `KR6d` extends that vol. 9 nucleus outward to absorb all Chinese-language Lotus commentary and the entire Tiāntái scholastic apparatus that grows out of it, because in East-Asian classification the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal tradition — including its meditation manuals, doctrinal-classification literature, and ritual / *chànyí* 懺儀 works — is canonically attached to the Lotus Sūtra rather than treated as an independent *zōng* 宗 section.

The principal scholarly tradition organising the division is therefore Tiāntái, whose founder Zhìyǐ 智顗 (538–597) was traditionally regarded as the patriarch and whose 593–597 lectures at Yùquánsì 玉泉寺, redacted by Guàndǐng 灌頂 (561–632), produced the *Tiāntái sāndàbù* 天台三大部 ("Three Great Treatises of Tiāntái") — *Fǎhuá xuányì* [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006), *Fǎhuá wénjù* [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014), and *Móhē zhǐguān* [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) — around which most of the division is structured (Wilkinson §29.5.7.1 on Tiāntái; Hurvitz 1963 on Zhìyǐ; Lopez 2016 and Teiser & Stone 2009 on the Lotus Sūtra). Pre-Tiāntái Liáng exegesis (Fǎyún 法雲), the early Suí Sānlùn 三論 reading by Jízàng 吉藏, and the Táng Faxiang 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 reading by Kuījī 窺基 are also represented; from the 8th century onward the division is dominated by Zhànrán 湛然 (711–782) and his Sòng-period successors of the Tiāntái revival, and from the 11th century by the long *shānjiā* / *shānwài* 山家／山外 controversy and its literature. The division extends through Yuán, Míng (with the Tiāntái revival under Zhìxù 智旭 1599–1655), and Qīng (under Língyào 靈耀 and Tōnglǐ 通理) to roughly the mid-18th century.

### Important texts and text clusters

The 249 per-text notes in `kb/KR6d/` organise into five recognisable clusters.

#### The Lotus Sūtra itself and its parallel translations

- *Zhèng fǎhuá jīng* 正法華經 [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002) — Dharmarakṣa's 竺法護 translation of 286 CE, the earliest complete Chinese Lotus, surviving in 10 *juan*.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001) — Kumārajīva's 鳩摩羅什 translation of 406 CE, the dominant East-Asian recension in 7 *juan* and 28 chapters; the literary base for virtually all subsequent Lotus exegesis in Chinese.
- *Tiānpǐn miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 添品妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003) — the Suí (601) collation by Jñānagupta 闍那崛多 and Dharmagupta 笈多, incorporating the *Devadatta* chapter and the *Pǔmén pǐn* 普門品 verses.
- *Sàtán fēntuólì jīng* 薩曇分陀利經 [KR6d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0004) — a Western Jìn anonymous partial translation of the *Devadatta* episode, preserving a textual stratum independent of the three full versions.

#### Satellite Lotus-cycle sūtras (vol. 9)

- *Wúliàng yì jīng* 無量義經 [KR6d0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0118) — the Liáng-period "Sūtra of Innumerable Meanings," traditionally the prologue of the East-Asian "Threefold Lotus" 法華三部經.
- *Fóshuō Guān Pǔxián púsà xíngfǎ jīng* 佛說觀普賢菩薩行法經 [KR6d0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0120) — the Liú-Sòng-period "Sūtra of the Contemplation of Samantabhadra's Practice," the epilogue of the same triad.
- *Fóshuō fǎhuá sānmèi jīng* 佛說法華三昧經 [KR6d0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0108), *Bùtuìzhuǎn fǎlún jīng* 不退轉法輪經 [KR6d0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0106), *Dà fǎgǔ jīng* 大法鼓經 [KR6d0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0109), *Dà sàzhē Nígānzǐ suǒshuō jīng* 大薩遮尼乾子所說經 [KR6d0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0111) — Mahāyāna sūtras grouped with the Lotus on doctrinal and thematic grounds (one-vehicle teaching, irreversibility, the Tathāgata's hidden lifespan).

#### The *Tiāntái sāndàbù* 天台三大部 and their commentaries

- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuányì* 妙法蓮華經玄義 [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006) — Zhìyǐ's 593 Yùquánsì lectures on the doctrinal meaning of the Lotus, recorded by Guàndǐng; the foundational systematic theology of Tiāntái, source for the *wǔshí bājiào* 五時八教 classification.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng wénjù* 妙法蓮華經文句 [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014) — Zhìyǐ's 587 phrase-by-phrase commentary on Kumārajīva's Lotus, recorded by Guàndǐng; pairs with the *Xuányì* as the doctrinal-plus-textual exegetical core.
- *Móhē zhǐguān* 摩訶止觀 [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) — Zhìyǐ's 594 lectures on Tiāntái meditation, recorded by Guàndǐng; the most systematic *śamatha-vipaśyanā* manual in Chinese, organised on the *shíjìng × shíchéng* 十境十乘 matrix.
- *Fǎhuá xuányì shìqiān* 法華玄義釋籤 [KR6d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0007), *Fǎhuá wénjù jì* 法華文句記 [KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015), and *Zhǐguān fǔxíng zhuànhóngjué* 止觀輔行傳弘決 [KR6d0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0131) — Zhànrán's 湛然 (711–782) standard sub-commentaries on each member of the *sāndàbù*; the principal textual base of the Sòng Tiāntái revival.

#### Alternative Lotus-commentary traditions

- *Fǎhuá jīng yìjì* 法華經義記 [KR6d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0005) — Fǎyún's 法雲 Liáng-period exegesis, the principal southern pre-Tiāntái reading and the polemical target of Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì*.
- *Fǎhuá xuánlùn* 法華玄論 [KR6d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0023), *Fǎhuá yìshū* 法華義疏 [KR6d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0024), *Fǎhuá yóuyì* 法華遊意 [KR6d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0025) — Jízàng's 吉藏 (549–623) Sānlùn 三論-school readings, doctrinally distinct from Tiāntái.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuánzàn* 妙法蓮華經玄贊 [KR6d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0026) — Kuījī's 窺基 (632–682) Cí'ēn 慈恩 / Yogācāra reading of the Lotus, the principal Faxiang interpretation.
- *Fǎhuá zōngyào* 法華宗要 [KR6d0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0032) — the Sillan master Wǒnhyo's 元曉 short doctrinal synthesis, an important East-Asian non-Chinese voice.

#### Tiāntái doctrinal, meditation, and ritual literature (vol. 46)

- *Sìjiào yì* 四教義 [KR6d0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0166) and *Tiāntái sìjiào yí* 天台四教儀 [KR6d0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0168) — Zhìyǐ's and the late-Táng / Korean Chégwan 諦觀's expositions of the four doctrinal teachings, the most-studied Tiāntái catechetical works.
- *Shí bùèr mén* 十不二門 [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and the very large body of commentary it provoked (e.g. *Shí bùèr mén zhǐyào chāo* [KR6d0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0158) by Zhīlǐ 知禮) — Zhànrán's 10-fold non-duality scheme, the textual flashpoint of the *shānjiā / shānwài* controversy.
- *Jīngāngbēi* 金剛錍 [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175) — Zhànrán's polemical defense of *wúqíng yǒu xìng* 無情有性 (Buddha-nature in insentient things), generative of a sub-commentary tradition into the Sòng.
- *Fǎhuá sānmèi chànyí* 法華三昧懺儀 [KR6d0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0191) and the related *chànyí* / *xíngfǎ* corpus — Zhìyǐ's Lotus-Samādhi liturgy and its Sòng elaborations (Zūnshì 遵式, Zhīlǐ 知禮), the principal Tiāntái ritual texts.
- *Sìmíng zūnzhě jiàoxíng lù* 四明尊者教行錄 [KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186) — Zōngxiǎo's 宗曉 collected works of Zhīlǐ, the textual monument of the Sòng *shānjiā* school.
- *Jiàoguān gāngzōng* 教觀綱宗 [KR6d0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0188) — Zhìxù's 智旭 (1599–1655) Míng-period summary of Tiāntái doctrine, the principal late-imperial textbook.

### Important persons

- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) — translator of the standard Lotus recension (T262 = [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001)); the literary register of his translation supplied the canonical Sinitic vocabulary of all subsequent Lotus exegesis in this division.
- [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) — translator of the earliest complete Chinese Lotus (T263 = [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002), 286) and of several satellite vol. 9 sūtras; his Lotus survives as the principal philological witness independent of Kumārajīva.
- [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) — co-translator with Dharmagupta 笈多 of the Suí Lotus recension (T264 = [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003), 601), source of the textual additions to the received Kumārajīva Lotus.
- [法雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%9B%B2) — Liáng-period exegete of the Lotus ([KR6d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0005)); the standard pre-Tiāntái southern reading, against which Zhìyǐ defined his own system.
- [慧思](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%80%9D) — Tiāntái second patriarch and Zhìyǐ's teacher; author of the *Fǎhuá jīng ānlèxíng yì* [KR6d0156](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0156) and other proto-Tiāntái Lotus-meditation works.
- [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) — third Tiāntái patriarch and de facto founder of Chinese Tiāntái doctrine; lecturer of the *sāndàbù* and dozens of other works in this division (the most-cited person in `KR6d`, named in ≈ 25 per-text notes).
- [灌頂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%81%8C%E9%A0%82) — Zhìyǐ's principal disciple and the redactor / co-author of nearly the entire Zhìyǐ corpus; also author of the *Guóqīng bǎilù* [KR6d0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0183), the documentary record of the early Tiāntái community.
- [吉藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%97%8F) — Sānlùn master whose Lotus commentaries ([KR6d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0023)–[KR6d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0025), [KR6d0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0128)) represent the principal alternative early-Suí exegetical line.
- [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) — Cí'ēn / Faxiang master who gave the Lotus a Yogācāra reading ([KR6d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0026)); the source of the *xuánzàn* sub-commentary tradition.
- [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) — sixth Tiāntái patriarch and reviver of the school in the mid-Táng; author of the canonical sub-commentaries on the *sāndàbù* ([KR6d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0007), [KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015), [KR6d0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0131)) and of the doctrinally generative *Shí bùèr mén* [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and *Jīngāngbēi* [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175).
- [空海](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A9%BA%E6%B5%B7) — founder of Japanese Shingon and author of seven Lotus-related Heian works in this division (e.g. [KR6d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0036)–[KR6d0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0042)), giving the Lotus its esoteric / *mìjiào* 密教 reading.
- [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) — leader of the Sòng *shānjiā* 山家 branch of Tiāntái and the dominant figure of the 11th-century revival; the second-most-cited person in `KR6d` (≈ 11 notes), with the *Shí bùèr mén zhǐyào chāo* [KR6d0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0158) and his liturgical *xíngfǎ* corpus.
- [遵式](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%B5%E5%BC%8F) — Zhīlǐ's contemporary and the principal Sòng ritual compiler; author of Tiāntái *chànyí* and devotional works (e.g. [KR6d0195](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0195), [KR6d0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0199)).
- [仁岳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BB%81%E5%B2%B3) — Zhīlǐ's disciple who later turned to the *shānwài* 山外 position; author of the *Sìmíng Rényuè yìshuō cóngshū* [KR6d0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0224), the principal *shānwài* counter-statement.
- [從義](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%9E%E7%BE%A9) — late-Sòng commentator on the *Móhē zhǐguān* and *Shí bùèr mén* whose works ([KR6d0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0139)–[KR6d0141](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0141)) preserve the post-Zhīlǐ scholastic apparatus.
- [宗曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E6%9B%89) — Sòng compiler of the *Sìmíng zūnzhě jiàoxíng lù* [KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186), the corpus of Zhīlǐ's writings; principal documentary editor of *shānjiā* Tiāntái.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) — Míng-period reviver of Tiāntái and author of the *Jiàoguān gāngzōng* [KR6d0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0188); the principal late-imperial systematiser whose works re-frame Tiāntái for the Míng-Qīng setting.
- [靈耀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9D%88%E8%80%80) — Qīng-period Tiāntái commentator on the *Móhē zhǐguān* and the *sāndàbù* ([KR6d0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0142) and related); his work is the principal Qīng Tiāntái scholastic continuation.

### Topics

- **The ekayāna 一乘 doctrine and *kāiquán xiǎnshí* 開權顯實.** The proclamation in chapters 2–9 of the Lotus that the *śrāvaka* / *pratyekabuddha* / *bodhisattva* three vehicles are provisional (*quán* 權) and the Buddha-vehicle alone is real (*shí* 實) is the central scriptural commitment around which the entire Tiāntái doctrinal apparatus is built, and almost every Sinitic Lotus exegete from Fǎyún onward addresses its hermeneutic status.
- **The *jìmén* / *běnmén* 跡門／本門 division.** The split of the Lotus into a "trace-gate" (chapters 1–14) and an "origin-gate" (15–28) is associated with Dàoxuān's preface to Kumārajīva ([KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001)) and given systematic articulation in Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì* [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006); it remains the standard Sinitic exegetical schema through the entire division.
- **The *wǔshí bājiào* 五時八教 classification.** Zhìyǐ's chronological-and-modal organisation of the Buddha's *kerygma* into five periods (*Huāyán*, *Lùyuàn / Āhán*, *Fāngděng*, *Bōrě*, *Fǎhuá-Nièpán*) and eight modes is developed in the *Xuányì*, summarised in [KR6d0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0166) and [KR6d0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0167), and given canonical compact form in Chégwan's *Tiāntái sìjiào yí* [KR6d0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0168); it is the basic doctrinal-classification apparatus of the division.
- **Tiāntái meditation: *yīxīn sānguān* 一心三觀, *yīniàn sānqiān* 一念三千, *zhǐguān bùèr* 止觀不二.** Articulated principally in the *Móhē zhǐguān* [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) and its commentaries; the most systematic Mahāyāna meditation theory in Chinese, organised on the *shíjìng × shíchéng* 十境十乘 matrix.
- **The *shānjiā / shānwài* 山家／山外 controversy.** The 11th-century Sòng-period split between Zhīlǐ's [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) "mountain-house" *shānjiā* — defending the Tiāntái doctrine of evil in the Buddha-nature (*xìng-è* 性惡) and Guàndǐng's role in the early canon — and the *shānwài* counter-position of Yuánqīng 源清, Zhìyuán 智圓, and (later) Rényuè 仁岳, particularly over the interpretation of Zhànrán's *Shí bùèr mén* [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and the status of Guàndǐng's *Guānyīn xuányì* commentary [KR6d0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0046). The dispute generated the large mid-Sòng polemical literature visible in [KR6d0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0184)–[KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186) and [KR6d0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0220)–[KR6d0235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0235).
- **Buddha-nature in the insentient (*wúqíng yǒu xìng* 無情有性).** Zhànrán's claim in the *Jīngāngbēi* [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175) that even insentient things possess Buddha-nature; the Tiāntái counter-position to the Chán and Huāyán readings on the same question, generating the *Jīngāngbēi*-commentary sub-tradition ([KR6d0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0176)–[KR6d0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0181)).
- **The Lotus liturgy: *Fǎhuá sānmèi* 法華三昧 and the *chànyí* tradition.** Zhìyǐ's Lotus-Samādhi practice from the *Móhē zhǐguān* and the *Fǎhuá sānmèi chànyí* [KR6d0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0191) is the textual base for a Sòng-period ritual literature, principally elaborated by Zūnshì and Zhīlǐ, that fed back into ordinary monastic and lay practice and shaped the late-imperial Tiāntái devotional landscape.
- **The Guānyīn 觀音 sub-cult.** The detachment of the *Pǔmén pǐn* 普門品 (Lotus chapter 25) as an independent devotional unit, with its own commentarial corpus ([KR6d0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0046)–[KR6d0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0057)) — Zhìyǐ's *Guānyīn xuányì* and *yìshū* and their Sòng / Míng / Qīng commentaries — is one of the principal vehicles by which the Lotus's textual presence extended into popular ritual practice.
- **Japanese Lotus reception: Tendai 天台 and Shingon 真言 readings.** The Heian-period esoteric / *mìjiào* interpretations of the Lotus by Kūkai 空海 ([KR6d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0036)–[KR6d0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0044)) and the early Japanese Tendai materials (e.g. [KR6d0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0220)) constitute a distinct Lotus reading transmitted within the same division.
- **The Míng–Qīng Tiāntái revival.** Zhìxù's [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) 17th-century systematisation, the Qīng-period Tiāntái commentaries by Língyào, Tōnglǐ, and others ([KR6d0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0084)–[KR6d0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0098), [KR6d0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0142)), and the late-imperial *Sìjiào yí* sub-commentaries ([KR6d0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0169)–[KR6d0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0174)) constitute the final phase of pre-modern Lotus scholarship represented in the division.

## Division note: [KR6p 淨土宗著述部 *Jìngtǔ zōng zhùshù bù* — Buddhist Canon — Compositions of the Pure Land School](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6p collects the Chinese-language compositions of the Pure Land school (*jìngtǔ zōng* 淨土宗) — the body of doctrinal treatises, sūtra-commentaries, liturgical *zàn* / *chàn* / *yí* texts, devotional anthologies, biographies, and devotional poetry that grew up around the three principal Pure Land sūtras: the *Larger Sukhāvatī-vyūha* (*Wúliángshòu jīng* 無量壽經), the *Smaller Sukhāvatī-vyūha* (*Āmítuó jīng* 阿彌陀經), and the apocryphal *Contemplation Sūtra* (*Guān wúliángshòu jīng* 觀無量壽經). The 140 works gathered here are drawn from three regions of the Sino-Japanese canon: (i) the Taishō *Zhū-zōng bù* 諸宗部 (vol. 47, nos. 1957–1984) — the principal classical Pure Land treatises from Tánluán through Sòng-period Tiantai; (ii) the supplementary *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏 (vols. 1, 2, 22, 61, 62, 74) — the great bulk of Sòng–Qīng commentaries, ritual handbooks, and lay-Buddhist anthologies that the early-twentieth-century Japanese editors recovered from Chinese monastic libraries; and (iii) the Taishō *Gǔyì bù* 古逸部 (vol. 85, nos. 2826–2830), preserving Dunhuang-recovered Pure Land liturgies. The corresponding Taishō structural division — `div31.xml` 諸宗部 — is the formal canonical container, but the Kanripo arrangement extracts the Pure Land subset and supplements it heavily from the *Xùzàngjīng*.

Chronologically the division spans c. 530 CE (Tánluán 曇鸞's foundational tracts) through the very end of the Qīng (c. 1900). The internal centre of gravity is unusually late: roughly two-thirds of the entries date from the Míng-Qīng period, reflecting the fact that Pure Land devotion became the dominant lay-monastic practice of late imperial China and produced an immense vernacular literature absent from earlier canonical strata. Three transmissional issues run through the division: the inflation of the *Wúliángshòu* sūtra-corpus through apocryphal "translations" preserved only in the *Xùzàngjīng* (KR6p0031–0035); the Tiantai monopoly on the *Guān-jīng* commentarial tradition via the 觀經疏妙宗鈔 chain initiated by Zhīlǐ 知禮; and the steady migration of Pure Land authorship from the cloister to the lay literati class, culminating in the Péng Shàoshēng circle of the eighteenth century and Wèi Yuán's *Huìyì* recension of 1854.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **Wúliángshòu jīng 無量壽經 (Larger Sukhāvatī-vyūha) corpus** — *Wúliángshòu jīng huìyì* 無量壽經會譯 [KR6p0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0001) (Wèi Yuán 魏源, 1854), *Wúliángshòu jīng jì* 無量壽經記 [KR6p0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0002) (Xuányī 玄一, Táng), *Wúliángshòu jīng qǐxìn lùn* 無量壽經起信論 [KR6p0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0003) (Péng Jìqīng 彭際清, late 18th c.), and Wáng Gēngxīn 王耕心's *Móhē Āmítuó jīng zhōnglùn* 摩訶阿彌陀經衷論 [KR6p0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0004); together they constitute the most sustained East-Asian commentarial engagement with the *larger* Pure Land sūtra.

- **Qīng lay-Buddhist Pure Land movement** — built around Péng Shàoshēng / Péng Jìqīng 彭紹升 / 彭際清 (1740–1796), who is here represented by no fewer than nine works: doctrinal treatises *Wúliángshòu jīng qǐxìn lùn* [KR6p0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0003), *Guān-jīng yuē lùn* [KR6p0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0013), *Āmítuó jīng yuē lùn* [KR6p0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0028); anthologies *Chóngdìng xīfāng gōngjù* 重訂西方公據 [KR6p0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0099) and *Niànfó jǐngcè* 念佛警策 [KR6p0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0100); the *Shěng'ān fǎshī yǔlù* 省菴法師語錄 [KR6p0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0098); and the poetic collections *Èrlín chànghé shī* 二林唱和詩 [KR6p0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0128), *Guānhé jí jiéchāo* 觀河集節鈔 [KR6p0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0129), *Cèhǎi jí jiéchāo* 測海集節鈔 [KR6p0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0130). Around Péng cluster Shíxián 實賢 (Xǐng'ān 省菴), Xíngcè 行策 (*Jìngtǔ jǐngyǔ* [KR6p0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0093), *Qǐyī xīn jīngjìn niànfó qīqī guīshì* [KR6p0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0094)), Chèwù 徹悟 (*Chèwù chánshī yǔlù* [KR6p0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0101)), Zhōu Mèngyán 周夢顏's *Xīguī zhízhǐ* 西歸直指 [KR6p0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0092), Sōng Shàndēng 沈善登's *Bàoēn lùn* 報恩論 [KR6p0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0124), and Wèi Yuán's *Huìyì*. The late-Qīng strand of Hangzhou-area devotional anthologies by Gǔkūn 古崑 ([KR6p0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0085), [KR6p0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0106), [KR6p0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0107), [KR6p0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0116), [KR6p0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0117)) forms the closing wave of the division.
- **Liturgical / praise (zàn 讚 / chàn 懺 / yí 儀) corpus** — beyond Shàndǎo's three liturgies and Zūnshì's *Chànyuàn yí* above: Tánluán's *Zàn Āmítuó fó jié* [KR6p0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0073); the Nāgārjuna *Shíèr lǐ* 十二禮 (tr. Jñānagupta 禪那崛多) [KR6p0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0080); Zhìshēng 智昇's *Jí zhū jīng lǐchàn yí* 集諸經禮懺儀 [KR6p0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0077); Fǎzhào 法照's *Jìngtǔ wǔhuì niànfó lüè fǎshì yízàn* 淨土五會念佛略法事儀讚 [KR6p0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0078) and *Wǔhuì niànfó sòngjīng guānxíng yí (juǎn zhōng, xià)* [KR6p0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0136); Yuánzhào and Jièdù's *Wúliángshòu fó zàn zhù* 無量壽佛讚註 [KR6p0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0083); and the Dunhuang stratum [KR6p0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0137)–[KR6p0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0140).
- **Dunhuang stratum (Taishō vol. 85)** — Huìrì 慧日's *Lüè zhū jīnglùn niànfó fǎmén wǎngshēng jìngtǔ jí (juǎn shàng)* 略諸經論念佛法門往生淨土集 [KR6p0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0135), the only surviving juǎn of Huìrì's three-juǎn defence of "*niànfó* by sūtra and treatise" composed before 748; Fǎzhào's *Wǔhuì* middle and lower fascicles [KR6p0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0136) (the upper juǎn survives independently as KR6p0078); and the anonymous *Dàshèng jìngtǔ zàn* 大乘淨土讚 [KR6p0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0137), *Chízhāi niànfó chànhuǐ lǐwén* 持齋念佛懺悔禮文 [KR6p0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0138), *Dào'ān fǎshī niànfó zàn* 道安法師念佛讚 [KR6p0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0139) / *zànwén* 道安法師念佛讚文 [KR6p0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0140) — the principal Northwest-Chinese witnesses to Pure-Land devotional practice independent of the central-Táng exegetical traditions.

### Important persons

- [曇鸞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E9%B8%9E) (Tánluán, c. 476–542) — the earliest Chinese Pure Land author preserved in the canon; the *Lüèlùn ānlè jìngtǔ yì* [KR6p0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0036) and the *Zàn Āmítuó fó jié* [KR6p0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0073) are the foundational texts of the *zìlì / tālì* (self-power / other-power) distinction.
- [道綽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E7%B6%BD) (Dàochuò, 562–645) — second of the "three masters of Xuánzhōng-sì 玄中寺"; the *Ānlè jí* [KR6p0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0037) is the principal Sui-Táng systematization of *niànfó* doctrine.
- [善導](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%96%84%E5%B0%8E) (Shàndǎo, 613–681) — the central figure of classical Pure Land; four works in the division ([KR6p0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0038), [KR6p0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0074)–[KR6p0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0076)) establishing both doctrinal and liturgical practice.
- [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) (Tiāntái Zhìyǐ, 538–597) — Sui Tiantai patriarch; *Jìngtǔ shíyí lùn* [KR6p0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0040) and *Wǔ fāngbiàn niànfó mén* [KR6p0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0041) traditionally attributed to him; the actual composition almost certainly Sòng-period under his name.
- [懷感](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E6%84%9F) (Huáigǎn, fl. 690–705) — Xuánzàng's disciple turned Pure-Land apologist; *Shì jìngtǔ qúnyí lùn* [KR6p0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0039) is the most rigorous early scholastic defence of Pure-Land practice within Yogācāra doctrine.
- [迦才](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%BF%A6%E6%89%8D) (Jiācái, fl. 645–670) — author of the early-Táng *Jìngtǔ lùn* [KR6p0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0042), an alternative scholastic systematization parallel to Dàochuò.
- [飛錫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A3%9B%E9%8C%AB) (Fēixī, fl. 742–779) — late-Táng author of *Niànfó sānmèi bǎowáng lùn* [KR6p0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0046), a key statement of the universal-scope reading of *niànfó*.
- [元曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E6%9B%89) (Wǒnhyo, 617–686) — Silla scholar; the *Yóuxīn ānlè dào* [KR6p0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0044) is the Korean voice in the Táng Pure Land canon.
- [慧日](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%97%A5) (Címǐn Huìrì, 680–748) — author of the Dunhuang *Lüè zhū jīnglùn niànfó fǎmén* [KR6p0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0135); an opponent of Chán quietism who insisted on textual-scholastic foundations for Pure Land.
- [法照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%85%A7) (Fǎzhào, c. 745–805) — Wǔtáishān-based liturgist; creator of the *wǔhuì niànfó* 五會念佛 chanting system represented by KR6p0078 and KR6p0136.
- [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) (Sìmíng Zhīlǐ, 960–1028) — the architect of Sòng-Tiantai Pure-Land thought; the *Miàozōng chāo* [KR6p0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0007), *Róngxīn jiě* [KR6p0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0008), and *Kē* [KR6p0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0006) together define the Tiantai reading of the *Guān-jīng* down to the present.
- [遵式](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%B5%E5%BC%8F) (Cíyún Zūnshì, 964–1032) — Zhīlǐ's contemporary; the *Juéyí xíngyuàn èrmén* [KR6p0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0047) and *Chànyuàn yí* [KR6p0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0079) codified Pure Land ritual for the Hángzhōu-area Tiantai network.
- [元照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E7%85%A7) (Língzhī Yuánzhào, 1048–1116) — Vinaya master who turned to Pure Land; *Āmítuó jīng yìshū* and *Wúliángshòu fó zàn zhù* together with the Jièdù sub-commentaries form a distinct Sòng-Vinaya reading of Pure Land texts.
- [戒度](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%92%E5%BA%A6) (Jièdù, fl. 1180–1240) — Yuánzhào's principal commentator; three works in the division ([KR6p0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0009), [KR6p0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0010), [KR6p0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0015)).
- [宗曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E6%9B%89) (Zōngxiǎo, 1151–1214) — Sòng-period anthologist whose *Lèbāng wénlèi* / *Lèbāng yígǎo* preserve the bulk of the Sòng prefatory and hagiographic corpus.
- [王日休](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%97%A5%E4%BC%91) (Wáng Rìxiū, d. 1173) — Sòng lay literatus; the *Lóngshū jìngtǔ wén* [KR6p0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0050) is the most widely circulated lay Pure-Land manual in pre-modern China.
- [懷則](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E5%89%87) (Huáizé, fl. 1290–1340) and [天如則](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E5%A6%82%E5%89%87) (Tiānrú Wéizé, c. 1286–1354) — Yuán Tiantai authors of, respectively, the *Jìngguān yàomén* and the *Jìngtǔ huòwèn*.
- [普度](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E5%BA%A6) (Yōután Pǔdù, d. 1330) — Yuán reformer of the White Lotus society; the *Lúshān liánzōng bǎojiàn* [KR6p0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0054) is the canonical lineage-history of the "Lotus society" tradition.
- [袾宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%BE%E5%AE%8F) (Yúnqī Zhūhóng, 1535–1615) — late-Míng master at Yúnqī-sì 雲棲寺; the dominant authorial presence in the division (eight works including the *Āmítuó jīng shūchāo*) and the architect of late-Míng Pure Land revival.
- [傳燈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%82%B3%E7%87%88) (Yōuxī Chuándēng, 1554–1627) — Míng Tiantai exegete; commentator on both the *Guān-jīng* and the *Āmítuó jīng* tradition, author of the *Jìngtǔ shēng-wúshēng lùn*.
- [大佑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A7%E4%BD%91) (Dàyòu, 1334–1407) — Yuán-Míng compiler bridging the two dynasties; three works in the division.
- [袁宏道](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%81%E5%AE%8F%E9%81%93) (Yuán Hóngdào, 1568–1610) — Gōng'ān-school literatus; *Xīfāng hé lùn* [KR6p0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0057) is the principal late-Míng literati statement of Pure Land doctrine.
- [李贄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E8%B4%84) (Lǐ Zhì, 1527–1602) — heterodox Míng literatus; *Jìngtǔ jué* [KR6p0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0062) places him in the Pure Land tradition.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) (Ǒuyì Zhìxù, 1599–1655) — last of the "four great Míng masters"; his *Āmítuó jīng yàojiě* (transmitted here in [KR6p0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0025)) is the standard Tiantai reading of the smaller sūtra.
- [成時](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%90%E6%99%82) (Chéngshí, 1618–1678) — Zhìxù's disciple; compiler of the *Jìngtǔ shíyào* [KR6p0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0067), the canonical late-Míng / early-Qīng Pure-Land anthology.
- [彭際清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E9%9A%9B%E6%B8%85) (Péng Shàoshēng / Jìqīng, 1740–1796) — leading Qīng lay-Buddhist scholar; nine works represent his doctrinal, anthological, and poetic output and define eighteenth-century lay Pure Land literature.
- [實賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E8%B3%A2) (Xǐng'ān Shíxián, 1686–1734) — Qīng patriarch of the Pure Land lineage; subject of [KR6p0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0098) and annotator of [KR6p0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0087) and [KR6p0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0097).
- [行策](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A1%8C%E7%AD%96) (Jiéliú Xíngcè, 1628–1682) — *Jìngtǔ jǐngyǔ* [KR6p0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0093) and *Niànfó qīqī guīshì* [KR6p0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0094); founder of the *fó-qī* 佛七 seven-day intensive *niànfó* retreat as a standardized form.
- [古崑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%A4%E5%B4%91) (Gǔkūn, fl. 1860–1890) — late-Qīng Hangzhou-area anthologist; five works form the closing wave of the division.
- [魏源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E6%BA%90) (Wèi Yuán, 1794–1857) — late-Qīng statecraft scholar; the *Wúliángshòu jīng huìyì* [KR6p0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0001) is the first sustained Chinese attempt at a synthetic conflated recension of the larger sūtra.
- [沈善登](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E5%96%84%E7%99%BB) (Shěn Shàndēng, 1830–1902) — *Bàoēn lùn* [KR6p0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0124); a late-Qīng intellectual systematization of Pure Land in dialogue with mid-nineteenth-century reformist Confucianism.

### Topics

- **The five Chinese versions of the *Wúliángshòu jīng* and the problem of a unified Larger Pure Land Sūtra** — running from the medieval translator-attributions through Yúnqī Zhūhóng's preference for the smaller sūtra to Wèi Yuán's nineteenth-century *huìyì* solution and Xià Liánjū's twentieth-century continuation; the principal philological problem of the division.
- **The status of the *Guān wúliángshòu jīng* as a Central-Asian / Chinese composition** — debate, beginning with Mochizuki Shinkō's mid-twentieth-century work and continuing into Fujita Kōtatsu and Stevenson's studies, over whether the sūtra is an Indian translation or a Sino-Central-Asian composition; the entire commentarial chain [KR6p0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0005)–[KR6p0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0013) presupposes it as canonical.
- **The Tiantai monopolization of *Guān-jīng* exegesis** — how Zhīlǐ's *Miàozōng chāo* established a doctrinal grid (*xìng-shàn xìng-è* 性善性惡, *yīniàn sānqiān* 一念三千) on top of the sūtra's contemplative scheme, and how this Tiantai reading survived as the only living *Guān-jīng* commentarial tradition through the Sòng, Yuán, and Míng periods.
- **The *niànfó sānmèi* debate** — whether *niànfó* is a propaedeutic ritual practice, a meditative *samādhi*, or an actualization of *zìxìng Mítuó wéixīn jìngtǔ* 自性彌陀唯心淨土 (the Amitābha-of-one's-own-nature, the Pure Land of mind-only); a debate that runs from Fēixī's *Bǎowáng lùn* [KR6p0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0046) through Yánshòu and Yuán Hóngdào to the late-Míng "*chán-jìng yī-zhì* 禪淨一致" (Chán–Pure-Land synthesis) of Yúnqī and Zhìxù.
- **Chán–Pure-Land synthesis (chán-jìng shuāngxiū 禪淨雙修)** — the Sòng-Míng-Qīng convergence of Chán practice and Pure Land devotion, most clearly thematized in Tiānrú Wéizé's *Huòwèn* [KR6p0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0053), Yuán Hóngdào's *Hé lùn* [KR6p0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0057), Jīhúng 濟能's *Jiǎohǔ jí* 角虎集 [KR6p0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0096), and Chèwù's *Yǔlù* [KR6p0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0101); defined the dominant late-imperial monastic style.
- **Pure Land hagiography and the "Lotus society" lineage** — the construction of an unbroken lineage from Lúshān Huìyuǎn 廬山慧遠's 4th-c. society through the Táng masters to the present, codified by Pǔdù's *Liánzōng bǎojiàn* [KR6p0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0054) and Zōngxiǎo's anthologies, and disseminated as the model of Pure Land religious community.
- **The migration of authorship from cloister to lay literati** — most visible in the eighteenth-century Péng Shàoshēng circle (his nine works represent the apex), but already prepared in the Sòng with Wáng Rìxiū, in the Míng with Yuán Hóngdào and Lǐ Zhì, and continuing into the late-Qīng with Wèi Yuán, Shěn Shàndēng, and Wáng Gēngxīn.
- **Pure Land devotional poetry as canonical literature** — the unusual fact, distinctive to this division within the Kanripo Buddhist canon, that *jìngtǔ shī* 淨土詩 collections are treated as canonical religious texts and admitted to the *Xùzàngjīng*; a Qīng phenomenon documented in [KR6p0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0072), [KR6p0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0128)–[KR6p0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0134).
- **The *fó-qī* 佛七 (seven-day intensive *niànfó*) and Pure Land monastic regulation** — the standardization of ritual recitation regimes traceable from Zhìshēng's *Lǐchàn yí* [KR6p0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0077) and Fǎzhào's *Wǔhuì* [KR6p0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0078) through Xíngcè's *Qīqī guīshì* [KR6p0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0094) to nineteenth-century Hangzhou practice in Gǔkūn's manuals; the operational practice underlying the doctrinal literature.
- **The Dunhuang independent witness** — the *Gǔyì bù* texts [KR6p0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0135)–[KR6p0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0140) preserve a Pure-Land devotional tradition (Címǐn Huìrì, Fǎzhào, anonymous liturgies) at least partly independent of the Chang'an-Luòyáng centres, and their survival only at Dunhuang shows how much medieval Chinese Pure Land literature has been lost in central transmission.

## Division note (scope only): [KR6q 禪宗著述部 *Chánzōng zhùshù bù* — Buddhist Canon — Compositions of the Chán School](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6q gathers the writings of the Chán school 禪宗 as preserved across three textual reservoirs: the *Shǐchuán bù* 史傳部 and *Zhū-zōng bù* 諸宗部 of the Taishō canon (T47, T48, T51), the Xuzangjing 卍續藏 Chán *yǔlù* run (X64–X88), and the Jiāxīng Canon 嘉興藏 *yǔlù* expansion (J20–J40 and the Wàihán *bùyí* 補遺). The division therefore spans the full literary output of an indigenous Chinese Buddhist tradition: transmission-of-the-lamp histories (*dēnglù* 燈錄) and their *xù-* / *guǎng-* / *liánxù-* / *zēngjí-* derivatives; the recorded sayings (*yǔlù* 語錄) of individual masters; the kōan / "old-cases" literature (*gōng'àn* 公案, *sòng gǔ* 頌古, *niāngǔ* 拈古, *píngchàng* 評唱) and its commentarial superstructure; Buddhist biographical jewelry (*sēngbǎo zhuàn* 僧寶傳); Chán monastic codes (*qīngguī* 清規); the admonitory-pastoral genre (*jǐng cè* 警策, *bǎoxùn* 寶訓); doctrinal compendia and sectarian polemics on the *wǔ jiā qī zōng* 五家七宗 lineages; verse cycles (notably the *shíniú tú sòng* 十牛圖頌 and the *Yǒngjiā Zhèngdào gē* 永嘉證道歌); and the literary collected works (*biéjí* 別集) of Chán masters. The 609 entries make KR6q the single largest Chán-literature corpus assembled anywhere in modern catalogs and the densest documentation of any East-Asian Buddhist school.

Chronologically the corpus stretches from the conventionally-dated 6th-century *Sì xíng guān* 四行觀 attributed to Bodhidharma (KR6q0112) through to the early-19th-century *Zhèngyuán lüèjí* 正源略集 of Jìchéng 際澄 (KR6q0031–0033, 1820–1828). Quantitatively, however, the division is overwhelmingly weighted toward the 17th century: roughly 335 of the 609 entries — about 55% — are 17th-century Jiāxīng-Canon *yǔlù* of late-Míng and early-Qīng Chán abbots, reflecting both the print boom of the Wàn-Lì 萬曆 reform and the Línjì-school 臨濟宗 revival under Mìyún Yuánwù 密雲圓悟 and his dharma-heirs. For Taishō structural context the relevant CANWWW divisions are `div21.xml` (史傳部, hosting the foundational *dēnglù* set) and the Chán portion of `div23.xml` / `div24.xml` (諸宗部 Chán entries). Modern critical reference for the *dēnglù* tradition runs through Yanagida Seizan 柳田聖山, T. Griffith Foulk, Albert Welter, and Morten Schlütter; for the late-Míng / Qīng *yǔlù* explosion, through Jiang Wu 吳疆, Beata Grant, and Hasebe Yūkei 長谷部幽蹊.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The foundational *dēnglù* sequence ("Five Lamps" 五燈 and after).** This is the structural backbone of the division and the principal narrative source for Chinese Chán self-history.

- *Zǔtáng jí* 祖堂集 [KR6q0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0002) — the 952 Quánzhōu 泉州 compilation, the earliest extant true lamp record; lost in China and recovered via Korean transmission.
- *Jǐngdé chuándēng lù* 景德傳燈錄 [KR6q0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0003) — Dàoyuán's 1004–1011 work, the imperially-presented Sòng prototype that gave the genre its canonical shape.
- *Tiānshèng guǎngdēng lù* 天聖廣燈錄 [KR6q0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0004) — Lǐ Zūnxù's 1029–1036 expansion, the first lay-compiled lamp record.
- *Jiànzhōng jìngguó xùdēng lù* 建中靖國續燈錄 [KR6q0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0007) — Wéibái's 1101 continuation.
- *Liándēng huìyào* 聯燈會要 [KR6q0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0008) — Wùmíng's 1183 harmonization of the previous three.
- *Jiātài pǔdēng lù* 嘉泰普燈錄 [KR6q0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0010) — Zhèngshòu's 1204 broadening to laity and women.
- *Wǔdēng huìyuán* 五燈會元 [KR6q0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0012) — Pǔjì's 1252 *editio definitiva* synthesizing the five preceding lamp records into a single 20-juan corpus; the most influential single text of the genre.
- *Xù chuándēng lù* 續傳燈錄 [KR6q0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0016) — the early-Míng (1401–1402) Yǒnglè-era imperial continuation.
- *Wǔdēng yántǒng* 五燈嚴統 [KR6q0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0019) / *Jiěhuò biān* [KR6q0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0020) — Fèiyǐn Tōngróng's 1653–1654 partisan Línjì rewrite and its self-defence, the most notorious sectarian intervention in the *dēnglù* tradition.
- *Wǔdēng quánshū* 五燈全書 [KR6q0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0022) — Jièlín Chāoyǒng's 120-juan Kāngxī-era (1697) compendium.
- *Zhǐyuè lù* 指月錄 [KR6q0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0023) — Qú Rǔjī's lay-compiled 1602 anthology.

**Kōan / old-cases tradition.** The *gōng'àn* literary tradition reframes encounter-dialogue narratives from the *dēnglù* as objects of literary commentary.

- *Bìyán lù* 碧巖錄 [KR6q0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0078) — Yuánwù Kèqín's *píngchàng* commentary (c. 1128) on Xuědòu Chóngxiǎn's 雪竇重顯 100 *sòng-gǔ* verses; the *locus classicus* of *wénzì chán* 文字禪.
- *Cóngróng ān lù* 從容庵錄 [KR6q0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0079) — Wànsōng Xíngxiù's 1223 commentary on Hóngzhì Zhèngjué's 宏智正覺 100 verses; Cáodòng counterpart to the *Bìyán lù*.
- *Wúmén guān* 無門關 [KR6q0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0080) — Wúmén Huìkāi's 1228 collection of 48 cases, the most internationally diffused kōan compendium.
- *Fóguǒ jījié lù* 佛果擊節錄 [KR6q0249](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0249), the Línquán 林泉 commentaries [KR6q0251](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0251) [KR6q0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0252), and the Tiānqí 天奇 directing commentaries [KR6q0250](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0250) [KR6q0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0253) continue the genre through the Yuán and Míng.

- *Zuìshàng shèng lùn* 最上乘論 attributed to Hóngrěn 弘忍 [KR6q0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0086).
