## Division note: [KR6e 華嚴部類 *Huáyán bùlèi* — Buddhist Canon — Huáyán (Avataṃsaka) Corpus](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6e gathers the Chinese-language literature of the *Huáyánjīng* 華嚴經 / *Buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra* tradition: the three full Chinese translations of the sūtra, the early Hàn-through-Jìn partial translations and parallel texts (兜沙經, 菩薩本業經, 漸備一切智德經 etc.), the *Daśabhūmika* and *Gaṇḍavyūha* clusters that circulated independently, the foundational śāstras of Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and Vasubandhu 天親, the writings of the Táng "five patriarchs" (Dùshùn 杜順, Zhìyǎn 智儼, Fǎzàng 法藏, Chéngguān 澄觀, Zōngmì 宗密) and of the parallel layman-exegete Lǐ Tōngxuán 李通玄, the Sillan Huāǒm 華嚴 contributions of Wǒnhyo 元曉 and Ǔisang 義湘, the Northern-Sòng "restoration" centred on Jìngyuán 淨源 and the Liáo-Sòng *Wǔjiào zhāng* subcommentarial tradition, and the Yuán-Míng-Qīng synthetic and ritual works that close the corpus. The division spans roughly seventeen centuries, from Lokakṣema's 支婁迦讖 *Dōushā jīng* in the Later Hàn (c. 178–189) to Péng Jìqīng's 彭際清 *Huáyán niànfó sānmèi lùn* (c. 1770–1796).

In Taishō organisation, the heart of the corpus is the *Huáyánbù* 華嚴部, running from T277 to T309. KR6e is broader than that division: it pulls in the *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā* 十住毘婆沙論 and the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra* 十地經論 from the Taishō treatise sections (T1521, T1522), Fǎzàng's and Chéngguān's exegetical works from the *Jīngshūbù* 經疏部 (T1731–T1740), the patriarchal essays from the *Zhūzōngbù* 諸宗部 (T1866–T1899), and Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng material from the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. The Kanripo grouping thus reflects sectarian rather than strictly bibliographic logic: it is the textual archive of the Huáyán *school* (Huáyánzōng 華嚴宗, also known as Xiánshǒuzōng 賢首宗 after Fǎzàng's posthumous title) read as a continuous tradition.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The three full translations of the *Huáyánjīng***.
  - *Liùshí Huáyán* 六十華嚴, [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001) — Buddhabhadra 佛馱跋陀羅's sixty-fascicle rendering completed at Yángzhōu in 418–420; the base text for Dùshùn, Zhìyǎn, Wǒnhyo and the early Huáyán synthesis.
  - *Bāshí Huáyán* 八十華嚴, [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010) — Śikṣānanda 實叉難陀's eighty-fascicle "new translation" of 695–699, sponsored by Wǔ Zétiān 武則天; supersedes the Liùshí Huáyán in Táng and later exegesis and is the version Fǎzàng (after revision), Chéngguān, and Lǐ Tōngxuán comment on.
  - *Sìshí Huáyán* 四十華嚴, [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) — Prajñā 般若's forty-fascicle translation of 796–798, which renders only the *Gaṇḍavyūha* 入法界品 but adds the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* / Pǔxián xíngyuàn 普賢行願 hymn that became the principal Huáyán liturgical text.
- **Early partial and parallel translations**. [KR6e0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0028) 兜沙經 (Lokakṣema, c. 178–189) is the oldest extant Chinese fragment of the corpus; [KR6e0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0029) 菩薩本業經 (Zhī Qiān 支謙, 222–253), [KR6e0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0030) 諸菩薩求佛本業經 (Niè Dàozhēn 聶道真), and [KR6e0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0031) 菩薩十住行道品 / [KR6e0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0032) 佛說菩薩十住經 form the Hàn-through-Jìn pre-history of the *Huáyán*'s reception in China.
- **The *Daśabhūmika* / 十地 cluster**. [KR6e0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0033) 漸備一切智德經 (Zhú Fǎhù 竺法護, 297), [KR6e0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0034) 十住經 (Kumārajīva 鳩摩羅什, c. 405), and [KR6e0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0035) 佛說十地經 (Śīladharma 尸羅達摩, 789–798) translate the same sūtra at three points; together with [KR6e0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0059) 十住毘婆沙論 (Nāgārjuna 龍樹 / Kumārajīva tr.) and [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060) 十地經論 (Vasubandhu / Bodhiruci 菩提流支, 508–511), they constitute the Indian doctrinal core that anchored the Northern Wèi Dìlùn 地論 school and through it the later Huáyán synthesis.
- **The *Gaṇḍavyūha* / 入法界品 cluster**. [KR6e0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0043) 羅摩伽經 (Shèngjiān 聖堅), [KR6e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0044) 大方廣佛華嚴經入法界品 (Divākara 地婆訶羅), and the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) all transmit Sudhana's 善財 pilgrimage; this cluster underlies [KR6e0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0115) 文殊指南圖讚 (Wéibái 惟白) and the standard iconographic programme of the fifty-three teachers.
- **Tathāgata-realm sūtras** (Wǔ-Zhōu-era expansions of the corpus). [KR6e0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0049) 不思議佛境界分, [KR6e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0050) 大方廣如來不思議境界經, [KR6e0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0052) 佛華嚴入如來德智不思議境界經, and [KR6e0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0053) 大方廣入如來智德不思議經 round out the Avataṃsaka literary horizon as it was received in early Táng.
- **The Táng patriarchal corpus**. Zhìyǎn's *Sōuxuán jì* 搜玄記 [KR6e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0003) and *Wǔshí yào wèndá* [KR6e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0083); Fǎzàng's *Tànxuán jì* 探玄記 [KR6e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0004), *Wénjì gāngmù* [KR6e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0005), the *Wǔjiào zhāng* 五教章 (Huáyán yīchéng jiàoyì fēnqí zhāng) [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074), the *Zhǐguī* [KR6e0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0085), *Yìhǎi bǎimén* [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089), *Wàngjìn huányuán guān* [KR6e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0090) and the *Jīnshīzǐ zhāng* 金獅子章 commentarial tradition [KR6e0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0097)–[KR6e0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0098); Chéngguān's massive *Dàshū* [KR6e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0011) and *Yǎnyìchāo* [KR6e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0012) together with the *Fǎjiè xuánjìng* [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and *Sānshèng yuánróng guānmén* [KR6e0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0099); and Zōngmì's *Zhù Fǎjiè guānmén* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) and *Yuánrén lùn* 原人論 [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105), the latter widely read as the school's most concise doctrinal statement.
- **Lǐ Tōngxuán's parallel tradition**. The *Xīn Huáyán jīng lùn* 新華嚴經論 [KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022), the *Juéyí lùn* [KR6e0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0024) and *Shímíng lùn* [KR6e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0112), later edited together with the sūtra as the *Huáyánjīng hélùn* 華嚴經合論 [KR6e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0066), offered an alternative reading of the *Bāshí Huáyán* outside the patriarchal lineage and exerted strong influence on Sòng Chán reception.
- **Sillan Huāǒm**. Wǒnhyo 元曉's surviving *Huáyán jīng shū* fascicle [KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009), Ǔisang 義湘's *Yīchéng fǎjiè tú* 一乘法界圖 [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109) with its later anthology [KR6e0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0110), Pyowǒn 表員's *Wényì yàojué wèndá* [KR6e0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0121), Gyǒndǔng 見登之's *Yīchéng chéngfó miàoyì* [KR6e0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0114) and Myǒnghyo 明皛's *Hǎiyìn sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0113) are the principal Korean contributions retained in the Chinese canon.
- **The *Wǔjiào zhāng* subcommentarial tradition**. Dàotíng 道亭's *Yìyuàn shū* [KR6e0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0075), Shīhuì 師會's *Fénxīn* [KR6e0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0076) and *Fùgǔ jì* [KR6e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0078), and Xīdí 希迪's *Jíchéng jì* [KR6e0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0079) and *Píngfùgǔjì* [KR6e0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0080) form the Sòng debate over Fǎzàng's foundational five-teachings classification.
- **Sòng-Liáo-Yuán exegesis**. Jìngyuán 淨源's *Huányuánguān kē* [KR6e0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0091) and related ritual reconstructions of the school in the Northern Sòng; the Liáo monk Xiānyǎn 鮮演's *Tánxuán juézé* [KR6e0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0119); the Yuán *Xuántán huìxuán jì* [KR6e0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0120) of Pǔruì 普瑞; Jièhuán 戒環's *Yàojiě* [KR6e0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0122) and Dàotōng 道通's *Tūnhǎi jí* [KR6e0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0123).
- **Late synthesis (Míng-Qīng)**. Chéngguān's *Gāngyào* (with Míng reorganisation) [KR6e0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0124), Xùfǎ 續法's *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí* [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) and *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí kāiméng* [KR6e0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0143) codifying the Qīng-dynasty school curriculum, and Péng Jìqīng 彭際清's lay-Buddhist *Yīchéng juéyí lùn* [KR6e0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0147) and *Huáyán niànfó sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) integrating Huáyán with Pure-Land practice.
- **Ritual and contemplative material**. The *Fǎjiè guānmén* 法界觀門 attributed to Dùshùn (preserved only via [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101)), [KR6e0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0081) 華嚴五教止觀, [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082) 華嚴一乘十玄門 (whose authenticity as Dùshùn's own work is contested), and the great repentance and offering manuals — [KR6e0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0149) 海印道場九會請佛儀, [KR6e0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0150) 海印道場懺儀, [KR6e0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0152)–[KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153) 普賢行願修證儀, and Zōngmì's [KR6e0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0155) 圓覺經道場修證儀 — establish Huáyán as a practice-tradition, not only an exegetical one.

### Important persons

- [佛馱跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%A6%B1%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Buddhabhadra, 359–429) — translator of the *Liùshí Huáyán* [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001) and of the early *Wénshū shīlì fāyuàn jīng* [KR6e0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0045); the figure through whom the *Avataṃsaka* first entered Chinese in its full form.
- [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) (Śikṣānanda, 652–710) — Khotanese monk recruited by Wǔ Zétiān to retranslate the sūtra; produced the *Bāshí Huáyán* [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010) and the parallel inconceivable-realm sūtras [KR6e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0050), [KR6e0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0053), [KR6e0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0047).
- [般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) (Prajñā, 744–810) — Kashmiri translator of the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) at the request of Emperor Dézōng 德宗; brought the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* into the corpus.
- [杜順](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E9%A0%86) (Dùshùn, 557–640) — traditional first patriarch; lifetime work survives only in attributions ([KR6e0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0081), [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082), [KR6e0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0160)) and through Chéngguān and Zōngmì's transmission of the *Fǎjiè guānmén* in [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100)–[KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101).
- [智儼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%84%BC) (Zhìyǎn, 602–668) — second patriarch; in the *Sōuxuán jì* [KR6e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0003) and the *Kǒngmù zhāng* [KR6e0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0084) he organised the *Liùshí Huáyán* into the analytical framework Fǎzàng would inherit.
- [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) (Fǎzàng, 643–712) — third patriarch and the systematiser of the school; sixteen distinct works in the division, anchoring the doctrinal core in the *Wǔjiào zhāng* [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074) and the meditative-metaphysical core in the *Wàngjìn huányuán guān* [KR6e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0090) and *Yìhǎi bǎimén* [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089).
- [澄觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BE%84%E8%A7%80) (Chéngguān, 738–839) — fourth patriarch; author of the largest single body of writing in the division (seventeen works), centred on the *Dàshū* and *Yǎnyìchāo* commentaries on the *Bāshí Huáyán* [KR6e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0011)–[KR6e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0012). The exegetical horizon of every later author rests on his work.
- [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) (Zōngmì, 780–841) — fifth patriarch and the bridge to Chán; his *Yuánrén lùn* [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105) is the most widely read short Huáyán text outside the school proper.
- [李通玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%80%9A%E7%8E%84) (Lǐ Tōngxuán, 645–740) — Táng layman; his *Xīn Huáyán jīng lùn* [KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022) and successor works developed a reading of the *Bāshí Huáyán* organised around the Wǔtáishān cosmology and the Sudhana pilgrimage, parallel and partly counter to the patriarchal tradition.
- [元曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E6%9B%89) (Wǒnhyo, 617–686) — Sillan exegete; his *Huáyán jīng shū* [KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009) survives only in fragments but is the earliest extant Korean Huáyán commentary.
- [義湘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B9%98) (Ǔisang, 625–702) — Sillan founder of Huāǒm; the *Yīchéng fǎjiè tú* [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109) is one of the school's iconic short doctrinal works.
- [慧苑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E8%8B%91) (Huìyuàn, fl. early 8th c.) — Fǎzàng's disciple; the *Xù-Huáyán-jīng lüèshū kāndìng jì* [KR6e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0065) reorganised his master's commentarial scheme on the new translation and was sharply contested in later transmission.
- [淨源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B7%A8%E6%BA%90) (Jìngyuán, 1011–1088) — the Northern-Sòng "restorer of the Huáyán teaching" (中興教主); a cluster of his works ([KR6e0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0091), [KR6e0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0092), [KR6e0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0152), [KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153), [KR6e0156](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0156), [KR6e0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0157)) reassembled the school's curriculum after the loss of major Táng texts.
- [師會](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B8%AB%E6%9C%83) (Shīhuì, fl. mid-12th c.) — central voice in the Sòng *Wǔjiào zhāng* debate; [KR6e0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0076)–[KR6e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0078) defend Fǎzàng's text against Huìyuàn's emendations and frame the later orthodox reading.
- [續法](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BA%8C%E6%B3%95) (Xùfǎ, 1641–1728) — Qīng compiler and self-styled twenty-eighth Huáyán patriarch; his *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí* [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) became the standard pedagogical entry into the school.
- [彭際清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E9%9A%9B%E6%B8%85) (Péng Jìqīng / Péng Shàoshēng 彭紹昇, 1740–1796) — Qing lay scholar; his integration of Huáyán with Pure-Land practice in [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) marks the final major intellectual moment of the corpus.

### Topics

- **The classification of teachings (*pànjiào* 判教)**. The school's signature project is the ranking of all Buddhist teachings into the *Wǔjiào* 五教 (Hīnayāna 小乘 / Elementary Mahāyāna 大乘始 / Final Mahāyāna 大乘終 / Sudden 頓 / Perfect 圓) and *Shízōng* 十宗 schemes laid out in Fǎzàng's *Wǔjiào zhāng* [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074). The contested Sòng-era reception of that text ([KR6e0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0075)–[KR6e0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0080)) and Xùfǎ's Qīng codification [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) map the boundaries of school orthodoxy across a millennium.
- **The Dharma-realm (*fǎjiè* 法界) and its four divisions**. Dùshùn's *Fǎjiè guānmén* — surviving only in Chéngguān's *Xuánjìng* [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and Zōngmì's *Zhù* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) — articulates the canonical fourfold scheme (*shìfǎjiè* 事法界 / *lǐfǎjiè* 理法界 / *lǐshì wúài fǎjiè* 理事無礙法界 / *shìshì wúài fǎjiè* 事事無礙法界). This is the doctrinal kernel from which all later Huáyán metaphysics is unfolded.
- **The Ten Mysterious Gates (*shíxuánmén* 十玄門) and the Six Marks (*liùxiàng* 六相)**. The cosmological apparatus that converts *fǎjiè* doctrine into the school's signature mereology of mutual interpenetration; older redaction in [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082), systematised by Zhìyǎn ([KR6e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0083), [KR6e0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0084)) and given its definitive form by Fǎzàng (notably in [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074) and [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089)).
- **The *Daśabhūmika* and the legacy of the Dìlùn school**. Vasubandhu's *Shídì jīng lùn* [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060), translated in the Northern Wèi, was the doctrinal core of the Dìlùn 地論 school and a direct ancestor of Huáyán; the school's debates over *ālayavijñāna* and the relation of the *tathāgatagarbha* to the bodhisattva path enter Huáyán through Zhìyǎn's reading of [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060) together with [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001).
- **Patriarchal lineage versus layman exegesis**. The five-patriarch line (Dùshùn → Zhìyǎn → Fǎzàng → Chéngguān → Zōngmì) is itself a Sòng-era retrospective construction; the parallel and historically prior reading of Lǐ Tōngxuán ([KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022), [KR6e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0066), [KR6e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0112)) provides a check on its self-presentation and exerted independent influence on Chán.
- **Cross-cultural transmission**. The Sillan contributions ([KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009), [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109), [KR6e0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0110), [KR6e0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0113), [KR6e0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0114), [KR6e0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0121)) — produced under and after the Korean monks who studied with Zhìyǎn and Fǎzàng — and the Khotanese, Kashmiri, and Sogdian translators ([KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001), [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010), [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041), [KR6e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0044), [KR6e0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0046)) make the *Huáyán* the most internationally produced corpus in the Chinese canon outside the Vinaya.
- **Huáyán as Chán and as Pure Land**. Zōngmì's *Yuánrén lùn* [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105) and *Zhù Fǎjiè guānmén* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) frame Huáyán doctrine for a Chán readership; Péng Jìqīng's *Niànfó sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) reframes it for a Pure-Land one. These two ends of the doctrinal afterlife are essential to reading Sòng-Qīng intellectual history.
- **The *Pǔxián xíngyuàn* 普賢行願 cult**. The hymn appended to the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) generated its own commentarial micro-corpus ([KR6e0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0069), [KR6e0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0070), [KR6e0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0071), [KR6e0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0072), [KR6e0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0073)) and the ritual structures of [KR6e0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0149)–[KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153); the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* is the daily liturgical text of East Asian Mahāyāna and originates here.
- **Pseudepigrapha and apocrypha**. Several works ascribed to Dùshùn (notably [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082)) are now thought to be Zhìyǎn's or later; the *Xíngyuàn pǐn biéxíng shūchāo* [KR6e0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0073) survives only in selection. Authenticity is a live problem across the early-Táng layer.

## Division note: [KR6e 華嚴部類 *Huáyán bùlèi* — Buddhist Canon — Huáyán (Avataṃsaka) Corpus](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6e gathers the Chinese-language literature of the *Huáyánjīng* 華嚴經 / *Buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra* tradition: the three full Chinese translations of the sūtra, the early Hàn-through-Jìn partial translations and parallel texts (兜沙經, 菩薩本業經, 漸備一切智德經 etc.), the *Daśabhūmika* and *Gaṇḍavyūha* clusters that circulated independently, the foundational śāstras of Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and Vasubandhu 天親, the writings of the Táng "five patriarchs" (Dùshùn 杜順, Zhìyǎn 智儼, Fǎzàng 法藏, Chéngguān 澄觀, Zōngmì 宗密) and of the parallel layman-exegete Lǐ Tōngxuán 李通玄, the Sillan Huāǒm 華嚴 contributions of Wǒnhyo 元曉 and Ǔisang 義湘, the Northern-Sòng "restoration" centred on Jìngyuán 淨源 and the Liáo-Sòng *Wǔjiào zhāng* subcommentarial tradition, and the Yuán-Míng-Qīng synthetic and ritual works that close the corpus. The division spans roughly seventeen centuries, from Lokakṣema's 支婁迦讖 *Dōushā jīng* in the Later Hàn (c. 178–189) to Péng Jìqīng's 彭際清 *Huáyán niànfó sānmèi lùn* (c. 1770–1796).

In Taishō organisation, the heart of the corpus is the *Huáyánbù* 華嚴部, running from T277 to T309. KR6e is broader than that division: it pulls in the *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā* 十住毘婆沙論 and the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra* 十地經論 from the Taishō treatise sections (T1521, T1522), Fǎzàng's and Chéngguān's exegetical works from the *Jīngshūbù* 經疏部 (T1731–T1740), the patriarchal essays from the *Zhūzōngbù* 諸宗部 (T1866–T1899), and Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng material from the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. The Kanripo grouping thus reflects sectarian rather than strictly bibliographic logic: it is the textual archive of the Huáyán *school* (Huáyánzōng 華嚴宗, also known as Xiánshǒuzōng 賢首宗 after Fǎzàng's posthumous title) read as a continuous tradition.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The three full translations of the *Huáyánjīng***.
  - *Liùshí Huáyán* 六十華嚴, [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001) — Buddhabhadra 佛馱跋陀羅's sixty-fascicle rendering completed at Yángzhōu in 418–420; the base text for Dùshùn, Zhìyǎn, Wǒnhyo and the early Huáyán synthesis.
  - *Bāshí Huáyán* 八十華嚴, [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010) — Śikṣānanda 實叉難陀's eighty-fascicle "new translation" of 695–699, sponsored by Wǔ Zétiān 武則天; supersedes the Liùshí Huáyán in Táng and later exegesis and is the version Fǎzàng (after revision), Chéngguān, and Lǐ Tōngxuán comment on.
  - *Sìshí Huáyán* 四十華嚴, [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) — Prajñā 般若's forty-fascicle translation of 796–798, which renders only the *Gaṇḍavyūha* 入法界品 but adds the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* / Pǔxián xíngyuàn 普賢行願 hymn that became the principal Huáyán liturgical text.
- **Early partial and parallel translations**. [KR6e0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0028) 兜沙經 (Lokakṣema, c. 178–189) is the oldest extant Chinese fragment of the corpus; [KR6e0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0029) 菩薩本業經 (Zhī Qiān 支謙, 222–253), [KR6e0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0030) 諸菩薩求佛本業經 (Niè Dàozhēn 聶道真), and [KR6e0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0031) 菩薩十住行道品 / [KR6e0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0032) 佛說菩薩十住經 form the Hàn-through-Jìn pre-history of the *Huáyán*'s reception in China.
- **The *Daśabhūmika* / 十地 cluster**. [KR6e0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0033) 漸備一切智德經 (Zhú Fǎhù 竺法護, 297), [KR6e0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0034) 十住經 (Kumārajīva 鳩摩羅什, c. 405), and [KR6e0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0035) 佛說十地經 (Śīladharma 尸羅達摩, 789–798) translate the same sūtra at three points; together with [KR6e0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0059) 十住毘婆沙論 (Nāgārjuna 龍樹 / Kumārajīva tr.) and [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060) 十地經論 (Vasubandhu / Bodhiruci 菩提流支, 508–511), they constitute the Indian doctrinal core that anchored the Northern Wèi Dìlùn 地論 school and through it the later Huáyán synthesis.
- **The *Gaṇḍavyūha* / 入法界品 cluster**. [KR6e0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0043) 羅摩伽經 (Shèngjiān 聖堅), [KR6e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0044) 大方廣佛華嚴經入法界品 (Divākara 地婆訶羅), and the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) all transmit Sudhana's 善財 pilgrimage; this cluster underlies [KR6e0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0115) 文殊指南圖讚 (Wéibái 惟白) and the standard iconographic programme of the fifty-three teachers.
- **Tathāgata-realm sūtras** (Wǔ-Zhōu-era expansions of the corpus). [KR6e0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0049) 不思議佛境界分, [KR6e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0050) 大方廣如來不思議境界經, [KR6e0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0052) 佛華嚴入如來德智不思議境界經, and [KR6e0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0053) 大方廣入如來智德不思議經 round out the Avataṃsaka literary horizon as it was received in early Táng.
- **The Táng patriarchal corpus**. Zhìyǎn's *Sōuxuán jì* 搜玄記 [KR6e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0003) and *Wǔshí yào wèndá* [KR6e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0083); Fǎzàng's *Tànxuán jì* 探玄記 [KR6e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0004), *Wénjì gāngmù* [KR6e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0005), the *Wǔjiào zhāng* 五教章 (Huáyán yīchéng jiàoyì fēnqí zhāng) [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074), the *Zhǐguī* [KR6e0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0085), *Yìhǎi bǎimén* [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089), *Wàngjìn huányuán guān* [KR6e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0090) and the *Jīnshīzǐ zhāng* 金獅子章 commentarial tradition [KR6e0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0097)–[KR6e0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0098); Chéngguān's massive *Dàshū* [KR6e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0011) and *Yǎnyìchāo* [KR6e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0012) together with the *Fǎjiè xuánjìng* [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and *Sānshèng yuánróng guānmén* [KR6e0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0099); and Zōngmì's *Zhù Fǎjiè guānmén* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) and *Yuánrén lùn* 原人論 [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105), the latter widely read as the school's most concise doctrinal statement.
- **Lǐ Tōngxuán's parallel tradition**. The *Xīn Huáyán jīng lùn* 新華嚴經論 [KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022), the *Juéyí lùn* [KR6e0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0024) and *Shímíng lùn* [KR6e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0112), later edited together with the sūtra as the *Huáyánjīng hélùn* 華嚴經合論 [KR6e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0066), offered an alternative reading of the *Bāshí Huáyán* outside the patriarchal lineage and exerted strong influence on Sòng Chán reception.
- **Sillan Huāǒm**. Wǒnhyo 元曉's surviving *Huáyán jīng shū* fascicle [KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009), Ǔisang 義湘's *Yīchéng fǎjiè tú* 一乘法界圖 [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109) with its later anthology [KR6e0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0110), Pyowǒn 表員's *Wényì yàojué wèndá* [KR6e0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0121), Gyǒndǔng 見登之's *Yīchéng chéngfó miàoyì* [KR6e0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0114) and Myǒnghyo 明皛's *Hǎiyìn sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0113) are the principal Korean contributions retained in the Chinese canon.
- **The *Wǔjiào zhāng* subcommentarial tradition**. Dàotíng 道亭's *Yìyuàn shū* [KR6e0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0075), Shīhuì 師會's *Fénxīn* [KR6e0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0076) and *Fùgǔ jì* [KR6e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0078), and Xīdí 希迪's *Jíchéng jì* [KR6e0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0079) and *Píngfùgǔjì* [KR6e0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0080) form the Sòng debate over Fǎzàng's foundational five-teachings classification.
- **Sòng-Liáo-Yuán exegesis**. Jìngyuán 淨源's *Huányuánguān kē* [KR6e0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0091) and related ritual reconstructions of the school in the Northern Sòng; the Liáo monk Xiānyǎn 鮮演's *Tánxuán juézé* [KR6e0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0119); the Yuán *Xuántán huìxuán jì* [KR6e0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0120) of Pǔruì 普瑞; Jièhuán 戒環's *Yàojiě* [KR6e0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0122) and Dàotōng 道通's *Tūnhǎi jí* [KR6e0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0123).
- **Late synthesis (Míng-Qīng)**. Chéngguān's *Gāngyào* (with Míng reorganisation) [KR6e0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0124), Xùfǎ 續法's *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí* [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) and *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí kāiméng* [KR6e0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0143) codifying the Qīng-dynasty school curriculum, and Péng Jìqīng 彭際清's lay-Buddhist *Yīchéng juéyí lùn* [KR6e0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0147) and *Huáyán niànfó sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) integrating Huáyán with Pure-Land practice.
- **Ritual and contemplative material**. The *Fǎjiè guānmén* 法界觀門 attributed to Dùshùn (preserved only via [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101)), [KR6e0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0081) 華嚴五教止觀, [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082) 華嚴一乘十玄門 (whose authenticity as Dùshùn's own work is contested), and the great repentance and offering manuals — [KR6e0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0149) 海印道場九會請佛儀, [KR6e0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0150) 海印道場懺儀, [KR6e0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0152)–[KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153) 普賢行願修證儀, and Zōngmì's [KR6e0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0155) 圓覺經道場修證儀 — establish Huáyán as a practice-tradition, not only an exegetical one.

### Important persons

- [佛馱跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%A6%B1%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Buddhabhadra, 359–429) — translator of the *Liùshí Huáyán* [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001) and of the early *Wénshū shīlì fāyuàn jīng* [KR6e0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0045); the figure through whom the *Avataṃsaka* first entered Chinese in its full form.
- [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) (Śikṣānanda, 652–710) — Khotanese monk recruited by Wǔ Zétiān to retranslate the sūtra; produced the *Bāshí Huáyán* [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010) and the parallel inconceivable-realm sūtras [KR6e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0050), [KR6e0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0053), [KR6e0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0047).
- [般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) (Prajñā, 744–810) — Kashmiri translator of the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) at the request of Emperor Dézōng 德宗; brought the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* into the corpus.
- [杜順](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E9%A0%86) (Dùshùn, 557–640) — traditional first patriarch; lifetime work survives only in attributions ([KR6e0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0081), [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082), [KR6e0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0160)) and through Chéngguān and Zōngmì's transmission of the *Fǎjiè guānmén* in [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100)–[KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101).
- [智儼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%84%BC) (Zhìyǎn, 602–668) — second patriarch; in the *Sōuxuán jì* [KR6e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0003) and the *Kǒngmù zhāng* [KR6e0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0084) he organised the *Liùshí Huáyán* into the analytical framework Fǎzàng would inherit.
- [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) (Fǎzàng, 643–712) — third patriarch and the systematiser of the school; sixteen distinct works in the division, anchoring the doctrinal core in the *Wǔjiào zhāng* [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074) and the meditative-metaphysical core in the *Wàngjìn huányuán guān* [KR6e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0090) and *Yìhǎi bǎimén* [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089).
- [澄觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BE%84%E8%A7%80) (Chéngguān, 738–839) — fourth patriarch; author of the largest single body of writing in the division (seventeen works), centred on the *Dàshū* and *Yǎnyìchāo* commentaries on the *Bāshí Huáyán* [KR6e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0011)–[KR6e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0012). The exegetical horizon of every later author rests on his work.
- [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) (Zōngmì, 780–841) — fifth patriarch and the bridge to Chán; his *Yuánrén lùn* [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105) is the most widely read short Huáyán text outside the school proper.
- [李通玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%80%9A%E7%8E%84) (Lǐ Tōngxuán, 645–740) — Táng layman; his *Xīn Huáyán jīng lùn* [KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022) and successor works developed a reading of the *Bāshí Huáyán* organised around the Wǔtáishān cosmology and the Sudhana pilgrimage, parallel and partly counter to the patriarchal tradition.
- [元曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E6%9B%89) (Wǒnhyo, 617–686) — Sillan exegete; his *Huáyán jīng shū* [KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009) survives only in fragments but is the earliest extant Korean Huáyán commentary.
- [義湘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B9%98) (Ǔisang, 625–702) — Sillan founder of Huāǒm; the *Yīchéng fǎjiè tú* [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109) is one of the school's iconic short doctrinal works.
- [慧苑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E8%8B%91) (Huìyuàn, fl. early 8th c.) — Fǎzàng's disciple; the *Xù-Huáyán-jīng lüèshū kāndìng jì* [KR6e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0065) reorganised his master's commentarial scheme on the new translation and was sharply contested in later transmission.
- [淨源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B7%A8%E6%BA%90) (Jìngyuán, 1011–1088) — the Northern-Sòng "restorer of the Huáyán teaching" (中興教主); a cluster of his works ([KR6e0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0091), [KR6e0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0092), [KR6e0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0152), [KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153), [KR6e0156](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0156), [KR6e0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0157)) reassembled the school's curriculum after the loss of major Táng texts.
- [師會](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B8%AB%E6%9C%83) (Shīhuì, fl. mid-12th c.) — central voice in the Sòng *Wǔjiào zhāng* debate; [KR6e0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0076)–[KR6e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0078) defend Fǎzàng's text against Huìyuàn's emendations and frame the later orthodox reading.
- [續法](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BA%8C%E6%B3%95) (Xùfǎ, 1641–1728) — Qīng compiler and self-styled twenty-eighth Huáyán patriarch; his *Xiánshǒu wǔjiào yí* [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) became the standard pedagogical entry into the school.
- [彭際清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E9%9A%9B%E6%B8%85) (Péng Jìqīng / Péng Shàoshēng 彭紹昇, 1740–1796) — Qing lay scholar; his integration of Huáyán with Pure-Land practice in [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) marks the final major intellectual moment of the corpus.

### Topics

- **The classification of teachings (*pànjiào* 判教)**. The school's signature project is the ranking of all Buddhist teachings into the *Wǔjiào* 五教 (Hīnayāna 小乘 / Elementary Mahāyāna 大乘始 / Final Mahāyāna 大乘終 / Sudden 頓 / Perfect 圓) and *Shízōng* 十宗 schemes laid out in Fǎzàng's *Wǔjiào zhāng* [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074). The contested Sòng-era reception of that text ([KR6e0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0075)–[KR6e0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0080)) and Xùfǎ's Qīng codification [KR6e0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0142) map the boundaries of school orthodoxy across a millennium.
- **The Dharma-realm (*fǎjiè* 法界) and its four divisions**. Dùshùn's *Fǎjiè guānmén* — surviving only in Chéngguān's *Xuánjìng* [KR6e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0100) and Zōngmì's *Zhù* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) — articulates the canonical fourfold scheme (*shìfǎjiè* 事法界 / *lǐfǎjiè* 理法界 / *lǐshì wúài fǎjiè* 理事無礙法界 / *shìshì wúài fǎjiè* 事事無礙法界). This is the doctrinal kernel from which all later Huáyán metaphysics is unfolded.
- **The Ten Mysterious Gates (*shíxuánmén* 十玄門) and the Six Marks (*liùxiàng* 六相)**. The cosmological apparatus that converts *fǎjiè* doctrine into the school's signature mereology of mutual interpenetration; older redaction in [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082), systematised by Zhìyǎn ([KR6e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0083), [KR6e0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0084)) and given its definitive form by Fǎzàng (notably in [KR6e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0074) and [KR6e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0089)).
- **The *Daśabhūmika* and the legacy of the Dìlùn school**. Vasubandhu's *Shídì jīng lùn* [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060), translated in the Northern Wèi, was the doctrinal core of the Dìlùn 地論 school and a direct ancestor of Huáyán; the school's debates over *ālayavijñāna* and the relation of the *tathāgatagarbha* to the bodhisattva path enter Huáyán through Zhìyǎn's reading of [KR6e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0060) together with [KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001).
- **Patriarchal lineage versus layman exegesis**. The five-patriarch line (Dùshùn → Zhìyǎn → Fǎzàng → Chéngguān → Zōngmì) is itself a Sòng-era retrospective construction; the parallel and historically prior reading of Lǐ Tōngxuán ([KR6e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0022), [KR6e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0066), [KR6e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0112)) provides a check on its self-presentation and exerted independent influence on Chán.
- **Cross-cultural transmission**. The Sillan contributions ([KR6e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0009), [KR6e0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0109), [KR6e0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0110), [KR6e0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0113), [KR6e0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0114), [KR6e0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0121)) — produced under and after the Korean monks who studied with Zhìyǎn and Fǎzàng — and the Khotanese, Kashmiri, and Sogdian translators ([KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001), [KR6e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0010), [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041), [KR6e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0044), [KR6e0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0046)) make the *Huáyán* the most internationally produced corpus in the Chinese canon outside the Vinaya.
- **Huáyán as Chán and as Pure Land**. Zōngmì's *Yuánrén lùn* [KR6e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0105) and *Zhù Fǎjiè guānmén* [KR6e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0101) frame Huáyán doctrine for a Chán readership; Péng Jìqīng's *Niànfó sānmèi lùn* [KR6e0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0148) reframes it for a Pure-Land one. These two ends of the doctrinal afterlife are essential to reading Sòng-Qīng intellectual history.
- **The *Pǔxián xíngyuàn* 普賢行願 cult**. The hymn appended to the *Sìshí Huáyán* [KR6e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0041) generated its own commentarial micro-corpus ([KR6e0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0069), [KR6e0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0070), [KR6e0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0071), [KR6e0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0072), [KR6e0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0073)) and the ritual structures of [KR6e0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0149)–[KR6e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0153); the *Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna* is the daily liturgical text of East Asian Mahāyāna and originates here.
- **Pseudepigrapha and apocrypha**. Several works ascribed to Dùshùn (notably [KR6e0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0082)) are now thought to be Zhìyǎn's or later; the *Xíngyuàn pǐn biéxíng shūchāo* [KR6e0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0073) survives only in selection. Authenticity is a live problem across the early-Táng layer.

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 8 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

## Division note: [KR6i 經集部 *Jīngjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Sūtra Collection (Mahāyāna Sūtrasaṃgraha)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6i mirrors the Taishō Tripiṭaka's 經集部 (*Jīngjí bù*, "Sūtrasaṃgraha"), the catch-all division in which the Taishō editors gathered the Mahāyāna sūtras that did not belong to one of the canon's named text-cycles. The principal axis is Taishō nos. 425–847 across Vols. 14–17, corresponding to CANWWW `div11.xml`; the Kanripo arrangement supplements this with Xuzangjing (卍續) commentaries, a handful of Jiāxīng-zàng titles, and — at the tail end (KR6i0589–0596) — a small block of Yogācāra 論釋 that drifted into the *jīng* collection through their attachment to single-sūtra commentary. Texts in the other "named" divisions are explicitly excluded: Prajñāpāramitā (KR6a), Ratnakūṭa (KR6b), Mahāsannipāta (KR6c), Avataṃsaka (KR6d), Nirvāṇa (KR6e), Lotus (KR6f), Bhadrakalpika (KR6g) and the Āgamas (KR6h) are catalogued elsewhere.

Because *Jīngjí bù* is structurally residual, its scholarly profile is not generic. The "leftover" works concentrate, in fact, several of the most consequential sūtras in the entire Chinese Mahāyāna corpus — *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa*, *Śūraṅgamasamādhi*, *Samādhirāja*, *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*, the three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras*, the *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra* and the *Anūnatva-apūrṇatva-nirdeśa*, the *Bhaiṣajyaguru* corpus, the Maitreya cycle, and the major Sinitic apocrypha *Yuánjué jīng* 圓覺經, *Zhànchá shàn'è yèbào jīng* 占察善惡業報經, *Yúlánpén jīng* 盂蘭盆經, and the *Shíwáng jīng* 十王經. The transmissional pattern is therefore stratigraphic: an Eastern Hàn–Western Jin layer of single-fascicle sūtras translated by Ān Shìgāo, Zhī Qiān, and above all Dharmarakṣa; a Yáo Qín / Northern Liáng turning-point in which Kumārajīva, Buddhabhadra, and Dharmakṣema fix the literary canon; a sixth- and seventh-century Yogācāra wave (Bodhiruci, Paramārtha, Saṅghapāla, Divākara, Xuánzàng); a Tang aftermath that adds re-translations and the great commentarial schools (Zhìyǐ, Jízàng, Kuījī, Zōngmì); and a Sòng coda of Indian translations from Shīhù 施護, Fǎtiān 法天, and Fǎxián 法賢. The chronological depth is matched by a high commentarial density — the *Vimalakīrti* alone carries some twenty exegetical works in this division.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The *Vimalakīrti* cluster.** *Wéimójié suǒshuō jīng* 維摩詰所說經 [KR6i0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0076) (Kumārajīva, 406) is the canonical Chinese *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa* and the most influential single text in the division — it shaped Chinese Buddhist literary style and supplied the central image of the bodhisattva-householder. Zhī Qiān's earlier *Fóshuō wéimójié jīng* 佛說維摩詰經 [KR6i0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0075) (Wú, c. 223–253) and Xuánzàng's *Shuō wúgòuchēng jīng* 說無垢稱經 [KR6i0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0077) preserve the parallel recensions. The exegetical apparatus runs from Sui–Tang masters — Huìyuǎn 慧遠 [KR6i0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0079), Zhìyǐ 智顗 [KR6i0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0080)–[KR6i0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0081), Jízàng 吉藏 [KR6i0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0083)–[KR6i0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0084), Kuījī 窺基 [KR6i0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0085) — through Song Tiāntái revival and Ming–Qing commentary, ending with the Qīng *Wéimó jīng wúwǒ shū* [KR6i0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0095) tradition.

**The Maitreya cluster.** A tight block of six canonical sūtras (KR6i0030–0036) covers the lower-birth (*xiàshēng*) and upper-birth (*shàngshēng*) traditions, including *Fóshuō mílè lái shí jīng* 佛說彌勒來時經 [KR6i0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0036), the briefest and most archaic of the canonical Maitreya texts. Tang commentarial elaboration comes via Jízàng [KR6i0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0037), Kuījī [KR6i0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0038), the Korean exegete Wǒnhyo 元曉 [KR6i0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0039), and Gyeongheung 憬興 [KR6i0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0040) — a rare witness to Silla Buddhist scholarship inside the Chinese canon.

**The *Bhaiṣajyaguru* (Medicine Buddha) cluster.** *Yàoshī liúlí guāng rúlái běnyuàn gōngdé jīng* 藥師琉璃光如來本願功德經 [KR6i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0048) (Xuánzàng, 650) is the canonical East Asian standard, with the seven-Buddha expanded recension *Yàoshī liúlí guāng qī fó běnyuàn gōngdé jīng* [KR6i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0049) (Yìjìng, 707) and a Tang ritual-manual lineage. Tang Dunhuang exegesis survives in two anonymous *Yàoshī jīng shū* [KR6i0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0054)–[KR6i0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0055) preserved in Taishō Vol. 85, and Ming–Qing devotional commentary revives the cluster with Língyào 靈耀's *Yàoshī jīng zhíjiě* [KR6i0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0056) and the Ming repentance-liturgy tradition (KR6i0057–0058).

**The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Golden Light) cluster.** Dharmakṣema's *Jīnguāngmíng jīng* 金光明經 [KR6i0301](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0301) (Northern Liáng, c. 414–426) is the earliest complete Chinese witness; Yìjìng's *Jīnguāngmíng zuìshèng wáng jīng* 金光明最勝王經 [KR6i0303](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0303) (Táng, 703) renders the full Sanskrit recension and supplies the canonical "Right Discourse on the Dharma of Kings" chapter foundational to East Asian state-protective Buddhism. The commentarial chain includes Zhìyǐ–Guàndǐng 灌頂 [KR6i0304](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0304), Zhīlǐ 知禮 [KR6i0305](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0305), Jízàng [KR6i0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0308), and a Tang Esoteric layer.

**The *tathāgatagarbha* / Laṅkāvatāra cluster.** The doctrinal core of East Asian Buddha-nature thought sits inside KR6i: Buddhabhadra's *Dàfāngděng rúláizàng jīng* 大方等如來藏經 [KR6i0323](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0323) (c. 420), Bodhiruci's *Fóshuō bù zēng bù jiǎn jīng* 佛說不增不減經 [KR6i0325](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0325) (c. 525), the three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras* — Guṇabhadra's four-fascicle *Léngqié ābáduōluó bǎo jīng* 楞伽阿跋多羅寶經 [KR6i0327](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0327) (443), Bodhiruci's ten-fascicle *Rù léngqié jīng* 入楞伽經 [KR6i0328](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0328) (513), and Śikṣānanda's seven-fascicle *Dàshèng rù léngqié jīng* 大乘入楞伽經 [KR6i0329](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0329) (700–704) — and Divākara's *Dàshèng mìyán jīng* 大乘密嚴經 [KR6i0359](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0359) (676–688). The Laṅkāvatāra triad is foundational both for East Asian Yogācāra and for early Chán self-identification as the "Laṅkāvatāra School" (楞伽宗).

**The samādhi cluster.** Three central Indian samādhi-sūtras stand together: Kumārajīva's *Shǒulèngyán sānmèi jīng* 佛說首楞嚴三昧經 [KR6i0279](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0279) (c. 402–409 — to be distinguished sharply from the apocryphal *Lèngyán jīng* T945), his *Sīyì fàntiān suǒwèn jīng* 思益梵天所問經 [KR6i0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0218) (c. 402–405), and Narendrayaśas's *Yuèdēng sānmèi jīng* 月燈三昧經 [KR6i0276](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0276) (Northern Qí, 557–559), the canonical Chinese witness to the *Samādhirāja-sūtra*.

**The Ullambana / filial-piety cluster.** *Fóshuō yúlán-pén jīng* 佛說盂蘭盆經 [KR6i0364](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0364) (attrib. Dharmarakṣa, but widely considered a Western Jin Chinese apocryphon) and its short twin *Fóshuō bào'ēn fèng-pén jīng* 佛說報恩奉盆經 [KR6i0376](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0376) together founded the East Asian *zhōngyuán* / Ghost Festival. Zōngmì's *Yúlán-pén jīng shū* [KR6i0365](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0365) and the ten or so subsequent Song–Qīng sub-commentaries make the cluster one of the densest commentarial bodies in the division. The related *Fùmǔ ēn nán bào jīng* 佛說父母恩難報經 [KR6i0363](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0363) (and the apocryphal *Fùmǔ ēnzhòng jīng* tradition) carry the same filial-piety theme into popular Buddhism.

**The *Yuánjué jīng* (Perfect Enlightenment) cluster.** *Dàfāngguǎng yuánjué xiūduōluó liǎoyì jīng* 大方廣圓覺修多羅了義經 [KR6i0551](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0551) — attributed to Buddhatrāta but securely identified as a Tang Chinese apocryphon (c. 690–750) — together with Zōngmì's massive *Yuánjué jīng dàshū* [KR6i0555](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0555) and the long Sòng–Míng commentarial chain (KR6i0553–0574) constitute the textual base of the Huáyán–Chán synthesis Zōngmì engineered.

**The Sinitic apocrypha and divinatory / underworld cluster.** Alongside *Yuánjué jīng*, the division contains the *Zhànchá shàn'è yèbào jīng* 占察善惡業報經 [KR6i0545](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0545) (Sui-period Sinitic apocryphon, foundational to the Kṣitigarbha cult and the unique wooden-block divination liturgy), Zàngchuān 藏川's *Shíwáng jīng* 佛說地藏菩薩發心因緣十王經 [KR6i0583](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0583) and *Yùxiū shíwáng shēngqī jīng* [KR6i0584](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0584) (Late Tang, foundational to East Asian ten-kings underworld iconography), and the late *Huàzhū bǎomìng zhēn jīng* [KR6i0586](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0586) (Míng *zhēn-jīng*-genre fusion of Buddhist form, Daoist neidan imagery, and popular medicine).

**The Mañjuśrī cluster.** Dharmarakṣa's *Wénshū shīlì xiàn bǎozàng jīng* 佛說文殊師利現寶藏經 [KR6i0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0062) (c. 270–308), Saṅghapāla's *Wénshū shīlì wèn jīng* 文殊師利問經 [KR6i0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0069) (Liáng, 515–520 — a principal canonical source for the eighteen Indian sectarian schools), and a series of Tang–Sòng Mañjuśrī texts down to Fǎxián's late-Sòng *Fóshuō miàojíxiáng púsà suǒwèn dàshèng fǎluó jīng* 佛說妙吉祥菩薩所問大乘法螺經 [KR6i0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0074) (989–1000) trace the gradual standardization of Mañjuśrī's Chinese epithets — from older phonetic *Wénshūshīlì* to the standardized Sòng rendering *Miàojíxiáng*.

**The Yogācāra tail (KR6i0589–0596).** Bandhuprabha *et al.*'s *Fódì jīng lùn* 佛地經論 [KR6i0589](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0589) (Xuánzàng, 649), three Vasubandhu-style *upadeśa* commentaries translated by Bodhiruci [KR6i0590](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0590)–[KR6i0592](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0592) and Vimokṣaprajñā [KR6i0593](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0593), and a Dunhuang-derived *Dàshèng sìfǎ jīng* exegetical trio [KR6i0594](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0594)–[KR6i0596](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0596) sit at the catalog's end. They are structurally 釋經論 (commentaries on single sūtras), and in Taishō proper occupy Vol. 26; their inclusion here reflects the Kanripo principle of grouping sūtra commentaries with the parent sūtra division.

### Important persons

- [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) (Dharmarakṣa, c. 239–316) — the single most prolific translator in this division (43 catalogued titles): *Xiánjié jīng*, the early Mañjuśrī texts, the Maitreya core, and a substantial Western-Jin Mahāyāna sūtra corpus.
- [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) (Zhī Qiān, fl. c. 222–253) — early Wu-period sūtra translator; 27 titles here, including the first Chinese *Vimalakīrti*.
- [安世高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96%E9%AB%98) (Ān Shìgāo, fl. 148–168) — Eastern Hàn pioneer; 26 short *jīng* of meditation and ethics surviving in this division.
- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Kumārajīva, 344–413) — fixed the canonical Chinese versions of *Vimalakīrti*, *Śūraṅgamasamādhi*, *Viśeṣacintābrahma-paripṛcchā*, and a clutch of other doctrinally central sūtras.
- [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema, 385–433) — Northern Liáng translator of the earliest complete *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*.
- [佛陀跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Buddhabhadra, 359–429) — translator of the *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra*, opening the textual base of East Asian Buddha-nature doctrine.
- [求那跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Guṇabhadra, 394–468) — translator of the four-fascicle *Laṅkāvatāra*, the lineage text of early Chán.
- [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) (Bodhiruci, fl. 508–537) — Northern Wei Yogācāra translator; ten-fascicle *Laṅkāvatāra*, *Anūnatva-apūrṇatva*, several Vasubandhu *upadeśa*.
- [僧伽婆羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E5%A9%86%E7%BE%85) (Saṅghapāla, 460–524) — Liáng translator of the *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā*.
- [那連提耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A3%E9%80%A3%E6%8F%90%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) (Narendrayaśas, 517–589) — translator of the *Samādhirāja-sūtra*.
- [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) (Jñānagupta, 523–600) — Sui-period sūtra retranslator.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — canonical *Bhaiṣajyaguru*, the *Buddhabhūmi-śāstra*, and several authoritative re-translations.
- [地婆訶羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%B0%E5%A9%86%E8%A8%B6%E7%BE%85) (Divākara, 613–688) — translator of the *Ghanavyūha-sūtra*.
- [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) (Śikṣānanda, 652–710) — seven-fascicle *Laṅkāvatāra*.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) (Yìjìng, 635–713) — the seven-Buddha *Bhaiṣajyaguru* and the long *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-uttamarāja*.

### Topics

- **The residual category as doctrinal repository.** Because the Taishō editors used *Jīngjí bù* as the bin for sūtras lacking a named cycle, the division accumulated isolates of unusual doctrinal density — single-text founders of major traditions (*Vimalakīrti*, *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra*, *Yuánjué jīng*) sit beside short ritual texts. Reading the division requires constant attention to which texts are doctrinal pivots and which are devotional or apotropaic miniatures.
- **Tathāgatagarbha and the Laṅkāvatāra problem.** The three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras* (KR6i0327–0329), the *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra* [KR6i0323](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0323), the *Anūnatva-apūrṇatva-nirdeśa* [KR6i0325](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0325), and the *Ghanavyūha* [KR6i0359](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0359) together form the textual base from which East Asian Buddha-nature theory was synthesized — including the question of whether *ālayavijñāna* and *tathāgatagarbha* are identical, the doctrine that became canonical for Huáyán and Chán.
- **Samādhi literature.** The trio of *Śūraṅgamasamādhi*, *Samādhirāja*, and *Viśeṣacintā* offers a coherent Indian sūtra theory of the bodhisattva's contemplative attainments; this is distinct from — and historically prior to — the apocryphal *Lèngyán jīng* T945 with which the *Śūraṅgamasamādhi* is often confused.
- **Sinitic apocrypha and lay Buddhism.** *Yuánjué jīng*, *Zhànchá jīng*, *Yúlánpén jīng*, *Fùmǔ ēnzhòng jīng*, and the *Shíwáng jīng* corpus are the clearest cases in the Mahāyāna canon of texts produced in China and re-presented as Indian sūtras. They are also the texts with the broadest social reach: filial piety, calendrical festival, divination, and post-mortem judgement.
- **State-protective Buddhism.** The two Chinese *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* recensions, particularly Yìjìng's "Right Discourse on the Dharma of Kings" chapter, supplied the dharmic ideology of East Asian Buddhist statecraft from Sui through Nara and beyond.
- **Filial piety as Buddhist genre.** The Ullambana cluster, the Tang *fùmǔ ēn* texts, the *Shíwáng jīng*, and the *Dìzàng púsà běnyuàn jīng* tradition (its earliest witnesses sit in this division) together constitute Buddhism's most successful response to Confucian objections about filial debt.
- **Translation history through multi-recension witnesses.** Several core texts survive in two or three Chinese versions spanning four to seven centuries — *Vimalakīrti* (Zhī Qiān, Kumārajīva, Xuánzàng), *Laṅkāvatāra* (Guṇabhadra, Bodhiruci, Śikṣānanda), *Bhaiṣajyaguru* (Xuánzàng + Yìjìng + earlier witnesses), *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Dharmakṣema + Yìjìng + Bǎoguì compendium). This makes KR6i an unusually rich laboratory for translation-history research.
- **The Chinese exegetical density.** The *Vimalakīrti* alone carries some twenty Chinese commentaries spanning Sui to Qīng, and the *Yuánjué jīng* almost as many. The exegetical superstructure here is comparable in scale to that built around the *Lotus*, even though no individual non-Lotus sūtra reaches the *Lotus*'s extreme commentarial density.

## Division note (scope only): [KR6e 華嚴部類 *Huáyán bùlèi* — Buddhist Canon — Huáyán (Avataṃsaka) Corpus](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6e gathers the Chinese-language literature of the *Huáyánjīng* 華嚴經 / *Buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra* tradition: the three full Chinese translations of the sūtra, the early Hàn-through-Jìn partial translations and parallel texts (兜沙經, 菩薩本業經, 漸備一切智德經 etc.), the *Daśabhūmika* and *Gaṇḍavyūha* clusters that circulated independently, the foundational śāstras of Nāgārjuna 龍樹 and Vasubandhu 天親, the writings of the Táng "five patriarchs" (Dùshùn 杜順, Zhìyǎn 智儼, Fǎzàng 法藏, Chéngguān 澄觀, Zōngmì 宗密) and of the parallel layman-exegete Lǐ Tōngxuán 李通玄, the Sillan Huāǒm 華嚴 contributions of Wǒnhyo 元曉 and Ǔisang 義湘, the Northern-Sòng "restoration" centred on Jìngyuán 淨源 and the Liáo-Sòng *Wǔjiào zhāng* subcommentarial tradition, and the Yuán-Míng-Qīng synthetic and ritual works that close the corpus. The division spans roughly seventeen centuries, from Lokakṣema's 支婁迦讖 *Dōushā jīng* in the Later Hàn (c. 178–189) to Péng Jìqīng's 彭際清 *Huáyán niànfó sānmèi lùn* (c. 1770–1796).

In Taishō organisation, the heart of the corpus is the *Huáyánbù* 華嚴部, running from T277 to T309. KR6e is broader than that division: it pulls in the *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā* 十住毘婆沙論 and the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra* 十地經論 from the Taishō treatise sections (T1521, T1522), Fǎzàng's and Chéngguān's exegetical works from the *Jīngshūbù* 經疏部 (T1731–T1740), the patriarchal essays from the *Zhūzōngbù* 諸宗部 (T1866–T1899), and Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng material from the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. The Kanripo grouping thus reflects sectarian rather than strictly bibliographic logic: it is the textual archive of the Huáyán *school* (Huáyánzōng 華嚴宗, also known as Xiánshǒuzōng 賢首宗 after Fǎzàng's posthumous title) read as a continuous tradition.

## Division note: [KR6i 經集部 *Jīngjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Sūtra Collection (Mahāyāna Sūtrasaṃgraha)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6i mirrors the Taishō Tripiṭaka's 經集部 (*Jīngjí bù*, "Sūtrasaṃgraha"), the catch-all division in which the Taishō editors gathered the Mahāyāna sūtras that did not belong to one of the canon's named text-cycles. The principal axis is Taishō nos. 425–847 across Vols. 14–17, corresponding to CANWWW `div11.xml`; the Kanripo arrangement supplements this with Xuzangjing (卍續) commentaries, a handful of Jiāxīng-zàng titles, and — at the tail end (KR6i0589–0596) — a small block of Yogācāra 論釋 that drifted into the *jīng* collection through their attachment to single-sūtra commentary. Texts in the other "named" divisions are explicitly excluded: Prajñāpāramitā (KR6a), Ratnakūṭa (KR6b), Mahāsannipāta (KR6c), Avataṃsaka (KR6d), Nirvāṇa (KR6e), Lotus (KR6f), Bhadrakalpika (KR6g) and the Āgamas (KR6h) are catalogued elsewhere.

Because *Jīngjí bù* is structurally residual, its scholarly profile is not generic. The "leftover" works concentrate, in fact, several of the most consequential sūtras in the entire Chinese Mahāyāna corpus — *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa*, *Śūraṅgamasamādhi*, *Samādhirāja*, *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*, the three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras*, the *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra* and the *Anūnatva-apūrṇatva-nirdeśa*, the *Bhaiṣajyaguru* corpus, the Maitreya cycle, and the major Sinitic apocrypha *Yuánjué jīng* 圓覺經, *Zhànchá shàn'è yèbào jīng* 占察善惡業報經, *Yúlánpén jīng* 盂蘭盆經, and the *Shíwáng jīng* 十王經. The transmissional pattern is therefore stratigraphic: an Eastern Hàn–Western Jin layer of single-fascicle sūtras translated by Ān Shìgāo, Zhī Qiān, and above all Dharmarakṣa; a Yáo Qín / Northern Liáng turning-point in which Kumārajīva, Buddhabhadra, and Dharmakṣema fix the literary canon; a sixth- and seventh-century Yogācāra wave (Bodhiruci, Paramārtha, Saṅghapāla, Divākara, Xuánzàng); a Tang aftermath that adds re-translations and the great commentarial schools (Zhìyǐ, Jízàng, Kuījī, Zōngmì); and a Sòng coda of Indian translations from Shīhù 施護, Fǎtiān 法天, and Fǎxián 法賢. The chronological depth is matched by a high commentarial density — the *Vimalakīrti* alone carries some twenty exegetical works in this division.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The *Vimalakīrti* cluster.** *Wéimójié suǒshuō jīng* 維摩詰所說經 [KR6i0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0076) (Kumārajīva, 406) is the canonical Chinese *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa* and the most influential single text in the division — it shaped Chinese Buddhist literary style and supplied the central image of the bodhisattva-householder. Zhī Qiān's earlier *Fóshuō wéimójié jīng* 佛說維摩詰經 [KR6i0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0075) (Wú, c. 223–253) and Xuánzàng's *Shuō wúgòuchēng jīng* 說無垢稱經 [KR6i0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0077) preserve the parallel recensions. The exegetical apparatus runs from Sui–Tang masters — Huìyuǎn 慧遠 [KR6i0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0079), Zhìyǐ 智顗 [KR6i0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0080)–[KR6i0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0081), Jízàng 吉藏 [KR6i0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0083)–[KR6i0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0084), Kuījī 窺基 [KR6i0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0085) — through Song Tiāntái revival and Ming–Qing commentary, ending with the Qīng *Wéimó jīng wúwǒ shū* [KR6i0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0095) tradition.

**The Maitreya cluster.** A tight block of six canonical sūtras (KR6i0030–0036) covers the lower-birth (*xiàshēng*) and upper-birth (*shàngshēng*) traditions, including *Fóshuō mílè lái shí jīng* 佛說彌勒來時經 [KR6i0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0036), the briefest and most archaic of the canonical Maitreya texts. Tang commentarial elaboration comes via Jízàng [KR6i0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0037), Kuījī [KR6i0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0038), the Korean exegete Wǒnhyo 元曉 [KR6i0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0039), and Gyeongheung 憬興 [KR6i0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0040) — a rare witness to Silla Buddhist scholarship inside the Chinese canon.

**The *Bhaiṣajyaguru* (Medicine Buddha) cluster.** *Yàoshī liúlí guāng rúlái běnyuàn gōngdé jīng* 藥師琉璃光如來本願功德經 [KR6i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0048) (Xuánzàng, 650) is the canonical East Asian standard, with the seven-Buddha expanded recension *Yàoshī liúlí guāng qī fó běnyuàn gōngdé jīng* [KR6i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0049) (Yìjìng, 707) and a Tang ritual-manual lineage. Tang Dunhuang exegesis survives in two anonymous *Yàoshī jīng shū* [KR6i0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0054)–[KR6i0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0055) preserved in Taishō Vol. 85, and Ming–Qing devotional commentary revives the cluster with Língyào 靈耀's *Yàoshī jīng zhíjiě* [KR6i0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0056) and the Ming repentance-liturgy tradition (KR6i0057–0058).

**The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Golden Light) cluster.** Dharmakṣema's *Jīnguāngmíng jīng* 金光明經 [KR6i0301](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0301) (Northern Liáng, c. 414–426) is the earliest complete Chinese witness; Yìjìng's *Jīnguāngmíng zuìshèng wáng jīng* 金光明最勝王經 [KR6i0303](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0303) (Táng, 703) renders the full Sanskrit recension and supplies the canonical "Right Discourse on the Dharma of Kings" chapter foundational to East Asian state-protective Buddhism. The commentarial chain includes Zhìyǐ–Guàndǐng 灌頂 [KR6i0304](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0304), Zhīlǐ 知禮 [KR6i0305](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0305), Jízàng [KR6i0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0308), and a Tang Esoteric layer.

**The *tathāgatagarbha* / Laṅkāvatāra cluster.** The doctrinal core of East Asian Buddha-nature thought sits inside KR6i: Buddhabhadra's *Dàfāngděng rúláizàng jīng* 大方等如來藏經 [KR6i0323](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0323) (c. 420), Bodhiruci's *Fóshuō bù zēng bù jiǎn jīng* 佛說不增不減經 [KR6i0325](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0325) (c. 525), the three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras* — Guṇabhadra's four-fascicle *Léngqié ābáduōluó bǎo jīng* 楞伽阿跋多羅寶經 [KR6i0327](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0327) (443), Bodhiruci's ten-fascicle *Rù léngqié jīng* 入楞伽經 [KR6i0328](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0328) (513), and Śikṣānanda's seven-fascicle *Dàshèng rù léngqié jīng* 大乘入楞伽經 [KR6i0329](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0329) (700–704) — and Divākara's *Dàshèng mìyán jīng* 大乘密嚴經 [KR6i0359](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0359) (676–688). The Laṅkāvatāra triad is foundational both for East Asian Yogācāra and for early Chán self-identification as the "Laṅkāvatāra School" (楞伽宗).

**The samādhi cluster.** Three central Indian samādhi-sūtras stand together: Kumārajīva's *Shǒulèngyán sānmèi jīng* 佛說首楞嚴三昧經 [KR6i0279](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0279) (c. 402–409 — to be distinguished sharply from the apocryphal *Lèngyán jīng* T945), his *Sīyì fàntiān suǒwèn jīng* 思益梵天所問經 [KR6i0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0218) (c. 402–405), and Narendrayaśas's *Yuèdēng sānmèi jīng* 月燈三昧經 [KR6i0276](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0276) (Northern Qí, 557–559), the canonical Chinese witness to the *Samādhirāja-sūtra*.

**The Ullambana / filial-piety cluster.** *Fóshuō yúlán-pén jīng* 佛說盂蘭盆經 [KR6i0364](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0364) (attrib. Dharmarakṣa, but widely considered a Western Jin Chinese apocryphon) and its short twin *Fóshuō bào'ēn fèng-pén jīng* 佛說報恩奉盆經 [KR6i0376](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0376) together founded the East Asian *zhōngyuán* / Ghost Festival. Zōngmì's *Yúlán-pén jīng shū* [KR6i0365](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0365) and the ten or so subsequent Song–Qīng sub-commentaries make the cluster one of the densest commentarial bodies in the division. The related *Fùmǔ ēn nán bào jīng* 佛說父母恩難報經 [KR6i0363](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0363) (and the apocryphal *Fùmǔ ēnzhòng jīng* tradition) carry the same filial-piety theme into popular Buddhism.

**The *Yuánjué jīng* (Perfect Enlightenment) cluster.** *Dàfāngguǎng yuánjué xiūduōluó liǎoyì jīng* 大方廣圓覺修多羅了義經 [KR6i0551](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0551) — attributed to Buddhatrāta but securely identified as a Tang Chinese apocryphon (c. 690–750) — together with Zōngmì's massive *Yuánjué jīng dàshū* [KR6i0555](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0555) and the long Sòng–Míng commentarial chain (KR6i0553–0574) constitute the textual base of the Huáyán–Chán synthesis Zōngmì engineered.

**The Sinitic apocrypha and divinatory / underworld cluster.** Alongside *Yuánjué jīng*, the division contains the *Zhànchá shàn'è yèbào jīng* 占察善惡業報經 [KR6i0545](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0545) (Sui-period Sinitic apocryphon, foundational to the Kṣitigarbha cult and the unique wooden-block divination liturgy), Zàngchuān 藏川's *Shíwáng jīng* 佛說地藏菩薩發心因緣十王經 [KR6i0583](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0583) and *Yùxiū shíwáng shēngqī jīng* [KR6i0584](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0584) (Late Tang, foundational to East Asian ten-kings underworld iconography), and the late *Huàzhū bǎomìng zhēn jīng* [KR6i0586](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0586) (Míng *zhēn-jīng*-genre fusion of Buddhist form, Daoist neidan imagery, and popular medicine).

**The Mañjuśrī cluster.** Dharmarakṣa's *Wénshū shīlì xiàn bǎozàng jīng* 佛說文殊師利現寶藏經 [KR6i0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0062) (c. 270–308), Saṅghapāla's *Wénshū shīlì wèn jīng* 文殊師利問經 [KR6i0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0069) (Liáng, 515–520 — a principal canonical source for the eighteen Indian sectarian schools), and a series of Tang–Sòng Mañjuśrī texts down to Fǎxián's late-Sòng *Fóshuō miàojíxiáng púsà suǒwèn dàshèng fǎluó jīng* 佛說妙吉祥菩薩所問大乘法螺經 [KR6i0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0074) (989–1000) trace the gradual standardization of Mañjuśrī's Chinese epithets — from older phonetic *Wénshūshīlì* to the standardized Sòng rendering *Miàojíxiáng*.

**The Yogācāra tail (KR6i0589–0596).** Bandhuprabha *et al.*'s *Fódì jīng lùn* 佛地經論 [KR6i0589](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0589) (Xuánzàng, 649), three Vasubandhu-style *upadeśa* commentaries translated by Bodhiruci [KR6i0590](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0590)–[KR6i0592](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0592) and Vimokṣaprajñā [KR6i0593](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0593), and a Dunhuang-derived *Dàshèng sìfǎ jīng* exegetical trio [KR6i0594](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0594)–[KR6i0596](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0596) sit at the catalog's end. They are structurally 釋經論 (commentaries on single sūtras), and in Taishō proper occupy Vol. 26; their inclusion here reflects the Kanripo principle of grouping sūtra commentaries with the parent sūtra division.

### Topics

- **The residual category as doctrinal repository.** Because the Taishō editors used *Jīngjí bù* as the bin for sūtras lacking a named cycle, the division accumulated isolates of unusual doctrinal density — single-text founders of major traditions (*Vimalakīrti*, *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra*, *Yuánjué jīng*) sit beside short ritual texts. Reading the division requires constant attention to which texts are doctrinal pivots and which are devotional or apotropaic miniatures.
- **Tathāgatagarbha and the Laṅkāvatāra problem.** The three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras* (KR6i0327–0329), the *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra* [KR6i0323](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0323), the *Anūnatva-apūrṇatva-nirdeśa* [KR6i0325](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0325), and the *Ghanavyūha* [KR6i0359](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0359) together form the textual base from which East Asian Buddha-nature theory was synthesized — including the question of whether *ālayavijñāna* and *tathāgatagarbha* are identical, the doctrine that became canonical for Huáyán and Chán.
- **Samādhi literature.** The trio of *Śūraṅgamasamādhi*, *Samādhirāja*, and *Viśeṣacintā* offers a coherent Indian sūtra theory of the bodhisattva's contemplative attainments; this is distinct from — and historically prior to — the apocryphal *Lèngyán jīng* T945 with which the *Śūraṅgamasamādhi* is often confused.
- **Sinitic apocrypha and lay Buddhism.** *Yuánjué jīng*, *Zhànchá jīng*, *Yúlánpén jīng*, *Fùmǔ ēnzhòng jīng*, and the *Shíwáng jīng* corpus are the clearest cases in the Mahāyāna canon of texts produced in China and re-presented as Indian sūtras. They are also the texts with the broadest social reach: filial piety, calendrical festival, divination, and post-mortem judgement.
- **State-protective Buddhism.** The two Chinese *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* recensions, particularly Yìjìng's "Right Discourse on the Dharma of Kings" chapter, supplied the dharmic ideology of East Asian Buddhist statecraft from Sui through Nara and beyond.
- **Filial piety as Buddhist genre.** The Ullambana cluster, the Tang *fùmǔ ēn* texts, the *Shíwáng jīng*, and the *Dìzàng púsà běnyuàn jīng* tradition (its earliest witnesses sit in this division) together constitute Buddhism's most successful response to Confucian objections about filial debt.
- **Translation history through multi-recension witnesses.** Several core texts survive in two or three Chinese versions spanning four to seven centuries — *Vimalakīrti* (Zhī Qiān, Kumārajīva, Xuánzàng), *Laṅkāvatāra* (Guṇabhadra, Bodhiruci, Śikṣānanda), *Bhaiṣajyaguru* (Xuánzàng + Yìjìng + earlier witnesses), *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Dharmakṣema + Yìjìng + Bǎoguì compendium). This makes KR6i an unusually rich laboratory for translation-history research.
- **The Chinese exegetical density.** The *Vimalakīrti* alone carries some twenty Chinese commentaries spanning Sui to Qīng, and the *Yuánjué jīng* almost as many. The exegetical superstructure here is comparable in scale to that built around the *Lotus*, even though no individual non-Lotus sūtra reaches the *Lotus*'s extreme commentarial density.

### Timeline

- 222–253 — Zhī Qiān's *Fóshuō wéimójié jīng* 佛說維摩詰經 [KR6i0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0075) — the first Chinese *Vimalakīrti*.
- 265–311 — *Fóshuō yúlán-pén jīng* 佛說盂蘭盆經 [KR6i0364](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0364), traditionally Dharmarakṣa, more likely Western Jin Sinitic apocryphon: founder of the East Asian Ghost Festival.
- 266–308 — *Fóshuō wénshū shīlì xiàn bǎozàng jīng* 佛說文殊師利現寶藏經 [KR6i0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0062) (Dharmarakṣa).
- 300 — *Xiánjié jīng* 賢劫經 [KR6i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0001) (Dharmarakṣa, Yǒngkāng 1) — earliest precisely dated text in the division and source of the thousand-Buddhas of the present aeon.
- 317–420 — *Fóshuō mílè lái shí jīng* 佛說彌勒來時經 [KR6i0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0036): the shortest Maitreya sūtra and probably the most archaic surviving recension.
