### Topics

- ***Foxing* 佛性 / Buddha-nature.** The central doctrine of the division. The MPNS articulates the position that all sentient beings — including *icchantikas* (一闡提 *yīchǎntí*), the class traditionally regarded as forever excluded from Buddhahood — possess Buddha-nature and are capable of attaining Buddhahood. This universalising claim is the foundation of mature East-Asian *tathāgatagarbha* doctrine (paralleling but distinct from its other principal scriptural vehicle the *Śrīmālā-sūtra* [KR6f0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0045)) and the conceptual underpinning of subsequent Chinese Buddhist soteriology through Chán, Huáyán and the *Awakening of Faith*.
- **The *Northern Recension* / *Southern Recension* doublet.** Dharmakṣema's 40-fascicle [KR6g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0001) *Běiběn* and Huìyán *et al.*'s 36-fascicle [KR6g0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0003) *Nánběn* coexist in the canon as the two parallel canonical texts of the same sūtra — the *Nánběn* re-organised into 25 chapters and harmonised with Fǎxiǎn's short [KR6g0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0022) recension, the *Běiběn* preserving the original Dharmakṣema chapter division. The doublet became one of the foundational data-points of Liú-Sòng-period Buddhist intellectual history, and the parallel-text method (reading the two against each other) became one of the canonical East-Asian exegetical techniques.
- **The Dàoshēng 道生 controversy and the doctrine of universal Buddha-nature.** [竺道生](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E9%81%93%E7%94%9F) Dàoshēng's pre-emptive insistence that even *icchantikas* possess Buddha-nature — formulated from Fǎxiǎn's [KR6g0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0022) short recension before Dharmakṣema's [KR6g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0001) full recension was available to confirm it — became the most-told story of Chinese Buddhist intellectual history. The controversy was the great theological debate of fifth-century Chinese Buddhism; its resolution in favour of Dàoshēng's universalism shaped all subsequent East-Asian Buddhist soteriology.
- **The *Nièpán jīng* as one of the three foundational *yuánjiào* 圓教 sūtras.** Together with the *[Avataṃsaka](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001)* and the *Lotus*, the *Nièpán jīng* is one of the three sūtras canonically classified as *yuánjiào* / "complete teaching" in Tiāntái doctrinal classification (*pànjiào* 判教); the canonical Tiāntái apparatus of Guàndǐng [KR6g0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0005) / [KR6g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0007) and Zhànrán [KR6g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0016) makes the *Nièpán jīng* the consummation of the Buddha's teaching career, doctrinally subordinate only to the *Lotus*.
- **The *běn yǒu jīn wú* 本有今無 verse and the metaphysics of Buddha-nature.** The famous verse of the MPNS — "originally existing, now non-existing; originally non-existing, now existing" — is the doctrinal crux of mature Buddha-nature theology, addressing the relation between the eternally-abiding Buddha-nature and the temporally-conditioned phenomenal world. Vasubandhu's [KR6g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0052) *Běn yǒu jīn wú jì lùn* makes this verse the explicit subject of its own *śāstra*.
- ***Mòfǎ* 末法 / decline-of-the-Dharma prophecy.** Several texts in the division — [KR6g0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0029) *Mahāmāyā-sūtra*, [KR6g0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0032) *Lián huā miàn jīng*, [KR6g0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0040) *Dānglái biàn jīng*, [KR6g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0041) *Fǎ miè jìn jīng* — articulate the standard Buddhist prophecy of the gradual decline and eventual extinction of the Dharma after the Buddha's parinirvāṇa. The *mòfǎ* doctrine becomes politically and devotionally consequential in Suí–Táng Buddhism (Sānjiējiào 三階教, Pure-Land soteriology, Buddhist apocalyptic literature) and is one of the principal canonical sources for those traditions.
- **The Tiāntái commentarial succession on the *Nièpán jīng*.** Guàndǐng (Suí) → Dàoxiān / Xíngmǎn (mid-Táng) → Zhànrán (Táng) → Zhìyuán (N. Sòng) constitutes one of the most genealogically explicit commentarial lineages in East Asian Buddhism: each generation rewrites and supplements the previous, the canonical [KR6g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0007) *Shū* of Guàndǐng becoming successively the subject of [KR6g0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0017)–[KR6g0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0018) *sījì*, then [KR6g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0016) *huìshū*, then [KR6g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0014) *kē* and [KR6g0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0019) *zhǐ guī*. The division is therefore the principal canonical site for studying the structural evolution of Chinese Buddhist commentary across half a millennium.
- **The *Yíjiào jīng* as the canonical short monastic exhortation.** Kumārajīva's [KR6g0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0043) *Yíjiào jīng* — at one fascicle, the shortest principal text in the division — is one of the most widely-chanted Buddhist texts in East Asian monastic life, and the principal site of *vinaya*-themed exhortation outside the *Vinaya-piṭaka* proper. The *Yíjiào jīng* commentarial tradition runs from Vasubandhu's [KR6g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0044) *Yíjiào jīng lùn* through the Sòng commentaries of Jìngyuán, Yuánzhào, and Guānfù, the joint Sòng–Míng *Bǔ zhù* of Shǒusuì / Liǎotóng [KR6g0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0047), and Zhìxù's late-Míng [KR6g0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0048) *Yíjiào jīng jiě*.
- ***Antarābhava* 中陰 / the intermediate state.** Zhú Fóniàn's [KR6g0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0031) *Zhōng yīn jīng* is one of the principal Chinese canonical sources for the doctrine of an intermediate-state existence between death and rebirth, a doctrine variously affirmed and denied across Buddhist schools and one of the principal Indian Abhidharma controversies entering East-Asian Buddhism through the *Nièpán bù*.
- **Political theology of the *Dà yún jīng*.** Dharmakṣema's [KR6g0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0033) *Dà fāngděng wúxiǎng jīng* / *Dà yún jīng* is one of the most politically consequential Mahāyāna scriptures in East Asian history: a Táng re-translation / forgery of it was used in 690 to justify Empress [武則天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%A6%E5%89%87%E5%A4%A9) Wǔ Zétiān's usurpation of the Táng throne, on the basis that the sūtra prophesies the appearance of a female cakravartin queen. The text became one of the foundational scriptures of imperial Buddhist political theology in China.
- **The Buddha's death-scene as a literary corpus.** The short sūtras T0390–T0396 ([KR6g0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0035)–[KR6g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0041)) constitute a small but coherent literature of the Buddha's *parinirvāṇa* as narrative and ritual event — the coffining, cremation, funeral, Mahākāśyapa's arrival, Vajrapāṇi's lamentation, the *abiding* of the Dharma. The corpus is the textual basis for Buddhist memorial liturgy and for the parinirvāṇa-iconography of East-Asian Buddhist art.
- **Pseudepigraphy and attribution problems.** The Indian-school authorial unity of Vasubandhu across [KR6g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0044), [KR6g0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0051), [KR6g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0052) is questioned in modern scholarship but preserved as canonical here. The Táng "re-translation" of the *Dà yún jīng* used by Wǔ Zétiān is widely regarded as a Chinese forgery rather than a genuine retranslation. Several short anonymous parinirvāṇa-narrative sūtras (T0392, T0394, T0396) are likely Chinese compositions rather than Indian translations.

## Division note: [KR6g 涅槃部 *Nièpán bù* — Buddhist Canon — Nirvāṇa Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6g` is the Kanripo mirror of the Taishō *Nièpán bù* 涅槃部 — the canonical division that gathers the Mahāyāna *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* (MPNS) corpus in its full transmissional and exegetical extent. In CANWWW the division is `div19`; the Taishō core runs from `T12N0374` (Dharmakṣema's 40-fascicle Northern Recension) through `T12N0396` and is preceded in the canon's architecture by the *Bǎojī bù* 寶積部 ([KR6f](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/), `div03`). `KR6g` extends the Taishō *Nièpán bù* by absorbing the entire commentarial superstructure attached to the *Nièpán jīng* and to its short companion-text the *Yíjiào jīng* 遺教經: the *jīngshū bù* Tiāntái cluster from Taishō volumes 37–38 (T1763–T1769), the Dūnhuáng MPNS-commentary fragments from volume 85 (T2764A, T2764B, T2765), the Indian *śāstra* layer on the *Yíjiào jīng* and on the *Nièpán jīng*'s doctrinal cruxes from volume 26 (T1527–T1529), the *Yíjiàojīnglùn shū* tradition from volume 40 (T1820), the *Manji Xùzàngjīng* commentaries on the MPNS and on the *Yíjiào jīng* (X656–X666, X845–X846), and a Northern Yongle-canon witness — 52 works in total.

The chronological span runs from Dharmarakṣa's 竺法護 late-third-century Western-Jìn translations of pre-MPNS parinirvāṇa material ([KR6g0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0024) *Fāngděng bān ní huán jīng* of c. 266–313, [KR6g0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0036) *Bān ní huán hòu guàn là jīng*) through to the mid-seventeenth-century late-Ming commentary of Ǒuyì Zhìxù 蕅益智旭 ([KR6g0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0048) *Yíjiàojīng jiě* of 1620–1655), with the active Indic-translation phase concentrated in the fifth century (Dharmakṣema, Fǎxiǎn, the Huìyán / Huìguān editorial team) and the active East-Asian commentarial phase running from the Liáng compiled commentary of Bǎoliàng 寶亮 ([KR6g0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0004) of c. 488–509) through the late-Míng synthesis. The principal transmissional traditions a reader must keep in mind are five: (i) the late-third- / early-fourth-century pre-MPNS translation lineage of Dharmarakṣa 竺法護 and Zhú Fóniàn 竺佛念 in Cháng'ān, whose short *bānníhuán* texts established the basic Chinese terminology for the Buddha's death-scene; (ii) the early-fifth-century Northern Liáng / Eastern Jìn translation lineage of Dharmakṣema 曇無讖 and Fǎxiǎn 法顯, which produced the two definitive Chinese MPNS recensions (long 40-fasc. and short 6-fasc.) within the same decade; (iii) the Liú-Sòng editorial lineage of Huìyán 慧嚴 and [慧觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E8%A7%80) Huìguān at Jiànkāng, which produced the harmonised *Southern Recension* (南本 *Nánběn*) [KR6g0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0003) that became the dominant text in southern monastic establishments; (iv) the Suí–Táng Tiāntái commentarial lineage of Guàndǐng 灌頂 ([KR6g0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0005), [KR6g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0007)) → Dàoxiān 道暹 / Xíngmǎn 行滿 ([KR6g0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0017)–[KR6g0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0018)) → Zhànrán 湛然 ([KR6g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0016)) → Zhìyuán 智圓 ([KR6g0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0006), [KR6g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0014), [KR6g0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0019)), which constituted the canonical scholastic apparatus on the *Nièpán jīng*; and (v) the Sòng–Míng *Yíjiào jīng* commentarial tradition of Jìngyuán 淨源, Shǒusuì 守遂, Yuánzhào 元照, Guānfù 觀復 and Zhìxù 智旭, which made Kumārajīva's [KR6g0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0043) one-fascicle *Yíjiào jīng* one of the most-commented short Buddhist texts in East Asia. The division is therefore the principal canonical arena for the Mahāyāna *tathāgatagarbha* / Buddha-nature (*fóxìng* 佛性) doctrine and for the literature of the Buddha's *parinirvāṇa* in all its scriptural, narrative and ritual dimensions.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra and its recensions

- *Dà bān niè pán jīng* 大般涅槃經 [KR6g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0001) — Dharmakṣema 曇無讖's 40-fascicle ***Northern Recension*** (*Běiběn* 北本, T0374, 414–421); the great Mahāyāna *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* and the principal scriptural source for the doctrine of universal Buddha-nature (*fóxìng* 佛性), including the controversial inclusion of *icchantikas* (一闡提 *yīchǎntí*). Together with the *Avataṃsaka* ([KR6e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001)) and the *Lotus*, it is one of the three foundational *yuánjiào* / "complete teaching" sūtras of East Asian Mahāyāna.
- *Dà bān niè pán jīng* 大般涅槃經 (*Southern Recension*) [KR6g0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0003) — Huìyán 慧嚴, [慧觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E8%A7%80) Huìguān *et al.*'s 36-fascicle ***Southern Recension*** (*Nánběn* 南本, T0375, 433–443); the Liú-Sòng editorial revision of Dharmakṣema's text, harmonised with Fǎxiǎn / Buddhabhadra's earlier short translation and re-divided into 25 chapters. The *Nánběn* / *Běiběn* doublet became the canonical East-Asian MPNS corpus, with the *Nánběn* preferred in the south and the *Běiběn* in the north.
- *Fó shuō dà bān ní huán jīng* 佛說大般泥洹經 [KR6g0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0022) — Fǎxiǎn 法顯's 6-fascicle ***short / pre-MPNS recension*** (T0376, 416–418), brought back from India by Fǎxiǎn on his great pilgrimage and translated in collaboration with Buddhabhadra at the Dàochǎngsì 道場寺 in Jiànkāng. Predating the full Dharmakṣema translation by a few years, it was the textual basis for Dàoshēng 道生's pre-emptive *Buddha-nature* doctrinal stance.
- *Dà bān niè pán jīng hòu fēn* 大般涅槃經後分 [KR6g0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0023) — Jñānabhadra 若那跋陀羅's 2-fascicle ***Latter Section*** (T0377, 660–700); the Táng supplementary continuation of the MPNS narrating the Buddha's actual *parinirvāṇa* and post-cremation events, the canonical capstone of the corpus.
- *Fó shuō fāngděng bān ní huán jīng* 佛說方等般泥洹經 [KR6g0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0024) (Dharmarakṣa 竺法護, W. Jìn) and *Bān ní huán hòu guàn là jīng* 般泥洹後灌臘經 [KR6g0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0036) (Dharmarakṣa) — the **earliest Chinese parinirvāṇa material**, predating the full MPNS tradition; provide the basic vocabulary (*bān ní huán* 般泥洹 / *bān niè pán* 般涅槃) and the ritual frame (*guàn là* — ablution-and-sacrifice) for the later corpus.

#### Major MPNS commentaries (Taishō *jīngshū bù*)

- *Dà bān niè pán jīng jí jiě* 大般涅槃經集解 [KR6g0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0004) — Bǎoliàng 寶亮 *et al.*'s 71-fascicle Liáng-period **compiled commentary** (T1763, c. 488–509), gathering the work of multiple Nièpán-school authorities into a single comprehensive apparatus; one of the largest single commentaries in pre-Táng Chinese Buddhism.
- *Dà bān niè pán jīng yì jì* 大般涅槃經義記 [KR6g0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0002) — Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn 淨影慧遠's 10-fascicle Suí commentary (T1764, 580–592); the foundational *Dìlùn*-school reading and one of the principal Suí scholastic statements of Buddha-nature doctrine.
- **Tiāntái MPNS commentaries by Guàndǐng 灌頂** — [KR6g0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0005) *Xuán yì* 玄義 (2 fasc., T1765, doctrinal preamble) and [KR6g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0007) *Shū* 疏 (33 fasc., T1767, full sectional commentary) of c. 597–632; the canonical Tiāntái apparatus on the *Nièpán jīng*, paralleling Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì* / *Wénjù* / *Zhǐguān* triad on the *Lotus*.
- *Niè pán jīng yóu yì* 涅槃經遊意 [KR6g0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0008) — Jízàng 吉藏's 1-fascicle Sānlùn-school "roving reflections" (T1768, 595–623); the Sānlùn alternative to the Tiāntái synthesis.
- *Niè pán zōng yào* 涅槃宗要 [KR6g0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0009) — Wǒnhyo 元曉's Sillan compendium on the doctrinal essence of the MPNS (T1769, 660–686); paralleling his [KR6f0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0067) *Zōngyào* on the *Larger Sukhāvatī*.
- *Niè pán xuán yì fā yuán jī yào* 涅槃玄義發源機要 [KR6g0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0006) — Zhìyuán 智圓's Northern-Sòng sub-commentary on Guàndǐng's *Xuán yì* (T1766, 990–1022); the Sòng *Shānwài* 山外 Tiāntái reading.
- **Dūnhuáng MPNS-commentary fragments** — [KR6g0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0010) *Nièpánjīng yì jì* (T2764A), [KR6g0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0011) *Dànièpánjīng yì jì juàn dì sì* (T2764B), [KR6g0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0012) *Nièpánjīng shū* (T2765); the Táng-period anonymous Dūnhuáng witnesses to the otherwise-lost early MPNS-commentary tradition.

#### MPNS commentaries in the *Manji Xùzàngjīng*

- *Niè pán jīng huìshū* 涅槃經會疏 [KR6g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0016) — the 36-fascicle composite "combined commentary" assembling Guàndǐng's *Shū* with Zhànrán's 湛然 Táng editorial revision and [本純](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%AC%E7%B4%94) Honjun's Edo-Japanese editorial *fēn huì* (X659); the standard Japanese-Tendai working text on the MPNS. Its prolegomenon [KR6g0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0013) *Xuán yì wén jù* (X656) and its outline [KR6g0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0015) *Tiáo gě* (X658) form a single editorial complex.
- **Sòng Tiāntái sub-commentaries on Guàndǐng's *Shū*** — [KR6g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0014) *Zhìdìng shū kē* 治定疏科 (10 fasc., X657, structural outline), [KR6g0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0019) *Sān dé zhǐ guī* 三德指歸 (19 fasc., X662, doctrinal sub-commentary) — both by Zhìyuán 智圓 of the Northern Sòng. Together they constitute the great *Shānwài*-school 山外 apparatus on the MPNS-commentary tradition.
- **Táng Tiāntái sub-commentaries (*sījì* 私記)** — [KR6g0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0017) *Sījì* of Xíngmǎn 行滿 (12 fasc., X660) and [KR6g0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0018) *Sījì* of Dàoxiān 道暹 (9 fasc., X661); the mid-Táng sub-commentarial layer between Guàndǐng and Zhànrán.
- **Yuán editorial works on the *Nánběn*** — [KR6g0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0020) *Kē Nánběn Nièpánjīng* 科南本涅槃經 ([師正](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B8%AB%E6%AD%A3) Shīzhèng, X663) and [KR6g0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0021) *Nièpán jīng huìshū jiě* 涅槃經會疏解 (Shīzhèng + [圓澄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%BE%84) Yuánchéng, X664); structural-outline and explication of the Southern Recension and its commentary tradition.

#### Related Mahāyāna sūtras (T12 0379–0388)

The Taishō editors grouped a cluster of independent Mahāyāna sūtras around the MPNS on grounds of doctrinal and narrative affinity — *samādhi*-doctrine, Mahāmāyā / Buddha-mother literature, *mòfǎ* prophecy, *antarābhava* (intermediate state):

- *Sì tóng zǐ sānmèi jīng* 四童子三昧經 [KR6g0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0025) — Jñānagupta 闍那崛多 (Suí, T0379), Mahāyāna *samādhi*-sūtra.
- *Dà bēi jīng* 大悲經 [KR6g0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0026) — Narendrayaśas 那連提耶舍 (N. Qí, T0380), the *Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra*.
- *Děng jí zhòng dé sānmèi jīng* 等集眾德三昧經 [KR6g0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0027) — Dharmarakṣa (W. Jìn, T0381), another *samādhi* sūtra; paralleled by [KR6g0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0028) *Jí yīqiè fúdé sānmèi jīng* (Kumārajīva 鳩摩羅什, Yáo-Qín, T0382, *Sarvapuṇya-samuccaya-samādhi*).
- *Mó hē mó yē jīng* 摩訶摩耶經 [KR6g0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0029) — Tánjǐng 曇景 (Xiāo-Qí, T0383), the *Mahāmāyā-sūtra* narrating the Buddha's parinirvāṇa from the perspective of his mother Mahā-māyā in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven; contains the standard *mòfǎ* 末法 prophecy of the decline of the Dharma.
- *Púsà cóng dōushùtiān jiàng shén mǔtāi shuō guǎng pǔ jīng* 菩薩從兜術天降神母胎說廣普經 [KR6g0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0030) — Zhú Fóniàn 竺佛念 (Yáo-Qín, T0384), the "descent from Tuṣita" sūtra. Paralleled by [KR6g0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0031) *Zhōng yīn jīng* 中陰經 (Zhú Fóniàn, T0385), the principal Chinese sūtra on the *antarābhava* / intermediate state.
- *Lián huā miàn jīng* 蓮華面經 [KR6g0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0032) — Narendrayaśas (Suí, T0386), prophecy of the destruction of the Dharma by King Mihirakula.
- *Dà fāngděng wúxiǎng jīng* 大方等無想經 [KR6g0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0033) — Dharmakṣema (N. Liáng, T0387) — the famous *Dà yún jīng* 大雲經 / *Mahāmegha-sūtra*, politically consequential in Táng history: a re-translation / forgery of it was used by Empress [武則天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%A6%E5%89%87%E5%A4%A9) Wǔ Zétiān in 690 to justify her usurpation, on the basis that the *Dà yún jīng* prophesies the appearance of a female cakravartin queen. Followed by the fragmentary [KR6g0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0034) *Dà yún wú xiǎng jīng juàn dì jiǔ* (T0388).

#### Buddha-parinirvāṇa narrative and ritual short sūtras (T390–T396)

A cluster of short anonymous and attributed sūtras transmitting the narrative and ritual surround of the Buddha's death-scene; the textual basis for monastic memorial liturgy:

- *Fó lín niè pán jì fǎ zhù jīng* 佛臨涅槃記法住經 [KR6g0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0035) — Xuánzàng 玄奘 (Táng, T0390); on the *abiding of the Dharma* (*fǎ zhù*) after the Buddha's death.
- *Fó miè dù hòu guān liǎn zàng sòng jīng* 佛滅度後棺斂葬送經 [KR6g0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0037) (anonymous, T0392) — on the coffining, cremation and funeral.
- *Jiāyè fù fó bān niè pán jīng* 迦葉赴佛般涅槃經 [KR6g0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0038) — Zhú Tánwúlán 竺曇無蘭 (E. Jìn, T0393), Mahākāśyapa's hastening to the Buddha's *parinirvāṇa*.
- *Fó rù niè pán mìjì jīngāng lìshì āiliàn jīng* 佛入涅槃密迹金剛力士哀戀經 [KR6g0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0039) (anonymous, T0394) — Vajrapāṇi's lamentation.
- *Fó shuō dāng lái biàn jīng* 佛說當來變經 [KR6g0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0040) — Dharmarakṣa (W. Jìn, T0395), prophecy of coming changes.
- *Fó shuō fǎ miè jìn jīng* 佛說法滅盡經 [KR6g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0041) (anonymous, T0396) — prophecy of the extinction of the Dharma; together with [KR6g0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0029) and [KR6g0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0032) one of the principal *mòfǎ* scriptural sources.
- *Fó shuō jiù hù shēn mìng jīng* 佛說救護身命經 [KR6g0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0042) — [比丘道真](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%94%E4%B8%98%E9%81%93%E7%9C%9F) Bǐqiū Dàozhēn (Fángshān 房山 *Shíjīng*) — a Fángshān stone-canon witness to a protective-incantation text grouped here on narrative grounds.

#### The *Yíjiào jīng* cluster

The *Yíjiào jīng* 遺教經 — Kumārajīva's one-fascicle rendering of the Buddha's last admonition — is the single most-chanted short Buddhist text in East Asian monastic life, and the principal site of *vinaya*-themed exhortation outside the *Vinaya-piṭaka* proper:

- *Fó chuí bān niè pán lüè shuō jiào jiè jīng* 佛垂般涅槃略說教誡經 [KR6g0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0043) — Kumārajīva 鳩摩羅什 (Yáo-Qín, T0389, 402–412); the foundational *Yíjiào jīng*. The Buddha's final disciplinary admonition delivered immediately before *parinirvāṇa*, gathering the essential instructions for the *saṅgha*.
- *Yíjiào jīng lùn* 遺教經論 [KR6g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0044) — Vasubandhu 天親 / Paramārtha 真諦 (Chén, T1529, 557–569); the Indian *śāstra*-commentary on the *Yíjiào jīng*.
- **Sòng–Míng *Yíjiàojīnglùn* commentaries** — [KR6g0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0045) Jìngyuán 淨源's *Lùn shū jié yào* 論疏節要 (T1820) with [袾宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%BE%E5%AE%8F) Zhūhóng's Míng supplementary annotation; [KR6g0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0046) Jìngyuán's Yongle-canon recension of the same work; [KR6g0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0049) Yuánzhào 元照's *Zhù fǎ jì* 住法記 (X845); [KR6g0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0050) Guānfù 觀復's *Lùn jì* 論記 (X846). Together they constitute the Sòng-period *Yíjiàojīnglùn* sub-commentarial corpus.
- **Sòng–Míng commentaries on the *Yíjiào jīng* itself** — [KR6g0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0047) *Bǔ zhù* 補註 of Shǒusuì 守遂 with Liǎotóng 了童's Míng supplementary annotation (X665); [KR6g0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0048) *Yíjiào jīng jiě* 遺教經解 of Ǒuyì Zhìxù 蕅益智旭 (X666, 1620–1655), the canonical late-Míng commentary by one of the *Four Great Masters of the Late Míng*.

#### *Śāstras* on the *Nièpán jīng* doctrine

- *Niè pán lùn* 涅槃論 [KR6g0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0051) — Vasubandhu 婆藪槃豆 / Dharmabodhi 達磨菩提 (N. Wèi, T1527, 508–535); the Indian *Nirvāṇa-śāstra* on Mahāyāna *parinirvāṇa* doctrine.
- *Niè pán jīng běn yǒu jīn wú jì lùn* 涅槃經本有今無偈論 [KR6g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0052) — Vasubandhu / Paramārtha (Chén, T1528, 557–569); the Indian commentary on the famous *běn yǒu jīn wú* 本有今無 ("originally existed, now non-existent") verse of the MPNS, doctrinally central to mature Buddha-nature theology.

### Important persons

- [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema, 385–433) — Central-Indian master at the Northern-Liáng court of Gūzàng 姑臧; translator of [KR6g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0001) the 40-fascicle *Northern Recension* MPNS (414–421), the foundational text of the division and one of the most consequential Mahāyāna scriptures in East Asia. Also responsible for [KR6g0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0033) the politically-consequential *Dà yún jīng*. Killed at the orders of [蒙遜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%AE%E6%B8%A0%E8%92%99%E9%81%9C) Mèngxùn in 433.
- [法顯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%A1%AF) (Fǎxiǎn, 337–422) — Eastern-Jìn pilgrim-monk, the first Chinese Buddhist to bring back an Indian text of the MPNS; translator (with Buddhabhadra) of [KR6g0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0022) the short pre-MPNS recension at Jiànkāng's Dàochǎngsì 道場寺. His *Fóguó jì* 佛國記 is the foundational pilgrimage record of Chinese Buddhism.
- [慧嚴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E5%9A%B4) (Huìyán, 363–443) — Liú-Sòng monk; principal editor (with [慧觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E8%A7%80) Huìguān) of [KR6g0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0003) the 36-fascicle *Southern Recension* MPNS, the harmonised Liú-Sòng working text that became dominant in southern monastic establishments.
- [寶亮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%B6%E4%BA%AE) (Bǎoliàng, 444–509) — Liáng-period master; principal compiler of [KR6g0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0004) the 71-fascicle *Nièpánjīng jí jiě*, the great Liáng compiled commentary that gathered the work of multiple earlier Nièpán-school authorities.
- [慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) (Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn 淨影慧遠, 523–592) — Suí *Dìlùn*-school exegete (not to be confused with the Lúshān Huìyuǎn of the Eastern Jìn); author of [KR6g0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0002) *Dà bān niè pán jīng yì jì*, the foundational Suí scholastic reading of the MPNS, alongside his commentaries on the *Larger Sukhāvatī* ([KR6f0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0065)), *Visualization Sūtra* ([KR6f0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0072)) and *Śrīmālā* ([KR6f0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0057)) in `KR6f`.
- [灌頂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%81%8C%E9%A0%82) (Guàndǐng / Zhāng'ān 章安, 561–632) — principal disciple of [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) Zhìyǐ and second patriarch of the Tiāntái 天台 school; author of the canonical Tiāntái MPNS apparatus [KR6g0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0005) *Xuán yì*, [KR6g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0007) *Shū* (33 fasc.) and the composite [KR6g0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0013) / [KR6g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0016) works. His commentaries are the doctrinal pivot of the Tiāntái reading of the *Nièpán jīng*.
- [吉藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%97%8F) (Jízàng, 549–623) — Sānlùn 三論 patriarch; author of [KR6g0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0008) *Niè pán jīng yóu yì*, the Sānlùn-school alternative to the Tiāntái synthesis. The *yóu yì* genre is one of his distinctive contributions across the Mahāyāna sūtra corpus.
- [元曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E6%9B%89) (Wǒnhyo, 617–686) — Sillan master; author of [KR6g0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0009) *Niè pán zōng yào*, parallel to his *Wúliàngshòujīng zōng yào* ([KR6f0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0067)) and other *zōng yào* compendia — the principal Sillan contribution to the division.
- [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) (Zhànrán / Jīngxī 荊溪, 711–782) — sixth Tiāntái patriarch and the great Táng restorer of the school; editorial revisor of Guàndǐng's *Shū* in [KR6g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0016) the *Huìshū* 會疏 (X659), the standard Tiāntái working text of the MPNS-commentary tradition.
- [行滿](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A1%8C%E6%BB%BF) (Xíngmǎn, c. 8th–9th c.) and [道暹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E6%9A%B9) (Dàoxiān, c. 8th–9th c.) — mid-Táng Tiāntái sub-commentators; authors of the twin *Sījì* 私記 [KR6g0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0017) and [KR6g0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0018) on Guàndǐng's *Shū*. Together they document the mid-Táng Tiāntái sub-commentarial layer between Guàndǐng and Zhànrán.
- [智圓](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%9C%93) (Zhìyuán, 976–1022) — Northern-Sòng Tiāntái master of the *Shānwài* 山外 (Off-Mountain) branch; author of [KR6g0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0006) *Niè pán xuán yì fā yuán jī yào*, [KR6g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0014) *Zhìdìng shū kē* (10 fasc.) and [KR6g0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0019) *Sān dé zhǐ guī* (19 fasc.) — the largest single attribution in the division's commentarial tradition and the foundational *Shānwài* apparatus on the MPNS.
- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Kumārajīva, 344–413) — Yáo-Qín Cháng'ān translator; translator of [KR6g0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0043) the *Yíjiào jīng*, the most widely-chanted short Buddhist text in East Asia, and of [KR6g0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0028) the *Sarvapuṇya-samuccaya-samādhi* sūtra.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha / Zhēndì, 499–569) — Chén-period translator at Jiànkāng; translator of [KR6g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0044) *Yíjiào jīng lùn* (Vasubandhu's *śāstra*) and [KR6g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0052) *Běn yǒu jīn wú jì lùn* (Vasubandhu's commentary on the MPNS's central verse). The principal vector of Indian *śāstra* commentary on the division into Chinese.
- [天親菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E8%A6%AA%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Vasubandhu / Tiānqīn / Pósǒupándòu 婆藪槃豆) — Indian *śāstra*-author; the three principal *śāstras* on the division's doctrine ([KR6g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0044) *Yíjiào jīng lùn*, [KR6g0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0051) *Niè pán lùn*, [KR6g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0052) *Běn yǒu jīn wú jì lùn*) are attributed to him in their Chinese transmission. The traditional Indian-school authorial unity is questioned in modern scholarship but preserved as canonical.

### Topics

- ***Foxing* 佛性 / Buddha-nature.** The central doctrine of the division. The MPNS articulates the position that all sentient beings — including *icchantikas* (一闡提 *yīchǎntí*), the class traditionally regarded as forever excluded from Buddhahood — possess Buddha-nature and are capable of attaining Buddhahood. This universalising claim is the foundation of mature East-Asian *tathāgatagarbha* doctrine (paralleling but distinct from its other principal scriptural vehicle the *Śrīmālā-sūtra* [KR6f0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6f/KR6f0045)) and the conceptual underpinning of subsequent Chinese Buddhist soteriology through Chán, Huáyán and the *Awakening of Faith*.
- **The *Northern Recension* / *Southern Recension* doublet.** Dharmakṣema's 40-fascicle [KR6g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0001) *Běiběn* and Huìyán *et al.*'s 36-fascicle [KR6g0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0003) *Nánběn* coexist in the canon as the two parallel canonical texts of the same sūtra — the *Nánběn* re-organised into 25 chapters and harmonised with Fǎxiǎn's short [KR6g0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0022) recension, the *Běiběn* preserving the original Dharmakṣema chapter division. The doublet became one of the foundational data-points of Liú-Sòng-period Buddhist intellectual history, and the parallel-text method (reading the two against each other) became one of the canonical East-Asian exegetical techniques.
- **The Dàoshēng 道生 controversy and the doctrine of universal Buddha-nature.** [竺道生](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E9%81%93%E7%94%9F) Dàoshēng's pre-emptive insistence that even *icchantikas* possess Buddha-nature — formulated from Fǎxiǎn's [KR6g0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0022) short recension before Dharmakṣema's [KR6g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0001) full recension was available to confirm it — became the most-told story of Chinese Buddhist intellectual history. The controversy was the great theological debate of fifth-century Chinese Buddhism; its resolution in favour of Dàoshēng's universalism shaped all subsequent East-Asian Buddhist soteriology.
- **The *Nièpán jīng* as one of the three foundational *yuánjiào* 圓教 sūtras.** Together with the *[Avataṃsaka](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0001)* and the *Lotus*, the *Nièpán jīng* is one of the three sūtras canonically classified as *yuánjiào* / "complete teaching" in Tiāntái doctrinal classification (*pànjiào* 判教); the canonical Tiāntái apparatus of Guàndǐng [KR6g0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0005) / [KR6g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0007) and Zhànrán [KR6g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0016) makes the *Nièpán jīng* the consummation of the Buddha's teaching career, doctrinally subordinate only to the *Lotus*.
- **The *běn yǒu jīn wú* 本有今無 verse and the metaphysics of Buddha-nature.** The famous verse of the MPNS — "originally existing, now non-existing; originally non-existing, now existing" — is the doctrinal crux of mature Buddha-nature theology, addressing the relation between the eternally-abiding Buddha-nature and the temporally-conditioned phenomenal world. Vasubandhu's [KR6g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0052) *Běn yǒu jīn wú jì lùn* makes this verse the explicit subject of its own *śāstra*.
- ***Mòfǎ* 末法 / decline-of-the-Dharma prophecy.** Several texts in the division — [KR6g0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0029) *Mahāmāyā-sūtra*, [KR6g0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0032) *Lián huā miàn jīng*, [KR6g0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0040) *Dānglái biàn jīng*, [KR6g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0041) *Fǎ miè jìn jīng* — articulate the standard Buddhist prophecy of the gradual decline and eventual extinction of the Dharma after the Buddha's parinirvāṇa. The *mòfǎ* doctrine becomes politically and devotionally consequential in Suí–Táng Buddhism (Sānjiējiào 三階教, Pure-Land soteriology, Buddhist apocalyptic literature) and is one of the principal canonical sources for those traditions.
- **The Tiāntái commentarial succession on the *Nièpán jīng*.** Guàndǐng (Suí) → Dàoxiān / Xíngmǎn (mid-Táng) → Zhànrán (Táng) → Zhìyuán (N. Sòng) constitutes one of the most genealogically explicit commentarial lineages in East Asian Buddhism: each generation rewrites and supplements the previous, the canonical [KR6g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0007) *Shū* of Guàndǐng becoming successively the subject of [KR6g0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0017)–[KR6g0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0018) *sījì*, then [KR6g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0016) *huìshū*, then [KR6g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0014) *kē* and [KR6g0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0019) *zhǐ guī*. The division is therefore the principal canonical site for studying the structural evolution of Chinese Buddhist commentary across half a millennium.
- **The *Yíjiào jīng* as the canonical short monastic exhortation.** Kumārajīva's [KR6g0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0043) *Yíjiào jīng* — at one fascicle, the shortest principal text in the division — is one of the most widely-chanted Buddhist texts in East Asian monastic life, and the principal site of *vinaya*-themed exhortation outside the *Vinaya-piṭaka* proper. The *Yíjiào jīng* commentarial tradition runs from Vasubandhu's [KR6g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0044) *Yíjiào jīng lùn* through the Sòng commentaries of Jìngyuán, Yuánzhào, and Guānfù, the joint Sòng–Míng *Bǔ zhù* of Shǒusuì / Liǎotóng [KR6g0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0047), and Zhìxù's late-Míng [KR6g0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0048) *Yíjiào jīng jiě*.
- ***Antarābhava* 中陰 / the intermediate state.** Zhú Fóniàn's [KR6g0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0031) *Zhōng yīn jīng* is one of the principal Chinese canonical sources for the doctrine of an intermediate-state existence between death and rebirth, a doctrine variously affirmed and denied across Buddhist schools and one of the principal Indian Abhidharma controversies entering East-Asian Buddhism through the *Nièpán bù*.
- **Political theology of the *Dà yún jīng*.** Dharmakṣema's [KR6g0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0033) *Dà fāngděng wúxiǎng jīng* / *Dà yún jīng* is one of the most politically consequential Mahāyāna scriptures in East Asian history: a Táng re-translation / forgery of it was used in 690 to justify Empress [武則天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%A6%E5%89%87%E5%A4%A9) Wǔ Zétiān's usurpation of the Táng throne, on the basis that the sūtra prophesies the appearance of a female cakravartin queen. The text became one of the foundational scriptures of imperial Buddhist political theology in China.
- **The Buddha's death-scene as a literary corpus.** The short sūtras T0390–T0396 ([KR6g0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0035)–[KR6g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0041)) constitute a small but coherent literature of the Buddha's *parinirvāṇa* as narrative and ritual event — the coffining, cremation, funeral, Mahākāśyapa's arrival, Vajrapāṇi's lamentation, the *abiding* of the Dharma. The corpus is the textual basis for Buddhist memorial liturgy and for the parinirvāṇa-iconography of East-Asian Buddhist art.
- **Pseudepigraphy and attribution problems.** The Indian-school authorial unity of Vasubandhu across [KR6g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0044), [KR6g0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0051), [KR6g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6g/KR6g0052) is questioned in modern scholarship but preserved as canonical here. The Táng "re-translation" of the *Dà yún jīng* used by Wǔ Zétiān is widely regarded as a Chinese forgery rather than a genuine retranslation. Several short anonymous parinirvāṇa-narrative sūtras (T0392, T0394, T0396) are likely Chinese compositions rather than Indian translations.

## Division note: [KR6i 經集部 *Jīngjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Sūtra Collection (Mahāyāna Sūtrasaṃgraha)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6i mirrors the Taishō Tripiṭaka's 經集部 (*Jīngjí bù*, "Sūtrasaṃgraha"), the catch-all division in which the Taishō editors gathered the Mahāyāna sūtras that did not belong to one of the canon's named text-cycles. The principal axis is Taishō nos. 425–847 across Vols. 14–17, corresponding to CANWWW `div11.xml`; the Kanripo arrangement supplements this with Xuzangjing (卍續) commentaries, a handful of Jiāxīng-zàng titles, and — at the tail end (KR6i0589–0596) — a small block of Yogācāra 論釋 that drifted into the *jīng* collection through their attachment to single-sūtra commentary. Texts in the other "named" divisions are explicitly excluded: Prajñāpāramitā (KR6a), Ratnakūṭa (KR6b), Mahāsannipāta (KR6c), Avataṃsaka (KR6d), Nirvāṇa (KR6e), Lotus (KR6f), Bhadrakalpika (KR6g) and the Āgamas (KR6h) are catalogued elsewhere.

Because *Jīngjí bù* is structurally residual, its scholarly profile is not generic. The "leftover" works concentrate, in fact, several of the most consequential sūtras in the entire Chinese Mahāyāna corpus — *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa*, *Śūraṅgamasamādhi*, *Samādhirāja*, *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*, the three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras*, the *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra* and the *Anūnatva-apūrṇatva-nirdeśa*, the *Bhaiṣajyaguru* corpus, the Maitreya cycle, and the major Sinitic apocrypha *Yuánjué jīng* 圓覺經, *Zhànchá shàn'è yèbào jīng* 占察善惡業報經, *Yúlánpén jīng* 盂蘭盆經, and the *Shíwáng jīng* 十王經. The transmissional pattern is therefore stratigraphic: an Eastern Hàn–Western Jin layer of single-fascicle sūtras translated by Ān Shìgāo, Zhī Qiān, and above all Dharmarakṣa; a Yáo Qín / Northern Liáng turning-point in which Kumārajīva, Buddhabhadra, and Dharmakṣema fix the literary canon; a sixth- and seventh-century Yogācāra wave (Bodhiruci, Paramārtha, Saṅghapāla, Divākara, Xuánzàng); a Tang aftermath that adds re-translations and the great commentarial schools (Zhìyǐ, Jízàng, Kuījī, Zōngmì); and a Sòng coda of Indian translations from Shīhù 施護, Fǎtiān 法天, and Fǎxián 法賢. The chronological depth is matched by a high commentarial density — the *Vimalakīrti* alone carries some twenty exegetical works in this division.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The *Vimalakīrti* cluster.** *Wéimójié suǒshuō jīng* 維摩詰所說經 [KR6i0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0076) (Kumārajīva, 406) is the canonical Chinese *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa* and the most influential single text in the division — it shaped Chinese Buddhist literary style and supplied the central image of the bodhisattva-householder. Zhī Qiān's earlier *Fóshuō wéimójié jīng* 佛說維摩詰經 [KR6i0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0075) (Wú, c. 223–253) and Xuánzàng's *Shuō wúgòuchēng jīng* 說無垢稱經 [KR6i0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0077) preserve the parallel recensions. The exegetical apparatus runs from Sui–Tang masters — Huìyuǎn 慧遠 [KR6i0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0079), Zhìyǐ 智顗 [KR6i0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0080)–[KR6i0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0081), Jízàng 吉藏 [KR6i0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0083)–[KR6i0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0084), Kuījī 窺基 [KR6i0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0085) — through Song Tiāntái revival and Ming–Qing commentary, ending with the Qīng *Wéimó jīng wúwǒ shū* [KR6i0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0095) tradition.

**The Maitreya cluster.** A tight block of six canonical sūtras (KR6i0030–0036) covers the lower-birth (*xiàshēng*) and upper-birth (*shàngshēng*) traditions, including *Fóshuō mílè lái shí jīng* 佛說彌勒來時經 [KR6i0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0036), the briefest and most archaic of the canonical Maitreya texts. Tang commentarial elaboration comes via Jízàng [KR6i0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0037), Kuījī [KR6i0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0038), the Korean exegete Wǒnhyo 元曉 [KR6i0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0039), and Gyeongheung 憬興 [KR6i0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0040) — a rare witness to Silla Buddhist scholarship inside the Chinese canon.

**The *Bhaiṣajyaguru* (Medicine Buddha) cluster.** *Yàoshī liúlí guāng rúlái běnyuàn gōngdé jīng* 藥師琉璃光如來本願功德經 [KR6i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0048) (Xuánzàng, 650) is the canonical East Asian standard, with the seven-Buddha expanded recension *Yàoshī liúlí guāng qī fó běnyuàn gōngdé jīng* [KR6i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0049) (Yìjìng, 707) and a Tang ritual-manual lineage. Tang Dunhuang exegesis survives in two anonymous *Yàoshī jīng shū* [KR6i0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0054)–[KR6i0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0055) preserved in Taishō Vol. 85, and Ming–Qing devotional commentary revives the cluster with Língyào 靈耀's *Yàoshī jīng zhíjiě* [KR6i0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0056) and the Ming repentance-liturgy tradition (KR6i0057–0058).

**The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Golden Light) cluster.** Dharmakṣema's *Jīnguāngmíng jīng* 金光明經 [KR6i0301](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0301) (Northern Liáng, c. 414–426) is the earliest complete Chinese witness; Yìjìng's *Jīnguāngmíng zuìshèng wáng jīng* 金光明最勝王經 [KR6i0303](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0303) (Táng, 703) renders the full Sanskrit recension and supplies the canonical "Right Discourse on the Dharma of Kings" chapter foundational to East Asian state-protective Buddhism. The commentarial chain includes Zhìyǐ–Guàndǐng 灌頂 [KR6i0304](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0304), Zhīlǐ 知禮 [KR6i0305](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0305), Jízàng [KR6i0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0308), and a Tang Esoteric layer.

**The *tathāgatagarbha* / Laṅkāvatāra cluster.** The doctrinal core of East Asian Buddha-nature thought sits inside KR6i: Buddhabhadra's *Dàfāngděng rúláizàng jīng* 大方等如來藏經 [KR6i0323](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0323) (c. 420), Bodhiruci's *Fóshuō bù zēng bù jiǎn jīng* 佛說不增不減經 [KR6i0325](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0325) (c. 525), the three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras* — Guṇabhadra's four-fascicle *Léngqié ābáduōluó bǎo jīng* 楞伽阿跋多羅寶經 [KR6i0327](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0327) (443), Bodhiruci's ten-fascicle *Rù léngqié jīng* 入楞伽經 [KR6i0328](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0328) (513), and Śikṣānanda's seven-fascicle *Dàshèng rù léngqié jīng* 大乘入楞伽經 [KR6i0329](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0329) (700–704) — and Divākara's *Dàshèng mìyán jīng* 大乘密嚴經 [KR6i0359](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0359) (676–688). The Laṅkāvatāra triad is foundational both for East Asian Yogācāra and for early Chán self-identification as the "Laṅkāvatāra School" (楞伽宗).

**The samādhi cluster.** Three central Indian samādhi-sūtras stand together: Kumārajīva's *Shǒulèngyán sānmèi jīng* 佛說首楞嚴三昧經 [KR6i0279](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0279) (c. 402–409 — to be distinguished sharply from the apocryphal *Lèngyán jīng* T945), his *Sīyì fàntiān suǒwèn jīng* 思益梵天所問經 [KR6i0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0218) (c. 402–405), and Narendrayaśas's *Yuèdēng sānmèi jīng* 月燈三昧經 [KR6i0276](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0276) (Northern Qí, 557–559), the canonical Chinese witness to the *Samādhirāja-sūtra*.

**The Ullambana / filial-piety cluster.** *Fóshuō yúlán-pén jīng* 佛說盂蘭盆經 [KR6i0364](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0364) (attrib. Dharmarakṣa, but widely considered a Western Jin Chinese apocryphon) and its short twin *Fóshuō bào'ēn fèng-pén jīng* 佛說報恩奉盆經 [KR6i0376](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0376) together founded the East Asian *zhōngyuán* / Ghost Festival. Zōngmì's *Yúlán-pén jīng shū* [KR6i0365](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0365) and the ten or so subsequent Song–Qīng sub-commentaries make the cluster one of the densest commentarial bodies in the division. The related *Fùmǔ ēn nán bào jīng* 佛說父母恩難報經 [KR6i0363](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0363) (and the apocryphal *Fùmǔ ēnzhòng jīng* tradition) carry the same filial-piety theme into popular Buddhism.

**The *Yuánjué jīng* (Perfect Enlightenment) cluster.** *Dàfāngguǎng yuánjué xiūduōluó liǎoyì jīng* 大方廣圓覺修多羅了義經 [KR6i0551](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0551) — attributed to Buddhatrāta but securely identified as a Tang Chinese apocryphon (c. 690–750) — together with Zōngmì's massive *Yuánjué jīng dàshū* [KR6i0555](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0555) and the long Sòng–Míng commentarial chain (KR6i0553–0574) constitute the textual base of the Huáyán–Chán synthesis Zōngmì engineered.

**The Sinitic apocrypha and divinatory / underworld cluster.** Alongside *Yuánjué jīng*, the division contains the *Zhànchá shàn'è yèbào jīng* 占察善惡業報經 [KR6i0545](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0545) (Sui-period Sinitic apocryphon, foundational to the Kṣitigarbha cult and the unique wooden-block divination liturgy), Zàngchuān 藏川's *Shíwáng jīng* 佛說地藏菩薩發心因緣十王經 [KR6i0583](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0583) and *Yùxiū shíwáng shēngqī jīng* [KR6i0584](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0584) (Late Tang, foundational to East Asian ten-kings underworld iconography), and the late *Huàzhū bǎomìng zhēn jīng* [KR6i0586](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0586) (Míng *zhēn-jīng*-genre fusion of Buddhist form, Daoist neidan imagery, and popular medicine).

**The Mañjuśrī cluster.** Dharmarakṣa's *Wénshū shīlì xiàn bǎozàng jīng* 佛說文殊師利現寶藏經 [KR6i0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0062) (c. 270–308), Saṅghapāla's *Wénshū shīlì wèn jīng* 文殊師利問經 [KR6i0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0069) (Liáng, 515–520 — a principal canonical source for the eighteen Indian sectarian schools), and a series of Tang–Sòng Mañjuśrī texts down to Fǎxián's late-Sòng *Fóshuō miàojíxiáng púsà suǒwèn dàshèng fǎluó jīng* 佛說妙吉祥菩薩所問大乘法螺經 [KR6i0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0074) (989–1000) trace the gradual standardization of Mañjuśrī's Chinese epithets — from older phonetic *Wénshūshīlì* to the standardized Sòng rendering *Miàojíxiáng*.

**The Yogācāra tail (KR6i0589–0596).** Bandhuprabha *et al.*'s *Fódì jīng lùn* 佛地經論 [KR6i0589](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0589) (Xuánzàng, 649), three Vasubandhu-style *upadeśa* commentaries translated by Bodhiruci [KR6i0590](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0590)–[KR6i0592](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0592) and Vimokṣaprajñā [KR6i0593](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0593), and a Dunhuang-derived *Dàshèng sìfǎ jīng* exegetical trio [KR6i0594](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0594)–[KR6i0596](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0596) sit at the catalog's end. They are structurally 釋經論 (commentaries on single sūtras), and in Taishō proper occupy Vol. 26; their inclusion here reflects the Kanripo principle of grouping sūtra commentaries with the parent sūtra division.

### Important persons

- [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) (Dharmarakṣa, c. 239–316) — the single most prolific translator in this division (43 catalogued titles): *Xiánjié jīng*, the early Mañjuśrī texts, the Maitreya core, and a substantial Western-Jin Mahāyāna sūtra corpus.
- [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) (Zhī Qiān, fl. c. 222–253) — early Wu-period sūtra translator; 27 titles here, including the first Chinese *Vimalakīrti*.
- [安世高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96%E9%AB%98) (Ān Shìgāo, fl. 148–168) — Eastern Hàn pioneer; 26 short *jīng* of meditation and ethics surviving in this division.
- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Kumārajīva, 344–413) — fixed the canonical Chinese versions of *Vimalakīrti*, *Śūraṅgamasamādhi*, *Viśeṣacintābrahma-paripṛcchā*, and a clutch of other doctrinally central sūtras.
- [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema, 385–433) — Northern Liáng translator of the earliest complete *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*.
- [佛陀跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Buddhabhadra, 359–429) — translator of the *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra*, opening the textual base of East Asian Buddha-nature doctrine.
- [求那跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Guṇabhadra, 394–468) — translator of the four-fascicle *Laṅkāvatāra*, the lineage text of early Chán.
- [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) (Bodhiruci, fl. 508–537) — Northern Wei Yogācāra translator; ten-fascicle *Laṅkāvatāra*, *Anūnatva-apūrṇatva*, several Vasubandhu *upadeśa*.
- [僧伽婆羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E5%A9%86%E7%BE%85) (Saṅghapāla, 460–524) — Liáng translator of the *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā*.
- [那連提耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A3%E9%80%A3%E6%8F%90%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) (Narendrayaśas, 517–589) — translator of the *Samādhirāja-sūtra*.
- [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) (Jñānagupta, 523–600) — Sui-period sūtra retranslator.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — canonical *Bhaiṣajyaguru*, the *Buddhabhūmi-śāstra*, and several authoritative re-translations.

### Topics

- **The residual category as doctrinal repository.** Because the Taishō editors used *Jīngjí bù* as the bin for sūtras lacking a named cycle, the division accumulated isolates of unusual doctrinal density — single-text founders of major traditions (*Vimalakīrti*, *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra*, *Yuánjué jīng*) sit beside short ritual texts. Reading the division requires constant attention to which texts are doctrinal pivots and which are devotional or apotropaic miniatures.
- **Tathāgatagarbha and the Laṅkāvatāra problem.** The three Chinese *Laṅkāvatāras* (KR6i0327–0329), the *Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra* [KR6i0323](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0323), the *Anūnatva-apūrṇatva-nirdeśa* [KR6i0325](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0325), and the *Ghanavyūha* [KR6i0359](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0359) together form the textual base from which East Asian Buddha-nature theory was synthesized — including the question of whether *ālayavijñāna* and *tathāgatagarbha* are identical, the doctrine that became canonical for Huáyán and Chán.
- **Samādhi literature.** The trio of *Śūraṅgamasamādhi*, *Samādhirāja*, and *Viśeṣacintā* offers a coherent Indian sūtra theory of the bodhisattva's contemplative attainments; this is distinct from — and historically prior to — the apocryphal *Lèngyán jīng* T945 with which the *Śūraṅgamasamādhi* is often confused.
- **Sinitic apocrypha and lay Buddhism.** *Yuánjué jīng*, *Zhànchá jīng*, *Yúlánpén jīng*, *Fùmǔ ēnzhòng jīng*, and the *Shíwáng jīng* corpus are the clearest cases in the Mahāyāna canon of texts produced in China and re-presented as Indian sūtras. They are also the texts with the broadest social reach: filial piety, calendrical festival, divination, and post-mortem judgement.
- **State-protective Buddhism.** The two Chinese *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* recensions, particularly Yìjìng's "Right Discourse on the Dharma of Kings" chapter, supplied the dharmic ideology of East Asian Buddhist statecraft from Sui through Nara and beyond.
- **Filial piety as Buddhist genre.** The Ullambana cluster, the Tang *fùmǔ ēn* texts, the *Shíwáng jīng*, and the *Dìzàng púsà běnyuàn jīng* tradition (its earliest witnesses sit in this division) together constitute Buddhism's most successful response to Confucian objections about filial debt.
- **Translation history through multi-recension witnesses.** Several core texts survive in two or three Chinese versions spanning four to seven centuries — *Vimalakīrti* (Zhī Qiān, Kumārajīva, Xuánzàng), *Laṅkāvatāra* (Guṇabhadra, Bodhiruci, Śikṣānanda), *Bhaiṣajyaguru* (Xuánzàng + Yìjìng + earlier witnesses), *Suvarṇaprabhāsa* (Dharmakṣema + Yìjìng + Bǎoguì compendium). This makes KR6i an unusually rich laboratory for translation-history research.
- **The Chinese exegetical density.** The *Vimalakīrti* alone carries some twenty Chinese commentaries spanning Sui to Qīng, and the *Yuánjué jīng* almost as many. The exegetical superstructure here is comparable in scale to that built around the *Lotus*, even though no individual non-Lotus sūtra reaches the *Lotus*'s extreme commentarial density.

# 大小乘釋律部 (X38)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 18 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6k 律部 *Lǜ bù* — Buddhist canon — Vinaya (monastic discipline)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/): 18 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6k 律部 *Lǜ bù* — Buddhist canon — Vinaya (monastic discipline)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6k` 律部 (*Lǜ bù*, "Vinaya section") is the Kanripo mirror of the Vinaya division of the Chinese Buddhist canon — the canonical *Vinaya-piṭaka* together with its Indic and East-Asian exegetical and ritual-procedural literature. In CANWWW  the material is distributed across three divisions: `div13` 律部 holds the Vinayas proper and their *prātimokṣa-*, *karman-* and *paripṛcchā-*satellites (T22 No. 1421 — T24 No. 1504); `div14` 律疏部 holds the principal Suí–Tang exegetical layer (T40 Nos. 1804–1815, plus T45 Nos. 1892–1910); `div27` 續律疏部 holds the later Sòng–Míng–Qīng Chinese sub-commentaries together with the Japanese scholastic apparatus. Kanripo `KR6k` integrates these three CANWWW divisions and supplements them with a large Wàn xùzàng 卍續藏 (X) commentarial tail, so that 263 works are catalogued here in total — roughly the same order of magnitude as the *Prajñāpāramitā* division [KR6c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/) but with a quite different shape: where the *Bōrě bù* is anchored by a small handful of recurrently retranslated Indic sūtras, the Vinaya division is anchored by five Indic disciplinary corpora belonging to five different *nikāya* schools, all surviving only in their Chinese form, together with a much larger East-Asian scholastic and ritual-procedural superstructure.

The corpus falls into six historically and doctrinally distinct strata. (1) The **early-fifth-century translation wave** (404–431) at Chángān and Jiànyè brought into Chinese the full disciplinary literature of four Indic *nikāya* schools — the *Shísòng lǜ* 十誦律 of the Sarvāstivāda, the *Sìfēn lǜ* 四分律 of the Dharmaguptaka, the *Móhēsēngqí lǜ* 摩訶僧祇律 of the Mahāsāṃghika, and the *Wǔfēn lǜ* 五分律 of the Mahīśāsaka — together with supplementary texts of the Kāśyapīya and Sammitīya. The Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṃghika, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas survive in no other language, so this stratum is the principal evidentiary base for *all* modern comparative-Vinaya scholarship (Clarke 2015; *cf.* Wilkinson §29.5.7.6). (2) The **Tang *Sìfēnlǜ* scholastic synthesis** at Chángān (620–697) saw the *Sìfēn lǜ* gradually displace the *Shísòng lǜ* as the practical Vinaya of Chinese monasticism, under three competing exegetical schools — Fǎlì's 法礪 ([法礪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%A4%AA)) Xiāngbù 相部, Dàoxuān's 道宣 ([道宣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%A3)) Nánshān 南山, and Huáisù's 懷素 ([懷素](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E7%B4%A0)) Dōngtǎ 東塔 — of which the Nánshān school's victory under the imperial decree of Dàizōng (777) made Dàoxuān's *San dàbù* 三大部 the canonical Chinese Vinaya curriculum thereafter. (3) The **Yìjìng Mūlasarvāstivāda programme** (700–714) translated the disciplinary corpus of the late-Indic Mūlasarvāstivāda — by then the dominant Vinaya school of Indian Buddhism and (still later) the canonical Vinaya of the Tibetan, Mongolian, and Bhutanese traditions — into Chinese as a single eighteen-text *vastu*-by-*vastu* programme, but this Vinaya never displaced the *Sìfēn* in Chinese practice. (4) The **Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* stream** is anchored by the apocryphal *Fànwǎng jīng* 梵網經 ([KR6k0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0076), attributed to Kumārajīva but Chinese in origin) and runs in parallel to the school-Vinaya tradition, generating its own large commentarial corpus (Zhìyǐ 智顗, Fǎzàng 法藏, Wǒnhyo 元曉, Tàixián 太賢, Yúnqī Zhūhóng 雲棲袾宏, Ǒuyì Zhìxù 蕅益智旭); the alternative *Yogācāra*-school *bodhisattva-precepts* (Maitreya / Asaṅga, translated by Dharmakṣema and re-translated by Xuánzàng) provided the Mahāyāna stream with a second textual base. (5) The **Sòng *Língzhī*-school revival** (Yǔnkān 允堪 1005–1061; Yuánzhào 元照 1048–1116; Shǒuyī 守一 / Miàolián 妙蓮 in the Southern Sòng) produced an extensive sub-commentarial apparatus on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù*, recovered the doctrine of the precept-body (戒體 *jiètǐ*), and re-anchored Vinaya practice in the Tiāntái doctrinal system. (6) The **late-Míng / Qīng Vinaya revival** (Yúnqī Zhūhóng, Zhìxù, Dúté 讀體 1601–1679 at Bǎohuáshān 寶華山, Hóngzàn 弘贊 1611–1685 at Dǐnghú-shān 鼎湖山, the *Sānfēng* line of Fǎzàng 法藏 1573–1635) re-standardised Chinese ordination practice through the new *sāntán* 三壇 (three-platform) ordination system, generated the daily-use Vinaya manual that has remained in use to the present (*Píní rìyòng qièyào* [KR6k0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0224)), and produced the most thorough Qīng-period commentaries on every layer of the disciplinary tradition.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The four (then five) school-Vinayas

- *Sìfēn lǜ* 四分律 [KR6k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0009) — the **Dharmaguptaka** Vinaya translated 410–412 by [佛陀耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D) (Buddhayaśas) and [竺佛念](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E4%BD%9B%E5%BF%B5) (Zhú Fóniàn). After the Tang imperial decree of 777 the canonical Chinese Vinaya and the operational basis of Chinese, Korean, Japanese, and Vietnamese monasticism to the present. Its *bhikṣu-prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0010) / [KR6k0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0011); the *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0012); the early *karmavācanā* compendia [KR6k0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0013) [KR6k0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0014) [KR6k0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0015).
- *Shísòng lǜ* 十誦律 [KR6k0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0016) — the **Sarvāstivāda** Vinaya translated 404–409 by [弗若多羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%97%E8%8B%A5%E5%A4%9A%E7%BE%85) (Puṇyatāra) and [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Kumārajīva). The first complete Indian Vinaya translated into Chinese and the dominant Vinaya of southern-Chinese monasticism through the Liú-Sòng and Qí–Liáng. Its *prātimokṣa* is [KR6k0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0017) / [KR6k0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0018); the *karmavācanā* manuals [KR6k0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0019) [KR6k0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0020); the principal Indic commentary [KR6k0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0021) *Sàpóduō pínì pípóshā* and the *mātṛkā* [KR6k0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0022).
- *Móhēsēngqí lǜ* 摩訶僧祇律 [KR6k0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0006) — the **Mahāsāṃghika** Vinaya translated 416–418 by [法顯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%A1%AF) (Fǎxiǎn) and [佛陀跋陀羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85) (Buddhabhadra), based on the manuscript Fǎxiǎn brought back from Pāṭaliputra. #### Dàoxuān's *Three Great Works* of the Nánshān school

The institutional triad of the Tang *Sìfēnlǜ* curriculum, codified at Zhōngnánshān 終南山 by Dàoxuān between 626 and 667:

- *Sìfēn lǜ shānfán bǔquē xíngshì chāo* 四分律刪繁補闕行事鈔 [KR6k0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0128) (T1804) — the procedural manual of monastic practice; the most-studied Vinaya book in pre-modern East Asia.
- *Sìfēn lǜ shānbǔ suíjī jiémó* 四分律刪補隨機羯磨 [KR6k0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0046) (T1808) — the codified *karmavācanā* compendium for all monastic legal acts.
- *Sìfēn lǜ bǐqiū hánzhù jièběn* 四分律比丘含注戒本 [KR6k0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0131) (T1806) — Dàoxuān's annotated *prātimokṣa* recension; with the parallel *Sìfēn bǐqiūnī chāo* 四分比丘尼鈔 [KR6k0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0155) for the women's saṅgha.

Around the *San dàbù* runs the principal Tang *Nánshān* sub-commentarial cluster — Dàoxuān's own *Yìchāo* 義鈔 [KR6k0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0176), the Five-Dynasties *Jiǎnzhèng jì* [KR6k0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0167) of Jǐng Xiāo 景霄, and the eighth-century *Sōuxuán lù* [KR6k0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0162) of Zhì Hóng 志鴻; the Tang Xiāngbù tradition is represented by Fǎlì's *Shū* [KR6k0161](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0161) with Dìngbīn's *Shìzōng yìjì* [KR6k0163](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0163) and Dìngbīn's *Bǐqiū jièběn shū* [KR6k0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0132); the Tang Dōngtǎ tradition by Huáisù's *Kāizōng jì* [KR6k0165](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0165) and his alternative *karmavācanā* recensions [KR6k0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0047) [KR6k0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0048).

The principal Sòng *jì* — running line-by-line sub-commentaries on Dàoxuān's *San dàbù* by Yǔnkān 允堪 and Yuánzhào 元照, the two pillars of the *Língzhī* 靈芝 revival — fill out the Vinaya scholastic apparatus: Yuánzhào's *Zīchí jì* [KR6k0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0129) on the *Xíngshì chāo*; his *Xíngzōng jì* [KR6k0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0146) on the *Hánzhù jièběn shū*; his *Jìyuán jì* [KR6k0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0158) on the *Suíjī jiémó shū*; Yǔnkān's *Fāhuī jì* [KR6k0144](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0144) on the same; the *Fǔyào jì* [KR6k0177](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0177) on the *Yìchāo*; the Japanese *Zīxíng chāo* [KR6k0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0130) by Shōen 照遠 (14th c., Tō-ji Vinaya scholar). Yuánzhào's wider Vinaya prose — the *Zhīyuán jí* [KR6k0217](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0217), *Bǔxù Zhīyuán jí* [KR6k0218](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0218), *Zhīyuán yíbiān* [KR6k0216](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0216) — preserves the doctrinal foundations of the *Língzhī* revival.

#### Dàoxuān's wider Vinaya treatises

A distinct cluster of nine Dàoxuān works on institutional and ritual aspects of monastic discipline that fall outside the *San dàbù* proper:

- *Jiètán tújīng* 戒壇圖經 [KR6k0178](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0178) — the canonical Tang manual on the architectural form of the ordination platform; the foundational document for every East-Asian Vinaya-school ordination hall.
- *Jìngxīn jièguān fǎ* 淨心戒觀法 [KR6k0179](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0179) — Vinaya observance integrated with meditative practice.
- *Zhāngfú yí* 釋門章服儀 [KR6k0180](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0180) — the canonical regulation of monastic vestments.
- *Liàngchù qīngzhòng yí* 量處輕重儀 [KR6k0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0181) — the disposition of a deceased monk's property.
- *Guījìng yí* 釋門歸敬儀 [KR6k0182](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0182) — refuge-taking.
- *Xínghù lǜyí* 教誡新學比丘行護律儀 [KR6k0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0183) — novice instruction.
- *Lǜxiàng gǎntōng zhuàn* 律相感通傳 [KR6k0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0184) — the hagiographic Wèituó 韋陀 tradition.
- *Qíhuánsì tújīng* 中天竺舍衛國祇洹寺圖經 [KR6k0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0185) — the cosmographic blueprint of the standard Buddhist monastery.

The cluster's Sòng running commentaries — Yuánzhào and Liángxìn's *Yìngfǎ jì* [KR6k0214](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0214) on the *Zhāngfú yí*; Yuánzhào's *Liùwù tú* [KR6k0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0186) (the *Pratītyasamutpāda* of robes and bowl); Miàoshēng's *Sānyī xiǎnzhèng tú* [KR6k0254](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0254) and *Liùwù tú biàné* [KR6k0187](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0187) — together with the Tiāntái-line subcommentary *Tōngzhēn jì* [KR6k0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0253) and *Hùfǎ jì* [KR6k0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0252) on the *Guījìng yí* — preserve the most extensive Sòng-period institutional-Vinaya scholarship.

#### The *Fànwǎng jīng* + Mahāyāna *bodhisattva-vinaya* cluster

The Mahāyāna disciplinary stream is anchored by the *Brahma-net Sūtra*, the foundational scripture of East-Asian *bodhisattva-precepts*, generating one of the densest commentarial clusters in the entire Buddhist canon:

- *Fànwǎng jīng* 梵網經 [KR6k0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0076) (T1484) — canonically ascribed to Kumārajīva but widely recognised as a Chinese apocryphon composed c. 440–480; the canonical scripture of the Mahāyāna ten-major-precepts and forty-eight-minor-precepts system. With Kūkai's [空海](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A9%BA%E6%B5%B7) Shingon *Fànwǎngjīng kāití* [KR6k0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0077).
- The **Tang scholastic commentarial cluster** spans every major doctrinal school. Tiāntái: Zhìyǐ–Guàndǐng *Púsàjiè yìshū* [KR6k0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0078) and its Tang revision by Míngkuàng [KR6k0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0079) and Guàndǐng's independent *Yìshū* [KR6k0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0084). Huáyán: Fǎzàng *Púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0080). The Silla/Korean cluster: Wǒnhyo *Sījì* [KR6k0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0090) (the Korean scholastic foundation), Ŭijŏk *Púsà jièběn shū* [KR6k0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0082) (Silla Yogācāra), Tàixián *Gǔjì jì* [KR6k0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0083), Sŭngjang *Shùjì* [KR6k0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0091), and the Cí'ēn Yogācāra readings of Zhī Zhōu [KR6k0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0092) and Fǎ Xiǎn [KR6k0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0093).
