## Division note: [KR6o 論集部 *Lùnjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Treatise Collection](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6o corresponds to the *Lùnjí bù* 論集部 of the Taishō canon (vol. 32, nos. 1628–1692), together with the commentarial overflow in vol. 44 (nos. 1839–1850) and a small group of Dūnhuáng-recovered manuscripts in vol. 85 (nos. 2813–2816). The division is the canon's general miscellany of doctrinal treatises (*lùn* 論, śāstra) and the verse-collections (*sòng* 頌, *zàn* 讚, *gāthā* 伽他) attached to them. Unlike the dedicated divisions for Mādhyamaka and Yogācāra commentary on specific sūtras (`KR6m` 釋經論部, `KR6n` 毘曇部, 瑜伽部), KR6o gathers freestanding śāstras that do not belong to a single school or sūtra-commentary lineage: hetuvidyā (yīnmíng 因明) logic, Madhyamaka and Sautrāntika doctrinal works, the *Satyasiddhi-śāstra* of the 成實宗 school, *pratītyasamutpāda* tracts, *bodhicitta* literature, the *Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda* (*Awakening of Faith*) corpus, the Sino-Buddhist *Milindapañha* (*Nā xiān bǐqiū jīng*), and an extensive stotra/*gāthā* section. 

Chronologically the division spans c. 150 CE (the Indian source-strata of treatises by Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva, Dignāga) through 1911 (a late-Qīng vernacular gloss on *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn*), with the densest layers in (i) the fifth-/sixth-century translation projects of Kumārajīva, Paramārtha and Bodhiruci, (ii) the Táng Xuánzàng–Yìjìng era, (iii) the Northern Sòng translation bureau under Tiānxīsāi 天息災, Dānapāla 施護 and Dharmadeva 法天 (c. 982–1000), and (iv) the Heian–Kamakura and late-Míng waves of native East-Asian commentary on *yīnmíng* and *Qǐxìnlùn*. The principal transmissional issue throughout is the apocryphal or pseudepigraphic status of several of its most influential texts — *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn*, *Shì móhēyǎn lùn*, *Zhāng suǒzhī lùn*, the Sino-Tibetan-Mongol *Bāsībā* tract — for which East-Asian and modern scholarship has reached very different conclusions.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **Yīnmíng 因明 (Buddhist logic) cluster** — *Yīnmíng zhènglǐmén lùn běn* 因明正理門論本 [KR6o0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0001) (Dignāga 大域龍, tr. Xuánzàng), *Yīnmíng rù zhènglǐ lùn* 因明入正理論 [KR6o0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0003) (Śaṅkarasvāmin 商羯羅主, tr. Xuánzàng), and a parallel re-translation by Yìjìng [KR6o0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0002) form the doctrinal core of East-Asian Buddhist logic; the commentarial chain runs through Shéntài 神泰 [KR6o0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0007), Kuījī 窺基's *Yīnmíng dàshū* 因明大疏 [KR6o0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0008), Wǒnhyo's *Pànbǐliàng lùn* 判比量論 [KR6o0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0034), the Heian *Yīnmíng lùnshū míngdēng chāo* 因明論疏明燈抄 [KR6o0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0009) of Zenju 善珠, and the Edo *Yīnmíng dàshū róngguàn chāo* [KR6o0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0011) of Hōtan 鳳潭.
- **Nāgārjuna's logical-Madhyamaka treatises** — *Huízhèng lùn* 迴諍論 [KR6o0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0004) (*Vigrahavyāvartanī*), *Fāngbiàn xīn lùn* 方便心論 [KR6o0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0005) (*Upāyahṛdaya*), and *Rúshí lùn* 如實論 [KR6o0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0006) (*Tarkaśāstra*, tr. Paramārtha) preserve the earliest layer of Indian Buddhist epistemology.
- **Satyasiddhi-śāstra** — *Chéngshí lùn* 成實論 [KR6o0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0050) (Harivarman 訶梨跋摩, tr. Kumārajīva 411–412); the foundational text of the short-lived Chinese 成實宗 school and a major bridge between Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma and emerging Mahāyāna.
- **Doctrinal tracts of the Paramārtha and Bodhiruci circles** — *Suíxiāng lùn* 隨相論 [KR6o0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0045), *Sìdì lùn* 四諦論 [KR6o0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0051), *Lìshì āpítán lùn* 立世阿毘曇論 [KR6o0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0048), *Shíèr yīnyuán lùn* 十二因緣論 [KR6o0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0055), *Típó púsà pò lèngqié jīng zhōng wàidào xiǎochéng sìzōng lùn* 提婆菩薩破楞伽經中外道小乘四宗論 [KR6o0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0043) and its companion 涅槃論 [KR6o0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0044); together they constitute the sixth-century North Indian doxographic and ontological strata in Chinese translation.
- **Bodhicitta cluster** — Centred on the *Pútí xíng jīng* 菩提行經 [KR6o0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0067) (Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatāra* in Tiānxīzāi's Sòng-period rendering), with *Pútí zīliáng lùn* 菩提資糧論 [KR6o0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0065), *Guǎng shì pútíxīn lùn* 廣釋菩提心論 [KR6o0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0069), and the Vajrayāna *Jīngāngdǐng yújiā zhōng fā ānòuduōluó sānmiǎo sānpútí xīn lùn* 金剛頂瑜伽中發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心論 [KR6o0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0070) (attr. Nāgārjuna, tr. Amoghavajra 不空), which became the principal *bodhicitta* text of Shingon and attracted a dense Heian–Kamakura commentarial layer ([KR6o0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0071)–[KR6o0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0075)).
- **Awakening of Faith corpus** — *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn* 大乘起信論 attr. Aśvaghoṣa 馬鳴菩薩, in the Paramārtha [KR6o0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0078) and Śikṣānanda 實叉難陀 [KR6o0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0079) recensions; the single most consequential text of the division and arguably of East-Asian Buddhism, generating an enormous commentarial tradition represented here by Huìyuǎn 慧遠 of Jìngyǐng [KR6o0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0100), Wǒnhyo 元曉 [KR6o0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0103)/[KR6o0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0104), Fǎzàng 法藏 [KR6o0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0105)/[KR6o0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0106), Zǐxuán 子璿 [KR6o0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0107), Taehyŏn 太賢 [KR6o0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0108), Zhìxù 智旭 [KR6o0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0109), and late-Míng/Qīng glosses [KR6o0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0114)–[KR6o0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0120); plus the Dūnhuáng-recovered Tánkuàng 曇曠 layer [KR6o0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0121)/[KR6o0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0122) and an anonymous *Qǐxìnlùn zhù* [KR6o0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0123) preserved as T2814.
- **Shì móhēyǎn lùn 釋摩訶衍論 sub-cluster** — *Shì móhēyǎn lùn* [KR6o0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0084), attributed to Nāgārjuna and a translator (Vṛddhimati 筏提摩多) for whom no other works survive; almost certainly a late-eighth-century Sino-Korean apocryphon, but enormously influential in Japanese Shingon and Tendai exegesis, with thirteen commentaries here ([KR6o0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0085)–[KR6o0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0097)).
- **Apocryphal and pseudepigraphic foundational treatises** — *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn* 大宗地玄文本論 [KR6o0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0098) attr. Mǎmíng / tr. Paramārtha (very probably a Sui-Tang Chinese composition); *Zhāng suǒzhī lùn* 彰所知論 [KR6o0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0049) composed in Chinese by ʼPhags-pa Blo-gros rgyal-mtshan 八思巴 in 1278 for Qubilai's heir Zhēnjīn 真金.
- **Nā xiān bǐqiū jīng 那先比丘經 (Milindapañha)** — Two parallel early Chinese recensions [KR6o0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0124) and [KR6o0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0125), the principal Chinese witness to the Theravāda *Milindapañha* tradition.
- **Stotra / verse-praise (zàn 讚 / sòng 頌 / gāthā 伽他) cluster** — Three Chinese translations of Nāgārjuna's *Suhṛllekha* (Letter to King Gautamīputra): *Lóngshù púsà wèi Chántuójiā wáng shuō fǎyào jì* 龍樹菩薩為禪陀迦王說法要偈 [KR6o0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0127), *Quànfā zhū wáng yào jì* 勸發諸王要偈 [KR6o0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0128), and *Lóngshù púsà quànjiè wáng sòng* 龍樹菩薩勸誡王頌 [KR6o0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0129); plus *Yī bǎi wǔshí zàn fó sòng* 一百五十讚佛頌 [KR6o0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0135) (Mātṛceṭa, tr. Yìjìng), *Zàn fǎjiè sòng* 讚法界頌 [KR6o0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0130), *Fú gài zhèngxíng suǒjí jīng* 福蓋正行所集經 [KR6o0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0126), and the Sòng-period block of brief hymns [KR6o0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0130)–[KR6o0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0143).

- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) — translator of the *yīnmíng* core (Dignāga's *Nyāyamukha*, Śaṅkarasvāmin's *Nyāyapraveśa*) and of doctrinal compendia (*Yuánshēng lùn*, *Pútí zīliáng lùn*), founder of the East-Asian *yīnmíng* tradition.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) — re-translator of the *Nyāyamukha* [KR6o0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0002), the *Suhṛllekha* [KR6o0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0129), the *Bǎo xíng wáng zhèng lùn* [KR6o0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0061), and of several treatises (*Shǒuzhàng lùn* [KR6o0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0062), *Zhǐguān mén lùn sòng* [KR6o0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0060)) reflecting late-seventh-century Indian doctrinal style.

- [大域龍菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A7%E5%9F%9F%E9%BE%8D%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dignāga) and [商羯羅主菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%95%86%E7%BE%AF%E7%BE%85%E4%B8%BB%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Śaṅkarasvāmin) — Indian founders of Buddhist *pramāṇa* logic, whose texts head the division.

### Topics

- **Buddhist logic (yīnmíng 因明 / hetuvidyā)** — the structure of the three-membered syllogism (三支比量), the analysis of the nine reasons (九句因) and the four kinds of pseudo-reason (四相違), the boundary between perception (現量) and inference (比量); a topic that runs from Dignāga's *Nyāyamukha* [KR6o0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0001) through Kuījī's *Dàshū* [KR6o0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0008) and the Japanese *Sìxiāngwéi* sub-commentaries [KR6o0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0014)–[KR6o0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0017) to late-Míng synthetic restatements [KR6o0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0026)–[KR6o0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0029).
- **The status of the *Awakening of Faith* and the *Shì móhēyǎn lùn*** — whether they are translations of lost Indian originals or East-Asian (Chinese, Korean, or possibly Central-Asian) compositions; the textual history of the doubled *Qǐxìnlùn* translation under Paramārtha and Śikṣānanda; the philological independence (or not) of the *Shì móhēyǎn lùn* from the *Qǐxìnlùn* itself. This is the principal modern philological debate in the division.
- **Pseudepigraphy and translator-attribution forgery** — *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn* and *Shì móhēyǎn lùn* travel in the canon under unverifiable translator names (Paramārtha, Vṛddhimati 筏提摩多), allowing comparison of the formal traits by which East-Asian apocrypha were inserted into a canon of putative Indian śāstras.
- **The *bodhicitta* tradition's bifurcation** — between the exoteric, ethical reading represented by Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatāra* [KR6o0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0067) and the esoteric, ritual reading represented by the Vajraśekhara *Pútíxīn lùn* [KR6o0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0070); the latter's commentarial chain in Heian Japan is the densest sub-cluster in the division.
- **The 成實宗 question** — whether Harivarman's *Chéngshí lùn* belongs to Sautrāntika, to a transitional position between Sthaviravāda and Mahāyāna, or constitutes an independent doctrinal lineage; the disappearance of the Chinese 成實宗 school in the early Táng.
- **The fivefold Pratītyasamutpāda corpus** — five short treatises ([KR6o0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0055)–[KR6o0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0059)) translating overlapping Indian materials on dependent origination, of unusual value for comparative study because they preserve parallel Chinese renderings of related Sanskrit verse-cores.
- **The transmission of Buddhist verse genres into Chinese** — how *gāthā* / *stotra* / *sòng* forms were rendered, including the three-translation problem of Nāgārjuna's *Suhṛllekha* [KR6o0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0127)–[KR6o0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0129) and the metrical conventions of the Sòng translation bureau ([KR6o0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0130)–[KR6o0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0143)).
- **The Dūnhuáng *Qǐxìnlùn* layer** — the unique witness of Tánkuàng's mid-eighth-century *Qǐxìnlùn* lectures preserved only at Dunhuang (T2813–T2814 = [KR6o0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0121)/[KR6o0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0122)/[KR6o0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0123)), evidence for a North-West-Chinese reading tradition independent of the central Táng commentaries.

### Timeline

- c. 150–250 — *Yīnyuán xīn lùn sòng / shì* 因緣心論頌因緣心論釋 中文 [KR6o0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0058) — earliest stratum; attributed to Nāgārjuna in a short Indian verse-commentary form.
- 317–420 — *Nā xiān bǐqiū jīng* 那先比丘經 中文 [KR6o0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0124) / [KR6o0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0125) — Eastern Jìn anonymous translations of the *Milindapañha*; the earliest Chinese witness to the dialogue.
- c. 350–431 — *Sānmídǐbù lùn* 三彌底部論 中文 [KR6o0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0053) and *Pìzhīfó yīnyuán lùn* 辟支佛因緣論 中文 [KR6o0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0054) — anonymous Sixteen-Kingdoms translations of Sthaviravāda doctrinal tracts.
- 401–413 — *Fā pútíxīn jīng lùn* 發菩提心經論 中文 [KR6o0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0064) — Latter-Qín; attributed to the Kumārajīva circle.
- 411–412 — *Chéngshí lùn* 成實論 中文 [KR6o0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0050) — Kumārajīva's translation of Harivarman; foundational for the 成實宗.
- 426–437 — *Rù dàshèng lùn* 入大乘論 中文 [KR6o0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0038) — Liú-Sòng-period rendering attributed to Daoyao 道泰.
- 431 — *Lóngshù púsà wèi Chántuójiā wáng shuō fǎyào jì* 龍樹菩薩為禪陀迦王說法要偈 中文 [KR6o0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0127) — Guṇavarman 求那跋摩's translation of the *Suhṛllekha*.
- 434–442 — *Quànfā zhū wáng yào jì* 勸發諸王要偈 中文 [KR6o0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0128) — Saṅghavarman 僧伽跋摩's second *Suhṛllekha* translation.
- 435–468 — *Bīntóulú tūluóshé wèi Yōutuóyán wáng shuō fǎ jīng* 賓頭盧突羅闍為優陀延王說法經 中文 [KR6o0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0145) — early Sòng-period *Piṇḍolabhāradvāja* tract.

## Division note (scope only): [KR6o 論集部 *Lùnjí bù* — Buddhist Canon — Treatise Collection](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6o corresponds to the *Lùnjí bù* 論集部 of the Taishō canon (vol. 32, nos. 1628–1692), together with the commentarial overflow in vol. 44 (nos. 1839–1850) and a small group of Dūnhuáng-recovered manuscripts in vol. 85 (nos. 2813–2816). The division is the canon's general miscellany of doctrinal treatises (*lùn* 論, śāstra) and the verse-collections (*sòng* 頌, *zàn* 讚, *gāthā* 伽他) attached to them. Unlike the dedicated divisions for Mādhyamaka and Yogācāra commentary on specific sūtras (`KR6m` 釋經論部, `KR6n` 毘曇部, 瑜伽部), KR6o gathers freestanding śāstras that do not belong to a single school or sūtra-commentary lineage: hetuvidyā (yīnmíng 因明) logic, Madhyamaka and Sautrāntika doctrinal works, the *Satyasiddhi-śāstra* of the 成實宗 school, *pratītyasamutpāda* tracts, *bodhicitta* literature, the *Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda* (*Awakening of Faith*) corpus, the Sino-Buddhist *Milindapañha* (*Nā xiān bǐqiū jīng*), and an extensive stotra/*gāthā* section. 

Chronologically the division spans c. 150 CE (the Indian source-strata of treatises by Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva, Dignāga) through 1911 (a late-Qīng vernacular gloss on *Dà zōngdì xuánwén běn lùn*), with the densest layers in (i) the fifth-/sixth-century translation projects of Kumārajīva, Paramārtha and Bodhiruci, (ii) the Táng Xuánzàng–Yìjìng era, (iii) the Northern Sòng translation bureau under Tiānxīsāi 天息災, Dānapāla 施護 and Dharmadeva 法天 (c. 982–1000), and (iv) the Heian–Kamakura and late-Míng waves of native East-Asian commentary on *yīnmíng* and *Qǐxìnlùn*. The principal transmissional issue throughout is the apocryphal or pseudepigraphic status of several of its most influential texts — *Dà shèng qǐxìn lùn*, *Shì móhēyǎn lùn*, *Zhāng suǒzhī lùn*, the Sino-Tibetan-Mongol *Bāsībā* tract — for which East-Asian and modern scholarship has reached very different conclusions.

## Division note: [KR6n 瑜伽部 *Yújiā bù* — Yogācāra works](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6n collects the Chinese canon's holdings for the Yogācāra (瑜伽 *yújiā*) doctrinal stream — the abhidharmic-idealist tradition that descends from the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* and the works of Asaṅga 無著菩薩 and Vasubandhu 世親菩薩 in fourth- and fifth-century North India, and that becomes the East Asian Fǎxiàng 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 school after Xuánzàng 玄奘 reimports it in the mid-seventh century. The doctrinal core is established by the CANWWW Taishō *Yújiā bù* (`div30`, Taishō Vol. 30–31, Nos. 1579–1627): the *Yogācārabhūmi* and its summaries, the *Madhyāntavibhāga* and *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* of the so-called Maitreya corpus, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* of Asaṅga, the *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā* of Vasubandhu, the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the *Ratnagotravibhāga*, the Hundred-Dharmas list, Dignāga's 陳那菩薩 *Ālambanaparīkṣā*, and the Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha hybrids preserved at T1610–1611 and T1626–1627.

The division as catalogued in Kanripo, however, extends well beyond the Taishō *Yújiā bù* proper: it folds in the Cí'ēn-school commentarial canon of Vols. 42–45 (Kuījī's 窺基 *Chéng wéishí lùn shùjì* and *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng*; Huìzhāo 慧沼 and Zhìzhōu 智周 sub-commentaries), the late-Táng to Wǔdài Dūnhuáng Yogācāra fragments of Taishō Vol. 85, the Japanese Hossō 法相 scholastic apparatus of Vols. 65–70, and a sizeable late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng-revival corpus in *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 39 and 46–55. Three transmissional layers must therefore be kept distinct when reading the division: the **Old-Yogācāra** layer of Paramārtha 真諦 (c. 546–569), which is closer to a Valabhī recension and preserves the *trisvabhāva* and *amalavijñāna* in idiosyncratic form; the **New-Yogācāra** layer of Xuánzàng (646–664), based on Nālandā materials and Dharmapāla's 護法菩薩 reading; and the **East Asian scholastic** layer (Táng Cí'ēn school, Korean Hyŏnyu monks at Cháng'ān, Heian/Kamakura Hossō, Ming Cíbēi-Cí'ēn revivalists), in which the imported Indian texts become objects of an autonomous and very long-lived commentarial industry. The chronological span runs from c. 414 (Dharmakṣema's 曇無讖 *Bodhisattvabhūmi* [KR6n0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0003)) to the late seventeenth century (Ouyi Zhixu's 智旭 *Xiàngzōng bā yào zhíjiě* [KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145)) — roughly twelve centuries of continuous Yogācāra scholasticism in Chinese.

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Yúqié shī dì lùn* 瑜伽師地論 [KR6n0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0001) — Xuánzàng's 646–648 translation of the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* in 100 *juǎn*; the encyclopaedic root text of the entire division, conventionally attributed to Maitreya 彌勒菩薩 but in fact a multi-author stratified compilation of the Asaṅga circle. The exegetical aid *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* 瑜伽師地論釋 [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002) of Jinaputra 最勝子 accompanies it.
- *Chéng wéishí lùn* 成唯識論 [KR6n0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0016) — Xuánzàng and Kuījī's 659 redaction of the ten Indian *Triṃśikā*-bhāṣyas around Dharmapāla's reading; the doctrinal charter of the Cí'ēn school. The commentarial pyramid stacked over it — Kuījī's *Shùjì* 述記 [KR6n0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0026), *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào* 掌中樞要 [KR6n0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0029), Huìzhāo's *Liǎoyì dēng* 了義燈 [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030), Zhìzhōu's *Yǎnmì* 演祕 [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032), and Taehyŏn's 太賢 *Xuéjì* 學記 [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041) — defines Táng-period Fǎxiàng orthodoxy.
- *Wéishí sānshí lùn sòng* 唯識三十論頌 [KR6n0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0022) and *Wéishí èrshí lùn* 唯識二十論 [KR6n0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0055) — Vasubandhu's *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā*, translated by Xuánzàng in 648 and 661; the textual nucleus around which both Indian and Chinese consciousness-only argumentation organises itself. Paramārtha's earlier renderings as *Zhuǎn shí lùn* 轉識論 [KR6n0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0024), *Wéishí lùn* 唯識論 [KR6n0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0053), and *Dàshèng wéishí lùn* 大乘唯識論 [KR6n0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0054) preserve the Old-Yogācāra reception.
- The *Shè dàshèng lùn* 攝大乘論 cluster — Asaṅga's *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, surviving in three Chinese translations (Buddhaśānta 531–534 [KR6n0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0058), Paramārtha 563–564 [KR6n0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0059), Xuánzàng 648–649 [KR6n0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0060)) plus the *Bhāṣya* in three further versions [KR6n0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0061) [KR6n0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0063) [KR6n0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0064) [KR6n0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0065) and a thicket of Sui–Táng commentaries and Dūnhuáng *zhāng* fragments [KR6n0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0066)–[KR6n0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0070). The cluster is the principal vehicle by which the *ālayavijñāna* doctrine enters China, and the Paramārtha line generates the Shèlùn 攝論 lineage that the Cí'ēn school then displaces.
- The *Madhyāntavibhāga* cluster — Paramārtha's *Zhōngbiān fēnbié lùn* 中邊分別論 [KR6n0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0071) and Xuánzàng's *Biàn zhōngbiān lùn* 辯中邊論 [KR6n0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0072) plus its verse [KR6n0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0073) and Kuījī's *Shùjì* [KR6n0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0075); with the closely related *Shíbā kōng lùn* 十八空論 [KR6n0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0074) and *Sān wúxìng lùn* 三無性論 [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) of the Paramārtha corpus.
- *Dàshèng zhuāngyán jīng lùn* 大乘莊嚴經論 [KR6n0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0080) — the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* with Vasubandhu-circle commentary, Prabhākaramitra 630–633; together with *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn* 顯揚聖教論 [KR6n0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0077), Asaṅga's digest of the *Yogācārabhūmi* in Xuánzàng's 645–646 rendering.
- *Dàshèng āpídámó jí lùn* 大乘阿毘達磨集論 [KR6n0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0081) and its expanded *Zájí lùn* 雜集論 [KR6n0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0082) — Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya* and Sthiramati's bhāṣya; the Yogācāra abhidharma proper. Read in China together with the *Dàshèng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘五蘊論 [KR6n0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0094), the *Guǎng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘廣五蘊論 [KR6n0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0095), and the *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn* 大乘百法明門論 [KR6n0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0096) of Vasubandhu, the four works form the standard East Asian curriculum in Yogācāra dharma-taxonomy.
- The tathāgatagarbha-Yogācāra hybrids — *Fóxìng lùn* 佛性論 [KR6n0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0087), the *Ratnagotravibhāga* (*Jiūjìng yīshèng bǎoxìng lùn* 究竟一乘寶性論) [KR6n0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0088), and the two recensions of *Dàshèng fǎjiè wú chābié lùn* 大乘法界無差別論 [KR6n0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0089) [KR6n0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0090) — bridge the division to the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q and were a central battleground in the East Asian one-vehicle / five-natures controversy.
- The *Ālambanaparīkṣā* cluster — Dignāga's *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* 觀所緣緣論 [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) with Dharmapāla's commentary [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113), and a late-Míng wave of revival commentaries [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117) — anchors the epistemological side of the division.
- The Cí'ēn doctrinal compendia — Kuījī's *Dàshèng fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* 大乘法苑義林章 [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), Huìzhāo's *Quànfā pútí xīn jí* 勸發菩提心集 [KR6n0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0127) and *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* 能顯中邊慧日論 [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128), Zhìzhōu's *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* 大乘入道次第 [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129) — codify the Cí'ēn school's doctrinal positions, including the five-gotras doctrine and the polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk's 圓測 readings.
- The *Bā shí guījǔ* 八識規矩 cluster ([KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131)–[KR6n0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0140)) — Xuánzàng's (apocryphally attributed) verses on the eight consciousnesses, with Putai's 普泰 1530s Yuán-Míng-transition commentary [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) and a dense Wànlì-Chongzhen-era stratum from Mingyu 明昱, Zhixu 智旭, Deqing 德清, and others. These short verse cycles, together with the *Xiàngzōng bā yào* 相宗八要 anthology [KR6n0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0143)–[KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145), are the late-Míng Fǎxiàng revival's basic curriculum and the principal channel by which Cí'ēn doctrine survives into the Qīng.
- *Dàshèng yìzhāng* 大乘義章 [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) — Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn's 慧遠 580–592 doctrinal encyclopaedia: not a pure Yogācāra work, but a Sui-era Shèlùn-tradition synthesis included here because it remains the most systematic pre-Xuánzàng treatment of the Yogācāra dharma-list in Chinese.

### Important persons

- [彌勒菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%8C%E5%8B%92%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) — the traditional speaker of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and the so-called Maitreya corpus (*Madhyāntavibhāga*, *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra*, etc.); historicity disputed in modern scholarship, but the canonical attribution shapes every East Asian reading of the division.
- [無著菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%84%A1%E8%91%97%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Asaṅga, c. 4th c.) — author of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, the *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn*, and the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*; the architect of the systematic Yogācāra in this division.
- [世親菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%96%E8%A6%AA%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Vasubandhu, c. 4th–5th c.; also rendered 天親菩薩) — author of the *Triṃśikā*, *Viṃśatikā*, *Pañcaskandhaka*, *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn*, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, and *Dàshèng chéngyè lùn* [KR6n0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0086); the most heavily commented author in the division.
- [安慧菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E6%85%A7%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Sthiramati, 6th c.) — author of the *Abhidharmasamuccaya-vyākhyā* underlying T1606 and of the *Madhyāntavibhāga-ṭīkā* underlying parts of T1599; the principal "Old-Yogācāra" exegete reaching China through Paramārtha.
- [護法菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%B7%E6%B3%95%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dharmapāla, c. 530–561) — Nālandā commentator whose reading of the *Triṃśikā* is the spine of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* and whose *Ālambanaparīkṣā-vṛtti* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113) founds the Cí'ēn epistemological tradition.
- [陳那菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%82%A3%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dignāga, c. 480–540) — author of *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and, by implication, of the epistemological reorientation that drives the *Ālambanaparīkṣā* and *Buddhabhūmi-vyākhyāna* portions of the corpus.
- [親光菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%AA%E5%85%89%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Bandhuprabha) — credited author of the *Buddhabhūmi-śāstra* materials underlying the *Chéng wéishí lùn* synthesis.
- [最勝子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%80%E5%8B%9D%E5%AD%90) (Jinaputra) — Indian compiler of *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002), the canonical exegetical key to the *Yogācārabhūmi*.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha, 499–569) — translator of the bulk of the Old-Yogācāra layer (T1584, T1587, T1589, T1593, T1595, T1599, T1610, T1616–1620); the rival transmissional lineage that the Xuánzàng school later partly supersedes.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — translator of the New-Yogācāra core (T1579, T1585, T1586, T1590, T1594, T1597, T1600–1606, T1612, T1614 and many others); the single most important figure for the division and the founder of its Chinese school.
- [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) (Kuījī, 632–682) — Xuánzàng's principal disciple and the doctrinal architect of the Cí'ēn / Fǎxiàng school; author of the *Shùjì*, *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào*, *Yúqié shī dì lùn lüèzuǎn* [KR6n0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0008), *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), and the *Wéishí èrshí lùn shùjì* [KR6n0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0057).
- [慧沼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%B2%BC) (Huìzhāo, 650–714) — second of the Cí'ēn "three masters" (慈恩三祖); author of the *Liǎoyì dēng* [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030) and of the principal polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk in *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- [智周](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%91%A8) (Zhìzhōu, 668–723) — third of the Cí'ēn three masters; author of the *Yǎnmì* [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032) and *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129); closes the Táng commentarial canon of the school.
- [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) (Wǒnch'ǔk, 613–696) — Korean monk at Cháng'ān, lifelong rival of Kuījī; his independent reading of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* is preserved largely in fragments and citations, and his disagreements with the Cí'ēn line drive much of the *Liǎoyì dēng* polemic.
- [太賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E8%B3%A2) (Taehyŏn, fl. mid-8th c.) — Silla Fǎxiàng systematiser; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn xuéjì* [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041), one of the longest sub-commentaries on the *Shùjì*.
- [遁倫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%81%E5%80%AB) (Tullyun, late 7th – early 8th c.) — Korean monk; compiler of *Yúqié lùn jì* 瑜伽論記 [KR6n0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0007), the standard exegetical companion to the *Yogācārabhūmi* throughout East Asia.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) (Yìjìng, 635–713) — translator of *Chéng wéishí bǎoshēng lùn* [KR6n0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0056), *Liùmén jiàoshòu xí dìng lùn* [KR6n0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0084), and *Guān suǒyuán lùn shì* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113); supplies the post-Xuánzàng Indian materials that round out the *Triṃśikā* / *Ālambanaparīkṣā* commentary set.
- [達摩笈多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%94%E6%91%A9%E7%AC%88%E5%A4%9A) (Dharmagupta, d. 619), [佛陀扇多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E6%89%87%E5%A4%9A) (Buddhaśānta), [般若流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) (Prajñāruci), [提雲般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E9%9B%B2%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) (Devaprajña), [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema), [求那跋摩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E6%91%A9) (Guṇavarman) — the chain of pre-Xuánzàng translators through whom the Yogācāra corpus arrives in China between the early fifth and early seventh centuries.
- [慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) (Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn, 523–592) — Sui doctrinal encyclopaedist; the *Dàshèng yìzhāng* [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) is the most influential pre-Xuánzàng Chinese systematisation of Yogācāra topics.
- [普泰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E6%B3%B0) (Pǔtài, fl. 1530s) — late-Míng Fǎxiàng pioneer; the *Bā shí guījǔ bǔzhù* [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) is the catalyst of the late-Míng *Bā shí guījǔ* commentarial wave.
- [王肯堂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%82%AF%E5%A0%82) (Wáng Kěntáng, 1549–1613) — Wànlì-era *jūshì* physician-Buddhist; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn zhèngyì* [KR6n0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0045), a key bridge from the late-Míng *jūshì* scholarship into Fǎxiàng exegesis.
- [通潤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%9A%E6%BD%A4) (Tōngrùn, 1565–1624) — Yúfēng 玉峯 master; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn jíjiě* [KR6n0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0044) and one of the leading Fǎxiàng-revivalist preachers of the Wànlì–Tianqi period.
- [明昱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%98%8E%E6%98%B1) (Míngyù, late 16th – early 17th c.) — late-Míng Fǎxiàng commentator on *Bā shí guījǔ*, *Bǎifǎ*, and *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn*; the single most prolific late-Míng author within the division.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) (Ouyi Zhìxù, 1599–1655) — late-Míng Tiāntái–Pure Land master whose *zhíjiě* 直解 commentaries on the *Bā shí guījǔ*, *Bǎifǎ*, *Chéng wéishí lùn*, *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn*, and *Xiàngzōng bā yào* ([KR6n0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0047), [KR6n0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0051), [KR6n0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0106), [KR6n0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0115), [KR6n0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0137), [KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145)) integrate Cí'ēn doctrine into the Ming syncretic synthesis.
- [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) (Hānshān Déqīng, 1546–1623) — one of the "four great masters of the late Míng"; his *Bā shí guījǔ tōngshuō* [KR6n0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0135) gives the eight-consciousnesses schema its Chán-inflected late-Míng reading.

### Topics

- **Vijñaptimātra / cittamātra** (唯識 *wéishí*). The thesis that what appears as an external object is a transformation of consciousness; argued textually through Vasubandhu's *Viṃśatikā* and *Triṃśikā* and exegetically through the entire *Chéng wéishí lùn* commentarial pyramid.
- **The eight consciousnesses** (八識 *bā shí*), with particular attention to the *ālayavijñāna* (阿賴耶識) as substrate and *kliṣṭamanas* (染汚意) as the sixth-to-seventh-consciousness link. Paramārtha's idiosyncratic positing of a ninth, *amalavijñāna* 阿摩羅識, is one of the principal Old-Yogācāra peculiarities. The *Bā shí guījǔ* tradition turns the eight-consciousness schema into a Ming pedagogical genre.
- **The three natures** (三性 *sān xìng*, *trisvabhāva*): *parikalpita* (遍計所執), *paratantra* (依他起), *pariniṣpanna* (圓成實). The cross-cutting **three non-natures** (三無性) doctrine is foregrounded in Paramārtha's *Sān wúxìng lùn* [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) and is the principal hermeneutic key for reconciling the Yogācāra ontology with the Prajñāpāramitā emptiness teaching.
- **Five gotras / five natures** (五姓各別 *wǔxìng gèbié*). The Yogācārabhūmi taxonomy of five fixed spiritual lineages, against which Wǒnch'ǔk and the East Asian one-vehicle traditions argue. The Cí'ēn defence of the five-gotras position is the principal polemical thread of Huìzhāo's *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- **The Hundred Dharmas** (百法 *bǎifǎ*). Vasubandhu's 5-category × 100-item taxonomy of dharmas (T1614); becomes the standard East Asian Buddhist abhidharmic primer and generates a long commentarial chain from Kuījī's *Dàshèng bǎifǎ míngmén lùn shū* [KR6n0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0098) through the Dūnhuáng *Kāizōng yìjì* [KR6n0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0107) to the Wànlì-era revivalist commentaries [KR6n0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0103)–[KR6n0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0106).
- **Stages of the Yoga practitioner** (瑜伽師地 *yúqié shī dì*) — the seventeen-bhūmi structure of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, organising the entire division.
- **Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha synthesis**. T1610 *Fóxìng lùn*, T1611 *Bǎoxìng lùn*, T1626–1627 *Fǎjiè wú chābié lùn*, and T1612 *Wǔyùn lùn* sit at the seam between Yogācāra and the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q; the question of whether the *tathāgatagarbha* is reducible to the *ālayavijñāna* shapes both the Old-Yogācāra reception in China and the *Awakening of Faith* tradition.
- **Epistemology of perception (所緣緣)**. Through Dignāga's *Ālambanaparīkṣā* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and its commentaries, the question of what constitutes a valid object of perception becomes a Yogācāra theme; it is taken up again in the Wànlì–early Qīng commentary wave of [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117).
- **Old- vs. New-Yogācāra** (舊譯 *jiùyì* / 新譯 *xīnyì*). The Paramārtha-line readings of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* and *Triṃśikā* differ systematically from Xuánzàng's: on *amalavijñāna*, on the status of the *paratantra*, and on the relation between *vāsanā* and the *ālaya*. The division as a whole preserves both layers in parallel — the cataloguing principle is doctrinal subject matter, not translatorial school.
- **Cí'ēn school polemics**. Internal to the Táng layer: Kuījī vs. Wǒnch'ǔk on the reading of T1585; Huìzhāo's continuation of that polemic; Zhìzhōu's consolidation. These polemics define the canonical shape of the Fǎxiàng curriculum.
- **East Asian transmission and revival**. The division is the textual basis for three successive scholastic traditions: Táng Cí'ēn (mid-7th to early 8th c., centred at Cháng'ān, with Silla and Goguryeo participation), Heian–Kamakura Hossō (Vols. 65–70 of the Taishō, c. 800–1500), and late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng revival (c. 1530–1660, *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 46–55).

## Division note: [KR6n 瑜伽部 *Yújiā bù* — Yogācāra works](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6n collects the Chinese canon's holdings for the Yogācāra (瑜伽 *yújiā*) doctrinal stream — the abhidharmic-idealist tradition that descends from the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* and the works of Asaṅga 無著菩薩 and Vasubandhu 世親菩薩 in fourth- and fifth-century North India, and that becomes the East Asian Fǎxiàng 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 school after Xuánzàng 玄奘 reimports it in the mid-seventh century. The doctrinal core is established by the CANWWW Taishō *Yújiā bù* (`div30`, Taishō Vol. 30–31, Nos. 1579–1627): the *Yogācārabhūmi* and its summaries, the *Madhyāntavibhāga* and *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* of the so-called Maitreya corpus, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* of Asaṅga, the *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā* of Vasubandhu, the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the *Ratnagotravibhāga*, the Hundred-Dharmas list, Dignāga's 陳那菩薩 *Ālambanaparīkṣā*, and the Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha hybrids preserved at T1610–1611 and T1626–1627.

The division as catalogued in Kanripo, however, extends well beyond the Taishō *Yújiā bù* proper: it folds in the Cí'ēn-school commentarial canon of Vols. 42–45 (Kuījī's 窺基 *Chéng wéishí lùn shùjì* and *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng*; Huìzhāo 慧沼 and Zhìzhōu 智周 sub-commentaries), the late-Táng to Wǔdài Dūnhuáng Yogācāra fragments of Taishō Vol. 85, the Japanese Hossō 法相 scholastic apparatus of Vols. 65–70, and a sizeable late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng-revival corpus in *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 39 and 46–55. Three transmissional layers must therefore be kept distinct when reading the division: the **Old-Yogācāra** layer of Paramārtha 真諦 (c. 546–569), which is closer to a Valabhī recension and preserves the *trisvabhāva* and *amalavijñāna* in idiosyncratic form; the **New-Yogācāra** layer of Xuánzàng (646–664), based on Nālandā materials and Dharmapāla's 護法菩薩 reading; and the **East Asian scholastic** layer (Táng Cí'ēn school, Korean Hyŏnyu monks at Cháng'ān, Heian/Kamakura Hossō, Ming Cíbēi-Cí'ēn revivalists), in which the imported Indian texts become objects of an autonomous and very long-lived commentarial industry. The chronological span runs from c. 414 (Dharmakṣema's 曇無讖 *Bodhisattvabhūmi* [KR6n0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0003)) to the late seventeenth century (Ouyi Zhixu's 智旭 *Xiàngzōng bā yào zhíjiě* [KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145)) — roughly twelve centuries of continuous Yogācāra scholasticism in Chinese.

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Yúqié shī dì lùn* 瑜伽師地論 [KR6n0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0001) — Xuánzàng's 646–648 translation of the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* in 100 *juǎn*; the encyclopaedic root text of the entire division, conventionally attributed to Maitreya 彌勒菩薩 but in fact a multi-author stratified compilation of the Asaṅga circle. The exegetical aid *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* 瑜伽師地論釋 [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002) of Jinaputra 最勝子 accompanies it.
- *Chéng wéishí lùn* 成唯識論 [KR6n0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0016) — Xuánzàng and Kuījī's 659 redaction of the ten Indian *Triṃśikā*-bhāṣyas around Dharmapāla's reading; the doctrinal charter of the Cí'ēn school. The commentarial pyramid stacked over it — Kuījī's *Shùjì* 述記 [KR6n0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0026), *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào* 掌中樞要 [KR6n0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0029), Huìzhāo's *Liǎoyì dēng* 了義燈 [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030), Zhìzhōu's *Yǎnmì* 演祕 [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032), and Taehyŏn's 太賢 *Xuéjì* 學記 [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041) — defines Táng-period Fǎxiàng orthodoxy.
- *Wéishí sānshí lùn sòng* 唯識三十論頌 [KR6n0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0022) and *Wéishí èrshí lùn* 唯識二十論 [KR6n0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0055) — Vasubandhu's *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā*, translated by Xuánzàng in 648 and 661; the textual nucleus around which both Indian and Chinese consciousness-only argumentation organises itself. Paramārtha's earlier renderings as *Zhuǎn shí lùn* 轉識論 [KR6n0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0024), *Wéishí lùn* 唯識論 [KR6n0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0053), and *Dàshèng wéishí lùn* 大乘唯識論 [KR6n0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0054) preserve the Old-Yogācāra reception.
- The *Shè dàshèng lùn* 攝大乘論 cluster — Asaṅga's *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, surviving in three Chinese translations (Buddhaśānta 531–534 [KR6n0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0058), Paramārtha 563–564 [KR6n0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0059), Xuánzàng 648–649 [KR6n0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0060)) plus the *Bhāṣya* in three further versions [KR6n0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0061) [KR6n0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0063) [KR6n0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0064) [KR6n0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0065) and a thicket of Sui–Táng commentaries and Dūnhuáng *zhāng* fragments [KR6n0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0066)–[KR6n0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0070). The cluster is the principal vehicle by which the *ālayavijñāna* doctrine enters China, and the Paramārtha line generates the Shèlùn 攝論 lineage that the Cí'ēn school then displaces.
- The *Madhyāntavibhāga* cluster — Paramārtha's *Zhōngbiān fēnbié lùn* 中邊分別論 [KR6n0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0071) and Xuánzàng's *Biàn zhōngbiān lùn* 辯中邊論 [KR6n0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0072) plus its verse [KR6n0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0073) and Kuījī's *Shùjì* [KR6n0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0075); with the closely related *Shíbā kōng lùn* 十八空論 [KR6n0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0074) and *Sān wúxìng lùn* 三無性論 [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) of the Paramārtha corpus.
- *Dàshèng zhuāngyán jīng lùn* 大乘莊嚴經論 [KR6n0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0080) — the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* with Vasubandhu-circle commentary, Prabhākaramitra 630–633; together with *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn* 顯揚聖教論 [KR6n0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0077), Asaṅga's digest of the *Yogācārabhūmi* in Xuánzàng's 645–646 rendering.
- *Dàshèng āpídámó jí lùn* 大乘阿毘達磨集論 [KR6n0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0081) and its expanded *Zájí lùn* 雜集論 [KR6n0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0082) — Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya* and Sthiramati's bhāṣya; the Yogācāra abhidharma proper. Read in China together with the *Dàshèng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘五蘊論 [KR6n0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0094), the *Guǎng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘廣五蘊論 [KR6n0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0095), and the *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn* 大乘百法明門論 [KR6n0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0096) of Vasubandhu, the four works form the standard East Asian curriculum in Yogācāra dharma-taxonomy.
- The tathāgatagarbha-Yogācāra hybrids — *Fóxìng lùn* 佛性論 [KR6n0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0087), the *Ratnagotravibhāga* (*Jiūjìng yīshèng bǎoxìng lùn* 究竟一乘寶性論) [KR6n0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0088), and the two recensions of *Dàshèng fǎjiè wú chābié lùn* 大乘法界無差別論 [KR6n0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0089) [KR6n0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0090) — bridge the division to the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q and were a central battleground in the East Asian one-vehicle / five-natures controversy.
- The *Ālambanaparīkṣā* cluster — Dignāga's *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* 觀所緣緣論 [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) with Dharmapāla's commentary [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113), and a late-Míng wave of revival commentaries [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117) — anchors the epistemological side of the division.
- The Cí'ēn doctrinal compendia — Kuījī's *Dàshèng fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* 大乘法苑義林章 [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), Huìzhāo's *Quànfā pútí xīn jí* 勸發菩提心集 [KR6n0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0127) and *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* 能顯中邊慧日論 [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128), Zhìzhōu's *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* 大乘入道次第 [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129) — codify the Cí'ēn school's doctrinal positions, including the five-gotras doctrine and the polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk's 圓測 readings.
- The *Bā shí guījǔ* 八識規矩 cluster ([KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131)–[KR6n0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0140)) — Xuánzàng's (apocryphally attributed) verses on the eight consciousnesses, with Putai's 普泰 1530s Yuán-Míng-transition commentary [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) and a dense Wànlì-Chongzhen-era stratum from Mingyu 明昱, Zhixu 智旭, Deqing 德清, and others. These short verse cycles, together with the *Xiàngzōng bā yào* 相宗八要 anthology [KR6n0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0143)–[KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145), are the late-Míng Fǎxiàng revival's basic curriculum and the principal channel by which Cí'ēn doctrine survives into the Qīng.
- *Dàshèng yìzhāng* 大乘義章 [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) — Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn's 慧遠 580–592 doctrinal encyclopaedia: not a pure Yogācāra work, but a Sui-era Shèlùn-tradition synthesis included here because it remains the most systematic pre-Xuánzàng treatment of the Yogācāra dharma-list in Chinese.

### Important persons

- [彌勒菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%8C%E5%8B%92%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) — the traditional speaker of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and the so-called Maitreya corpus (*Madhyāntavibhāga*, *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra*, etc.); historicity disputed in modern scholarship, but the canonical attribution shapes every East Asian reading of the division.
- [無著菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%84%A1%E8%91%97%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Asaṅga, c. 4th c.) — author of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, the *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn*, and the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*; the architect of the systematic Yogācāra in this division.
- [世親菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%96%E8%A6%AA%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Vasubandhu, c. 4th–5th c.; also rendered 天親菩薩) — author of the *Triṃśikā*, *Viṃśatikā*, *Pañcaskandhaka*, *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn*, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, and *Dàshèng chéngyè lùn* [KR6n0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0086); the most heavily commented author in the division.
- [安慧菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E6%85%A7%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Sthiramati, 6th c.) — author of the *Abhidharmasamuccaya-vyākhyā* underlying T1606 and of the *Madhyāntavibhāga-ṭīkā* underlying parts of T1599; the principal "Old-Yogācāra" exegete reaching China through Paramārtha.
- [護法菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%B7%E6%B3%95%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dharmapāla, c. 530–561) — Nālandā commentator whose reading of the *Triṃśikā* is the spine of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* and whose *Ālambanaparīkṣā-vṛtti* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113) founds the Cí'ēn epistemological tradition.
- [陳那菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%82%A3%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dignāga, c. 480–540) — author of *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and, by implication, of the epistemological reorientation that drives the *Ālambanaparīkṣā* and *Buddhabhūmi-vyākhyāna* portions of the corpus.
- [親光菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%AA%E5%85%89%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Bandhuprabha) — credited author of the *Buddhabhūmi-śāstra* materials underlying the *Chéng wéishí lùn* synthesis.
- [最勝子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%80%E5%8B%9D%E5%AD%90) (Jinaputra) — Indian compiler of *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002), the canonical exegetical key to the *Yogācārabhūmi*.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha, 499–569) — translator of the bulk of the Old-Yogācāra layer (T1584, T1587, T1589, T1593, T1595, T1599, T1610, T1616–1620); the rival transmissional lineage that the Xuánzàng school later partly supersedes.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — translator of the New-Yogācāra core (T1579, T1585, T1586, T1590, T1594, T1597, T1600–1606, T1612, T1614 and many others); the single most important figure for the division and the founder of its Chinese school.
- [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) (Kuījī, 632–682) — Xuánzàng's principal disciple and the doctrinal architect of the Cí'ēn / Fǎxiàng school; author of the *Shùjì*, *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào*, *Yúqié shī dì lùn lüèzuǎn* [KR6n0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0008), *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), and the *Wéishí èrshí lùn shùjì* [KR6n0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0057).
- [慧沼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%B2%BC) (Huìzhāo, 650–714) — second of the Cí'ēn "three masters" (慈恩三祖); author of the *Liǎoyì dēng* [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030) and of the principal polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk in *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- [智周](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%91%A8) (Zhìzhōu, 668–723) — third of the Cí'ēn three masters; author of the *Yǎnmì* [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032) and *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129); closes the Táng commentarial canon of the school.
- [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) (Wǒnch'ǔk, 613–696) — Korean monk at Cháng'ān, lifelong rival of Kuījī; his independent reading of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* is preserved largely in fragments and citations, and his disagreements with the Cí'ēn line drive much of the *Liǎoyì dēng* polemic.
- [太賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E8%B3%A2) (Taehyŏn, fl. mid-8th c.) — Silla Fǎxiàng systematiser; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn xuéjì* [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041), one of the longest sub-commentaries on the *Shùjì*.
- [遁倫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%81%E5%80%AB) (Tullyun, late 7th – early 8th c.) — Korean monk; compiler of *Yúqié lùn jì* 瑜伽論記 [KR6n0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0007), the standard exegetical companion to the *Yogācārabhūmi* throughout East Asia.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) (Yìjìng, 635–713) — translator of *Chéng wéishí bǎoshēng lùn* [KR6n0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0056), *Liùmén jiàoshòu xí dìng lùn* [KR6n0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0084), and *Guān suǒyuán lùn shì* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113); supplies the post-Xuánzàng Indian materials that round out the *Triṃśikā* / *Ālambanaparīkṣā* commentary set.
- [達摩笈多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%94%E6%91%A9%E7%AC%88%E5%A4%9A) (Dharmagupta, d. 619), [佛陀扇多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E6%89%87%E5%A4%9A) (Buddhaśānta), [般若流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) (Prajñāruci), [提雲般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E9%9B%B2%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) (Devaprajña), [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema), [求那跋摩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E6%91%A9) (Guṇavarman) — the chain of pre-Xuánzàng translators through whom the Yogācāra corpus arrives in China between the early fifth and early seventh centuries.
- [慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) (Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn, 523–592) — Sui doctrinal encyclopaedist; the *Dàshèng yìzhāng* [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) is the most influential pre-Xuánzàng Chinese systematisation of Yogācāra topics.
- [普泰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E6%B3%B0) (Pǔtài, fl. 1530s) — late-Míng Fǎxiàng pioneer; the *Bā shí guījǔ bǔzhù* [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) is the catalyst of the late-Míng *Bā shí guījǔ* commentarial wave.
- [王肯堂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%82%AF%E5%A0%82) (Wáng Kěntáng, 1549–1613) — Wànlì-era *jūshì* physician-Buddhist; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn zhèngyì* [KR6n0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0045), a key bridge from the late-Míng *jūshì* scholarship into Fǎxiàng exegesis.
- [通潤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%9A%E6%BD%A4) (Tōngrùn, 1565–1624) — Yúfēng 玉峯 master; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn jíjiě* [KR6n0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0044) and one of the leading Fǎxiàng-revivalist preachers of the Wànlì–Tianqi period.
- [明昱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%98%8E%E6%98%B1) (Míngyù, late 16th – early 17th c.) — late-Míng Fǎxiàng commentator on *Bā shí guījǔ*, *Bǎifǎ*, and *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn*; the single most prolific late-Míng author within the division.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) (Ouyi Zhìxù, 1599–1655) — late-Míng Tiāntái–Pure Land master whose *zhíjiě* 直解 commentaries on the *Bā shí guījǔ*, *Bǎifǎ*, *Chéng wéishí lùn*, *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn*, and *Xiàngzōng bā yào* ([KR6n0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0047), [KR6n0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0051), [KR6n0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0106), [KR6n0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0115), [KR6n0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0137), [KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145)) integrate Cí'ēn doctrine into the Ming syncretic synthesis.
- [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) (Hānshān Déqīng, 1546–1623) — one of the "four great masters of the late Míng"; his *Bā shí guījǔ tōngshuō* [KR6n0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0135) gives the eight-consciousnesses schema its Chán-inflected late-Míng reading.

### Topics

- **Vijñaptimātra / cittamātra** (唯識 *wéishí*). The thesis that what appears as an external object is a transformation of consciousness; argued textually through Vasubandhu's *Viṃśatikā* and *Triṃśikā* and exegetically through the entire *Chéng wéishí lùn* commentarial pyramid.
- **The eight consciousnesses** (八識 *bā shí*), with particular attention to the *ālayavijñāna* (阿賴耶識) as substrate and *kliṣṭamanas* (染汚意) as the sixth-to-seventh-consciousness link. Paramārtha's idiosyncratic positing of a ninth, *amalavijñāna* 阿摩羅識, is one of the principal Old-Yogācāra peculiarities. The *Bā shí guījǔ* tradition turns the eight-consciousness schema into a Ming pedagogical genre.
- **The three natures** (三性 *sān xìng*, *trisvabhāva*): *parikalpita* (遍計所執), *paratantra* (依他起), *pariniṣpanna* (圓成實). The cross-cutting **three non-natures** (三無性) doctrine is foregrounded in Paramārtha's *Sān wúxìng lùn* [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) and is the principal hermeneutic key for reconciling the Yogācāra ontology with the Prajñāpāramitā emptiness teaching.
- **Five gotras / five natures** (五姓各別 *wǔxìng gèbié*). The Yogācārabhūmi taxonomy of five fixed spiritual lineages, against which Wǒnch'ǔk and the East Asian one-vehicle traditions argue. The Cí'ēn defence of the five-gotras position is the principal polemical thread of Huìzhāo's *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- **The Hundred Dharmas** (百法 *bǎifǎ*). Vasubandhu's 5-category × 100-item taxonomy of dharmas (T1614); becomes the standard East Asian Buddhist abhidharmic primer and generates a long commentarial chain from Kuījī's *Dàshèng bǎifǎ míngmén lùn shū* [KR6n0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0098) through the Dūnhuáng *Kāizōng yìjì* [KR6n0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0107) to the Wànlì-era revivalist commentaries [KR6n0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0103)–[KR6n0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0106).
- **Stages of the Yoga practitioner** (瑜伽師地 *yúqié shī dì*) — the seventeen-bhūmi structure of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, organising the entire division.
- **Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha synthesis**. T1610 *Fóxìng lùn*, T1611 *Bǎoxìng lùn*, T1626–1627 *Fǎjiè wú chābié lùn*, and T1612 *Wǔyùn lùn* sit at the seam between Yogācāra and the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q; the question of whether the *tathāgatagarbha* is reducible to the *ālayavijñāna* shapes both the Old-Yogācāra reception in China and the *Awakening of Faith* tradition.
- **Epistemology of perception (所緣緣)**. Through Dignāga's *Ālambanaparīkṣā* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and its commentaries, the question of what constitutes a valid object of perception becomes a Yogācāra theme; it is taken up again in the Wànlì–early Qīng commentary wave of [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117).
- **Old- vs. New-Yogācāra** (舊譯 *jiùyì* / 新譯 *xīnyì*). The Paramārtha-line readings of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* and *Triṃśikā* differ systematically from Xuánzàng's: on *amalavijñāna*, on the status of the *paratantra*, and on the relation between *vāsanā* and the *ālaya*. The division as a whole preserves both layers in parallel — the cataloguing principle is doctrinal subject matter, not translatorial school.
- **Cí'ēn school polemics**. Internal to the Táng layer: Kuījī vs. Wǒnch'ǔk on the reading of T1585; Huìzhāo's continuation of that polemic; Zhìzhōu's consolidation. These polemics define the canonical shape of the Fǎxiàng curriculum.
- **East Asian transmission and revival**. The division is the textual basis for three successive scholastic traditions: Táng Cí'ēn (mid-7th to early 8th c., centred at Cháng'ān, with Silla and Goguryeo participation), Heian–Kamakura Hossō (Vols. 65–70 of the Taishō, c. 800–1500), and late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng revival (c. 1530–1660, *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 46–55).

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6n collects the Chinese canon's holdings for the Yogācāra (瑜伽 *yújiā*) doctrinal stream — the abhidharmic-idealist tradition that descends from the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* and the works of Asaṅga 無著菩薩 and Vasubandhu 世親菩薩 in fourth- and fifth-century North India, and that becomes the East Asian Fǎxiàng 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 school after Xuánzàng 玄奘 reimports it in the mid-seventh century. The doctrinal core is established by the CANWWW Taishō *Yújiā bù* (`div30`, Taishō Vol. 30–31, Nos. 1579–1627): the *Yogācārabhūmi* and its summaries, the *Madhyāntavibhāga* and *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* of the so-called Maitreya corpus, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* of Asaṅga, the *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā* of Vasubandhu, the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the *Ratnagotravibhāga*, the Hundred-Dharmas list, Dignāga's 陳那菩薩 *Ālambanaparīkṣā*, and the Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha hybrids preserved at T1610–1611 and T1626–1627.

The division as catalogued in Kanripo, however, extends well beyond the Taishō *Yújiā bù* proper: it folds in the Cí'ēn-school commentarial canon of Vols. 42–45 (Kuījī's 窺基 *Chéng wéishí lùn shùjì* and *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng*; Huìzhāo 慧沼 and Zhìzhōu 智周 sub-commentaries), the late-Táng to Wǔdài Dūnhuáng Yogācāra fragments of Taishō Vol. 85, the Japanese Hossō 法相 scholastic apparatus of Vols. 65–70, and a sizeable late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng-revival corpus in *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 39 and 46–55. Three transmissional layers must therefore be kept distinct when reading the division: the **Old-Yogācāra** layer of Paramārtha 真諦 (c. 546–569), which is closer to a Valabhī recension and preserves the *trisvabhāva* and *amalavijñāna* in idiosyncratic form; the **New-Yogācāra** layer of Xuánzàng (646–664), based on Nālandā materials and Dharmapāla's 護法菩薩 reading; and the **East Asian scholastic** layer (Táng Cí'ēn school, Korean Hyŏnyu monks at Cháng'ān, Heian/Kamakura Hossō, Ming Cíbēi-Cí'ēn revivalists), in which the imported Indian texts become objects of an autonomous and very long-lived commentarial industry. The chronological span runs from c. 414 (Dharmakṣema's 曇無讖 *Bodhisattvabhūmi* [KR6n0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0003)) to the late seventeenth century (Ouyi Zhixu's 智旭 *Xiàngzōng bā yào zhíjiě* [KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145)) — roughly twelve centuries of continuous Yogācāra scholasticism in Chinese.

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Yúqié shī dì lùn* 瑜伽師地論 [KR6n0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0001) — Xuánzàng's 646–648 translation of the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* in 100 *juǎn*; the encyclopaedic root text of the entire division, conventionally attributed to Maitreya 彌勒菩薩 but in fact a multi-author stratified compilation of the Asaṅga circle. The exegetical aid *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* 瑜伽師地論釋 [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002) of Jinaputra 最勝子 accompanies it.
- *Chéng wéishí lùn* 成唯識論 [KR6n0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0016) — Xuánzàng and Kuījī's 659 redaction of the ten Indian *Triṃśikā*-bhāṣyas around Dharmapāla's reading; the doctrinal charter of the Cí'ēn school. The commentarial pyramid stacked over it — Kuījī's *Shùjì* 述記 [KR6n0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0026), *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào* 掌中樞要 [KR6n0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0029), Huìzhāo's *Liǎoyì dēng* 了義燈 [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030), Zhìzhōu's *Yǎnmì* 演祕 [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032), and Taehyŏn's 太賢 *Xuéjì* 學記 [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041) — defines Táng-period Fǎxiàng orthodoxy.
- *Wéishí sānshí lùn sòng* 唯識三十論頌 [KR6n0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0022) and *Wéishí èrshí lùn* 唯識二十論 [KR6n0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0055) — Vasubandhu's *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā*, translated by Xuánzàng in 648 and 661; the textual nucleus around which both Indian and Chinese consciousness-only argumentation organises itself. Paramārtha's earlier renderings as *Zhuǎn shí lùn* 轉識論 [KR6n0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0024), *Wéishí lùn* 唯識論 [KR6n0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0053), and *Dàshèng wéishí lùn* 大乘唯識論 [KR6n0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0054) preserve the Old-Yogācāra reception.
- The *Shè dàshèng lùn* 攝大乘論 cluster — Asaṅga's *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, surviving in three Chinese translations (Buddhaśānta 531–534 [KR6n0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0058), Paramārtha 563–564 [KR6n0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0059), Xuánzàng 648–649 [KR6n0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0060)) plus the *Bhāṣya* in three further versions [KR6n0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0061) [KR6n0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0063) [KR6n0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0064) [KR6n0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0065) and a thicket of Sui–Táng commentaries and Dūnhuáng *zhāng* fragments [KR6n0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0066)–[KR6n0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0070). The cluster is the principal vehicle by which the *ālayavijñāna* doctrine enters China, and the Paramārtha line generates the Shèlùn 攝論 lineage that the Cí'ēn school then displaces.
- The *Madhyāntavibhāga* cluster — Paramārtha's *Zhōngbiān fēnbié lùn* 中邊分別論 [KR6n0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0071) and Xuánzàng's *Biàn zhōngbiān lùn* 辯中邊論 [KR6n0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0072) plus its verse [KR6n0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0073) and Kuījī's *Shùjì* [KR6n0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0075); with the closely related *Shíbā kōng lùn* 十八空論 [KR6n0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0074) and *Sān wúxìng lùn* 三無性論 [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) of the Paramārtha corpus.
- *Dàshèng zhuāngyán jīng lùn* 大乘莊嚴經論 [KR6n0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0080) — the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* with Vasubandhu-circle commentary, Prabhākaramitra 630–633; together with *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn* 顯揚聖教論 [KR6n0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0077), Asaṅga's digest of the *Yogācārabhūmi* in Xuánzàng's 645–646 rendering.
- *Dàshèng āpídámó jí lùn* 大乘阿毘達磨集論 [KR6n0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0081) and its expanded *Zájí lùn* 雜集論 [KR6n0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0082) — Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya* and Sthiramati's bhāṣya; the Yogācāra abhidharma proper. Read in China together with the *Dàshèng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘五蘊論 [KR6n0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0094), the *Guǎng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘廣五蘊論 [KR6n0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0095), and the *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn* 大乘百法明門論 [KR6n0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0096) of Vasubandhu, the four works form the standard East Asian curriculum in Yogācāra dharma-taxonomy.
- The tathāgatagarbha-Yogācāra hybrids — *Fóxìng lùn* 佛性論 [KR6n0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0087), the *Ratnagotravibhāga* (*Jiūjìng yīshèng bǎoxìng lùn* 究竟一乘寶性論) [KR6n0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0088), and the two recensions of *Dàshèng fǎjiè wú chābié lùn* 大乘法界無差別論 [KR6n0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0089) [KR6n0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0090) — bridge the division to the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q and were a central battleground in the East Asian one-vehicle / five-natures controversy.
- The *Ālambanaparīkṣā* cluster — Dignāga's *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* 觀所緣緣論 [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) with Dharmapāla's commentary [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113), and a late-Míng wave of revival commentaries [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117) — anchors the epistemological side of the division.
- The Cí'ēn doctrinal compendia — Kuījī's *Dàshèng fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* 大乘法苑義林章 [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), Huìzhāo's *Quànfā pútí xīn jí* 勸發菩提心集 [KR6n0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0127) and *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* 能顯中邊慧日論 [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128), Zhìzhōu's *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* 大乘入道次第 [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129) — codify the Cí'ēn school's doctrinal positions, including the five-gotras doctrine and the polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk's 圓測 readings.
- The *Bā shí guījǔ* 八識規矩 cluster ([KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131)–[KR6n0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0140)) — Xuánzàng's (apocryphally attributed) verses on the eight consciousnesses, with Putai's 普泰 1530s Yuán-Míng-transition commentary [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) and a dense Wànlì-Chongzhen-era stratum from Mingyu 明昱, Zhixu 智旭, Deqing 德清, and others. These short verse cycles, together with the *Xiàngzōng bā yào* 相宗八要 anthology [KR6n0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0143)–[KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145), are the late-Míng Fǎxiàng revival's basic curriculum and the principal channel by which Cí'ēn doctrine survives into the Qīng.
- *Dàshèng yìzhāng* 大乘義章 [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) — Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn's 慧遠 580–592 doctrinal encyclopaedia: not a pure Yogācāra work, but a Sui-era Shèlùn-tradition synthesis included here because it remains the most systematic pre-Xuánzàng treatment of the Yogācāra dharma-list in Chinese.

### Important persons

- [彌勒菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%8C%E5%8B%92%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) — the traditional speaker of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and the so-called Maitreya corpus (*Madhyāntavibhāga*, *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra*, etc.); historicity disputed in modern scholarship, but the canonical attribution shapes every East Asian reading of the division.
- [無著菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%84%A1%E8%91%97%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Asaṅga, c. 4th c.) — author of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, the *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn*, and the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*; the architect of the systematic Yogācāra in this division.
- [世親菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%96%E8%A6%AA%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Vasubandhu, c. 4th–5th c.; also rendered 天親菩薩) — author of the *Triṃśikā*, *Viṃśatikā*, *Pañcaskandhaka*, *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn*, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, and *Dàshèng chéngyè lùn* [KR6n0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0086); the most heavily commented author in the division.
- [安慧菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E6%85%A7%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Sthiramati, 6th c.) — author of the *Abhidharmasamuccaya-vyākhyā* underlying T1606 and of the *Madhyāntavibhāga-ṭīkā* underlying parts of T1599; the principal "Old-Yogācāra" exegete reaching China through Paramārtha.
- [護法菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%B7%E6%B3%95%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dharmapāla, c. 530–561) — Nālandā commentator whose reading of the *Triṃśikā* is the spine of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* and whose *Ālambanaparīkṣā-vṛtti* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113) founds the Cí'ēn epistemological tradition.
- [陳那菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%82%A3%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dignāga, c. 480–540) — author of *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and, by implication, of the epistemological reorientation that drives the *Ālambanaparīkṣā* and *Buddhabhūmi-vyākhyāna* portions of the corpus.
- [親光菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%AA%E5%85%89%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Bandhuprabha) — credited author of the *Buddhabhūmi-śāstra* materials underlying the *Chéng wéishí lùn* synthesis.
- [最勝子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%80%E5%8B%9D%E5%AD%90) (Jinaputra) — Indian compiler of *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002), the canonical exegetical key to the *Yogācārabhūmi*.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha, 499–569) — translator of the bulk of the Old-Yogācāra layer (T1584, T1587, T1589, T1593, T1595, T1599, T1610, T1616–1620); the rival transmissional lineage that the Xuánzàng school later partly supersedes.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — translator of the New-Yogācāra core (T1579, T1585, T1586, T1590, T1594, T1597, T1600–1606, T1612, T1614 and many others); the single most important figure for the division and the founder of its Chinese school.
- [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) (Kuījī, 632–682) — Xuánzàng's principal disciple and the doctrinal architect of the Cí'ēn / Fǎxiàng school; author of the *Shùjì*, *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào*, *Yúqié shī dì lùn lüèzuǎn* [KR6n0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0008), *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), and the *Wéishí èrshí lùn shùjì* [KR6n0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0057).
- [慧沼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%B2%BC) (Huìzhāo, 650–714) — second of the Cí'ēn "three masters" (慈恩三祖); author of the *Liǎoyì dēng* [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030) and of the principal polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk in *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- [智周](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%91%A8) (Zhìzhōu, 668–723) — third of the Cí'ēn three masters; author of the *Yǎnmì* [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032) and *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129); closes the Táng commentarial canon of the school.
- [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) (Wǒnch'ǔk, 613–696) — Korean monk at Cháng'ān, lifelong rival of Kuījī; his independent reading of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* is preserved largely in fragments and citations, and his disagreements with the Cí'ēn line drive much of the *Liǎoyì dēng* polemic.
- [太賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E8%B3%A2) (Taehyŏn, fl. mid-8th c.) — Silla Fǎxiàng systematiser; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn xuéjì* [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041), one of the longest sub-commentaries on the *Shùjì*.
- [遁倫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%81%E5%80%AB) (Tullyun, late 7th – early 8th c.) — Korean monk; compiler of *Yúqié lùn jì* 瑜伽論記 [KR6n0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0007), the standard exegetical companion to the *Yogācārabhūmi* throughout East Asia.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) (Yìjìng, 635–713) — translator of *Chéng wéishí bǎoshēng lùn* [KR6n0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0056), *Liùmén jiàoshòu xí dìng lùn* [KR6n0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0084), and *Guān suǒyuán lùn shì* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113); supplies the post-Xuánzàng Indian materials that round out the *Triṃśikā* / *Ālambanaparīkṣā* commentary set.
- [達摩笈多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%94%E6%91%A9%E7%AC%88%E5%A4%9A) (Dharmagupta, d. 619), [佛陀扇多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E6%89%87%E5%A4%9A) (Buddhaśānta), [般若流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) (Prajñāruci), [提雲般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E9%9B%B2%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) (Devaprajña), [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema), [求那跋摩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E6%91%A9) (Guṇavarman) — the chain of pre-Xuánzàng translators through whom the Yogācāra corpus arrives in China between the early fifth and early seventh centuries.
- [慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) (Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn, 523–592) — Sui doctrinal encyclopaedist; the *Dàshèng yìzhāng* [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) is the most influential pre-Xuánzàng Chinese systematisation of Yogācāra topics.
- [普泰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E6%B3%B0) (Pǔtài, fl. 1530s) — late-Míng Fǎxiàng pioneer; the *Bā shí guījǔ bǔzhù* [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) is the catalyst of the late-Míng *Bā shí guījǔ* commentarial wave.
- [王肯堂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%82%AF%E5%A0%82) (Wáng Kěntáng, 1549–1613) — Wànlì-era *jūshì* physician-Buddhist; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn zhèngyì* [KR6n0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0045), a key bridge from the late-Míng *jūshì* scholarship into Fǎxiàng exegesis.
