# 諸宗著述部 (X54)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 10 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6m 中觀部 *Zhōngguān bù* — Buddhist canon — Madhyamaka treatises](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/): 10 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6m 中觀部 *Zhōngguān bù* — Buddhist canon — Madhyamaka treatises](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6m` 中觀部 (*Zhōngguān bù*, "Madhyamaka section") is the Kanripo mirror of the Madhyamaka — Sānlùn 三論 — section of the Chinese Buddhist canon: the Indic Mādhyamaka *śāstras* by Nāgārjuna 龍樹, Āryadeva 提婆 / 聖天, Bhāviveka 清辯, Sthiramati 安慧, Dharmapāla 護法 and others, together with the East-Asian commentarial superstructure they generated, from Sēngzhào's 僧肇 *Zhào lùn* in the early-fifth century down through the late-Ming "*Wù bù qiān*" controversy of the 1590s and the Heian–Edo Japanese Sānlùn scholasticism. In CANWWW  the division's primary translations sit in `div20` between T30N1564 and T30N1578 (interleaved with the abhidharma-period Indic *śāstras* of vol. 30); the Suí–Tang exegetical apparatus runs in `div16` 論疏部 (T1824–T1827, T1852–T1860); and the Sòng–Yuán–Míng sub-commentaries are gathered in `div28` 續論疏部. Kanripo `KR6m` integrates these three CANWWW divisions into one division of 51 catalogued works, organised around the doctrinal core of the *Sān lùn* 三論 ("Three Treatises") that Kumārajīva's Cháng'ān workshop translated in 404–409 and that became, through Jízàng 吉藏 (549–623), the textual basis of an independent Chinese-Buddhist exegetical school.

The corpus falls into six historically distinct strata. (1) The **early-fifth-century Cháng'ān translations** of Kumārajīva (鳩摩羅什, 344–413) under Hòu-Qín 後秦 patronage created the *Three Treatises* foundation: *Bǎi lùn* [KR6m0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0012) (404), *Shí'èr-mén lùn* [KR6m0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0008) (408–409) and *Zhōng lùn* [KR6m0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0001) (409), framed by the Huìyuǎn–Kumārajīva *Dàyì* correspondence [KR6m0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0036) (c. 405–413) and Sēngzhào's *Zhào lùn* [KR6m0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0038) (c. 404–414). (2) **Northern-dynasty and Northern-Liáng retranslations** brought further Indic Mādhyamaka material into Chinese: the Bodhiruci-circle *Bǎizì lùn* [KR6m0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0017), the Prajñāruci translations *Shùnzhōng lùn* [KR6m0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0003) and *Yīshūlújiā lùn* [KR6m0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0018), and the Hexi-corridor *Dàzhàngfū lùn* [KR6m0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0022) of Dào Tài 道泰. (3) The **early-seventh-century Tang renewal** added Bhāviveka's *Prajñāpradīpa* as *Bōrědēng lùn shì* [KR6m0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0004) (Prabhākaramitra, 630–632), then Xuánzàng's 玄奘 cluster of 649–650: the *Karatalaratna* as *Dàshèng zhǎngzhēn lùn* [KR6m0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0023), the Āryadeva root-text *Guǎngbǎi lùn běn* [KR6m0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0014), and Dharmapāla's *Catuḥśataka* commentary as *Dàshèng guǎngbǎi lùn shìlùn* [KR6m0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0015). (4) The **Suí–Tang Sānlùn exegetical synthesis** under Jízàng 吉藏 produced the most coherent doctrinal treatment of the corpus in any East-Asian language — the *Sānlùn xuányì* [KR6m0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0026) (597–599), *Èrdì yì* [KR6m0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0034), *Dàshèng xuánlùn* [KR6m0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0031), and the three running sub-commentaries [KR6m0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0006) [KR6m0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0009) [KR6m0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0013). (5) The **late-Northern-Sòng translation programme** under Dānapāla 施護 retranslated three short Nāgārjuna verse-treatises ([KR6m0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0019), [KR6m0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0020), [KR6m0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0021)), and the Wéijìng 惟淨 group rendered Sthiramati's *Madhyamakavṛtti* as *Dàshèng zhōngguān shìlùn* [KR6m0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0005) (1009–1023) — the only Chinese witness to that commentarial layer. (6) The **late-imperial Chinese reception** is dominated by the Míng-period *Zhàolùn* commentaries of Hānshān Déqīng 憨山德清 [KR6m0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0046) and by the *Wù bù qiān* polemical controversy of 1590–1617 [KR6m0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0047) [KR6m0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0048) [KR6m0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0049), the most articulate late-imperial Chinese-Buddhist case of explicit doctrinal critique of an established canonical text.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The Three Treatises (三論) and the Cháng'ān foundation

The doctrinal core of the division: three Indic Mādhyamaka *śāstras* translated at Cháng'ān 長安 in 404–409 under [姚興](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E8%88%88) Yáo Xìng's patronage and grouped from [僧叡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E5%8F%A1) Sēngruì onward as a single canonical triad.

- *Zhōng lùn* 中論 [KR6m0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0001) (T1564, 409) — Kumārajīva's four-fascicle Chinese rendering of Nāgārjuna's *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* in 27 *pǐn* 品 of negative dialectic, embedded in Piṅgala's (Fànzhì Qīngmù 梵志青目) prose commentary. The principal Chinese witness to the *Mūlamadhyamaka*-commentary layer otherwise lost in Sanskrit; the locus classicus of the *sāndì jì* 三諦偈 (24.18) that became the textual foundation of Tiāntái 天台 doctrine.
- *Shí'èr-mén lùn* 十二門論 [KR6m0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0008) (T1568, 408–409) — Nāgārjuna's twelve-gate companion treatise, condensing the *Mūlamadhyamaka* method into a dozen short investigations.
- *Bǎi lùn* 百論 [KR6m0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0012) (T1569, 404) — Āryadeva's 提婆 *Hundred-Verse Treatise*, the polemical companion to the *Mūlamadhyamaka*, with the prose commentary of *Vasu* (Pósǒu 婆藪).
- *Jiūmóluóshí fǎshī dàyì* 鳩摩羅什法師大義 [KR6m0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0036) (T1856, c. 405–413) — the doctrinal correspondence between [慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) Lúshān Huìyuǎn and Kumārajīva, the principal early-fifth-century epistolary exchange on Mahāyāna doctrine; preserves Huìyuǎn's queries on *dharmakāya*, *prajñā*, and *nirmāṇakāya* with Kumārajīva's Mādhyamaka responses.

#### Sēngzhào and the *Zhào lùn* tradition

The first wholly Chinese articulation of Mādhyamaka and one of the most influential Buddhist works composed in any East-Asian language. The commentarial cluster runs continuously from the Liú-Sòng to the late Míng — a transmission depth matched by only a handful of works in the entire Buddhist canon.

- *Zhào lùn* 肇論 [KR6m0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0038) (T1858, c. 404–414) — Sēngzhào's four-treatise corpus (*Wù bù qiān lùn* 物不遷論, *Bù zhēn kōng lùn* 不真空論, *Bōrě wú zhī lùn* 般若無知論, *Nièpán wú míng lùn* 涅槃無名論), the foundational Chinese-Buddhist articulation of *kōng* 空 in *xuánxué*-inflected idiom. With the pseudepigraphic *Bǎozàng lùn* 寶藏論 [KR6m0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0037) (T1857, attributed but actually Tang, c. 700–900; cf. Sharf 2002).
- The early sub-commentary tradition: [惠達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%A0%E9%81%94) Huìdá's *Zhàolùn shū* [KR6m0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0041) (X866, 5th c., the earliest surviving commentary); Yuánkāng's 元康 Tang *Zhàolùn shū* [KR6m0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0039) (T1859, c. 650–680); Wéncái's 文才 Yuán *Zhàolùn xīnshū* [KR6m0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0040) (T1860, 1300–1320) with its companion *Yóurèn* [KR6m0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0045).
- The Northern-Sòng *Zūnshì–Xiǎoyuè* cluster: Zūnshì's 遵式 *Zhù Zhàolùn shū* [KR6m0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0044) (X870, 1010–1032) and *Zhàolùn shū kē* [KR6m0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0042) (X868, 1050–1100); Xiǎoyuè's 曉月 *Jiākē Zhàolùn xù zhù* [KR6m0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0043) (X869, 1050–1100).
- The late-Míng commentarial flowering: Hānshān Déqīng's 憨山德清 *Zhàolùn lüèzhù* [KR6m0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0046) (X873, 1606–1623) — the principal Chinese late-imperial reading of the *Zhào lùn* and a foundational document of the *Wànlì* Buddhist revival.

#### The *Wù bù qiān* controversy (1590–1617)

A late-Míng doctrinal-philosophical controversy over the proper reading of the second treatise of the *Zhào lùn* — among the principal cases in late-imperial Chinese Buddhism of explicit critique of an established canonical text, and a striking parallel from within Buddhism to the *kǎozhèng* 考證 sensibility of contemporary Confucian scholarship.

- *Wù bù qiān zhèngliàng lùn* 物不遷正量論 [KR6m0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0048) (X879, c. 1590–1617) — Yuèchuān Zhènchéng's 月川鎮澄 (1547–1617) sustained polemical critique of Sēngzhào's *Wù bù qiān lùn*, charging that the formulation 物各性住 unwittingly adopts a substantialist position in tension with the Mahāyāna doctrine of intrinsic emptiness (*xìngkōng* 性空).
- *Wù bù qiān zhèngliàng zhèng* 物不遷正量證 [KR6m0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0047) (X878) by Dàohéng 道衡 and *Wù bù qiān lùn biànjiě* 物不遷論辯解 [KR6m0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0049) (X880) by Zhēnjiè 真界 — the principal contemporary refutations defending the orthodox reading.

#### Jízàng's Sānlùn corpus and the Suí scholastic synthesis

Jízàng 吉藏 (549–623), the founder of the Sānlùn 三論 school, produced at Jiāxiángsì 嘉祥寺 the most coherent doctrinal articulation of the Three-Treatise tradition in any East-Asian language. The cluster of Suí-period works is the single most consequential body of original East-Asian Mādhyamaka thought.

- *Sānlùn xuányì* 三論玄義 [KR6m0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0026) (T1852, 597–599) — the most-studied programmatic statement of Sānlùn doctrine; the canonical introduction to the school for every subsequent commentator (with the Heian–Kamakura–Edo Japanese sub-commentary stratum [KR6m0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0027) [KR6m0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0028) [KR6m0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0029) [KR6m0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0030)).
- *Dàshèng xuánlùn* 大乘玄論 [KR6m0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0031) (T1853, 605–615) — Jízàng's mature five-fascicle synthesis of the Mahāyāna doctrinal categories.
- *Èrdì yì* 二諦義 [KR6m0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0034) (T1854, 597–615) — the principal Sānlùn treatment of the two-truths doctrine, foundational for the entire Chinese reception of Mādhyamaka.
- *Sānlùn lüèzhāng* 三論略章 [KR6m0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0051) (X876) — Jízàng's compact introduction to the *Three Treatises*.
- The three running sub-commentaries: *Zhōngguān lùn shū* 中觀論疏 [KR6m0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0006) (T1824) on the *Zhōng lùn*, *Shí'èr-mén lùn shū* 十二門論疏 [KR6m0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0009) (T1825) on the *Shí'èr-mén lùn*, and *Bǎi lùn shū* 百論疏 [KR6m0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0013) (T1827) on the *Bǎi lùn* — a unified scholastic apparatus on the entire *Three-Treatise* corpus.

#### Other Indic Mādhyamaka treatises in Chinese

The wider Indic Mādhyamaka corpus, brought into Chinese in waves over six centuries:

- *Shùnzhōng lùn* 順中論 [KR6m0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0003) (T1565, 538–543, Prajñāruci 瞿曇般若流支) — Asaṅga's 無著 commentary on Nāgārjuna's *Mūlamadhyamaka*, the unique Indic case of a Yogācāra master commenting on a Mādhyamaka root text.
- *Bōrědēng lùn shì* 般若燈論釋 [KR6m0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0004) (T1566, 630–632, Prabhākaramitra 波羅頗蜜多羅) — Bhāviveka's 清辯 *Prajñāpradīpa*, the principal Svātantrika-Mādhyamaka commentary on the *Mūlamadhyamaka*; Bhāviveka appears here under his alternative Chinese name 分別明菩薩.
- *Dàshèng zhōngguān shìlùn* 大乘中觀釋論 [KR6m0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0005) (T1567, 1009–1023, [惟淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%9F%E6%B7%A8) Wéijìng et al.) — Sthiramati's 安慧 commentary on the *Mūlamadhyamaka*, the unique Chinese witness to that layer of Mādhyamaka exegesis (with the second part preserved only in the Tripiṭaka Koreana K1482).
- *Guǎngbǎi lùn běn* 廣百論本 [KR6m0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0014) (T1570, 650, Xuánzàng) and *Dàshèng guǎngbǎi lùn shìlùn* 大乘廣百論釋論 [KR6m0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0015) (T1571, 650, Xuánzàng) — Āryadeva's *Catuḥśataka* root verses with Dharmapāla's 護法 commentary; the principal Chinese witness to Dharmapāla's Mādhyamaka exegesis. With Wéngui's 文軌 single-fascicle Tang sub-commentary [KR6m0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0016) (T2800) preserved among the Dūnhuáng manuscripts.
- *Bǎizì lùn* 百字論 [KR6m0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0017) (T1572, 508–535, Bodhiruci 菩提流支) — a short Āryadeva treatise.
- *Yīshūlújiā lùn* 壹輸盧迦論 [KR6m0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0018) (T1573, 538–543, Prajñāruci) — a single-verse Nāgārjuna treatise (*Eka-śloka-śāstra*) with auto-commentary.
- *Dàzhàngfū lùn* 大丈夫論 [KR6m0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0022) (T1577, 414–426, Dào Tài 道泰) — *Devala*-bodhisattva's two-fascicle bodhisattva-conduct treatise, translated in Hexi during the Northern Liáng.
- *Dàshèng zhǎngzhēn lùn* 大乘掌珍論 [KR6m0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0023) (T1578, 649, Xuánzàng) — Bhāviveka's *Karatalaratna* ("Jewel in the Hand"), the unique Chinese witness to this short Svātantrika-Mādhyamaka treatise (no Tibetan parallel survives). With the Tang sub-commentary *Zhǎngzhēn lùn shū* [KR6m0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0025) (X788) and the Heian Japanese *Zhǎngzhēn liàng dào* [KR6m0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0024) (T2258).

#### Dānapāla's Sòng Mādhyamaka programme

The late-Northern-Sòng *Yìjīngyuàn* 譯經院 retranslation programme under Emperor Tàizōng 太宗 added three short Nāgārjuna verse-treatises in fresh translations by Dānapāla 施護 (Shīhù):

- *Dàshèng pòyǒu lùn* 大乘破有論 [KR6m0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0019) (T1574, 982–1000) — short refutation of substance-views.
- *Liùshí sòng rúlǐ lùn* 六十頌如理論 [KR6m0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0020) (T1575) — the *Yuktiṣaṣṭikā*, one of Nāgārjuna's six core *yukti* treatises.
- *Dàshèng èrshí sòng lùn* 大乘二十頌論 [KR6m0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0021) (T1576) — short twenty-verse treatise.

#### Other Suí–Tang Sānlùn material

- *Sānlùn yóuyì yì* 三論遊意義 [KR6m0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0035) (T1855, c. 580–610) — the *Qī fǎshī* 磧法師's compact pre-Jízàng Sānlùn manual; one of the few surviving non-Jízàng witnesses to early Sānlùn doctrine.
- *Dàshèng sìlùn xuányì* 大乘四論玄義 [KR6m0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0050) (X784, 620–680, by 均正 Jūnzhèng) — the Tang *Sìlùn xuányì*, expanding the Sānlùn frame to include the *Dà zhì dù lùn* as a fourth foundation; the principal Tang Sānlùn-school work outside Jízàng's corpus.

#### The Heian–Kamakura–Edo Japanese Sānlùn stratum

The transmission of Sānlùn to Japan in the Nara period generated a distinct scholastic tradition that survived through to the Edo, of which the Taishō preserves a substantial corpus:

- *Zhōng lùn shū jì* 中論疏記 [KR6m0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0007) (T2255, c. 780–814) — Anchō's 安澄 sub-commentary on Jízàng's *Zhōngguān lùn shū*; the principal Heian-period Sānlùn work.
- *Shí'èrmén lùn shū wénsī jì* 十二門論疏聞思記 [KR6m0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0011) (T2257, Heian) — Zōkai's 藏海 sub-commentary on Jízàng's *Shí'èr-mén lùn shū*.
- *Zhōngguān lùn èrshíqī pǐn biéshì* 中觀論二十七品別釋 [KR6m0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0002) (T2256, 1527, Kaiken 快憲) — a Muromachi-period systematic re-treatment of the 27 *pǐn* of the *Zhōng lùn*.
- The Chinkai 珍海 (1091–1152) Heian cluster: *Sānlùn xuánshū wényì yào* [KR6m0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0027) (T2299), *Dàshèng xuán wèndá* [KR6m0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0032) (T2303), *Yīchéng yì sījì* [KR6m0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0033) (T2304).
- The later sub-commentaries on Jízàng's *Sānlùn xuányì*: Chōzen's 澄禪 *Sānlùn xuányì jiǎnyōu jí* [KR6m0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0028) (T2300, 1280, Kamakura), Teikai's 貞海 *Sānlùn xuányì chāo* [KR6m0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0029) (T2301), and Bunshō's 聞證 Edo-period *Sānlùn xuányì yòuméng* [KR6m0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0030) (T2302, 1686).

#### Fǎzàng's Huayan reading of the *Shí'èr-mén lùn*

- *Shí'èr-mén lùn zōngzhì yìjì* 十二門論宗致義記 [KR6m0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0010) (T1826, 690–712, by [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) Fǎzàng) — the principal Huáyán-school reading of a Sānlùn root text; documents the late-Tang absorption of Sānlùn doctrine into the Huáyán scholastic frame after the Sānlùn school proper had ceased to be an independent institutional tradition.

### Important persons

#### The Indic Mādhyamaka authors

- [龍樹菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BE%8D%E6%A8%B9%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Lóngshù púsà / Nāgārjuna, c. 150–250) — root author of the Mādhyamaka tradition; in `KR6m` credited with eight texts including the *Zhōng lùn* root verses [KR6m0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0001), the *Shí'èr-mén lùn* [KR6m0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0008), the *Yīshūlújiā lùn* [KR6m0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0018), the Sòng-translated *Dàshèng pòyǒu lùn* [KR6m0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0019), the *Liùshí sòng rúlǐ lùn* [KR6m0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0020), and the *Dàshèng èrshí sòng lùn* [KR6m0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0021). The principal authorial figure of the entire division.
- [提婆菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E5%A9%86%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) / [聖天菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%81%96%E5%A4%A9%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Típó púsà / Shèngtiān / Āryadeva, c. 170–270) — Nāgārjuna's principal disciple; author of the *Bǎi lùn* [KR6m0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0012), *Bǎizì lùn* [KR6m0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0017), and the *Catuḥśataka* root verses [KR6m0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0014). The *Shèngtiān* form is Xuánzàng's seventh-century re-rendering; *Típó* is the Kumārajīva-era transliteration.
- [梵志青目](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A2%B5%E5%BF%97%E9%9D%92%E7%9B%AE) (Fànzhì Qīngmù / Piṅgala, c. 4th c.) — author of the prose commentary on the *Mūlamadhyamaka* embedded in [KR6m0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0001); the unique Chinese witness to this layer of early Mādhyamaka exegesis.
- [清辯菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B8%85%E8%BE%AF%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) / [分別明菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%88%86%E5%88%A5%E6%98%8E%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Qīngbiàn / Fēnbiémíng / Bhāviveka, c. 500–570) — founder of the Svātantrika branch of Mādhyamaka; author of the *Prajñāpradīpa* (= [KR6m0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0004)) and the *Karatalaratna* (= [KR6m0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0023)). The two Chinese names are alternative renderings of the same Sanskrit name.
- [護法菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%B7%E6%B3%95%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Hùfǎ púsà / Dharmapāla, c. 530–561) — Yogācāra master at Nālandā; author of the *Catuḥśataka* commentary [KR6m0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0015), in which his characteristic Yogācāra doctrinal positions are read into the Mādhyamaka root text.
- [安慧菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E6%85%A7%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Ānhuì púsà / Sthiramati, c. 510–570) — Yogācāra master; author of the *Madhyamakavṛtti* preserved only in Chinese as [KR6m0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0005).
- [無著菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%84%A1%E8%91%97%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Wúzhuó púsà / Asaṅga, c. 4th c.) — founder of the Yogācāra school; author of the unusual Mādhyamaka commentary preserved as *Shùnzhōng lùn* [KR6m0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0003).
- [婆藪開士](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A9%86%E8%97%AA%E9%96%8B%E5%A3%AB) (Pósǒu kāishì / Vasu, c. 4th c.) — author of the prose commentary on the *Bǎi lùn* embedded in [KR6m0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0012).
- [提婆羅菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E5%A9%86%E7%BE%85%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Tipóluó / Devala, c. 4th–5th c.) — author of the *Dàzhàngfū lùn* [KR6m0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0022).

#### The translators

- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) (Jiūmóluóshí / Kumārajīva, 344–413) — the most consequential Buddhist translator in Chinese history; created the *Three Treatises* foundation of the division at Cháng'ān in 404–409 ([KR6m0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0001) [KR6m0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0008) [KR6m0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0012)) and conducted the *Dàyì* correspondence with Huìyuǎn ([KR6m0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0036)).
- [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) (Pútíliúzhī / Bodhiruci, fl. 508–535) and [瞿曇般若流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9E%BF%E6%9B%87%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) (Qútán Bōrěliúzhī / Prajñāruci, fl. 538–543) — the two principal Northern-dynasty translators of Mādhyamaka material ([KR6m0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0017), [KR6m0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0003), [KR6m0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0018)). The two are sometimes confused in the catalog tradition; they are distinct individuals.
- [道泰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E6%B3%B0) (Dào Tài, fl. 414–426) — Northern-Liáng translator of [KR6m0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0022); one of the principal Hexi-corridor translators of the early fifth century.
- [波羅頗蜜多羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%A2%E7%BE%85%E9%A0%97%E8%9C%9C%E5%A4%9A%E7%BE%85) (Bōluópōmìduōluó / Prabhākaramitra, 565–633) — early-Tang translator; rendered Bhāviveka's *Prajñāpradīpa* as [KR6m0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0004) in 630–632 at Cháng'ān.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — translated three Mādhyamaka treatises in 649–650 immediately following his return from India ([KR6m0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0014) [KR6m0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0015) [KR6m0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0023)); the principal Tang witness to Bhāviveka and Dharmapāla.
- [施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7) (Shīhù / Dānapāla, fl. 980–1017) — Indian translator-monk at the Sòng *Yìjīngyuàn*; rendered three short Nāgārjuna verse-treatises ([KR6m0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0019) [KR6m0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0020) [KR6m0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0021)).
- [惟淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%9F%E6%B7%A8) (Wéijìng, c. 973–1051) — Chinese imperial-translator at the *Yìjīngyuàn*; led the Sòng team that rendered Sthiramati's commentary as [KR6m0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0005).

#### The Chinese Sānlùn masters

- [僧肇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E8%82%87) (Sēngzhào, 374–414) — Kumārajīva's principal Cháng'ān disciple; author of the *Zhào lùn* [KR6m0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0038), the foundational Chinese Mādhyamaka work and the most-commented-on Chinese-Buddhist treatise after the *Awakening of Faith*. Pseudo-attributed author of the *Bǎozàng lùn* [KR6m0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0037).
- [慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) (Huìyuǎn of Lúshān 廬山, 334–416) — early-Eastern-Jìn Buddhist patriarch at Lúshān; questioner in the Kumārajīva *Dàyì* correspondence [KR6m0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0036).
- [吉藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%97%8F) (Jízàng / Jiāxiáng dàshī 嘉祥大師, 549–623) — founder of the Sānlùn school as an independent doctrinal tradition; author of seven works in `KR6m` ([KR6m0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0006) [KR6m0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0009) [KR6m0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0013) [KR6m0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0026) [KR6m0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0031) [KR6m0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0034) [KR6m0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0051)) including the *Sānlùn xuányì* and the three running sub-commentaries on the *Three Treatises*. The single most consequential exegetical figure in the division.
- [磧法師](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A3%A7%E6%B3%95%E5%B8%AB) (Qī fǎshī, fl. c. 580–610) — pre-Jízàng Suí-period Sānlùn teacher; author of [KR6m0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0035).
- [均正](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9D%87%E6%AD%A3) (Jūnzhèng, 7th c.) — Tang Sānlùn-school master; author of [KR6m0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0050) *Dàshèng sìlùn xuányì*.
- [元康](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E5%BA%B7) (Yuánkāng, fl. c. 650–680) — Tang scholar-monk; the principal Tang commentator on the *Zhào lùn* ([KR6m0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0039)).
- [文軌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%87%E8%BB%8C) (Wéngui, fl. c. 650–700) — Tang sub-commentator on the *Catuḥśataka*; author of [KR6m0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0016) preserved among the Dūnhuáng manuscripts.
- [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) (Fǎzàng, 643–712) — third Huáyán patriarch; appears in `KR6m` as the Huáyán-school reader of the *Shí'èr-mén lùn* in [KR6m0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0010).

#### The Sòng *Zhào lùn* commentators

- [遵式](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%B5%E5%BC%8F) (Zūnshì, c. 964–1032) — Northern-Sòng Tiāntái master; principal *Zhào lùn* commentator of his generation ([KR6m0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0044) *Zhù Zhàolùn shū*, [KR6m0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0042) *Zhàolùn shū kē*).
- [曉月](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%89%E6%9C%88) (Xiǎoyuè, fl. 1050–1100) — author of [KR6m0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0043) *Jiākē Zhàolùn xù zhù*.
- [文才](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%87%E6%89%8D) (Wéncái, 1241–1302) — Yuán scholar-monk; author of *Zhàolùn xīnshū* [KR6m0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0040) and its companion *Yóurèn* [KR6m0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0045).

#### The late-Míng *Wù bù qiān* polemicists

- [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) (Déqīng / Hānshān 憨山, 1546–1623) — the most influential Buddhist intellectual of the late Míng; principal commentator on the *Zhào lùn* in the Wànlì revival ([KR6m0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0046)).
- [鎮澄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%8E%AE%E6%BE%84) (Zhènchéng / Yuèchuān 月川, 1547–1617) — Mt Wǔtái 五臺山 master; author of the *Wù bù qiān zhèngliàng lùn* [KR6m0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0048) that initiated the controversy.
- [道衡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E8%A1%A1) (Dàohéng, fl. 1590–1617) and [真界](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E7%95%8C) (Zhēnjiè, fl. 1590–1617) — the principal contemporary respondents defending the orthodox reading of Sēngzhào ([KR6m0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0047) [KR6m0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0049)).

#### The Japanese Sānlùn scholastics

- [安澄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E6%BE%84) (Anchō, c. 763–814) — Heian-period Sānlùn master at Daian-ji 大安寺; author of the *Zhōng lùn shū jì* [KR6m0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0007), the principal Heian Sānlùn work.

### Topics

- **The *Three Treatises* as a canonical triad.** The grouping of *Zhōng lùn*, *Bǎi lùn*, and *Shí'èr-mén lùn* as a single canonical corpus (三論) is a Chinese — not Indian — formation: it originates with [僧叡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E5%8F%A1) Sēngruì's preface to the *Zhōng lùn* and is consolidated by Jízàng. The Indian Mādhyamaka tradition itself recognises no such triad. The doctrinal-architectural decision to read Nāgārjuna and Āryadeva as a single canonical voice, mediated through Kumārajīva's translation idiom, is the foundational move of East-Asian Mādhyamaka.
- **The Sānlùn school as institutional tradition.** Whether Sānlùn 三論 was an independent Buddhist "school" (*zōng* 宗) in any robust institutional sense is one of the running historiographic questions of East-Asian Buddhology. The institutional thread runs from Sēngzhào and Sēngruì through [僧朗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E6%9C%97) Sēnglǎng, [僧詮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E8%A9%AE) Sēngquán, and [法朗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%9C%97) Fǎlǎng to its high point in Jízàng (549–623), after which it ceased to exist as an independent Chinese-Buddhist tradition — though it survived in Japan as one of the six Nara schools.
- **The two truths (二諦).** The Sānlùn doctrine of *èrdì* — *súdì* 俗諦 (conventional truth) and *zhēndì* 真諦 (ultimate truth) — is the principal doctrinal vehicle of Chinese Mādhyamaka and the subject of Jízàng's most extensive single treatment in [KR6m0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0034). The Sānlùn formulation insists that the two truths are not parallel descriptions of two ontological levels but rather two pedagogical registers for a single non-dual reality.
- **The eight negations (八不).** The Mādhyamaka formula of "neither arising nor ceasing, neither permanent nor annihilated, neither one nor different, neither coming nor going" 不生不滅不常不斷不一不異不來不去, drawn from the dedicatory verses of the *Zhōng lùn*, became in the Sānlùn tradition the condensed doctrinal formula of the *zhōngdào* 中道 ("middle way") and the principal mnemonic of Mādhyamaka instruction in East Asia.
- **Mādhyamaka–Yogācāra relations.** The presence in `KR6m` of three Yogācāra-authored commentaries on Mādhyamaka root texts — Asaṅga on the *Mūlamadhyamaka* ([KR6m0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0003)), Sthiramati on the same ([KR6m0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0005)), and Dharmapāla on the *Catuḥśataka* ([KR6m0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0015)) — documents the Indic and Sino-Indic dialectic between the two great Mahāyāna scholastic traditions. The Tang doctrinal controversy between the Sānlùn / Tiāntái Mādhyamaka reading and the Cí'ēn 慈恩 Yogācāra reading is one of the central debates of Tang Buddhism.
- **Svātantrika versus Prāsaṅgika.** The Indian Mādhyamaka split between Bhāviveka's *svatantra* (positive-syllogistic) method and Buddhapālita's / Candrakīrti's *prasaṅga* (purely-refutative) method enters Chinese only through Bhāviveka — Buddhapālita and Candrakīrti are unknown to the Chinese tradition, the *Prasannapadā* never having been translated. The Chinese reception of Mādhyamaka is therefore implicitly a Svātantrika tradition, and the Tibetan-school distinction is not a live category in the East Asian sources.
- **Kumārajīva's translation idiom.** The doctrinal-philosophical vocabulary that Kumārajīva forged at Cháng'ān in 404–409 to render Indic Mādhyamaka — *kōng* 空 for *śūnya*, *jiǎ* 假 for *prajñapti*, *zhōng* 中 for *madhyama*, *èrdì* 二諦 for *satya-dvaya* — became the operative Buddhist Chinese throughout East Asia and shaped the conceptual vocabulary of every subsequent Chinese-Buddhist tradition, Mādhyamaka or otherwise.
- **The Huìyuǎn–Kumārajīva correspondence.** The *Dàyì* [KR6m0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0036) preserves the principal early-fifth-century epistolary witness to the doctrinal questions a Chinese Buddhist of the late Eastern Jin would raise about Mahāyāna — the nature of the *dharmakāya*, the operation of *prajñā*, the post-mortem persistence of awareness — and to Kumārajīva's Mādhyamaka responses. The text is the foundational document for the early-Chinese-Buddhist intellectual encounter with Indian Mādhyamaka.
- **Sēngzhào and *xuánxué*.** Sēngzhào's *Zhào lùn* [KR6m0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0038) is the principal case in early Chinese Buddhism of the deliberate use of *xuánxué* 玄學 idiom and Lao-Zhuang vocabulary to render Mādhyamaka doctrine. The interpretive question of whether this constitutes successful translation, problematic syncretism, or genuine doctrinal innovation runs from Liebenthal (1948, 1968) and Robinson (1967) through the present.
- **The *Wù bù qiān* controversy.** The 1590–1617 polemical engagement of Zhènchéng with Sēngzhào ([KR6m0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0048) [KR6m0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0047) [KR6m0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0049)) is one of the principal cases in late-imperial Chinese Buddhism of explicit doctrinal critique of an established canonical text — a stance more familiar from late-imperial Confucian *kǎozhèng* 考證 scholarship than from the conventional Buddhist commentarial tradition, and a significant marker of late-Ming Buddhist intellectual sophistication.
- **The Sòng retranslation programme.** Dānapāla's late-Northern-Sòng translations ([KR6m0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0019)–[KR6m0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0021)) document the imperial-court attempt under Tàizōng and Zhēnzōng to systematically retranslate the late-Indic Buddhist treatise corpus into Chinese — a programme that gave Chinese its only versions of several core Nāgārjuna verse-treatises (the *Yuktiṣaṣṭikā* in particular) but never displaced the Kumārajīva translations as the operative basis of Chinese Mādhyamaka.
- **Pseudepigraphic transmission.** The *Bǎozàng lùn* [KR6m0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0037) is a Tang-period pseudepigraphic *śāstra* canonised under Sēngzhào's name and transmitted as authentic for over a millennium. Sharf 2002 has shown its importance for the formation of pre-Sòng Chan literature, and the work is a case-study in the way the East-Asian canon absorbed and re-attributed later texts to early-Buddhist authorities.
- **East-Asian transmission.** Sānlùn was carried to Japan by [慧灌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E7%81%8C) Hyegwan in the early seventh century and became one of the six Nara schools (*Sanron-shū* 三論宗); the Japanese reception is documented in `KR6m` by the Heian–Kamakura–Edo commentarial stratum ([KR6m0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0007) [KR6m0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0011) [KR6m0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0027)–[KR6m0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0030) [KR6m0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0032) [KR6m0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0033) [KR6m0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6m/KR6m0002)), which preserves a continuous interpretive tradition of Jízàng's Suí-period scholarship into the Edo period.

- [KR6d 法華部 *Fǎhuá bù* — Buddhist Canon — Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Lotus) Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/): 16 texts (48%)

## Division note: [KR6n 瑜伽部 *Yújiā bù* — Yogācāra works](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6n collects the Chinese canon's holdings for the Yogācāra (瑜伽 *yújiā*) doctrinal stream — the abhidharmic-idealist tradition that descends from the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* and the works of Asaṅga 無著菩薩 and Vasubandhu 世親菩薩 in fourth- and fifth-century North India, and that becomes the East Asian Fǎxiàng 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 school after Xuánzàng 玄奘 reimports it in the mid-seventh century. The doctrinal core is established by the CANWWW Taishō *Yújiā bù* (`div30`, Taishō Vol. 30–31, Nos. 1579–1627): the *Yogācārabhūmi* and its summaries, the *Madhyāntavibhāga* and *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* of the so-called Maitreya corpus, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* of Asaṅga, the *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā* of Vasubandhu, the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, the *Ratnagotravibhāga*, the Hundred-Dharmas list, Dignāga's 陳那菩薩 *Ālambanaparīkṣā*, and the Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha hybrids preserved at T1610–1611 and T1626–1627.

The division as catalogued in Kanripo, however, extends well beyond the Taishō *Yújiā bù* proper: it folds in the Cí'ēn-school commentarial canon of Vols. 42–45 (Kuījī's 窺基 *Chéng wéishí lùn shùjì* and *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng*; Huìzhāo 慧沼 and Zhìzhōu 智周 sub-commentaries), the late-Táng to Wǔdài Dūnhuáng Yogācāra fragments of Taishō Vol. 85, the Japanese Hossō 法相 scholastic apparatus of Vols. 65–70, and a sizeable late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng-revival corpus in *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 39 and 46–55. Three transmissional layers must therefore be kept distinct when reading the division: the **Old-Yogācāra** layer of Paramārtha 真諦 (c. 546–569), which is closer to a Valabhī recension and preserves the *trisvabhāva* and *amalavijñāna* in idiosyncratic form; the **New-Yogācāra** layer of Xuánzàng (646–664), based on Nālandā materials and Dharmapāla's 護法菩薩 reading; and the **East Asian scholastic** layer (Táng Cí'ēn school, Korean Hyŏnyu monks at Cháng'ān, Heian/Kamakura Hossō, Ming Cíbēi-Cí'ēn revivalists), in which the imported Indian texts become objects of an autonomous and very long-lived commentarial industry. The chronological span runs from c. 414 (Dharmakṣema's 曇無讖 *Bodhisattvabhūmi* [KR6n0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0003)) to the late seventeenth century (Ouyi Zhixu's 智旭 *Xiàngzōng bā yào zhíjiě* [KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145)) — roughly twelve centuries of continuous Yogācāra scholasticism in Chinese.

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Yúqié shī dì lùn* 瑜伽師地論 [KR6n0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0001) — Xuánzàng's 646–648 translation of the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* in 100 *juǎn*; the encyclopaedic root text of the entire division, conventionally attributed to Maitreya 彌勒菩薩 but in fact a multi-author stratified compilation of the Asaṅga circle. The exegetical aid *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* 瑜伽師地論釋 [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002) of Jinaputra 最勝子 accompanies it.
- *Chéng wéishí lùn* 成唯識論 [KR6n0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0016) — Xuánzàng and Kuījī's 659 redaction of the ten Indian *Triṃśikā*-bhāṣyas around Dharmapāla's reading; the doctrinal charter of the Cí'ēn school. The commentarial pyramid stacked over it — Kuījī's *Shùjì* 述記 [KR6n0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0026), *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào* 掌中樞要 [KR6n0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0029), Huìzhāo's *Liǎoyì dēng* 了義燈 [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030), Zhìzhōu's *Yǎnmì* 演祕 [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032), and Taehyŏn's 太賢 *Xuéjì* 學記 [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041) — defines Táng-period Fǎxiàng orthodoxy.
- *Wéishí sānshí lùn sòng* 唯識三十論頌 [KR6n0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0022) and *Wéishí èrshí lùn* 唯識二十論 [KR6n0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0055) — Vasubandhu's *Triṃśikā* and *Viṃśatikā*, translated by Xuánzàng in 648 and 661; the textual nucleus around which both Indian and Chinese consciousness-only argumentation organises itself. Paramārtha's earlier renderings as *Zhuǎn shí lùn* 轉識論 [KR6n0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0024), *Wéishí lùn* 唯識論 [KR6n0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0053), and *Dàshèng wéishí lùn* 大乘唯識論 [KR6n0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0054) preserve the Old-Yogācāra reception.
- The *Shè dàshèng lùn* 攝大乘論 cluster — Asaṅga's *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, surviving in three Chinese translations (Buddhaśānta 531–534 [KR6n0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0058), Paramārtha 563–564 [KR6n0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0059), Xuánzàng 648–649 [KR6n0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0060)) plus the *Bhāṣya* in three further versions [KR6n0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0061) [KR6n0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0063) [KR6n0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0064) [KR6n0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0065) and a thicket of Sui–Táng commentaries and Dūnhuáng *zhāng* fragments [KR6n0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0066)–[KR6n0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0070). The cluster is the principal vehicle by which the *ālayavijñāna* doctrine enters China, and the Paramārtha line generates the Shèlùn 攝論 lineage that the Cí'ēn school then displaces.
- The *Madhyāntavibhāga* cluster — Paramārtha's *Zhōngbiān fēnbié lùn* 中邊分別論 [KR6n0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0071) and Xuánzàng's *Biàn zhōngbiān lùn* 辯中邊論 [KR6n0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0072) plus its verse [KR6n0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0073) and Kuījī's *Shùjì* [KR6n0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0075); with the closely related *Shíbā kōng lùn* 十八空論 [KR6n0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0074) and *Sān wúxìng lùn* 三無性論 [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) of the Paramārtha corpus.
- *Dàshèng zhuāngyán jīng lùn* 大乘莊嚴經論 [KR6n0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0080) — the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra* with Vasubandhu-circle commentary, Prabhākaramitra 630–633; together with *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn* 顯揚聖教論 [KR6n0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0077), Asaṅga's digest of the *Yogācārabhūmi* in Xuánzàng's 645–646 rendering.
- *Dàshèng āpídámó jí lùn* 大乘阿毘達磨集論 [KR6n0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0081) and its expanded *Zájí lùn* 雜集論 [KR6n0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0082) — Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya* and Sthiramati's bhāṣya; the Yogācāra abhidharma proper. Read in China together with the *Dàshèng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘五蘊論 [KR6n0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0094), the *Guǎng wǔyùn lùn* 大乘廣五蘊論 [KR6n0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0095), and the *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn* 大乘百法明門論 [KR6n0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0096) of Vasubandhu, the four works form the standard East Asian curriculum in Yogācāra dharma-taxonomy.
- The tathāgatagarbha-Yogācāra hybrids — *Fóxìng lùn* 佛性論 [KR6n0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0087), the *Ratnagotravibhāga* (*Jiūjìng yīshèng bǎoxìng lùn* 究竟一乘寶性論) [KR6n0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0088), and the two recensions of *Dàshèng fǎjiè wú chābié lùn* 大乘法界無差別論 [KR6n0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0089) [KR6n0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0090) — bridge the division to the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q and were a central battleground in the East Asian one-vehicle / five-natures controversy.
- The *Ālambanaparīkṣā* cluster — Dignāga's *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* 觀所緣緣論 [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) with Dharmapāla's commentary [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113), and a late-Míng wave of revival commentaries [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117) — anchors the epistemological side of the division.
- The Cí'ēn doctrinal compendia — Kuījī's *Dàshèng fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* 大乘法苑義林章 [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), Huìzhāo's *Quànfā pútí xīn jí* 勸發菩提心集 [KR6n0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0127) and *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* 能顯中邊慧日論 [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128), Zhìzhōu's *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* 大乘入道次第 [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129) — codify the Cí'ēn school's doctrinal positions, including the five-gotras doctrine and the polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk's 圓測 readings.
- The *Bā shí guījǔ* 八識規矩 cluster ([KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131)–[KR6n0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0140)) — Xuánzàng's (apocryphally attributed) verses on the eight consciousnesses, with Putai's 普泰 1530s Yuán-Míng-transition commentary [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) and a dense Wànlì-Chongzhen-era stratum from Mingyu 明昱, Zhixu 智旭, Deqing 德清, and others. These short verse cycles, together with the *Xiàngzōng bā yào* 相宗八要 anthology [KR6n0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0143)–[KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145), are the late-Míng Fǎxiàng revival's basic curriculum and the principal channel by which Cí'ēn doctrine survives into the Qīng.
- *Dàshèng yìzhāng* 大乘義章 [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) — Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn's 慧遠 580–592 doctrinal encyclopaedia: not a pure Yogācāra work, but a Sui-era Shèlùn-tradition synthesis included here because it remains the most systematic pre-Xuánzàng treatment of the Yogācāra dharma-list in Chinese.

### Important persons

- [彌勒菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%8C%E5%8B%92%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) — the traditional speaker of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and the so-called Maitreya corpus (*Madhyāntavibhāga*, *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra*, etc.); historicity disputed in modern scholarship, but the canonical attribution shapes every East Asian reading of the division.
- [無著菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%84%A1%E8%91%97%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Asaṅga, c. 4th c.) — author of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha*, the *Xiǎnyáng shèngjiào lùn*, and the *Abhidharmasamuccaya*; the architect of the systematic Yogācāra in this division.
- [世親菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%96%E8%A6%AA%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Vasubandhu, c. 4th–5th c.; also rendered 天親菩薩) — author of the *Triṃśikā*, *Viṃśatikā*, *Pañcaskandhaka*, *Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn*, the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, and *Dàshèng chéngyè lùn* [KR6n0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0086); the most heavily commented author in the division.
- [安慧菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E6%85%A7%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Sthiramati, 6th c.) — author of the *Abhidharmasamuccaya-vyākhyā* underlying T1606 and of the *Madhyāntavibhāga-ṭīkā* underlying parts of T1599; the principal "Old-Yogācāra" exegete reaching China through Paramārtha.
- [護法菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%B7%E6%B3%95%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dharmapāla, c. 530–561) — Nālandā commentator whose reading of the *Triṃśikā* is the spine of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* and whose *Ālambanaparīkṣā-vṛtti* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113) founds the Cí'ēn epistemological tradition.
- [陳那菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%82%A3%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Dignāga, c. 480–540) — author of *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and, by implication, of the epistemological reorientation that drives the *Ālambanaparīkṣā* and *Buddhabhūmi-vyākhyāna* portions of the corpus.
- [親光菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%AA%E5%85%89%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Bandhuprabha) — credited author of the *Buddhabhūmi-śāstra* materials underlying the *Chéng wéishí lùn* synthesis.
- [最勝子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%80%E5%8B%9D%E5%AD%90) (Jinaputra) — Indian compiler of *Yúqié shī dì lùn shì* [KR6n0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0002), the canonical exegetical key to the *Yogācārabhūmi*.
- [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (Paramārtha, 499–569) — translator of the bulk of the Old-Yogācāra layer (T1584, T1587, T1589, T1593, T1595, T1599, T1610, T1616–1620); the rival transmissional lineage that the Xuánzàng school later partly supersedes.
- [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng, 602–664) — translator of the New-Yogācāra core (T1579, T1585, T1586, T1590, T1594, T1597, T1600–1606, T1612, T1614 and many others); the single most important figure for the division and the founder of its Chinese school.
- [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) (Kuījī, 632–682) — Xuánzàng's principal disciple and the doctrinal architect of the Cí'ēn / Fǎxiàng school; author of the *Shùjì*, *Zhǎngzhōng shūyào*, *Yúqié shī dì lùn lüèzuǎn* [KR6n0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0008), *Fǎyuàn yìlín zhāng* [KR6n0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0124), and the *Wéishí èrshí lùn shùjì* [KR6n0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0057).
- [慧沼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%B2%BC) (Huìzhāo, 650–714) — second of the Cí'ēn "three masters" (慈恩三祖); author of the *Liǎoyì dēng* [KR6n0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0030) and of the principal polemic against Wǒnch'ǔk in *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- [智周](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%91%A8) (Zhìzhōu, 668–723) — third of the Cí'ēn three masters; author of the *Yǎnmì* [KR6n0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0032) and *Dàshèng rùdào cìdì* [KR6n0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0129); closes the Táng commentarial canon of the school.
- [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) (Wǒnch'ǔk, 613–696) — Korean monk at Cháng'ān, lifelong rival of Kuījī; his independent reading of the *Chéng wéishí lùn* is preserved largely in fragments and citations, and his disagreements with the Cí'ēn line drive much of the *Liǎoyì dēng* polemic.
- [太賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E8%B3%A2) (Taehyŏn, fl. mid-8th c.) — Silla Fǎxiàng systematiser; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn xuéjì* [KR6n0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0041), one of the longest sub-commentaries on the *Shùjì*.
- [遁倫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%81%E5%80%AB) (Tullyun, late 7th – early 8th c.) — Korean monk; compiler of *Yúqié lùn jì* 瑜伽論記 [KR6n0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0007), the standard exegetical companion to the *Yogācārabhūmi* throughout East Asia.
- [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) (Yìjìng, 635–713) — translator of *Chéng wéishí bǎoshēng lùn* [KR6n0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0056), *Liùmén jiàoshòu xí dìng lùn* [KR6n0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0084), and *Guān suǒyuán lùn shì* [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113); supplies the post-Xuánzàng Indian materials that round out the *Triṃśikā* / *Ālambanaparīkṣā* commentary set.
- [達摩笈多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%94%E6%91%A9%E7%AC%88%E5%A4%9A) (Dharmagupta, d. 619), [佛陀扇多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E6%89%87%E5%A4%9A) (Buddhaśānta), [般若流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) (Prajñāruci), [提雲般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E9%9B%B2%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) (Devaprajña), [曇無讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E7%84%A1%E8%AE%96) (Dharmakṣema), [求那跋摩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E6%91%A9) (Guṇavarman) — the chain of pre-Xuánzàng translators through whom the Yogācāra corpus arrives in China between the early fifth and early seventh centuries.
- [慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) (Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn, 523–592) — Sui doctrinal encyclopaedist; the *Dàshèng yìzhāng* [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122) is the most influential pre-Xuánzàng Chinese systematisation of Yogācāra topics.
- [普泰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E6%B3%B0) (Pǔtài, fl. 1530s) — late-Míng Fǎxiàng pioneer; the *Bā shí guījǔ bǔzhù* [KR6n0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0131) is the catalyst of the late-Míng *Bā shí guījǔ* commentarial wave.
- [王肯堂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%82%AF%E5%A0%82) (Wáng Kěntáng, 1549–1613) — Wànlì-era *jūshì* physician-Buddhist; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn zhèngyì* [KR6n0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0045), a key bridge from the late-Míng *jūshì* scholarship into Fǎxiàng exegesis.
- [通潤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%9A%E6%BD%A4) (Tōngrùn, 1565–1624) — Yúfēng 玉峯 master; author of *Chéng wéishí lùn jíjiě* [KR6n0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0044) and one of the leading Fǎxiàng-revivalist preachers of the Wànlì–Tianqi period.
- [明昱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%98%8E%E6%98%B1) (Míngyù, late 16th – early 17th c.) — late-Míng Fǎxiàng commentator on *Bā shí guījǔ*, *Bǎifǎ*, and *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn*; the single most prolific late-Míng author within the division.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) (Ouyi Zhìxù, 1599–1655) — late-Míng Tiāntái–Pure Land master whose *zhíjiě* 直解 commentaries on the *Bā shí guījǔ*, *Bǎifǎ*, *Chéng wéishí lùn*, *Guān suǒyuányuán lùn*, and *Xiàngzōng bā yào* ([KR6n0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0047), [KR6n0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0051), [KR6n0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0106), [KR6n0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0115), [KR6n0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0137), [KR6n0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0145)) integrate Cí'ēn doctrine into the Ming syncretic synthesis.
- [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) (Hānshān Déqīng, 1546–1623) — one of the "four great masters of the late Míng"; his *Bā shí guījǔ tōngshuō* [KR6n0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0135) gives the eight-consciousnesses schema its Chán-inflected late-Míng reading.

### Topics

- **Vijñaptimātra / cittamātra** (唯識 *wéishí*). The thesis that what appears as an external object is a transformation of consciousness; argued textually through Vasubandhu's *Viṃśatikā* and *Triṃśikā* and exegetically through the entire *Chéng wéishí lùn* commentarial pyramid.
- **The eight consciousnesses** (八識 *bā shí*), with particular attention to the *ālayavijñāna* (阿賴耶識) as substrate and *kliṣṭamanas* (染汚意) as the sixth-to-seventh-consciousness link. Paramārtha's idiosyncratic positing of a ninth, *amalavijñāna* 阿摩羅識, is one of the principal Old-Yogācāra peculiarities. The *Bā shí guījǔ* tradition turns the eight-consciousness schema into a Ming pedagogical genre.
- **The three natures** (三性 *sān xìng*, *trisvabhāva*): *parikalpita* (遍計所執), *paratantra* (依他起), *pariniṣpanna* (圓成實). The cross-cutting **three non-natures** (三無性) doctrine is foregrounded in Paramārtha's *Sān wúxìng lùn* [KR6n0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0079) and is the principal hermeneutic key for reconciling the Yogācāra ontology with the Prajñāpāramitā emptiness teaching.
- **Five gotras / five natures** (五姓各別 *wǔxìng gèbié*). The Yogācārabhūmi taxonomy of five fixed spiritual lineages, against which Wǒnch'ǔk and the East Asian one-vehicle traditions argue. The Cí'ēn defence of the five-gotras position is the principal polemical thread of Huìzhāo's *Néng xiǎn zhōngbiān huìrì lùn* [KR6n0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0128).
- **The Hundred Dharmas** (百法 *bǎifǎ*). Vasubandhu's 5-category × 100-item taxonomy of dharmas (T1614); becomes the standard East Asian Buddhist abhidharmic primer and generates a long commentarial chain from Kuījī's *Dàshèng bǎifǎ míngmén lùn shū* [KR6n0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0098) through the Dūnhuáng *Kāizōng yìjì* [KR6n0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0107) to the Wànlì-era revivalist commentaries [KR6n0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0103)–[KR6n0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0106).
- **Stages of the Yoga practitioner** (瑜伽師地 *yúqié shī dì*) — the seventeen-bhūmi structure of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, organising the entire division.
- **Yogācāra–tathāgatagarbha synthesis**. T1610 *Fóxìng lùn*, T1611 *Bǎoxìng lùn*, T1626–1627 *Fǎjiè wú chābié lùn*, and T1612 *Wǔyùn lùn* sit at the seam between Yogācāra and the *tathāgatagarbha* literature of KR6q; the question of whether the *tathāgatagarbha* is reducible to the *ālayavijñāna* shapes both the Old-Yogācāra reception in China and the *Awakening of Faith* tradition.
- **Epistemology of perception (所緣緣)**. Through Dignāga's *Ālambanaparīkṣā* [KR6n0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0112) and its commentaries, the question of what constitutes a valid object of perception becomes a Yogācāra theme; it is taken up again in the Wànlì–early Qīng commentary wave of [KR6n0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0114)–[KR6n0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0117).
- **Old- vs. New-Yogācāra** (舊譯 *jiùyì* / 新譯 *xīnyì*). The Paramārtha-line readings of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* and *Triṃśikā* differ systematically from Xuánzàng's: on *amalavijñāna*, on the status of the *paratantra*, and on the relation between *vāsanā* and the *ālaya*. The division as a whole preserves both layers in parallel — the cataloguing principle is doctrinal subject matter, not translatorial school.
- **Cí'ēn school polemics**. Internal to the Táng layer: Kuījī vs. Wǒnch'ǔk on the reading of T1585; Huìzhāo's continuation of that polemic; Zhìzhōu's consolidation. These polemics define the canonical shape of the Fǎxiàng curriculum.
- **East Asian transmission and revival**. The division is the textual basis for three successive scholastic traditions: Táng Cí'ēn (mid-7th to early 8th c., centred at Cháng'ān, with Silla and Goguryeo participation), Heian–Kamakura Hossō (Vols. 65–70 of the Taishō, c. 800–1500), and late-Míng / early-Qīng Fǎxiàng revival (c. 1530–1660, *Xùzàngjīng* Vols. 46–55).

## Division note (scope only): [KR6d 法華部 *Fǎhuá bù* — Buddhist Canon — Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Lotus) Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6d` corresponds to the *Fǎhuá bù* 法華部 of the Taishō structural ordering — the Lotus Sūtra and its satellite scriptures in Taishō volume 9, the Lotus sub-commentary tradition in Taishō volumes 26 and 33–34, the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal-and-meditation corpus in Taishō volume 46, the Lotus Dūnhuáng 敦煌 fragments in volume 85, and the very large Sòng–Qīng manuscript continuation of all these strands preserved in the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. In Wilkinson's outline of the Taishō (§29.5.8), volume 9 is identified as "*Fǎhuá bù* (Lotus and other Mahāyāna sūtras)"; Kanripo's `KR6d` extends that vol. 9 nucleus outward to absorb all Chinese-language Lotus commentary and the entire Tiāntái scholastic apparatus that grows out of it, because in East-Asian classification the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal tradition — including its meditation manuals, doctrinal-classification literature, and ritual / *chànyí* 懺儀 works — is canonically attached to the Lotus Sūtra rather than treated as an independent *zōng* 宗 section.

### Scope and scholarly tradition

### Important texts and text clusters

The 249 per-text notes in `kb/KR6d/` organise into five recognisable clusters.

#### The Lotus Sūtra itself and its parallel translations

- *Zhèng fǎhuá jīng* 正法華經 [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002) — Dharmarakṣa's 竺法護 translation of 286 CE, the earliest complete Chinese Lotus, surviving in 10 *juan*.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001) — Kumārajīva's 鳩摩羅什 translation of 406 CE, the dominant East-Asian recension in 7 *juan* and 28 chapters; the literary base for virtually all subsequent Lotus exegesis in Chinese.
- *Tiānpǐn miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 添品妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003) — the Suí (601) collation by Jñānagupta 闍那崛多 and Dharmagupta 笈多, incorporating the *Devadatta* chapter and the *Pǔmén pǐn* 普門品 verses.
- *Sàtán fēntuólì jīng* 薩曇分陀利經 [KR6d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0004) — a Western Jìn anonymous partial translation of the *Devadatta* episode, preserving a textual stratum independent of the three full versions.

#### Satellite Lotus-cycle sūtras (vol. 9)

- *Wúliàng yì jīng* 無量義經 [KR6d0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0118) — the Liáng-period "Sūtra of Innumerable Meanings," traditionally the prologue of the East-Asian "Threefold Lotus" 法華三部經.
- *Fóshuō Guān Pǔxián púsà xíngfǎ jīng* 佛說觀普賢菩薩行法經 [KR6d0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0120) — the Liú-Sòng-period "Sūtra of the Contemplation of Samantabhadra's Practice," the epilogue of the same triad.
- *Fóshuō fǎhuá sānmèi jīng* 佛說法華三昧經 [KR6d0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0108), *Bùtuìzhuǎn fǎlún jīng* 不退轉法輪經 [KR6d0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0106), *Dà fǎgǔ jīng* 大法鼓經 [KR6d0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0109), *Dà sàzhē Nígānzǐ suǒshuō jīng* 大薩遮尼乾子所說經 [KR6d0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0111) — Mahāyāna sūtras grouped with the Lotus on doctrinal and thematic grounds (one-vehicle teaching, irreversibility, the Tathāgata's hidden lifespan).

#### The *Tiāntái sāndàbù* 天台三大部 and their commentaries

- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuányì* 妙法蓮華經玄義 [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006) — Zhìyǐ's 593 Yùquánsì lectures on the doctrinal meaning of the Lotus, recorded by Guàndǐng; the foundational systematic theology of Tiāntái, source for the *wǔshí bājiào* 五時八教 classification.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng wénjù* 妙法蓮華經文句 [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014) — Zhìyǐ's 587 phrase-by-phrase commentary on Kumārajīva's Lotus, recorded by Guàndǐng; pairs with the *Xuányì* as the doctrinal-plus-textual exegetical core.
- *Móhē zhǐguān* 摩訶止觀 [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) — Zhìyǐ's 594 lectures on Tiāntái meditation, recorded by Guàndǐng; the most systematic *śamatha-vipaśyanā* manual in Chinese, organised on the *shíjìng × shíchéng* 十境十乘 matrix.
- *Fǎhuá xuányì shìqiān* 法華玄義釋籤 [KR6d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0007), *Fǎhuá wénjù jì* 法華文句記 [KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015), and *Zhǐguān fǔxíng zhuànhóngjué* 止觀輔行傳弘決 [KR6d0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0131) — Zhànrán's 湛然 (711–782) standard sub-commentaries on each member of the *sāndàbù*; the principal textual base of the Sòng Tiāntái revival.

#### Alternative Lotus-commentary traditions

- *Fǎhuá jīng yìjì* 法華經義記 [KR6d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0005) — Fǎyún's 法雲 Liáng-period exegesis, the principal southern pre-Tiāntái reading and the polemical target of Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì*.
- *Fǎhuá xuánlùn* 法華玄論 [KR6d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0023), *Fǎhuá yìshū* 法華義疏 [KR6d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0024), *Fǎhuá yóuyì* 法華遊意 [KR6d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0025) — Jízàng's 吉藏 (549–623) Sānlùn 三論-school readings, doctrinally distinct from Tiāntái.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng xuánzàn* 妙法蓮華經玄贊 [KR6d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0026) — Kuījī's 窺基 (632–682) Cí'ēn 慈恩 / Yogācāra reading of the Lotus, the principal Faxiang interpretation.

#### Tiāntái doctrinal, meditation, and ritual literature (vol. 46)

- *Sìjiào yì* 四教義 [KR6d0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0166) and *Tiāntái sìjiào yí* 天台四教儀 [KR6d0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0168) — Zhìyǐ's and the late-Táng / Korean Chégwan 諦觀's expositions of the four doctrinal teachings, the most-studied Tiāntái catechetical works.

- [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) — translator of the standard Lotus recension (T262 = [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001)); the literary register of his translation supplied the canonical Sinitic vocabulary of all subsequent Lotus exegesis in this division.
- [竺法護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E6%B3%95%E8%AD%B7) — translator of the earliest complete Chinese Lotus (T263 = [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002), 286) and of several satellite vol. 9 sūtras; his Lotus survives as the principal philological witness independent of Kumārajīva.
- [闍那崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%97%8D%E9%82%A3%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) — co-translator with Dharmagupta 笈多 of the Suí Lotus recension (T264 = [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003), 601), source of the textual additions to the received Kumārajīva Lotus.
- [法雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E9%9B%B2) — Liáng-period exegete of the Lotus ([KR6d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0005)); the standard pre-Tiāntái southern reading, against which Zhìyǐ defined his own system.
- [慧思](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%80%9D) — Tiāntái second patriarch and Zhìyǐ's teacher; author of the *Fǎhuá jīng ānlèxíng yì* [KR6d0156](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0156) and other proto-Tiāntái Lotus-meditation works.
- [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) — third Tiāntái patriarch and de facto founder of Chinese Tiāntái doctrine; lecturer of the *sāndàbù* and dozens of other works in this division (the most-cited person in `KR6d`, named in ≈ 25 per-text notes).
- [灌頂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%81%8C%E9%A0%82) — Zhìyǐ's principal disciple and the redactor / co-author of nearly the entire Zhìyǐ corpus; also author of the *Guóqīng bǎilù* [KR6d0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0183), the documentary record of the early Tiāntái community.
- [吉藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%97%8F) — Sānlùn master whose Lotus commentaries ([KR6d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0023)–[KR6d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0025), [KR6d0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0128)) represent the principal alternative early-Suí exegetical line.
- [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) — Cí'ēn / Faxiang master who gave the Lotus a Yogācāra reading ([KR6d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0026)); the source of the *xuánzàn* sub-commentary tradition.
- [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) — sixth Tiāntái patriarch and reviver of the school in the mid-Táng; author of the canonical sub-commentaries on the *sāndàbù* ([KR6d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0007), [KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015), [KR6d0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0131)) and of the doctrinally generative *Shí bùèr mén* [KR6d0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0157) and *Jīngāngbēi* [KR6d0175](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0175).
- [空海](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A9%BA%E6%B5%B7) — founder of Japanese Shingon and author of seven Lotus-related Heian works in this division (e.g. [KR6d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0036)–[KR6d0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0042)), giving the Lotus its esoteric / *mìjiào* 密教 reading.

- [仁岳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BB%81%E5%B2%B3) — Zhīlǐ's disciple who later turned to the *shānwài* 山外 position; author of the *Sìmíng Rényuè yìshuō cóngshū* [KR6d0224](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0224), the principal *shānwài* counter-statement.
- [從義](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%9E%E7%BE%A9) — late-Sòng commentator on the *Móhē zhǐguān* and *Shí bùèr mén* whose works ([KR6d0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0139)–[KR6d0141](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0141)) preserve the post-Zhīlǐ scholastic apparatus.
- [宗曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E6%9B%89) — Sòng compiler of the *Sìmíng zūnzhě jiàoxíng lù* [KR6d0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0186), the corpus of Zhīlǐ's writings; principal documentary editor of *shānjiā* Tiāntái.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) — Míng-period reviver of Tiāntái and author of the *Jiàoguān gāngzōng* [KR6d0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0188); the principal late-imperial systematiser whose works re-frame Tiāntái for the Míng-Qīng setting.
- [靈耀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9D%88%E8%80%80) — Qīng-period Tiāntái commentator on the *Móhē zhǐguān* and the *sāndàbù* ([KR6d0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0142) and related); his work is the principal Qīng Tiāntái scholastic continuation.

### Topics

- **The ekayāna 一乘 doctrine and *kāiquán xiǎnshí* 開權顯實.** The proclamation in chapters 2–9 of the Lotus that the *śrāvaka* / *pratyekabuddha* / *bodhisattva* three vehicles are provisional (*quán* 權) and the Buddha-vehicle alone is real (*shí* 實) is the central scriptural commitment around which the entire Tiāntái doctrinal apparatus is built, and almost every Sinitic Lotus exegete from Fǎyún onward addresses its hermeneutic status.
- **The *jìmén* / *běnmén* 跡門／本門 division.** The split of the Lotus into a "trace-gate" (chapters 1–14) and an "origin-gate" (15–28) is associated with Dàoxuān's preface to Kumārajīva ([KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001)) and given systematic articulation in Zhìyǐ's *Xuányì* [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006); it remains the standard Sinitic exegetical schema through the entire division.
- **The *wǔshí bājiào* 五時八教 classification.** Zhìyǐ's chronological-and-modal organisation of the Buddha's *kerygma* into five periods (*Huāyán*, *Lùyuàn / Āhán*, *Fāngděng*, *Bōrě*, *Fǎhuá-Nièpán*) and eight modes is developed in the *Xuányì*, summarised in [KR6d0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0166) and [KR6d0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0167), and given canonical compact form in Chégwan's *Tiāntái sìjiào yí* [KR6d0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0168); it is the basic doctrinal-classification apparatus of the division.

## Division note: [KR6d 法華部 *Fǎhuá bù* — Buddhist Canon — Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Lotus) Section](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR6d` corresponds to the *Fǎhuá bù* 法華部 of the Taishō structural ordering — the Lotus Sūtra and its satellite scriptures in Taishō volume 9, the Lotus sub-commentary tradition in Taishō volumes 26 and 33–34, the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal-and-meditation corpus in Taishō volume 46, the Lotus Dūnhuáng 敦煌 fragments in volume 85, and the very large Sòng–Qīng manuscript continuation of all these strands preserved in the *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏經. In Wilkinson's outline of the Taishō (§29.5.8), volume 9 is identified as "*Fǎhuá bù* (Lotus and other Mahāyāna sūtras)"; Kanripo's `KR6d` extends that vol. 9 nucleus outward to absorb all Chinese-language Lotus commentary and the entire Tiāntái scholastic apparatus that grows out of it, because in East-Asian classification the Tiāntái 天台 doctrinal tradition — including its meditation manuals, doctrinal-classification literature, and ritual / *chànyí* 懺儀 works — is canonically attached to the Lotus Sūtra rather than treated as an independent *zōng* 宗 section.

The principal scholarly tradition organising the division is therefore Tiāntái, whose founder Zhìyǐ 智顗 (538–597) was traditionally regarded as the patriarch and whose 593–597 lectures at Yùquánsì 玉泉寺, redacted by Guàndǐng 灌頂 (561–632), produced the *Tiāntái sāndàbù* 天台三大部 ("Three Great Treatises of Tiāntái") — *Fǎhuá xuányì* [KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006), *Fǎhuá wénjù* [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014), and *Móhē zhǐguān* [KR6d0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0130) — around which most of the division is structured (Wilkinson §29.5.7.1 on Tiāntái; Hurvitz 1963 on Zhìyǐ; Lopez 2016 and Teiser & Stone 2009 on the Lotus Sūtra). Pre-Tiāntái Liáng exegesis (Fǎyún 法雲), the early Suí Sānlùn 三論 reading by Jízàng 吉藏, and the Táng Faxiang 法相 / Cí'ēn 慈恩 reading by Kuījī 窺基 are also represented; from the 8th century onward the division is dominated by Zhànrán 湛然 (711–782) and his Sòng-period successors of the Tiāntái revival, and from the 11th century by the long *shānjiā* / *shānwài* 山家／山外 controversy and its literature. The division extends through Yuán, Míng (with the Tiāntái revival under Zhìxù 智旭 1599–1655), and Qīng (under Língyào 靈耀 and Tōnglǐ 通理) to roughly the mid-18th century.

### Important texts and text clusters

The 249 per-text notes in `kb/KR6d/` organise into five recognisable clusters.

#### The Lotus Sūtra itself and its parallel translations

- *Zhèng fǎhuá jīng* 正法華經 [KR6d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0002) — Dharmarakṣa's 竺法護 translation of 286 CE, the earliest complete Chinese Lotus, surviving in 10 *juan*.
- *Miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0001) — Kumārajīva's 鳩摩羅什 translation of 406 CE, the dominant East-Asian recension in 7 *juan* and 28 chapters; the literary base for virtually all subsequent Lotus exegesis in Chinese.
- *Tiānpǐn miàofǎ liánhuá jīng* 添品妙法蓮華經 [KR6d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0003) — the Suí (601) collation by Jñānagupta 闍那崛多 and Dharmagupta 笈多, incorporating the *Devadatta* chapter and the *Pǔmén pǐn* 普門品 verses.
- *Sàtán fēntuólì jīng* 薩曇分陀利經 [KR6d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0004) — a Western Jìn anonymous partial translation of the *Devadatta* episode, preserving a textual stratum independent of the three full versions.
