# 諸宗著述部 (X62)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 47 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6p 淨土宗著述部 *Jìngtǔ zōng zhùshù bù* — Buddhist Canon — Compositions of the Pure Land School](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/): 47 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6p 淨土宗著述部 *Jìngtǔ zōng zhùshù bù* — Buddhist Canon — Compositions of the Pure Land School](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6p collects the Chinese-language compositions of the Pure Land school (*jìngtǔ zōng* 淨土宗) — the body of doctrinal treatises, sūtra-commentaries, liturgical *zàn* / *chàn* / *yí* texts, devotional anthologies, biographies, and devotional poetry that grew up around the three principal Pure Land sūtras: the *Larger Sukhāvatī-vyūha* (*Wúliángshòu jīng* 無量壽經), the *Smaller Sukhāvatī-vyūha* (*Āmítuó jīng* 阿彌陀經), and the apocryphal *Contemplation Sūtra* (*Guān wúliángshòu jīng* 觀無量壽經). The 140 works gathered here are drawn from three regions of the Sino-Japanese canon: (i) the Taishō *Zhū-zōng bù* 諸宗部 (vol. 47, nos. 1957–1984) — the principal classical Pure Land treatises from Tánluán through Sòng-period Tiantai; (ii) the supplementary *Xùzàngjīng* 卍續藏 (vols. 1, 2, 22, 61, 62, 74) — the great bulk of Sòng–Qīng commentaries, ritual handbooks, and lay-Buddhist anthologies that the early-twentieth-century Japanese editors recovered from Chinese monastic libraries; and (iii) the Taishō *Gǔyì bù* 古逸部 (vol. 85, nos. 2826–2830), preserving Dunhuang-recovered Pure Land liturgies. The corresponding Taishō structural division — `div31.xml` 諸宗部 — is the formal canonical container, but the Kanripo arrangement extracts the Pure Land subset and supplements it heavily from the *Xùzàngjīng*.

Chronologically the division spans c. 530 CE (Tánluán 曇鸞's foundational tracts) through the very end of the Qīng (c. 1900). The internal centre of gravity is unusually late: roughly two-thirds of the entries date from the Míng-Qīng period, reflecting the fact that Pure Land devotion became the dominant lay-monastic practice of late imperial China and produced an immense vernacular literature absent from earlier canonical strata. Three transmissional issues run through the division: the inflation of the *Wúliángshòu* sūtra-corpus through apocryphal "translations" preserved only in the *Xùzàngjīng* (KR6p0031–0035); the Tiantai monopoly on the *Guān-jīng* commentarial tradition via the 觀經疏妙宗鈔 chain initiated by Zhīlǐ 知禮; and the steady migration of Pure Land authorship from the cloister to the lay literati class, culminating in the Péng Shàoshēng circle of the eighteenth century and Wèi Yuán's *Huìyì* recension of 1854.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **Wúliángshòu jīng 無量壽經 (Larger Sukhāvatī-vyūha) corpus** — *Wúliángshòu jīng huìyì* 無量壽經會譯 [KR6p0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0001) (Wèi Yuán 魏源, 1854), *Wúliángshòu jīng jì* 無量壽經記 [KR6p0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0002) (Xuányī 玄一, Táng), *Wúliángshòu jīng qǐxìn lùn* 無量壽經起信論 [KR6p0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0003) (Péng Jìqīng 彭際清, late 18th c.), and Wáng Gēngxīn 王耕心's *Móhē Āmítuó jīng zhōnglùn* 摩訶阿彌陀經衷論 [KR6p0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0004); together they constitute the most sustained East-Asian commentarial engagement with the *larger* Pure Land sūtra.
- **Guān wúliángshòu jīng 觀無量壽經 (Contemplation Sūtra) commentarial chain** — the apex is Zhìyǐ 智顗 (attr.) and Zhīlǐ 知禮's *Guān wúliángshòu fó jīng shū miàozōng chāo* 觀無量壽佛經疏妙宗鈔 [KR6p0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0007) (preface 1021), the canonical Tiantai reading of the sūtra, around which a dense Sòng-period sub-cluster forms — Zhīlǐ's own *Róngxīn jiě* 融心解 [KR6p0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0008), Jièdù 戒度's *Fúxīn lùn* 扶新論 [KR6p0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0009) and *Zhèngguān jì* 正觀記 [KR6p0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0010), Chuándēng 傳燈's *Túsòng* 圖頌 [KR6p0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0011), Xùfǎ 續法's *Zhízhǐ shū* 直指疏 [KR6p0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0012), and Péng Jìqīng's *Yuē lùn* 約論 [KR6p0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0013); the *Kē* 妙宗鈔科 [KR6p0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0006) supplies the structural outline. Earlier strata are Fǎcōng 法聰's *Jì* 釋觀無量壽佛經記 [KR6p0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0005) (Táng).
- **Āmítuó jīng 阿彌陀經 (Smaller Sukhāvatī-vyūha) commentaries** — Yuánzhào 元照 and Jièdù 戒度's *Yìshū wénchí jì* 阿彌陀經義疏聞持記 [KR6p0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0015) (Sòng); Xìngchéng 性澄's Yuán-period *Jùjiě* 句解 [KR6p0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0016); Dàyòu 大佑's *Lüèjiě* 略解 [KR6p0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0017) and its sub-commentary by Chuándēng [KR6p0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0018); the magnum opus of the division, Yúnqī Zhūhóng 雲棲袾宏's *Āmítuó jīng shūchāo* 阿彌陀經疏鈔 [KR6p0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0019) (1584) with its companion *Shìyì* 事義 [KR6p0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0020) and *Wènbiàn* 問辯 [KR6p0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0021) and the great sub-commentary *Yǎnyì* 演義 [KR6p0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0022) by Gǔdé fǎshī 古德法師; the matching Tiantai reading is Zhìxù 智旭's *Yàojiě* 要解 (preserved here only with Dámò 達默's *Biànméng chāo* 便蒙鈔 [KR6p0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0025)); plus the *Āmítuó jīng yìběn* 阿彌陀經異本 [KR6p0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0014) (a variant text), Xùfǎ's *Lüèzhù* 略註 [KR6p0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0026), and a handful of Qīng glosses ([KR6p0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0027)–[KR6p0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0030)).
- **Pure-Land apocrypha and pseudepigraphic dhāraṇī** — *Fó shuō wúliángshòu fó mínghào lìyì dàshì yīnyuán jīng* 佛說無量壽佛名號利益大事因緣經 attributed to Kāng Sēngkǎi 康僧鎧 [KR6p0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0031), *Guānshìyīn púsà wǎngshēng jìngtǔ běnyuán jīng* 觀世音菩薩往生淨土本緣經 [KR6p0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0032), *Niànfó chāotuō lúnhuí jiéjìng jīng* 念佛超脫輪迴捷徑經 [KR6p0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0033), *Shí wǎngshēng Āmítuó fó guó jīng* 十往生阿彌陀佛國經 [KR6p0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0034), and *Fó shuō Āmítuó fó gēnběn mìmì shénzhòu jīng* 佛說阿彌陀佛根本祕密神咒經 attributed to Bodhiruci 菩提流支 [KR6p0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0035). These are almost certainly Táng-Sòng Chinese compositions, transmitted only in the *Xùzàngjīng* supplement, and they are the principal evidence base for studying the textual inflation of the Pure Land sūtra-corpus in medieval China.
- **Tánluán–Dàochuò–Shàndǎo doctrinal foundation** — *Lüèlùn ānlè jìngtǔ yì* 略論安樂淨土義 [KR6p0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0036) and *Zàn Āmítuó fó jié* 讚阿彌陀佛偈 [KR6p0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0073) of Tánluán 曇鸞 (c. 530–542); *Ānlè jí* 安樂集 [KR6p0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0037) of Dàochuò 道綽 (c. 620–645); Shàndǎo 善導's *Guānniàn fǎmén* 觀念阿彌陀佛相海三昧功德法門 [KR6p0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0038) together with his liturgical trilogy *Fǎshì zàn* 法事讚 [KR6p0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0074), *Wǎngshēng lǐzàn jié* 往生禮讚偈 [KR6p0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0075), and *Bānzhōu sānmèi xíngdào wǎngshēng zàn* 般舟三昧行道往生讚 [KR6p0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0076). These six works constitute the Indian-Chinese doctrinal patrimony that all later Pure Land literature retransmits.
- **Sui-Táng monastic theology** — *Jìngtǔ shíyí lùn* 淨土十疑論 [KR6p0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0040) and *Wǔ fāngbiàn niànfó mén* 五方便念佛門 [KR6p0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0041) attributed to Zhìyǐ 智顗; Huáigǎn 懷感's *Shì jìngtǔ qúnyí lùn* 釋淨土群疑論 [KR6p0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0039) (Táng), the most substantial late-seventh-century systematic defence of Pure Land practice against Yogācāra critique; Jiācái 迦才's *Jìngtǔ lùn* 淨土論 [KR6p0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0042); Kuījī 窺基's *Xīfāng yàojué shìyí tōngguī* 西方要決釋疑通規 [KR6p0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0043); Wǒnhyo 元曉's Korean-Silla *Yóuxīn ānlè dào* 遊心安樂道 [KR6p0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0044); Dàojìng 道鏡 and Shàndào's *Niànfó jìng* 念佛鏡 [KR6p0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0045); and Fēixī 飛錫's *Niànfó sānmèi bǎowáng lùn* 念佛三昧寶王論 [KR6p0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0046).
- **Sòng-Tiantai systematization** — *Wǎngshēng jìngtǔ juéyí xíngyuàn èrmén* 往生淨土決疑行願二門 [KR6p0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0047) and *Wǎngshēng jìngtǔ chànyuàn yí* 往生淨土懺願儀 [KR6p0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0079) of Cíyún Zūnshì 慈雲遵式 (1000–1032); Zōngxiǎo 宗曉's two great anthologies *Lèbāng wénlèi* 樂邦文類 [KR6p0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0048) and *Lèbāng yígǎo* 樂邦遺稿 [KR6p0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0049) (1200–1214), the principal Sòng-period repositories of Pure Land prefaces, epigraphy, and hagiography; Chéngyù 澄彧's *Zhù shíyí lùn* 注十疑論 [KR6p0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0051); and Wáng Rìxiū 王日休's vastly influential lay manual *Lóngshū zēngguǎng jìngtǔ wén* 龍舒增廣淨土文 [KR6p0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0050) (c. 1160–1173).
- **Yuan-period synthesis** — Huáizé 懷則's *Jìngtǔ jìngguān yàomén* 淨土境觀要門 [KR6p0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0052); Tiānrú Wéizé 天如惟則's *Jìngtǔ huòwèn* 淨土或問 [KR6p0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0053) (c. 1350), the model dialectical defence of Pure Land against Chán objections; Pǔdù 普度's *Lúshān liánzōng bǎojiàn* 廬山蓮宗寶鑑 [KR6p0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0054) (c. 1300), the canonical history of the "Lotus society" lineage; the Yánshòu-attributed *Sānshí xìniàn* 三時繫念佛事 [KR6p0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0081) and *Yífàn* 儀範 [KR6p0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0082); and Wáng Zǐchéng 王子成's monumental *Lǐniàn Mítuó dàochǎng chànfǎ* 禮念彌陀道場懺法 [KR6p0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0084).
- **Late-Míng lay-monastic revival cluster** — Yúnqī Zhūhóng 雲棲袾宏's prolific oeuvre, including the *Shūchāo* (above), *Jìngtǔ yíbiàn* 淨土疑辨 [KR6p0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0058), *Dá sìshíbā wèn* 答四十八問 [KR6p0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0063), *Xīfāng yuànwén* 西方願文 [KR6p0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0064), and the encyclopaedic *Jìngtǔ zīliáng quánjí* 淨土資糧全集 [KR6p0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0065); Chuándēng 傳燈's Tiantai-school *Jìngtǔ shēng-wúshēng lùn* 淨土生無生論 [KR6p0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0056) with its commentaries [KR6p0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0070)/[KR6p0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0071); Yuán Hóngdào 袁宏道's Gōng'ān-school *Xīfāng hé lùn* 西方合論 [KR6p0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0057) (1599) and the Míng-Qīng commentary on it [KR6p0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0068); Lǐ Zhì 李贄's *Jìngtǔ jué* 淨土決 [KR6p0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0062); the *Jìngtǔ zhǐguī jí* 淨土指歸集 of Dàyòu 大佑 [KR6p0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0059); Dàoyǎn 道衍's *Jìngtǔ jiǎnyào lù* 淨土簡要錄 [KR6p0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0060); Zōngběn 宗本's *Guīyuán zhízhǐ jí* 歸元直指集 [KR6p0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0061); and the apex anthology of late-Míng / early-Qīng Pure Land, Chéngshí 成時's *Jìngtǔ shíyào* 淨土十要 [KR6p0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0067) (1655–1678).
- **Qīng lay-Buddhist Pure Land movement** — built around Péng Shàoshēng / Péng Jìqīng 彭紹升 / 彭際清 (1740–1796), who is here represented by no fewer than nine works: doctrinal treatises *Wúliángshòu jīng qǐxìn lùn* [KR6p0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0003), *Guān-jīng yuē lùn* [KR6p0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0013), *Āmítuó jīng yuē lùn* [KR6p0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0028); anthologies *Chóngdìng xīfāng gōngjù* 重訂西方公據 [KR6p0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0099) and *Niànfó jǐngcè* 念佛警策 [KR6p0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0100); the *Shěng'ān fǎshī yǔlù* 省菴法師語錄 [KR6p0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0098); and the poetic collections *Èrlín chànghé shī* 二林唱和詩 [KR6p0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0128), *Guānhé jí jiéchāo* 觀河集節鈔 [KR6p0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0129), *Cèhǎi jí jiéchāo* 測海集節鈔 [KR6p0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0130). Around Péng cluster Shíxián 實賢 (Xǐng'ān 省菴), Xíngcè 行策 (*Jìngtǔ jǐngyǔ* [KR6p0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0093), *Qǐyī xīn jīngjìn niànfó qīqī guīshì* [KR6p0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0094)), Chèwù 徹悟 (*Chèwù chánshī yǔlù* [KR6p0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0101)), Zhōu Mèngyán 周夢顏's *Xīguī zhízhǐ* 西歸直指 [KR6p0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0092), Sōng Shàndēng 沈善登's *Bàoēn lùn* 報恩論 [KR6p0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0124), and Wèi Yuán's *Huìyì*. The late-Qīng strand of Hangzhou-area devotional anthologies by Gǔkūn 古崑 ([KR6p0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0085), [KR6p0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0106), [KR6p0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0107), [KR6p0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0116), [KR6p0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0117)) forms the closing wave of the division.
- **Liturgical / praise (zàn 讚 / chàn 懺 / yí 儀) corpus** — beyond Shàndǎo's three liturgies and Zūnshì's *Chànyuàn yí* above: Tánluán's *Zàn Āmítuó fó jié* [KR6p0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0073); the Nāgārjuna *Shíèr lǐ* 十二禮 (tr. Jñānagupta 禪那崛多) [KR6p0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0080); Zhìshēng 智昇's *Jí zhū jīng lǐchàn yí* 集諸經禮懺儀 [KR6p0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0077); Fǎzhào 法照's *Jìngtǔ wǔhuì niànfó lüè fǎshì yízàn* 淨土五會念佛略法事儀讚 [KR6p0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0078) and *Wǔhuì niànfó sòngjīng guānxíng yí (juǎn zhōng, xià)* [KR6p0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0136); Yuánzhào and Jièdù's *Wúliángshòu fó zàn zhù* 無量壽佛讚註 [KR6p0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0083); and the Dunhuang stratum [KR6p0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0137)–[KR6p0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0140).
- **Dunhuang stratum (Taishō vol. 85)** — Huìrì 慧日's *Lüè zhū jīnglùn niànfó fǎmén wǎngshēng jìngtǔ jí (juǎn shàng)* 略諸經論念佛法門往生淨土集 [KR6p0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0135), the only surviving juǎn of Huìrì's three-juǎn defence of "*niànfó* by sūtra and treatise" composed before 748; Fǎzhào's *Wǔhuì* middle and lower fascicles [KR6p0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0136) (the upper juǎn survives independently as KR6p0078); and the anonymous *Dàshèng jìngtǔ zàn* 大乘淨土讚 [KR6p0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0137), *Chízhāi niànfó chànhuǐ lǐwén* 持齋念佛懺悔禮文 [KR6p0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0138), *Dào'ān fǎshī niànfó zàn* 道安法師念佛讚 [KR6p0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0139) / *zànwén* 道安法師念佛讚文 [KR6p0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0140) — the principal Northwest-Chinese witnesses to Pure-Land devotional practice independent of the central-Táng exegetical traditions.
- **Devotional poetry (jìngtǔ shī 淨土詩) cluster** — Guǎngguì 廣貴's *Liánbāng shīxuǎn* 蓮邦詩選 [KR6p0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0072) (late Míng); Péng Shàoshēng's *Èrlín chànghé shī* and the *Jiéchāo* pair (above); Táo Shàn 陶善's *Qiónglóu yíngǎo jiéchāo* 瓊樓吟稿節鈔 [KR6p0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0131); Děrǔn 德潤's *Pǔnéng Sōng chánshī jìngtǔ shī* 普能嵩禪師淨土詩 [KR6p0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0133); and Kuānliàng 寬量's *Jìngtǔ jiùshēngchuán shī* 淨土救生船詩 [KR6p0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0134) — a distinctive Qīng vernacular genre giving the division much of its mid-late character.

### Important persons

- [曇鸞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E9%B8%9E) (Tánluán, c. 476–542) — the earliest Chinese Pure Land author preserved in the canon; the *Lüèlùn ānlè jìngtǔ yì* [KR6p0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0036) and the *Zàn Āmítuó fó jié* [KR6p0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0073) are the foundational texts of the *zìlì / tālì* (self-power / other-power) distinction.
- [道綽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E7%B6%BD) (Dàochuò, 562–645) — second of the "three masters of Xuánzhōng-sì 玄中寺"; the *Ānlè jí* [KR6p0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0037) is the principal Sui-Táng systematization of *niànfó* doctrine.
- [善導](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%96%84%E5%B0%8E) (Shàndǎo, 613–681) — the central figure of classical Pure Land; four works in the division ([KR6p0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0038), [KR6p0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0074)–[KR6p0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0076)) establishing both doctrinal and liturgical practice.
- [智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) (Tiāntái Zhìyǐ, 538–597) — Sui Tiantai patriarch; *Jìngtǔ shíyí lùn* [KR6p0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0040) and *Wǔ fāngbiàn niànfó mén* [KR6p0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0041) traditionally attributed to him; the actual composition almost certainly Sòng-period under his name.
- [懷感](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E6%84%9F) (Huáigǎn, fl. 690–705) — Xuánzàng's disciple turned Pure-Land apologist; *Shì jìngtǔ qúnyí lùn* [KR6p0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0039) is the most rigorous early scholastic defence of Pure-Land practice within Yogācāra doctrine.
- [迦才](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%BF%A6%E6%89%8D) (Jiācái, fl. 645–670) — author of the early-Táng *Jìngtǔ lùn* [KR6p0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0042), an alternative scholastic systematization parallel to Dàochuò.
- [飛錫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A3%9B%E9%8C%AB) (Fēixī, fl. 742–779) — late-Táng author of *Niànfó sānmèi bǎowáng lùn* [KR6p0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0046), a key statement of the universal-scope reading of *niànfó*.
- [元曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E6%9B%89) (Wǒnhyo, 617–686) — Silla scholar; the *Yóuxīn ānlè dào* [KR6p0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0044) is the Korean voice in the Táng Pure Land canon.
- [慧日](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%97%A5) (Címǐn Huìrì, 680–748) — author of the Dunhuang *Lüè zhū jīnglùn niànfó fǎmén* [KR6p0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0135); an opponent of Chán quietism who insisted on textual-scholastic foundations for Pure Land.
- [法照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E7%85%A7) (Fǎzhào, c. 745–805) — Wǔtáishān-based liturgist; creator of the *wǔhuì niànfó* 五會念佛 chanting system represented by KR6p0078 and KR6p0136.
- [知禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E7%A6%AE) (Sìmíng Zhīlǐ, 960–1028) — the architect of Sòng-Tiantai Pure-Land thought; the *Miàozōng chāo* [KR6p0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0007), *Róngxīn jiě* [KR6p0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0008), and *Kē* [KR6p0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0006) together define the Tiantai reading of the *Guān-jīng* down to the present.
- [遵式](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%B5%E5%BC%8F) (Cíyún Zūnshì, 964–1032) — Zhīlǐ's contemporary; the *Juéyí xíngyuàn èrmén* [KR6p0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0047) and *Chànyuàn yí* [KR6p0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0079) codified Pure Land ritual for the Hángzhōu-area Tiantai network.
- [元照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E7%85%A7) (Língzhī Yuánzhào, 1048–1116) — Vinaya master who turned to Pure Land; *Āmítuó jīng yìshū* and *Wúliángshòu fó zàn zhù* together with the Jièdù sub-commentaries form a distinct Sòng-Vinaya reading of Pure Land texts.
- [戒度](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%92%E5%BA%A6) (Jièdù, fl. 1180–1240) — Yuánzhào's principal commentator; three works in the division ([KR6p0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0009), [KR6p0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0010), [KR6p0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0015)).
- [宗曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E6%9B%89) (Zōngxiǎo, 1151–1214) — Sòng-period anthologist whose *Lèbāng wénlèi* / *Lèbāng yígǎo* preserve the bulk of the Sòng prefatory and hagiographic corpus.
- [王日休](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%97%A5%E4%BC%91) (Wáng Rìxiū, d. 1173) — Sòng lay literatus; the *Lóngshū jìngtǔ wén* [KR6p0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0050) is the most widely circulated lay Pure-Land manual in pre-modern China.
- [懷則](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%B7%E5%89%87) (Huáizé, fl. 1290–1340) and [天如則](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E5%A6%82%E5%89%87) (Tiānrú Wéizé, c. 1286–1354) — Yuán Tiantai authors of, respectively, the *Jìngguān yàomén* and the *Jìngtǔ huòwèn*.
- [普度](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E5%BA%A6) (Yōután Pǔdù, d. 1330) — Yuán reformer of the White Lotus society; the *Lúshān liánzōng bǎojiàn* [KR6p0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0054) is the canonical lineage-history of the "Lotus society" tradition.
- [袾宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%BE%E5%AE%8F) (Yúnqī Zhūhóng, 1535–1615) — late-Míng master at Yúnqī-sì 雲棲寺; the dominant authorial presence in the division (eight works including the *Āmítuó jīng shūchāo*) and the architect of late-Míng Pure Land revival.
- [傳燈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%82%B3%E7%87%88) (Yōuxī Chuándēng, 1554–1627) — Míng Tiantai exegete; commentator on both the *Guān-jīng* and the *Āmítuó jīng* tradition, author of the *Jìngtǔ shēng-wúshēng lùn*.
- [大佑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A7%E4%BD%91) (Dàyòu, 1334–1407) — Yuán-Míng compiler bridging the two dynasties; three works in the division.
- [袁宏道](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%81%E5%AE%8F%E9%81%93) (Yuán Hóngdào, 1568–1610) — Gōng'ān-school literatus; *Xīfāng hé lùn* [KR6p0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0057) is the principal late-Míng literati statement of Pure Land doctrine.
- [李贄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E8%B4%84) (Lǐ Zhì, 1527–1602) — heterodox Míng literatus; *Jìngtǔ jué* [KR6p0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0062) places him in the Pure Land tradition.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) (Ǒuyì Zhìxù, 1599–1655) — last of the "four great Míng masters"; his *Āmítuó jīng yàojiě* (transmitted here in [KR6p0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0025)) is the standard Tiantai reading of the smaller sūtra.
- [成時](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%90%E6%99%82) (Chéngshí, 1618–1678) — Zhìxù's disciple; compiler of the *Jìngtǔ shíyào* [KR6p0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0067), the canonical late-Míng / early-Qīng Pure-Land anthology.
- [彭際清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E9%9A%9B%E6%B8%85) (Péng Shàoshēng / Jìqīng, 1740–1796) — leading Qīng lay-Buddhist scholar; nine works represent his doctrinal, anthological, and poetic output and define eighteenth-century lay Pure Land literature.
- [實賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E8%B3%A2) (Xǐng'ān Shíxián, 1686–1734) — Qīng patriarch of the Pure Land lineage; subject of [KR6p0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0098) and annotator of [KR6p0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0087) and [KR6p0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0097).
- [行策](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A1%8C%E7%AD%96) (Jiéliú Xíngcè, 1628–1682) — *Jìngtǔ jǐngyǔ* [KR6p0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0093) and *Niànfó qīqī guīshì* [KR6p0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0094); founder of the *fó-qī* 佛七 seven-day intensive *niànfó* retreat as a standardized form.
- [古崑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%A4%E5%B4%91) (Gǔkūn, fl. 1860–1890) — late-Qīng Hangzhou-area anthologist; five works form the closing wave of the division.
- [魏源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E6%BA%90) (Wèi Yuán, 1794–1857) — late-Qīng statecraft scholar; the *Wúliángshòu jīng huìyì* [KR6p0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0001) is the first sustained Chinese attempt at a synthetic conflated recension of the larger sūtra.
- [沈善登](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E5%96%84%E7%99%BB) (Shěn Shàndēng, 1830–1902) — *Bàoēn lùn* [KR6p0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0124); a late-Qīng intellectual systematization of Pure Land in dialogue with mid-nineteenth-century reformist Confucianism.

### Topics

- **The five Chinese versions of the *Wúliángshòu jīng* and the problem of a unified Larger Pure Land Sūtra** — running from the medieval translator-attributions through Yúnqī Zhūhóng's preference for the smaller sūtra to Wèi Yuán's nineteenth-century *huìyì* solution and Xià Liánjū's twentieth-century continuation; the principal philological problem of the division.
- **The status of the *Guān wúliángshòu jīng* as a Central-Asian / Chinese composition** — debate, beginning with Mochizuki Shinkō's mid-twentieth-century work and continuing into Fujita Kōtatsu and Stevenson's studies, over whether the sūtra is an Indian translation or a Sino-Central-Asian composition; the entire commentarial chain [KR6p0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0005)–[KR6p0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0013) presupposes it as canonical.
- **The Tiantai monopolization of *Guān-jīng* exegesis** — how Zhīlǐ's *Miàozōng chāo* established a doctrinal grid (*xìng-shàn xìng-è* 性善性惡, *yīniàn sānqiān* 一念三千) on top of the sūtra's contemplative scheme, and how this Tiantai reading survived as the only living *Guān-jīng* commentarial tradition through the Sòng, Yuán, and Míng periods.
- **The *niànfó sānmèi* debate** — whether *niànfó* is a propaedeutic ritual practice, a meditative *samādhi*, or an actualization of *zìxìng Mítuó wéixīn jìngtǔ* 自性彌陀唯心淨土 (the Amitābha-of-one's-own-nature, the Pure Land of mind-only); a debate that runs from Fēixī's *Bǎowáng lùn* [KR6p0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0046) through Yánshòu and Yuán Hóngdào to the late-Míng "*chán-jìng yī-zhì* 禪淨一致" (Chán–Pure-Land synthesis) of Yúnqī and Zhìxù.
- **Chán–Pure-Land synthesis (chán-jìng shuāngxiū 禪淨雙修)** — the Sòng-Míng-Qīng convergence of Chán practice and Pure Land devotion, most clearly thematized in Tiānrú Wéizé's *Huòwèn* [KR6p0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0053), Yuán Hóngdào's *Hé lùn* [KR6p0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0057), Jīhúng 濟能's *Jiǎohǔ jí* 角虎集 [KR6p0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0096), and Chèwù's *Yǔlù* [KR6p0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0101); defined the dominant late-imperial monastic style.
- **Pure Land hagiography and the "Lotus society" lineage** — the construction of an unbroken lineage from Lúshān Huìyuǎn 廬山慧遠's 4th-c. society through the Táng masters to the present, codified by Pǔdù's *Liánzōng bǎojiàn* [KR6p0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0054) and Zōngxiǎo's anthologies, and disseminated as the model of Pure Land religious community.
- **The migration of authorship from cloister to lay literati** — most visible in the eighteenth-century Péng Shàoshēng circle (his nine works represent the apex), but already prepared in the Sòng with Wáng Rìxiū, in the Míng with Yuán Hóngdào and Lǐ Zhì, and continuing into the late-Qīng with Wèi Yuán, Shěn Shàndēng, and Wáng Gēngxīn.
- **Pure Land devotional poetry as canonical literature** — the unusual fact, distinctive to this division within the Kanripo Buddhist canon, that *jìngtǔ shī* 淨土詩 collections are treated as canonical religious texts and admitted to the *Xùzàngjīng*; a Qīng phenomenon documented in [KR6p0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0072), [KR6p0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0128)–[KR6p0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0134).
- **The *fó-qī* 佛七 (seven-day intensive *niànfó*) and Pure Land monastic regulation** — the standardization of ritual recitation regimes traceable from Zhìshēng's *Lǐchàn yí* [KR6p0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0077) and Fǎzhào's *Wǔhuì* [KR6p0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0078) through Xíngcè's *Qīqī guīshì* [KR6p0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0094) to nineteenth-century Hangzhou practice in Gǔkūn's manuals; the operational practice underlying the doctrinal literature.
- **The Dunhuang independent witness** — the *Gǔyì bù* texts [KR6p0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0135)–[KR6p0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6p/KR6p0140) preserve a Pure-Land devotional tradition (Címǐn Huìrì, Fǎzhào, anonymous liturgies) at least partly independent of the Chang'an-Luòyáng centres, and their survival only at Dunhuang shows how much medieval Chinese Pure Land literature has been lost in central transmission.

# 諸宗著述部 (X63)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

This volume holds 39 texts. In the Ask Bunkankun catalog, which follows CBETA's subject classes rather than Taishō/Zokuzōkyō volumes, they belong to:

- [KR6q 禪宗著述部 *Chánzōng zhùshù bù* — Buddhist Canon — Compositions of the Chán School](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/): 39 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6q 禪宗著述部 *Chánzōng zhùshù bù* — Buddhist Canon — Compositions of the Chán School](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6q gathers the writings of the Chán school 禪宗 as preserved across three textual reservoirs: the *Shǐchuán bù* 史傳部 and *Zhū-zōng bù* 諸宗部 of the Taishō canon (T47, T48, T51), the Xuzangjing 卍續藏 Chán *yǔlù* run (X64–X88), and the Jiāxīng Canon 嘉興藏 *yǔlù* expansion (J20–J40 and the Wàihán *bùyí* 補遺). The division therefore spans the full literary output of an indigenous Chinese Buddhist tradition: transmission-of-the-lamp histories (*dēnglù* 燈錄) and their *xù-* / *guǎng-* / *liánxù-* / *zēngjí-* derivatives; the recorded sayings (*yǔlù* 語錄) of individual masters; the kōan / "old-cases" literature (*gōng'àn* 公案, *sòng gǔ* 頌古, *niāngǔ* 拈古, *píngchàng* 評唱) and its commentarial superstructure; Buddhist biographical jewelry (*sēngbǎo zhuàn* 僧寶傳); Chán monastic codes (*qīngguī* 清規); the admonitory-pastoral genre (*jǐng cè* 警策, *bǎoxùn* 寶訓); doctrinal compendia and sectarian polemics on the *wǔ jiā qī zōng* 五家七宗 lineages; verse cycles (notably the *shíniú tú sòng* 十牛圖頌 and the *Yǒngjiā Zhèngdào gē* 永嘉證道歌); and the literary collected works (*biéjí* 別集) of Chán masters. The 609 entries make KR6q the single largest Chán-literature corpus assembled anywhere in modern catalogs and the densest documentation of any East-Asian Buddhist school.

Chronologically the corpus stretches from the conventionally-dated 6th-century *Sì xíng guān* 四行觀 attributed to Bodhidharma (KR6q0112) through to the early-19th-century *Zhèngyuán lüèjí* 正源略集 of Jìchéng 際澄 (KR6q0031–0033, 1820–1828). Quantitatively, however, the division is overwhelmingly weighted toward the 17th century: roughly 335 of the 609 entries — about 55% — are 17th-century Jiāxīng-Canon *yǔlù* of late-Míng and early-Qīng Chán abbots, reflecting both the print boom of the Wàn-Lì 萬曆 reform and the Línjì-school 臨濟宗 revival under Mìyún Yuánwù 密雲圓悟 and his dharma-heirs. For Taishō structural context the relevant CANWWW divisions are `div21.xml` (史傳部, hosting the foundational *dēnglù* set) and the Chán portion of `div23.xml` / `div24.xml` (諸宗部 Chán entries). Modern critical reference for the *dēnglù* tradition runs through Yanagida Seizan 柳田聖山, T. Griffith Foulk, Albert Welter, and Morten Schlütter; for the late-Míng / Qīng *yǔlù* explosion, through Jiang Wu 吳疆, Beata Grant, and Hasebe Yūkei 長谷部幽蹊.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The foundational *dēnglù* sequence ("Five Lamps" 五燈 and after).** This is the structural backbone of the division and the principal narrative source for Chinese Chán self-history.

- *Zǔtáng jí* 祖堂集 [KR6q0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0002) — the 952 Quánzhōu 泉州 compilation, the earliest extant true lamp record; lost in China and recovered via Korean transmission.
- *Jǐngdé chuándēng lù* 景德傳燈錄 [KR6q0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0003) — Dàoyuán's 1004–1011 work, the imperially-presented Sòng prototype that gave the genre its canonical shape.
- *Tiānshèng guǎngdēng lù* 天聖廣燈錄 [KR6q0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0004) — Lǐ Zūnxù's 1029–1036 expansion, the first lay-compiled lamp record.
- *Jiànzhōng jìngguó xùdēng lù* 建中靖國續燈錄 [KR6q0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0007) — Wéibái's 1101 continuation.
- *Liándēng huìyào* 聯燈會要 [KR6q0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0008) — Wùmíng's 1183 harmonization of the previous three.
- *Jiātài pǔdēng lù* 嘉泰普燈錄 [KR6q0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0010) — Zhèngshòu's 1204 broadening to laity and women.
- *Wǔdēng huìyuán* 五燈會元 [KR6q0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0012) — Pǔjì's 1252 *editio definitiva* synthesizing the five preceding lamp records into a single 20-juan corpus; the most influential single text of the genre.
- *Xù chuándēng lù* 續傳燈錄 [KR6q0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0016) — the early-Míng (1401–1402) Yǒnglè-era imperial continuation.
- *Wǔdēng yántǒng* 五燈嚴統 [KR6q0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0019) / *Jiěhuò biān* [KR6q0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0020) — Fèiyǐn Tōngróng's 1653–1654 partisan Línjì rewrite and its self-defence, the most notorious sectarian intervention in the *dēnglù* tradition.
- *Wǔdēng quánshū* 五燈全書 [KR6q0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0022) — Jièlín Chāoyǒng's 120-juan Kāngxī-era (1697) compendium.
- *Zhǐyuè lù* 指月錄 [KR6q0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0023) — Qú Rǔjī's lay-compiled 1602 anthology.

**Kōan / old-cases tradition.** The *gōng'àn* literary tradition reframes encounter-dialogue narratives from the *dēnglù* as objects of literary commentary.

- *Bìyán lù* 碧巖錄 [KR6q0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0078) — Yuánwù Kèqín's *píngchàng* commentary (c. 1128) on Xuědòu Chóngxiǎn's 雪竇重顯 100 *sòng-gǔ* verses; the *locus classicus* of *wénzì chán* 文字禪.
- *Cóngróng ān lù* 從容庵錄 [KR6q0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0079) — Wànsōng Xíngxiù's 1223 commentary on Hóngzhì Zhèngjué's 宏智正覺 100 verses; Cáodòng counterpart to the *Bìyán lù*.
- *Wúmén guān* 無門關 [KR6q0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0080) — Wúmén Huìkāi's 1228 collection of 48 cases, the most internationally diffused kōan compendium.
- *Fóguǒ jījié lù* 佛果擊節錄 [KR6q0249](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0249), the Línquán 林泉 commentaries [KR6q0251](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0251) [KR6q0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0252), and the Tiānqí 天奇 directing commentaries [KR6q0250](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0250) [KR6q0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0253) continue the genre through the Yuán and Míng.

### Topics

- **The *dēnglù* and the construction of patriarchal lineage.** The *dēnglù* genre invented and then iteratively re-edited the canonical lineage chart of Chinese Chán: the *Xī tiān èr-shí-bā zǔ* 西天二十八祖 + *Dōng-tǔ liù zǔ* 東土六祖 + *wǔ jiā qī zōng* 五家七宗 schema. Every text in [KR6q0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0001)–[KR6q0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0039) is a re-articulation of this charter narrative, with sectarian rewrites (e.g. [KR6q0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0019) *Wǔdēng yántǒng*) using the genre to *redistribute* dharma-heir assignments between Cáodòng and Línjì.
- **Encounter-dialogue (*jīyuán wèndá* 機緣問答) as literary form.** The *yǔlù* and *dēnglù* together generate the encounter-dialogue paradigm — short, edited dialogues between master and disciple structured around live language, demotic speech, paradox, and physical action — which becomes the master genre of Chinese Buddhist literature and the proximate source-material for the kōan tradition.
- **The *gōng'àn* and *wénzì chán* / *kàn huà* / *mòzhào* debate.** The Sòng kōan tradition splits along three axes: literary commentary on edited cases (*Bìyán lù*, *Cóngróng lù*), *kàn huàtóu* introspection on a single critical phrase (Dàhuì Zōnggǎo, [KR6q0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0060)–[KR6q0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0063)), and *mòzhào chán* silent-illumination practice (Hóngzhì Zhèngjué, [KR6q0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0070) and Tiāntóng Rújìng, [KR6q0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0072)). The Sòng controversy between Dàhuì and Hóngzhì is the principal doctrinal debate documented in the division.
- **The *wǔ jiā qī zōng* doctrinal classification.** The *wǔ jiā* — Guī-yǎng 溈仰, Línjì, Cáodòng, Yúnmén, Fǎyǎn — and the *qī zōng* extension with the two Línjì sub-houses (Huánglóng 黃龍 and Yángqí 楊岐) provide the categorical grid against which every *dēnglù* and *zōngmén* compendium ([KR6q0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0081), [KR6q0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0005), [KR6q0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0167)–[KR6q0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0169)) organizes its material.
- **Sòng-Chán syncretism with Huáyán-Tiāntái doctrine and the *jiào-chán yī-zhì* 教禪一致 program.** Anchored by Zōngmì's *Chányuán zhū quán jí dūxù* [KR6q0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0091) and developed at scale in Yǒngmíng Yánshòu's *Zōngjìng lù* [KR6q0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0092), this syncretic stream argues against Chán-school anti-textualism and re-grounds the *patriarchal vehicle* in canonical doctrine.
- **Pure Land convergence (*chán-jìng shuāng-xiū* 禪淨雙修).** From Yánshòu onward, and intensified in the late-Míng synthesis of Zhūhóng, Hānshān, and Ǒuyì, the division documents the long convergence between Chán and Pure Land practice — visible in the *Wànshàn tóngguī jí* [KR6q0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0093), the *Wéixīn jué* [KR6q0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0094), and across the Zhūhóng / Hānshān / Ǒuyì corpora.
- **Late-Míng / Qīng lineage disputes and the print boom.** The mid-17th-century controversy between the Línjì-Mìyún descendants and the Cáodòng line is the most concentrated polemical episode in Chinese Buddhist history: [KR6q0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0018)–[KR6q0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0020), [KR6q0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0167)–[KR6q0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0169), and the *Zhèngyuán lüèjí* tradition [KR6q0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0031)–[KR6q0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0033) all participate. The Jiāxīng-Canon 嘉興藏 print enterprise (1589–c. 1712) is the medium through which the resulting *yǔlù* explosion reaches the canon.
- **Chán monastic codes and the institutional history of the school.** [KR6q0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0102), [KR6q0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0136), and the *qīngguī* continuations [KR6q0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0139)–[KR6q0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0142) track the institutional discipline of the Chán monastery from Sòng through Qīng — the basis for any historical reconstruction of *cónglín* 叢林 life.
- **Lay Buddhism and women practitioners.** The lamp records open progressively to lay and female practitioners across the 13th–17th centuries: *Jūshì fēndēng lù* 居士分燈錄 [KR6q0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0039) (lay), *Yōupóyí zhì* [KR6q0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0051) (laywomen), [KR6q0273](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0273) *Páng jūshì yǔlù* (the iconic Páng Yùn 龐蘊 family), and *yǔlù* of Buddhist nuns scattered in the late-Míng / Qīng Jiāxīng-Canon range.
- **Transmission to Korea and Japan.** The division preserves: the Koryŏ-Sŏn corpus of Chinul [KR6q0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0095)–[KR6q0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0097) and the Chosŏn corpus of Sŏsan Hyujŏng [KR6q0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0146); the *Zǔtáng jí* itself, transmitted through Korea; Japanese Edo-period re-editions of the Cáodòng founders [KR6q0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0066)–[KR6q0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0069); and Dōgen's 道元 *Zuòchán zhēn* 坐禪箴 [KR6q0241](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0241) in its Sino-Japanese textual form.
- **Chán authors writing on the Three Teachings.** The division also collects works by Chán authors on non-Buddhist canonical texts — most prominently Ǒuyì's *Zhōuyì chánjiě* 周易禪解 [KR6q0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0184), *Qī yuán zhǐtōng* (Zhuāngzǐ) [KR6q0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0219), and *Dàodé jīng shùn zhū* [KR6q0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0227) — a witness to the late-Míng *sān jiào* 三教 conversation as conducted from inside the *cónglín*.

# 諸宗著述部 (X64)

## Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君 divisions

- [KR6q 禪宗著述部 *Chánzōng zhùshù bù* — Buddhist Canon — Compositions of the Chán School](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/): 12 texts (100%)

## Division note: [KR6q 禪宗著述部 *Chánzōng zhùshù bù* — Buddhist Canon — Compositions of the Chán School](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6q gathers the writings of the Chán school 禪宗 as preserved across three textual reservoirs: the *Shǐchuán bù* 史傳部 and *Zhū-zōng bù* 諸宗部 of the Taishō canon (T47, T48, T51), the Xuzangjing 卍續藏 Chán *yǔlù* run (X64–X88), and the Jiāxīng Canon 嘉興藏 *yǔlù* expansion (J20–J40 and the Wàihán *bùyí* 補遺). The division therefore spans the full literary output of an indigenous Chinese Buddhist tradition: transmission-of-the-lamp histories (*dēnglù* 燈錄) and their *xù-* / *guǎng-* / *liánxù-* / *zēngjí-* derivatives; the recorded sayings (*yǔlù* 語錄) of individual masters; the kōan / "old-cases" literature (*gōng'àn* 公案, *sòng gǔ* 頌古, *niāngǔ* 拈古, *píngchàng* 評唱) and its commentarial superstructure; Buddhist biographical jewelry (*sēngbǎo zhuàn* 僧寶傳); Chán monastic codes (*qīngguī* 清規); the admonitory-pastoral genre (*jǐng cè* 警策, *bǎoxùn* 寶訓); doctrinal compendia and sectarian polemics on the *wǔ jiā qī zōng* 五家七宗 lineages; verse cycles (notably the *shíniú tú sòng* 十牛圖頌 and the *Yǒngjiā Zhèngdào gē* 永嘉證道歌); and the literary collected works (*biéjí* 別集) of Chán masters. The 609 entries make KR6q the single largest Chán-literature corpus assembled anywhere in modern catalogs and the densest documentation of any East-Asian Buddhist school.

Chronologically the corpus stretches from the conventionally-dated 6th-century *Sì xíng guān* 四行觀 attributed to Bodhidharma (KR6q0112) through to the early-19th-century *Zhèngyuán lüèjí* 正源略集 of Jìchéng 際澄 (KR6q0031–0033, 1820–1828). Quantitatively, however, the division is overwhelmingly weighted toward the 17th century: roughly 335 of the 609 entries — about 55% — are 17th-century Jiāxīng-Canon *yǔlù* of late-Míng and early-Qīng Chán abbots, reflecting both the print boom of the Wàn-Lì 萬曆 reform and the Línjì-school 臨濟宗 revival under Mìyún Yuánwù 密雲圓悟 and his dharma-heirs. For Taishō structural context the relevant CANWWW divisions are `div21.xml` (史傳部, hosting the foundational *dēnglù* set) and the Chán portion of `div23.xml` / `div24.xml` (諸宗部 Chán entries). Modern critical reference for the *dēnglù* tradition runs through Yanagida Seizan 柳田聖山, T. Griffith Foulk, Albert Welter, and Morten Schlütter; for the late-Míng / Qīng *yǔlù* explosion, through Jiang Wu 吳疆, Beata Grant, and Hasebe Yūkei 長谷部幽蹊.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The foundational *dēnglù* sequence ("Five Lamps" 五燈 and after).** This is the structural backbone of the division and the principal narrative source for Chinese Chán self-history.

- *Zǔtáng jí* 祖堂集 [KR6q0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0002) — the 952 Quánzhōu 泉州 compilation, the earliest extant true lamp record; lost in China and recovered via Korean transmission.
- *Jǐngdé chuándēng lù* 景德傳燈錄 [KR6q0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0003) — Dàoyuán's 1004–1011 work, the imperially-presented Sòng prototype that gave the genre its canonical shape.
- *Tiānshèng guǎngdēng lù* 天聖廣燈錄 [KR6q0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0004) — Lǐ Zūnxù's 1029–1036 expansion, the first lay-compiled lamp record.
- *Jiànzhōng jìngguó xùdēng lù* 建中靖國續燈錄 [KR6q0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0007) — Wéibái's 1101 continuation.
- *Liándēng huìyào* 聯燈會要 [KR6q0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0008) — Wùmíng's 1183 harmonization of the previous three.
- *Jiātài pǔdēng lù* 嘉泰普燈錄 [KR6q0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0010) — Zhèngshòu's 1204 broadening to laity and women.
- *Wǔdēng huìyuán* 五燈會元 [KR6q0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0012) — Pǔjì's 1252 *editio definitiva* synthesizing the five preceding lamp records into a single 20-juan corpus; the most influential single text of the genre.
- *Xù chuándēng lù* 續傳燈錄 [KR6q0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0016) — the early-Míng (1401–1402) Yǒnglè-era imperial continuation.
- *Wǔdēng yántǒng* 五燈嚴統 [KR6q0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0019) / *Jiěhuò biān* [KR6q0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0020) — Fèiyǐn Tōngróng's 1653–1654 partisan Línjì rewrite and its self-defence, the most notorious sectarian intervention in the *dēnglù* tradition.
- *Wǔdēng quánshū* 五燈全書 [KR6q0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0022) — Jièlín Chāoyǒng's 120-juan Kāngxī-era (1697) compendium.
- *Zhǐyuè lù* 指月錄 [KR6q0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0023) — Qú Rǔjī's lay-compiled 1602 anthology.

**Kōan / old-cases tradition.** The *gōng'àn* literary tradition reframes encounter-dialogue narratives from the *dēnglù* as objects of literary commentary.

- *Bìyán lù* 碧巖錄 [KR6q0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0078) — Yuánwù Kèqín's *píngchàng* commentary (c. 1128) on Xuědòu Chóngxiǎn's 雪竇重顯 100 *sòng-gǔ* verses; the *locus classicus* of *wénzì chán* 文字禪.
- *Cóngróng ān lù* 從容庵錄 [KR6q0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0079) — Wànsōng Xíngxiù's 1223 commentary on Hóngzhì Zhèngjué's 宏智正覺 100 verses; Cáodòng counterpart to the *Bìyán lù*.
- *Wúmén guān* 無門關 [KR6q0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0080) — Wúmén Huìkāi's 1228 collection of 48 cases, the most internationally diffused kōan compendium.
- *Fóguǒ jījié lù* 佛果擊節錄 [KR6q0249](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0249), the Línquán 林泉 commentaries [KR6q0251](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0251) [KR6q0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0252), and the Tiānqí 天奇 directing commentaries [KR6q0250](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0250) [KR6q0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0253) continue the genre through the Yuán and Míng.

**Early Chán and the *Liù zǔ* 六祖 corpus.** A tight cluster of works either attributed to or recovered from the early Tang Chán milieu, much of it Dūnhuáng-attested.

- The two recensions of the *Liùzǔ tánjīng* 六祖壇經 (Dūnhuáng [KR6q0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0082); the standard Yuán recension [KR6q0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0083)).
- *Shǎoshì liù mén* 少室六門 [KR6q0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0084) and the four short Bodhidharma treatises (*Xuèmài lùn*, *Wùxìng lùn*, *Pòxiàng lùn*, *Sì xíng guān*) at [KR6q0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0112)–[KR6q0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0115).
- *Xìnxīn míng* 信心銘 attributed to Sēngcàn 僧璨 [KR6q0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0085).
- *Zuìshàng shèng lùn* 最上乘論 attributed to Hóngrěn 弘忍 [KR6q0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0086).
- *Léngqié shīzī jì* 楞伽師資記 [KR6q0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0109) and *Chuán fǎ bǎo jì* 傳法寶記 [KR6q0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0110) — the principal Northern-school lineage records, recovered from Dūnhuáng.
- The Huángbò Xīyùn 黃檗希運 corpus recorded by Péi Xiū 裴休: *Chuánxīn fǎyào* [KR6q0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0087) and *Wǎnlíng lù* [KR6q0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0088).
- *Dùnwù rùdào yàomén lùn* 頓悟入道要門論 [KR6q0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0117) by Dàzhū Huìhǎi 大珠慧海.
- *Yǒngjiā jí* [KR6q0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0089) and *Yǒngjiā Zhèngdào gē* [KR6q0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0090).
- *Chányuán zhū quán jí dūxù* 禪源諸詮集都序 [KR6q0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0091) — Guīfēng Zōngmì's 圭峰宗密 doctrinal classification of Chán.

**Sòng-Chán masters' *yǔlù* — the "core canon".** The classical *yǔlù* of the five-house founders and the major Sòng Línjì / Cáodòng lines.

- *Sì jiā yǔlù* 四家語錄 [KR6q0266](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0266)–[KR6q0269](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0269) — the canonical Mǎ-zǔ 馬祖, Bǎizhàng 百丈, Huángbò, Línjì set.

**Doctrinal compendia and sectarian polemics.** The *zōngmén* 宗門 literature in which the Chán school theorized its own lineage and doctrinal claims.

- *Zōngjìng lù* 宗鏡錄 [KR6q0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0092) — Yǒngmíng Yánshòu's 永明延壽 100-juan synthesis of Chán with Huáyán-Tiāntái doctrine (c. 961); the most ambitious doctrinal compendium in the division. Companion works at [KR6q0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0093) *Wànshàn tóngguī jí* and [KR6q0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0094) *Wéixīn jué*.

### Topics

- **The *dēnglù* and the construction of patriarchal lineage.** The *dēnglù* genre invented and then iteratively re-edited the canonical lineage chart of Chinese Chán: the *Xī tiān èr-shí-bā zǔ* 西天二十八祖 + *Dōng-tǔ liù zǔ* 東土六祖 + *wǔ jiā qī zōng* 五家七宗 schema. Every text in [KR6q0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0001)–[KR6q0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0039) is a re-articulation of this charter narrative, with sectarian rewrites (e.g. [KR6q0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0019) *Wǔdēng yántǒng*) using the genre to *redistribute* dharma-heir assignments between Cáodòng and Línjì.
- **Encounter-dialogue (*jīyuán wèndá* 機緣問答) as literary form.** The *yǔlù* and *dēnglù* together generate the encounter-dialogue paradigm — short, edited dialogues between master and disciple structured around live language, demotic speech, paradox, and physical action — which becomes the master genre of Chinese Buddhist literature and the proximate source-material for the kōan tradition.
- **The *gōng'àn* and *wénzì chán* / *kàn huà* / *mòzhào* debate.** The Sòng kōan tradition splits along three axes: literary commentary on edited cases (*Bìyán lù*, *Cóngróng lù*), *kàn huàtóu* introspection on a single critical phrase (Dàhuì Zōnggǎo, [KR6q0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0060)–[KR6q0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0063)), and *mòzhào chán* silent-illumination practice (Hóngzhì Zhèngjué, [KR6q0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0070) and Tiāntóng Rújìng, [KR6q0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0072)). The Sòng controversy between Dàhuì and Hóngzhì is the principal doctrinal debate documented in the division.
- **The *wǔ jiā qī zōng* doctrinal classification.** The *wǔ jiā* — Guī-yǎng 溈仰, Línjì, Cáodòng, Yúnmén, Fǎyǎn — and the *qī zōng* extension with the two Línjì sub-houses (Huánglóng 黃龍 and Yángqí 楊岐) provide the categorical grid against which every *dēnglù* and *zōngmén* compendium ([KR6q0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0081), [KR6q0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0005), [KR6q0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0167)–[KR6q0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0169)) organizes its material.
- **Sòng-Chán syncretism with Huáyán-Tiāntái doctrine and the *jiào-chán yī-zhì* 教禪一致 program.** Anchored by Zōngmì's *Chányuán zhū quán jí dūxù* [KR6q0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0091) and developed at scale in Yǒngmíng Yánshòu's *Zōngjìng lù* [KR6q0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0092), this syncretic stream argues against Chán-school anti-textualism and re-grounds the *patriarchal vehicle* in canonical doctrine.
- **Pure Land convergence (*chán-jìng shuāng-xiū* 禪淨雙修).** From Yánshòu onward, and intensified in the late-Míng synthesis of Zhūhóng, Hānshān, and Ǒuyì, the division documents the long convergence between Chán and Pure Land practice — visible in the *Wànshàn tóngguī jí* [KR6q0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0093), the *Wéixīn jué* [KR6q0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0094), and across the Zhūhóng / Hānshān / Ǒuyì corpora.
- **Late-Míng / Qīng lineage disputes and the print boom.** The mid-17th-century controversy between the Línjì-Mìyún descendants and the Cáodòng line is the most concentrated polemical episode in Chinese Buddhist history: [KR6q0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0018)–[KR6q0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0020), [KR6q0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0167)–[KR6q0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0169), and the *Zhèngyuán lüèjí* tradition [KR6q0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0031)–[KR6q0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0033) all participate. The Jiāxīng-Canon 嘉興藏 print enterprise (1589–c. 1712) is the medium through which the resulting *yǔlù* explosion reaches the canon.
- **Chán monastic codes and the institutional history of the school.** [KR6q0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0102), [KR6q0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0136), and the *qīngguī* continuations [KR6q0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0139)–[KR6q0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0142) track the institutional discipline of the Chán monastery from Sòng through Qīng — the basis for any historical reconstruction of *cónglín* 叢林 life.
- **Lay Buddhism and women practitioners.** The lamp records open progressively to lay and female practitioners across the 13th–17th centuries: *Jūshì fēndēng lù* 居士分燈錄 [KR6q0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0039) (lay), *Yōupóyí zhì* [KR6q0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0051) (laywomen), [KR6q0273](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0273) *Páng jūshì yǔlù* (the iconic Páng Yùn 龐蘊 family), and *yǔlù* of Buddhist nuns scattered in the late-Míng / Qīng Jiāxīng-Canon range.
- **Transmission to Korea and Japan.** The division preserves: the Koryŏ-Sŏn corpus of Chinul [KR6q0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0095)–[KR6q0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0097) and the Chosŏn corpus of Sŏsan Hyujŏng [KR6q0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0146); the *Zǔtáng jí* itself, transmitted through Korea; Japanese Edo-period re-editions of the Cáodòng founders [KR6q0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0066)–[KR6q0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0069); and Dōgen's 道元 *Zuòchán zhēn* 坐禪箴 [KR6q0241](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0241) in its Sino-Japanese textual form.
- **Chán authors writing on the Three Teachings.** The division also collects works by Chán authors on non-Buddhist canonical texts — most prominently Ǒuyì's *Zhōuyì chánjiě* 周易禪解 [KR6q0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0184), *Qī yuán zhǐtōng* (Zhuāngzǐ) [KR6q0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0219), and *Dàodé jīng shùn zhū* [KR6q0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0227) — a witness to the late-Míng *sān jiào* 三教 conversation as conducted from inside the *cónglín*.

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR6q gathers the writings of the Chán school 禪宗 as preserved across three textual reservoirs: the *Shǐchuán bù* 史傳部 and *Zhū-zōng bù* 諸宗部 of the Taishō canon (T47, T48, T51), the Xuzangjing 卍續藏 Chán *yǔlù* run (X64–X88), and the Jiāxīng Canon 嘉興藏 *yǔlù* expansion (J20–J40 and the Wàihán *bùyí* 補遺). The division therefore spans the full literary output of an indigenous Chinese Buddhist tradition: transmission-of-the-lamp histories (*dēnglù* 燈錄) and their *xù-* / *guǎng-* / *liánxù-* / *zēngjí-* derivatives; the recorded sayings (*yǔlù* 語錄) of individual masters; the kōan / "old-cases" literature (*gōng'àn* 公案, *sòng gǔ* 頌古, *niāngǔ* 拈古, *píngchàng* 評唱) and its commentarial superstructure; Buddhist biographical jewelry (*sēngbǎo zhuàn* 僧寶傳); Chán monastic codes (*qīngguī* 清規); the admonitory-pastoral genre (*jǐng cè* 警策, *bǎoxùn* 寶訓); doctrinal compendia and sectarian polemics on the *wǔ jiā qī zōng* 五家七宗 lineages; verse cycles (notably the *shíniú tú sòng* 十牛圖頌 and the *Yǒngjiā Zhèngdào gē* 永嘉證道歌); and the literary collected works (*biéjí* 別集) of Chán masters. The 609 entries make KR6q the single largest Chán-literature corpus assembled anywhere in modern catalogs and the densest documentation of any East-Asian Buddhist school.

Chronologically the corpus stretches from the conventionally-dated 6th-century *Sì xíng guān* 四行觀 attributed to Bodhidharma (KR6q0112) through to the early-19th-century *Zhèngyuán lüèjí* 正源略集 of Jìchéng 際澄 (KR6q0031–0033, 1820–1828). Quantitatively, however, the division is overwhelmingly weighted toward the 17th century: roughly 335 of the 609 entries — about 55% — are 17th-century Jiāxīng-Canon *yǔlù* of late-Míng and early-Qīng Chán abbots, reflecting both the print boom of the Wàn-Lì 萬曆 reform and the Línjì-school 臨濟宗 revival under Mìyún Yuánwù 密雲圓悟 and his dharma-heirs. For Taishō structural context the relevant CANWWW divisions are `div21.xml` (史傳部, hosting the foundational *dēnglù* set) and the Chán portion of `div23.xml` / `div24.xml` (諸宗部 Chán entries). Modern critical reference for the *dēnglù* tradition runs through Yanagida Seizan 柳田聖山, T. Griffith Foulk, Albert Welter, and Morten Schlütter; for the late-Míng / Qīng *yǔlù* explosion, through Jiang Wu 吳疆, Beata Grant, and Hasebe Yūkei 長谷部幽蹊.

- *Tiānshèng guǎngdēng lù* 天聖廣燈錄 [KR6q0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0004) — Lǐ Zūnxù's 1029–1036 expansion, the first lay-compiled lamp record.
- *Jiànzhōng jìngguó xùdēng lù* 建中靖國續燈錄 [KR6q0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0007) — Wéibái's 1101 continuation.
- *Liándēng huìyào* 聯燈會要 [KR6q0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0008) — Wùmíng's 1183 harmonization of the previous three.
- *Jiātài pǔdēng lù* 嘉泰普燈錄 [KR6q0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0010) — Zhèngshòu's 1204 broadening to laity and women.
- *Wǔdēng huìyuán* 五燈會元 [KR6q0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0012) — Pǔjì's 1252 *editio definitiva* synthesizing the five preceding lamp records into a single 20-juan corpus; the most influential single text of the genre.
- *Xù chuándēng lù* 續傳燈錄 [KR6q0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0016) — the early-Míng (1401–1402) Yǒnglè-era imperial continuation.
- *Wǔdēng yántǒng* 五燈嚴統 [KR6q0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0019) / *Jiěhuò biān* [KR6q0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0020) — Fèiyǐn Tōngróng's 1653–1654 partisan Línjì rewrite and its self-defence, the most notorious sectarian intervention in the *dēnglù* tradition.
- *Wǔdēng quánshū* 五燈全書 [KR6q0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0022) — Jièlín Chāoyǒng's 120-juan Kāngxī-era (1697) compendium.
- *Zhǐyuè lù* 指月錄 [KR6q0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0023) — Qú Rǔjī's lay-compiled 1602 anthology.

**Kōan / old-cases tradition.** The *gōng'àn* literary tradition reframes encounter-dialogue narratives from the *dēnglù* as objects of literary commentary.

- *Bìyán lù* 碧巖錄 [KR6q0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0078) — Yuánwù Kèqín's *píngchàng* commentary (c. 1128) on Xuědòu Chóngxiǎn's 雪竇重顯 100 *sòng-gǔ* verses; the *locus classicus* of *wénzì chán* 文字禪.
- *Cóngróng ān lù* 從容庵錄 [KR6q0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0079) — Wànsōng Xíngxiù's 1223 commentary on Hóngzhì Zhèngjué's 宏智正覺 100 verses; Cáodòng counterpart to the *Bìyán lù*.
- *Wúmén guān* 無門關 [KR6q0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0080) — Wúmén Huìkāi's 1228 collection of 48 cases, the most internationally diffused kōan compendium.
- *Fóguǒ jījié lù* 佛果擊節錄 [KR6q0249](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0249), the Línquán 林泉 commentaries [KR6q0251](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0251) [KR6q0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0252), and the Tiānqí 天奇 directing commentaries [KR6q0250](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0250) [KR6q0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0253) continue the genre through the Yuán and Míng.

**Early Chán and the *Liù zǔ* 六祖 corpus.** A tight cluster of works either attributed to or recovered from the early Tang Chán milieu, much of it Dūnhuáng-attested.

- The two recensions of the *Liùzǔ tánjīng* 六祖壇經 (Dūnhuáng [KR6q0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0082); the standard Yuán recension [KR6q0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0083)).
- *Shǎoshì liù mén* 少室六門 [KR6q0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0084) and the four short Bodhidharma treatises (*Xuèmài lùn*, *Wùxìng lùn*, *Pòxiàng lùn*, *Sì xíng guān*) at [KR6q0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0112)–[KR6q0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0115).
- *Xìnxīn míng* 信心銘 attributed to Sēngcàn 僧璨 [KR6q0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0085).
- *Zuìshàng shèng lùn* 最上乘論 attributed to Hóngrěn 弘忍 [KR6q0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0086).
- *Léngqié shīzī jì* 楞伽師資記 [KR6q0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0109) and *Chuán fǎ bǎo jì* 傳法寶記 [KR6q0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0110) — the principal Northern-school lineage records, recovered from Dūnhuáng.
- The Huángbò Xīyùn 黃檗希運 corpus recorded by Péi Xiū 裴休: *Chuánxīn fǎyào* [KR6q0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0087) and *Wǎnlíng lù* [KR6q0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0088).
- *Dùnwù rùdào yàomén lùn* 頓悟入道要門論 [KR6q0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0117) by Dàzhū Huìhǎi 大珠慧海.
- *Yǒngjiā jí* [KR6q0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0089) and *Yǒngjiā Zhèngdào gē* [KR6q0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0090).
- *Chányuán zhū quán jí dūxù* 禪源諸詮集都序 [KR6q0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0091) — Guīfēng Zōngmì's 圭峰宗密 doctrinal classification of Chán.

**Sòng-Chán masters' *yǔlù* — the "core canon".** The classical *yǔlù* of the five-house founders and the major Sòng Línjì / Cáodòng lines.

- *Línjì lù* 臨濟錄 [KR6q0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0053); *Yúnmén guǎnglù* 雲門廣錄 [KR6q0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0073); *Cáoshān yǔlù* (in [KR6q0269](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0269)); *Fǎyǎn yǔlù* (in [KR6q0270](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0270)).
- The Línjì-Yángqí 楊岐 line: *Fényáng* [KR6q0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0054), *Huánglóng* [KR6q0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0055), *Yángqí* [KR6q0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0056) [KR6q0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0057), *Fǎyǎn* (Wǔzǔ Fǎyǎn 五祖法演) [KR6q0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0058), *Yuánwù Kèqín* 圓悟克勤 [KR6q0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0059), *Dàhuì Zōnggǎo* 大慧宗杲 [KR6q0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0060)–[KR6q0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0063), *Mì'ān Xiánjié* 密菴 [KR6q0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0064), *Xūtáng Zhìyú* 虛堂智愚 [KR6q0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0065).
- The Cáodòng line: *Hóngzhì guǎnglù* 宏智廣錄 [KR6q0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0070), *Tiāntóng Rújìng yǔlù* 天童如淨 [KR6q0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0072), *Dòngshān* / *Cáoshān* in [KR6q0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0066)–[KR6q0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0069).
- *Gǔ zūnsù yǔlù* 古尊宿語錄 [KR6q0261](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0261) / [KR6q0263](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0263) and its continuations *Xù gǔ zūnsù yǔyào* [KR6q0265](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0265) — the Sòng anthologies of pre-five-house master sayings.
- *Sì jiā yǔlù* 四家語錄 [KR6q0266](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0266)–[KR6q0269](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0269) — the canonical Mǎ-zǔ 馬祖, Bǎizhàng 百丈, Huángbò, Línjì set.

**Doctrinal compendia and sectarian polemics.** The *zōngmén* 宗門 literature in which the Chán school theorized its own lineage and doctrinal claims.

- *Zōngjìng lù* 宗鏡錄 [KR6q0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0092) — Yǒngmíng Yánshòu's 永明延壽 100-juan synthesis of Chán with Huáyán-Tiāntái doctrine (c. 961); the most ambitious doctrinal compendium in the division. Companion works at [KR6q0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0093) *Wànshàn tóngguī jí* and [KR6q0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0094) *Wéixīn jué*.
- *Rén tiān yǎnmù* 人天眼目 [KR6q0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0081) — Zhìzhāo's 智昭 1188 systematic exposition of the *wǔ jiā* methods.
- *Wǔ jiā zhèngzōng zàn* 五家正宗贊 [KR6q0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0005) — Shàotán's 紹曇 1254 verse-encomium of the five houses.
- *Wǔ zōng yuán* 五宗原 [KR6q0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0167), *Pìwàng jiùlüè shuō* 闢妄救略說 [KR6q0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0168), *Wǔ jiā zōngzhǐ zuǎnyào* 五家宗旨纂要 [KR6q0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0169) — the mid-17th-century Línjì-school polemical trilogy around the Mìyún-Yuánwù dharma-heirs' rewriting of lineage history.
- *Chánjiā guījiàn* 禪家龜鑑 [KR6q0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0146) — Korean Sŏn introduction by Sŏsan Hyujŏng 西山休靜.

**Chán biographical compendia.**

- *Chánlín sēngbǎo zhuàn* 禪林僧寶傳 [KR6q0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0040) — Juéfàn Huìhóng's 覺範慧洪 1119–1124 collection, the genre's prototype.
- *Sēngbǎo zhèngxù zhuàn* 僧寶正續傳 [KR6q0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0041).
- *Nán-Sòng Yuán-Míng chánlín sēngbǎo zhuàn* [KR6q0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0042) — Zìróng 自融 and Xìnglěi 性磊, 1654.
- *Huáng-Míng míngsēng jí lüè* 皇明名僧輯略 [KR6q0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0043) — Zhūhóng 袾宏 (Yúnqī).
- *Bāshíbā zǔ dàoyǐng zhuànzàn* 八十八祖道影傳贊 [KR6q0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0045) — Hānshān Déqīng 憨山德清.

**Monastic codes and pastoral-regulatory literature.**

- *Chìxiū Bǎizhàng qīngguī* 敕修百丈清規 [KR6q0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0102) — the 1335 Yuán imperial recension of the Chán monastic code attributed to Bǎizhàng Huáihǎi 百丈懷海.
- *Chányuàn qīngguī* 禪苑清規 [KR6q0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0136) — the 1103 Sòng recension by Cháng-lú Zōngzé 長蘆宗賾, the earliest surviving Chán code.
- *Chánlín bǎoxùn* 禪林寶訓 [KR6q0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0099) with its four Míng-Qīng commentaries [KR6q0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0153)–[KR6q0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0157).
- *Zī mén jǐngxùn* 緇門警訓 [KR6q0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0100) — Míng-period encyclopedic admonition anthology.
- *Chánguān cèjìn* 禪關策進 [KR6q0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0101) — Zhūhóng's 1600 practice-encouragement anthology.

**Comprehensive *guǎnglù* and Jiāxīng-Canon *biéjí*.** The late-Míng / Qīng print expansion. The principal monumental sets include *Yǒngjué Yuánxián chánshī guǎnglù* [KR6q0367](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0367), *Bù shuǐ tái jí* 布水臺集 [KR6q0200](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0200) of Mùchén Dàomín 木陳道忞 (with a preface by Qián Qiānyì 錢謙益), *Wúyì Yuánlái guǎnglù* [KR6q0365](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0365), the Hānshān 憨山 corpus *Mèngyóu jí* [KR6q0386](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0386) / *Quánjí* [KR6q0389](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0389), and the Zǐbǎi 紫柏 *Zūnzhě quánjí* [KR6q0382](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0382).

### Important persons

- [菩提達磨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E9%81%94%E7%A3%A8) (Pútídámó) — the conventional first patriarch of Chinese Chán; pseudepigraphic attributee for the Bodhidharma corpus and the *Sì xíng guān*.
- [慧能](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E8%83%BD) (Huìnéng, 638–713) — the Sixth Patriarch and the authorial figure for the *Liùzǔ tánjīng* recensions [KR6q0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0082) [KR6q0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0083).
- [希運](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B8%8C%E9%81%8B) (Huángbò Xīyùn, d. c. 850) — Tang Chán master, the *Chuánxīn fǎyào* / *Wǎnlíng lù* are his sayings as recorded by Péi Xiū 裴休.
- [義玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E7%8E%84) (Línjì Yìxuán, d. 866) — founder of the Línjì line; the *Línjì lù* [KR6q0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0053) is the canonical record.
- [文偃](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%87%E5%81%83) (Yúnmén Wényǎn, 864–949) — founder of the Yúnmén house; recorded sayings at [KR6q0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0073).
- [文益](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%87%E7%9B%8A) (Fǎyǎn Wényì, 885–958) — founder of the Fǎyǎn house.
- [宗密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E5%AF%86) (Guīfēng Zōngmì, 780–841) — Hèzé–Huáyán synthesist; his *Chányuán zhū quán jí dūxù* [KR6q0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0091) is the foundational doctrinal taxonomy of Chán.
- [延壽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BB%B6%E5%A3%BD) (Yǒngmíng Yánshòu, 904–975) — author of the *Zōngjìng lù* and architect of the Sòng-period Chán-doctrinal synthesis.
- [道原](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%8E%9F) (Dàoyuán, fl. early 11th c.) — compiler of the *Jǐngdé chuándēng lù*.
- [重顯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8D%E9%A1%AF) (Xuědòu Chóngxiǎn, 980–1052) — Yúnmén-line master whose 100 *sòng-gǔ* verses are the verse-substrate of the *Bìyán lù*.
- [克勤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%8B%E5%8B%A4) (Yuánwù Kèqín, 1063–1135) — author of the *Bìyán lù*; central figure of Sòng *wénzì chán*.
- [宗杲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%97%E6%9D%B2) (Dàhuì Zōnggǎo, 1089–1163) — Yuánwù's heir, theorist of *kàn huàtóu* 看話頭 method; 4-text corpus at [KR6q0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0060)–[KR6q0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0063).
- [正覺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%A3%E8%A6%BA) (Hóngzhì Zhèngjué, 1091–1157) — Cáodòng partisan of *mòzhào chán* 默照禪; *guǎnglù* at [KR6q0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0070).
- [行秀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A1%8C%E7%A7%80) (Wànsōng Xíngxiù, 1166–1246) — Jīn-Yuán Cáodòng-line commentator on Hóngzhì's verses (*Cóngróng lù*).
- [慧開](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%96%8B) (Wúmén Huìkāi, 1183–1260) — compiler of the *Wúmén guān*.
- [慧洪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%B4%AA) (Juéfàn Huìhóng, 1071–1128) — author of the *Sēngbǎo zhuàn* and a principal Sòng Chán literary theorist.
- [智昭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%98%AD) (Zhìzhāo, fl. 1188) — compiler of the *Rén tiān yǎnmù*.
- [普濟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E6%BF%9F) (Pǔjì, 1178–1253) — compiler of the *Wǔdēng huìyuán*.
- [紹曇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%B4%B9%E6%9B%87) (Shàotán, fl. 1254) — author of the *Wǔ jiā zhèngzōng zàn*.
- [守一](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%88%E4%B8%80) (Shǒuyī, fl. 1183) — co-figure in the *Liándēng huìyào*.
- [知訥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%A5%E8%A8%A5) (Chinul, 1158–1210) — Koryŏ Sŏn synthesist; three works at [KR6q0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0095)–[KR6q0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0097) anchor the Korean presence.
- [袾宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%BE%E5%AE%8F) (Yúnqī Zhūhóng, 1535–1615) — late-Míng monastic reformer; the *Chánguān cèjìn* and *Huáng-Míng míngsēng jí lüè* are his.
- [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) (Hānshān Déqīng, 1546–1623) — late-Míng polymath; substantial *guǎnglù* / *quánjí* corpus.
- [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) (Ǒuyì Zhìxù, 1599–1655) — late-Míng exegete uniting Chán with Tiāntái doctrine and Yìjīng-Lǎo-Zhuāng reading.
- [元賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E8%B3%A2) (Yǒngjué Yuánxián, 1578–1657) — Cáodòng patriarch of the Gǔshān 鼓山 line; *guǎnglù* at [KR6q0367](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0367) and *Jìdēng lù* at [KR6q0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0038).

### Topics

- **The *dēnglù* and the construction of patriarchal lineage.** The *dēnglù* genre invented and then iteratively re-edited the canonical lineage chart of Chinese Chán: the *Xī tiān èr-shí-bā zǔ* 西天二十八祖 + *Dōng-tǔ liù zǔ* 東土六祖 + *wǔ jiā qī zōng* 五家七宗 schema. Every text in [KR6q0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0001)–[KR6q0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0039) is a re-articulation of this charter narrative, with sectarian rewrites (e.g. [KR6q0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0019) *Wǔdēng yántǒng*) using the genre to *redistribute* dharma-heir assignments between Cáodòng and Línjì.
- **Encounter-dialogue (*jīyuán wèndá* 機緣問答) as literary form.** The *yǔlù* and *dēnglù* together generate the encounter-dialogue paradigm — short, edited dialogues between master and disciple structured around live language, demotic speech, paradox, and physical action — which becomes the master genre of Chinese Buddhist literature and the proximate source-material for the kōan tradition.
- **The *gōng'àn* and *wénzì chán* / *kàn huà* / *mòzhào* debate.** The Sòng kōan tradition splits along three axes: literary commentary on edited cases (*Bìyán lù*, *Cóngróng lù*), *kàn huàtóu* introspection on a single critical phrase (Dàhuì Zōnggǎo, [KR6q0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0060)–[KR6q0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0063)), and *mòzhào chán* silent-illumination practice (Hóngzhì Zhèngjué, [KR6q0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0070) and Tiāntóng Rújìng, [KR6q0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0072)). The Sòng controversy between Dàhuì and Hóngzhì is the principal doctrinal debate documented in the division.
- **The *wǔ jiā qī zōng* doctrinal classification.** The *wǔ jiā* — Guī-yǎng 溈仰, Línjì, Cáodòng, Yúnmén, Fǎyǎn — and the *qī zōng* extension with the two Línjì sub-houses (Huánglóng 黃龍 and Yángqí 楊岐) provide the categorical grid against which every *dēnglù* and *zōngmén* compendium ([KR6q0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0081), [KR6q0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0005), [KR6q0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0167)–[KR6q0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0169)) organizes its material.
- **Sòng-Chán syncretism with Huáyán-Tiāntái doctrine and the *jiào-chán yī-zhì* 教禪一致 program.** Anchored by Zōngmì's *Chányuán zhū quán jí dūxù* [KR6q0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0091) and developed at scale in Yǒngmíng Yánshòu's *Zōngjìng lù* [KR6q0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0092), this syncretic stream argues against Chán-school anti-textualism and re-grounds the *patriarchal vehicle* in canonical doctrine.
- **Pure Land convergence (*chán-jìng shuāng-xiū* 禪淨雙修).** From Yánshòu onward, and intensified in the late-Míng synthesis of Zhūhóng, Hānshān, and Ǒuyì, the division documents the long convergence between Chán and Pure Land practice — visible in the *Wànshàn tóngguī jí* [KR6q0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0093), the *Wéixīn jué* [KR6q0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0094), and across the Zhūhóng / Hānshān / Ǒuyì corpora.
- **Late-Míng / Qīng lineage disputes and the print boom.** The mid-17th-century controversy between the Línjì-Mìyún descendants and the Cáodòng line is the most concentrated polemical episode in Chinese Buddhist history: [KR6q0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0018)–[KR6q0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0020), [KR6q0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0167)–[KR6q0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0169), and the *Zhèngyuán lüèjí* tradition [KR6q0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0031)–[KR6q0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0033) all participate. The Jiāxīng-Canon 嘉興藏 print enterprise (1589–c. 1712) is the medium through which the resulting *yǔlù* explosion reaches the canon.
- **Chán monastic codes and the institutional history of the school.** [KR6q0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0102), [KR6q0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0136), and the *qīngguī* continuations [KR6q0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0139)–[KR6q0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0142) track the institutional discipline of the Chán monastery from Sòng through Qīng — the basis for any historical reconstruction of *cónglín* 叢林 life.
- **Lay Buddhism and women practitioners.** The lamp records open progressively to lay and female practitioners across the 13th–17th centuries: *Jūshì fēndēng lù* 居士分燈錄 [KR6q0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0039) (lay), *Yōupóyí zhì* [KR6q0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0051) (laywomen), [KR6q0273](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0273) *Páng jūshì yǔlù* (the iconic Páng Yùn 龐蘊 family), and *yǔlù* of Buddhist nuns scattered in the late-Míng / Qīng Jiāxīng-Canon range.
- **Transmission to Korea and Japan.** The division preserves: the Koryŏ-Sŏn corpus of Chinul [KR6q0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0095)–[KR6q0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0097) and the Chosŏn corpus of Sŏsan Hyujŏng [KR6q0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0146); the *Zǔtáng jí* itself, transmitted through Korea; Japanese Edo-period re-editions of the Cáodòng founders [KR6q0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0066)–[KR6q0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0069); and Dōgen's 道元 *Zuòchán zhēn* 坐禪箴 [KR6q0241](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0241) in its Sino-Japanese textual form.
- **Chán authors writing on the Three Teachings.** The division also collects works by Chán authors on non-Buddhist canonical texts — most prominently Ǒuyì's *Zhōuyì chánjiě* 周易禪解 [KR6q0184](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0184), *Qī yuán zhǐtōng* (Zhuāngzǐ) [KR6q0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0219), and *Dàodé jīng shùn zhū* [KR6q0227](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0227) — a witness to the late-Míng *sān jiào* 三教 conversation as conducted from inside the *cónglín*.
