# 書類 (KR1b)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1b 書類 *Shū lèi* — Classics — Book of Documents](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR1b 書類 collects 60 works of *Shàngshū* 尚書 (also *Shū jīng* 書經) scholarship — the canonical anthology of speeches, decrees, and counsels traditionally ascribed to the Yú, Xià, Shāng, and Zhōu dynasties, together with the layered tradition of commentary, sub-commentary, paraphrase, and philological audit that grew up around it from the Hàn through the high Qīng. Within the Sìkù quánshū macro-arrangement the division stands second inside `KR1` 經部 (Classics), immediately after `KR1a` 易類 and reflecting the *Shū*'s position as second of the Five Classics. Wilkinson notes that the oldest parts of the *Shū* date from the tenth century BCE, that the received text as we now have it was assembled around 317 CE and entered the Kāichéng 開成 stone Classics in 837, and that the once-standard contrast between an "Ancient-script" (*gǔwén* 古文) and a "Modern-script" (*jīnwén* 今文) recension is itself a misunderstanding that recent scholarship has worked to dispel (Wilkinson §58.6.3.1).

The chronological span of the collected works runs from the Hàn *Shàngshū dà zhuàn* 尚書大傳 attributed to Fú Shēng 伏勝 ([KR1b0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0059)), through the imperially-canonical Táng *Shàngshū zhèngyì* 尚書正義 of Kǒng Yǐngdá 孔穎達 ([KR1b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0003) / [KR1b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0004)), the Northern-Sòng cosmological reading of the *Hóngfàn* 洪範 chapter inaugurated by Hú Yuán 胡瑗 ([KR1b0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0005)), Cài Shěn's 蔡沈 epoch-defining *Shū jīng jízhuàn* 書經集傳 of 1209 ([KR1b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0017)) — the standard examination commentary for the next six centuries — the Yuán Cài-Shěn-centric subcommentaries, the Míng imperial *Shū jīng dàquán* 書經大全 of 1415 ([KR1b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0037)), and the Qīng evidential demolition of the 25 "Old-Text" chapters by Yán Ruòqú 閻若璩 in his *Shàngshū gǔwén shū zhèng* 尚書古文疏證 ([KR1b0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0048)). By count the Sòng (≈ 21 works) and Qīng (≈ 14) layers dominate, with smaller but pivotal Hàn, Táng, Yuán, and Míng strata. The division thus tracks two intertwined trajectories: a long *yìlǐ* 義理 reading tradition culminating in Cài Shěn and the Míng *Dàquán*, and a textual-philological tradition that, beginning quietly with Méi Zhuó 梅鷟 in the early sixteenth century and erupting into method with Yán Ruòqú a hundred and fifty years later, dismantled half of the received classic.

### Important texts and text clusters

**Canonical text and Hàn layer.**
- *Shàngshū (zhèngwén)* 尚書(正文) [KR1b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0001) — the canonical text itself, the starting point for every commentary in the division.
- *Shàngshū dà zhuàn* 尚書大傳 [KR1b0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0059) — attributed to Fú Shēng 伏勝, with Zhèng Xuán's 鄭玄 annotations and a Qīng-era reconstruction by Sūn Zhīlù 孫之騄; the principal Hàn-era hermeneutic work transmitted under the *Shū*.
- *Shàngshū* (Sòng-printed Kǒng Ān'guó *zhuàn*) [KR1b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0002) — the received recension of the *Kǒng zhuàn* 孔傳 ascribed to Kǒng Ān'guó 孔安國 with the Táng *yīnyì* 音義 of Lù Démíng 陸德明; the textual base that Yán Ruòqú would later impeach.

**Táng official subcommentary.**
- *Shàngshū zhèngyì* 尚書正義 [KR1b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0003) — Kǒng Yǐngdá's 孔穎達 imperially-commissioned subcommentary on the Kǒng Ān'guó *zhuàn*, completed during the Zhēnguān-Yǒnghuī years (642–653); part of the *Wǔjīng zhèngyì* synthesis and the textbook *Shū* of the next four centuries.
- *Shàngshū zhùshū* 尚書注疏 [KR1b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0004) — the integrated edition combining the Kǒng Ān'guó *zhuàn*, Kǒng Yǐngdá's *zhèngyì*, Lù Démíng's *yīnyì*, and the Qīng evidential *kǎozhèng* of Qí Zhàonán 齊召南 and Chén Hào 陳浩 added on the imperial *Shíjīng* commission; effectively the layered scholarly *Shū* in its received Sìkù form.

**Northern Sòng — *Hóngfàn* cosmology and the rise of philosophical reading.**
- *Hóngfàn kǒuyì* 洪範口義 [KR1b0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0005) — Hú Yuán's 胡瑗 lecture-style reading of the single chapter that, more than any other, would license Sòng cosmological speculation about the Five Phases and Nine Categories.
- *Shū zhuàn* 書傳 [KR1b0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0006) — Sū Shì's 蘇軾 *Dōngpō Shū zhuàn*, the most distinguished northern-Sòng literary-philosophical commentary, paired in tone with his *Yìzhuàn* in [KR1a0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0015).

**Southern Sòng — the *Yǔgòng* sub-tradition and the road to Cài Shěn.**
- *Shàngshū quánjiě* 尚書全解 [KR1b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0007) — Lín Zhīqí's 林之奇 capacious commentary, transmitted in revised form and repeatedly cited by Cài Shěn.
- *Yǔgòng zhǐnán* 禹貢指南 [KR1b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0008), *Yǔgòng lùn* 禹貢論 [KR1b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0009), *Yǔgòng shuō duàn* 禹貢說斷 [KR1b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0012) — Máo Huàng 毛晃, Chéng Dàchāng 程大昌, and Fù Yín 傅寅 founding the historical-geographical study of the *Yǔgòng* 禹貢 chapter as a free-standing sub-genre.
- *Shàngshū jiǎngyì* 尚書講義 [KR1b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0010), *Shàngshū xiángjiě* 尚書詳解 [KR1b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0011) — Shǐ Hào 史浩 and Xià Sǒng 夏僎: representative high-Sòng reading commentaries.
- *Zēngxiū Dōnglái Shū shuō* 增修東萊書說 [KR1b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0013) — Lǚ Zǔqiān's 呂祖謙 lecture commentary expanded by Shí Lán 時瀾, parallel to Lǚ's 古周易 textual reconstruction in [KR1a0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0043).
- *Shū jīng jízhuàn* 書經集傳 [KR1b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0017) — Cài Shěn's 蔡沈 imperially-prescribed commentary, written 1199–1209 at Zhū Xī's 朱熹 deathbed commission; the single most consequential post-classical *Shū* work, governing the examination curriculum from the Yuán reform of 1313 through the late Qīng. The functional counterpart in this division to Zhū Xī's *Zhōuyì běnyì* in [KR1a0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0031).
- *Shàngshū jīngyì* 尚書精義 [KR1b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0018), *Chén shì Shàngshū xiángjiě* 陳氏尚書詳解 [KR1b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0019), *Róngtáng Shū jiě* 融堂書解 [KR1b0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0020) — Huáng Lún 黃倫, Chén Jīng 陳經, and Qián Shí 錢時: the dense Southern Sòng reading layer that surrounds and partly anticipates Cài Shěn.
- *Shàngshū yàoyì* 尚書要義 [KR1b0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0022) — Wèi Liǎowēng's 魏了翁 distillation, alongside his parallel *Yàoyì* compilations on the *Yì* and *Lǐ* classics.
- *Shū jízhuàn huòwèn* 書集傳或問 [KR1b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0023) — Chén Dàyóu 陳大猷, the first sustained dialogic apparatus around Cài Shěn's *Jízhuàn*.
- *Shàngshū biǎo zhù* 尚書表注 [KR1b0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0025) — Jīn Lǚxiáng's 金履祥 annotated table-format reading; the late-Sòng / early-Yuán transition piece.

**Yuán — codification of Cài Shěn.**
- *Shū zuǎn yán* 書纂言 [KR1b0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0026) — Wú Chéng's 吳澄 paired companion to his *Yì zuǎn yán* in [KR1a0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0071).
- *Shū jízhuàn zuǎnshū* 書集傳纂疏 [KR1b0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0027) — Chén Lì's 陳櫟 systematic subcommentary on Cài Shěn, the model for the genre.
- *Dú shū cóngshuō* 讀書叢說 [KR1b0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0028) — Xǔ Qiān's 許謙 reading-notes commentary in the Jīn-Wáng (金華) Daoxue line.
- *Shū chuán jí lù zuǎn zhù* 書傳輯錄纂註 [KR1b0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0029), *Shū Cài shì zhuàn pángtōng* 書蔡氏傳旁通 [KR1b0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0031) — Dǒng Dǐng 董鼎 and Chén Shīkǎi 陳師凱: explicit Cài Shěn commentaries marketed for the new examination curriculum.
- *Shàngshū tōngkǎo* 尚書通考* [KR1b0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0030) — Huáng Zhènchéng 黃鎮成: a classified-topic compilation of *Shū* lore.
- *Dú shū guǎnjiàn* 讀書管見 [KR1b0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0032), *Shū yì jīnshì* 書義矜式 [KR1b0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0060) — Wáng Chōngyún's 王充耘 paired works, the latter explicitly an examination handbook.
- *Shū yì duàn fǎ* 書義斷法* [KR1b0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0033) — Chén Yuèdào 陳悅道, similarly examination-oriented.
- *Shàngshū zuǎn zhuàn* 尚書纂傳 [KR1b0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0034) — Wáng Tiānyǔ 王天與: the most ambitious Yuán synthetic commentary outside the Cài Shěn line.
- *Shàngshū jù jiě* 尚書句解 [KR1b0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0035) — Zhū Zǔyì 朱祖義: Yuán plain-style line-by-line gloss, designed for school use.

**Míng — official compendia and the first cracks in the *Gǔwén*.**
- *Shū chuán huìxuǎn* 書傳會選 [KR1b0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0036) — Liú Sānwú's 劉三吾 1394 imperially-commissioned compilation, a brief Hóngwǔ-era counterpart to the later *Dàquán*.
- *Shū jīng dàquán* 書經大全 [KR1b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0037) — Hú Guǎng's 胡廣 1415 imperial compendium; canonical for the Míng-Qīng examination system, paired with [KR1a0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0091) and the parallel *Sìshū dàquán*.
- *Shàngshū kǎo yì* 尚書考異 [KR1b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0038) — Méi Zhuó's 梅鷟 sixteenth-century textual audit; the first sustained scholarly suspicion that the *Gǔwén* chapters and the Kǒng Ān'guó *zhuàn* could not be authentic, anticipating Yán Ruòqú by a century and a half.
- *Shàngshū yíyì* 尚書疑義 [KR1b0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0039), *Shàngshū rìjì* 尚書日記 [KR1b0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0040), *Shàngshū biān Cài biān* 尚書砭蔡編 [KR1b0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0041), *Shàngshū zhù kǎo* 尚書注考 [KR1b0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0042), *Shàngshū shū yǎn* 尚書疏衍 [KR1b0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0043) — Mǎ Míngháng 馬明衡, Wáng Qiáo 王樵, Yuán Rén 袁仁, Chén Tàijiāo 陳泰交, and Chén Dì 陳第: a clutch of late-Míng works increasingly willing to take issue with Cài Shěn or to test the canonical text against epigraphic and phonological evidence — the Cài-shèn-critical strain among them anticipating the Qīng turn.
- *Hóngfàn míngyì* 洪範明義 [KR1b0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0044) — Huáng Dàozhōu's 黃道周 cosmological reading of the *Hóngfàn*, parallel to his late-Míng *Yì xiàng zhèng* in [KR1a0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0110) and written against the same backdrop of impending dynastic collapse.

**Qīng — imperial codification, and the demolition of the *Gǔwén*.**
- *Rì jiǎng Shū jīng jiě yì* 日講書經解義 [KR1b0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0045) — the Kāngxī imperial lecture-commentary completed by Kūlènà 庫勒納 and Yè Fāng'ài 葉方藹 in 1678–80, paralleling the *Yì* and *Shī* lecture-commentaries.
- *Qīndìng Shūjīng zhuànshuō huìzuǎn* 欽定書經傳說彙纂 [KR1b0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0046) — Wáng Xūlíng's 王頊齡 great Yōngzhèng-Qiánlóng compilation, the *Shū* counterpart to [KR1a0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0117) *Yù zuàn Zhōuyì zhézhōng*.
- *Shàngshū bài shū* 尚書稗疏 [KR1b0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0047) — Wáng Fūzhī's 王夫之 austere *Shū* reading, pendant to his *Zhōuyì bài shū* in [KR1a0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0120).
- *Shàngshū gǔwén shū zhèng* 尚書古文疏證 [KR1b0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0048) — Yán Ruòqú's 閻若璩 evidential demolition of the 25 "Old-Text" chapters and the Kǒng Ān'guó *zhuàn*, in 128 numbered arguments; the founding monument of high-Qīng *kǎozhèng* method and arguably the single most consequential work of premodern Chinese philology. Decisively settled the question of the *Gǔwén Shàngshū* for all subsequent scholarship.
- *Gǔwén Shàngshū yuān cí* 古文尚書冤詞 [KR1b0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0049), *Shàngshū guǎngtīng lù* 尚書廣聽錄 [KR1b0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0050) — Máo Qílíng's 毛奇齡 vigorous and ultimately unsuccessful counter-attack defending the authenticity of the *Gǔwén*; despite its failure, a methodologically important rejoinder that forced Yán Ruòqú's followers to sharpen their case.
- *Shàngshū píchuán* 尚書埤傳 [KR1b0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0051), *Yǔgòng chángjiān* 禹貢長箋 [KR1b0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0052) — Zhū Hèlíng 朱鶴齡: a paired Cài Shěn supplement and *Yǔgòng* monograph from the early Qīng.
- *Yǔgòng zhuīzhǐ* 禹貢錐指 [KR1b0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0053) — Hú Wèi's 胡渭 systematic historical-geographical commentary on the *Yǔgòng*, the definitive monograph in the *Yǔgòng* sub-tradition; pendant to his demolition of the Sòng diagrams of the *Yì* in [KR1a0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0138).
- *Hóngfàn zhènglùn* 洪範正論 [KR1b0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0054) — Hú Wèi's parallel monograph on the *Hóngfàn*, similarly purgative of Sòng cosmological accretion.
- *Shàngshū qī piān jiěyì* 尚書七篇解義 [KR1b0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0055) — Lǐ Guāngdì's 李光地 selective commentary on seven core chapters; pendant to his role as director of [KR1a0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0117).
- *Shū jīng zhōnglùn* 書經衷論 [KR1b0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0056), *Shàngshū dìlǐ jīnshì* 尚書地理今釋 [KR1b0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0057), *Yǔgòng huì jiān* 禹貢會箋 [KR1b0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0058) — Zhāng Yīng 張英, Jiǎng Tíngxī 蔣廷錫, and Xú Wénjìng 徐文靖: the late-Kāngxī to mid-Qiánlóng layer, mostly historical-geographical or topical.

### Important persons

- [伏勝](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BC%8F%E5%8B%9D) (Fú Shēng) — Hàn transmitter to whom the *Shàngshū dà zhuàn* [KR1b0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0059) is ascribed; the legendary fountainhead of post-Qín *Shàngshū* knowledge.
- [孔安國](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E5%AE%89%E5%9C%8B) (Kǒng Ān'guó) — putative Hàn author of the *Kǒng zhuàn* [KR1b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0002) [KR1b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0004); the central figure whose authentic involvement Yán Ruòqú definitively impeached.
- [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) (Zhèng Xuán) — Hàn synthesizer whose annotations on the *Shàngshū dà zhuàn* [KR1b0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0059) preserve the principal Hàn hermeneutic stratum.
- [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) (Lù Démíng) — Táng compiler of the *Jīngdiǎn shìwén* whose *Shàngshū yīnyì* [KR1b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0002) [KR1b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0004) supplied the standard phonological apparatus.
- [孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94) (Kǒng Yǐngdá) — Táng director of the *Wǔjīng zhèngyì* [KR1b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0003) [KR1b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0004), the imperial subcommentary that fixed the *Shū* reading from the seventh through eleventh centuries.
- [胡瑗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E7%91%97) (Hú Yuán) — Northern Sòng teacher whose [KR1b0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0005) inaugurated the Sòng cosmological reading of the *Hóngfàn*.
- [蘇軾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE) (Sū Shì) — Northern Sòng polymath whose [KR1b0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0006) is the most distinguished literary-philosophical *Shū* commentary of the era.
- [林之奇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9E%97%E4%B9%8B%E5%A5%87) (Lín Zhīqí) — Southern Sòng commentator whose [KR1b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0007) supplied much of the raw material absorbed into Cài Shěn's *Jízhuàn*.
- [毛晃](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E6%99%83) (Máo Huàng), [程大昌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A8%8B%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8C) (Chéng Dàchāng), [傅寅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%82%85%E5%AF%85) (Fù Yín) — Southern-Sòng founders of the *Yǔgòng* monograph as a sub-genre [KR1b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0008) [KR1b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0009) [KR1b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0012).
- [呂祖謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E7%A5%96%E8%AC%99) (Lǚ Zǔqiān) — Southern Sòng polymath whose [KR1b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0013) is the parallel of his textual reconstruction work in [KR1a0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0043).
- [蔡沈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E6%B2%88) (Cài Shěn) — author of [KR1b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0017), by Zhū Xī's deathbed commission; defines the orthodox late-imperial reading of the *Shū* for six centuries.
- [魏了翁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E4%BA%86%E7%BF%81) (Wèi Liǎowēng) — Southern Sòng compiler-distiller [KR1b0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0022), paralleling his *Yàoyì* on other classics.
- [金履祥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%91%E5%B1%A5%E7%A5%A5) (Jīn Lǚxiáng) — late-Sòng / early-Yuán commentator [KR1b0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0025) in the Jīn-Wáng Daoxue line.
- [吳澄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%BE%84) (Wú Chéng), [陳櫟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%AB%9F) (Chén Lì), [許謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E8%AC%99) (Xǔ Qiān), [董鼎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%A3%E9%BC%8E) (Dǒng Dǐng), [陳師凱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%B8%AB%E5%87%B1) (Chén Shīkǎi), [黃鎮成](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E9%8E%AE%E6%88%90) (Huáng Zhènchéng), [王充耘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%85%85%E8%80%98) (Wáng Chōngyún), [陳悅道](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%82%85%E9%81%93) (Chén Yuèdào), [王天與](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A4%A9%E8%88%87) (Wáng Tiānyǔ), [朱祖義](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%A5%96%E7%BE%A9) (Zhū Zǔyì) — Yuán codifiers of Cài Shěn for the new examination system [KR1b0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0026) [KR1b0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0027) [KR1b0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0028) [KR1b0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0029) [KR1b0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0031) [KR1b0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0030) [KR1b0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0032) [KR1b0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0060) [KR1b0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0033) [KR1b0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0034) [KR1b0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0035).

### Topics

The division's principal interpretive axes:

- **The 古文 / 今文 (*gǔwén* / *jīnwén*) controversy and the false Old Text.** The most consequential single problem in *Shū* studies. From the Eastern Jìn through the Yuán, the received *Shàngshū* circulated in 58 chapters comprising the 33 "Modern-script" chapters and 25 putatively "Old-Script" chapters with the *Kǒng zhuàn* — all four of which (chapters, recension, commentary, attribution) Yán Ruòqú demonstrated in [KR1b0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0048) to be an Eastern-Jìn fabrication. Méi Zhuó in [KR1b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0038) anticipated the case by a century and a half; Máo Qílíng in [KR1b0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0049) [KR1b0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0050) mounted the principal counter-attack; Yán Ruòqú prevailed. Wilkinson now warns that the very *gǔwén / jīnwén* labels are themselves a misunderstanding, but the Qīng victory over the false Old Text remains the canonical philological success story of the division.

- **The Cài Shěn settlement.** Cài Shěn's *Shū jīng jízhuàn* [KR1b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0017), composed under Zhū Xī's express deathbed commission, was prescribed as the standard examination *Shū* by the Yuán reform of 1313 and confirmed in the Míng *Dàquán* [KR1b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0037). The bulk of the Yuán production in the division is explicit Cài Shěn subcommentary ([KR1b0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0027) [KR1b0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0029) [KR1b0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0031)) or Cài-Shěn-tested reading ([KR1b0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0026) [KR1b0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0028) [KR1b0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0034)); the late-Míng layer increasingly criticizes him ([KR1b0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0041)); the Qīng imperial compilations ([KR1b0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0045) [KR1b0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0046)) reaffirm him.

- **The *Yǔgòng* 禹貢 sub-tradition.** A single chapter — the schematic geographical survey ascribed to Yǔ — generates a free-standing scholarly genre. Begun in the Sòng by Máo Huàng [KR1b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0008), Chéng Dàchāng [KR1b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0009), and Fù Yín [KR1b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0012), extended by Zhū Hèlíng [KR1b0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0052), and culminating in Hú Wèi's *Yǔgòng zhuīzhǐ* [KR1b0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0053) and Xú Wénjìng's *Yǔgòng huì jiān* [KR1b0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0058). The sub-genre is also the seedbed of premodern Chinese historical geography more broadly; James Legge's separate translation of "The tribute of Yü" (1865) confirms its singular status in nineteenth-century Western reception.

- **The *Hóngfàn* 洪範 sub-tradition.** A second chapter — the "Great Plan" with its Five Phases (*wǔxíng* 五行) and Nine Categories (*jiǔ chóu* 九疇) — generates a parallel cosmological-political sub-genre, beginning with Hú Yuán [KR1b0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0005), extended by Zhào Shànxiāng's *Hóngfàn tǒngyī* [KR1b0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0021), reaching late-Míng cosmological maturity in Huáng Dàozhōu [KR1b0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0044), and pruned of accretion in the Qīng by Hú Wèi [KR1b0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0054).

- **義理 *yìlǐ* vs. textual recovery.** As in the *Yì* division, an opposition between meaning-and-principle reading (Sòng-Yuán Daoxue, culminating in Cài Shěn) and philological textual audit (Méi Zhuó, Yán Ruòqú, Hú Wèi). Unlike the *Yì*, where the textual side recovers the lost Hàn 象數, in the *Shū* the textual side dispatches half the canon as forgery — a decisive rather than recuperative outcome.

- **The Sòng-printed Kǒng Ān'guó *zhuàn* and its philological status.** [KR1b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0002) preserves the recension that Yán Ruòqú impeached; [KR1b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0004) preserves it integrated with Kǒng Yǐngdá's subcommentary and the Qīng evidential overlay. Reading the four together — base text, *Kǒng zhuàn*, *zhèngyì*, *kǎozhèng* — is reading the entire layered history of the *Shū* on one page.

# 詩類 (KR1c)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1c 詩類 *Shī lèi* — Classics — Book of Poetry](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

The 詩類 (*Shī lèi*) is the *jīngbù* 經部 subdivision dedicated to the *Shījīng* 詩經 / *Máoshī* 毛詩 — the 305-poem canon transmitted under the headings *Fēng* 風 (160 *Guófēng* "Airs of the States"), *Yǎ* 雅 (105 *Xiǎo yǎ* + *Dà yǎ* court odes), and *Sòng* 頌 (40 dynastic hymns of Zhōu, Lǔ, and Shāng). The poems themselves span roughly the eleventh through sixth centuries BCE; the received text reached its present form, in the gǔwén 古文 (Ancient Script) recension of [毛亨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E4%BA%A8) and [毛萇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E8%90%87), during the late third century BCE, and was philologically settled under [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) (Zhèng Xuán)'s *jiān* 箋 of 187 CE (Wilkinson, *Chinese History: A New Manual* §28.4.3, §58.6.3.1). Three rival jīnwén 今文 (Modern Script) traditions — the *Lǔ Shī* 魯詩, *Qí Shī* 齊詩, and *Hán Shī* 韓詩 (the *sānjiā shī* 三家詩 of the *Hànshū yìwénzhì* 漢書·藝文志) — atrophied between Late Hàn and Northern Sòng; only the *Hán Shī wài zhuàn* ([KR1c0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0066)) survives as a substantial textual remnant, and the entire Three-Family corpus had to be reconstructed from citations by Qīng scholars such as [范家相](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8C%83%E5%AE%B6%E7%9B%B8).

KR1c therefore divides cleanly into three transmissional phases that any reader must hold in mind: (1) Hàn–Táng *Máo–Zhèng* philological orthodoxy, culminating in the imperially-sponsored *Máoshī zhùshū* 毛詩注疏 ([KR1c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0004)) under [孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94) in 653; (2) Sòng *yìlǐ* 義理 reform centred on [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9)'s *Shī jí zhuàn* ([KR1c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0009) / [KR1c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0015)), which after Yánjǐng 4 (1317) became examination orthodoxy for six centuries; and (3) Qīng *Hànxué* 漢學 reaction, which retrieved the Mao apparatus and the Three-Family fragments against the Cheng-Zhū framework. Wilkinson (§28.4.3) underlines that the work was customarily called simply *Shī* 詩 or *Máoshī* 毛詩 and only infrequently *Shījīng* 詩經; the late-imperial term *Shī jīng* gained currency precisely through Zhū Xī's title-tradition.

### Important texts and text clusters

**Base text and the *Máo–Zhèng–Kǒng* standard**
- *Máoshī (zhèngwén)* 毛詩(正文) [KR1c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0001) — the bare 305-poem Mao recension that every commentary in the division reads.
- *Máoshī* 毛詩 [KR1c0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0002) — the SBCK edition of the Mao recension carrying [毛亨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E4%BA%A8)'s *zhuàn* 傳, [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84)'s *jiān* 箋, and [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E)'s *yīnyì* 音義 (the canonical Hàn–Táng commentarial layer).
- *Máoshī zhùshū* 毛詩注疏 [KR1c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0004) — [孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94)'s *zhèngyì* 正義 of 642–653, the *Wǔjīng zhèngyì* 五經正義 *Shī* volume, the orthodox sub-commentary that froze the Mao reading for a millennium.
- *Shīxù* 詩序 [KR1c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0003) — the *xù* 序 (Great Preface + 305 Small Prefaces), pseudepigraphically ascribed to [卜商](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8D%9C%E5%95%86) (子夏), printed with [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9)'s polemical *Biànshuō* 辨說; the single most contested document in the division.

**The Three-Family (*sānjiā shī*) line**
- *Hán Shī wài zhuàn* 韓詩外傳 [KR1c0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0066) — by [韓嬰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%93%E5%AC%B0) (c. 180–130 BCE), the only substantially-extant pre-Mao tradition, preserving the *Hán Shī*'s exegetical and exemplum apparatus.
- *Sān jiā Shī shí yí* 三家詩拾遺 [KR1c0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0062) — [范家相](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8C%83%E5%AE%B6%E7%9B%B8)'s 1760 reconstruction of the *Lǔ*, *Qí*, and *Hán* fragments from cross-citations.

**Northern Sòng reformist exegesis**
- *Shī běnyì* 詩本義 [KR1c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0008) — [歐陽修](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%90%E9%99%BD%E4%BF%AE)'s 1050s opening of the "doubt the Hàn" tradition: the first sustained critique of Máo and Zhèng readings on textual grounds.
- *Sūshì shī jí zhuàn* 蘇氏詩集傳 [KR1c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0010) — [蘇轍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BD%8D)'s independent collected commentary, a key step between Ōuyáng Xiū and Zhū Xī.
- *Máoshī míngwù jiě* 毛詩名物解 [KR1c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0011) — [蔡卞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E5%8D%9E)'s expansion of the natural-history tradition first set out by Lù Jī.

**The Zhū Xī cluster — the watershed**
- *Shī jí zhuàn* 詩集傳 [KR1c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0009) (SBCK, 20 *juǎn*) / *Shī jīng jí zhuàn* 詩經集傳 [KR1c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0015) (WYG, 8 *juǎn*) — [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9)'s epoch-defining commentary in its two surviving editorial divisions; identical text. Its rejection of the *xù*, its identification of seven "licentious airs" (*yín fēng* 淫風) in *Zhèng* and *Wèi*, and its systematic *bǐ–xìng–fù* 比興賦 reading-method governed *Shī* reception from the Yuán to 1905.
- *Shī tóngzǐ wèn* 詩童子問 [KR1c0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0021) — Zhū Xī's direct disciple [輔廣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%BC%94%E5%BB%A3)'s catechetical exposition of the *jí zhuàn*.
- *Shī zhuàn yíshuō* 詩傳遺說 [KR1c0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0024) — Zhū Xī's grandson [朱鑑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E9%91%91)'s collection of Zhū's *yǔlù* 語錄 remarks on the *Shī*, the principal record of his oral teaching.

**The Lǚ school: Sòng *xù*-defending exegesis**
- *Lǚshì jiāshú dú Shī jì* 呂氏家塾讀詩記 [KR1c0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0017) — [呂祖謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E7%A5%96%E8%AC%99)'s deferential reading, the principal Sòng survival of the *zōng xù* 宗序 (preface-following) position, and the work whose conservatism Yáng Shèn credited with provoking Zhū Xī's late anti-*xù* shift.
- *Xù Lǚshì jiāshú dú Shī jì* 續呂氏家塾讀詩記 [KR1c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0018) — [戴溪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%B4%E6%BA%AA)'s continuation.
- *Cíhú Shī zhuàn* 慈湖詩傳 [KR1c0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0016) — [楊簡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E7%B0%A1)'s Lù Wáng *xīnxué* 心學 reading; a minority voice but the only Sòng-Yuán *Shī* commentary committed to the Lù school programme.

**The Sòng synthesis: bridging Hàn and Sòng readings**
- *Shī jí* 詩緝 [KR1c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0023) — [嚴粲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9A%B4%E7%B2%B2)'s mid-thirteenth-century combination of *Máo–Zhèng* glosses with Zhū Xī's framework; widely judged by Qīng reviewers (cf. the *Sìkù tíyào*) the best balanced Sòng commentary.

**The Wáng Yīnglín antiquarian line**
- *Shī kǎo* 詩考 [KR1c0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0025) — [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F)'s late-Sòng reconstruction of *Lǔ*, *Qí*, and *Hán* fragments from pre-Tang citations; the prototype for Qīng *sānjiā shī* scholarship.
- *Shī dìlǐ kǎo* 詩地理考 [KR1c0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0026) — Wáng's parallel geographical concordance, locating the place names in the *Guófēng*.

**Yuán *jí zhuàn* tradition and Míng imperial codification**
- *Shī jí zhuàn míngwù chāo* 詩集傳名物鈔 [KR1c0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0027) — [許謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E8%AC%99)'s natural-history supplement to Zhū Xī.
- *Shī zhuàn tōngshì* 詩傳通釋 [KR1c0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0028) — [劉瑾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E7%91%BE)'s comprehensive Yuán sub-commentary on the *jí zhuàn*.
- *Shījīng shūyì huìtōng* 詩經疏義會通 [KR1c0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0030) — [朱公遷](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%85%AC%E9%81%B7)'s Yuán-Míng synthesis.
- *Shī zhuàn dàquán* 詩傳大全 [KR1c0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0035) — [胡廣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E5%BB%A3)'s 1414–1415 imperial *Yǒnglè* compilation that codified the *jí zhuàn* as exam orthodoxy.

**Late Míng natural-history scholarship**
- *Lùshì Shī shū guǎngyào* 陸氏詩疏廣要 [KR1c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0006) — [毛晉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E6%99%89)'s 1620s–1650s expansion of Lù Jī's third-century *cǎomù niǎoshòu chóngyú shū* 草木鳥獸蟲魚疏.
- *Liù jiā Shī míngwù shū* 六家詩名物疏 [KR1c0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0039) — [馮復京](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AE%E5%BE%A9%E4%BA%AC)'s six-school synthesis of the names-of-things tradition.

**Qīng Hànxué reaction and reconstruction**
- *Máoshī jī gǔ biān* 毛詩稽古編 [KR1c0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0049) — [陳啟源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%95%9F%E6%BA%90)'s 1687 *Hànxué* manifesto: a chapter-by-chapter retrieval of *Máo–Zhèng* readings against Zhū Xī.
- *Shī jīng tōng yì* 詩經通義 [KR1c0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0048) — [朱鶴齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E9%B6%B4%E9%BD%A1)'s early-Qīng critical commentary, an important precursor to *Hànxué*.
- *Shī jīng bài shū* 詩經稗疏 [KR1c0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0047) — [王夫之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A4%AB%E4%B9%8B)'s philosophically charged Ming-loyalist reading.
- The [毛奇齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E5%A5%87%E9%BD%A1) tetralogy: *Máo Shī xiě guān jì* 毛詩寫官記 [KR1c0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0051), *Shī zhá* 詩札 [KR1c0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0052), *Shī zhuàn Shī shuō bó yì* 詩傳詩說駁義 [KR1c0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0053), *Xù Shī zhuàn niǎo míng juǎn* 續詩傳鳥名卷 [KR1c0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0054) — the most aggressive Qīng polemic against the *jí zhuàn* tradition.

**Imperially-sponsored Qīng compendia**
- *Qīndìng Shījīng zhuànshuō huìzuǎn* 欽定詩經傳說彙纂 [KR1c0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0044) — [王鴻緒](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%B4%BB%E7%B7%92)'s 1721–1727 Kāngxī-era compendium that gives *jí zhuàn* primacy but appends the *xù*-tradition readings.
- *Yùzuǎn Shīyì zhézhōng* 御纂詩義折中 [KR1c0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0045) — [傅恒](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%82%85%E6%81%92)'s 1755 Qiánlóng-era follow-up, the official Qīng "middle way" between Hàn and Sòng.

**The late-Qīng settlement**
- *Yúdōng xuéshī* 虞東學詩 [KR1c0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0065) — [顧鎮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E9%8E%AE)'s mediating position: only the opening line of each *xù* is genuine, which became the standard balanced view by the Qiánlóng–Jiāqìng generation.

### Important persons

- [毛亨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E4%BA%A8) (Máo Hēng) — the *Dà Máo gōng* 大毛公, founder of the gǔwén Mao recension whose tradition became the unique received form.
- [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) (Zhèng Xuán, 127–200) — Hàn *jiān* 箋 of 187 CE, the second textual layer that defined *Shī* reading until Zhū Xī.
- [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) (Lù Démíng, 556–627) — *Jīngdiǎn shìwén* 經典釋文 phonological glossing; the principal source for Hàn pronunciations of the *Shī*.
- [孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94) (Kǒng Yǐngdá, 574–648) — chief editor of the *Wǔjīng zhèngyì* and so of the standard *Shī* sub-commentary [KR1c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0004).
- [陸璣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E7%92%A3) (Lù Jī, 3rd century) — author of the prototypical natural-history sub-commentary *Máoshī cǎomù niǎoshòu chóngyú shū* [KR1c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0005), the origin of the *míngwù* 名物 line.
- [歐陽修](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%90%E9%99%BD%E4%BF%AE) (Ōuyáng Xiū, 1007–1072) — opened the Sòng "doubt-Hàn" turn with [KR1c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0008).
- [蘇轍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BD%8D) (Sū Zhé, 1039–1112) — Northern Sòng *jí zhuàn*-style synthesizer.
- [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) (Zhū Xī, 1130–1200) — author of the watershed *Shī jí zhuàn*; defines the division's second half.
- [呂祖謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E7%A5%96%E8%AC%99) (Lǚ Zǔqiān, 1137–1181) — leading *zōng xù* voice and Zhū Xī's principal Sòng interlocutor on the *Shī*.
- [嚴粲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9A%B4%E7%B2%B2) (Yán Càn, *fl.* 1248) — Hàn–Sòng bridge commentator.
- [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) (Wáng Yīnglín, 1223–1296) — antiquarian whose *Shī kǎo* and *Shī dìlǐ kǎo* founded the Three-Family fragment- and geography-recovery traditions.
- [胡廣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E5%BB%A3) (Hú Guǎng, 1370–1418) — chief editor of the *Shī zhuàn dàquán*, the channel through which Zhū Xī's commentary entered the examination system.
- [陳啟源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%95%9F%E6%BA%90) (Chén Qǐyuán, d. 1689) — Qīng *Hànxué* programmatic restoration of the Mao reading.
- [毛奇齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E5%A5%87%E9%BD%A1) (Máo Qílíng, 1623–1716) — most prolific Qīng polemicist against the *jí zhuàn*.
- [王夫之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A4%AB%E4%B9%8B) (Wáng Fūzhī, 1619–1692) — Ming-loyalist philosophical reader of the *Shī*.
- [范家相](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8C%83%E5%AE%B6%E7%9B%B8) (Fàn Jiāxiàng) — author of the two principal Qiánlóng-era *Shī* reconstructions [KR1c0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0062) and [KR1c0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0063).
- [顧鎮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E9%8E%AE) (Gù Zhèn, 1718–1792) — formulator of the late-Qīng *xù*-mediation position.
- [毛晉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E6%99%89) (Máo Jìn, 1599–1659) — late-Míng publisher and natural-history compiler.

### Topics

- **The Mao *xù* 序 question.** The genuineness of the *Great Preface* and the 305 *Small Prefaces* is the single axis around which the division organizes itself. The Hàn–Táng *Máo–Zhèng–Kǒng* line treats them as Confucian-school transmissions; Zhū Xī ([KR1c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0009) / [KR1c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0015)) treats them as Hàn-period allegoresis to be jettisoned; the *Hànxué* revival ([KR1c0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0049)) reasserts them; the late-Qīng mediating position ([KR1c0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0065)) accepts only the opening sentence of each. Every Sòng-onward commentary in KR1c can be placed on this axis.
- **The Three-Family vs. Mao transmissional puzzle.** Why did the gǔwén *Máoshī* alone survive while the three court-supported jīnwén traditions disappeared? The recovery of the *sānjiā shī* from citation fragments (Wáng Yīnglín's [KR1c0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0025) as prototype, Fàn Jiāxiàng's [KR1c0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0062) as the major Qīng synthesis) is one of the principal antiquarian projects of the division.
- **The "licentious airs" (*yín fēng* 淫風) problem.** Zhū Xī's reading of certain *Guófēng* poems — especially in *Zhèng* 鄭 and *Wèi* 衛 — as ordinary love-songs rather than political allegory triggered both Yuán-Míng moral debate and Qīng *Hànxué* rejection. Cf. [KR1c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0009) for the original move; [KR1c0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0049) for the Qīng counter-argument.
- **Bǐ–Xìng–Fù 比興賦 trope-analysis.** Zhū Xī's systematic classification of each ode as *bǐ* (comparison), *xìng* (evocation), or *fù* (direct narration) — adopted from the *Zhōuli* *liù yì* 六義 scheme — became the standard analytic framework from the Yuán onward and is the principal poetological framework of the division.
- **The *míngwù* 名物 (names of things) tradition.** A continuous natural-history line from [陸璣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E7%92%A3)'s third-century *cǎomù niǎoshòu chóngyú shū* [KR1c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0005) through [毛晉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E6%99%89)'s expansion [KR1c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0006), [許謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E8%AC%99)'s [KR1c0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0027), [馮復京](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AE%E5%BE%A9%E4%BA%AC)'s six-school synthesis [KR1c0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0039), and the cluster of Qīng natural-history works ([KR1c0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0054), [KR1c0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0055), [KR1c0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0056), [KR1c0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0060)) identifies the plants, birds, animals, insects, fish, and material objects named in the poems.
- **Geographical and historical contextualization.** Wáng Yīnglín's *Shī dìlǐ kǎo* [KR1c0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0026) inaugurated and [顧棟高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E6%A3%9F%E9%AB%98)'s *Máo Shī lèi shì* [KR1c0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0060) consolidated the project of locating the *Guófēng* in concrete Zhōu geography and the *Yǎ* in concrete dynastic events.
- **Examination orthodoxy and its discontents.** After 1317 Zhū Xī's *jí zhuàn* became compulsory for examination candidates; this institutional fact gave rise to a vast Yuán–Míng exegetical apparatus ([KR1c0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0028), [KR1c0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0030), [KR1c0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0035)), and structured the Qīng reaction as well — the imperial *huìzuǎn* ([KR1c0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0044)) and *zhézhōng* ([KR1c0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0045)) attempting to subordinate the *jí zhuàn* to a broader synthesis without dethroning it.
- **The Hàn–Sòng polemic in its mature Qīng form.** From [陳啟源](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%95%9F%E6%BA%90)'s 1687 *Máoshī jī gǔ biān* [KR1c0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0049) to [毛奇齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E5%A5%87%E9%BD%A1)'s polemical tetralogy [KR1c0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0051)–[KR1c0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0054), the eighteenth century reframed the entire history of *Shī* commentary as a contest between Hàn (philological, *xù*-following) and Sòng (philosophical, *xù*-rejecting) reading practices — a framing partly imposed retroactively and partly faithful to the textual record.

# 禮類 (KR1d)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1d 禮類 *Lǐ lèi* — Classics — Rituals](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR1d 禮類 (*Lǐ lèi*, "Rituals") is the ritual section of the Classics branch (*jīngbù* 經部, KR1) of the *Sìkù quánshū* fourfold scheme. The division collects the three canonical ritual classics — *Zhōulǐ* 周禮 [KR1d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0001), *Yílǐ* 儀禮 [KR1d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0025), *Lǐjì* 禮記 [KR1d0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0052) — together with their pre-modern commentaries, sub-commentaries, abridgements, and topical recastings, and a sizeable terminal cluster of synthesizing *Sānlǐ* compendia, *zōnglèi* 總類 reference works (illustrated diagrams, mourning encyclopedias, the *Wǔlǐ tōngkǎo*), and the practical-ritual / family-ritual manuals that descend from Sīmǎ Guāng's *Shūyí* [KR1d0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0088) and Zhū Xī's *Jiālǐ* [KR1d0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0089). The 92 texts span from a pair of pre-Hàn / Western-Hàn canonical recensions (the three *jīng* themselves and the *Dà-Dài Lǐjì* [KR1d0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0076)) through the great Eastern-Hàn / Táng layered editions of Zhèng Xuán 鄭玄 and Jiǎ Gōngyàn 賈公彥 / Kǒng Yǐngdá 孔穎達 (mid-7th c.), Northern-Sòng reformist re-readings (Wáng Ānshí's *Zhōuguān xīnyì* [KR1d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0004)), Southern-Sòng / Yuán scholastic compendia (Wèi Shí 衞湜 *Lǐjì jíshuō* [KR1d0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0057); Chén Hào 陳澔 *Lǐjì jíshuō* [KR1d0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0059); the ambitious *Yílǐ jīngzhuàn tōngjiě* [KR1d0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0085) of Zhū Xī and his school), and the high-Qīng evidential / imperial flowering (the three *Qīndìng yìshū* [KR1d0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0018), [KR1d0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0037), [KR1d0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0068) of the Qiánlóng court; Qín Huìtián's 262-juan *Wǔlǐ tōngkǎo* [KR1d0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0087)).

The reader must keep three structural facts in mind. First, the three canonical classics are heterogeneous in genre — the *Zhōulǐ* is an idealised bureaucratic blueprint, the *Yílǐ* a manual of ceremonial procedure, the *Lǐjì* a heterogeneous Confucian-school anthology — and were welded into a unitary *Sānlǐ* 三禮 corpus only retrospectively, by Zhèng Xuán in the late 2nd c. CE (Wilkinson §28.4.3). Second, the *Zhōulǐ* was the principal Old-Text classic (*gǔwén* 古文) of the late Western Hàn and remained controversial throughout the imperial period: Wáng Ānshí used it as the constitutional grounding for the Xīnfǎ 新法 reforms, Kāng Yǒuwéi reignited the *jīnwén/gǔwén* dispute in 1891 with the claim that it was a Liú Xīn forgery, and Qīng evidential scholars devoted disproportionate energy to its philology (Wilkinson §28.7). Third, the *Lǐjì* is the only ritual classic whose materials migrated outside the corpus: its *Dàxué* 大學 and *Zhōngyōng* 中庸 chapters were extracted by the Chéng brothers and Zhū Xī to form half of the *Sì shū* 四書 (Wilkinson §28.4.4), which means that the per-text notes here cover only the *Lǐjì* qua ritual canon and its commentaries; the *Sì shū* literature on *Dàxué* and *Zhōngyōng* sits in KR1g.

### Important texts and text clusters

The principal works fall into four clusters plus a terminal compendium cluster.

**The *Zhōulǐ* cluster ([KR1d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0001)–0024).** *Zhōulǐ* 周禮 [KR1d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0001), the canonical text, anchors the cluster as the foundational idealised-bureaucracy classic in six "ministries" (*liù guān* 六官) corresponding to the seasons, with the lost *Dōngguān* 冬官 supplied by the artisanal *Kǎogōngjì* 考工記. *Zhōulǐ zhùshū* 周禮注疏 [KR1d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0003) is the standard layered edition combining Zhèng Xuán's Eastern-Hàn annotation, Jiǎ Gōngyàn's Táng sub-commentary, and Lù Démíng's *yīnyì* — one of the cornerstones of the *Shísān jīng zhùshū*. *Zhōuguān xīnyì* 周官新義 [KR1d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0004) is the *locus classicus* of Wáng Ānshí's politically charged Xīnfǎ reading of the classic. *Zhōulǐ dìngyì* 周禮訂義 [KR1d0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0010) of Wáng Yǔzhī 王與之 is the largest Sòng *Zhōulǐ* compendium (80 juan), preserving the bulk of mid-Sòng commentarial opinion. *Qīndìng Zhōuguān yìshū* 欽定周官義疏 [KR1d0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0018) is the Qiánlóng court's official synthesis. *Zhōulǐ yíyì jǔyào* 周禮疑義舉要 [KR1d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0024) of Jiāng Yǒng 江永 is the most acute mid-Qīng evidential treatment of textual cruces.

**The *Yílǐ* cluster ([KR1d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0025)–0051).** *Yílǐ* 儀禮 [KR1d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0025), the canonical text in 17 *piān*, is the principal pre-Hàn source for actual ceremonial procedure (capping, marriage, archery, sacrifice, mourning); under the original short title *Lǐ* 禮 it was the only one of the three classics included in the Hàn *Wǔ jīng* (Wilkinson §28.4.3). *Yílǐ zhùshū* 儀禮注疏 [KR1d0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0028) is the parallel Zhèng-Jiǎ-Lù layered edition. *Yílǐ jíshuō* 儀禮集說 [KR1d0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0035) of Áo Jìgōng 敖繼公 is the most influential Yuán revisionist re-reading, displacing portions of the Zhèng commentary. *Yílǐ Zhèngzhù jùdòu* 儀禮鄭註句讀 [KR1d0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0038) of Zhāng Ěrqí 張爾岐 reopened the *Yílǐ* for early-Qīng study after generations of neglect, with Gù Yánwǔ 顧炎武's high praise. *Qīndìng Yílǐ yìshū* 欽定儀禮義疏 [KR1d0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0037) and *Yílǐ jíbiān* 儀禮集編 [KR1d0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0049) of Shèng Shìzuǒ 盛世佐 are the great mid-Qīng synthetic editions. *Dúlǐ tōngkǎo* 讀禮通考 [KR1d0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0051) of Xú Qiánxué 徐乾學, a 120-juan encyclopedia of mourning ritual (*xiōnglǐ* 凶禮) organised around the *Yílǐ Sāngfú* 喪服 chapter, is the principal Qīng-period work on the largest specialised ritual category and the seed from which Qín Huìtián's later *Wǔlǐ tōngkǎo* grew.

**The *Lǐjì* cluster ([KR1d0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0052)–0075).** *Lǐjì* 禮記 [KR1d0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0052), the Xiǎo Dài 小戴 49-chapter recension, is one of the *Wǔ jīng* and the largest of the three ritual classics. *Lǐjì zhùshū* 禮記注疏 [KR1d0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0053) is the Zhèng-Kǒng-Lù layered edition; *Lǐjì zhèngyì cán* 禮記正義殘 [KR1d0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0061) preserves a fragmentary witness to the early state of Kǒng Yǐngdá's sub-commentary. *Lǐjì jíshuō* 禮記集說 [KR1d0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0057) of Wèi Shí 衞湜 in 160 juan is the largest Sòng-period *Lǐjì* compendium and an indispensable witness to lost Sòng commentary. *Lǐjì jíshuō* 禮記集說 [KR1d0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0059) of Chén Hào 陳澔 (1322) is the work that displaced all others: it became the official examination textbook on the *Lǐjì* from the Yuán to the end of the Qīng. *Lǐjì dàquán* 禮記大全 [KR1d0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0060) is the Yǒnglè-era Hú Guǎng 胡廣 compilation, one of the three *Dàquán* shoring up the Sòng-Yuán Chéng-Zhū orthodoxy. The five thematic monographs of Huáng Dàozhōu 黃道周 — *Yuèlìng míngyì* [KR1d0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0062), *Biǎojì jízhuàn* [KR1d0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0063), *Fāngjì jízhuàn* [KR1d0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0064), *Zīyī jízhuàn* [KR1d0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0065), *Rúxíng jízhuàn* [KR1d0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0066) — form a self-contained late-Míng project on individual *Lǐjì* chapters. *Qīndìng Lǐjì yìshū* 欽定禮記義疏 [KR1d0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0068) completes the imperial *Sānlǐ* trilogy.

**The *Dà-Dài* and *Sānlǐ* studies cluster ([KR1d0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0076)–0083).** *Dà-Dài Lǐjì* 大戴禮記 [KR1d0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0076) of Dài Dé 戴德, the parallel ritual-records anthology that survives only in fragments (39 *piān* out of an original 85), is the indispensable secondary witness to Western Hàn ritual literature. *Xià xiǎo zhèng Dàishì zhuàn* 夏小正戴氏傳 [KR1d0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0077) of Fù Sōngqīng 傅崧卿 isolates the *Xià xiǎo zhèng* (the earliest agrarian calendar) embedded in the *Dà-Dài*. *Sānlǐ tú jízhù* 三禮圖集注 [KR1d0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0078) of Niè Chóngyì 聶崇義 (Northern Sòng) is the standard illustrated companion to the three classics. *Xuélǐ zhíyí* 學禮質疑 [KR1d0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0080) of Wàn Sīdà 萬斯大 inaugurates the Qīng evidential critique of received ritual interpretation.

**The terminal Sānlǐ-compendium and family-ritual cluster ([KR1d0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0084)–0092).** Three Sòng-Qīng "great syntheses" frame the division: *Lǐshū* 禮書 [KR1d0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0084) of Chén Xiángdào 陳祥道 (Sòng, 150 juan); *Yílǐ jīngzhuàn tōngjiě* 儀禮經傳通解 [KR1d0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0085) of Zhū Xī 朱熹 and his disciples Huáng Gàn 黃榦 and Yáng Fù 楊復 (66-juan combined recension, organised topically — the most ambitious *Sānlǐ* re-edition of pre-modern China); and *Wǔlǐ tōngkǎo* 五禮通考 [KR1d0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0087) of Qín Huìtián 秦蕙田 (Qīng, 262 juan) — the largest single ritual compendium ever produced, covering all five *wǔlǐ* 五禮 categories. *Lǐshū gāngmù* 禮書綱目 [KR1d0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0086) of Jiāng Yǒng is its mid-Qīng companion. The family-ritual sub-cluster — *Shūyí* 書儀 [KR1d0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0088) of Sīmǎ Guāng 司馬光, *Jiālǐ* 家禮 [KR1d0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0089) of Zhū Xī (massively influential throughout East Asia, including Korea and Japan; Wilkinson §7.8.1), *Tàiquán xiānglǐ* [KR1d0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0090), *Zhūzǐ lǐzuǎn* [KR1d0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0091), and *Biàndìng jìlǐ tōngsú pǔ* [KR1d0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0092) — extends the canonical ritual tradition into the lived domain of the literati household.

### Topics

- **The formation of the *Sānlǐ* corpus.** The three classics were welded together by Zhèng Xuán's late-Eastern-Hàn unified annotation, before which the canonical *Lǐ* was the *Yílǐ* alone (under the Hàn name *Shìlǐ* 士禮; Wilkinson §28.4.3). The cluster organisation of KR1d — first *Zhōulǐ*, then *Yílǐ*, then *Lǐjì*, finally synthesising compendia — reproduces Zhèng's hierarchy, not the historical order of the texts.
- **Ancient Script vs. Current Script in ritual scholarship.** The *Zhōulǐ* is the principal *gǔwén* 古文 classic in the Old-Text / New-Text controversy (Wilkinson §28.7.1), surfacing in the Western Hàn under Liú Xīn's sponsorship and never accepted by Current-Script court orthodoxy until the post-Hàn period. Kāng Yǒuwéi's late-Qīng claim that the *Zhōulǐ* was a Liú Xīn forgery is the modern terminus of this debate, rejected by mainstream twentieth-century scholarship but still informing readings of the text.
- **The political *Zhōulǐ*.** From Wáng Mǎng 王莽 (whose institutional programme was *Zhōulǐ*-based) through Wáng Ānshí [KR1d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0004) to the Tàipíng Tiānguó, the *Zhōulǐ* repeatedly functioned as a reform constitution. The Sòng-Qīng *Zhōulǐ* commentaries in this division — particularly [KR1d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0004), [KR1d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0005), [KR1d0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0009), [KR1d0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0010) — should be read against this political-canonical backdrop (Elman and Kern, eds., *Statecraft and Classical Learning*, 2010; Wilkinson §58.6.3.1).
- **Procedure (*Yílǐ*) versus essay (*Lǐjì*) — and the imperial preference.** The *Yílǐ* presents itself as a sequence of step-by-step procedural scripts; the *Lǐjì* as a discursive Confucian-school anthology. The fortunes of the two diverged sharply at Yuán-Míng: the *Lǐjì* became central to the examination curriculum via Chén Hào's [KR1d0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0059), while the *Yílǐ* sank into relative neglect until Zhāng Ěrqí [KR1d0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0038) revived it in the Kāngxī era.
- **Dài Dé vs. Dài Shèng.** The Western Hàn produced two parallel Confucian-ritual anthologies under the same family-name lineage — the *Dà-Dài Lǐjì* [KR1d0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0076) (Dài Dé, the elder) and the canonical *Xiǎo Dài Lǐjì* [KR1d0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0052) (Dài Shèng, the younger). The *Xiǎo Dài* version was canonised; the *Dà-Dài* version survives in fragmentary state. The relationship between the two is the principal philological problem of pre-canonical Hàn ritual literature.
- **The 五禮 (Wǔlǐ) typology.** From the post-Hàn ritual codes onward, the canonical typology *jí lǐ* 吉禮 / *xiōng lǐ* 凶禮 / *jūn lǐ* 軍禮 / *bīn lǐ* 賓禮 / *jiā lǐ* 嘉禮 organises imperial ritual programmes. The terminal compendia [KR1d0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0086), [KR1d0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0087) follow this typology; the mourning-only [KR1d0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0051) treats one of the five.
- **Family ritual and the literati household.** Sīmǎ Guāng's *Shūyí* [KR1d0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0088) and Zhū Xī's *Jiālǐ* [KR1d0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0089) founded a parallel tradition of household-scale ritual codification that became the de facto practical norm of literati life through the Yuán, Míng, and Qīng, and exported to Korean and Japanese Neo-Confucian households (Wilkinson §7.8.1).
- **The 月令 (Monthly Ordinances) sub-tradition.** The *Yuèlìng* chapter of the *Lǐjì*, with its cosmological correlation of months, colours, sounds, and ritual obligations, generated its own commentarial micro-tradition — *Yuèlìng jiě* [KR1d0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0056) (Zhāng Xí), *Yuèlìng míngyì* [KR1d0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0062) (Huáng Dàozhōu).
- **Qiánlóng imperial codification.** The three *Qīndìng yìshū* [KR1d0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0018), [KR1d0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0037), [KR1d0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0068), all dated to 1736–1748, are the high-water mark of imperial ritual-classics standardisation and the proximate model for Qín Huìtián's [KR1d0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1d/KR1d0087) synthesis.

# 春秋類 (KR1e)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1e 春秋類 *Chūnqiū lèi* — Classics — Spring and Autumn Annals](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR1e 春秋類 (*Chūnqiū lèi*, "Spring and Autumn Annals") is the *Chūnqiū*-classics section of the Classics branch (*jīngbù* 經部, KR1) of the *Sìkù quánshū* fourfold scheme. The division collects the canonical *Chūnqiū* 春秋 itself, its three transmitted commentaries — *Zuǒzhuàn* 左傳, *Gōngyáng zhuàn* 公羊傳, *Gǔliáng zhuàn* 穀梁傳 (the *Sānzhuàn* 三傳) — and the entire received corpus of pre-modern exegesis, sub-commentary, polemic, topical reorganisation, calendrical and prosopographical reference works built around them. The 121 per-text notes in this directory span from a Western-Hàn standalone canonical text ([KR1e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0001)) through the foundational Hàn-Jìn-Táng combined editions (Dù Yù 杜預, Hé Xiū 何休, Fàn Níng 范甯, Kǒng Yǐngdá 孔穎達), the Táng *Dàn–Zhào–Lù* 啖–趙–陸 radical revival, the Northern-Sòng *xīnyì* 新義 movement and Hú Ānguó's 胡安國 Southern-Sòng *Chūnqiū zhuàn* 春秋傳, the late-Sòng / Yuán radical-sceptical commentaries of Cuī Zǐfāng 崔子方, Chéng Duānxué 程端學 and Zhào Fǎng 趙汸, the Míng *xìnjīng bùxìnzhuàn* 信經不信傳 reaction culminating in Lù Càn 陸粲 and the Dōnglín 東林 commentators, the Qīng imperial trilogy of Kāngxī and Qiánlóng, and the high-Qīng evidential summa of Gù Yánwǔ 顧炎武, Gù Dònggāo 顧棟高, Huì Dòng 惠棟 and Jiāng Yǒng 江永.

The reader must keep four structural facts in mind. First, the *Chūnqiū* itself is a 17,000-character court chronicle of the state of Lǔ 魯 covering 722–481 BCE; for nearly 2,400 years most readers held it to have been edited by Confucius so as to convey his "lofty principles in subtle words" (*wēiyán dàyì* 微言大義) (Wilkinson §48.1.1), and almost every commentary in this division is a position taken in the resulting hermeneutic — whether the *jīng* really transmits hidden *bāobiǎn* 褒貶 (praise-and-blame) judgements, and if so, by what regulatory keys. Second, the three commentaries are radically different in character: the *Gōngyáng* and *Gǔliáng* are short *bāobiǎn*-driven catechisms in question-and-answer form, while the *Zuǒzhuàn* — over ten times their combined length — is a fully-narrative pre-Hàn historical work that was attached to the *Chūnqiū* as commentary only secondarily, and is "the prime source on the entire period" (Wilkinson §48.1.1.1). Much of the division's history is the long oscillation between *Zuǒ*-primary historiographical reading and *Gōngyáng*/*Gǔliáng*-primary moral-hermeneutic reading. Third, the integrated *Sānzhuàn* edition with all three commentaries interlinear with the *Chūnqiū* is a Northern-Sòng product, and the standard *Shísān jīng zhùshū* 十三經注疏 form in which it is now read dates only from 1815 (Wilkinson §48.1.1.1); the foundational layered editions in this division ([KR1e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0004), [KR1e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0006), [KR1e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0010)) descend from this stratification. Fourth, after Hú Ānguó's *Chūnqiū zhuàn* [KR1e0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0036) was made the official examination commentary in 1313 (and reaffirmed in the 1415 *Wǔjīng dàquán* 五經大全 [KR1e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0074)), it remained the orthodox state textbook for nearly six centuries, and a great many entries from the Yuán onward are best read as either elaborations of, or polemical attacks on, the Hú-school orthodoxy.

### Important texts and text clusters

The principal works fall into eleven clusters.

**The canonical text and Hàn-Jìn-Táng *Sānzhuàn* ([KR1e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0001)–0011, plus [KR1e0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0122)).** *Chūnqiū Zuǒzhuàn (zhèngwén)* 春秋左傳(正文) [KR1e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0001) is a standalone canonical edition of the *jīng* + *Zuǒ* without commentary. *Chūnqiū jīngzhuàn jíjiě* 春秋經傳集解 [KR1e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0002), composed by Dù Yù 杜預 in semi-retirement after the Jìn conquest of Wú in 280, is the foundational edition that combined the *Chūnqiū* and *Zuǒzhuàn* into a single integrated text — the move that made Dù Yù's reading the default *Zuǒ* tradition for the next 1,700 years; *Chūnqiū shìlì* 春秋釋例 [KR1e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0012) is its systematic counterpart organised around Dù Yù's theory of the fifty *fán* 凡 (regulatory items). *Chūnqiū zhèngyì* 春秋正義 [KR1e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0003) is Kǒng Yǐngdá's 孔穎達 official Táng sub-commentary, and *Chūnqiū Zuǒzhuàn zhùshū* 春秋左傳注疏 [KR1e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0004) is the resulting layered Dù-Kǒng-Lù edition. The parallel *Gōngyáng* and *Gǔliáng* layered editions are *Chūnqiū Gōngyáng zhuàn zhùshū* 春秋公羊傳注疏 [KR1e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0006) (Hé Xiū 何休's *Jiě gǔ* 解詁 + Xú Yàn 徐彥's Táng sub-commentary) and *Chūnqiū Gǔliáng zhùshū* 春秋穀梁注疏 [KR1e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0010) (Fàn Níng 范甯's *Jí jiě* + Yáng Shìxūn 楊士勛's Táng sub-commentary). *Chūnqiū Gōngyáng jīngzhuàn jiěgǔ* 春秋公羊經傳解詁 [KR1e0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0007) is the standalone Hé Xiū work, fruit of seventeen years' labour and the polemical centre of Hàn *Gōngyáng* learning. *Zhēn gāohuāng* 箴膏肓 [KR1e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0011) preserves Zhèng Xuán's 鄭玄 rebuttal of Hé Xiū in the long Hàn dispute over the relative authority of the three commentaries. *Chūnqiū fánlù* 春秋繁露 [KR1e0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0122) of Dǒng Zhòngshū 董仲舒 is the Western-Hàn *Gōngyáng*-school cosmological treatise that grafted *yīnyáng wǔxíng* onto Confucian moral-political thought — the indispensable Hàn-period theoretical companion to the *Gōngyáng* tradition, even though the received text contains layers down to the Sòng.

**The Táng *Dàn–Zhào–Lù* radical school ([KR1e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0013)–0015).** Lù Chún's 陸淳 trilogy — *Chūnqiū jízhuàn zuǎn lì* 春秋集傳纂例 [KR1e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0013), *Chūnqiū jízhuàn wēizhǐ* 春秋集傳微旨 [KR1e0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0014), *Chūnqiū jízhuàn biànyí* 春秋集傳辨疑 [KR1e0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0015) — transmits the lost teachings of Dàn Zhù 啖助 and Zhào Kuāng 趙匡, the mid-Táng founders of the *Chūnqiū* "rejection-of-the-three-commentaries" tradition. The trilogy is the proximate methodological ancestor of the entire Northern-Sòng *xīnyì* movement; its *biànyí* is the polemical charge against the *Sānzhuàn* and the *zuǎn lì* the constructive replacement.

**Northern-Sòng *xīnyì* and ritual / regulatory commentaries ([KR1e0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0017)–0024, 0028–0031).** The cluster opens with Sūn Fù's 孫復 *Chūnqiū zūnwáng fāwēi* 春秋尊王發微 [KR1e0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0018), whose *yǒubiǎn wúbāo* 有貶無褒 doctrine — Confucius criticises but never praises — set the radical-rigorist tone of the whole. *Chūnqiū huánggāng lùn* 春秋皇綱論 [KR1e0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0019) of Wáng Xī 王晳 stands almost alone in resisting both Sūn Fù's rigorism and the Dàn Zhào tendency. Liú Chǎng's 劉敞 four-work programme — *Chūnqiū quánhéng* 春秋權衡 [KR1e0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0021), *Liúshì Chūnqiū zhuàn* 劉氏春秋傳 [KR1e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0022), *Liúshì Chūnqiū yìlín* 劉氏春秋意林 [KR1e0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0023), *Chūnqiū chuánshuō lì* 春秋傳說例 [KR1e0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0024) — is the methodologically most rigorous Northern-Sòng *xīnyì* corpus, anchored in classical ritual. Cuī Zǐfāng's 崔子方 *Cuīshì Chūnqiū jīngjiě* 崔氏春秋經解 [KR1e0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0028) and *Chūnqiū běnlì* 春秋本例 [KR1e0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0029) developed the distinctive *rìyuè lì* 日月例 (day-month item) theory — that the calendrical detail of each *Chūnqiū* entry encodes *bāobiǎn*. Zhāng Dàhēng's 張大亨 *Chūnqiū wǔlǐ lìzōng* 春秋五禮例宗 [KR1e0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0030) redistributes the entire *Chūnqiū* under the canonical *wǔ lǐ* 五禮 typology.

**The Hú Ānguó school and its institutional triumph ([KR1e0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0036), [KR1e0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0071), [KR1e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0074)).** Hú Ānguó's 胡安國 *Húshì Chūnqiū zhuàn* 胡氏春秋傳 [KR1e0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0036) — written under the shadow of the Jīn 金 invasions and reading the *Chūnqiū* as cipher for political-ethical judgement on contemporary frontier policy — became the foundational Southern-Sòng commentary; its later canonisation as the *fourth* official *Chūnqiū* tradition (alongside the *Sānzhuàn*) made it the longest-standing imperial orthodoxy in this division. *Chūnqiū Húzhuàn fùlù zuǎnshū* 春秋胡傳附錄纂疏 [KR1e0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0071) of Wāng Kèkuān 汪克寬 is its standard Yuán-period sub-commentary and the Yuán-Míng examination textbook. *Chūnqiū dàquán* 春秋大全 [KR1e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0074) of Hú Guǎng 胡廣, the Yǒnglè-era imperial compilation in the *Wǔjīng dàquán* programme, codified Hú Ānguó's reading as Míng state orthodoxy.

**Southern-Sòng *Zuǒ*-primary, *Dàoxué*, and Yǒngjiā commentaries ([KR1e0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0032)–0035, 0037–0048).** Yè Mèngdé's 葉夢得 tetrad — *Yèshì Chūnqiū zhuàn* 葉氏春秋傳 [KR1e0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0032), *Chūnqiū kǎo* 春秋考 [KR1e0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0033), *Chūnqiū Zuǒzhuàn yàn* 春秋左傳讞 [KR1e0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0034) (the *Gōngzhuàn yàn* and *Gǔzhuàn yàn* are lost) — sets the methodologically careful middle path between Sūn Fù and Sū Zhé. *Lǚshì Chūnqiū jíjiě* 呂氏春秋集解 [KR1e0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0035) of Lǚ Běnzhōng 呂本中 anthologises the major Northern-Sòng commentators. Lǚ Zǔqiān's 呂祖謙 *Zuǒ*-trilogy — *Zuǒshì zhuànshuō* 左氏傳說 [KR1e0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0039), *Zuǒshì zhuàn xùshuō* 左氏傳續說 [KR1e0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0040), *Zuǒshì bóyì* 左氏博議 [KR1e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0041) — together with his topical recasting *Dōnglái Lǚ Tàishǐ Chūnqiū Zuǒzhuàn lèibiān* 東萊呂太史春秋左傳類編 [KR1e0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0043) — makes Lǚ Zǔqiān the central Southern-Sòng *Zuǒ* exegete; *Zuǒshì bóyì* in particular, with its 168 evaluative essays on *Zuǒ* episodes, became the most popular Sòng *Chūnqiū* book. *Chūnqiū hòu zhuàn* 春秋後傳 [KR1e0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0038) of Chén Fùliáng 陳傅良 is the leading work of the Yǒngjiā 永嘉 statecraft school. *Chūnqiū jíyì* 春秋集義 [KR1e0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0047) of Lǐ Míngfù 李明復 is the most comprehensive Southern-Sòng *Dàoxué*-school *Chūnqiū* compilation; *Zhāngshì Chūnqiū jízhù* 張氏春秋集注 [KR1e0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0048) of Zhāng Qià 張洽 is the principal *Chūnqiū* commentary by a Zhū Xī disciple. *Chūnqiū fēnjì* 春秋分記 [KR1e0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0045) of Chéng Gōngshuō 程公說 is the most ambitious Southern-Sòng *Shǐjì*-modeled historiographical reorganisation of the *Chūnqiū*.

**Late-Sòng / Yuán radical-sceptical and synthetic commentaries ([KR1e0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0049)–0065).** *Chūnqiū tōngshuō* 春秋通說 [KR1e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0050) of Huáng Zhòngyán 黃仲炎 makes the strong thesis that the *Chūnqiū* is a book of *teaching* and *admonition*, not *bāobiǎn*. *Chūnqiū jīngquán* 春秋經筌 [KR1e0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0052) of Zhào Péngfēi 趙鵬飛 — programmatically refusing to use any commentary at all — is the sharpest Sòng instance of the radical-sceptical tendency. Chéng Duānxué's 程端學 trilogy — *Chūnqiū běnyì* 春秋本義 [KR1e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0060), *Chéngshì Chūnqiū huòwèn* 程氏春秋或問 [KR1e0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0061), *Sānzhuàn biànyí* 三傳辨疑 [KR1e0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0062) — pushes the position to its limit, treating the *Zuǒzhuàn* as a forgery and the *Gōngyáng* and *Gǔliáng* as worthless; this is the late-Yuán radical centre. *Chūnqiū jízhuàn shìyì dàchéng* 春秋集傳釋義大成 [KR1e0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0056) of Yú Gāo 兪皋 introduces the four-*zhuàn* parallel format (Zuǒ, Gōng, Gǔ, Hú under each lemma) that became standard. *Chūnqiū huìtōng* 春秋會通 [KR1e0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0064) of Lǐ Lián 李廉 stakes out the synthetic middle.

**The Yuán Xīn'ān school and Zhào Fǎng's five-work programme ([KR1e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0066)–0071).** *Chūnqiū jízhuàn* 春秋集傳 [KR1e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0066), *Chūnqiū shīshuō* 春秋師說 [KR1e0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0067), *Chūnqiū Zuǒshì zhuàn bǔzhù* 春秋左氏傳補註 [KR1e0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0068), *Chūnqiū jīn-suǒ-shi* 春秋金鎖匙 [KR1e0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0069), *Chūnqiū shǔcí* 春秋屬辭 [KR1e0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0070) together constitute Zhào Fǎng's 趙汸 *Chūnqiū* programme — the most coherent single-author *Chūnqiū* corpus of the entire pre-modern tradition, organised around the methodological key *cèshū* / *bǐxuē* 策書/筆削 (court-record vs. Confucian editorial brush). *Chūnqiū shīshuō* preserves the otherwise-lost teachings of his teacher Huáng Zé 黃澤. The shorter *Chūnqiū quèyí* 春秋闕欵 [KR1e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0065) of Zhèng Yù 鄭玉 brings the late-Yuán *quēyí* 闕疑 (acknowledged limit-of-knowledge) doctrine to its sharpest formulation.

**Míng *xìnjīng bùxìnzhuàn* and Dōnglín commentaries ([KR1e0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0072)–0092).** *Chūnqiū chūnwáng zhèngyuè kǎo* 春秋春王正月考 [KR1e0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0072) of Zhāng Yǐníng 張以寧 (1370) opens the Míng with a calendrical refutation of Hú Ānguó's *yǐ Xiàshí guàn Zhōuyuè* 以夏時冠周月 doctrine. *Zuǒzhuàn fù zhù* 左傳附注 [KR1e0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0077) and *Chūnqiū Húshì zhuàn biànyí* 春秋胡氏傳辨疑 [KR1e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0078) of Lù Càn 陸粲 inaugurate the mid-Míng *kǎozhèng*-style philological revision that Gù Yánwǔ would build on. *Chūnqiū míngzhì lù* 春秋明志錄 [KR1e0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0079) of Xióng Guō 熊過 is the most systematic mid-Míng *xìnjīng bùxìnzhuàn* monograph. *Chūnqiū kǒngyì* 春秋孔義 [KR1e0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0088) of Gāo Pānlóng 高攀龍 is the principal Dōnglín-school *Chūnqiū* work; its *yǐ jīng jiě jīng* method ("explain the canon by the canon") is a key statement of late-Míng *Chūnqiū* hermeneutic. *Chūnqiū biànyì* 春秋辯義 [KR1e0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0089) of Zhuó Ěrkāng 卓爾康 is the largest single Míng *Chūnqiū* commentary, encyclopedic in form. *Zuǒzhuàn Dù-Lín hézhù* 左傳杜林合注 [KR1e0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0092) is the late-Míng composite student edition (Dù Yù annotation + Lín Yáosǒu 林堯叟 paraphrase) that became the standard handbook for several generations.

**The Qīng imperial trilogy ([KR1e0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0093)–0095).** *Rìjiǎng Chūnqiū jiěyì* 日講春秋解義 [KR1e0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0093) is the Kāngxī court lecture-cycle, anchoring on Hú Ānguó while purging the most extreme readings; *Qīndìng Chūnqiū chuánshuō huìzuǎn* 欽定春秋傳說彙纂 [KR1e0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0094) (1721) is the Kāngxī-commissioned official synthesis, designed to fill the gap that Zhū Xī had left by composing no *Chūnqiū* commentary; *Yùzuǎn Chūnqiū zhíjiě* 御纂春秋直解 [KR1e0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0095) (1758) completes the trilogy under Qiánlóng, with a polemical critique of the *Dàn–Zhào–Lù* school.

**Qīng evidential *Zuǒzhuàn* philology and the Wúpài / Wú-Jiāng lineages ([KR1e0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0096)–0117).** *Zuǒzhuàn Dùjiě bǔzhèng* 左傳杜解補正 [KR1e0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0096) of Gù Yánwǔ 顧炎武 is the foundational text of Qīng *Zuǒzhuàn* evidential research and the model for the entire Wú-Jiāng school; *Dú Zuǒ rìchāo* 讀左日鈔 [KR1e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0100) of Zhū Hèlíng 朱鶴齡 is its companion. *Chūnqiū bàishū* 春秋稗疏 [KR1e0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0097) of Wáng Fūzhī 王夫之 supplies the geographic / calendrical / *shūfǎ* substratum. *Zuǒzhuàn shìwěi* 左傳事緯 [KR1e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0101) of Mǎ Sù 馬驌 is genre-redefining, disaggregating and regrouping the *Zuǒ* under 108 topical headings. Máo Qílíng's 毛奇齡 ritualist trilogy — *Chūnqiū Máoshì zhuàn* 春秋毛氏傳 [KR1e0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0102), *Chūnqiū jiǎnshū kānwù* 春秋簡書刋誤 [KR1e0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0103), *Chūnqiū shǔcí bǐshì jì* 春秋屬辭比事記 [KR1e0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0104) — is the polemical core of the early-Qīng anti-Hú reaction. The Wúpài 吳派 lineage opens with Huì Shìqí's 惠士奇 *Huìshì Chūnqiū shuō* 惠氏春秋說 [KR1e0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0113) and matures in his son Huì Dòng's 惠棟 *Huìshì Chūnqiū Zuǒzhuàn bǔzhù* 惠氏春秋左傳補註 [KR1e0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0116), with Shěn Tóng's 沈彤 *Chūnqiū Zuǒzhuàn xiǎo shū* 春秋左傳小疏 [KR1e0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0117) as its specialist philological complement. *Sānzhuàn zhézhū* 三傳折諸 [KR1e0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0107) of Zhāng Shàngyuàn 張尚瑗 is the magnum opus of the Wú-Jiāng *yǐ jīng zhèng zhuàn* programme.

**Qīng anti-Hú reaction, Tóngchéng school, and reference apparatus ([KR1e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0105)–0121).** *Chūnqiū dìmíng kǎo lüè* 春秋地名考略 [KR1e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0105) of Gāo Shìqí 高士奇 is the imperial-period historical-geographical lexicon. *Chūnqiū shìzú pǔ* 春秋世族譜 [KR1e0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0111) of Chén Hòuyào 陳厚耀 reconstructs *Chūnqiū* prosopography; *Chūnqiū chánglì* 春秋長歷 [KR1e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0112) of the same author corrects Dù Yù's calendrical scheme by one intercalation and is the defining work of Qīng *Chūnqiū* calendrical reconstruction. *Sānzhèng kǎo* 三正考 [KR1e0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0119) of Wú Nài 吳鼐 settles the *sān zhèng* 三正 problem in favour of the Zhōu calendar. *Chūnqiū dìlǐ kǎoshí* 春秋地理考實 [KR1e0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0118) of Jiāng Yǒng 江永 is the most concise authoritative eighteenth-century gazetteer. *Chūnqiū dàshì biǎo* 春秋大事表 [KR1e0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0114) of Gù Dònggāo 顧棟高, in fifty-fold tabular form, is the largest single-author *Chūnqiū* reference work in the Chinese tradition and remains, alongside Yáng Bójùn 楊伯峻's annotated edition, indispensable. The Tóngchéng-school 桐城派 line — *Chūnqiū tōnglùn* 春秋通論 [KR1e0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0110) of Fāng Bāo 方苞 and *Chūnqiū jiū yí* 春秋究遺 [KR1e0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0120) of Yè Yǒu 葉酉 — reroutes orthodox-Zhū *Chūnqiū* hermeneutic into prose-and-meaning literary practice. *Chūnqiū quèrú biān* 春秋闕如編 [KR1e0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0108) of Jiāo Yuánxī 焦袁熹 is the most elegant statement of the early-Qīng reaction against harsh-moralist exegesis.

BCE) — the blind Lǔ scribe to whom Sīmǎ Qiān attributed the *Zuǒzhuàn*; modern scholarship (since Gù Yánwǔ) treats the work as composed by several hands over the late Warring States period (Wilkinson §48.1.1.1).

BCE) — eponymous traditional founders of the *Gōngyáng* and *Gǔliáng* commentarial traditions. Both works appear in our textual record only in early Western Hàn ([KR1e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0006), [KR1e0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0008)).
