### Topics

- **Did Confucius edit the *Chūnqiū*?** The presupposition that the canonical text encodes Confucius's *wēiyán dàyì* drives almost the entire *bāobiǎn* tradition (Wilkinson §48.1.1). Most pre-modern commentators in this division accept this premise; the radical sceptical line — Wáng Ānshí's "fragmentary court gazette" remark, the Dàn Zhào school, Zhào Péngfēi [KR1e0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0052), Chéng Duānxué [KR1e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0060)–[KR1e0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0062), down through Lù Càn [KR1e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0078) and Wáng Fūzhī [KR1e0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0097) — challenges it. The modern consensus that the *Chūnqiū*'s "omissions and variations are the result of natural causes" rather than cryptographic praise-and-blame (Kennedy 1942; Van Auken 2008; Wilkinson §48.1.1.1) is in effect a vindication of the radical sceptical line.
- **The relative authority of the three commentaries.** The Hàn-period dispute over which of the three commentaries to privilege (Hé Xiū vs. Zhèng Xuán in [KR1e0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0007) / [KR1e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0011)) is the foundational version of a problem that recurs in every period: Dù Yù's Jìn-period commitment to *Zuǒ* primacy [KR1e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0002), Lù Chún's Táng rejection of all three [KR1e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0013)–[KR1e0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0015), the Sòng promotion of Hú Ānguó [KR1e0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0036) *as* a fourth tradition, the Qīng restoration of *Zuǒ*-primary historiography under the Wú-Jiāng school [KR1e0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0096) / [KR1e0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0107) / [KR1e0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0116).
- **The *Zuǒzhuàn* as historical narrative vs. as commentary.** Already in the Hàn the *Zuǒ* was understood to be qualitatively different from the *Gōngyáng* and *Gǔliáng* — a fully-narrative pre-Hàn historical work attached secondarily to the *Chūnqiū* (Wilkinson §48.1.1.1). The Sòng-Qīng tradition repeatedly mines this difference, either to elevate the *Zuǒ* as the prime source for the period (Lǚ Zǔqiān's *Zuǒ*-trilogy [KR1e0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0039)–[KR1e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0041); Mǎ Sù [KR1e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0101)) or to attack it as a forgery interpolated to look like a commentary (Chéng Duānxué [KR1e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0060)–[KR1e0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0062)).
- ***Bāobiǎn* versus admonition / teaching.** The *yǒubiǎn wúbāo* programme of Sūn Fù [KR1e0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0018) sets one extreme; Huáng Zhòngyán's *Chūnqiū* as a book of *teaching and admonition* [KR1e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0050) sets a different one; Lǚ Dàguī [KR1e0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0053) and Jiāo Yuánxī [KR1e0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0108) reject *bāobiǎn* altogether. The political stakes — what the *Chūnqiū* authorises a sovereign to praise or condemn — make the question structural to imperial ritual reading, especially in the Hú-school readings under Jīn / Mongol / Qīng pressure.
- **Calendrical hermeneutics.** Cuī Zǐfāng's *rìyuè lì* theory [KR1e0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0028)–[KR1e0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0029) holds that calendrical detail in each entry encodes *bāobiǎn*; the Qīng rebuttal proceeds via independent calendrical reconstruction (Chén Hòuyào *Chūnqiū chánglì* [KR1e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0112)), which corrects Dù Yù's scheme by one intercalation, and via the *sān zhèng* 三正 settlement of Wú Nài [KR1e0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0119) — clinching the case that the *Chūnqiū* uses the Zhōu calendar straight, without hermeneutic encoding. Zhāng Yǐníng [KR1e0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0072) had already used calendrical evidence against Hú Ānguó's *yǐ Xiàshí guàn Zhōuyuè* doctrine.
- **Topical / categorical reorganisation.** A long sub-tradition recasts the *Chūnqiū* (or the *Zuǒzhuàn*) by topic rather than chronology: Zhāng Dàhēng under the *wǔ lǐ* [KR1e0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0030), Lǚ Zǔqiān under nineteen topical heads [KR1e0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0043), Chéng Gōngshuō *Shǐjì*-style [KR1e0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0045), Qí Lǚqiān state-by-state [KR1e0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0059), Wú Chéng under seven cosmic-ritual heads [KR1e0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0057), Mǎ Sù under 108 headings [KR1e0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0101), Gù Dònggāo in fifty tables [KR1e0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0114). This is one of the division's most productive genres and the proximate ancestor of modern reference works on the period.
- **Reference apparatus: prosopography, geography, calendar.** The Qīng evidential turn produced a triple reference apparatus: prosopography (Chén Hòuyào *Chūnqiū shìzú pǔ* [KR1e0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0111), Chéng Tíngzuò *Chūnqiū shíxiǎo lù* [KR1e0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0115)); historical geography (Gāo Shìqí [KR1e0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0105), Jiāng Yǒng [KR1e0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0118)); calendar (Chén Hòuyào *Chūnqiū chánglì* [KR1e0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0112), Wú Nài [KR1e0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0119)). Together these make the *Chūnqiū* corpus continuously usable as a primary historical source.
- **Hú Ānguó's six-century institutional reign.** From its 1313 elevation to the official examination commentary through the Yǒnglè *Dàquán* [KR1e0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0074) to the high-Qīng, Hú Ānguó's *Chūnqiū zhuàn* [KR1e0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0036) was the orthodox state textbook. The Míng-Qīng landscape of the division is in large measure a landscape of stances toward Hú: Wāng Kèkuān *fùlù zuǎnshū* [KR1e0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0071), Lù Càn anti-Hú [KR1e0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0078), Yuán Rén *kǎowù* [KR1e0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0085), the Qīng imperial trilogy [KR1e0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0093)–[KR1e0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0095) keeping Hú as anchor while purging extremes, Xú Tíngyuán anti-Hú reaction [KR1e0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0106).
- **Dōnglín and Tóngchéng readings.** The late-Míng Dōnglín circle (Gāo Pānlóng [KR1e0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0088)) and the early-to-mid-Qīng Tóngchéng school (Fāng Bāo [KR1e0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0110), Yè Yǒu [KR1e0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1e/KR1e0120)) supply two distinct moralist *Chūnqiū* hermeneutics that bridge between Sòng *yìlǐ* readings and Qīng evidential philology.

# 孝經類 (KR1f)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1f 孝經類 *Xiàojīng lèi* — Classics — Classic of Filial Piety](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR1f gathers the *Xiàojīng* 孝經 (*Classic of Filial Piety*) and its commentarial tradition, plus the closely-modelled apocryphal *Zhōngjīng* 忠經 (*Classic of Loyalty*). It is the sixth subdivision of the *jīngbù* 經部 (KR1, Classics) and corresponds exactly to the *Xiàojīng* branch of the *Sìkù quánshū* classification (Wilkinson §28.5, [Box 161]). The canonical work itself is the shortest of the *Thirteen Classics* — c. 1,800 graphs in 18 short *zhāng* 章 (Wilkinson §28.4.4) — a Confucian–Zēngzǐ dialogue on filial piety (*xiào* 孝) as the root of moral order and the foundation of government. From the Hàn through the late Qīng it was the standard primer with which children in China, Korea, Japan, and Vietnam began their classical education (Wilkinson §28.4.4), and it survives in two competing recensions whose dispute organizes the entire division: a *jīnwén* 今文 ("Current Script") recension in 18 *zhāng* transmitted by Yán Zhī 顏芝 and canonized by the Táng emperor Xuánzōng in 722–743, and a *gǔwén* 古文 ("Ancient Script") recension in 22 *zhāng* attributed to Kǒng Ānguó 孔安國 and preserved largely in Japan (Wilkinson §28.7.1; see [KR1f0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0001), [KR1f0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0003)).

Three layers shape the division's commentarial history: (1) a Táng imperial layer crystallizing the *jīnwén* recension under Xuánzōng's *yùzhù* 御注 of 743, with Lù Démíng's 陸德明 phonetic glosses and Xíng Bǐng's 邢昺 *zhèngyì* 正義 of 1001 producing the *Shísān jīng zhùshū* form ([KR1f0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0002), [KR1f0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0004)); (2) a Sòng–Yuán Daoxue layer in which Sīmǎ Guāng and Fàn Zǔyǔ revived the *gǔwén* ([KR1f0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0005)) and Zhū Xī's *Kānwù* 刋誤 of 1186 ([KR1f0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0006)) restructured the text into "1 *jīng* + *zhuàn*" form and excised 223 characters, transmitted onward by Dǒng Dǐng ([KR1f0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0007)) and Wú Chéng ([KR1f0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0008)); (3) a Míng–Qīng layer in which late-Míng philosophical readings ([KR1f0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0009), [KR1f0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0010)), two Qīng imperial commentaries ([KR1f0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0011), [KR1f0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0012)), Qīng kǎozhèng polemics ([KR1f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0013)), and the Edo Japanese rediscovery of the Kǒng-attributed *gǔwén zhuàn* ([KR1f0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0003)) all contend with one another. The *Xiàojīng* is also the only Confucian classic annotated by four reigning emperors — Táng Xuánzōng, Sòng Zhēnzōng, Qīng Shùnzhì, and Qīng Yōngzhèng — paralleling the imperial annotation of the *Dàodé jīng* 道德經 (Wilkinson §65451).

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The canonical text.** *Xiàojīng* 孝經 [KR1f0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0001) — the bare 18-*zhāng* *jīnwén* recension, the philological starting-point of the entire division and the form in which children in East Asia memorized the work for two millennia.

- **The Táng imperial / Sòng *zhèngyì* line.** *Xiàojīng* 孝經 [KR1f0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0002) — Táng Xuánzōng's *yùzhù* of 722, revised 743, the recension that eclipsed all rival commentaries and was carved on the *Shítái Xiàojīng* 石臺孝經 stele in 745. *Xiàojīng zhùshū* 孝經注疏 [KR1f0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0004) — Xíng Bǐng's 1001 *zhèngyì* trimming Yuán Xíngchōng's 元行冲 c. 745 sub-commentary onto the imperial *zhù*, the form in which the work entered the *Shísān jīng zhùshū* and the *Sìkù quánshū*. Together these two are the canonical Táng–Sòng form of the *Xiàojīng*.

- **The Sòng *gǔwén* revival.** *Gǔwén Xiàojīng zhǐjiě* 古文孝經指解 [KR1f0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0005) — Sīmǎ Guāng's *zhǐjiě* (c. 1054) appended to Fàn Zǔyǔ's *shuō* (c. 1085), the primary Sòng witness to the 22-chapter *gǔwén* text independent of the post-1731 Japanese line, and the principal pre-Zhū defence of the *gǔwén* against the established *jīnwén*.

- **The Zhū Xī editorial line.** *Xiàojīng kānwù* 孝經刋誤 [KR1f0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0006) — Zhū Xī's 1186 restructuring of the *gǔwén* into "1 *jīng* + 14 *zhuàn*" with 223 characters excised, the most consequential single intervention in the *Xiàojīng* canon after the Táng imperial commentary; *Xiàojīng dàyì* 孝經大義 [KR1f0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0007) (Dǒng Dǐng, c. 1290–1305) and *Xiàojīng dìngběn* 孝經定本 [KR1f0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0008) (Wú Chéng, 1303) are the two Yuán expositions that turned Zhū's polemic into a stable curricular text and carried the *Kānwù* recension into the Yuán–Míng examination world.

- **The Edo *gǔwén* recovery.** *Gǔwén Xiàojīng Kǒngshì zhuàn* 古文孝經孔氏傳 [KR1f0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0003) — the Japanese-preserved *gǔwén* 22-chapter recension with the Kǒng-attributed *zhuàn*, fixed in 1731 by Dazai Shundai 太宰純 and reintroduced into China in 1776; assessed as a Sòng-or-later Japanese fabrication by the *Sìkù* editors but a vital independent witness to pre-Xuánzōng textual states.

- **The late-Míng philosophical commentary.** *Xiàojīng jízhuàn* 孝經集傳 [KR1f0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0010) — Huáng Dàozhōu's 1638–1643 prison-and-imprisonment commentary, the most ambitious philosophical reading of the work in the late Míng and the one that explicitly executes Zhū Xī's never-realized *wàizhuàn* 外傳 programme.

- **The Qīng imperial pair.** *Yùdìng Xiàojīng zhù* 御定孝經注 [KR1f0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0011) — Shùnzhì's 1656 commentary, deliberately avoiding both the *jīnwén / gǔwén* dispute and the Zhū Xī *Kānwù*; *Yùzuǎn Xiàojīng jízhù* 御纂孝經集註 [KR1f0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0012) — Yōngzhèng's 1727 compact compilation modelled on Zhū Xī's *Sìshū zhāngjù jízhù*, the standard ceremonial Qīng recension. The pair (with the unincluded 100-*juàn* Kāngxī *Xiàojīng yǎnyì* 孝經衍義) constitutes the high-Qīng imperial *Xiàojīng* programme.

- **The Qīng kǎozhèng critique.** *Xiàojīng wèn* 孝經問 [KR1f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0013) — Máo Qílíng's polemical *wèndá* of c. 1685–1716, the most important Qīng critique of the Zhū Xī editorial tradition and a key document of early kǎozhèngxué.

- **The fragmentary outlier.** *Xiàojīng shùzhù* 孝經述註 [KR1f0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0009) — Xiàng Bīn's early-Míng commentary, lost from circulation and recovered by the *Sìkù* editors from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* 永樂大典; included as the principal early-Míng witness in the division.

- **The companion apocryphon.** *Zhōngjīng* 忠經 [KR1f0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0014) — the pseudepigraphic *Classic of Loyalty* in 18 *zhāng*, attributed to Mǎ Róng 馬融 with a Zhèng Xuán-attributed commentary, actually a late-Táng or early-Sòng imitation of the *jīnwén Xiàojīng*. Excluded from the *Sìkù* but bibliographically paired with the *Xiàojīng* since the Sòng *Tōngzhì* 通志.

### Important persons

- [孔子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E5%AD%90) — traditional attributed author of the *Xiàojīng*'s spoken half; the *Hàn shū yìwén zhì* says "Zhòngní spoke and Zēngzǐ wrote it down."
- 曾子 — traditional attributed redactor (or, in a subsidiary attribution, author); the disciple of Confucius in the canonical opening dialogue.
- [孔安國](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E5%AE%89%E5%9C%8B) — pseudepigraphic author of the *gǔwén zhuàn* (see [KR1f0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0003)), the figurehead of the Old-Text tradition in the *Xiàojīng* sub-canon.

### Topics

- ***Jīnwén* 今文 vs. *gǔwén* 古文.** The defining controversy of the division. The 18-chapter *jīnwén* recension transmitted by Yán Zhī and the 22-chapter *gǔwén* recension attributed to Kǒng Ānguó (containing the additional *Guīmén* 閨門 chapter on familial relations and three further chapter-divisions) became canonized as rivals already in the Suí (Wáng Shào, Liú Xuàn) and Táng (Liú Zhījī, Sīmǎ Zhēn); Xuánzōng's 722 commentary closed the dispute by adopting the *jīnwén*; Sòng *Daoxue* scholars (Sīmǎ Guāng, Fàn Zǔyǔ, Zhū Xī) revived the *gǔwén*; Yuán commentators (Dǒng Dǐng, Wú Chéng) split between them; the Edo recovery of the Kǒng-attributed *zhuàn* (Dazai 1731) reopened the question; Qīng kǎozhèng (Wú Chéng's character-count argument, repeated by Máo Qílíng) effectively dissolved it by showing that the substantive textual differences are minor (under thirty characters plus the *Guīmén* chapter).

- **Imperial annotation of the canon.** The *Xiàojīng* is the only Confucian classic annotated by four reigning emperors — Táng Xuánzōng, Sòng Zhēnzōng, Qīng Shùnzhì, Qīng Yōngzhèng — paralleling the imperial annotation of the *Dàodé jīng* (Wilkinson §65451). The recurrence is not coincidental: the *Xiàojīng*'s extension of filial piety from family to state (*shì jūn* 事君 modelled on *shì qīn* 事親) made it the natural Confucian text for an emperor to take in hand. The succession Shùnzhì 1656 ⇒ Kāngxī *yǎnyì* 100 *juàn* ⇒ Yōngzhèng 1727 *jízhù* registers an explicit Qīng imperial *Xiàojīng* programme.

- **Editorial liberty vs textual conservation.** Zhū Xī's *Kānwù* of 1186 excised 223 characters of the canon — the most aggressive Daoxue editorial intervention in any *jīng*, going further even than his rearrangement of the *Dàxué* 大學. The post-Zhū tradition split: Dǒng Dǐng and Wú Chéng accepted and worked from the edited recension; Huáng Dàozhōu, the Qīng imperial commentaries, and especially Máo Qílíng repudiated it. The *Sìkù* editors' own *tíyào* on [KR1f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0013) explicitly endorses Máo's standpoint ("standing firmly on the inherited text and refusing to license the corruption of the ancient canon"), making the *Xiàojīng* sub-canon one of the clearest sites at which the kǎozhèng critique of *Daoxue* editorial liberty can be observed in action.

- **The *Xiàojīng* as primer and political instrument.** From the Hàn imperial school onward the *Xiàojīng* was the entry text of the curriculum (Wilkinson §24.2.1 cites the *Sìmín yuè lìng* 四民月令: in the eleventh month "*the young children read the* Xiàojīng *and the* Lúnyǔ"), shorter and more accessible than the *Wǔjīng*, and pedagogically prior to the *Sìshū*. The Qīng imperial commentaries (especially Yōngzhèng's compact *jízhù*) and works like the *Shèng yù guǎng xùn* 聖諭廣訓 of 1724 made this primer function a central element of Qīng administrative ideology — see Kutcher (1999) on *xiào* as instrument of state ideology in the Qīng.

- **Cross-canon imitation.** The *Xiàojīng* generated a small genre of formal imitations: the *Zhōngjīng* 忠經 (see [KR1f0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0014)), pseudonymously ascribed to Mǎ Róng, extending the model from filial piety to political loyalty; the *Nǚ xiàojīng* 女孝經 ascribed to "Lady née Zhèng" c. 730 (Wilkinson §11790; Murray 1988, 1990), extending it to women's filial duty. These imitations are not in the *Sìkù* but were bibliographically paired with the *Xiàojīng* in the Sòng *Tōngzhì* and the Yuán *Wénxiàn tōngkǎo*.

- **The *Guīmén* 閨門 chapter and dynastic taboo.** The 24-character *Guīmén* chapter peculiar to the *gǔwén* (on family relations within the home) was excised in the Táng *jīnwén* recension; Yuán-Míng commentators (Xióng Hé in his preface to [KR1f0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0007), Sūn Běn) read this as a deliberate court-taboo response to Wǔ Zétiān 武則天 and Wéi Hòu 韋后 — an interpretation explicitly refuted at length by the *Sìkù* editors in the *Tíyào* to [KR1f0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1f/KR1f0004). The dispute is a useful indicator of how moralized readings of textual history were contested in the Qīng evidential-scholarship project.

### Timeline

# 五經總義類 (KR1g)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1g 五經總義類 *Wǔjīng zǒngyì lèi* — Classics — General Works on the Five Classics](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

*Wǔjīng zǒngyì* 五經總義 is the *Sìkù quánshū* 四庫全書 sub-category that collects works which range across more than one of the Confucian canon rather than expounding a single classic. Wilkinson treats it under §28.5 as one of the two branches the Qing bibliographers added to the *jīngbù* 經部 (the other being *Sì shū* 四書), correlating to the *Wǔjīng zhùshū* 五經注疏 / *Shísān jīng zhùshū* 十三經注疏 print tradition described under his §28.7. In practice, the division gathers four distinct kinds of writing: (1) Hàn–Táng compendia of glosses, pronunciations, and inter-school disagreements which treat the canon as a whole; (2) Sòng–Yuán *jīngshuō* 經說 essay collections produced under the Dàoxué reorientation; (3) text-critical, collation, and *zhíyīn* 直音 handbooks supporting block-printing of the *Classics*; and (4) the long Qing arc of *kǎozhèng* 考證 philology that ends with the apparatus criticus on which Ruǎn Yuán's 阮元 1815 *Shísān jīng zhùshū jiào kān jì* 十三經注疏校勘記 was built.

Two structural points govern the division. First, its chronological range runs from the second-century-CE exchange between Xǔ Shèn 許愼 and Zhèng Xuán 鄭玄 — Wilkinson §28.7.2 makes Lù Démíng's 陸德明 *Jīngdiǎn shìwén* 經典釋文 (compiled c. 583, the second of the "two most influential annotated editions of the *Classics* up to the Song") the keystone of the early stratum — through to the late-eighteenth-century Sūzhōu school of Huì Dòng 惠棟 and his disciple Yú Xiāokè 余蕭客. Second, the *Sìkù* compilers consistently used this division to register methodological reorientations: the appearance of Liú Chǎng's 劉敞 *Gōngshì Qī jīng xiǎo zhuàn* 公是七經小傳 ([KR1g0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0004)) for the Sòng break with Hàn-Táng *zhāngjù* 章句, of Sūn Jué's 孫瑴 *Gǔwēi shū* 古微書 ([KR1g0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0032)) for the pre-modern recovery of the *chènwěi* 讖緯 apocrypha (Wilkinson §28.6), and of Huì Dòng's *Jiǔ jīng gǔ yì* 九經古義 ([KR1g0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0024)) for the programmatic Hàn-learning turn. The single conspicuous gap in the present catalog is the *Qīndìng fānyì Wǔjīng Sìshū* 欽定繙譯五經四書 ([KR1g0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0019), the Qiánlóng-era Manchu translation), for which no per-text note exists yet.

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Bó Wǔjīng yìyì* 駁五經異義 [KR1g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0001) and *Zhèng zhì* 鄭志 [KR1g0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0002) — the two Hàn–Wèi works (Xǔ Shèn → Zhèng Xuán → Zhèng Xiǎotóng 鄭小同) that put the new-text / old-text disputes of the Eastern Hàn into the canonical record; both survive only as fragment-reconstructions assembled by *Sìkù* editors.
- *Jīngdiǎn shìwén* 經典釋文 [KR1g0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0003) — Lù Démíng's thirty-*juàn* *yīnyì* 音義 corpus for fourteen classics (the *Thirteen Classics* minus the *Mèngzǐ*, plus *Lǎozǐ* and *Zhuāngzǐ*); Wilkinson identifies it as the single philological keystone of the pre-Sòng canonical tradition, citing roughly 230 Hàn–Six-Dynasties authorities now otherwise lost.
- The **Northern Sòng break** — *Gōngshì Qī jīng xiǎo zhuàn* 公是七經小傳 [KR1g0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0004) (Liú Chǎng's conjectural-emendation programme, regularly named as the proximate precursor of Wáng Ānshí's 王安石 *Xīn jīngyì* 新經義) and *Chéng shì jīng shuō* 程氏經說 [KR1g0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0005) (Chéng Yí 程頤 on the classics outside the *Yì*, including the redacted *Dàxué* 大學 that Zhū Xī 朱熹 later took as the basis of his *Zhāngjù* 章句).
- The **Sòng *tú* / *zhíyīn* / *yán'gé* collation cluster** — *Liù jīng tú* 六經圖 [KR1g0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0006) (309 illustrated schemata, Yáng Jiǎ 楊甲 supplemented by Máo Bānghàn 毛邦翰); *Liù jīng zhèng wù* 六經正誤 [KR1g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0007) (Máo Jūzhèng's 毛居正 1223 collator's notes, including engraver falsifications); *Jiǔ jīng sān zhuàn yán'gé lì* 九經三傳沿革例 [KR1g0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0008) (Yuè Kē's 岳珂 seven-principle editorial manifesto for the Xiāngtāi 相臺 cut); and the anonymous *Míngběn pái zì Jiǔ jīng zhí yīn* 明本排字九經直音 [KR1g0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0012) (a Sòng-Yuán Míngzhōu 明州 commercial sound-gloss handbook, surviving in the 1287 cut).
- *Róngtáng Sì shū guǎn jiàn* 融堂四書管見 [KR1g0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0009) — Qián Shí's 錢時 Lù-Cíhú 陸慈湖 *xīnxué* 心學 commentary on a heterodox "Sì shū" (*Lúnyǔ*, *Xiàojīng*, *Dàxué*, *Zhōngyōng*), pointedly excluding the *Mèngzǐ*; the principal pre-Yángmíng *xīnxué* counter-canon in the division.
- *Liù jīng ào lùn* 六經奧論 [KR1g0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1g/KR1g0011) — an anonymous late-Sòng examination-prep compendium falsely ascribed to Zhèng Qiáo 鄭樵; included as the textbook *Sìkù* case-study in attribution criticism (the editors' six-strand demolition is a model of *kǎozhèng* method).

# 四書類 (KR1h)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1h 四書類 *Sìshū lèi* — Classics — Four Books](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR1h covers the *Sìshū* 四書 ("Four Books") branch of the Classics, the latest of the ten sub-categories of the *jīngbù* 經部 in the *Sìkù quánshū* 四庫全書 classification. As Wilkinson observes (Wilkinson § 28.4.4, § 28.5), the *Sìshū* — *Dàxué* 大學, *Zhōngyōng* 中庸, *Lúnyǔ* 論語, *Mèngzǐ* 孟子 — were first assembled as a curricular unit by Chéng Hào 程顥 and Chéng Yí 程頤 in the Northern Sòng and given their canonical form by Zhū Xī 朱熹, who issued them as a set in 1190 under the title *Sìzǐ* 四子 with his own commentaries. After the 1227 acceptance of Zhū's commentaries as the standard primer and especially after 1315, when the Yuán reinstituted the examination system on the basis of the *Sìshū* with Zhū Xī's notes, the four texts became the single most-memorized body of writing in late imperial East Asia, supplanting in pedagogical centrality even the *Wǔjīng* 五經 to which the *Classics* branch had originally been devoted.

The KR1h division therefore has a distinctive shape compared with the older *jīng* sub-categories: there is no pre-Hàn classic to which all later commentaries directly attach. The *Lúnyǔ* 論語 and *Mèngzǐ* 孟子 each function as a base text in their own right (and were not formally placed in the Classics branch until the Sòng — *Mèngzǐ* was moved out of the masters branch only at that point, Wilkinson § 28.5), while *Dàxué* and *Zhōngyōng* are short chapters extracted from the *Lǐjì* 禮記 whose independent transmission is essentially a Sòng-and-later phenomenon and is represented in KR1h through later commentarial collections rather than through a separate base recension. The bulk of the division is consequently medieval-to-Qīng: a Hàn–Táng floor of *Lúnyǔ* and *Mèngzǐ* commentary (Zhào Qí 趙岐, Hé Yàn 何晏, Huáng Kǎn 皇侃, Xíng Bǐng 邢昺), an enormous Sòng-Yuán build-up of Dàoxué readings centred on Zhū Xī, the 1415 Ming imperial *Sìshū dàquán* 四書大全 that froze the orthodoxy for the next four centuries, and a Qīng response that ranges from Lù Lǒngqí 陸隴其's defence of Zhū-school orthodoxy to Máo Qílíng 毛奇齡 and Yán Ruòqú 閻若璩's evidential-philology critique. The division thus traces the entire arc by which Neo-Confucianism took institutional shape (Wilkinson § 28.7.3) and then came under empirical scrutiny in the late empire.

### Important texts and text clusters

**Base texts.** The bare canonical texts on which the division depends:

- *Mèngzǐ (zhèngwén)* 孟子(正文) [KR1h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0001) — the Mencius extracted from the Ruǎn-Yuán 阮元 1816 reprint of the Sòng *Mèngzǐ zhùshū*; the principal base text for all the *Mèngzǐ*-related commentaries below.
- *Lúnyǔ (zhèngwén)* 論語(正文) [KR1h0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0004) — the Analects base text from the same series.

**Hàn–Táng commentarial floor on the *Lúnyǔ* and *Mèngzǐ*.** The pre-Sòng layer in the division:

- *Mèngzǐ* 孟子 (Zhào Qí zhù) [KR1h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0002) and *Mèngzǐ zhùshū* 孟子注疏 [KR1h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0003) — Zhào Qí's 趙岐 (d. 201) Hàn annotations, with the late-Sòng *yīnyì* of Sūn Shì 孫奭 attached; the only complete Hàn commentary on the *Mèngzǐ* to survive.
- *Lúnyǔ* (Hé Yàn jíjiě) 論語 [KR1h0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0005), *Lúnyǔ jíjiě yìshū* 論語集解義疏 [KR1h0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0006) (Huáng Kǎn 皇侃, c. 545), and *Lúnyǔ zhùshū* 論語注疏 [KR1h0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0007) (Hé Yàn / Xíng Bǐng) — the foundational layered commentary tradition on the *Analects* from Cáo-Wèi through Northern Sòng. Huáng Kǎn's *yìshū*, transmitted in Japan and re-imported in the 18th c., is the principal southern-dynasties witness.
- *Lúnyǔ bǐjiě* 論語筆解 [KR1h0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0008) — the Hán Yù 韓愈 / Lǐ Áo 李翱 "pen-and-brush glosses," the earliest text in the division standing inside the late-Táng Confucian revival that Wilkinson treats as the genealogical root of Neo-Confucianism (§ 28.7.3).

**The Zhū Xī core and its immediate satellites.** The Southern Sòng cluster that fixed the Four Books as a unit:

- *Sìshū zhāngjù jízhù* 四書章句集注 [KR1h0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0015) — Zhū Xī's section-and-sentence commentary, the most consequential single work in the division and the textual basis of six centuries of examinations.
- *Sìshū huòwèn* 四書或問 [KR1h0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0016) — Zhū's companion question-and-answer volume defending and extending the *Jízhù*'s readings.
- *Lùn Mèng jīngyì* 論孟精義 [KR1h0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0017) — Zhū's earlier (1163–1172) gathering of Northern Sòng masters' (esp. Chéng-brothers) glosses on *Lúnyǔ* and *Mèngzǐ*, the workbook out of which the *Jízhù* grew.
- *Zhōngyōng jíluè* 中庸輯略 [KR1h0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0018) — Shí Zǐzhòng's 石𡼖 anthology cut and re-edited by Zhū Xī, fixing the Northern-Sòng readings of the *Zhōngyōng*.

**Sòng critiques and alternative readings.** Works that argue with, or partly against, the Zhū consensus:

- *Mèngzǐ yīnyì* 孟子音義 [KR1h0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0009) — Sūn Shì's 孫奭 (962–1033) pre-Zhū *yīnyì*, the principal Northern Sòng technical apparatus on the *Mèngzǐ*.
- *Lúnyǔ shíyí* 論語拾遺 [KR1h0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0010) / *Mèngzǐ jiě* 孟子解 [KR1h0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0011) — Sū Zhé 蘇轍's short interventions, characteristic of Shǔ-school 蜀學 alternatives to Chéng-Zhū.
- *Lúnyǔ quánjiě* 論語全解 [KR1h0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0012) — Chén Xiángdào 陳祥道's reading from inside the Wáng Ānshí 王安石 *Xīnxué* circle.
- *Zūn Mèng biàn* 尊孟辨 [KR1h0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0014) — Yú Yǔnwén 余允文's polemic against Sī-Mǎ Guāng 司馬光's *Yí Mèng* 疑孟, the defining text of the 12th-c. controversy over Mencius' canonicity.
- *Guǐsì Lúnyǔ jiě* 癸巳論語解 [KR1h0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0021) and *Guǐsì Mèngzǐ shuō* 癸巳孟子說 [KR1h0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0022) — Zhāng Shì 張栻's pair, the major Hú-Xiāng 湖湘 school readings and Zhū Xī's most important dialogue partner.
- *Shígǔ Lúnyǔ dáwèn* 石鼓論語答問* [KR1h0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0019) — Dài Xī 戴溪's classroom catechism from the Shígǔ shūyuàn 石鼓書院.

**Late-Sòng / Yuán Cheng-Zhu consolidation.** The big sub-commentarial compendia by which Zhū Xī's reading became scholastically codified:

- *Sìshū jíbiān* 四書集編 [KR1h0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0024) — Zhēn Déxiù's 眞德秀, the first major attempt to assemble Zhū's apparatus into a single book.
- *Sìshū zuǎnshū* 四書纂疏 [KR1h0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0028) — Zhào Shùnsūn 趙順孫's, completed in the last decades of the Sòng.
- *Sìshū jíyì jīngyào* 四書集義精要 [KR1h0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0031) — Liú Yīn 劉因's Yuán-period digest.
- *Sìshū tōng* 四書通 [KR1h0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0034) — Hú Bǐngwén 胡炳文's authoritative Yuán-period sub-commentary, often paired with…
- *Sìshū tōngzhèng* 四書通證 [KR1h0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0035) (Zhāng Cúnzhōng 張存中), *Sìshū zuǎnjiān* 四書纂箋 [KR1h0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0038) (Zhān Dàochuán 詹道傳) and *Dú Sìshū cóngshuō* 讀四書叢說 [KR1h0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0033) (Xǔ Qiān 許謙) as the canonical Yuán reference shelf.
- *Sìshū biànyí* 四書辨疑 [KR1h0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0032) — Chén Tiānxiáng 陳天祥's, a rare Yuán *critique* of Zhū's commentary written inside the same Cheng-Zhu world.
- *Sìshū jīngyí guàntōng* 四書經疑貫通* [KR1h0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0037) (1333) — Wáng Chōngyún 王充耘's, designed specifically for the *jīngyí* question-format of the Yuán-restored examinations.

**The Ming imperial frame.** The text that defines the Ming-Qīng orthodoxy:

- *Sìshū dàquán* 四書大全 [KR1h0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0043) — Hú Guǎng 胡廣 et al., 1415, the Yǒnglè-era imperial compendium that bound a curated set of Sòng-Yuán sub-commentaries to Zhū Xī's *Jízhù* and made the result the sole reference for the examination essay for the next five centuries.

**Ming and Qīng critical and devotional readings.**

- *Sìshū méngyǐn* 四書蒙引 [KR1h0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0044) — Cài Qīng 蔡清, the principal mid-Ming examination-school exposition of the *Dàquán*.
- *Lúnyǔ lèikǎo* 論語類考 [KR1h0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0047) and *Mèngzǐ zájì* 孟子雜記 [KR1h0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0048) — Chén Shìyuán 陳士元 (1544), pioneering thematic-philological treatments.
- *Lúnyǔ xué'àn* 論語學案 [KR1h0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0051) — Liú Zōngzhōu 劉宗周, the late-Ming Dōnglín-adjacent 心學-tinged reading.
- *Mèngzǐ shīshuō* 孟子師說 [KR1h0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0055) — Huáng Zōngxī 黃宗羲's record of Liú Zōngzhōu's *Mèngzǐ* lectures, a key Ming–Qīng transition text. (The catalog gives the misspelling 黃宗義 for 黃宗羲, corrected here and in the per-text note.)
- *Rìjiǎng Sìshū jiěyì* 日講四書解義 [KR1h0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0053) — Lāshālǐ 喇沙里 et al., 1677, the Kāngxī court's authoritative imperial-lecture exposition.
- *Sìshū jiǎngyì kùnmiǎn lù* 四書講義困勉錄 [KR1h0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0057) and *Sōngyáng jiǎngyì* 松陽講義 [KR1h0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0058) — Lù Lǒngqí 陸隴其, the canonical Qīng defence of Zhū-school orthodoxy.
- *Lúnyǔ jīqiú piān* 論語稽求篇 [KR1h0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0060), *Sìshū shèngyán* 四書賸言 [KR1h0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0061) and *Dàxué zhèngwén* 大學證文 [KR1h0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0062) — Máo Qílíng 毛奇齡's polemical evidential critiques of Zhū Xī's readings, particularly of the *Dàxué* re-arrangement.
- *Sìshū shìdì* 四書釋地 [KR1h0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0063) — Yán Ruòqú 閻若璩's geographical-historical investigations of *Sìshū* references, a model exercise of Qīng *kǎozhèng* applied to the canon.
- *Xiāngdǎng túkǎo* 鄉黨圖考 [KR1h0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0067) — Jiāng Yǒng 江永's diagrammatic philological reconstruction of the ritual practices behind *Lúnyǔ* "Xiāngdǎng," one of the high points of Qīng evidential scholarship on the *Sìshū*.

### Important persons

- [趙岐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E5%B2%90) (d. 201) — author of the only complete extant Hàn commentary on the *Mèngzǐ*, the textual base of all later *Mèng* commentary.
- [何晏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E6%99%8F) (d. 249) — chief compiler of the *Lúnyǔ jíjiě*, the Cáo-Wèi synthesis that displaced earlier Hàn readings and became the standard *Lúnyǔ* commentary through the Táng.
- [皇侃](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9A%87%E4%BE%83) (488–545) — author of the Liáng-dynasty *Lúnyǔ yìshū*, the principal Six-Dynasties subcommentary, lost in China but transmitted in Japan and re-imported in the Qīng.
- [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) (c. 556–627) — *yīnyì* glossator whose work was absorbed into the standard *Lúnyǔ zhùshū*.
- [邢昺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A2%E6%98%BA) (932–1010) — author of the Northern-Sòng *zhèngyì* on the *Lúnyǔ*, completing the *Shísānjīng zhùshū* layer for the *Analects*.
- [孫奭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E5%A5%AD) (962–1033) — the *Mèngzǐ yīnyì* and the *zhèngyì* traditionally attached to Zhào Qí; the figure most responsible for the *Mèngzǐ*'s formal inscription into the canon in the early Northern Sòng.
- [韓愈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%93%E6%84%88) (768–824) and [李翱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E7%BF%B1) (772–841) — joint authors of the *Lúnyǔ bǐjiě*, the bridge between the late-Táng Confucian revival and the Sòng *Sìshū*.
- [蘇轍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BD%8D) (1039–1112) — author of the *Lúnyǔ shíyí* and *Mèngzǐ jiě*; the Shǔ-school alternative to Chéng-Zhū inside the division.
- [張栻](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%A0%BB) (1133–1180) — the leading Hú-Xiāng-school reader of the *Sìshū*, Zhū Xī's most consequential intellectual interlocutor.
- [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) (1130–1200) — the indispensable figure of the division. His *Sìshū zhāngjù jízhù*, *Sìshū huòwèn*, *Lùn Mèng jīngyì*, and *Zhōngyōng jíluè* between them define the textual unit, the standard reading, and the curricular form that all subsequent KR1h works react to.
- [眞德秀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9E%E5%BE%B7%E7%A7%80) (1178–1235) — *Sìshū jíbiān*; the prototype Sòng *Sìshū* sub-commentarial compendium.
- [金履祥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%91%E5%B1%A5%E7%A5%A5) (1232–1303) — *Dàxué shūyì* and *Lùn Mèng jízhù kǎozhèng*; the most precise late-Sòng / early-Yuán philological exegete of Zhū Xī.
- [胡炳文](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E7%82%B3%E6%96%87) (1250–1333) — *Sìshū tōng*; the canonical Yuán sub-commentary, repeatedly cited in the 1415 *Dàquán*.
- [許謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E8%AC%99) (1270–1337) — *Dú Sìshū cóngshuō*; the Jīn-Huá 金華 lineage reading.
- [胡廣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E5%BB%A3) (1370–1418) — chief editor (*fèngchì zhuàn* 奉敕撰) of the *Sìshū dàquán*; through his compilation the division acquired the orthodoxy under which it was read until 1905.
- [蔡清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E6%B8%85) (1453–1508) — *Sìshū méngyǐn*; the most influential mid-Ming examination-essay handbook.
- [劉宗周](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AE%97%E5%91%A8) (1578–1645) — *Lúnyǔ xué'àn*; the major late-Ming devotional-philosophical reading of the *Analects*.
- [黃宗羲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%AE%97%E7%BE%B2) (1610–1695) — *Mèngzǐ shīshuō*; preserver of Liú Zōngzhōu's *Mèngzǐ* lectures and pivotal Ming-Qīng transition figure.
- [陸隴其](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E9%9A%B4%E5%85%B6) (1630–1693) — *Sìshū jiǎngyì kùnmiǎn lù* and *Sōngyáng jiǎngyì*; the chief Qīng defender of strict Zhū-school orthodoxy.
- [毛奇齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E5%A5%87%E9%BD%A1) (1623–1716) — *Lúnyǔ jīqiú piān*, *Sìshū shèngyán*, *Dàxué zhèngwén*; the most aggressive Qīng critic of Zhū's *Sìshū* arrangements.
- [閻若璩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%96%BB%E8%8B%A5%E7%92%A9) (1636–1704) — *Sìshū shìdì*; the model of geographic-historical *kǎozhèng* applied to the *Sìshū*.
- [江永](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%9F%E6%B0%B8) (1681–1762) — *Xiāngdǎng túkǎo*; the pinnacle of mid-Qīng evidential scholarship on the *Lúnyǔ*'s ritual material.

### Topics

- **Formation of the unit.** The historical question of how four originally heterogeneous texts — two pre-Hàn canonical books (*Lúnyǔ*, *Mèngzǐ*) and two chapters of a Hàn ritual anthology (*Dàxué*, *Zhōngyōng* from the *Lǐjì*) — were welded into a single curricular package by the Chéng brothers and Zhū Xī. The division's organization mirrors this history: there is no single base recension to which all commentaries attach, only the four-book *suite*. See Wilkinson § 28.4.4.

- **The *Mèngzǐ*'s elevation to canon.** Mencius' move from masters branch to *jīng* branch (Wilkinson § 28.5), the 12th-c. "doubting Mencius" (*Yí Mèng* 疑孟) controversy associated with Sī-Mǎ Guāng, and Yú Yǔnwén's [KR1h0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0014) defence are landmark events in late-imperial Confucianism that the KR1h corpus tracks closely.

- **The structure of the *Dàxué*.** Whether Zhū Xī's emendation of the *Dàxué* — re-ordering the *jīng* / *zhuàn* structure, supplying a missing "investigation of things" (*géwù* 格物) paragraph — was textually defensible. This is the single most contested philological question in the division: Hú Wèi's *Dàxué yìzhēn* [KR1h0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0056) and Máo Qílíng's *Dàxué zhèngwén* [KR1h0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0062) are the two principal Qīng investigations on each side of the question.

- **Cheng-Zhu orthodoxy versus alternative readings.** The division stages the long contest between the Dàoxué reading (Chéng-Zhū, *lǐqì* 理氣, *xìnglǐ* 性理) and its critics: Northern-Sòng Shǔxué (Sū Zhé), Hú-Xiāng (Zhāng Shì), Yuán-period internal critics (Chén Tiānxiáng [KR1h0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0032)), late-Ming *xīnxué*-inflected readings (Liú Zōngzhōu, Huáng Zōngxī), and Qīng evidential critique (Máo Qílíng, Yán Ruòqú).

- **The examination essay.** From 1315 onward almost every text in KR1h is shaped by the *Sìshū*'s role as the basis of the *kējǔ* 科舉 essay. Works specifically engineered for the exam — Wáng Chōngyún's *jīngyí* manual [KR1h0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0037), Cài Qīng's *Méngyǐn* [KR1h0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0044) — sit side by side with Lù Lǒngqí's lecture-hall expositions and the Kāngxī court's *Rìjiǎng* [KR1h0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0053). See Wilkinson § 24.8 on the role of the *Sìshū* in late imperial education.

- **Geography, ritual realia, and *kǎozhèng*.** A characteristic Qīng turn: treating the *Sìshū* not as a metaphysical primer but as a historical-philological object. Yán Ruòqú on *Sìshū* geography [KR1h0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0063), Jiāng Yǒng on the *Xiāngdǎng* ritual code [KR1h0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0067), Chén Shìyuán's *lèikǎo* / *zájì* [KR1h0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0047), [KR1h0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0048).

# 樂類 (KR1i)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1i 樂類 *Yuè lèi* — Classics — Music](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

The *Yuè lèi* 樂類 sits inside the *Jīngbù* 經部 (Classics) as the systematic literature on ritual music — pitch-pipe theory (*lǜlǚ* 律呂), instrument construction, modal practice, court song repertoire, and the philological and metaphysical commentary tradition that grew up around them. It is, by Sìkù convention, the smallest of the seven *jīngbù* subdivisions, and its scholarly horizon is conditioned by a peculiar absence: as Wilkinson notes (§34.2), of the original Six Classics it was the *Yuè* 樂 itself that the Hàn "mislaid," with the consequence that the entire premodern Chinese music classic-tradition is, in effect, an ongoing reconstructive enterprise. Authors work from surviving fragments embedded in the *Lǐ jì Yuè jì* 禮記·樂記, the music monographs of the standard histories ("seventeen of the *Histories* have treatises on music and seven on tuning standards" — Wilkinson §34.2), the music chapters of the encyclopaedic *lèishū*, and the live tradition of imperial *yǎyuè* 雅樂 ceremony. The Sìkù compilers therefore treat the genre as canon-adjacent rather than canon-internal: the works gathered here are the *jīngzhuàn* 經傳 ("classic-and-commentary") of a classic that was never in fact transmitted.

The corpus collected at WYG runs from Northern Sòng (1053) to mid-Qián-lóng (mid-18th century), 22 works in all (19 currently cataloged). Three constants run across the seven centuries: (1) repeated imperial commissions to standardize the *zhōnglǜ* 鐘律 system for court ritual — the Sòng *Huángyòu* reform, the Kāngxī *Lǜlǚ zhèngyì* and its sequels; (2) the Cài-Zhū *xiàngshù* 象數 tradition descended from Cài Yuándìng 蔡元定 ([KR1i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0003)), which gave the genre its standard mathematical idiom; and (3) the polemical drive — most visible in [KR1i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0009) *Yuèlǜ quán shū* and the late-Qīng *kǎozhèng* treatises — to anchor music theory in observable measurement rather than speculative number, culminating in Zhū Zàiyù's mathematically explicit equal temperament (Wilkinson §34.2.3).

### Important texts and text clusters

**The Northern Sòng imperial monuments.** Two works survive complete from the official Sòng music reforms.
- *Huángyòu xīn yuè tú jì* 皇祐新樂圖記 [KR1i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0001) — the illustrated official record of the 1053 *zhōnglǜ* recension under Sòng Rénzōng, the foundational Northern-Sòng artefact of imperial *yuèlǜ* design.
- *Yuèshū* 樂書 [KR1i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0002) — Chén Yáng's 200-juan encyclopaedic treatise (presented 1101–1106), the largest single work in the division and the principal anthology of music passages from the Three Rites and the rest of the canon.

**The Cài-Zhū *Dàoxué* tradition.** The interpretive backbone of the Sòng-Yuán-Míng portion of the division.
- *Lǜlǚ xīn shū* 律呂新書 [KR1i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0003) — Cài Yuándìng's foundational two-juan treatise (1187), written in collaboration with Zhū Xī; the standard reference text for every later author in the division.
- *Lǜlǚ chéng shū* 律呂成書 [KR1i0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0006) — Liú Jǐn's 1347 systematic Yuán synthesis of Cài's system with Péng Sī's *Huángzhōng lǜ shuō*.
- *Yuànluò zhì yuè* 苑洛志樂 [KR1i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0007) — Hán Bāngqí's 20-juan Míng treatise that opens with a "direct exposition" of Cài's *Xīn shū* and then reconstructs the six legendary court dances by *wǔdé* element-correspondence.
- *Zhōnglǜ tōngkǎo* 鐘律通考 [KR1i0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0008) — Ní Fù's 1526 mid-Míng synthesis, doctrinally orthodox to Cài but less polemically forceful than [KR1i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0007).

**Reconstruction-of-lost-music projects.** The recurrent enterprise of supplying-what-was-lost (*bǔ wáng* 補亡).
- *Sè pǔ* 瑟譜 [KR1i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0004) — Xióng Pénglái's six-juan reconstruction (early Yuán) of the *sè* 瑟 zither tradition for the temple-hall *yòugē* 侑歌, with the most detailed pre-Míng performance-practice notation for any single classical instrument.
- *Sháowǔ jiǔchéng yuèbǔ* 韶舞九成樂補 [KR1i0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0005) — Yú Zǎi's diagrammatic reconstruction of the legendary *Sháo* 韶 court dance.
- *Gǔ yuè jīng zhuàn* 古樂經傳 [KR1i0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0013) — Lǐ Guāngdì's Kāngxī-era reconstruction of the lost *Yuè jīng* itself, by extracting the music-officer chapters from the *Zhōu lǐ* and treating them as a recovered *Jīng* glossed by the *Lǐ jì Yuè jì*.
- *Gǔ yuè shū* 古樂書 [KR1i0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0014) — Yìng Huīqiān's two-juan early-Qīng treatise, distinguished by its precise reconstruction of the *Kǎogōng jì* bell-shape geometry.

**Zhū Zàiyù and the discovery of equal temperament.** The intellectual high-water mark of the genre and one of the few premodern Chinese mathematical achievements with global comparative significance (Wilkinson §34.2.3).
- *Yuèlǜ quán shū* 樂律全書 [KR1i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0009) — the 42-juan collected works of Zhū Zàiyù (presented 1606), within which the *Lǜlǚ jīngyì* 律呂精義 (1584–1596) gives the mathematically explicit derivation of *shíèr píngjūn lǜ* 十二平均律 — the twelfth root of two computed to twenty-five-decimal-place accuracy, a decade before Simon Stevin's parallel European derivation.
- *Lǜlǚ chǎnwēi* 律呂闡微 [KR1i0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0021) — Jiāng Yǒng's mid-Qīng exposition of Zhū's mathematical method, recomputing it with Zǔ Chōngzhī's high-precision *mìlǜ* 密率 (π = 22/7, refined).

**The Máo Qílíng trilogy and its school.** The most polemically distinctive late-Kāngxī cluster.
- *Shèngyù yuèběn jiěshuō* 聖諭樂本解說 [KR1i0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0015) — Máo's clause-by-clause commentary on Kāngxī's *Sacred Edict* on the *jìng* 1 / *wéi* 3 and *gé bā xiāng shēng* doctrines.
- *Huángyán dìngshēng lù* 皇言定聲錄 [KR1i0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0016) — the eight-juan theoretical core, propounding Máo's distinctive *jiǔ shēng qī diào* 九聲七調 ("nine tones and seven modes") doctrine.
- *Jìngshān yuèlù* 竟山樂錄 [KR1i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0017) — Máo's most radical work, dismissing the entire pre-Sòng *sānfēn sǔnyì* tradition as fiction on the basis of a (lost) Tang flute-fingering chart.
- *Lǐshì xuéyuè lù* 李氏學樂錄 [KR1i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0018) — the disciple Lǐ Gōng's record of his studies with Máo, the only systematic exposition of Máo's seven-tone *qìsè* 器色 fingering doctrine.

**Mid-Qīng *kǎozhèng* music theory.** The empirical, philologically rigorous treatises that close the division.
- *Yuèlǜ biǎowēi* 樂律表微 [KR1i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0019) — Hú Yànshēng's eight-juan four-part treatise (length-pitch / tone discrimination / mode construction / instrument examination), arguing that the entire *biànlǜ* 變律 (derived-pitch) apparatus from Jīng Fáng to Cài Yuándìng is unnecessary.
- *Lǜlǚ xīn lùn* 律呂新論 [KR1i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0020) — Jiāng Yǒng's most theoretically precise work, deriving every doctrinal proposition from empirical sources (the *qín* string-fret nodes, actually-cut pitch-pipes, the volumetric basis of the Zhōu *fǔ* 鬴 measure) and rejecting *biànlǜ*, *sānfēn sǔnyì*, and wind-watching as insufficiently anchored.
- *Qín zhǐ* 琴旨 [KR1i0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0022) — Wáng Tǎn's two-juan systematic treatise on *qínlǜ* 琴律 (zither-string pitch theory), held by the Sìkù compilers to be the most accomplished mid-Qīng work in this niche.

(Three further texts — [KR1i0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0010) *Yù zhì Lǜlǚ zhèngyì* of Kāngxī, [KR1i0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0011) *Hòu biān* of the Qiánlóng court, and [KR1i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0012) *Qīndìng Shī jīng yuèpǔ quán shū* — are present in the catalog but not yet cataloged here. These are the principal Qīng imperial music codifications and form the official counterpart to the private treatises listed above.)

### Topics

- **The status of the *Yuè jīng*.** Whether the music classic existed before the Qín book-burning, whether anything substantive of it can be recovered from the *Lǐ jì Yuè jì* and the *Zhōu lǐ* music chapters, and what counts as a defensible reconstruction. The defining debate of the division; foregrounded most explicitly by [李光地](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%85%89%E5%9C%B0) in [KR1i0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0013) but implicit in every reconstruction project.
- ***Lǜlǚ* 律呂 and the mathematics of pitch.** The derivation of the twelve pitch-pipes from the *huángzhōng* 黃鐘, the *sānfēn sǔnyì* 三分損益 (cut-and-add-by-thirds) generating procedure, and the inability of *sānfēn* to close the circle and return to the starting pitch — the mathematical problem that motivates the *biànlǜ* 變律 (derived-pitch) tradition (Jīng Fáng, Qián Lèzhī, Cài Yuándìng) and that [朱載堉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E8%BC%89%E5%A0%89) resolved by abandoning *sānfēn* altogether for the twelfth root of two.
- ***Biànlǜ* and the *èr biàn shēng*.** Whether derived pitches and the two derived tones (*biàngōng*, *biànzhǐ*) are necessary at all. Defended by Cài Yuándìng [KR1i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0003); rejected by [KR1i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0019) and by Jiāng Yǒng [KR1i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0020).
- **Imperial reform vs. private scholarship.** The repeated tension between standardizing court ritual music by imperial fiat (the Sòng *Huángyòu*, the Kāngxī *Zhèngyì*) and the private reconstructive scholarship that critiques and extends it. Most pointed in Máo Qílíng's positioning of his trilogy as commentary on Kāngxī's own *Sacred Edict*.
- **Empirical anchoring.** The mid-Qīng *kǎozhèng* turn that requires music-theoretical claims be tied to measurable phenomena: cut pipes, *qín* fret nodes (*huī* 徽), the volumetric basis of the Zhōu *fǔ*. Definitive in Jiāng Yǒng [KR1i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0020) and Hú Yànshēng [KR1i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0019).
- **The *Sháo* and the legendary court dances.** The recurrent attempt to reconstruct the music and choreography of the legendary sage-king dances (*Yúnmén*, *Xiánchí*, *Dàzhāng*, *Dàxià*, *Dàsháo*, *Dàhù*), known by name only from the *Zhōu guān*. Pursued by Yú Zǎi [KR1i0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0005), Hán Bāngqí [KR1i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0007), and Zhū Zàiyù [KR1i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0009) (the last with detailed dance-step diagrams that, as Wilkinson §34.2 notes, are the first such surviving for Chinese ritual dance).
- **Notation and instrumental practice.** The *gōngchě* 工尺 fingering tradition, the *qín* and *sè* zither traditions, and the question whether any pre-Sòng music can in fact be performed. Foregrounded by Xióng Pénglái [KR1i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0004), Máo Qílíng [KR1i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0017), Lǐ Gōng [KR1i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0018), and Wáng Tǎn [KR1i0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1i/KR1i0022).

### Timeline

# 小學類 (KR1j)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR1j 小學類 *Xiǎoxué lèi* — Classics — Philology and Lexicography](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

*Xiǎoxué* 小學 — literally "lesser learning," but in bibliographic usage the *study of language and the characters* — is the last of the ten sub-categories of the Sìkù quánshū's *Jīngbù* 經部 (`KR1`). From the Hàn down to the early twentieth century, every work on script, lexicon, dialect, or rhyme was classed here rather than with secular philology, on the axiomatic grounds that scrupulous understanding of the *Wǔjīng* 五經 depended on a correct grasp of the words and graphs in which the Classics were written (Wilkinson § 6.2.1). The catalog therefore gathers together what a modern reader would call dictionaries, paleographic studies, dialect glossaries, treatises on the *liùshū* 六書, rhyme tables, and reconstructions of archaic pronunciation, and treats them as a single ancillary discipline serving classical exegesis.

The division falls naturally into three traditional clusters, in the order the Sìkù editors themselves preserved: (1) **訓詁** *xùngǔ* — the *Ěryǎ* 爾雅 lineage of glossaries and synonymicons ([KR1j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0002)–[KR1j0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0016)); (2) **字書** *zìshū* — the *Shuōwén* 說文 / *Yùpiān* 玉篇 / *Kāngxī zìdiǎn* 康熙字典 lineage of character dictionaries, *liùshū* analyses, and clerical- and seal-script studies ([KR1j0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0017)–[KR1j0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0053)); and (3) **韻書** *yùnshū* — the *Qièyùn* 切韻 → *Guǎngyùn* 廣韻 → *Jíyùn* 集韻 line of rhyme books, the *děngyùn* 等韻 rhyme-table tradition, and the Míng–Qīng *gǔyīnxué* 古音學 reconstruction of archaic phonology ([KR1j0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0054)–[KR1j0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0087)). The works span roughly two millennia, from the late Western Hàn *Jíjiù piān* 急就篇 of Shǐ Yóu 史遊 (c. -33) to the late-Qiánlóng imperial compilations of 1773–1786; the great inflection points are the late Hàn (Xǔ Shèn 許慎, Liú Xī 劉熙), the late Tángliutu·early Sòng restoration (the Xú brothers 徐鉉/徐鍇, *Guǎngyùn*, *Jíyùn*), and the Qīng *kǎojù* 考據 reconstruction of Old Chinese phonology associated with Gù Yánwǔ 顧炎武 and Jiāng Yǒng 江永.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The *Ěryǎ* 爾雅 cluster (訓詁).** The pre-Hàn synonym-thesaurus *Ěryǎ* 爾雅 [KR1j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0002) — a Classic in its own right since the Kāichéng 開成 stone *Jīng* of 837 (Wilkinson § 6.2.1.2) — anchors the entire division. The Sòng *zhèngyì* 正義 lineage is represented by Xíng Bǐng's 邢昺 *Ěryǎ shū* 爾雅疏 [KR1j0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0003) and the composite *Ěryǎ zhùshū* 爾雅注疏 [KR1j0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0004) coupling Guō Pú's 郭璞 (276–324) Jìn-era notes to Xíng Bǐng's sub-commentary; Zhèng Qiáo's 鄭樵 own *Ěryǎ zhù* 爾雅註 [KR1j0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0005) supplies a more independent Southern Sòng reading. Yáng Xióng's 揚雄 *Fāngyán* 方言 [KR1j0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0006) (full title *Yóuxuān shǐzhě juédài yǔshì biéguó fāngyán* 輶軒使者絕代語釋別國方言) extends the *Ěryǎ* method to regional dialect, and Liú Xī's 劉熙 *Shìmíng* 釋名 [KR1j0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0007) (Wilkinson § 6.2.1.4) turns it toward etymology by rhyming pun. Zhāng Yī's 張揖 Wèi-period *Guǎngyǎ* 廣雅 [KR1j0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0008) is the standard expansion. Sòng additions to the genre — Lù Diàn's 陸佃 *Píyǎ* 埤雅 [KR1j0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0011) and Luó Yuàn's 羅願 *Ěryǎ yì* 爾雅翼 [KR1j0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0012) — concentrate on natural-history terminology. The Míng *Piányǎ* 駢雅 [KR1j0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0013) of Zhū Móuwěi 朱謀㙔 and Qīng *Xù Fāngyán* 續方言 [KR1j0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0015), *Biéyǎ* 別雅 [KR1j0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0016), and *Zìgǔ* 字詁 [KR1j0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0014) are the late-imperial supplements.

**The *Shuōwén* 說文 cluster (字書, Hàn–Sòng).** Xǔ Shèn's 許慎 *Shuōwén jiězì* 說文解字 [KR1j0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0018) of 121 CE (Wilkinson § 6.2.1.3) is the foundational Chinese character dictionary: 9,353 entries (in the postface count) under 540 *bù* 部 classifiers, organized by graphic structure rather than by sound or meaning, and the perennial source for *liùshū* analysis. The Southern-Táng *Xú* brothers preserve the work in two recensions — Xú Kǎi's 徐鍇 *Shuōwén xìzhuàn* 說文繫傳 [KR1j0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0019) (the *Xiǎo Xú běn* 小徐本) and its *Zhuànyùnpǔ* 篆韻譜 [KR1j0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0021). Imperially-commissioned Sòng character-books continue the lineage: Sīmǎ Guāng's 司馬光 *Lèipiān* 類篇 [KR1j0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0029), the *Yùpiān*-based *Chóngxiū Yùpiān* 重修玉篇 [KR1j0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0022) and *Dàguǎng yìhuì Yùpiān* 大廣益會玉篇 [KR1j0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0056) of Chén Péngnián 陳彭年, and Jiǎ Chāngcháo's 賈昌朝 *Qúnjīng yīnbiàn* 羣經音辨 [KR1j0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0010) for variant readings across the Classics.

**Standard-form and clerical-script handbooks (Táng–Sòng).** Yán Yuánsūn's 顏元孫 *Gānlù zìshū* 干祿字書 [KR1j0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0023), Zhāng Cān's 張參 *Wǔjīng wénzì* 五經文字 [KR1j0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0024) and Táng Xuándù's 唐玄度 *Jiǔjīng zìyàng* 九經字樣 [KR1j0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0025) regulate the orthography of Classical citations, in the context of the Kāichéng stone *Jīng* project. Guō Zhōngshù's 郭忠恕 *Hànjiǎn* 汗簡 [KR1j0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0026) and *Pèiguī* 佩觽 [KR1j0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0027) and Xià Sǒng's 夏竦 *Gǔwén sìshēng yùn* 古文四聲韻 [KR1j0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0028) are the principal Sòng compilations of pre-Qín *gǔwén* 古文 graph forms. Zhāng Yǒu's 張有 *Fùgǔ biān* 復古編 [KR1j0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0031), Lóu Jī's 婁機 *Bān-Mǎ zìlèi* 班馬字類 [KR1j0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0032) and *Hànlì zìyuán* 漢隸字源 [KR1j0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0033), Xuē Shànggōng's 薛尚功 *Lìdài zhōngdǐng yíqì kuǎnshì fǎtiē* 歷代鐘鼎彝器款識法帖 [KR1j0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0030), and Lǐ Cóngzhōu's 李從周 *Zìtōng* 字通 [KR1j0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0035) together constitute the Sòng paleographic / epigraphic strand. The Liáo Buddhist lexicon *Lóngkān shǒujiàn* 龍龕手鑑 [KR1j0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0036) of Shì Xíngjūn 釋行均, included in the WYG over Qiánlóng objections, preserves the most extensive collection of variant graphs of its time.

***Liùshū* 六書 theory (Sòng–Míng).** A specifically theoretical sub-strand grows out of the *Shuōwén* — Dài Tóng's 戴侗 *Liùshū gù* 六書故 [KR1j0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0034), Yáng Huán's 楊桓 *Liùshū tǒng* 六書統 [KR1j0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0037), Zhōu Bóqí's 周伯琦 *Liùshū zhèngé* 六書正譌 [KR1j0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0041) and *Shuōwén zìyuán* 說文字原 [KR1j0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0040), Lǐ Wénzhòng's 李文仲 *Zìjiàn* 字鑑 [KR1j0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0039), Zhào Huīqiān's 趙撝謙 *Liùshū běnyì* 六書本義 [KR1j0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0043), and Yè Bǐngjìng's 葉秉敬 *Zìluán* 字㝈 [KR1j0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0047). Wú Qiūyǎn's 吾丘衍 *Zhōu-Qín kèshí shìyīn* 周秦刻石釋音 [KR1j0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0038) applies the same analytic apparatus to bronze and stone inscriptions.

**The *Qièyùn* 切韻 → *Guǎngyùn* 廣韻 line (韻書, Sòng).** The unmodified pre-imperial Northern Sòng *Yuánběn Guǎngyùn* 原本廣韻 [KR1j0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0054) and the 1011 imperially-revised *Chóngxiū Guǎngyùn* 重修廣韻 [KR1j0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0055) of Chén Péngnián 陳彭年 and Qiū Yōng 丘雍 transmit the 206-rhyme system descending from Lù Fǎyán's 陸法言 *Qièyùn* 切韻 (601) and the Táng *Tángyùn* 唐韻 (Wilkinson § 1.2.2). Dīng Dù's 丁度 *Jíyùn* 集韻 [KR1j0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0057) (1067), with Sīmǎ Guāng, expands the rhyme dictionary to over 53,000 lemmas; his *Lǐbù yùnlüè* 禮部韻略 in its later glossed redactions — *Fù shìwén hùzhù Lǐbù yùnlüè* 附釋文互註禮部韻略 [KR1j0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0060), the Máo Huǎng / Máo Jūzhèng 毛晃/毛居正 *Zēngxiū hùzhù Lǐbù yùnlüè* 增修互註禮部韻略 [KR1j0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0061), Ōuyáng Délóng 歐陽德隆 and Guō Shǒuzhèng's *Yāyùn shìyí* 增修校正押韻釋疑 [KR1j0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0062) and Yáng Bóyán's 楊伯嵒 *Jiǔjīng bǔyùn* 九經補韻 [KR1j0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0063) — is the rhyme handbook of the Sòng examination system. Sīmǎ Guāng's *Qièyùn zhǐzhǎngtú* 切韻指掌圖 [KR1j0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0058) is the canonical Northern Sòng *děngyùn* 等韻 rhyme table.

**Jīn–Yuán–Míng rhyme books.** Hán Dàozhāo's 韓道昭 Jīn-period *Wǔyīn jíyùn* 五音集韻 [KR1j0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0064) reorganizes the *Guǎngyùn* by initial-tone phonetics; Huáng Gōngshào 黃公紹 and Xióng Zhōng's 熊忠 *Gǔjīn yùnhuì jǔyào* 古今韻會擧要 [KR1j0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0065) is the principal Yuán synthesis. The anonymous *Sìshēng quánxíng děngzǐ* 四聲全形等子 [KR1j0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0066) and Liú Jiàn's 劉鑑 *Jīngshǐ zhèngyīn qièyùn zhǐnán* 經史正音切韻指南 [KR1j0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0067) continue the rhyme-table tradition. Yuè Sháofèng 樂韶鳳 and Sòng Lián's 宋濂 *Hóngwǔ zhèngyùn* 洪武正韻 [KR1j0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0068) is the Hóngwǔ-imperial standard.

**Míng–Qīng *gǔyīnxué* 古音學 (archaic phonology).** Yáng Shèn 楊愼 led the first systematic Míng reconstruction effort with *Gǔyīn cóngmù* 古音叢目 [KR1j0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0069), *Gǔyīn lüèlì* 古音略例 [KR1j0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0070), *Zhuǎnzhù gǔyīn lüè* 轉注古音略 [KR1j0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0071), *Qízì yùn* 奇字韻 [KR1j0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0044) and *Gǔyīn piánzì* 古音駢字 [KR1j0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0045). Chén Dì's 陳第 *Qū-Sòng gǔyīn yì* 屈宋古音義 [KR1j0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0073) decisively rejected the *xiéyùn* 叶韻 doctrine of accommodation. The early-Qīng monument is the five-treatise *Yīnxué wǔshū* 音學五書 of Gù Yánwǔ 顧炎武: *Yīn lùn* 音論 [KR1j0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0078), *Shī běnyīn* 詩本音 [KR1j0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0079), *Yì yīn* 易音 [KR1j0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0080), *Tángyùn zhèng* 唐韻正 [KR1j0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0081) and *Gǔyīn biǎo* 古音表 [KR1j0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0082), with the supplementary *Yùn bǔ zhèng* 韻補正 [KR1j0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0083). Máo Qíling's 毛奇齡 *Gǔjīn tōngyùn* 古今通韻 [KR1j0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0084) and *Yì yùn* 易韻 [KR1j0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0085) and Jì Róngshū's 紀容舒 *Sūnshì Tángyùn kǎo* 孫氏唐韻考 [KR1j0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0086) are the principal mid-Qīng reactions to and corrections of Gù; Jiāng Yǒng's 江永 *Gǔyùn biāozhǔn* 古韻標準 [KR1j0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0087) of 1759 represents the next refinement and the bridge to Duàn Yùcái 段玉裁.

**Qīng imperial *xiǎoxué* compilations.** The *Yùdìng Kāngxī zìdiǎn* 御定康熙字典 [KR1j0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0048) of 1716 (Wilkinson § 6.2.1.5), under the nominal headship of Zhāng Yùshū 張玉書 and Chén Tíngjìng 陳廷敬, contains 47,043 head-characters arranged by the 214-classifier system inherited from the *Zìhuì* 字彙, and remained the authoritative character dictionary until the twentieth century. Lǐ Guāngdì's 李光地 *Yùdìng yīnyùn chǎnwēi* 御定音韻闡微 [KR1j0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0074) (1726) is the matching imperial rhyme-book. The Qiánlóng-era *Qīndìng tóngwén yùntǒng* 欽定同文韻統 [KR1j0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0075), *Qīndìng xiéyùn huìjí* 欽定叶韻彙輯 [KR1j0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0076) and *Qīndìng yīnyùn shùwēi* 欽定音韻述微 [KR1j0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0077) complete the suite of state-sponsored phonological references. Gù Àijí's 顧藹吉 *Lì biàn* 隸辨 [KR1j0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0052) and Zhōu Jìng's 周靖 *Zhuànlì kǎoyì* 篆隸考異 [KR1j0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0053) are the classic Kāngxī-era clerical-script reference works.

**Other notable items.** The Hàn primer *Jíjiù piān* 急就篇 [KR1j0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0017) of Shǐ Yóu 史遊, transmitted with Yán Shīgǔ's 顏師古 Táng notes and Wáng Yìnglín's 王應麟 Sòng *bǔzhù* 補注, is the earliest character primer preserved entire and an important source for Hàn lexicon. Yán Shīgǔ's *Kuāngmiù zhèngsú* 匡謬正俗 [KR1j0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0009) is a unique Táng compendium of philological corrections. Shū Tiānmín's 舒天民 Yuán-period *Liùyì gāngmù* 六藝綱目 [KR1j0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0088) is a primer that summarizes the *liùyì* 六藝 (the six elementary arts) and is here grouped with *xiǎoxué* by association with the *Zhōulǐ* curriculum.

### Important persons

- [許愼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E6%84%BC) — Eastern Hàn lexicographer of the *Wǔjīng*; compiler of the *Shuōwén jiězì* 說文解字, the structural foundation of all subsequent Chinese character lexicography.
- [揚雄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%9A%E9%9B%84) — Western Hàn polymath whose *Fāngyán* 方言 inaugurated dialect lexicography in China and remained the only such work for over a millennium.
- [劉熙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E7%86%99) — Late Hàn scholar of the *Bèihǎi* 北海 circle; author of the *Shìmíng*, the earliest sustained etymological project working through phonetic affinity (*shēngxùn* 聲訓).
- [郭璞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E7%92%9E) — Western Jìn polymath whose annotations to the *Ěryǎ*, *Fāngyán* and *Shānhǎijīng* defined the medieval reception of all three.
- [顏師古](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E5%B8%AB%E5%8F%A4) — Táng exegete whose annotations dominate the transmission of the *Hànshū* and supply the standard medieval gloss on the *Jíjiù piān* and on textual variants generally.
- [徐鉉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E9%89%89), [徐鍇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E9%8D%87) — The Xú brothers of the Southern Táng who rescued the *Shuōwén* from textual collapse and produced the two recensions (*Dà Xú* and *Xiǎo Xú*) on which all later editions depend.
- [邢昺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A2%E6%98%BA) — Northern Sòng compiler of the official *Ěryǎ shū*, fixing the Sòng *zhèngyì* form of the work.
- [陳彭年](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%BD%AD%E5%B9%B4), [丘雍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%98%E9%9B%8D) — Lead editors of the 1011 imperial *Chóngxiū Guǎngyùn* and of the 1013 *Chóngxiū Yùpiān*, the foundational Sòng rhyme- and character-books.
- [丁度](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%81%E5%BA%A6) — Compiler of the *Jíyùn* and *Lǐbù yùnlüè*, which fixed the rhyme system of Sòng examination poetry.
- [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) — Took over the *Lèipiān* and the *Jíyùn* after Dīng Dù's death and contributed the *Qièyùn zhǐzhǎngtú*, bridging dictionary and rhyme-table traditions.
- [鄭樵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E6%A8%B5) — Southern Sòng historian whose theoretical interventions on *wén* 文 and *zì* 字 reshaped how the *Shuōwén* was read, including by Duàn Yùcái.
- [戴侗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%B4%E4%BE%97), [周伯琦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E4%BC%AF%E7%90%A6), [趙撝謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E6%92%9D%E8%AC%99) — The principal Sòng–Míng *liùshū* theorists.
- [楊愼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E6%84%BC) — Míng scholar in exile in Yúnnán who produced the first sustained corpus of works on archaic rhyme, framing the eventual Qīng programme.
- [陳第](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E7%AC%AC) — Late-Míng author of the *Máoshī gǔyīn kǎo* and *Qū-Sòng gǔyīn yì*; rejected the *xiéyùn* doctrine and inaugurated the rigorous reconstruction of pre-Qín phonology.
- [顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6) — Early-Qīng polymath; the *Yīnxué wǔshū* 音學五書 is the founding monument of Qīng *gǔyīnxué*.
- [毛奇齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E5%A5%87%E9%BD%A1) — Vigorous critic of Gù Yánwǔ; preserved an alternative reading of Old Chinese rhyme that fed into eighteenth-century debate.
- [江永](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%9F%E6%B0%B8) — Anhuī-Wǎn 皖 school philologist who refined Gù's rhyme groups and trained Dài Zhèn 戴震; *Gǔyùn biāozhǔn* is the immediate predecessor of Duàn Yùcái's seventeen-rhyme system.
- [張玉書](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E7%8E%89%E6%9B%B8), [陳廷敬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%BB%B7%E6%95%AC) — Nominal supervisors of the *Kāngxī zìdiǎn* compilation (1710–1716).
- [李光地](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%85%89%E5%9C%B0) — Compiler of the *Yīnyùn chǎnwēi*, the official Kāngxī rhyme-book companion to the *Zìdiǎn*.

### Topics

- **The unity of *xiǎoxué* with classical exegesis.** Throughout the division, no work is offered as a study of language for its own sake; the *Ěryǎ* and *Shuōwén* are framed as instruments for understanding the *Wǔjīng* and *Shàngshū*, and the rhyme books as aids for the examination essay and the recitation of the *Shī*. This is the bibliographic premise that holds the category together (Wilkinson § 6.2.1).
- **訓詁 vs. 字書 vs. 韻書.** The three sub-genres correspond to the three faces of the Chinese sign: meaning (*yì* 義), graph (*xíng* 形), and sound (*yīn* 音). Each generates its own canonical chain — *Ěryǎ* → *Fāngyán* → *Guǎngyǎ*; *Shuōwén* → *Yùpiān* → *Lèipiān* → *Kāngxī zìdiǎn*; *Qièyùn* → *Guǎngyùn* → *Jíyùn* → *Hóngwǔ zhèngyùn* — and the dialectic between them is one of the principal interpretive problems of the field.
- **The *liùshū* 六書.** Xǔ Shèn's six analytic categories (*xiàngxíng* 象形, *zhǐshì* 指事, *huìyì* 會意, *xíngshēng* 形聲, *zhuǎnzhù* 轉注, *jiǎjiè* 假借) become the master grid for all later character analysis (Wilkinson § 2.4); their interpretation, especially of *zhuǎnzhù* and *jiǎjiè*, is contested from Dài Tóng through Zhōu Bóqí to the Qīng Shuōwén scholars.
- **The 540-*bù* vs. 214-classifier systems.** The reorganization of the character lexicon away from Xǔ Shèn's 540 *Shuōwén* classifiers toward the 214-classifier scheme stabilized by the *Zìhuì* 字彙 (Wànlì era) and inherited by the *Kāngxī zìdiǎn* is the principal structural transformation of the *zìshū* tradition.
- **The *Qièyùn* / *Guǎngyùn* phonological system.** The 206-rhyme system of the *Qièyùn* / *Guǎngyùn*, later collapsed into the 106 *Píngshuǐ* 平水 rhymes for examination use, supplies the Middle-Chinese reference grid against which Old Chinese is later reconstructed (Wilkinson § 1.2.2).
- ***Xiéyùn* 叶韻 vs. *gǔyīn* 古音.** Sòng scholars (following Wú Yù 吳棫, [KR1j0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0059)) treated mismatches between the rhymes of the *Shī* and contemporary pronunciation as ad-hoc *xiéyùn* accommodations. Chén Dì rejected this in principle, arguing for systematic phonological change over time; Gù Yánwǔ converted this into a research programme. The Qīng *gǔyīnxué* tradition develops from this rejection.
- **Imperial standardization.** From the Kāichéng stone *Jīng* through the *Hóngwǔ zhèngyùn* to the Kāngxī- and Qiánlóng-era imperial dictionaries, the state repeatedly intervenes in *xiǎoxué* to fix examination orthography and pronunciation; *昭同文之治* (Wilkinson § 6.2.1.5) is an explicit imperial frame for the *Kāngxī zìdiǎn*.
- **Paleography and inscriptional evidence.** Sòng *jīnshíxué* 金石學 (Xuē Shànggōng, Guō Zhōngshù) and Yuán *gǔwén* analysis (Wú Qiūyǎn) extend *xiǎoxué* to bronze and stone inscriptions, prefiguring the much fuller integration of oracle-bone and bronze evidence after 1899.
- **Dialect and the spoken vernacular.** Outside Yáng Xióng's *Fāngyán* and its Qīng *Xù Fāngyán*, the spoken language is largely absent from the division — a structural consequence of the classical-text orientation of *xiǎoxué* (Wilkinson § 6.2.1).
- **Clerical and seal scripts.** Lóu Jī's 漢隸 studies, Wú Qiūyǎn's *Zhōu-Qín kèshí*, Gù Àijí's *Lì biàn* and Zhōu Jìng's *Zhuànlì kǎoyì* form a distinct connoisseurial sub-tradition focused on the visual history of the script.
