# 正史類 (KR2a)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2a 正史類 *Zhèngshǐ lèi* — Histories — Standard Histories](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR2a 正史類 (*Zhèngshǐ lèi*, "Standard Histories") collects the canonical dynastic histories of imperial China together with their classical commentaries, supplements, and works of textual rectification. The category is the head of KR2 史部 (Histories), and within the *Sìkù quánshū* taxonomy it occupies the most prestigious position among historical genres: every other history-section subcategory — annals (編年), unofficial history (別史), miscellaneous history (雜史), biography (傳記), geography (地理), bureaucratic monographs (職官), bibliography (目錄), and so on — is defined in part by its difference from, or supplement to, the *zhèngshǐ*. The defining textual form is the *jìzhuàn tǐ* 紀傳體 ("annals-and-biographies form") modelled on Sīmǎ Qiān's 司馬遷 *Shǐjì* 史記 and Bān Gù's 班固 *Hànshū* 漢書, in which a court chronicle (*běnjì* 本紀) is followed by chronological tables (*biǎo* 表), topical treatises (*zhì* 志 / *shū* 書), and exemplary biographies (*lièzhuàn* 列傳). Wilkinson (§49) traces how the term *zhèngshǐ* itself was first applied to single-dynasty *jìzhuàn* histories in the Liáng 梁 (502–57), and how dynastic sponsorship of an "official" history of the previous dynasty became, from the early Táng onwards, one of the principal devices by which a new regime affirmed its claim to *zhèngtǒng* 正統 (legitimate succession; see Wilkinson §49.5, §A.2.6).

The thirty-nine texts in this division cover the full chronological span of the imperial era, from the *Shǐjì* (composed under Hàn Wǔdì 漢武帝 in the late 2nd / early 1st century BCE) to the *Qīng shǐ gǎo* 清史稿 (drafted 1914–27 by holdover Qīng officials under the Republic). They divide cleanly into three layers: (i) the twenty-four *zhèngshǐ* canonized in the *Sìkù* selection plus the Republican-era *Qīng shǐ gǎo* — twenty-five core histories in all, one per legitimate dynasty (with *Sānguó zhì* 三國志 covering the Three Kingdoms collectively and three parallel pairs of *Tángshū* / *Wǔdài shǐ* / *Hòu Hànshū*-with-treatises representing successive recensions); (ii) the great early commentaries that became inseparable from their host texts — Péi Yīn's 裴駰 *Jíjiě* 集解, Sīmǎ Zhēn's 司馬貞 *Suǒyǐn* 索隱, and Zhāng Shǒujié's 張守節 *Zhèngyì* 正義 on the *Shǐjì*; Yán Shīgǔ's 顏師古 commentary on the *Hànshū*; Péi Sōngzhī's 裴松之 commentary on the *Sānguó zhì*; Lǐ Xián's 李賢 commentary on the *Hòu Hànshū*; (iii) Sòng– and Qīng–era works of *kǎoyì* 考異, *bǔyí* 補遺, *jiūmiù* 糾謬 and *biànwù* 辨誤 — corrections, supplements, and tabular reconstructions that became part of the apparatus through which the histories were read.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The Sì shǐ 四史 ("Four Histories") cluster.** The first four *zhèngshǐ* — *Shǐjì*, *Hànshū*, *Hòu Hànshū*, and *Sānguó zhì* — are by long convention treated as a unit, both because they cover the formative imperial period (Hàn through Three Kingdoms) and because they are the most stylistically and historiographically accomplished members of the genre. Wilkinson (§59) treats them together as the foundational corpus of historical Chinese.

- *Shǐjì* 史記 [KR2a0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0001) — Sīmǎ Qiān's universal history from the Yellow Thearch to Hàn Wǔdì, the prototype of every later *zhèngshǐ* and the origin of the *jìzhuàn* form. Carried in the WYG together with the three Táng-era commentaries below as the *Sānjiā zhù* 三家注 *Shǐjì*.
- *Shǐjì jíjiě* 史記集解 [KR2a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0002) — Péi Yīn's mid-5th-century compilation of Hàn–Six-Dynasties glosses on the *Shǐjì*, the first of the *Sānjiā zhù* and the channel through which most pre-Táng *Shǐjì* scholarship survives.
- *Shǐjì suǒyǐn* 史記索隱 [KR2a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0003) — Sīmǎ Zhēn's Táng commentary, especially valued for its critical engagement with Péi Yīn and for the *Bǔ Sānhuáng běnjì* 補三皇本紀.
- *Shǐjì zhèngyì* 史記正義 [KR2a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0004) — Zhāng Shǒujié's Táng commentary, the most geographically detailed of the three and the principal source for Táng-period topographical identifications of *Shǐjì* place names.
- *Qián Hànshū* 前漢書 [KR2a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0007) — Bān Gù's history of the Western Hàn, the first single-dynasty *zhèngshǐ* and the model of organization (annals + tables + treatises + biographies, all bounded by one dynasty) followed by every successor.
- *Hòu Hànshū* 後漢書 [KR2a0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0009) — Fàn Yè's Liú-Sòng compilation covering the Eastern Hàn, transmitted with the eight *zhì* (treatises) of Sīmǎ Biāo's 司馬彪 *Xù Hàn shū* 續漢書 (annotated by Liú Zhāo 劉昭) substituted for the lost monographs Fàn Yè had planned, and with Lǐ Xián's 李賢 Táng commentary.
- *Sānguó zhì* 三國志 [KR2a0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0012) — Chén Shòu's late-3rd-century history of Wèi, Shǔ, and Wú, indispensable for its expansion in the early 5th century by Péi Sōngzhī, whose commentary preserves more than two hundred lost works in extenso.

**Comparative and corrective Sòng scholarship on the Sì shǐ.** The Sòng marked the first sustained scholarly engagement with the foundational histories as objects of *kǎozhèng* 考證.

- *Bān-Mǎ yìtóng* 班馬異同 [KR2a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0008) — Ní Sī's 倪思 systematic juxtaposition of the *Shǐjì* and *Hànshū*, registering Bān Gù's silent edits to passages he inherited from Sīmǎ Qiān, with marginal evaluation by Liú Chénwēng 劉辰翁.
- *Bǔ Hòu Hànshū niánbiǎo* 補後漢書年表 [KR2a0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0010) — Xióng Fāng's 熊方 reconstruction of the chronological tables Fàn Yè never compiled, supplying for the *Hòu Hànshū* the *biǎo* layer that the *Shǐjì* / *Hànshū* model required.
- *Liǎng Hàn kānwù bǔyí* 兩漢刋誤補遺 [KR2a0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0011) — Wú Rénjié's 吳仁傑 textual corrections to both *Hàn* histories.

**The Tang single-dynasty Histories (Eight Histories of the early Táng).** Between 629 and 656 the Táng court produced or supervised eight successive *zhèngshǐ* covering every regime from Jìn to Suí, fixing the model of imperially commissioned historiography that lasted to the end of the dynastic era.

- *Jìnshū* 晉書 [KR2a0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0015) — compiled under Fáng Xuánlíng 房玄齡 by an editorial board appointed by Tàizōng 太宗 in 644, drawing on (and superseding) more than a dozen earlier Jìn histories.
- *Sòngshū* 宋書 [KR2a0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0016) — Shěn Yuē's 沈約 history of the Liú-Sòng, completed already in the Liáng (487/488) and incorporated into the canon as the standard account of that dynasty.
- *Nán Qí shū* 南齊書 [KR2a0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0017) — Xiāo Zǐxiǎn 蕭子顯 of the Liáng on the dynasty in which his own ancestor reigned.
- *Liáng shū* 梁書 [KR2a0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0018) — drafted by Yáo Chá 姚察 (Liáng/Chén) and completed by his son Yáo Sīlián 姚思廉 under Táng auspices.
- *Chénshū* 陳書 [KR2a0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0019) — companion volume by the same Yáo father–son line, completed in 636.
- *Wèishū* 魏書 [KR2a0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0020) — Wèi Shōu's 魏收 controversial Northern-Qí history of the Tuòbá Bei-Wèi, written in 551–54.
- *Běi Qí shū* 北齊書 [KR2a0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0021) — begun by Lǐ Délín 李德林 in the Suí, finished by his son Lǐ Bǎiyào 李百藥 in 636.
- *Zhōu shū* 周書 [KR2a0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0022) — Lìnghú Défēn's 令狐德棻 history of the Bei-Zhōu (629–636).
- *Suí shū* 隋書 [KR2a0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0023) — annals/biographies under Wèi Zhēng 魏徵 (629–636) and the encyclopaedic *Wǔdài shǐzhì* 五代史志 (treatises) under Zhǎngsūn Wújì 長孫無忌 (656), the latter covering all of the Liáng, Chén, Bei-Qí, Bei-Zhōu and Suí jointly.
- *Nán shǐ* 南史 [KR2a0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0024) and *Běi shǐ* 北史 [KR2a0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0025) — Lǐ Yánshòu's 李延壽 single-handed synthesis (completed 659/676) of the eight separate Southern- and Northern-Dynasty histories into two continuous regional narratives.

**The Old / New histories pairs.** Twice in the canon a Sòng-era replacement was deemed insufficient to displace its predecessor, so both versions were retained.

- *Jiù Tángshū* 舊唐書 [KR2a0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0026) — completed under Liú Xù 劉昫 in 945 (Hòu Jìn) from late-Táng veritable records.

- *Xīn Tángshū jiūmiù* 新唐書糾謬 [KR2a0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0028) — Wú Zhěn's 吳縝 detailed enumeration of factual errors in the *Xīn Tángshū*, the single most cited Sòng critique of an imperially sponsored history.
- *Jiù Wǔdài shǐ* 舊五代史 [KR2a0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0029) — Xuē Jūzhèng's 薛居正 official history of the Five Dynasties (974); lost in the Yuán/Míng transmission and reconstructed under Shào Jìnhán 邵晉涵 from *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* 永樂大典 quotations during the *Sìkù* project.
- *Xīn Wǔdài shǐ* 新五代史 [KR2a0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0030) — Ōuyáng Xiū's privately drafted alternative, presented posthumously in 1077 and praised for its terse *Chūnqiū* 春秋-style historical judgements.

**The Yuán Three Histories and after.** The compilation of the *Sòng*, *Liáo*, and *Jīn* histories under Toqto'a in the 1340s settled the question of legitimate succession by granting all three rival regimes a *zhèngshǐ* of their own — the so-called *gè yǔ zhèngtǒng* 各與正統 ("each is granted legitimacy") solution.

- *Yuán shǐ* 元史 [KR2a0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0036) — produced under Sòng Lián 宋濂 in just 188 days (1369–70) at the start of the Míng, the most hastily compiled of all the *zhèngshǐ* and the one most extensively rewritten in later private histories.

### Topics

- **The *jìzhuàn* 紀傳 form and its alternatives.** Why the annals-and-biographies model, rather than the chronicle (*biānnián* 編年, KR2b) form of the *Zuǒzhuàn* and *Zīzhì tōngjiàn*, became the dynastic norm; what the inclusion or omission of *biǎo* 表 and *zhì* 志 entails for periods (notably Eastern Hàn, Three Kingdoms, Liáng, Chén, Northern Qí, Northern Zhōu) where the original compiler omitted one or both.
- **State sponsorship and *zhèngtǒng* 正統.** The link between imperial commissioning of a "previous-dynasty" history and the new dynasty's claim to legitimacy; the deliberate doubling of *Tángshū* and *Wǔdài shǐ*; the political force of the *gè yǔ zhèngtǒng* settlement applied to the Sòng / Liáo / Jīn triad and contested by Zhū Xī 朱熹 in his *Tōngjiàn gāngmù* 通鑑綱目 (Wilkinson §A.2.6).
- **The annotative supplement as historical scholarship.** The Péi-Sōngzhī model — substantive commentary that doubles the size of the host text by quoting lost sources verbatim — and its later imitators (Lǐ Xián, Háng Shìjùn).
- **The *kǎoyì* 考異 tradition on the *zhèngshǐ*.** From Wú Zhěn's Sòng *jiūmiù* / *zuǎnwù*, through the *Sìkù* *kǎozhèng* 考證 layer attached to every WYG history (visible in this division as the dozens of *kǎozhèng* persons in each text's frontmatter), to the great Qīng critical apparatus of Qián Dàxīn 錢大昕 and others.
- **The relation between the *Shǐjì* and the *Hànshū*.** Where Bān Gù copies, adapts, or silently revises Sīmǎ Qiān, and the implications for early-imperial source criticism — the explicit subject of the *Bān-Mǎ yìtóng*.
- **Reconstruction and recovery.** The *Jiù Wǔdài shǐ* as the paradigmatic case of a *zhèngshǐ* re-assembled from encyclopaedia quotations after centuries of loss; *bǔbiǎo* 補表 supplements (Xióng Fāng, Lì È) as a recurring scholarly response to the structural lacunae of the post-*Hàn* histories.
- **Translation, transcription, and the conquest dynasties.** The Qiánlóng *Guóyǔ jiě*'s retrospective standardization of Khitan, Jurchen, and Mongol names in the *Liáo*, *Jīn*, and *Yuán* histories — a politically motivated philological intervention that long obscured the underlying transcriptions and is now treated by modern scholarship as a textual problem in its own right.
- **The unresolved status of the *Qīng shǐ gǎo*.** A draft never imperially ratified, partially banned by the Republican Government in 1929, and not formally counted as the twenty-fifth *zhèngshǐ* — included here as the natural endpoint of the genre but explicitly marked as provisional.

# 編年類 (KR2b)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2b 編年 *Biānnián* — Histories — Annals](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR2b 編年 (*Biānnián*, "Annals") collects works composed in the *biānnián tǐ* 編年體 — the year-by-year chronicle form modelled ultimately on the *Chūnqiū* 春秋 and *Zuǒ zhuàn* 左傳 — within `KR2` 史部 (*Shǐ bù*, the Histories branch of the Sìkù quánshū). It is one of the two principal historiographical genres of the imperial period, standing alongside the *jìzhuàn tǐ* 紀傳體 ("annals-biography" form) of the official *Histories* collected in [KR2a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/) 正史. Wilkinson (§48) traces the genre from the earliest surviving examples — the *Chūnqiū* itself and the *Zhúshū jìnián* 竹書紀年 ([KR2b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0001)) — through the Hàn-period dynastic annals of [荀悅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8D%80%E6%82%85) ([KR2b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0003)) and [袁宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%81%E5%AE%8F) ([KR2b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0004)), an extended hiatus during which the official *jìzhuàn* form crowded out private annalistic composition, and the Northern-Sòng restoration of the form by [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) in the *Zī zhì tōng jiàn* 資治通鑑 ([KR2b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0007)). After Sīmǎ Guāng the *biānnián* mode became "once again on a par with the annals-biography" (Wilkinson §48.3) and dominated late-imperial reading habits: from the Sòng to the twentieth century, what most educated people read of Chinese history was the *Tōng jiàn* and Zhū Xī's *Gāngmù* 綱目 (catalogued in `KR2a`), not the dynastic *Histories*.

The chronological span of the works gathered here runs from the late second century CE (Xún Yuè's *Qián Hàn jì*, 198–200 CE) to the Qiánlóng court compilations of the 1770s and 1780s ([KR2b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0037), [KR2b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0038), [KR2b0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0039)). The corpus is unusually concentrated: of the forty cataloged works, twenty-four are tied directly to the *Tōng jiàn* — as its apparatus, commentary, continuation, pre-history, abridgment, or *Gāngmù*-form recasting. KR2b is therefore in effect a working library for reading and extending one book.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The two surviving Hàn-Jìn dynastic annals.** The genre's earliest extant exemplars after the *Chūnqiū*-tradition Classics are *Qián Hàn jì* 前漢紀 [KR2b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0003) of [荀悅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8D%80%E6%82%85) (commissioned by Hàn Xiàndì 漢獻帝 and presented in 200 CE) and *Hòu Hàn jì* 後漢紀 [KR2b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0004) of [袁宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%81%E5%AE%8F) (mid-fourth century). Wilkinson §48.2 notes that these are the only two of many Hàn-Táng annalistic histories to survive intact, the rest having been crowded out by the official *jìzhuàn* *Histories* and then by Sīmǎ Guāng's *Tōng jiàn*.

**Pre-imperial annalistic survivals.** *Zhúshū jìnián* 竹書紀年 [KR2b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0001) survives in the WYG only as the late-Míng "current text" (*jīnběn* 今本) recension of c. 1570, the genuine 281 CE Jíxiàn 汲縣 tomb-recovery having been reduced to fragments by the Southern Sòng. *Zhúshū tǒngjiān* 竹書統箋 [KR2b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0002) of [徐文靖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E6%96%87%E9%9D%96) is the standard Qīng commentary on the *jīnběn*.

**The *Tōng jiàn* core.** *Zī zhì tōng jiàn* 資治通鑑 [KR2b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0007) of [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89), the foundational text of the division and the model for every subsequent universal chronicle, presented in 1084 in 294 *juǎn* and covering 403 BCE to 959 CE. Composed alongside it are the three apparatus works also written by Sīmǎ Guāng: *Zī zhì tōng jiàn kǎo yì* 資治通鑑考異 [KR2b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0008) (the source-critical collation in 30 *juǎn*), *Zī zhì tōng jiàn mù lù* 資治通鑑目錄 [KR2b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0010) (the analytical index with synchronised calendrical and astronomical tables), and *Zī zhì tōng jiàn shì lì* 資治通鑑釋例 [KR2b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0009) (the editorial-conventions handbook). To these belongs also *Jīgǔ lù* 稽古錄 [KR2b0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0014), Sīmǎ Guāng's own short universal outline from Fúxī to 1067, presented in 1086 as a portable companion to the *Tōng jiàn*. The standard premodern commentary, the *yīnzhù* 音注 of [胡三省](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E4%B8%89%E7%9C%81) completed in 1295, is woven throughout the WYG transmission of the base text.

**The *Tōng jiàn* commentary and apparatus tradition.** *Zī zhì tōng jiàn wài jì* 資治通鑑外紀 [KR2b0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0015) of [劉恕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E6%81%95) (1078) supplies the pre-403-BCE prequel that Liú Shù had originally been commissioned to write for the *Tōng jiàn* but that did not enter the main work. *Zī zhì tōng jiàn shì wén* 資治通鑑釋文 [KR2b0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0016) of [史炤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B2%E7%82%A4) (mid-twelfth century) is the earliest substantial phonetic-and-gloss commentary, later corrected by Hú Sānxǐng's *Tōng jiàn shì wén biàn wù* 通鑑釋文辨誤 [KR2b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0012) (1295). *Tōngjiàn dìlǐ tōngshì* 通鑑地理通釋 [KR2b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0011) of [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) (late thirteenth century) is the standard geographical reference. *Tōngjiàn Hú zhù jǔ zhèng* 通鑑胡注擧正 [KR2b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0013) of [陳景雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%99%AF%E9%9B%B2) is the Qīng *kǎozhèng* correction of Hú Sānxǐng's geographical errors.

**The *Tōng jiàn* pre-history and continuations.** *Zī zhì tōng jiàn qián biān* 資治通鑑前編 [KR2b0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0033) of [金履祥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%91%E5%B1%A5%E7%A5%A5) (late thirteenth century) extends the chronicle backwards from 403 BCE to the legendary high-antiquity rulers. *Xù Zī zhì tōng jiàn cháng biān* 續資治通鑑長編 [KR2b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0019) of [李燾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E7%87%BE) (presented in instalments 1163–1183) is the most ambitious Northern-Sòng continuation, in 520 (originally 980) *juǎn*. *Tōng jiàn xù biān* 通鑑續編 [KR2b0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0034) of [陳桱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%A1%B1) (late Yuán) supplies a Sòng-Yuán continuation. *Zī zhì tōng jiàn hòu biān* 資治通鑑後編 [KR2b0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0040) of [徐乾學](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E4%B9%BE%E5%AD%B8) (presented 1694) is the leading early-Qīng continuation, covering 960–1367.

**The Sòng private annalistic histories.** A distinct cluster, written without imperial commission, fills out the late-Sòng-to-Yuán record where the *Tōng jiàn* stops. *Jiànyán yǐlái xìnián yào lù* 建炎以來繫年要錄 [KR2b0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0024) of [李心傳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%BF%83%E5%82%B3) (early thirteenth century) is the indispensable source for the Southern-Sòng founding under Gāozōng 高宗, an extension of Lǐ Tāo's project. *Zhōngxīng xiǎo jì* 中興小紀 [KR2b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0018) of [熊克](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%86%8A%E5%85%8B) is the parallel popular abridgment. *Jiǔcháo biānnián bèi yào* 九朝編年備要 [KR2b0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0025) of [陳均](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%9D%87) and *Liǎngcháo gāngmù bèi yào* 兩朝綱目備要 [KR2b0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0030) (anon.) cover the rest of the Northern and middle Southern Sòng. *Xù Sòng biānnián zī zhì tōng jiàn* 續宋編年資治通鑑 [KR2b0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0026) of [劉時擧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E6%99%82%E6%93%A7) gives the late-Sòng narrative. *Sòng shǐ quán wén* 宋史全文 [KR2b0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0032) (anon., late Sòng–Yuán) is the comprehensive single-dynasty annalistic Sòng record. *Sòng jì sān cháo zhèng yào* 宋季三朝政要 [KR2b0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0031) (anon. Yuán) and *Jìngkāng yào lù* 靖康要錄 [KR2b0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0029) (anon. Southern Sòng) document the dynasty's final crises. *Xī Hàn nián jì* 西漢年紀* [KR2b0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0028) of [王益之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%9B%8A%E4%B9%8B) applies the form to the Western Hàn, and *Dà shì jì* 大事記 [KR2b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0023) of [呂祖謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E7%A5%96%E8%AC%99) is a learned annalistic *kǎozhèng* through 481 BCE, continued in [王禕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%A6%95)'s *Dà shì jì xù biān* 大事記續編 [KR2b0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0035) of the early Míng.

**The *Gāngmù* 綱目 supplementary tradition.** Zhū Xī's own *Tōng jiàn gāngmù* is catalogued in `KR2a`; KR2b holds the Míng-Qīng continuations, critiques, and corrections. *Gāngmù xù lín* 綱目續麟 [KR2b0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0020) of [張自勳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E8%87%AA%E5%8B%B3) (1643) and *Gāngmù fēnzhù shí yí* 綱目分註拾遺 [KR2b0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0021) of [芮長恤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8A%AE%E9%95%B7%E6%81%A4) are critical supplements; *Gāngmù dìng wù* 綱目訂誤 [KR2b0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0022) of [陳景雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%99%AF%E9%9B%B2) corrects errors in the standard text. The Qīng imperial projects close the division: *Yù pī lìdài tōng jiàn jí lǎn* 御批歷代通鑑輯覽 [KR2b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0037) (1767, with Qiánlóng's personal interlinear comments), *Yù dìng zī zhì tōng jiàn gāngmù sān biān* 御定資治通鑑綱目三編 [KR2b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0038) (1746/1775, the Míng-history *Gāngmù* continuation), and *Huáng Qīng kāiguó fānglüè* 皇清開國方略 [KR2b0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0039) (1786, the official annalistic record of the Qīng founding).

**Outliers.** *Yuán jīng* 元經 [KR2b0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0005) is a pseudepigraphic Northern-Sòng fabrication ascribed to the Suí thinker [王通](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%9A) but actually compiled by [阮逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%98%AE%E9%80%B8) (c. 1027–1063), still preserved in the WYG under the older attribution. *Táng chuàngyè qǐjūzhù* 唐創業起居注 [KR2b0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0006) of [溫大雅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BA%AB%E5%A4%A7%E9%9B%85) is the only Táng court diary (*qǐjūzhù* 起居注) to survive, an eye-witness chronicle of the 617–618 Lǐyuán uprising. *Biānnián tōng zǎi* 編年通載 (殘) [KR2b0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0027) of [章衡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%A0%E8%A1%A1) (1074), now a 4-juan fragment of an originally 10-juan work, is the most condensed universal chronicle of the Northern Sòng — exactly contemporary with Sīmǎ Guāng's project but independent of it. *Huángwáng dà jì* 皇王大紀 [KR2b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0017) of [胡宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E5%AE%8F) is the Southern-Sòng *dàoxué* annalistic treatment of the sage-king age. *Yuán shǐ xù biān* 元史續編 [KR2b0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0036) of [胡粹中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E7%B2%B9%E4%B8%AD) (early Míng) supplements the post-Sòng Yuán in *Gāngmù* form where the official *Yuán shǐ* is thin.

### Important persons

- [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) (1019–1086) — the central figure of the division; author of *Zī zhì tōng jiàn* and its three companion apparatus works ([KR2b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0007)–[KR2b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0010)), of the parallel *Jīgǔ lù* [KR2b0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0014), and the architect of the *cóngmù* 叢目 / *chángbiān* 長編 / *zhèngwén* 正文 three-stage compositional method that became the model for all subsequent universal chronicles.
- [劉恕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E6%81%95) (1032–1078) — one of Sīmǎ Guāng's three principal collaborators on the *Tōng jiàn* (responsible for the Three Kingdoms through Northern-and-Southern Dynasties drafts), and on his own the author of the pre-history *Wài jì* [KR2b0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0015). Sīmǎ Guāng judged him the most original of the three collaborators.
- [胡三省](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E4%B8%89%E7%9C%81) (1230–1302) — author of the standard premodern *Tōng jiàn* commentary ([KR2b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0007)) and the *Biàn wù* [KR2b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0012) that corrects Shǐ Zhào's [KR2b0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0016) earlier glosses. Wrote in secret under Yuán rule and survived the *Jǐchǒu* (1289) coastal raids by sealing his manuscript in a cellar.
- [李燾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E7%87%BE) (1115–1184) — author of the *Xù Zī zhì tōng jiàn cháng biān* [KR2b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0019), the indispensable source for Northern Sòng history.
- [李心傳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%BF%83%E5%82%B3) (1167–1244) — author of *Jiànyán yǐlái xìnián yào lù* [KR2b0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0024), the corresponding indispensable source for the Southern-Sòng founding under Gāozōng.
- [呂祖謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E7%A5%96%E8%AC%99) (1137–1181) — author of *Dà shì jì* [KR2b0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0023); major dàoxué historian whose annalistic *kǎozhèng* method influenced later commentators on the *Gāngmù*.
- [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) (1223–1296) — author of *Tōngjiàn dìlǐ tōngshì* [KR2b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0011), the standard geographical reference for the *Tōng jiàn*; the leading polymath of late Southern Sòng *kǎozhèng*.
- [金履祥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%91%E5%B1%A5%E7%A5%A5) (1232–1303) — author of *Tōng jiàn qián biān* [KR2b0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0033); a leading Jīn-Huá-school disciple of Wáng Bǎi 王柏 who extended the *Tōng jiàn* backwards into the legendary period in Zhū Xī's *Gāngmù* form.
- [徐乾學](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E4%B9%BE%E5%AD%B8) (1631–1694) — author of *Tōng jiàn hòu biān* [KR2b0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0040) (compiled with Wàn Sītóng 萬斯同); the leading early-Qīng patron of *Tōng jiàn*-tradition scholarship.
- [陳景雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%99%AF%E9%9B%B2) (1670–1747) — author of two corrective Qīng-period sub-commentaries, *Tōngjiàn Hú zhù jǔ zhèng* [KR2b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0013) and *Gāngmù dìng wù* [KR2b0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0022); representative of Qīng *kǎozhèng* applied to the *Tōng jiàn* tradition.
- [徐文靖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E6%96%87%E9%9D%96) (1668–1756) — author of *Zhúshū tǒngjiān* [KR2b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0002); the most ambitious Qīng commentator on the *Zhúshū jìnián* before Wáng Guówéi.
- [高宗弘曆](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E5%AE%97%E5%BC%98%E6%9B%86) (Qiánlóng, 1711–1799) — imperial patron and active editor of *Yù pī lìdài tōng jiàn jí lǎn* [KR2b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0037); supplied a substantial body of his own marginal comments (over 150,000 characters) and decisively shaped Qīng-period orthodox views of legitimate dynastic succession.
- [荀悅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8D%80%E6%82%85) (148–209) and [袁宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%81%E5%AE%8F) (328–376) — authors of the two surviving Hàn-Jìn annalistic dynastic histories ([KR2b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0003), [KR2b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0004)); together they preserved the *biānnián* form across the *jìzhuàn* eight centuries before Sīmǎ Guāng.

### Topics

- ***Biānnián* vs. *jìzhuàn* — the genre's recurring rivalry.** From the *Shǐjì* onwards the composite annals-biography form was the official mode, with the *biānnián* form recovering primacy only in 1084. Sīmǎ Guāng's programmatic complaint that the *jìzhuàn Histories* are "prolix" (*fánróng* 煩冗) and force the reader to chase events across scattered chapters is the founding manifesto of the post-Hàn revival of the chronicle form.
- **The *Tōng jiàn*'s three-stage compositional method.** *Cóngmù* 叢目 (chronological assembly of primary sources) → *chángbiān* 長編 (long-form topical drafts) → *zhèngwén* 正文 (final compression). This is the most influential methodological innovation in the history of Chinese historiography and survives as a model in the term *chángbiān* — preserved in the title of [KR2b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0019) and used through to twentieth-century compilations of similar scope.
- ***Kǎo yì* 考異 — variant-reading collation as historiographical apparatus.** Sīmǎ Guāng's parallel *Tōng jiàn kǎo yì* [KR2b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0008), in which contested points are openly discussed and the source-critical decisions defended, is the prototype of every subsequent Chinese *kǎo yì* and a remarkable anticipation of modern critical-edition practice.
- **The *zhèng tǒng* 正統 problem and Zhū Xī's reordering.** Sīmǎ Guāng adopted a pragmatic single-thread succession (Wèi over Shǔ Hàn, the Northern Dynasties over the Southern, the Five Dynasties as legitimate) for narrative convenience. Zhū Xī's *Gāngmù* drastically recast the same material around moralist *zhèng tǒng* criteria, granting legitimacy instead to Shǔ Hàn (against Wèi), the Eastern Jìn and the Southern Dynasties (against the North), and disqualifying the Five Dynasties as a *wútǒng* 無統 interregnum. The reverberations of this dispute run through every Míng-Qīng continuation in this division — most explicitly through the corrective sub-commentaries of [張自勳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E8%87%AA%E5%8B%B3) [KR2b0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0020), [芮長恤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8A%AE%E9%95%B7%E6%81%A4) [KR2b0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0021), and [陳景雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%99%AF%E9%9B%B2) [KR2b0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0022), and through the imperial reinterpretations of Qiánlóng in [KR2b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0037) and [KR2b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0038).
- **Imperial patronage in the Qīng.** Three of the four longest works in the division ([KR2b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0037), [KR2b0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0038), [KR2b0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0039)) are court-commissioned compilations executed under direct Qiánlóng-era oversight. They mark the late-imperial recapture of the *biānnián* tradition by the state and supply the dominant pedagogical historiography of the nineteenth century.
- **The *Zhúshū* problem.** The *jīnběn Zhúshū jìnián* ([KR2b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0001)) preserved in the WYG is, by the Qīng *kǎozhèng* consensus codified by [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F)'s successor scholars and definitively by Wáng Guówéi (1916), a late-Míng reconstitution rather than the genuine 281 CE recovery. The Sìkù editors themselves denounced it, in one of the most painstaking textual demonstrations in the entire *tíyào*; modern revisionist work (Shào Dōngfāng, Nivison, Shaughnessy) has rehabilitated parts of its chronology against the Qīng verdict. The case is the locus classicus for the problem of received recension versus authentic source in the early-annalistic tradition.
- **Geographic and philological apparatus.** The *Tōng jiàn* tradition is unusually rich in dedicated geographical and phonetic reference works ([KR2b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0011), [KR2b0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0016), [KR2b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0012)) — the form's exhaustive coverage of pre-Sòng institutional and toponymic detail demanded specialised companion volumes.

# 紀事本末類 (KR2c)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2c 紀事本末類 *Jìshì běnmò lèi* — Histories — Topically Arranged Histories](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

The *jìshì běnmò* 紀事本末 ("from beginning to end of an event", topically arranged) class collects works in the third of the three great forms of Chinese historiography — the form invented in 1173–74 when the Southern Sòng scholar Yuán Shū 袁樞 took Sīmǎ Guāng's annalistic *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* 資治通鑑 ([KR2k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0001)), gathered the dispersed entries of each event into 239 self-contained, individually titled narratives, and so produced the genre-founding *Tōngjiàn jìshì běnmò* ([KR2c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0001)). Wilkinson, *Chinese History*, ch. 50, sets the genre alongside the older *biānnián* 編年 (annals, KR2b) and *jìzhuàn* 紀傳 (annals-biographies, the *Histories* in [KR2a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/)) and notes that, with one exception, *jìshì běnmò* writers tended to rearrange existing material rather than open new sources — the function of the form is navigational, making the dynastic record tractable to readers.

The Sìkù compilers placed under this rubric three distinct kinds of work: (i) topical rearrangements of pre-existing year-by-year or biographical records (Yuán Shū's archetype, the Sòng/Yuán/Míng *jìshì běnmò* of [KR2c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0007), [KR2c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0008), [KR2c0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0020), and the *Zuǒzhuàn* treatments of [KR2c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0003) and [KR2c0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0022)); (ii) topically organised regional and frontier histories ([KR2c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0005), [KR2c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0006), [KR2c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0019)); and (iii) the *fānglüè* 方略 / *jìlüè* 紀略 — the imperially-commissioned Qīng campaign histories that Wilkinson treats separately at §66.6.1 as a special form of episodic history but which the *Sìkù* curators folded into the *jìshì běnmò* class. The *fānglüè* dominate the late-Qīng portion of the division: ten of the twenty-three works in KR2c are imperial campaign histories of operations between 1673 and 1788. The division thus runs in compass from 270 (the Jìn-period commentary on the *Yì Zhōushū* preserved in [KR2c0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0002)) to 1789, with its centre of gravity in two periods: the Southern Sòng founding moment of the genre (1173–1235) and the Qiánlóng-era *fānglüè* office (1750–1789).

### Important texts and text clusters

**The founding work and its Classical extensions.** *Tōngjiàn jìshì běnmò* 通鑑紀事本末 [KR2c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0001) — Yuán Shū's 239-topic rearrangement of Sīmǎ Guāng, the matrix from which every other work in the division descends. *Chūnqiū Zuǒzhuàn shìlèi shǐmò* 春秋左傳事類始末 [KR2c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0003) (Zhāng Chōng 章沖, 1185) — the earliest application of the method to a Classic, written nine years after Yuán Shū's enterprise saw print. *Zuǒzhuàn jìshì běnmò* 左傳紀事本末 [KR2c0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0022) (Gāo Shìqí 高士奇, 1690) — the much larger 53-*juǎn* Kāngxī replacement, organised by state rather than by year, that supersedes Zhāng Chōng's slighter book. *Yì shǐ* 繹史 [KR2c0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0021) (Mǎ Sù 馬驌, c. 1670–75) — the great 160-*juǎn* topical antiquity-history of the Three Augusts through the fall of Qín, distinctive within the genre for preserving its source-texts whole and so anticipating evidential-research method.

**The Sòng–Yuán–Míng "trilogy".** *Sòngshǐ jìshì běnmò* 宋史紀事本末 [KR2c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0007) (Féng Qí 馮琦 / Chén Bāngzhān 陳邦瞻, 1605) — the standard topical key to the unwieldy *Sòngshǐ*. *Yuánshǐ jìshì běnmò* 元史紀事本末 [KR2c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0008) (Chén Bāngzhān, 1606) — the immediate sequel by the same hand. *Míngshǐ jìshì běnmò* 明史紀事本末 [KR2c0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0020) (Gǔ Yìngtài 谷應泰, 1655–58) — the principal topical history of the Míng, unique within the genre for being substantively independent of any prior dynastic history (it was written eighty years before the official *Míngshǐ* itself). Wilkinson singles Gǔ out as the one *jìshì běnmò* writer who added new evidence rather than rearranging an existing record.

**The Sòng documentary compilation.** *Sānzhāo běiméng huìbiān* 三朝北盟會編 [KR2c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0004) (Xú Mèngxīn 徐夢莘, presented 1194) — the 250-*juǎn* documentary compendium on Sòng–Jīn relations 1117–1161, sitting in this class on the strength of its part-by-part topical structure (Zhèngxuān, Jìngkāng, Yánxīng) but operating as a documentary archive rather than a narrative history; Wilkinson (§62.2 #11) ranks it second only to Lǐ Xīnchuán's *Jiànyán yǐlái xìnián yàolù* ([KR2k0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0008)) among Southern-Sòng private histories.

**Regional and frontier histories.** *Shǔ jiàn* 蜀鑑 [KR2c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0005) (Guō Yǔndǎo 郭允蹈, 1235–36) — the strategic-topographical military history of Sìchuān across twelve centuries. *Yánjiǎo jìwén* 炎徼紀聞 [KR2c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0006) (Tián Rǔchéng 田汝成, 1558) — the southwest-frontier critique. *Diāncháo* 滇考 [KR2c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0019) (Féng Sū 馮甦, 1665) — the Yúnnán topical history. *Suíkòu jìlüè* 綏寇紀略 [KR2c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0018) (Wú Wěiyè 吳偉業, 1652 onward) — the late-Míng poet-historian's twelve-piece account of the peasant rebellions and the fall of the Míng.

**The Qīng imperial campaign histories (*fānglüè* / *jìlüè*).** *Píngdìng sānnì fānglüè* 平定三逆方略 [KR2c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0009) (Lè Déhóng 勒德洪, 1682–86) — the precedent-setting first imperially-commissioned Qīng *fānglüè*, the model for everything after. *Qīnzhēng pīngdìng shuòmò fānglüè* [KR2c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0010) (Wēn Dá 溫達, 1708–10) — the Kāngxī Galdan campaign, the first to carry an imperial preface. *Qīndìng pīngdìng Jīnchuān fānglüè* [KR2c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0011) (Lái Bǎo 來保, 1750–52, on the First Jīnchuān war) and the comprehensive *Píngdìng liǎng Jīnchuān fānglüè* [KR2c0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0013) (Āguì 阿桂, 1781–89, on both Jīnchuān wars). *Píngdìng zhǔn'gā'ěr fānglüè* 平定準噶爾方略 [KR2c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0012) (Fù Héng 傅恆, 1763–70) — 173 *juǎn* on the destruction of the Dzungar Khanate and the conquest of Xīnjiāng. ### Topics

- **The invention of a third historiographical form.** The division is anchored on Yuán Shū's recognition that pure *biānnián* fragments an event across years and pure *jìzhuàn* fragments it across persons; the *jìshì běnmò* method gathers each event into one place while preserving chronology within. Every text in the division is, at base, an experiment in this method.
- **Rearrangement vs. original research.** The deep methodological question Wilkinson raises (§50): does *jìshì běnmò* generate new historical knowledge, or only re-package an existing record? The division supplies both kinds of answer: most works ([KR2c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0007), [KR2c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0008), [KR2c0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0022)) are rearrangements of a single prior text; a minority ([KR2c0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0020), [KR2c0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0021), [KR2c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0018)) draw on an open source-base and are substantively new.
- **Topical arrangement of the Classics.** A distinct sub-tradition treats the *Zuǒzhuàn* as if it were a *biānnián* like the *Tōngjiàn* and applies Yuán Shū's method to it ([KR2c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0003), [KR2c0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0022)). Mǎ Sù's *Yì shǐ* extends the same logic across the entire pre-imperial corpus.
- **Documentary compendium vs. narrative history.** The *Sānzhāo běiméng huìbiān* [KR2c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0004) sits in the division on the strength of its three-part topical structure but is documentary, not narrative — Xú Mèngxīn juxtaposes contradictory sources without adjudicating. The contrast with Yuán Shū's purely narrative *jìshì běnmò* defines two poles of the genre.
- **The *fānglüè* institution.** The Qīng court's establishment of a standing *fānglüè* / *jìlüè* compilation office, beginning with the Three Feudatories campaign of 1673–81 and reaching maturity in the late-Qiánlóng campaign-history bureau, gives the division its single largest internal cluster (10 of 23 works). The *fānglüè* are documentary, day-by-day records of imperial military operations; they are tightly bound to the *Shíquán wǔgōng* 十全武功 ("Ten Complete Military Victories") cycle that the Qiánlóng emperor cultivated as legitimating ideology.
- **Frontier history and the southwest.** A surprisingly large share of the regional *jìshì běnmò* concerns the southern and southwestern marches: Tián Rǔchéng on the *yánjiǎo* southwest [KR2c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0006), Guō Yǔndǎo on Sìchuān [KR2c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0005), Féng Sū on Yúnnán [KR2c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0019), Lán Dǐngyuán on Taiwan [KR2c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0023), and the Qīng *fānglüè* on Jīnchuān [KR2c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0011) [KR2c0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0013) and Taiwan [KR2c0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0017). The cluster is a window on three centuries of central-court engagement with Tibetan-speaking *tǔsī*, Hui Muslim communities, southern non-Hàn peoples, and the Tài-speaking polities at the Burmese border.
- **Sectarian uprisings and the *jìlüè* genre's selectivities.** The Wáng Lún ([KR2c0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0014)), Sū Sìshísān ([KR2c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0015)), and Tián Wǔ ([KR2c0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2c/KR2c0016)) *jìlüè* are the principal documentary entry points into the late-Qiánlóng court's understanding of *Bāguà jiào* / White Lotus and Naqshbandiyya Jahriyya mass movements; Susan Naquin's analyses of how the *jìlüè* editorial line systematically distorts the underlying record (overstating Manchu valour, suppressing official negligence) have been taken as paradigmatic for the *fānglüè* genre.

# 別史類 (KR2d)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2d 別史類 *Biéshǐ lèi* — Histories — Other Histories](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

*Biéshǐ* 別史 (lit. "other / separate histories") is a residual bibliographical category, not a genre. The term first appears in Chén Zhènsūn's 陳振孫 *Zhízhāi shūlù jiětí* 直齋書錄解題 (13th c.), where *biéshǐ* are characterised as more serious works than *záshǐ* 雜史 yet not weighty enough to rank as *zhèngshǐ* 正史 — they lie "somewhere between *zhèngshǐ* on the one hand and *záshǐ* on the other" (Wilkinson, *Chinese History*, §52.1). The Qīng Sìkù 四庫 editors made *biéshǐ* the fourth subcategory in the History branch (《史部》), absorbing into it many works that earlier catalogs had placed in *záshǐ*; the original Sìkù tally is 20 *biéshǐ* in the body of the catalog and 36 more in the *cúnmù* 存目 sections (Wilkinson, *Chinese History*, §52.1, Table 73). The Kanripo `KR2d` division reproduces the Sìkù listing and supplements it with SBCK *Sānbiān* additions — privately compiled Míng and early-Qīng works, most of them once proscribed, that were impossible to admit into a Qiánlóng-era imperial catalog and that re-entered the bibliographic record only in the early twentieth century.

The works collected here span more than two millennia. The earliest is the *Yì Zhōushū* 逸周書 ([KR2d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0001)), a heterogeneous Warring-States compilation framed as the residue of the pre-canonical *Shū* corpus; the latest are early- and mid-Qīng products — Wàn Sītóng's 萬斯同 supplementary tables ([KR2d0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0021)), Yáo Zhīyīn's 姚之駰 reconstitutions of the lost Eastern-Hàn histories ([KR2d0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0022)), and Lǐ Kǎi's 李鍇 hundred-*juǎn* recasting of the pre-imperial historical record ([KR2d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0024)). The category covers, among other forms, *jìzhuàn* 紀傳 recastings of received histories (蘇轍, 蕭常, 郝經, 李鍇), institutional encyclopaedias of the *Sāntōng* 三通 tradition (鄭樵's *Tōngzhì* and the Qiánlóng *Xù tōngzhì*), private dynastic histories (王稱, 查繼佐), histories of alien dynasties written from the Hàn point of view (Liáo, Jīn, the Mongol *Yuáncháo bìshǐ*), mythohistorical compendia of pre-imperial antiquity (羅泌, 蘇轍), and Qīng-era recoveries (*jíyì* 輯佚) of lost histories. A reader navigating this division must keep in mind that the unifying feature is *not* form but *bibliographic placement* — these are works that the cataloguer had nowhere else to put.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The *Sāntōng* universal-history tradition**: Zhèng Qiáo 鄭樵's *Tōngzhì* 通志 ([KR2d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0006)) — the second of the three institutional encyclopaedias (after Dù Yòu's *Tōngdiǎn* and before Mǎ Duānlín's *Wénxiàn tōngkǎo*) — and its Qiánlóng-era continuation *Qīndìng xù tōngzhì* 欽定續通志 ([KR2d0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0020), in the catalog meta but not yet cataloged here; see Wilkinson, *Chinese History*, §51.2). Both are placed in *biéshǐ* by the Sìkù editors because their inclusion of biographies disqualifies them from the *zhèngshū* 政書 category proper.

- **Shǔ-Hàn 蜀漢 *zhèngtǒng* recastings of the Sānguó zhì**: Xiāo Cháng 蕭常's *Xiāoshì Xù Hòu-Hànshū* 蕭氏續後漢書 ([KR2d0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0012), Southern Sòng, 1200) and Hǎo Jīng 郝經's independently-conceived *Hǎoshì Xù Hòu-Hànshū* 郝氏續後漢書 ([KR2d0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0013), composed in captivity at Yízhēn, 1260–1273). Both reorganise Chén Shòu's 陳壽 *Sānguó zhì* 三國志 ([KR2a0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0010)) so as to recognise Liú Bèi's Shǔ-Hàn rather than Cáo Wèi as the legitimate inheritor of the Hàn — a doctrinal commitment that Zhū Xī 朱熹 had recently codified in the *Tōngjiàn gāngmù* 通鑑綱目.

- **Hàn-history recoveries**: the *Dōngguān Hànjì* 東觀漢記 ([KR2d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0002)) — the first dynastic compilation undertaken after the *Shǐjì*, one of the *Sānshǐ* 三史 for five centuries until displaced by Fàn Yè's *Hòu-Hànshū*, lost by the Yuán, and reconstructed by the Sìkù editors from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* — and Yáo Zhīyīn 姚之駰's *Hòu-Hànshū bǔyì* 後漢書補逸 ([KR2d0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0022), 1713), which provided the foundation for the later *Dōngguān* recovery by collecting fragments of eight further lost Eastern-Hàn histories. Together these constitute the principal Qīng-era *jíyì* 輯佚 ("recovery of lost texts") effort on the Hàn historiographical canon.

- **Alien-dynasty companion histories**: Yè Lónglǐ 葉隆禮's *Qìdān guózhì* 契丹國志 ([KR2d0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0009), 1180) on the Liáo and the attributed Yǔwén Màozhāo 宇文懋昭 *Dà-Jīn guózhì* 大金國志 ([KR2d0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0010), dated 1234 but partially later interpolation) on the Jīn — both surviving in *chóngdìng* 重訂 (imperially revised) recensions produced by the Qiánlóng-era Sìkù editors. Companion to these is the *Yuáncháo bìshǐ* 元朝秘史 ([KR2d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0014)) — the Hàn-character phonetic transcription of the *Mongqol-un niuča tobča'an*, *Secret History of the Mongols*, the most important single source for early-Mongol history and one of the foundational documents of Mongolic historical linguistics.

- **Pre-imperial mythohistorical compendia**: Sū Zhé 蘇轍's *Gǔshǐ* 古史 ([KR2d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0005), 1100–1112) — a 60-*juǎn* recasting of the *Shǐjì* in deliberately classicising form; Luó Bì 羅泌's *Lùshǐ* 路史 ([KR2d0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0008), 1170) — a syncretic synthesis drawing on the Hàn weft-texts, Daoist sources, and the standard canon; Lǐ Kǎi 李鍇's *Shàngshǐ* 尚史 ([KR2d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0024), 1730–1745) — built by direct quotation-citation from Mǎ Sù's *Yìshǐ* and the original sources. Closely related are two Kāngxī-era *Chūnqiū-Zhànguó*-period miscellanies: Chén Hòuyào 陳厚耀's *Chūnqiū Zhànguó yìcí* 春秋戰國異辭 ([KR2d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0023)) and Xuē Yújī 薛虞畿's late-Míng *Chūnqiū bièdiǎn* 春秋別典 ([KR2d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0015)).

- **Sòng private dynastic histories**: the *Lóngpíng jí* 隆平集 ([KR2d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0004), attributed to Zēng Gǒng 曾鞏 but probably later), Wáng Chèn 王稱's *Dōngdū shìlüè* 東都事略 ([KR2d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0007), 1180–1195) — long regarded as one of the three great Sòng private histories of the lost Northern Sòng (with Lǐ Tāo and Lǐ Xīnchuán) — and Huáng Zhèn 黃震's *Gǔjīn jìyào* 古今紀要 ([KR2d0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0011), 1256–1276), one of the earliest substantial textbook implementations of the Zhū Xī *gāngmù* doctrine of *zhèngtǒng*.

- **Late-Míng / early-Qīng proscribed private histories** (the SBCK *Sānbiān* contribution to `KR2d`): Zhuāng Tínglóng 莊廷鑨's *Míngshǐ chāolüè cán* 明史鈔略殘 ([KR2d0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0016)), the surviving fragments of the work that triggered the great *Míngshǐ àn* 明史案 literary inquisition of 1663; and Zhā Jìzuǒ 查繼佐's two sister-works composed in secret over twenty-five years and concealed in his Hǎiníng wall — the comprehensive *Zuìwéi lù* 罪惟錄 ([KR2d0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0017)) and the regionally-organised Southern-Míng record *Dōngshān guóyǔ* 東山國語 ([KR2d0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0018)).

- **Imperial and supplementary chronologies**: the *Yùdìng lìdài jìshì niánbiǎo* 御定歷代紀事年表 ([KR2d0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0019), Kāngxī commission, 1707–1712) — a 100-*juǎn* synoptic table of 3,725 years of Chinese history modelled on the *Shǐjì* and *Tōngjiàn mùlù* — and Wàn Sītóng 萬斯同's *Bǔ lìdài shǐbiǎo* 補歷代史表 ([KR2d0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0021), 1678–1692), which supplied the chronological tables missing from the standard histories and effectively founded the Qīng *bǔbiǎo* 補表 ("supplementary tables") tradition.

- **Survivors from earlier strata**: at the head of the division stand the *Yì Zhōushū* 逸周書 ([KR2d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0001)) with Kǒng Cháo 孔晁's Jìn-era commentary, and at one remove from it Xǔ Sōng 許嵩's *Jiànkāng shílù* 建康實錄 ([KR2d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0003), 756–762), the principal annalistic synthesis of the Six Dynasties (Wú through Chén) with their shared capital at Jiànkāng.

### Important persons

- [鄭樵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E6%A8%B5) — Pútián polymath (1104–1162); author of the *Tōngzhì* and the architect of the *Èrshí lüè* 二十略, the twenty topical treatises whose methodology shaped subsequent institutional historiography.
- [蘇轍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BD%8D) — Northern-Sòng prose-master (1039–1112); reconceived the *Shǐjì* in classicising *jìzhuàn* form as the *Gǔshǐ*.
- [羅泌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%85%E6%B3%8C) — Southern-Sòng Lúlíng antiquarian (ca. 1131–after 1189); compiler of the syncretic *Lùshǐ*.
- [黃震](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E9%9C%87) — Southern-Sòng Zhū Xī school Confucian (1213–1281); his *Gǔjīn jìyào* implements Zhū Xī's *gāngmù* programme in textbook form.
- [蕭常](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%95%AD%E5%B8%B8) — Southern-Sòng Lúlíng *jìnshì* (12th c.); completed his father Xiāo Shòupéng's project of recasting the *Sānguó zhì* with Shǔ-Hàn *zhèngtǒng*.
- [郝經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%9D%E7%B6%93) — Yuán scholar-diplomat (1223–1275); composed his independently-conceived *Xù Hòu-Hànshū* over sixteen years of detention at the Sòng envoy lodgings.
- [葉隆禮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%89%E9%9A%86%E7%A6%AE) — Southern-Sòng official (*jìnshì* 1247); imperially commissioned compiler of the *Qìdān guózhì*.
- [王稱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%A8%B1) — Southern-Sòng historian of Méizhōu (fl. 1180s–1195); private historian of the lost Northern Sòng.
- [萬斯同](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%90%AC%E6%96%AF%E5%90%8C) — early-Qīng Zhè-dōng-school historian (1638–1702); compiler of the *Bǔ lìdài shǐbiǎo* and founder of the Qīng *bǔbiǎo* tradition.
- [查繼佐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%A5%E7%B9%BC%E4%BD%90) — Hǎiníng Míng-loyalist (1601–1677); composer of the *Zuìwéi lù* and the *Dōngshān guóyǔ* under Qīng proscription, both rediscovered in the twentieth century.
- [莊廷鑨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8E%8A%E5%BB%B7%E9%91%A8) — wealthy late-Míng Nánxún literatus (d. ca. 1660); commissioner of the *Míngshǐ chāolüè*, the work whose proscription triggered the *Míngshǐ àn* of 1663.
- [姚之駰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E4%B9%8B%E9%A7%B0) — Kāngxī-era Qiántáng scholar (fl. 1713); first systematic recoverer of the lost Eastern-Hàn histories.
- [陳厚耀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%8E%9A%E8%80%80) — Kāngxī-era evidential historian and mathematical astronomer (1648–1722); compiler of the *Chūnqiū Zhànguó yìcí*.
- [李鍇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%8D%87) — Hàn-bannerman scholar (b. 1686, d. 1755); compiler of the *Shàngshǐ* by the technique of direct citation-anthology.
- [孔晁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E6%99%81) — Jìn-era commentator (late 3rd c. CE); the only continuous early commentary on the *Yì Zhōushū*.

### Topics

- **The *zhèngtǒng* 正統 problem.** More than any other concern, the question of dynastic legitimacy organises this division. The most conspicuous instance is the Sòng-and-after rehabilitation of Shǔ-Hàn against Cáo Wèi (Xiāo Cháng [KR2d0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0012), Hǎo Jīng [KR2d0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0013), Huáng Zhèn [KR2d0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0011)) — a doctrinal commitment following Zhū Xī's reformulation of Xí Zuòchǐ 習鑿齒's *Hàn-Jìn chūnqiū*. Equally important is the Sòng-vs-Liáo/Jīn legitimacy dispute, which the Qiánlóng-era Sìkù editors arbitrated retrospectively in their *chóngdìng* revisions of the *Qìdān guózhì* and *Dà-Jīn guózhì* ([KR2d0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0009), [KR2d0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0010)) — silently rearranging the Sòng-Liáo-Jīn reign-year orderings of the original Southern-Sòng compilers.

- **Recasting of received histories.** Several works in `KR2d` are not new histories but reorganisations of the *zhèngshǐ*: Sū Zhé's *Gǔshǐ* rewrites the *Shǐjì* in classicising form; Xiāo Cháng and Hǎo Jīng both rewrite the *Sānguó zhì* to reverse its legitimacy line; Lǐ Kǎi's *Shàngshǐ* recasts the entire pre-imperial record from the materials Mǎ Sù had collected as the *Yìshǐ*. The form is in each case classical *jìzhuàn*; the contribution is hermeneutic.

- **Recovery (*jíyì* 輯佚) of lost histories.** A signature mid-and-late-Qīng activity: Yáo Zhīyīn's recovery of eight Eastern-Hàn histories ([KR2d0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0022)) provides the foundation for the Sìkù editors' 24-*juǎn* reconstruction of the *Dōngguān Hànjì* ([KR2d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0002)), itself drawn from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn*, the Lǐ Xián commentary on the *Hòu-Hànshū*, the Liú Zhāo commentary on the *Xù-Hànshū* treatises, and the great Táng *lèishū* (*Běitáng shūchāo*, *Yìwén lèijù*, *Chūxué jì*). The Sìkù-era recovery of the *Hǎoshì Xù Hòu-Hànshū* ([KR2d0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0013)) from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* belongs to the same effort.

- **The *Sāntōng* / 三通 tradition.** Zhèng Qiáo's *Tōngzhì* and its Qiánlóng-era continuation establish the institutional-encyclopaedia line that, with Dù Yòu's *Tōngdiǎn* and Mǎ Duānlín's *Wénxiàn tōngkǎo*, constitutes the foundational triad of Chinese institutional historiography (Wilkinson, *Chinese History*, §51.2). The Sìkù editors classified the *Tōngzhì* lineage as *biéshǐ* — rather than as *zhèngshū* 政書 — because the works contain biographies.

- **Pre-imperial mythohistory and the *Chūnqiū* outside the Three Commentaries.** Sòng and Qīng *biéshǐ* show a sustained effort to handle the antiquity that lay outside or beneath the canonical histories: Luó Bì's *Lùshǐ* draws on the Hàn weft-texts and Daoist sources; Sū Zhé's *Gǔshǐ* polemically suppresses what its author judges legendary in the *Shǐjì*; and Xuē Yújī's *Chūnqiū bièdiǎn* ([KR2d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0015)) and Chén Hòuyào's *Chūnqiū Zhànguó yìcí* ([KR2d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0023)) together gather precisely the *Chūnqiū*-period evidence that lies outside the *Sānzhuàn*.

- **Private vs imperial historiography, and the Qīng literary inquisitions.** The contrast between officially commissioned works (Wáng Zhīshū's *Yùdìng lìdài jìshì niánbiǎo* [KR2d0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0019), the Sìkù-era *chóngdìng* recensions of [KR2d0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0009) and [KR2d0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0010), Jī Huáng's *Xù tōngzhì*) and clandestinely composed private histories (Zhuāng Tínglóng [KR2d0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0016), Zhā Jìzuǒ [KR2d0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0017), [KR2d0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0018)) runs through the whole division. The *Míngshǐ àn* 明史案 of 1663 — the most severe of the early-Qīng literary inquisitions — is the political event that explains why several of these private works survive only in twentieth-century rediscovery and entered the bibliographic record outside the Sìkù line.

- **Alien-dynasty histories and Mongol historiography.** The Liáo–Jīn–Mongol horizon produces three of the most important works in `KR2d`: the *Qìdān guózhì*, the *Dà-Jīn guózhì*, and above all the *Yuáncháo bìshǐ* ([KR2d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0014)), whose Hàn-character transcription is the principal surviving witness to the Mongolian original.

- **Supplementary tables (*bǔbiǎo* 補表).** Wàn Sītóng's *Bǔ lìdài shǐbiǎo* opens a tradition of methodical reconstruction of the chronological tables the standard histories omit — a Zhè-dōng-school complement to the Wú-school *kǎojù* 考據 evidential scholarship of the same period.

- 62–225 CE — *Dōngguān Hànjì* 東觀漢記 [KR2d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2d/KR2d0002) — the first imperial *guóshǐ* compilation after the *Shǐjì*; lost by the Yuán, present recension a Sìkù-era reconstruction.

# 雜史類 (KR2e)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2e 別史類 *Biéshǐ lèi* — Histories — Other Histories](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/)

*Other Histories*

### Scope and scholarly tradition

*Biéshǐ* 別史 ("other / separate histories") is a residual bibliographical category, not a literary genre. The term was coined in Chén Zhènsūn's 陳振孫 *Zhízhāi shūlù jiětí* 直齋書錄解題 in the thirteenth century to designate works "more serious than *zashi* 雜史, lying somewhere between *zhèngshǐ* 正史 on the one hand and *zashi* on the other," and was adopted by the Sìkù 四庫 editors as the fourth subdivision of the History branch in place of the *zashi* of earlier catalogs. As Endymion Wilkinson notes in §52 (*Miscellaneous Histories*) of *Chinese History: A New Manual*, the category gathers works of various kinds — both privately and officially compiled — that the editors judged worthy of preservation alongside the dynastic standard histories without being assimilable to them, and is therefore best rendered in English as "other histories." The Sìkù *zhèngběn* contains twenty *biéshǐ* and the *Sìkù zǒngmù* lists a further thirty-six in the *cúnmù* 存目 sections.

The twenty-two works gathered here in the Kanripo's KR2e span almost two millennia, from the late–Warring-States *Guóyǔ* 國語 [KR2e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0001) through the Qiānlóng-court 1777 Chinese translation of a 1662 Mongol chronicle [KR2e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0022). Internally the corpus falls into three families: (i) pre-imperial historiographical compendia together with their post-classical commentarial traditions — the *Guóyǔ* and the *Zhànguócè* 戰國策 [KR2e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0003) clusters; (ii) Táng–Yuán supplementary, eyewitness, and topically-organized records that fill gaps left by the official histories, including a substantial body of Sòng-Jīn captivity literature and works recovered by the Sìkù compilers from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* 永樂大典; and (iii) Míng-Qīng *kǎozhèng* 考證 critique of the dynastic historiographical record together with the imperial-translation programme that brought non-Hàn historical traditions into the canonical corpus.

### Important texts and text clusters

**Pre-imperial historiographical classics.** The *Guóyǔ* 國語 [KR2e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0001), the late–Warring-States state-by-state speech compendium taken in Hàn convention as the *wàizhuàn* 外傳 (outer commentary) to the *Chūnqiū* 春秋, is here printed in Wéi Zhāo's 韋昭 21-*juǎn* recension — the only continuous classical commentary on the work to survive. Sòng Xiáng's 宋庠 *Guóyǔ bǔyīn* 國語補音 [KR2e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0002) reworks an inherited Táng anonymous *yīn* 音 into the only Sòng phonological apparatus to the *Guóyǔ* still extant.

**The *Zhànguócè* cluster.** Three of the Sìkù's principal recensions of Liú Xiàng's 劉向 redaction of the late–pre-imperial intriguers' (*zòngheng* 縱橫) speeches sit side-by-side: the Hàn-Sòng received text with Gāo Yòu 高誘's truncated annotation supplemented by Yáo Hóng 姚宏's *xùzhù* 續注 [KR2e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0003); Bào Biāo 鮑彪's 1147 Sòng-Confucian re-arrangement of the work into 10 chronological *juǎn* with a brand-new continuous commentary [KR2e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0004); and Wú Shīdào 吳師道's Yuán critical re-annotation in *bǔ* 補 / *zhèng* 正 interlinear tags correcting Bào against Yáo Hóng [KR2e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0005). Together these three works are the principal pre-modern editorial layers through which the *Zhànguócè* is read.

**Mirror-of-princes and Táng historiography.** *Zhēnguān zhèngyào* 貞觀政要 [KR2e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0006), Wú Jīng's 吳兢 thematically arranged compendium of dialogues between Táng Tàizōng 唐太宗 and his court (here in Gē Zhí 戈直's 1333 Yuán *jíping* recension), is the East-Asian classic of the genre, repeatedly drawn on by the Sòng *jīngyán* 經筵 imperial lectures and by Hēian, Tokugawa, and Chosŏn court ideology. The late-Táng regional history *Zhǔgōng jiùshì* 渚宮舊事 [KR2e0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0007) (Yú Zhīgǔ 余知古, focused on Jīng-Chǔ 荊楚 from Yùxióng 鬻熊 through the Táng) survives in only the first 5 of its original 10 *juǎn*, while Péi Tíngyù's 裴庭裕 *Dōngguān zòujì* 東觀奏記 [KR2e0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0008) preserves the otherwise lost record of the Xuānzōng 宣宗 reign (846–859) reconstructed from oral testimony after the *qǐjū zhù* 起居注 perished.

**Five-Dynasties supplements.** *Wǔdài shǐ quèwén* 五代史闕文 [KR2e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0009) by Wáng Yǔchēng 王禹偁 (998–1001) and *Wǔdài shǐ bǔ* 五代史補 [KR2e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0010) by Táo Yuè 陶岳 (1012) together supplement the early-Sòng official *Jiù Wǔdài shǐ* 舊五代史 of Xuē Jūzhèng 薛居正; both were drawn on by Ōuyáng Xiū 歐陽修's *Xīn Wǔdài shǐ* 新五代史 [KR2b0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0024) and by Sīmǎ Guāng's *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* 資治通鑑.

**Sòng-Jīn eyewitness historiography.** A tightly grouped cluster of first-hand records of the Jìngkāng 靖康 catastrophe and the Sòng-Jīn diplomatic and prisoner-of-war regime: *Běi shòu jiànwén lù* 北狩見聞錄 [KR2e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0011) by Cáo Xūn 曹勛, principal eyewitness to the abdicated Huīzōng 徽宗's removal to the Jīn camp; *Sōngmò jìwén* 松漠紀聞 [KR2e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0012) by Hóng Hào 洪皓, reconstructed from memory after his fifteen-year Jīn captivity; and *Dà Jīn diàofá lù* 大金弔伐錄 [KR2e0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0016), an anonymous Jīn-period documentary archive of the formal state correspondence between Jīn and Sòng (and the Jīn-installed Chǔ 楚 / Qí 齊 puppets), recovered by the Sìkù editors from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn*.

**Sòng institutional and topical compendia.** *Yānyì yímóu lù* 燕翼詒謀錄 [KR2e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0013) by Wáng Yǒng 王栐 (1227) gathers 162 founding institutional precedents of the early Northern Sòng from the official archive, drawing explicitly *not* on *bài guān xiǎoshuō* 稗官小說. *Tàipíng zhìjī tǒnglèi* 太平治迹統類 [KR2e0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0014) by Péng Bǎichuān 彭百川 organizes Northern-Sòng governmental affairs by 88 *mén* 門 (categories), and is the most rigorous of the late-Sòng "categorized institutional digest" tradition that includes Jiāng Shǎoyú's *Huángcháo shìshí lèiyuàn* and Lǐ Xīnchuán's *Jiànyán yǐlái cháoyě záji*.

**Late-Sòng / Jīn / Yuán transition records.** *Xiánchún yíshì* 咸淳遺事 [KR2e0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0015) (anonymous, recovered from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn*) is the documentary record of the Xiánchún 咸淳 reign of Sòng Dùzōng 度宗 (1265–1272 only — the final two years are missing). *Rǔnán yíshì* 汝南遺事 [KR2e0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0017) is Wáng È 王鶚's day-by-day eyewitness diary of the Jīn collapse at Cài 蔡州 in 1234, in 107 dated *gāngmù* 綱目 entries and a principal source for the *Jīnshǐ* "Āizōng běnjì." *Qiántáng yíshì* 錢塘遺事 [KR2e0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0018) is Liú Yīqīng 劉一清's heavy compilation centred on a critique of Jiǎ Sìdào 賈似道's chancellorship. *Píng Sòng lù* 平宋錄 [KR2e0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0019) is Liú Mǐnzhōng 劉敏中's contemporary record of the 1276 Yuán conquest of Lín'ān 臨安, restored to its true author by the Sìkù editors against the long-standing misattribution to Píng Qìng'ān 平慶安.

**Míng *kǎozhèng* and Qīng translation.** *Yǎnshāntáng biéjí* 弇山堂別集 [KR2e0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0020) by Wáng Shìzhēn 王世貞 (100 *juǎn*) — combining narrative compendia of remarkable Míng affairs, the foundational *Shǐchéng kǎowù* 史乘考誤 critique of the Míng *shílù*, sixty-seven sub-categories of biographical tables, and sixteen institutional treatises — is the largest single work in the division and one of the founding documents of late-imperial evidential scholarship's approach to the Míng historiographical record. *Géchú yìshǐ* 革除逸史 [KR2e0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0021) by Zhū Mùzhì 朱睦㮮 is the most balanced of the Míng treatments of the Jiànwén 建文 reign that Yǒnglè 永樂 had "erased" from the dynastic chronology. *Qīndìng Měnggǔ yuánliú* 欽定蒙古源流 [KR2e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0022) is the Qiánlóng court's 1777 Chinese translation of Saghang Sechen Hong-tayiji 薩囊徹辰鴻台吉's 1662 Ordos-Mongol *Erdeni-yin tobchi* — the principal indigenous-Mongol historical synthesis of the post-Yuán steppe and a Qing imperial corrective to centuries of garbled Sino-centric transcription of Mongol names.

- [宋庠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E5%BA%A0) — early Northern-Sòng senior statesman, compiler of the only Sòng phonological apparatus on the *Guóyǔ*.
- [高誘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E8%AA%98) — Hàn-period commentator on the *Zhànguócè*, the partial survival of whose annotation provided the foundation on which the Sòng recensions were built.
- [姚宏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E5%AE%8F) — Southern-Sòng continuator of Gāo Yòu's *Zhànguócè* commentary; his *xùzhù* 續注 is the Sìkù base text.
- [鮑彪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AE%91%E5%BD%AA) — Southern-Sòng scholar who rearranged the *Zhànguócè* chronologically into 10 *juǎn* and produced the first thoroughly Sòng-Confucian re-reading of the work.
- [吳師道](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E5%B8%AB%E9%81%93) — Yuán critical annotator who collated Bào Biāo against Yáo Hóng using *bǔ* / *zhèng* interlinear tags.
- [吳兢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E5%85%A2) — Táng court historian, compiler of the *Zhēnguān zhèngyào* — the East-Asian classic of the mirror-of-princes genre.
- [戈直](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%88%E7%9B%B4) — Yuán *jíping* 集評 editor whose 1333 recension of the *Zhēnguān zhèngyào*, gathering the comments of twenty-two Sòng-Yuán scholars, is the Sìkù base text.
- [裴庭裕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A3%B4%E5%BA%AD%E8%A3%95) — late-Táng *shǐguǎn* 史館 historian, the principal recorder of the otherwise lost Xuānzōng reign.
- [王禹偁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%A6%B9%E5%81%81) — Northern-Sòng critic and Hànlín Academician, the foundational source-critical supplementer of the old *Wǔdài shǐ*.
- [陶岳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%B2%B3) — early-Sòng official whose 1012 *Wǔdài shǐ bǔ* is the principal narrative supplement on which Ōuyáng Xiū and Sīmǎ Guāng drew.
- [曹勛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%B9%E5%8B%9B) — Sòng official and principal eyewitness recorder of Huīzōng's removal into Jīn captivity.
- [洪皓](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E7%9A%93) — Sòng envoy and fifteen-year Jīn captive whose ethnographic record of the Jīn court is the most circumstantial Sòng-period firsthand account of the northern empire.
- [王栐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%A0%90) — Sòng-loyalist compiler of early-Sòng founding institutional precedents, the most authoritative compilation of its kind among the *biéshǐ*.
- [彭百川](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E7%99%BE%E5%B7%9D) — late-Southern-Sòng Méishān 眉山 historian, leading exponent of the topically-organized "categorized institutional digest" of Northern-Sòng affairs.
- [王鶚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%B6%9A) — Jīn-loyalist eyewitness to the dynasty's collapse and (later) early-Yuán Confucian official under Khubilai.

### Topics

- **The residual character of the category.** Following Chén Zhènsūn's original definition and Wilkinson §52, *biéshǐ* is not a genre but a placement between *zhèngshǐ* and *zashi*. The internal heterogeneity of the works — pre-imperial speech compendia next to Qīng translations of Mongol chronicles — is the structural condition of the category, not a flaw in its assembly.
- **Editorial layering of pre-imperial classics.** The Sìkù preserves multiple successive scholarly recensions of the same root text rather than a single recension. The *Zhànguócè* cluster [KR2e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0003) / [KR2e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0004) / [KR2e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0005) is the principal site at which the choice between Liú Xiàng's state-by-state arrangement and Bào Biāo's chronological re-arrangement was negotiated.
- **Eyewitness historiography of dynastic catastrophe.** The Sòng-Jīn captivity literature ([KR2e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0011), [KR2e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0012), [KR2e0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0017)) and the Sòng-Yuán transition records ([KR2e0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0015), [KR2e0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0019)) constitute one of the largest concentrations of first-person testimony in the entire Sìkù History branch.
- **The *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* recovery programme.** Several of the works ([KR2e0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0015), [KR2e0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0016)) survived only because the Sìkù compilers extracted them from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn*. Their inclusion in the *biéshǐ* category reflects the bibliographic logic of late-eighteenth-century recovery rather than any classical pedigree.
- **Supplementing the standard histories.** The Five-Dynasties supplement cluster ([KR2e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0009), [KR2e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0010)) reflects the early-Sòng response to perceived deficiencies of the official *Jiù Wǔdài shǐ*, and remained in circulation even after Ōuyáng Xiū's *Xīn Wǔdài shǐ* superseded it.
- **Mirror-of-princes literature.** *Zhēnguān zhèngyào* [KR2e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0006) and its commentarial afterlife are the principal vehicle through which the *biéshǐ* category enters the *jīngyán* curriculum and the East-Asian political-theological lexicon.
- **Topical/categorized historiography.** [KR2e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0013), [KR2e0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0014), and [KR2e0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0020) represent the *biéshǐ* category's hospitality to topically — as against annalistically — organized historical writing, a structural alternative to the *jìzhuàn* 紀傳 mould of the standard histories.
- **Erasure and rehabilitation.** The Jiànwén historiographical problem ([KR2e0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0021)) and Wáng Shìzhēn's *Shǐchéng kǎowù* attack on the *Tàizǔ shílù* ([KR2e0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0020)) make the division a focal site for late-Míng / early-Qīng questions about official memory and its corruption.
- **Non-Hàn historiography in Chinese translation.** [KR2e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0022) uniquely integrates an indigenous Mongol historical tradition into the imperial corpus via Qiánlóng-court translation, exemplifying the late-Qing classification practice of treating non-Hàn dynastic histories as authoritative.

- c. 720 – 1333 — *Zhēnguān zhèngyào* 貞觀政要 [KR2e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0006) — Wú Jīng's Táng compilation in Gē Zhí's Yuán *jíping* edition.
- c. 830–859 — *Zhǔgōng jiùshì* 渚宮舊事 [KR2e0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2e/KR2e0007) — late-Táng regional history of Jīng-Chǔ.
