# 詔令奏議類 (KR2f)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2f 詔令奏議類 *Zhàolìng zòuyì lèi* — Histories — Imperial Edicts and Memorials](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR2f is the *Zhàolìng zòuyì lèi* 詔令奏議類 (Imperial Edicts and Memorials), one of the fifteen subdivisions of the *Shǐbù* 史部 in the *Sìkù quánshū* taxonomy. Within the Sìkù scheme the category is itself bisected into two *zhī shǔ* 之屬: *zhàolìng* 詔令 (top-down imperial pronouncements — edicts, proclamations, rescripts, *shèngxùn*, *shàngyù*) and *zòuyì* 奏議 (bottom-up officials' memorials — *zòu* 奏, *yì* 議, *shū* 疏, *biǎo* 表, *zházǐ* 札子). [KR2f0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0001)–0011 cover the *zhàolìng* side, [KR2f0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0012)–0041 the *zòuyì* side. The division thus collects the two halves of the Chinese chancery-documentary tradition: what the throne sent down, and what its officials sent up.

The category as Sìkù defines it is younger than its contents. Bibliographically, *zhàolìng* anthologies were generally classed under *biéjí* or *zǒngjí* in the Tang–Song catalogs, and individual officials' *zòuyì* under *biéjí*; only with the *Sìkù* did the documentary-administrative function of these texts win them an autonomous subdivision under the histories. The chronological span of the works collected runs from the Hàn (whose edicts are extracted retrospectively in [KR2f0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0011) *Liǎng Hàn zhàolìng*) through 1786 (Qiánlóng's [KR2f0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0041) *Yùxuǎn Míngchén zòuyì*); the date of compilation, however, is concentrated in three peaks — Northern Sòng (the Sòng officials' own *zòuyì*), late-Sòng to early Míng (the great classified anthologies of [KR2f0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0038) and [KR2f0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0039)), and Kāngxī-to-Qiánlóng (the Qīng imperial *shèngxùn* / *shàngyù* / *zhūpī* program). Wilkinson 2018 treats the genre principally in §47.5 (Hàn documents and chancery typology), §61.3.7 (Táng *zhàolìng*), §62.3 (Sòng *zòuyì* and *míngchén* anthologies), and §65.3.7 (Míng–Qīng edicts and memorials); the per-text notes in this directory anchor their references to those sections.

The principal transmissional fact about KR2f is that it preserves what the *shílù* 實錄 and *qǐjūzhù* 起居注 have not. The Táng veritable records are entirely lost; the Sòng *shílù* (except for the fragmentary [KR2f0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0003)) are lost; the Yuán *shílù* is lost. For each of those periods, the surviving body of imperial-edict text and ministerial-memorial text — i.e. the actual documentary record of court business — has descended chiefly through the anthologies collected here.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### Imperial edicts (*zhàolìng*) — pre-Qīng anthologies

- *Táng dà zhàolìng jí* 唐大詔令集 [KR2f0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0010) — Sòng Mǐnqiú's 1070 collection (original 130 *juàn*, surviving 107) is the principal extant body of Táng-period imperial pronouncements, organized in 30 functional categories. Indispensable for Táng institutional history.
- *Liǎng Hàn zhàolìng* 兩漢詔令 [KR2f0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0011) — Lín Fú's *Xī Hàn zhàolìng* (preface 1109) and Lóu Fǎng's *Dōng Hàn zhàolìng* (preface 1222) joined as a single Sòng anthology, with Hóng Zīkuí's *zǒnglùn* essay on the typology of imperial documents.
- *Tàizōng huángdì shílù cán* 太宗皇帝實錄殘 [KR2f0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0003) — anomalously placed here: the only surviving fragment of any Northern Sòng *shílù*, edited by Qián Ruòshuǐ for *Tàizōng*'s reign.

#### Imperial pronouncements (*zhàolìng*) — Qīng imperial program

A tightly coordinated Kāngxī-to-Qiánlóng compilational program treating the dynasty's own ancestors as canonical authors:
- *Tàizǔ Gāohuángdì shèngxùn* 太祖高皇帝聖訓 [KR2f0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0001) (Nurhaci, ed. 1686);
- *Tàizōng Wénhuángdì shèngxùn* 太宗文皇帝聖訓 [KR2f0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0002) (Hóng Tàijí, ed. 1687);
- *Shìzǔ Zhānghuángdì shèngxùn* 世祖章皇帝聖訓 [KR2f0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0004) (Shùnzhì, ed. 1687);
- *Shèngzǔ Rénhuángdì shèngxùn* 聖祖仁皇帝shèngxùn [KR2f0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0005) (Kāngxī, ed. 1731);
- *Shìzōng Xiànhuángdì shèngxùn* 世宗憲皇帝聖訓 [KR2f0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0006) (Yōngzhèng, ed. 1741).

These five — and the contemporary *shàngyù* and *zhūpī* anthologies that flank them — function as the dynasty's self-canonization. The two *shàngyù* compilations, *Shìzōng Xiànhuángdì shàngyù bāqí* 世宗憲皇帝上諭八旗 [KR2f0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0007) and *Shìzōng Xiànhuángdì shàngyù nèigé* 世宗憲皇帝上諭內閣 [KR2f0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0008) (159 *juàn*), preserve the day-to-day Yōngzhèng pronouncements to the Eight Banners and to the Grand Secretariat. The crown jewel of the cluster is *Shìzōng Xiànhuángdì zhūpī yùzhǐ* 世宗憲皇帝硃批諭旨 [KR2f0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0009) — 360 *juàn* of Yōngzhèng's personal vermilion rescripts to provincial secret-memorial submitters, the largest single-emperor documentary monument in the Sìkù, and a foundational source for eighteenth-century Chinese administrative, fiscal, and frontier history.

#### Memorials (*zòuyì*) — individual Sòng officials

The Northern-Sòng generation of *míngchén* whose memorials founded the genre as an independent literary form: *Fàn Wénzhèng zòuyì* 范文正奏議 [KR2f0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0012) (Fàn Zhòngyān, the *Qìnglì* reform memorials), *Bāo Xiàosù zòuyì jí* 包孝肅奏議集 [KR2f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0013) (Bāo Zhěng), *Jìnyán jí* 盡言集 [KR2f0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0014) (Liú Ānshì), *Dǎnglùn jí* 讜論集 [KR2f0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0015) (Chén Cìshēng). The Southern Sòng is represented only by *Zuǒshǐ jiàncǎo* 左史諫草 [KR2f0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0016) (Lǚ Wǔ). These are the principal documentary witnesses to the policy debates of the *Qìnglì*, *Xīníng*, and *Yuányòu* eras.

#### Memorials (*zòuyì*) — individual Míng officials

The single largest cluster in KR2f: seventeen *biéjí*-style anthologies of individual Míng officials' memorials, from the *Tiānshùn*/*Chénghuà* generation (Shāng Lù, Wáng Shù, Mǎ Wénshēng) through the *Wànlì* and late-Míng (Pān Jìxùn, Lù Zhōnglì, Zhōu Qǐyuán). The cluster reads as a documentary commentary on the principal political debates of the Míng — the *Dà lǐ yì* 大禮議 (Yáng Tínghé [KR2f0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0022), Hé Mèngchūn [KR2f0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0023), Hú Shìníng [KR2f0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0021), Zhāng Yuán [KR2f0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0026), Xià Yán [KR2f0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0027)), the Hé Lǎotài 賀老菜 / *Dōnglín* 東林 opposition (Lù Zhōnglì [KR2f0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0032), Zhōu Qǐyuán [KR2f0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0033)), Yellow-River management (Pān Jìxùn [KR2f0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0030), [KR2f0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0031)), and military policy on the northern frontier and against Wokou pirates (Tán Lún [KR2f0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0029)). Of these, the two Pān Jìxùn memorial collections ([KR2f0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0030), [KR2f0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0031)) are the indispensable primary source for late-sixteenth-century hydraulic engineering.

#### Memorials (*zòuyì*) — individual Qīng officials

Three early-Qīng *biéjí*-style memorial collections selected by the Sìkù as exemplary: *Zhāng Xiāngzhuàng zòushū* 張襄壯奏疏 [KR2f0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0034) (Zhāng Yǒng, frontier-military), *Jìn Wénxiāng zòushū* 靳文襄奏疏 [KR2f0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0035) (Jìn Fǔ, Yellow-River management — Pān Jìxùn's institutional heir), *Huáyě shūgǎo* 華野疏稿 [KR2f0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0036) (Guō Xiù, Kāngxī-era reform).

#### Memorials (*zòuyì*) — the great classified anthologies

The four monumental thematic collections that define the *zòuyì* anthology as a Chinese bibliographic genre:
- *Wǔcháo míngchén yánxíng lù* 五朝名臣言行錄 [KR2f0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0037) — Zhū Xī's 1172–1188 biographical-anecdotal anthology of Northern Sòng moral exemplars, the foundation of the *míngchén* canon and one of the principal Sòng *dàoxué* textual operations.
- *Sòng míngchén zòuyì* 宋名臣奏議 [KR2f0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0038) — Zhào Rǔyú's 1186 collection of 1,630 Northern-Sòng memorials by 241 authors, organized in 12 thematic divisions and 114 sub-categories. The principal classified anthology of Northern-Sòng administrative documentation, and the site of the famous Zhū Xī / Zhào Rǔyú by-person-versus-by-theme editorial debate.
- *Lìdài míngchén zòuyì* 歷代名臣奏議 [KR2f0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0039) — Yáng Shìqí and Huáng Huái's 350-*juàn*, ~8,000-memorial Yǒng-lè-era anthology (1416), the largest single memorial-anthology in pre-modern Chinese bibliography. Indispensable for Sòng and especially Yuán *zòuyì* (the Yuán *shílù* being lost in toto).
- *Yùxuǎn Míngchén zòuyì* 御選明臣奏議 [KR2f0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0041) — Qiánlóng's 1781–1786 imperial selection of Míng memorials, organized by author. The Sìkù's own canonical synthesis of Míng *míngchén* memorial-literature.

To which the *Míngchén jīngjì lù* 名臣經濟錄 [KR2f0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0040) (Huáng Xùn, *c.* 1540s) — a Míng-period thematic compilation of *jīngjì* (statecraft) memorials — is a fifth, narrower-scope member of the same family.

### Important persons

- [宋敏求](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E6%95%8F%E6%B1%82) — Sòng Mǐnqiú (1019–1079). Compiler of [KR2f0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0010) *Táng dà zhàolìng jí*; the principal mediator through whom Táng chancery prose has descended to us.
- [林虙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9E%97%E8%99%99) and [樓昉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A8%93%E6%98%89) — joint compilers, separated by a century, of [KR2f0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0011) *Liǎng Hàn zhàolìng* (Lín 1109; Lóu 1222); through them the Hàn edict-corpus survives reign-organized.
- [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) — Zhū Xī (1130–1200). Compiler of [KR2f0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0037) *Wǔcháo míngchén yánxíng lù*; the architect of the *míngchén* canon as a *dàoxué* moral-cultivation resource.
- [趙汝愚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E6%B1%9D%E6%84%9A) — Zhào Rǔyú (1140–1196). Compiler of [KR2f0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0038) *Sòng míngchén zòuyì*; the principal pioneer of by-theme classified-anthology method for memorial-text, in explicit methodological opposition to Zhū Xī's by-person approach.
- [范仲淹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8C%83%E4%BB%B2%E6%B7%B9) — Fàn Zhòngyān (989–1052). Author of [KR2f0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0012); founding figure of the Sòng *jīngshì* (statecraft) memorial tradition.
- [包拯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8C%85%E6%8B%AF) — Bāo Zhěng (999–1062). Author of the memorials in [KR2f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0013); cultural archetype of the upright remonstrating official.
- [劉安世](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96) — Liú Ānshì (1048–1125). - [楊士奇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E5%A3%AB%E5%A5%87) and [黃淮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E6%B7%AE) — Yáng Shìqí (1365–1444) and Huáng Huái (1367–1449). Joint editors-in-chief of [KR2f0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0039) *Lìdài míngchén zòuyì*; Yǒnglè cabinet ministers and the senior literary administrators of the early Míng.
- [商輅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%95%86%E8%BC%85), [王恕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%81%95), [馬文升](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E6%96%87%E5%8D%87), [楊一清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E4%B8%80%E6%B8%85), [胡世寧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E4%B8%96%E5%AF%A7), [楊廷和](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E5%BB%B7%E5%92%8C), [何孟春](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E5%AD%9F%E6%98%A5), [夏言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%8F%E8%A8%80), [譚綸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%9A%E7%B6%B8), [潘季馴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BD%98%E5%AD%A3%E9%A6%B4) — the principal Míng *zòuyì* authors collected here, each representing a major mid-Míng policy domain (palace administration, Censorate reform, fiscal-military integration, the *Dà lǐ yì* controversy, frontier defence, hydraulics).

Yōngzhèng additionally appears as commissioning *author* of the *Zhūpī yùzhǐ* [KR2f0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0009).

- [靳輔](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9D%B3%E8%BC%94) — Jìn Fǔ (1633–1692). Author of [KR2f0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0035); Pān Jìxùn's institutional successor in Yellow-River administration.

### Topics

- **Genre typology of imperial documents.** The classical typology — *cèshū* 策書 (mandate documents for the highest ranks), *zhìshū* 制書 (administrative orders), *zhàoshū* 詔書 (general edicts), *jièchì* 誡敕 (admonishing instructions), *cèshū* 冊書 (investiture documents), with later additions of *shàngyù* 上諭 (Qīng imperial pronouncements) and *zhūpī* 硃批 (vermilion rescripts) — is laid out programmatically in Hóng Zīkuí's *zǒnglùn* prefixed to [KR2f0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0011) *Liǎng Hàn zhàolìng*. Wilkinson 2018 §47.5.7 is the standard modern treatment.
- **Memorial sub-genres.** Within the *zòuyì* side, the principal sub-genres — *zòu* 奏, *yì* 議, *shū* 疏, *biǎo* 表, *zházǐ* 札子, *qǐ* 啓, and the Sòng-introduced *zòuzhé* 奏摺 — each have distinct formal and rhetorical conventions. The Sòng officials' *biéjí*-style collections ([KR2f0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0012)–0016) tend to be mixed-genre; the Míng and Qīng collections increasingly specialize. The Qīng *zòuzhé* (secret memorial), preserved in [KR2f0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0009), is the institutional climax of the genre — a confidential channel between provincial officials and the emperor personally, bypassing the regular bureaucracy.
- **By-person versus by-theme.** The single most consequential editorial-methodological debate in the division is the explicit Zhū Xī / Zhào Rǔyú disagreement preserved in the *tíyào* of [KR2f0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0038) (with the *Sìkù* editors decisively endorsing Zhào's by-theme approach). The downstream history of the genre shows both methods in active use: [KR2f0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0037) and [KR2f0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0041) organize by person, [KR2f0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0038) and [KR2f0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0039) by theme.
- **The anthology as documentary archive.** Because the Táng, Sòng, and Yuán *shílù* and *qǐjūzhù* are almost entirely lost, the *zhàolìng* and *zòuyì* anthologies collected in KR2f function as the principal *de facto* state archive for those dynasties. [KR2f0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0038) preserves Sòng court documentation; [KR2f0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0039) preserves Sòng and Yuán; [KR2f0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0010) preserves Táng. The *Sìkù* editors are explicit about this archival function and frame it as the category's principal scholarly justification.
- **Imperial self-canonization.** The Qīng *shèngxùn* / *shàngyù* / *zhūpī* program ([KR2f0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0001)–0002, 0004–0009) treats the dynasty's own ancestral pronouncements as canonical texts in the manner of the Confucian classics, complete with thematic divisions modelled on the *Zhōu lǐ* and the *Zhōngyōng*. This is a specifically Qīng innovation in imperial-document compilation; earlier dynasties did not aggregate ancestral pronouncements at this scale.
- **The *míngchén* canon.** The lineage [KR2f0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0037) → [KR2f0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0038) → [KR2f0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0039) → [KR2f0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0040) → [KR2f0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0041) traces the construction and re-construction of a canonical list of "famous officials" across six centuries, with each successive compiler revising the canon to reflect his own moment's political-moral concerns (Zhū Xī's Daoxue moralism; Zhào's policy-pragmatic by-theme classification; Yáng Shìqí's Yǒng-lè-era universalism; Huáng Xùn's mid-Míng statecraft turn; Qiánlóng's late-imperial selective consolidation).
- **The *Dà lǐ yì* and the Míng cluster.** A disproportionate fraction of the Míng *biéjí* collections ([KR2f0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2f/KR2f0021), 0022, 0023, 0026, 0027) consists of memorials submitted around the Jia-jìng accession's Great Rites Controversy of 1521–1524 — the defining political-ritual crisis of the mid-Míng, and one of the principal scholarly uses of the KR2f Míng materials.

# 傳記類 (KR2g)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2g 傳記類 *Zhuàn-jì lèi* — Histories — Biographical Writings](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/)

*Histories — Biographical Writings*

### Scope and scholarly tradition

The *Zhuànjì lèi* is the seventh subdivision of the *Shǐbù* 史部 in the Imperial Library's fourfold scheme. It collects works of formal biography that fall outside the *lièzhuàn* 列傳 sections of the *Zhèngshǐ* 正史: free-standing chronological biographies (*niánpǔ* 年譜), single-life accounts (*xíngzhuàng* 行狀, *biézhuàn* 別傳), thematic biographical anthologies (women, recluses, eminent ministers, "talented men" of a dynasty, school-and-lineage compendia), prefectural and local *xiāngxián* collections, *xuéàn* 學案 (school cases) tracing Confucian transmission, eyewitness campaign and embassy records that double as biographies of their compilers, and (under the *Sìkù* editors' final rubric *biélùzhīshǔ* 別錄之屬) travel diaries with a strong autobiographical cast. As Wilkinson notes (§9, "Biographies and prosopography"), the term *zhuànjì* 傳記 displaces the older *zázhuàn* 雜傳 from the Sòng onward and becomes the standard cover-term for biography in the imperial bibliographic tradition; the genre's diversification — especially the rise of the *niánpǔ* in the Sòng and of the *xuéàn* in the late Míng / early Qīng — is what gives the *Sìkù*'s *Zhuànjì* division its distinctive shape.

The 61 works collected here span from the Western Hàn (Liú Xiàng's *Gǔ liènǚ zhuàn* 古列女傳, c. 16 BCE) through the high Qiánlóng (Lǐ Qīngfù's *Mǐnzhōng lǐxué yuānyuán kǎo* 閩中理學淵源考, c. 1755), with the heaviest representation from the Southern Sòng and the Míng-Qīng transition — the two periods in which biographical compilation and *Dàoxué* lineage history were most actively cultivated. The *Sìkù* editors organize the division along four traditional sub-categories: *shèngxiánzhīshǔ* 聖賢之屬 (sages, e.g. the Confucius cluster), *míngrénzhīshǔ* 名人之屬 (named individuals, dominated by *niánpǔ* and single-life *xíngzhuàng*), *zǒnglùzhīshǔ* 總錄之屬 (collective anthologies, the bulk of the division), and *biélùzhīshǔ* 別錄之屬 (separate records, where the campaign narratives and travel diaries are placed). Wilkinson observes (§9, Table 25) that perhaps 600,000 Chinese biographies survive, the vast majority in Míng-Qīng gazetteers; the *Sìkù*'s *Zhuànjì* selection is therefore a tightly filtered canonical core, with the *cúnmù* 存目 ledger catching everything else.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The Liú Xiàng anchor.** *Gǔ liènǚ zhuàn* 古列女傳 [KR2g0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0017) is the foundational Hàn anthology of women's biography and the model for the entire *zǒnglù* sub-category. Liú Xiàng's editorial procedure — thematic categories, terminal four-character *sòng* 頌, illustrated folding-screen format — set a template that was followed continuously down to the Míng court compilation *Gǔjīn liènǚ zhuàn* 古今列女傳 [KR2g0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0035).

- **The Confucius / Kǒng-family cluster.** *Kǒngzǐ biānnián* 孔子編年 [KR2g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0001), the *Sìkù* editors' chosen head of the division, is paired with the two great Kǒng-family gazetteer-genealogies, *Dōngjiā zájì* 東家雜記 [KR2g0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0002) (Southern Sòng) and *Kǒngshì zǔtíng guǎngjì* 孔氏祖庭廣記 [KR2g0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0006) (Jīn). *Yànzǐ chūnqiū* 晏子春秋 [KR2g0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0003) — formally a Warring-States compilation — is placed in the *shèngxián* sub-category alongside them.

- **The Sòng *niánpǔ* form.** *Dù gōngbù niánpǔ* 杜工部年譜 [KR2g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0007) and *Dù gōngbù shī niánpǔ* 杜工部詩年譜 [KR2g0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0008), paired in the *Sìkù* edition, are early specimens of the genre Wilkinson identifies as the most important Sòng innovation in biographical form (§9.5); *Zhūzǐ niánpǔ* 朱子年譜 [KR2g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0016) is the standard Qīng *niánpǔ* of Zhū Xī.

- **The *Yuè Fēi* documentary archive.** *Jīntuó cuìbiān* 金佗稡編 [KR2g0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0010) is the *locus classicus* for Yuè Fēi's posthumous rehabilitation and the documentary foundation of the entire Chinese "loyalist general" cult. Compiled in two stages (1218, 1228) by his grandson [岳珂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B2%B3%E7%8F%82), it sets the pattern for later imperially-sanctioned martyrology in the division — including *Zhōngzhēn lù* 忠貞錄 [KR2g0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0013) (the Hé Téngjiāo cult) and *Zhūgě zhōngwǔ shū* 諸葛忠武書 [KR2g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0014).

- **The Sòng *Dàoxué* lineage project.** *Yī Luò yuānyuán lù* 伊洛淵源錄 [KR2g0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0023) and *Sòng míngchén yánxíng lù qiánjí* 宋名臣言行錄前集 [KR2g0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0024) are Zhū Xī's twin prosopographical works that establish the *Cheng-Zhū* lineage and the *Bei-Sòng* ministerial canon respectively. [杜大珪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E5%A4%A7%E7%8F%AA)'s *Míngchén bēizhuàn wǎnyǎn zhī jí* 名臣碑傳琬琰之集 [KR2g0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0025) (1194) is the parallel stele-anthology, the principal working source for Sòng prosopography down to the present.

- **The Yuán prosopographies.** *Táng cáizǐ zhuàn* 唐才子傳 [KR2g0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0032) (1304) by [辛文房](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%BE%9B%E6%96%87%E6%88%BF) is the standard collective biography of Táng poets, while *Yuáncháo míngchén shìlüè* 元朝名臣事略 [KR2g0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0033) (1329) by [蘇天爵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E5%A4%A9%E7%88%B5) is the foundational document for Yuán-period prosopography, on whose scaffold the *Yuánshǐ* *lièzhuàn* were built.

- **The Míng-Qīng *xuéàn* / *Lǐxué* lineage compendia.** *Míngrú xuéàn* 明儒學案 [KR2g0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0046) is Huáng Zōngxī's foundational instance of the *xuéàn* sub-genre. Three early-Qīng counter-and-correctives stand alongside it: [萬斯同](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%90%AC%E6%96%AF%E5%90%8C)'s *Rúlín zōngpài* 儒林宗派 [KR2g0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0049), [沈佳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E4%BD%B3)'s *Cheng-Zhū*-leaning *Míngrú yánxíng lù* 明儒言行錄 [KR2g0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0050), and [朱軾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E8%BB%BE)'s Yōngzhèng-court synthesis *Shǐzhuàn sān biān* 史傳三編 [KR2g0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0051). [李清馥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%B8%85%E9%A6%A5)'s *Mǐnzhōng lǐxué yuānyuán kǎo* 閩中理學淵源考 [KR2g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0052) (c. 1742–1755) closes the sequence with the most extensive single account of the *Cheng-Zhū* lineage in Fújiàn.

- **The Qing imperial-Banner archive.** Four Qiánlóng *Qīndìng* 欽定 (imperially-fixed) compilations form a single documentary block on Manchu Banner and tributary-prince history: *Qīndìng Bāqí Mǎnzhōu shìzú tōngpǔ* 欽定八旗滿州氏族通譜 [KR2g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0044) (1744), *Qīndìng shèngcháo xùnjié zhūchén lù* 欽定勝朝殉節諸臣錄 [KR2g0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0045) (1776), *Qīndìng wàifān Měnggǔ Huíbù wánggōng biǎozhuàn* 欽定外藩蒙古回部王公表傳 [KR2g0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0043) (1779), and *Qīndìng zōngshì wánggōng gōngjī biǎozhuàn* 欽定宗室王公功績表傳 [KR2g0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0042) (1781). They are the indispensable sources for Manchu Banner prosopography and the official *Sìkù*-period statement of Qiánlóng's reading of the Qīng founders' history.

- **The Sòng-Yuán travel-diary cluster (*biélù*).** [滕甫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BB%95%E7%94%AB)'s *Zhēngnán lù* 征南錄 [KR2g0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0053) (Nóng Zhìgāo campaign, 1052–54), [陸游](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E6%B8%B8)'s *Rùshǔ jì* 入蜀記 [KR2g0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0056) (1170), and [范成大](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8C%83%E6%88%90%E5%A4%A7)'s pair *Cānluán lù* 驂鸞錄 [KR2g0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0054) (1172–75) and *Wúchuán lù* 吳船錄 [KR2g0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0055) (1177) together constitute the classical Southern-Sòng corpus of the *rìjì*-style travel-diary as biographical form. *Xīshǐ jì* 西使記 [KR2g0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0057) is the principal Chinese eyewitness record of the Mongol western campaign of 1252–60 (Cháng Dé's mission to Hülegü), and the canonical Chinese source on the destruction of Alamut and Baghdad.

- **The Míng-Qīng provincial *xiāngxián*.** *Jīngkǒu qíjiù zhuàn* 京口耆舊傳 [KR2g0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0029) (Zhènjiāng), *Pǔyáng rénwù jì* 浦陽人物記 [KR2g0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0034) (Pǔyáng), *Bǎiyuè xiānxián zhì* 百越先賢志 [KR2g0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0040) (Guǎngdōng), and *Zhōngzhōu rénwù kǎo* 中州人物考 [KR2g0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0047) (Hénán) exemplify the *xiāngxián* genre, a sub-form to which the *Sìkù* editors were notably hospitable.

### Topics

- **Moral exemplarity and its categories.** From Liú Xiàng onward, the *Zhuànjì* division is organized by moral category — *liènǚ* (chaste / exemplary women), *gāoshì* (eminent recluses), *liánlì* (incorrupt officials, see *Liánlì zhuàn* 廉吏傳 [KR2g0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0021)), *zhōngzhēn* (loyal-and-true), *míngrú* (eminent Confucians). The categories are not neutral filing-headers; they encode the work's normative argument.
- **The *niánpǔ* as biographical form.** A Sòng innovation (Wilkinson §9.5), applied first to the great Táng poets ([KR2g0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0007), [KR2g0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0008)) and to Confucius himself ([KR2g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0001)), then to the Sòng *Dàoxué* masters ([KR2g0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0016)). The genre's premise — that a single life can be reconstructed year by year from documentary fragments — anticipates and trains the *kǎozhèng* 考證 sensibility.
- **The *xuéàn* and the historiography of Confucian transmission.** Zhū Xī's *Yī Luò yuānyuán lù* [KR2g0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0023) is the methodological seed; Huáng Zōngxī's *Míngrú xuéàn* [KR2g0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0046) is the mature form; the early-Qīng quartet ([KR2g0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0049), [KR2g0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0050), [KR2g0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0051), [KR2g0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0052)) plays out the form's possibilities. The central debate is whether to organize by *xuépài* (school) or by chronology, and whether to admit *Yáojiāng* (Wáng Yángmíng) figures.
- **Sòng partisan documentation and the politics of rehabilitation.** *Jīntuó cuìbiān* [KR2g0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0010) and *Wèi Zhènggōng jiànlù* 魏鄭公諫錄 [KR2g0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0004) together with its Yuán continuation [KR2g0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0012) are documentary archives compiled to defend or restore a posthumous reputation; *Qìngyuán dǎngjìn* 慶元黨禁 [KR2g0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0027) is the partisan record of the 1196 *Dàoxué* proscription. The genre's premise is that historiography is itself a form of vindication.
- **The Qīng imperial reordering of dynastic memory.** The four Qiánlóng *Qīndìng* compilations [KR2g0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0042)–[KR2g0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0045) are not merely biographical; they are official re-readings — Dorgon rehabilitated, the Banner founders ennobled, the Míng martyrs canonized — that recast Qīng identity at the high point of the *Sìkù* project.
- **Travel-diary as autobiography.** The *biélù* sub-category at the end of the division ([KR2g0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0053)–[KR2g0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0061)) treats the eyewitness *rìjì* as a biographical form: the traveller's *kǎozhèng* notes, route observations, and self-positioning constitute a kind of indirect life-narrative. The Sòng pair Lù Yóu / Fàn Chéngdà is canonical; the Yuán *Xīshǐ jì* [KR2g0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2g/KR2g0057) extends the form to inter-civilizational embassy.
- **Provincial *xiāngxián* compilation.** *Xiāngxián* (local-worthy) anthologies of a single prefecture or province become a recognizable sub-form from the Southern Sòng onward; they are the prefectural-gazetteer's biographical core extracted and re-circulated as free-standing texts.

# 史鈔類 (KR2h)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2h 史鈔類 *Shǐchāo lèi* — Histories — History Excerpts](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition
KR2h gathers works the *Sìkù quánshū zǒngmù* 四庫全書總目 places under 史鈔類 (also written 史抄類): compilations that excerpt, abridge, or topically re-arrange one or more of the Standard Histories rather than producing fresh historical narrative of their own. The *Sìkù* editors' own programmatic statement — that *shǐchāo* descends from Confucius' editorial reduction of the *Documents* — is a polite way of giving a low-status genre an august pedigree, and Wilkinson (§49.6.1) classes the category accordingly as a useful but undervalued route into the historical corpus for readers who could not face the bulk of the *Standard Histories* whole. Two formal types are represented in the WYG selection: the **catchword-and-quotation** *shǐchāo*, which excerpts striking phrases or incidents from one or two parent histories under brief lemmata while preserving the parent's chapter order — the line that runs from [KR2h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0001) in the early Sòng to [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003) in the early Qīng; and the **topical re-arrangement** of an existing history, modeled on the *Cèfǔ yuánguī* 冊府元龜, represented by [KR2h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0002), which redistributes Sīmǎ Guāng's [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* 資治通鑑 [KR2b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0011) across 271 thematic sections (*mén* 門).

The division is small — three works survive in the WYG selection, spanning seven centuries — but methodologically coherent: each is a finder-aid for a literary user, not a critical edition for the historian. The principal scholarly interest of the category lies in (a) its source-critical value, since *shǐchāo* of this sort occasionally preserve commentary readings that the parent woodblock tradition has lost (the *Sìkù tíyào* on [KR2h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0001) makes this point sharply, citing the lost "Sì Hào" 四皓 entry of Yán Shīgǔ 顏師古 [顏師古](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E5%B8%AB%E5%8F%A4)); and (b) its documentation of late-imperial reading practice, particularly the late-Sòng vogue for *Tōngjiàn*-derivatives of which [KR2h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0002) is one of three principal exemplars.

### Important texts and text clusters
The three works in the WYG witness fall into two clusters separated by genealogy of method, not by date:

- The **catchword/quotation *shǐchāo*** of the Standard Histories
  - *Liǎng Hàn bówén* 兩漢博聞 [KR2h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0001) — Yáng Kǎn's [楊侃](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E4%BE%83) early Sòng (989–1032) excerpt-book of *Hànshū* (7 *juàn*) and *Hòu Hànshū* (5 *juàn*), reproducing each excerpt with the standard commentary of Yán Shīgǔ [顏師古](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E5%B8%AB%E5%8F%A4) or Lǐ Xián [李賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E8%B3%A2). The earliest surviving Sòng *shǐchāo* of the two Hàn histories, and the explicit methodological model for [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003).
  - *Nán shǐ shíxiǎo lù* 南史識小錄 (with *Běi shǐ shíxiǎo lù* 北史識小錄) [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003) — Shěn Míngsūn [沈名蓀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E5%90%8D%E8%93%80) and Zhū Kūntián [朱昆田](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E6%98%86%E7%94%B0)'s 1690 Qīng pair-volume on Lǐ Yánshòu's [李延壽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%BB%B6%E5%A3%BD) *Nánshǐ* 南史 and *Běishǐ* 北史 [KR2a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0006) [KR2a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2a/KR2a0007), transferring the *Liǎng Hàn bówén* method onto the Táng-period summary histories of the Northern and Southern Dynasties. A chrestomathy for poets and prose-stylists rather than a work of historical scholarship; the catalog title reflects only the *Nánshǐ* half of what is in fact a 16-*juàn* whole.
- The **topical re-arrangement** of a parent history
  - *Tōngjiàn zǒnglèi* 通鑑總類 [KR2h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0002) — Shěn Shū's [沈樞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E6%A8%9E) late Southern Sòng (*ca.* 1180–1208) topical compendium that breaks up Sīmǎ Guāng's *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* and redistributes its events across 271 thematic sections in chronological order within each section, preserving Sīmǎ Guāng's editorial *yuē* 曰 verdicts. Together with Yuán Shū's [袁樞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%81%E6%A8%9E) *Tōngjiàn jìshì běnmò* 通鑑紀事本末 (1175, narrative-by-event) and Zhū Xī's *Tōngjiàn gāngmù* 通鑑綱目 [KR2b0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0014) (moral-historical), this work is the third of the three canonical Southern Sòng re-arrangements of the *Tōngjiàn*, and the only one to organize its parent's material by *content category*.

### Important persons
- [楊侃](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E4%BE%83) (Yáng Kǎn, 964–1032; later Yáng Dàyǎ 楊大雅 after the Zhēnzōng taboo) — Qiántáng 錢塘 native, *jìnshì* of Duāngǒng 2 (989), Academician of the Hall of Worthies (集賢院學士). The earliest *shǐchāo* compiler represented in the division; established the catchword-and-commentary format that [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003) explicitly reproduces. (The catalog meta's "d. 521" is a conflation with the Northern Wèi homonym; see [KR2h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0001).)
- [沈樞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E6%A8%9E) (Shěn Shū, *zì* Chíyào 持要, posth. Xiànmǐn 憲敏) — Déqīng 德清 native, Shàoxīng-era *jìnshì*, retired Tàizǐ zhānshì 太子詹事 / Guānglù qīng 光祿卿. Compiled [KR2h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0002) in retirement, reportedly working on it past his ninetieth year, and so the division's exemplar of the topical-rearrangement type.
- [沈名蓀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E5%90%8D%E8%93%80) (Shěn Míngsūn, *zì* Jiànfāng 澗芳) — Qiántáng native of early Kāngxī Zhèjiāng literary circles; co-compiler of [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003). Lifedates are not securely known.
- [朱昆田](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E6%98%86%E7%94%B0) (Zhū Kūntián, *zì* Wén'àng 文盎, 1652–1699) — Xiùshuǐ 秀水 native, son of Zhū Yízūn 朱彝尊 [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A), and Shěn Míngsūn's co-compiler on [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003); brings the early-Qīng Pùshū tíng 曝書亭 milieu into the division.
- [樓鑰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A8%93%E9%91%B0) (Lóu Yuè, 1137–1213) — wrote the 1208 preface to [KR2h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0002) when its Cháoyáng 潮陽 print was being prepared by Shěn Shū's youngest son. Lóu's preface is the firmest *terminus ante quem* for the work and is the principal external testimony to Shěn Shū's life and method.

### Topics
- **The *shǐchāo* as method**: catchword + parent passage + commentary, with no editorial voice, no topical re-ordering ([KR2h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0001), [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003)) versus systematic content-categorial re-distribution of an entire parent history ([KR2h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0002)). The division is the cleanest place in the *Sìkù* to watch the two procedures side by side.
- **The literary function of history-excerpts.** All three works are addressed at least as much to the literary user — the poet looking for an allusion, the prose-stylist gathering well-cut diction — as to the historian. The *Sìkù tíyào* on [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003) makes the defense explicit, framing *shǐchāo* as the discipline that prizes the stylistic excess (especially Lǐ Yánshòu's notorious fondness for *jīxiáng* 機祥 / auspicia) that orthodox historiographic critique deplores.
- **The late-Sòng *Tōngjiàn*-derivatives boom.** [KR2h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0002) stands in a defined family with Yuán Shū's *jìshì běnmò* and Zhū Xī's *gāngmù* [KR2b0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0014); the division therefore documents one third of the late-Sòng reaction to the sheer bulk of [KR2b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0011).
- **Source-critical value.** The *Sìkù tíyào* on [KR2h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0001) singles out the *Sì Hào* entry to argue that *shǐchāo* can preserve commentary readings lost in the parent textual tradition — a point that justifies a low-prestige genre on philological rather than literary grounds.
- **Status of the genre.** The *Sìkù* editors place *shǐchāo* low in the hierarchy of 史部 categories (only three texts admitted, against many dozens for 編年 or 別史), yet open their category-preface with the Confucian Documents-editing pedigree. Wilkinson's §49.6.1 treats this stance even-handedly: the genre is minor, but the abbreviations it produced were a major actual route into historical knowledge for non-specialists.

### Timeline
- 989–1032 — *Liǎng Hàn bówén* 兩漢博聞 [KR2h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0001) — earliest surviving Sòng *shǐchāo* of the two Hàn histories; establishes the catchword-and-commentary format that the Qīng compilers of [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003) adopt verbatim.
- *ca.* 1180–1208 — *Tōngjiàn zǒnglèi* 通鑑總類 [KR2h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0002) — Southern Sòng topical re-arrangement of [KR2b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2b/KR2b0011) across 271 thematic sections; the division's sole representative of the *Cèfǔ yuánguī*-style method.
- 1690 — *Nán shǐ shíxiǎo lù* 南史識小錄 (with *Běi shǐ shíxiǎo lù*) [KR2h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2h/KR2h0003) — early-Kāngxī Qīng chrestomathy on Lǐ Yánshòu's two Táng-period dynastic histories; the latest entry in the WYG selection and the only Qīng work in the division.

# 載記類 (KR2i)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2i 載記類 *Zǎijì lèi* — Histories — Annals of Non-Legitimate Regimes](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

*Zǎijì* 載記 is the fourth-from-last of the fifteen *History* (史部) sub-categories in the *Sìkù quánshū zǒngmù* 四庫全書總目 (see Wilkinson §47 Table 89). The *Sìkù* editors borrowed the term from the *Jìnshū* 晉書, where Fáng Xuánlíng [房玄齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%BF%E7%8E%84%E9%BD%A1) had used it to house the basic annals of the fourteen of the *Wǔhú Shíliùguó* 五胡十六國 (Sixteen Kingdoms of the Five Barbarians) that the Táng court refused to grant *běnjì* 本紀 status. *Zǎijì* in turn replaces the earlier bibliographic labels *bàshǐ* 霸史 ("histories of hegemons" — used since the *Suízhì* 隋志) and the still earlier *wěishǐ* 偽史 ("false histories" — from Ruǎn Xiàoxù's 阮孝緒 *Qīlù* 七錄). The euphemism softens with each change, but the underlying judgement is constant: these are histories of states the central tradition did *not* recognize as standing in the orthodox dynastic succession (*zhèngtǒng* 正統). In the *Sìkù*, the rubric covers 23 works (Wilkinson §47, Table 89), and the corpus that follows here is exactly that *Sìkù* set.

The chronological reach of the category is unusually wide. The two earliest works are Later-Hàn narratives of the Spring-and-Autumn-period *Wú* 吳 and *Yuè* 越 ([KR2i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0001), [KR2i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0002)); the latest are early-Qīng. In between sit the major regional histories of every era of division — the Sixteen Kingdoms of the 4th–5th centuries ([KR2i0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0005), [KR2i0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0006)), the Sìchuān gazetteer *Huáyáng Guózhì* [KR2i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0003), the Hòu Zhào *Yèzhōng jì* [KR2i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0004), the *Mánshū* on Nánzhào [KR2i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0007), the dense cluster of Five-Dynasties / Ten-Kingdoms regional histories ([KR2i0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0008)–[KR2i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0019)), the early-Qīng synthesis of the Ten Kingdoms ([KR2i0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0021)), and finally a *fùlù* 附錄 of two East-Asian histories (Korea [KR2i0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0022), Vietnam [KR2i0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0023) and the related Vietnamese gazetteer [KR2i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0020)) — works on Sinographic states beyond the Chinese empire proper, retained by the *Sìkù* editors precisely on the principle that they too document polities outside the legitimate succession. The transmissional history is heavy with loss and reconstruction: a significant share of the corpus survives only through *Sìkù*-editor recovery from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* 永樂大典 (notably [KR2i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0004), [KR2i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0007), [KR2i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0012)), late-Míng learned re-compilation (the 100-juàn [KR2i0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0005) is a Tú Qiáosūn / Xiàng Lín reconstruction of Cuī Hóng's lost original), or single-line Chinese transmission of foreign-origin texts ([KR2i0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0023), lost in Vietnam itself).

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Wú Yuè Chūnqiū* 吳越春秋 [KR2i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0001) and *Yuè Jué Shū* 越絕書 [KR2i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0002) — the two great Later-Hàn narratives of the Wú-Yuè rivalry, founding works of the *bàshǐ* / *zǎijì* category and, along with the *Zhànguócè*, the earliest non-canonical histories with a clear regional focus.
- *Huáyáng Guózhì* 華陽國志 [KR2i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0003) — Cháng Qú's *c.* 348–354 gazetteer of Bā-Shǔ-Hànzhōng-Nánzhōng, **the earliest regional history to survive intact** (Wilkinson §60.3) and the source standing behind Lì Dàoyuán's *Shuǐjīng zhù* and Lè Shǐ's *Tàipíng huányǔ jì* for everything on the southwest.
- *Yèzhōng jì* 鄴中記 [KR2i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0004) — the unique pre-Táng witness to Hòu Zhào Yè under Shí Hǔ; the Tóngquè, Bīngjǐng, and Jīnfèng tái complexes are described nowhere else.
- The Sixteen Kingdoms pair, [KR2i0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0005) (100-juàn Wànlì recompilation of Cuī Hóng's lost original by Tú Qiáosūn 屠喬孫 and Xiàng Lín 項琳) and [KR2i0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0006) (16-juàn *Hàn-Wèi cóngshū* recension) — paired witnesses to a Northern-Wèi original lost in the Northern Sòng; together with the *Jìnshū Zǎijì* and Tāng Qiú's 湯球 *Shíliùguó Chūnqiū jíbǔ* they form the modern evidence-base for the period 304–439.
- *Mánshū* 蠻書 [KR2i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0007) — Fán Chuò's 862–864 ethnographic-strategic treatise on Nánzhào, the principal source behind Sòng Qí's *Nánmánzhuàn* in the *Xīn-Tángshū* and Sīmǎ Guāng's *Tōngjiàn* on Yúnnán; preserves the earliest external lexica of Tibeto-Burman *Bái* and *Yí*.
- **The Southern Táng cluster** — [KR2i0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0008) *Diàojī Lìtán*, [KR2i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0009) *Jiāngnán Yěshǐ*, [KR2i0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0010) *Jiāngnán Biélù*, [KR2i0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0011) *Jiāngbiǎo Zhì*, [KR2i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0012) *Jiāngnán Yúzǎi*, [KR2i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0017) *Mǎshì Nán Táng Shū*, [KR2i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0018) *Lùshì Nán Táng Shū*. This is the densest sub-cluster of the division — six privately-compiled early-Sòng witnesses (most by men with personal ties to the conquered court) plus the two great Sòng *Nán Táng shū* recensions by [馬令](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E4%BB%A4) (1105) and [陸游](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E6%B8%B8) (*c.* 1180–1209). Wilkinson §61.8.1 #5 notes that Lù Yóu's recension "corrects and polishes" Mǎ Lìng's but Mǎ Lìng "nevertheless remains the more important of the two."
- **The Shǔ cluster** — [KR2i0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0014) *Jǐnlǐ Qíjiù Zhuàn* (970) and [KR2i0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0016) *Shǔ Táowù* (Zhāng Tángyīng, *c.* 1064–1071) — the two principal Sòng-period chronicles of the Former and Latter Shǔ regimes; uniquely preserve the full *Guānzhēn* 官箴 of 孟昶 Mèng Chǎng, from which the four-line *Jièshí* 戒石 admonition was drawn.
- *Sān-Chǔ Xīnlù* 三楚新錄 [KR2i0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0013) — Zhōu Yǔchōng's early-Sòng chronicle of the three regional regimes of the Xiāng-Hàn basin (Mǎ-Chǔ, Wǔlíng, Jīngnán).
- *Wǔguó Gùshì* 五國故事 [KR2i0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0015) — an anonymous early-Sòng *xiǎoshuō*-style miscellany on the five southern Five-Dynasties regional regimes.
- *Wú-Yuè Bèishǐ* 吳越備史 [KR2i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0019) — Qián Yǎn's internal Wú-Yuè dynastic history, written under false attribution to the junior officials Fàn Jǐong 范坰 and Lín Yǔ 林禹; the unique narrative source for the *Bǎojìngānmín* 保境安民 ideology of the Qián family.
- *Shíguó Chūnqiū* 十國春秋 [KR2i0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0021) — Wú Rènchén's 114-juàn early-Qīng synthesis, the **definitive scholarly treatment** of the Ten Kingdoms. Drawing systematically on every Sòng-period regional history in this division (plus dozens of further sources, many lost), it pioneers the *zǐzhù* 子注 method of preserving alternative-source readings as sub-commentary. Wilkinson §61.8.1 #7 places it alongside the *Jiǔguó zhì* and the *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* as the principal references for the period.
- *Ānnán Zhìlüè* 安南志略 [KR2i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0020) — Lí Trắc's 1340 gazetteer of Đại Việt, the **earliest extant systematic Chinese-language description of Vietnam**, written by a Trần-dynasty defector to the Yuán.
- *Cháoxiān Shǐlüè* 朝鮮史略 [KR2i0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0022) and *Yuèshǐ Lüè* 越史略 [KR2i0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0023) — the *fùlù* 附錄 pair: a Joseon-period annalistic Korean history that reached China during the Imjin War, and an anonymous Trần-period Vietnamese chronicle (*Đại Việt sử lược* 大越史略) that, lost in Vietnam, survives only through Míng *Yǒnglè*-era Chinese transmission.

### Topics

The conceptual unity of the division is given by the bibliographic-political category *zǎijì* itself — a recognition that the polities recorded here stand outside the *zhèngtǒng* line and yet require historical treatment. Several recurring problems organize the corpus:

- **Legitimacy and the choice of historiographical form.** Whether a regional ruler receives *běnjì*, *zhǔ*, or *zǎijì* treatment is the central editorial question. Cuī Hóng's original *Shíliùguó Chūnqiū* (recorded by Liú Zhījī, *Shǐtōng*) dated events by Jìn / Sòng reign-names while writing as a Northern-Wèi official — a choice the *Sìkù* editors track through both the surviving Míng recensions. Lù Yóu's [KR2i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0018) takes the opposite path, granting *běnjì* to the Southern-Táng rulers in defiance of Liú Zhījī. Mǎ Lìng [KR2i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0017) takes the middle path of *zhǔ*. The lost recension of 胡恢 Hú Huī used *zǎijì*, on the *Jìnshū* model. Each choice is a thesis about legitimacy.

- **Forgery, recompilation, and *jíyì* 輯佚 reconstruction.** A high proportion of the corpus survives only through scholarly recovery: [KR2i0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0005) is a learned Wàn-lì-era reconstruction of a Northern-Wèi original lost in the Northern Sòng; [KR2i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0004) and [KR2i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0007) were recovered from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* by the *Sìkù* editors; [KR2i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0012) was recovered as a witness *to* [KR2i0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0011), which itself is partially mutilated. The category is therefore a sustained case-study in the methods and limits of late-imperial textual recovery.

- **Source-criticism and the *zǐzhù* method.** The early-Qīng *Shíguó Chūnqiū* [KR2i0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0021) is the methodological capstone of the category: Wú Rènchén embeds alternative-source readings as sub-commentary on the main narrative, anticipating modern critical-edition practice. The Southern-Táng cluster (six private histories that explicitly read and correct each other — [KR2i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0009) criticized by [KR2i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0012) criticized by [KR2i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0017) / [KR2i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0018)) is itself a model of cumulative source-criticism.

- **Regional ethnography and the *Yúdì* 輿地 tradition.** Several works are as much regional gazetteer as dynastic history. The *Huáyáng Guózhì* [KR2i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0003) is the prototype; the *Mánshū* [KR2i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0007), the *Yèzhōng jì* [KR2i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0004), the early sections of the *Yuè Jué Shū* [KR2i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0002), the *Ānnán Zhìlüè* [KR2i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0020), and the *Sìchuān* and *Yúnnán* portions of [KR2i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0007) all preserve ethnographic and linguistic material on non-Hàn populations not available elsewhere — Tibeto-Burman *Bái* and *Yí* lexica (*Mánshū*), Yuè military-command transcriptions (*Yuè Jué Shū*), and Sìchuān-southwestern *Cóng* / *Pánhú* / *Bīn* / *Sǒu* peoples (*Huáyáng Guózhì*).

- **External histories and the limits of the Sinographic record.** The two *fùlù* texts [KR2i0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0022) (Korea) and [KR2i0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0023) (Vietnam), together with the closely-paired [KR2i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0020), extend the *zǎijì* logic to states that were never inside the empire. The *Sìkù* editors' decision to retain them — explicitly framed in the *tíyào* of [KR2i0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0023) on the analogy of the *Chūnqiū*'s recording of Wú and Chǔ — preserves uniquely Vietnamese era-names and Korean royal genealogies suppressed from the standard *Yuánshǐ* / *Míngshǐ* *wàiguózhuàn*.

- **The Southern-Táng historiographical tradition.** Seven of the 23 works (≈ 30 % of the division) treat the Southern Táng. The cluster forms the densest case-study in late-imperial Chinese historiography of source-critical evolution: an official history (Xú Xuàn / Tāng Yuè's *Jiāngnán lù*, lost) generates a corrective tradition of private histories ([KR2i0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0008), [KR2i0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0010), [KR2i0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0011)), an alternative *yěshǐ* tradition ([KR2i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0009)), a Northern-Sòng meta-corrective ([KR2i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0012)), two great Sòng *Nán Táng shū* ([KR2i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0017), [KR2i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0018)), and an early-Qīng synthesis ([KR2i0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0021)).

### Timeline

- *c.* 25–100 — *Wú Yuè Chūnqiū* 吳越春秋 [KR2i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0001) — Later-Hàn narrative of Wú-Yuè; founding work of the *bàshǐ* / *zǎijì* category.
- *c.* 25–75 — *Yuè Jué Shū* 越絕書 [KR2i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0002) — companion regional history of Yuè by Yuán Kāng / Wú Píng; earliest substantial regional history of southeast China.
- *c.* 348–354 — *Huáyáng Guózhì* 華陽國志 [KR2i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0003) — Cháng Qú's gazetteer of the southwest; earliest surviving regional history in the corpus.
- *c.* 350–420 — *Yèzhōng jì* 鄴中記 [KR2i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0004) — Lù Huì's record of Hòu Zhào Yè, surviving only through *Sìkù* reconstruction.
- 862–864 — *Mánshū* 蠻書 [KR2i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0007) — Fán Chuò's strategic-ethnographic treatise on Nánzhào.
- 968–988 — *Wú-Yuè Bèishǐ* 吳越備史 [KR2i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0019) — Qián Yǎn's internal Wú-Yuè dynastic history (under false names).
- 970 — *Jǐnlǐ Qíjiù Zhuàn* 錦里耆舊傳 [KR2i0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0014) — Jù Yánqìng's annalistic chronicle of Former and Latter Shǔ.
- *c.* 970–1020 — *Sān-Chǔ Xīnlù* 三楚新錄 [KR2i0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0013) — Zhōu Yǔchōng's chronicle of Mǎ-Chǔ, Wǔlíng, and Jīngnán.
- *c.* 970–1010 — *Wǔguó Gùshì* 五國故事 [KR2i0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0015) — anonymous early-Sòng miscellany on the five southern Five-Dynasties regimes.
- *c.* 975–1000 — *Diàojī Lìtán* 釣磯立談 [KR2i0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0008) — the anonymous son of Shǐ Xūbái on the fall of the Southern Táng.
- *c.* 980–1010 — *Jiāngnán Biélù* 江南別錄 [KR2i0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0010) — Chén Péngnián's private supplement to the official *Jiāngnán lù*.
- *c.* 985–1020 — *Jiāngnán Yěshǐ* 江南野史 [KR2i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0009) — Lóng Gǔn's "wild" history of the Southern Táng.
- 1010 — *Jiāngbiǎo Zhì* 江表志 [KR2i0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0011) — Zhèng Wénbǎo's authoritative Southern-Táng chronicle (precisely datable).
- *c.* 1064–1071 — *Shǔ Táowù* 蜀檮杌 [KR2i0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0016) — Zhāng Tángyīng's chronological annals of Former and Latter Shǔ.
- *c.* 1075–1100 — *Jiāngnán Yúzǎi* 江南餘載 [KR2i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0012) — anonymous *Xīníng*-era corrective to the early-Sòng Southern-Táng tradition.
- 1105 — *Mǎshì Nán Táng Shū* 馬氏南唐書 [KR2i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0017) — Mǎ Lìng's 30-juàn *jìzhuàn* history (precisely datable).
- *c.* 1180–1209 — *Lùshì Nán Táng Shū* 陸氏南唐書 [KR2i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2i/KR2i0018) — Lù Yóu's austere 18-juàn redaction.

# 時令類 (KR2j)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2j 時令類 *Shílìng lèi* — Histories — Seasonal Ordinances](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

The *Shílìng* 時令 ("Seasonal Ordinances") category of the *Sìkù quánshū* gathers compilations on the calendar year, the festivals (*suìshí* 歲時 / *jiérì* 節日), the phenological signs (*wùhòu* 物候), and the ritual-administrative *yuèlìng* 月令 prescriptions that govern court and countryside through the twelve months. The genre's textual ancestry runs from the *Yuèlìng* 月令 chapter of the *Lǐjì* (itself drawn from the *Lǚshì chūnqiū* 呂氏春秋), through Cài Yōng's 蔡邕 and Kǒng Yǐngdá's 孔穎達 exegesis, through the Hàn agro-festival manuals (Cuī Shí's 崔寔 *Sìmín yuèlìng* 四民月令, late 2nd c.), the medieval almanacs (*Sìshí zuǎnyào* 四時纂要), and into the Sòng festival anthologies and late-Míng household encyclopedias. As an independent *Sìkù* category, *shílìng* is a relatively late editorial gesture: as Wilkinson notes (§39.15.1), the category was a Sòng innovation, with such works having previously been folded into agricultural and miscellaneous treatises in the *zǐbù*.

The *Sìkù* editors admitted only two titles to this category in the canon proper — a Southern Sòng compilation and a Kāngxī imperial revision of a late-Míng work. Together they bracket nearly five centuries of *yuèlìng* anthologizing and represent the genre's two principal modes: the eclectic *bàiguān* festival compendium of late-Sòng literati culture (*Suìshí guǎngjì* [KR2j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0001)) and the imperially-supervised, classically-anchored court compilation (*Yùdìng yuèlìng jíyào* [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002)). The division is therefore unusually small but conceptually self-contained — Wilkinson's seasonal-calendar discussion (§9.12, §39.15) treats the two as the matching late-Sòng and high-Qīng landmarks of the genre.

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Suìshí guǎngjì* 歲時廣記 [KR2j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0001) — Chén Yuánjìng's 陳元靚 four-juan late-Southern-Sòng anthology of festival lore arranged by month (春 46 / 夏 50 / 秋 32 / 冬 38 entries); the principal Sòng vehicle for the partially-lost *Jīng Chǔ suìshí jì* 荊楚歲時記 of Zōng Lǐn 宗懍, and the work in which the late-imperial Chinese festival year takes its received shape (Wilkinson §9.12.1).
- *Yùdìng yuèlìng jíyào* 御定月令輯要 [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002) — the Kāngxī court's 24-juan re-edition of Féng Yìngjīng's 馮應京 late-Míng *Yuèlìng guǎngyì* 月令廣義, with imperial preface dated Kāngxī 54.4.9 (12 May 1715); the standard imperial-Qīng *yuèlìng* repository, organized in a four-tier annual / seasonal / monthly / sub-monthly hierarchy and rebuilt on the editorial template *biéqǐ yìlì* 別起義例 dictated by Kāngxī himself.

The two titles together also mark a methodological contrast that is visible across the category: the Sòng compilation favours full quotation from informal narrative literature (*bàiguān* 稗官) and folk practice, while the Qīng compilation enforces the descending citation hierarchy classics → histories → philosophers → regional sources that organized the Wǔyīngdiàn 武英殿 imperial publishing programme.

### Important persons

- [陳元靚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%85%83%E9%9D%9A) — late-Southern-Sòng *jūshì* of Fújiàn / Mǐnběi book-trade origin, compiler of *Suìshí guǎngjì* [KR2j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0001) and of the foundational *rìyòng lèishū* 日用類書 *Shìlín guǎngjì* 事林廣記; the only attributed Sòng author in the category.
- [朱鑑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E9%91%91) (1190–1258) — eldest grandson of Zhū Xī 朱熹, *zhī Wúwéijūn Cháoxiàn shì*, author of the preface that anchors the *Suìshí guǎngjì* in Lǐzōng's reign and provides the principal evidence for the work's dating.
- [李光地](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%85%89%E5%9C%B0) (1642–1718) — *Wényuāngé dàxuéshì* and chief director (*zǒng yuè* 總閱) of the *Yùdìng yuèlìng jíyào* [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002); the senior figure in the late-Kāngxī Hànlín editorial cohort that produced the imperial revision.
- [王掞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%8E%9E) — *Wényuāngé dàxuéshì jiān Lǐbù shàngshū*, co-director of [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002).
- [何焯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E7%84%AF) (1661–1722) — the foremost philological textual critic of the Kāngxī Hànlín, member of the proof-collation team for [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002); his presence on the editorial roll is the principal sign of the work's bibliographic seriousness.
- [張廷玉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%BB%B7%E7%8E%89) (1672–1755), [蔣廷錫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E5%BB%B7%E9%8C%AB) (1669–1732), [陳邦彥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%82%A6%E5%BD%A5) (1678–1752), [楊名時](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E5%90%8D%E6%99%82) (1661–1736), [張照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E7%85%A7) (1691–1745), [陳鵬年](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%B5%AC%E5%B9%B4) (1663–1723) — junior Hànlín collators on [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002) who would go on to dominate the early Yōngzhèng and Qiánlóng courts; their participation locates the category's flagship work at the heart of the late-Kāngxī Hànlín *xuétáng* pipeline that staffed the Wǔyīngdiàn imperial-publishing programme.

### Topics

- **The *yuèlìng* lineage.** The *Lǐjì* *Yuèlìng* chapter and the *Lǚshì chūnqiū*, mediated through Cài Yōng and Kǒng Yǐngdá, anchor every work in the category. The compilers of [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002) make the lineage explicit in the imperial preface, naming *Sìmín yuèlìng* 四民月令, *Sìshí zuǎnyào* 四時纂要, *Qiānjīn yuèlìng* 千金月令, *Jǐndài* 錦帶, *Suìhuá jìlì* 歲華紀麗, and *Suìshí zá jì* 歲時雜記 as the genre's medieval and Sòng exemplars.
- **Phenology and the calendar of the husbandman.** The four-tier *suìlìng / yuèlìng / jiéxù / hòu* time-grid of [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002) and the month-by-month structure of [KR2j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0001) both serve a practical agronomic and ritual function: phenological signs (*hòu* 候) signal the times for sowing, harvesting, sacrifice, and state observance.
- **Correlative cosmology.** The illustrated *juànshǒu* of [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002) (18 diagrams: *Tàijí* — *Liǎngyí* — *Sìxiàng* — *Bāguà*, the 12 *bì* hexagrams, the 24 *qì*, the 72 *hòu*, the *lǜlǚ* 律呂 pitch-pipes and five-tones, the *Tàisuì* stem-and-branch tables) embeds the *yuèlìng* tradition in the Sòng *Yìxué* (Shào Yōng, Zhū Xī) and Hàn correlative *yīnyáng wǔxíng* schemes — and includes the *tǔ wáng* 土王 (earth-phase interregnum) juan absent from the *Lǐjì Yuèlìng* but central to Hàn cosmology.
- **Festival history and the late-imperial canon.** [KR2j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0001) is the textual point at which the late-imperial Chinese festival year takes recognizable form: the firm attachment of Qū Yuán 屈原 to the Duānwǔ 端午, the centralization of dragon-boat racing as *lóngzhōu jìngdù* 龍舟競渡, the linking of the Chóngyáng 重陽 hill-climbing custom to Fèi Chángfáng 費長房 (Wilkinson §9.12.4).
- **Canonical calendar vs. operative calendar.** The *Yùdìng yuèlìng jíyào* makes explicit at j. 24 that its phenological table follows the Jesuit-reformed Qīng *Shíxiàn lì* 時憲曆 and "differs slightly from the *Yuèlìng*" — a methodological tension between the canonical-correlative *yuèlìng* and the operative civil calendar that runs through the entire category.
- **Citation hierarchy.** The Sòng compilation draws heavily on informal narrative literature (*bàiguān* 稗官) and is criticized by the *Sìkù* editors for under-using *Ěryǎ* 爾雅 and *Huáinánzǐ* 淮南子; the Qīng compilation enforces a descending priority of canonical exegesis → histories and transmissions → philosophers, regional records, gazetteers. The shift mirrors the moral-philological orientation of the late-Kāngxī court.
- **Transmission and editorial loss.** The *Sìkù*-edition of [KR2j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0001) descends from Cáo Róng's 曹溶 *Xuéhǎi lèibiān* 學海類編 recension and has lost the prefatory diagrams (*tú shuō* 圖說) described in Qián Zēng's 錢曾 *Dúshū mǐnqiú jì* 讀書敏求記 — a reminder that the *Sìkù* recensions are not always the fullest available witnesses.

### Timeline

- 1220–1265 — *Suìshí guǎngjì* 歲時廣記 [KR2j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0001) — late-Southern-Sòng (Lǐzōng's reign) anthology of festival lore by month; the bibliographic landmark at which the late-imperial festival year takes its received form.
- 1700–1715 — *Yùdìng yuèlìng jíyào* 御定月令輯要 [KR2j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2j/KR2j0002) — imperially-supervised Kāngxī court compilation, preface dated 12 May 1715, name-list promulgated April 1716; the standard imperial-Qīng *yuèlìng* repository, succeeding and re-editing Féng Yìngjīng's late-Míng *Yuèlìng guǎngyì*.

# 地理類 (KR2k)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR2k 地理類 *Dìlǐ lèi* — Histories — Geography](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

The *Dìlǐ* 地理 ("Geography") category of the *Sìkù quánshū* is the largest single sub-category of the *Shǐbù* 史部 (152 titles in the Wényuāngé recension) and the principal home of the imperial Chinese geographical, hydrographical, urban-historical, ethnographic, and travel literatures. As Wilkinson notes (§16.3), the bibliographical placement of *dìlǐ* in the History branch is one of the durable structural features of the *sìbù* classification, retained even in modern PRC library systems (§75.2); it reflects the inherited assumption that Chinese geographical writing existed not as a freestanding natural science but as an instrument of statecraft — providing incoming officials, military planners, ritual specialists, and historiographers with the *yán'gé* 沿革 (administrative-historical genealogy of place), *jiāngyù* 疆域 (boundaries), *shānchuān* 山川 (topography), *fēngsú* 風俗 (customs), and *wùchǎn* 物產 (products) of every administered unit in the empire (Wilkinson §16.4.1–2).

The genre's textual ancestry runs from the *Yúgòng* 禹貢 of the *Shàngshū* and the *Shānhǎi jīng* 山海經 (Wilkinson §16.3.1), through the *dìlǐ zhì* 地理志 treatises of the *Hànshū* and subsequent standard histories (§16.3.2), to the freestanding empire-wide comprehensive gazetteers (*zǒngzhì* 總志 / *yītǒng zhì* 一統志) and the vast Sòng–Qīng *fāngzhì* 方志 (local-gazetteer) literature. Within the Sìkù scheme the 152 titles of KR2k follow the canonical ten-fold sub-arrangement that the editors imposed across the division: 宮殿簿 (palace registers, [KR2k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0001)–[KR2k0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0002)); 總志 (empire-wide gazetteers, [KR2k0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0003)–[KR2k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0009)); 都會郡縣 (cities, prefectures, counties — the bulk of *fāngzhì* proper, [KR2k0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0010)–[KR2k0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0057)); 河渠 (waterways, [KR2k0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0058)–[KR2k0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0080)); 邊防 (frontier defence, [KR2k0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0081)–[KR2k0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0082)); 山川 (mountains and waters, [KR2k0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0083)–[KR2k0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0089)); 古蹟 (ancient monuments and antiquarian topographies, [KR2k0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0090)–[KR2k0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0103)); 雜記 (miscellaneous regional records, [KR2k0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0104)–[KR2k0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0132)); 遊記 (travel diaries, [KR2k0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0133)–[KR2k0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0135)); and 外紀 (foreign records, [KR2k0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0136)–[KR2k0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0152)). The chronological span runs from Jī Hán's 嵇含 early-4th-century botanical *Nánfāng cǎomù zhuàng* [KR2k0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0104) to the Qiánlóng-era imperial provincial *tōngzhì* of 1789, covering the entire imperial documentary tradition of place-writing in China.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### The empire-wide comprehensive gazetteers (總志)

- *Yuánhé jùnxiàn (tú)zhì* 元和郡縣(圖)志 [KR2k0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0003) — Lǐ Jífǔ's 李吉甫 (758–814) Yuánhé-era (813–814) gazetteer of the entire empire, the earliest extant separately-circulating empire-wide geography (Wilkinson §16.3.3 #1; §61.3.3). The *Yuánhé* sets the template — *yán'gé* prologue, then prefecture-by-prefecture survey of borders, products, and population — that all later *yītǒng zhì* will inherit.
- *Tàipíng huányǔ jì* 太平寰宇記 [KR2k0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0004) — Yuè Shǐ's 樂史 (930–1007) early-Sòng (979–987) compilation, the first comprehensive gazetteer of the unified Sòng empire and the work that introduces the inclusion of biographies, literary works, and ethnographic material into the *zǒngzhì* genre (Wilkinson §16.3.3 #2). The two great empire-wide compilations of the long 11th–13th c. that follow it — *Yuánfēng jiǔyù zhì* 元豐九域志 [KR2k0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0005) (Wáng Cún 王存, 1080) and *Yúdì guǎngjì* 輿地廣記 [KR2k0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0006) (Ōuyáng Mín 歐陽忞, 1111–1117) — extend its template into the high-Sòng administrative state.
- *Fāngyú shènglǎn* 方輿勝覽 [KR2k0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0007) — Zhù Mù's 祝穆 1239 Southern-Sòng compilation organized by *lù* 路, the principal Southern-Sòng cultural-geographical synthesis and the only major Sòng *zǒngzhì* still preserved in its full original form.
- *Míng yītǒng zhì* 明一統志 [KR2k0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0008) — Lǐ Xián's 李賢 imperially-commissioned 90-juan compendium of 1461, the standard Míng comprehensive gazetteer; and *Dà Qīng yītǒng zhì* 大清一統志 [KR2k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0009) — the 424-juan Hé-Shēn 和珅-supervised Qiánlóng-era revision (1764–1784) of the Kāngxī and Yōngzhèng *Yītǒng zhì* projects, the largest single work in the division and the standard imperial-Qīng repository (Wilkinson §16.3.3 #6).

#### Sòng–Yuán prefectural gazetteers and the *fāngzhì* tradition (都會郡縣)

The Sòng *fāngzhì* of [KR2k0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0010)–0027 are the principal surviving witnesses to a genre that produced over 1,000 titles in the Southern Sòng alone, of which fewer than 30 are extant (Wilkinson §16.4.1, §62.3.3.2). The cluster anchors the historical geography of the Jiāng-Zhè and Mǐn cultural cores:
- *Wújùn tújīng xùjì* 吳郡圖經續記 [KR2k0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0010) — Zhū Chángwén's 朱長文 1084 Sūzhōu prefectural continuation, the earliest extant work in the long Sūzhōu-prefectural-gazetteer series.
- The Línān / Hángzhōu cluster — *Qiándào Línān zhì* 乾道臨安志 [KR2k0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0011) (1169–1173) and *Xiánchún Línān zhì* 咸淳臨安志 [KR2k0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0022) (1268–1274), the two principal Southern-Sòng capital gazetteers.
- *Chúnxī Sānshān zhì* 淳熙三山志 [KR2k0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0012) — Liáng Kèjiā 梁克家, Fúzhōu 1179–1182; the earliest extant prefectural gazetteer of Fújiàn.
- *Wújùn zhì* 吳郡志 [KR2k0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0013) — Fàn Chéngdà's 范成大 50-juan Sūzhōu gazetteer (1192–1229).
- *Xīn'ān zhì* 新安志 [KR2k0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0014) (Huīzhōu, 1175), *Shàn lù* 剡錄 [KR2k0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0015) (Shèngzhōu, 1214–1215), *Huìjī zhì* 會稽志 [KR2k0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0016) (1201–1225), *Chìchéng zhì* 赤城志 [KR2k0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0017) (Tāizhōu, 1214–1223), *Bǎoqìng Sìmíng zhì* 寶慶四明志 [KR2k0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0018) (Níngbō, 1226–1227), and *Jǐngdìng Jiànkāng zhì* 景定建康志 [KR2k0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0021) (Nánjīng, 1261) — together the canonical Southern-Sòng prefectural-gazetteer set. As Wilkinson notes (§16.4.1), the first detailed *fánlì* (compilation rules) extant in the genre are in *Jǐngdìng Jiànkāng zhì*.
- Yuán continuations — *Zhìyuán Jiāhé zhì* 至元嘉禾志 [KR2k0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0023), *Yányòu Sìmíng zhì* 延祐四明志 [KR2k0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0025), *Qí chéng* 齊乘 [KR2k0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0026) (Yú Qīn 于欽's 1339 Shāndōng provincial gazetteer, the earliest extant provincial-level *fāngzhì*), and *Zhìdà Jīnlíng xīnzhì* 至大金陵新志 [KR2k0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0027) (Zhāng Xuàn 張鉉, 1344).

#### The high-Qīng imperial gazetteer programme (欽定 and 通志)

- *Qīndìng Rèhé zhì* 欽定熱河志 [KR2k0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0035), *Qīndìng Rìxià jiùwén kǎo* 欽定日下舊聞考 [KR2k0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0036) (the imperial-Qīng standard topography of Běijīng), *Qīndìng Mǎnzhōu yuánliú kǎo* 欽定滿洲源流考 [KR2k0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0038), *Qīndìng Huángyú Xīyù túzhì* 欽定皇輿西域圖志 [KR2k0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0039), and *Qīndìng Shèngjīng tōngzhì* 欽定盛京通志 [KR2k0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0040) — the late-Qiánlóng imperial-commissioned topographies of the Manchu dynastic homeland, the Mongol-Manchurian frontier, Xīnjiāng, and the Manchu second capital, jointly the documentary monument of the multi-ethnic Qīng-imperial geographical project.
- The 16 provincial *tōngzhì* of [KR2k0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0041)–[KR2k0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0056) (*Jīfǔ tōngzhì* through *Guìzhōu tōngzhì*) — the Qing imperial provincial-gazetteer programme, commissioned by edicts of Kāngxī 1672 and Yōngzhèng 1728 that ordered every province to compile a *fāngzhì* (Wilkinson §16.4.1). Sixty-five percent of all *fāngzhì* extant before 1912 were compiled in the Qīng (46 percent of those in the 18th century); these 16 imperial provincial *tōngzhì*, all completed between 1729 and 1742, are the apex of that programme.
- *Tiānxià jùnguó lìbìng shū* 天下郡國利病書 [KR2k0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0037) — Gù Yánwǔ's 顧炎武 (1613–1682) Ming-loyalist historical geography of strategic advantages and weaknesses, composed 1639–1662 from over a thousand local gazetteers; the founding monument of *kǎojù* historical geography and Wilkinson's first item under "Empire-wide Geographies" (§16.3.4 #1). Its admission to the *Sìkù* — despite its author's anti-Manchu posture and his close relations with the resistance — is the principal sign that the Qiánlóng court treated him as the standard-setter of late-imperial historical-geographical scholarship.

#### The hydraulic and watercourse tradition (河渠)

- *Shuǐjīng zhù* 水經注 [KR2k0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0058) — Lì Dàoyuán's 酈道元 (d. 527) Northern-Wèi commentary on the anonymous 3rd-c. *Shuǐjīng*, the foundational monument of Chinese historical hydrology and one of the great prose works of the medieval period (Wilkinson §16.3.1 closing note; §15.7.1). It is followed in the cluster by the two principal Qīng reconstructions — Shěn Bǐngxùn's 沈炳巽 *Shuǐjīngzhù jíshì dìngé* [KR2k0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0059) and Zhào Yīqīng's 趙一清 *Shuǐjīngzhù shì* [KR2k0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0060) — the texts at the centre of the famous Dài Zhèn 戴震 – Zhào Yīqīng *kǎojù* plagiarism controversy.
- The Sòng–Míng water-control compendia — *Wúzhōng shuǐlì shū* 吳中水利書 [KR2k0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0061) (Shàn È 單鍔, 1059–1091), *Héfáng yīlǎn* 河防一覽 [KR2k0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0066) (Pān Jìxún 潘季馴, 1591), *Wúzhōng shuǐlì quánshū* 吳中水利全書 [KR2k0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0071) (Zhāng Guówéi 張國維, 1636–1639) — and the Qīng monumental *Xíngshuǐ jīnjiàn* 行水金鑑 [KR2k0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0078) (Fù Zéhóng 傅澤洪, 175 juan, 1725), the standard imperial-Qīng reference for the Yellow River, Grand Canal, and Huái systems.
- *Shuǐdào tígāng* 水道提綱 [KR2k0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR2/KR2k/KR2k0079) — Qí Zhàonán's 齊召南 1761 comprehensive empire-wide hydrography on the new Kāngxī geodetic basis.
