# 譜錄類 (KR3i)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR3i 譜錄類 *Pǔ-lù lèi* — Masters — Treatises and Catalogues (Connoisseurship Monographs on Single Objects)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR3i corresponds to the *Sìkù quánshū* category 譜錄類 *pǔlù lèi*, the eighth division of the *Zǐbù* 子部 (Masters Branch), reserved for monographs that take a single physical object — an implement, a foodstuff, a plant, an animal, a mineral — as their subject and exhaust it from every angle: origin, manufacture, geography, taxonomy, anecdote, and poetry. As Wilkinson notes (§36.1, §36.20), the *Sìkù* editors created the category to gather the heterogeneous "miscellaneous handbooks" (his phrase) that had accumulated since the Tang and did not fit neatly into the older *zájiā* 雜家 or *nóngjiā* 農家 rubrics — works on tea, ink, inkstones, incense, flowers, fish, and crabs whose only common feature is the *single-object-monograph* form. The model is Lù Yǔ's 陸羽 *Chájīng* 茶經 (c. 760, [KR3i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0019)), whose audacious claim to *jīng* (classic) status — a title-form reserved in the Han–Tang tradition for canonical scripture — was accepted by later writers and made the X-*jīng* / X-*pǔ* / X-*lù* / X-*shǐ* monograph a legitimate Chinese literary kind.

The chronological centre of gravity of KR3i sits firmly in the Sòng (especially Northern Sòng to mid-Southern Sòng, c. 980–1250), the period in which literati connoisseurship of the studio-objects, of tea, wine, and flowers, and of regional specialties such as lychee and citrus crystallised into a self-conscious genre. Sū Yìjiǎn's *Wénfáng sìpǔ* 文房四譜 of 986 ([KR3i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0002)) is the foundational systematic *pǔ*, and Ōuyáng Xiū's *Luòyáng mǔdān jì* 洛陽牡丹記 of c. 1031–34 ([KR3i0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0029)) initiates the flower-treatise sub-tradition; the form is then taken up by Cài Xiāng, Mǐ Fú, Fàn Chéngdà, Hán Yànzhí, and many others. The division also collects a late-imperial layer of imperially-commissioned, court-printed compendia (*Qīndìng Xīqīng yànpǔ* of 1778 [KR3i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0009); *Qiánlù* of 1750 [KR3i0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0014); *Yùdìng Pèiwénzhāi guǎng qúnfāng pǔ* of 1708 [KR3i0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0044)), in which the private literati genre is reabsorbed into Qīng imperial cultural policy. A handful of pre-Sòng works (Dài Kǎizhī's *Zhúpǔ* of c. 400–490 [KR3i0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0040), Biàn Bīn's *Qínshòu juélù* of c. 483–500 [KR3i0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0051), Lù Yǔ's *Chájīng*, and Zhāng Yòuxīn's *Jiānchá shuǐjì* [KR3i0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0025)) furnish the genre's prehistory, while the early-Qīng *Xù chájīng* 續茶經 ([KR3i0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0024)) and the polymathic *Yìyú túzàn* cluster ([KR3i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0048)–[KR3i0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0050)) show its late afterlife. One conspicuous outlier — the *Qíqì túshuō* 奇器圖說 ([KR3i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0001)) of 1627, the Jesuit Johann Schreck's collaboration with Wáng Zhēng on European mechanical engineering — sits within KR3i only by *Sìkù* default, lacking any other obvious home; it should be read as Jesuit-Chinese collaboration literature, not as *pǔlù* properly.

### Important texts and text clusters

The principal texts and recognised clusters within KR3i, in rough thematic order:

- **The foundational monographs.** *Chájīng* 茶經 by Lù Yǔ ([KR3i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0019)) — the genre's seed and the model from which most later *pǔlù* derive. *Wénfáng sìpǔ* 文房四譜 by Sū Yìjiǎn ([KR3i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0002)) — the first systematic monograph on the *wénfáng sìbǎo* 文房四寶 (brush, inkstone, paper, ink) and the structural template for later studio-object treatises.

- **The inkstone (硯) cluster.** *Yànshǐ* 硯史 by Mǐ Fú ([KR3i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0003)) — the most influential single-author treatise on inkstones; *Shèzhōu yànpǔ* 歙州硯譜 ([KR3i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0004)), *Shèyàn shuō* 歙硯說 ([KR3i0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0005)), *Duānxī yànpǔ* 端溪硯譜 ([KR3i0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0006)), *Yànpǔ* 硯譜 ([KR3i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0007)), and *Yànjiān* 硯箋 by Gāo Sìsūn ([KR3i0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0008)) — a tight Sòng sub-tradition on the regional inkstones of Shèzhōu and Duānxī; *Qīndìng Xīqīng yànpǔ* 欽定西清硯譜 ([KR3i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0009)) — the Qiānlóng court's lavish catalogue of the imperial inkstone collection, which closes the cluster from above.

- **The ink (墨) cluster.** *Mòpǔ fǎshì* 墨譜法式 by Lǐ Xiàoměi ([KR3i0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0010)), *Mòjīng* 墨經 by Cháo Guànyī ([KR3i0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0011)), *Mòshǐ* 墨史 by Lù Yǒu ([KR3i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0012)), *Mòfǎ jíyào* 墨法集要 by Shěn Jìsūn ([KR3i0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0013)) — Sòng–Yuán–Míng treatises on ink-making (composition, soot-grading, glue, moulding) and on the canon of celebrated ink-makers.

- **The incense (香) cluster.** *Xiāngpǔ* 香譜 by Hóng Chú ([KR3i0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0015)), *Chénshì xiāngpǔ* 陳氏香譜 ([KR3i0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0016)), *Xiāngshèng* 香乘 by Zhōu Jiāzhòu ([KR3i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0017)) — Sòng-to-Míng monographs on aromatic materials, blends, and burning customs.

- **The tea (茶) cluster.** *Chájīng* ([KR3i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0019)), *Chálù* 茶錄 by Cài Xiāng ([KR3i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0020)), *Pǐnchá yàolù* 品茶要錄 by Huáng Rú ([KR3i0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0021)), *Xuānhé Beìyuàn gòngchá lù* 宣和北苑貢茶錄 ([KR3i0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0022)), *Dōngxī shìchá lù* 東溪試茶錄 ([KR3i0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0023)), *Xù chájīng* 續茶經 by Lù Tíngcàn ([KR3i0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0024)), *Jiānchá shuǐjì* 煎茶水記 ([KR3i0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0025)) — together the densest sub-corpus of the division, covering tea-cultivation, manufacture, tribute geography (especially the Beìyuàn 北苑 plantations in Fújiàn), brewing-method, and water-evaluation.

- **The wine and sugar texts.** *Beìshān jiǔjīng* 北山酒經 by Zhū Yìzhōng ([KR3i0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0026)) — the most technically detailed Sòng treatise on rice-wine brewing; *Jiǔpǔ* 酒譜 by Dòu Píng ([KR3i0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0027)); *Tángshuāng pǔ* 糖霜譜 by Wáng Zhuó ([KR3i0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0028)) — the first systematic monograph on crystallised sugar manufacture.

- **The flower treatises.** *Luòyáng mǔdān jì* 洛陽牡丹記 by Ōuyáng Xiū ([KR3i0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0029)) — the genre-founding flower-treatise; *Yángzhōu sháoyào pǔ* 揚州芍藥譜 ([KR3i0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0030)); the chrysanthemum sequence *Liúshì júpǔ* ([KR3i0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0031)), *Shǐshì júpǔ* ([KR3i0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0032)), *Fàncūn júpǔ* ([KR3i0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0034)), *Bǎijú jípǔ* ([KR3i0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0035)); *Fàncūn méipǔ* 范村梅譜 ([KR3i0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0033)) on plums; *Jīnzhāng lánpǔ* 金漳蘭譜 ([KR3i0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0036)) on the Zhāngzhōu orchids; *Hǎitáng pǔ* 海棠譜 ([KR3i0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0037)) on crab-apple — a tightly-knit Sòng connoisseurship literature on garden flowers, mostly tied to specific regional cultivars.

- **The fruit and plant monographs.** *Lìzhī pǔ* 荔枝譜 by Cài Xiāng ([KR3i0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0038)) — the foundational lychee monograph; *Júlù* 橘錄 by Hán Yànzhí ([KR3i0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0039)) — the foundational citrus monograph (Yǒngjiā citrus varieties); *Zhúpǔ* 竹譜 by Dài Kǎizhī ([KR3i0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0040)) — the oldest text in the division, a Six-Dynasties verse-treatise on bamboo; *Sǔnpǔ* 筍譜 by the monk Zànníng ([KR3i0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0041)); *Jūnpǔ* 菌譜 ([KR3i0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0042)) on mushrooms.

- **The dietetic and imperial-flora compendia.** *Yǐnshàn zhèngyào* 飲膳正要 ([KR3i0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0043)) — Hū Sīhuì's 忽思慧 Yuán imperial dietetic manual, distinctive among KR3i for its Inner-Asian (Mongol/Uyghur/Islamic) culinary stratum, treated at length in Wilkinson §36.20 #9; *Yùdìng Pèiwénzhāi guǎng qúnfāng pǔ* 御定佩文齋廣羣芳譜 ([KR3i0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0044)) — the Kāngxī-era 100-*juàn* imperial flora-and-agriculture compendium, the most encyclopaedic single work in the division.

- **The zoological treatises.** *Qínjīng* 禽經 ([KR3i0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0045)) — bird monograph pseudonymously attributed to Shī Kuàng 師曠 with a Zhāng Huá 張華 commentary, in fact a Sòng compilation; *Xièpǔ* 蟹譜 by Fù Gōng ([KR3i0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0046)) and *Xièlüè* 蟹略 by Gāo Sìsūn ([KR3i0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0047)) — the two crab monographs; the *Yìyú túzàn* cluster — Yáng Shèn's *Yìyú túzàn* 異魚圖贊 ([KR3i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0048)), Hú Shìān's 胡世安 *Yìyú túzàn jiān* ([KR3i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0049)) and *Yìyú túzàn bǔ* ([KR3i0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0050)) — Míng-Qīng illustrated encomia on strange fishes, in verse form; and the outlier *Qínshòu juélù* 禽獸決錄 by Biàn Bīn ([KR3i0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0051)), a Southern-Qí allegorical-satirical *jué* on the moral natures of beasts, surviving in fragments.

- **The numismatic, lithological, and Jesuit outliers.** *Qiánlù* 錢錄 ([KR3i0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0014)) — Liáng Shīzhèng's 1750 Qiānlóng imperial catalogue of coinage; *Yúnlín shípǔ* 雲林石譜 by Dù Wǎn ([KR3i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0018)) — the foundational monograph on ornamental scholar-stones; *Qíqì túshuō* 奇器圖說 ([KR3i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0001)) — the Schreck-Wáng Jesuit treatise on European mechanical devices, classified as *pǔlù* by the *Sìkù* for want of a better category.

### Important persons

- [陸羽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E7%BE%BD) (Lù Yǔ, 733–805) — author of the *Chájīng* ([KR3i0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0019)); the *cháshèng* 茶聖 (Sage of Tea), genre-founder of Chinese *pǔlù* literature.
- [蘇易簡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E6%98%93%E7%B0%A1) (Sū Yìjiǎn, 957–995) — Sòng Hànlín scholar; author of the *Wénfáng sìpǔ* ([KR3i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0002)) and the immediate genre-founder for the Sòng object-treatise tradition.
- [米芾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%B1%B3%E8%8A%BE) (Mǐ Fú, 1051–1107) — Northern Sòng calligrapher, painter, and connoisseur; his *Yànshǐ* ([KR3i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0003)) is the most influential single-author inkstone monograph.
- [歐陽修](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%90%E9%99%BD%E4%BF%AE) (Ōuyáng Xiū, 1007–1072) — the dominant Northern Sòng literatus; his *Luòyáng mǔdān jì* ([KR3i0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0029)) inaugurates the flower-treatise sub-genre.
- [蔡襄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E8%A5%84) (Cài Xiāng, 1012–1067) — Northern Sòng calligrapher and Fújiàn official; double presence in the division as author of *Chálù* ([KR3i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0020)) and *Lìzhī pǔ* ([KR3i0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0038)).
- [范成大](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8C%83%E6%88%90%E5%A4%A7) (Fàn Chéngdà, 1126–1193) — Southern Sòng poet and Sūzhōu-gardener; author of two flower-treatises on his own Fàncūn 范村 garden, *Fàncūn méipǔ* ([KR3i0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0033)) and *Fàncūn júpǔ* ([KR3i0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0034)).
- [高似孫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E4%BC%BC%E5%AD%AB) (Gāo Sìsūn, fl. 1184) — Southern Sòng polymath; author of *Yànjiān* ([KR3i0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0008)) and *Xièlüè* ([KR3i0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0047)), both representing the more philologically-erudite *jiān*/*lüè* sub-style of the genre.
- [周嘉胄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E5%98%89%E8%83%84) (Zhōu Jiāzhòu, d. c. 1660) — late-Míng compiler of *Xiāngshèng* ([KR3i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0017)), the most comprehensive single Chinese treatise on incense.
- [釋贊寧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E8%B4%8A%E5%AF%A7) (Shì Zànníng, 918–999) — the eminent Sòng-Buddhist historian; author of *Sǔnpǔ* ([KR3i0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0041)), an unusual case of a Buddhist monk producing a secular *pǔlù*.
- [戴凱之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%B4%E5%87%B1%E4%B9%8B) (Dài Kǎizhī, fl. 5th c.) — earliest *pǔlù* author preserved in the division; his *Zhúpǔ* ([KR3i0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0040)) is a Six-Dynasties verse-treatise antedating the rest of the corpus.
- [忽思慧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BF%BD%E6%80%9D%E6%85%A7) (Hū Sīhuì / Hoshoi, fl. 1314–1330) — Yuán court dietitian of probable Uyghur/Inner-Asian extraction; the *Yǐnshàn zhèngyào* ([KR3i0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0043)) introduces a substantial Mongol-Islamic dietetic stratum into the division.
- [楊愼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E6%84%BC) (Yáng Shèn, 1488–1559) — Míng polymath in Yúnnán exile; author of the *Yìyú túzàn* ([KR3i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0048)), basis for the strange-fish cluster.

### Topics

The principal subjects and interpretive problems running through KR3i:

- **The *pǔlù* as a literati genre.** The single-object monograph is one of the most distinctive Chinese contributions to non-fictional prose, and the Sòng explosion of *pǔlù* writing (c. 980–1250) is bound up with the formation of the Sòng literatus's material-cultural identity (Bol, Egan). The genre is unintelligible apart from the practice of literati connoisseurship — the assertion that ordinary objects, properly attended to, are worthy of *jīng* (classic) treatment.

- **The *jīng* / *pǔ* / *lù* / *shǐ* / *jiān* / *lüè* terminological hierarchy.** Authors choose the title-form (X-*jīng* = the most ambitious, claiming classic status; X-*shǐ* = a history of an object; X-*pǔ* = a treatise / catalogue; X-*lù* = a record; X-*jiān* = annotated notes; X-*lüè* = a concise survey) as a deliberate generic positioning. The interplay of these terms across the division — *Chájīng* vs. *Sǔnpǔ*, *Yànshǐ* vs. *Yànjiān*, *Mòjīng* vs. *Mòpǔ* vs. *Mòshǐ* — is a major topic in its own right.

- **Tribute geography and regional specialisation.** A large proportion of the division concerns objects associated with specific regional production sites: Beìyuàn 北苑 tribute tea (Fújiàn), Duānxī 端溪 inkstones (Guǎngdōng), Shèzhōu 歙州 inkstones (Ānhuī), Fújiàn lychee, Wēnzhōu / Yǒngjiā citrus, Luòyáng peonies, Yángzhōu herbaceous peonies, Sìchuān crystallised sugar, Zhāngzhōu orchids. The *pǔlù* genre is in part the literary face of the Sòng-and-later tribute economy.

- **Manufacturing technique and *kējì* literature.** Several texts contain detailed technical descriptions: ink-making procedure (*Mòfǎ jíyào*), wine-brewing (*Beìshān jiǔjīng*), tea-cake processing (*Chájīng*, *Beìyuàn gòngchá lù*), sugar-frost crystallisation (*Tángshuāng pǔ*). They are primary sources for Chinese science-and-technology history of considerable importance (Needham *SCC* draws on them extensively).

- **The literatus garden.** The flower-treatise cluster (peony, chrysanthemum, plum, orchid, crab-apple) is bound up with the Sòng-and-later cultural form of the named literatus garden — Ōuyáng Xiū's Luòyáng, Fàn Chéngdà's Fàncūn (Stone-Lake), etc. — and with the practice of cultivar-naming and rank-ordering as a connoisseurship activity.

- **Imperial appropriation of literati genres.** The late-imperial layer of the division (Pèiwénzhāi guǎng qúnfāng pǔ, Xīqīng yànpǔ, Qiánlù) shows the Qīng court systematically taking over the previously-private literati object-treatise form for ideological / display purposes. The Kāngxī and Qiānlóng emperors are visible patrons of this absorption.

- **The Buddhist and the Inner-Asian voice.** Two anomalous texts — Zànníng's *Sǔnpǔ* (a Buddhist monk's secular *pǔ*) and Hū Sīhuì's *Yǐnshàn zhèngyào* (a Mongol-court dietitian's Inner-Asian-inflected cookbook) — show that the genre was capable of accommodating non-literati voices, with consequences for the cultural-historical interpretation of the genre.

- **Pseudepigraphy and recompilation.** The *Qínjīng* ([KR3i0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0045)) is a pseudonymous Sòng compilation falsely attributed to the Spring-and-Autumn musician Shī Kuàng with a falsely-attributed Zhāng Huá commentary; the *Qínshòu juélù* ([KR3i0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3i/KR3i0051)) is a Qīng *jíyì* reconstruction of a Southern-Qí satirical work from quoted fragments. Both raise the standard textual-critical problems of the *pǔlù* corpus and of *Sìkù* recensions generally.

# 雜家類 (KR3j)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR3j 雜家類 *Zájiā lèi* — Masters — Miscellaneous (Syncretists, Investigations, Discourses, Connoisseurship, Compendia)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR3j is the *Zájiā lèi* 雜家類 of the *Sìkù quánshū* — the residual, syncretist, and notebook-form division of the Masters branch (子部, *Zǐbù*). The category has two roots. The first is the Hàn bibliographic class *Zájiā* 雜家 (rendered by Wilkinson as "Syncretists" in his table of the *Hànshū* *Yìwén zhì*'s ten Masters subclasses; cf. Wilkinson § 73.2 and Box 348), originally containing twenty works in which Confucian, Daoist, Mohist, Legalist, agriculturalist, and yīnyáng / Five-Phase teachings were deliberately combined — the *Lǚshì chūnqiū* [KR3j0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0009) and the *Huáinánzǐ* [KR3j0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0010) being the paradigmatic examples. The second root is the *bǐjì* 筆記 ("brush notes") of the post-Táng period, a genre Wilkinson devotes a full chapter to (§ 53): informal scholarly notebooks whose contents range across classical exegesis, history, geography, philology, anecdote, and connoisseurship, and which the *Sìkù* editors found impossible to file under any of the more specialised Masters subclasses. The *Sìkù* therefore enlarged the old Hàn *Zájiā* into a six-fold class — *zá xué* 雜學 (syncretist philosophy), *zá kǎo* 雜考 (evidential investigation), *zá shuō* 雜說 (miscellaneous discourse), *zá pǐn* 雜品 (connoisseurship), *zá zuǎn* 雜纂 (anthological compilation), *zá biān* 雜編 (multi-work compendia) — and used it to absorb the bulk of the *bǐjì* corpus. As Wilkinson notes (§ 53.1), *bǐjì* "often started as reading notes" and ranged across "scholastic points of history or philology … the flux of city life … local customs and practical guidebook-style advice"; their classification in the *Sìkù* was therefore split between *Zájiā* in the Masters branch and *záshǐ* 雜史 in the History branch, with *Zájiā* receiving the more reflective and philological writings while *záshǐ* received the more event-driven ones. Until the late nineteenth century, *cóngshū* 叢書 (multi-work compendia) had no separate place in the four-branch scheme and were filed inside *Zájiā*'s sixth subclass *zá biān* (Wilkinson § 73.2.3); the four KR3j *cóngshū* on disk are survivors of that older arrangement.

The 201 works catalogued in KR3j cover an unbroken span from the late Warring States to the early eighteenth century — *Mòzǐ* [KR3j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0002), the *Hèguānzǐ* [KR3j0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0006), the *Gōngsūn Lóngzǐ* [KR3j0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0007) and other survivors of the "Hundred Schools" at one end; the great Qīng *kǎozhèng* notebooks of [顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6), [閻若璩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%96%BB%E8%8B%A5%E7%92%A9), [何焯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E7%84%AF), and [王士禛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A3%AB%E7%A6%9B) at the other. KR3j is therefore not a single tradition but a holding-tank for several: the Hàn syncretist *zǐ*-book, the Six-Dynasties character-and-mores literature ([KR3j0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0011) *Rénwù zhì*, [KR3j0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0014) *Yánshì jiāxùn*), the Sòng evidential *bǐjì* (the works of [洪邁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E9%82%81), [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F), [程大昌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A8%8B%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8C)), the Sòng-Yuán-Míng connoisseurship treatises ([KR3j0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0167) *Dòngtiān qīnglù*, [KR3j0170](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0170) *Gégǔ yàolùn*, [KR3j0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0174) *Cháng wù zhì*), the late-Míng polymathic miscellanies ([KR3j0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0066) *Tōngyǎ*, [KR3j0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0190) *Shǎoshì shānfáng bǐcóng*, [KR3j0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0160) *Wùlǐ xiǎozhì*), and finally the Qīng evidential apex anchored by [KR3j0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0070) *Rì zhī lù*. Across this span the division acts as the *Sìkù*'s reservoir for serious intellectual work that did not fit the Masters branch's narrower philosophical, technical, or arts categories.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The pre-Qín masters cluster.** Six short books at the head of the division preserve the names — and contested texts — of pre-Qín thinkers who fell outside the four orthodox schools, and whose surviving recensions are mostly Hàn–Sòng reconstitutions: [KR3j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0001) *Yùzǐ* 鬻子 (attributed to the Zhōu-era [鬻熊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AC%BB%E7%86%8A) but transmitted with a Táng commentary by [逢行珪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%A2%E8%A1%8C%E7%8F%AA)), [KR3j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0002) *Mòzǐ* 墨子 (the principal surviving Mohist scripture), [KR3j0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0004) *Yǐnwénzǐ* 尹文子 (the *Míngjiā* 名家 / School of Names), [KR3j0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0005) *Shènzǐ* 慎子 (proto-Legalist), [KR3j0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0006) *Hèguānzǐ* 鶡冠子 (a Huáng Lǎo syncretist), [KR3j0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0007) *Gōngsūn Lóngzǐ* 公孫龍子 (the second of the two surviving *Míngjiā* texts), [KR3j0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0008) *Guǐgǔzǐ* 鬼谷子 (the *Zòngheng jiā* 縱橫家 / Strategists' manual), and [KR3j0194](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0194) *Shīzǐ* 尸子 (a Qīng *jíyì* reconstitution). The *Sìkù* editors filed them in *Zájiā* rather than in *Rújiā* or *Dàojiā* precisely because their schools had become extinct.

**The Hàn-syncretist hinge.** [KR3j0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0009) *Lǚshì chūnqiū* 呂氏春秋 (239 BCE) and [KR3j0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0010) *Huáinán hónglièjiě* 淮南鴻烈解 (the *Huáinánzǐ*, c. 139 BCE) are the locus classicus of Hàn-era *Zájiā* thought as Wilkinson uses the term in § 73.2 / Box 348. They self-consciously assemble Confucian, Daoist, Mohist, and yīnyáng material into a coherent imperial-state programme. [KR3j0192](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0192) *Xīnlùn* 新論 ([桓譚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A1%93%E8%AD%9A)), [KR3j0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0080) *Lùnhéng* 論衡 ([王充](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%85%85)), [KR3j0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0023) *Báihǔ tōngyì* 白虎通義 (attributed to [班固](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8F%AD%E5%9B%BA)), and [KR3j0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0081) *Fēngsú tōngyì* 風俗通義 ([應劭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%87%89%E5%8A%AD)) extend the syncretist *zǐ*-book idiom across the Eastern Hàn.

**Six Dynasties and Suí-Táng character / *jiāxùn* / governance literature.** [KR3j0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0011) *Rénwù zhì* 人物志 ([劉卲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%8D%B2)), the foundation text for Wèi-Jìn character-theory and physiognomic recruitment; [KR3j0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0012) *Jīnlóuzǐ* 金樓子 (Liáng [蕭繹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%95%AD%E7%B9%B9)); [KR3j0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0013) *Liúzǐ* 劉子 ([劉晝](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E6%99%9D)); [KR3j0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0014) *Yánshì jiāxùn* 顏氏家訓 ([顏之推](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E4%B9%8B%E6%8E%A8)), the most influential of all family-precepts books; [KR3j0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0015) *Cháng duǎn jīng* 長短經 (Táng [趙蕤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E8%95%A4), 716), a syncretist statecraft and stratagem manual; [KR3j0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0017) *Huà shū* 化書 (the Daoist-physiological treatise of [譚峭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%9A%E5%B3%AD)).

**The Sòng evidential *bǐjì*.** The most consequential single cluster in the division. [KR3j0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0038) *Róngzhāi suíbǐ* 容齋隨筆 ([洪邁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E9%82%81), begun 1162), [KR3j0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0055) *Kùnxué jìwén* 困學紀聞 ([王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F), composed after 1276), [KR3j0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0039) *Kǎogǔ biān* 攷古編 and [KR3j0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0040) *Yǎnfán lù* 演繁露 (both [程大昌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A8%8B%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8C)), [KR3j0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0034) *Nénggǎizhāi mànlù* 能改齋漫錄 ([吳曾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%9B%BE)), [KR3j0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0037) *Xuélín* 學林 ([王觀國](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%A7%80%E5%9C%8B)), [KR3j0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0041) *Wěi lüè* 緯略 ([高似孫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E4%BC%BC%E5%AD%AB)), [KR3j0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0045) *Yěkè cóngshū* 野客叢書 ([王楙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%A5%99)) and the rest of the long Sòng cluster from [KR3j0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0033) to [KR3j0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0057) collectively establish *kǎozhèng* 考證 as a recognisable scholarly mode three centuries before the Qīng apex; the Qīng editors of the *Sìkù* preserve them as the direct ancestors of [KR3j0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0070) *Rì zhī lù*.

**The polymath Sòng *bǐjì*.** Distinct from the strictly philological cluster but overlapping it. [KR3j0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0092) *Mèngxī bǐtán* 夢溪筆談 ([沈括](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E6%8B%AC), c. 1086–1095), the single most famous Chinese pre-modern technical-encyclopedic notebook (the *Bì Shēng* movable-type entry is its most-cited passage); [KR3j0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0093) *Chóuchí bǐjì* 仇池筆記 and [KR3j0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0094) *Dōngpō zhì lín* 東坡志林 ([蘇軾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE)); [KR3j0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0105) *Shílín yànyǔ* 石林燕語, [KR3j0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0106) *Bìshǔ lùhuà* 避暑錄話, [KR3j0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0107) *Yánxià fàngyán* 巖下放言 ([葉夢得](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%89%E5%A4%A2%E5%BE%97)); [KR3j0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0123) *Lǎo xué ān bǐjì* 老學庵筆記 ([陸游](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E6%B8%B8)); [KR3j0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0134) *Qí dōng yě yǔ* 齊東野語 ([周密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E5%AF%86)).

**Sòng–Yuán *cóngshū*-style anthological compilations** (*zá zuǎn* and *zá biān*): [KR3j0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0082) *Qún shū zhì yào* 群書治要 (Táng [魏徵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E5%BE%B5), 631 — the ancestor of the genre); [KR3j0178](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0178) *Yìlín* 意林 (Táng [馬總](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E7%B8%BD)); [KR3j0179](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0179) *Gàn zhū jí* 紺珠集 and [KR3j0180](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0180) *Lèi shuō* 類說 ([曾慥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%BE%E6%85%A5), 1136); [KR3j0181](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0181) *Shì shí lèi yuàn* 事實類苑; [KR3j0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0185) *Shuō fú* 說孚 ([陶宗儀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%AE%97%E5%84%80)).

**The Míng polymathic peak.** [KR3j0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0059) *Dān qiān yú lù* 丹鉛餘錄 ([楊愼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E6%84%BC)); [KR3j0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0066) *Tōngyǎ* 通雅 ([方以智](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%B9%E4%BB%A5%E6%99%BA), c. 1642), the most systematic Míng philological compendium and the proximate ancestor of Qīng *kǎozhèng* on the linguistic side; [KR3j0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0160) *Wùlǐ xiǎozhì* 物理小識 (also [方以智](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%B9%E4%BB%A5%E6%99%BA)), the parallel natural-philosophical compendium; [KR3j0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0190) *Shǎoshì shānfáng bǐcóng* 少室山房筆叢 ([胡應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F), 1602), the most ambitious Míng *bǐjì*-as-cóngshū; [KR3j0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0149) *Cǎo mù zǐ* 草木子 ([葉子奇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%89%E5%AD%90%E5%A5%87)).

**The Qīng evidential apex.** [KR3j0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0070) *Rì zhī lù* 日知錄 ([顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6), 1670s–82) is the single most influential intellectual work in the division and the foundation stone of Qīng *Hàn xué* 漢學; [KR3j0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0072) *Qiánqiū zhájì* 潛邱劄記 ([閻若璩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%96%BB%E8%8B%A5%E7%92%A9)); [KR3j0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0073) *Zhànyuán zhájì* 湛園札記 ([姜宸英](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9C%E5%AE%B8%E8%8B%B1)); [KR3j0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0076) *Yìmén dú shū jì* 義門讀書記 ([何焯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E7%84%AF)); [KR3j0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0074) *Bái tián zá zhù* 白田雜著 ([王懋竑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%8B%E7%AB%91)); [KR3j0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0069) *Yìfǔ* 義府 ([黃生](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E7%94%9F)) — collectively the canonical kǎozhèng cluster the *Sìkù* editors place beside Wáng Yīnglín as proof of the genre's continuity. The five-volume late-Qīng notebooks of [王士禛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A3%AB%E7%A6%9B) ([KR3j0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0162) *Jūyì lù* 居易錄, [KR3j0163](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0163) *Chí běi ǒu tán* 池北偶談, [KR3j0164](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0164) *Xiāng zǔ bǐjì* 香祖筆記, [KR3j0165](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0165) *Fēngān yúhuà* 分甘餘話, [KR3j0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0166) *Gǔfūyútíng zálù* 古夫於亭雜錄) close the division's chronological line at the turn of the eighteenth century.

**The connoisseurship cluster** (*zá pǐn*). [KR3j0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0167) *Dòngtiān qīnglù* 洞天清錄 ([趙希鵠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E5%B8%8C%E9%B5%A0), Sòng — antiques and the literati object); [KR3j0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0169) *Yún yān guò yǎn lù* 雲烟過眼錄 ([周密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E5%AF%86)); [KR3j0170](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0170) *Gégǔ yàolùn* 格古要論 ([曹昭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%B9%E6%98%AD), 1388); [KR3j0172](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0172) *Zūn shēng bā jiān* 遵生八牋 ([高濂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E6%BF%82), 1591); [KR3j0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0174) *Cháng wù zhì* 長物志 ([文震亨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%87%E9%9C%87%E4%BA%A8)), the canonical late-Míng manual of literati taste in furniture, gardens, and the things of the studio.

### Important persons

- [呂不韋](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E4%B8%8D%E9%9F%8B) (Lǚ Bùwéi, d. 235 BCE) — convener of the *Lǚshì chūnqiū* salon; the founding figure of imperial-state syncretism in this division.
- [劉安](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AE%89) (Liú Ān, c. 179–122 BCE) — Prince of Huáinán, convener of the *Huáinánzǐ* circle and the second canonical *Zájiā* syncretist.
- [王充](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%85%85) (Wáng Chōng, 27–c. 100) — Eastern Hàn rationalist polemicist; *Lùnhéng* is the most sustained early prose argument against portent-mongering and excess in the division.
- [顏之推](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E4%B9%8B%E6%8E%A8) (Yán Zhītuī, 531–c. 591) — author of the *Yánshì jiāxùn*, the model of the Six-Dynasties / Suí *jiāxùn* tradition and a major source for the social history of the period.
- [沈括](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E6%8B%AC) (Shěn Kuò, 1031–1095) — Northern Sòng polymath; the *Mèngxī bǐtán* is the single most influential pre-modern Chinese technical-scientific *bǐjì*.
- [蘇軾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE) (Sū Shì, 1037–1101) — model of the literati personal notebook ([KR3j0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0093), [KR3j0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0094)).
- [葉夢得](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%89%E5%A4%A2%E5%BE%97) (Yè Mèngdé, 1077–1148) — author of the *Shílín* trilogy ([KR3j0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0105)–[KR3j0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0107)), a Northern–Southern Sòng witness on court life and classical scholarship.
- [洪邁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E9%82%81) (Hóng Mài, 1123–1202) — author of *Róngzhāi suíbǐ*, the most consequential Sòng evidential *bǐjì* before Wáng Yīnglín and the work that did most to fix the form.
- [程大昌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%A8%8B%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8C) (Chéng Dàchāng, 1123–1195) — twin author of *Kǎogǔ biān* and *Yǎnfán lù*; a key Sòng *kǎozhèng* witness on ritual and institutions.
- [王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) (Wáng Yīnglín, 1223–1296) — Sòng-loyalist polymath; the *Kùnxué jìwén* is the most important single *kǎozhèng bǐjì* of the Sòng and a direct model for Qīng *Hàn xué*.
- [周密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E5%AF%86) (Zhōu Mì, 1232–1298) — Sòng-Yuán *yímín* whose work is split across two sub-genres in the division: *zá shuō* in *Qí dōng yě yǔ* and *zá pǐn* in *Yún yān guò yǎn lù*.
- [陸游](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E6%B8%B8) (Lù Yóu, 1125–1210) — author of the *Lǎo xué ān bǐjì*, one of the most-cited Sòng anecdotal-historical notebooks.
- [楊愼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E6%84%BC) (Yáng Shèn, 1488–1559) — the most prolific Míng *bǐjì* author and the principal target of subsequent Míng-Qīng rebuttals (e.g. [KR3j0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0062) *Zhèng Yáng* 正楊).
- [胡應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) (Hú Yīnglín, 1551–1602) — late-Míng bibliographer and polymath whose *Shǎoshì shānfáng bǐcóng* is the great Míng *bǐjì*-as-cóngshū.
- [方以智](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%B9%E4%BB%A5%E6%99%BA) (Fāng Yǐzhì, 1611–1671) — late-Míng / early-Qīng polymath; author of both *Tōngyǎ* (philology) and *Wùlǐ xiǎozhì* (natural philosophy) — the most ambitious bridge between Míng polymathy and Qīng evidential learning.
- [顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6) (Gù Yánwǔ, 1613–1682) — Sòng-loyalist refusenik whose *Rì zhī lù* defines the Qīng evidential tradition in this division.
- [閻若璩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%96%BB%E8%8B%A5%E7%92%A9) (Yán Ruòqú, 1636–1704) — Qīng evidential master whose *Qiánqiū zhájì* — together with his annotations on Wáng Yīnglín — institutionalised the Sòng-to-Qīng *kǎozhèng* lineage.
- [何焯](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E7%84%AF) (Hé Zhuō, 1661–1722) — early-Qīng evidential editor whose *Yìmén dú shū jì* and joint annotations to *Kùnxué jìwén* fix the Qīng reception of Wáng Yīnglín.
- [王士禛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A3%AB%E7%A6%9B) (Wáng Shìzhēn, 1634–1711) — the leading literary arbiter of the Kāngxī court whose five separate notebooks ([KR3j0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0162)–[KR3j0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0166)) are the most thoroughly preserved late-Qīng literati *bǐjì* in the division.

### Topics

- **The category as residual class.** *Zájiā* is, in both its Hàn and *Sìkù* incarnations, the bibliographer's category of last resort: works that do not belong in the four orthodox Masters subclasses (Confucians, Daoists, Legalists, Logicians) or in the more specialised technical subclasses (Military, Astronomy, Mantic Arts, Medicine, Arts, Connoisseurship in the narrow sense, *Lèishū*, Fiction) end up here. Reading the division therefore requires keeping the *Sìkù*'s six internal subclasses in view (see Scope, above).
- **The *bǐjì* genre.** Most of the division — roughly [KR3j0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0026) through [KR3j0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0166) plus most of the connoisseurship cluster — consists of *bǐjì* (Wilkinson § 53). The genre's range and unevenness, its mingling of factual and anecdotal entries, its frequent reading-notes form, and its synonyms (*bǐtán*, *cóngtán*, *suíbǐ*, *zájì*, *zázhì*, *zhájì*; Wilkinson Box 266) are all directly relevant. Wilkinson § 53.1 explicitly remarks that the *bǐjì* form was usually filed in *Zájiā* in the Masters branch — the division on disk is therefore one of the largest single homes of the genre in the *Sìkù*.
- **Pseudepigraphy and recension.** Most of the pre-Qín *zǐ* in the head of the division ([KR3j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0001), [KR3j0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0004), [KR3j0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0005), [KR3j0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0006)) are partially or wholly transmitted in post-Hàn recensions; some (the *Yùzǐ* in particular) are securely Táng. The *Sìkù* editors flag this consistently in their *tíyào*. Compositions dates in KR3j frontmatter therefore follow the project's policy (CLAUDE.md § Per-text procedure) of dating the **received recension**, not the attributed author's lifedates — so e.g. [KR3j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0001) is dated 600–653 (Táng) and [KR3j0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0003) is dated to its Sòng forger's lifetime.
- **The growth of evidential learning.** The division is the principal site at which the trajectory from Sòng *kǎozhèng bǐjì* (Hóng Mài, Wáng Yīnglín, Chéng Dàchāng) through Míng polymathy (Yáng Shèn, Hú Yīnglín, Fāng Yǐzhì) to Qīng *Hàn xué* (Gù Yánwǔ, Yán Ruòqú, Hé Zhuō) can be read continuously off the shelf. The *Sìkù* editors' selection deliberately preserves that lineage.
- **The connoisseurship sub-genre and literati material culture.** The twelve *zá pǐn* texts collect the canonical Sòng-to-Qīng manuals on antiques, calligraphy, painting, gardens, food, dress, and the literati object — a body of evidence indispensable for the social and material history of the late imperial elite.
- **The boundary with *xiǎoshuō* 小說 and with *zá shǐ* 雜史.** Many of the more anecdotal *bǐjì* in the division ([KR3j0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0083) *Fēngshì wén jiàn jì*, [KR3j0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0100) *Lěngzhāi yè huà*, [KR3j0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0127) *Hè lín yù lù*) shade towards what later catalogers would call *xiǎoshuō*; the *Sìkù* keeps them in *Zájiā* on the strength of their factual content, but Wilkinson § 53.3 and § 52.1 make clear that the line was always negotiable, and many of the same titles are re-classified elsewhere in modern editions.
- **The *cóngshū* problem.** The four *zá biān* compendia ([KR3j0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0188) *Yǎnshān wàijí*, [KR3j0189](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0189) *Gǔjīn shuōhǎi*, [KR3j0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0190) *Shǎoshì shānfáng bǐcóng*, [KR3j0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0191) *Dùnyín zálù*) preserve the older arrangement under which multi-work compendia were filed in *Zájiā* rather than constituting their own branch; the late nineteenth-century rise of *cóngshū* as a fifth branch (Wilkinson § 73.2.3) effectively drains this subclass.
- **Reconstituted pre-Táng fragments.** The closing krp-titles entries ([KR3j0196](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0196) *Shǐ xué piān*, [KR3j0197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0197) *Lù shì yào lǎn*, [KR3j0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0198) *Wùlǐ lùn*, [KR3j0199](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0199) *Guǎng zhì*, [KR3j0200](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3j/KR3j0200) *Fā méng jì*) are Qīng *jíyì* 輯佚 reconstitutions of lost Three Kingdoms / Jìn works whose fragments survive in *lèishū* — a final demonstration of the division's role as the *Sìkù*'s home for genre-hybrid Masters material.

# 類書類 (KR3k)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR3k 類書類 *Lèishū lèi* — Masters — Encyclopedias and Categorized Anthologies (Lèishū)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR3k collects the *lèishū* 類書 — literally "books arranged by category" — as defined and bounded by the *Sìkù quánshū* 四庫全書 editors of the 1780s. *Lèishū* are encyclopedic anthologies of excerpts from previous works, arranged under topical, prosopographical, or rhyme-based headings to be consulted by an emperor, an official, an examination candidate, or a literary writer searching for a precedent or a turn of phrase. The *Sìkù* placed them in the third (子, *Masters*) branch following the choice already made by the *Jiù Tángzhì* 舊唐志 (945), and split off the rhyme-organised lexical *lèishū* into the 小學 (*xiǎoxué*) category of the Classics branch — a division Wilkinson, *Chinese History: A New Manual* §72.1.1 follows and which is reflected here: KR3k contains the topical and prosopographical *lèishū* plus the major Qīng rhyme-treasuries that were nevertheless catalogued in 子部 (*Pèiwén yùnfǔ*, *Yùnfǔ qúnyù*).

The tradition runs from the lost early-3rd-century *Huánglǎn* 皇覽 commissioned for Wèi Wéndì 魏文帝 — conventionally the genre's founder — through to the great Kāngxī–Yōngzhèng imperial compendia of the early 18th century. Its chronological centre of gravity is the Sòng (works from 977 to 1296 dominate the catalog by both bulk and influence), but the surviving Suí–Táng nucleus ([KR3k0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0002), 0003, 0004, 0006) preserves citations from a thousand-plus pre-7th-century works, of which most no longer exist independently — so KR3k is also the largest single conduit by which the fragmentary pre-Táng book-world reaches the modern reader. Wilkinson §72.1.1 estimates that of the 1,400 books quoted in the *Yìwén lèijù* 藝文類聚 alone, roughly 90 % are otherwise lost. KR3k is therefore not just a genre-bin: it is, with KR1 (Classics) and KR2 (Histories), one of the principal evidence-bases for Chinese textual archaeology.

The genre splits into several distinct sub-traditions. Wilkinson §72.1.2 organises the canonical general *lèishū* by dynasty (Suí–Táng, Sòng–Yuán, Míng, Qīng); cross-cutting that chronological grid are the imperial-court mega-compendia ("the four great books of the Sòng" 宋四大書, of which three survive in KR3k); the literary-composition *lèishū* (allusion- and parallel-prose primers); the surname-and-pedigree (*xìngshì*) lineage; the *xiǎomíng* / *biéhào* prosopographical line founded by Liáng Yuándì 梁元帝; the *méngqiú* 蒙求 examination-and-children's primer line; the Southern-Sòng *cèyì* / *kǎojù* statecraft-crammer cluster (Yǒngjiā / Wùxué); the institutional-origins (*qǐyuán*) tradition; and the late-Míng / early-Qīng evidential and material-culture compendia. The *Sìkù* preface to the section warns explicitly that *lèishū* must be used with care because they typically quote from earlier *lèishū* rather than from the originals — a critique made famously caustic in Gù Yánwǔ's 顧炎武 dictum *gāotán ér bù gēn* 高談而不根 ("high talk without roots"; Wilkinson §72.1.1). The tension between *lèishū* as indispensable archive and *lèishū* as transcriptional sediment is the interpretive frame for the whole division.

### Important texts and text clusters

#### Founders of the genre (6th–7th c.)

- *Gǔjīn tóngxìngmíng lù* 古今同姓名錄 [KR3k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0001) — Liáng Yuándì 梁元帝's homonymic-prosopography compendium, the *Sìkù* editors' candidate for the oldest extant categorised *lèishū*; founder of a sub-genre that runs through to [KR3k0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0035), 0042, 0047, 0064 in this catalog.
- *Biānzhū* 編珠 [KR3k0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0002) — Suí Yáng-dì-period allusion-pair handbook attributed to Dù Gōngzhān 杜公瞻; the earliest surviving *lèishū* explicitly designed for the composition of *fù* 賦.
- *Běitáng shūchāo* 北堂書鈔 [KR3k0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0004) — Yú Shìnán's 虞世南 early-Táng compilation, conventionally the **earliest extant general *lèishū*** (Wilkinson §72.1.2.1); preserves a great many pre-Suí citations.

#### The Táng "four great *lèishū*" 唐代四大類書

The four canonical Táng general *lèishū* listed together in Wilkinson §72.1.2.1 are all present in KR3k:

- *Yìwén lèijù* 藝文類聚 [KR3k0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0003) — Ōuyáng Xún 歐陽詢, 624; arranged in 46 *bù* / 727 *mù*; landmark in interleaving facts (*shì*) with literary excerpts (*wén*).
- *Běitáng shūchāo* [KR3k0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0004) — see above.
- *Chūxué jì* 初學記 [KR3k0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0006) — Xú Jiān 徐堅 et al., compiled for the Tang Xuánzōng 唐玄宗's princes; introduces the tripartite *xùshì* / *shìduì* / *shīwén* internal layout.
- *Bái Kǒng liùtiē* 白孔六帖 [KR3k0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0008) — Bái Jūyì 白居易's *Liùtiē*, with Kǒng Chuán's 孔傳 Northern-Sòng continuation; the prototypical examination-preparation *lèishū*. Wilkinson §72.1.2.1 cites it for the famous anecdote of Bái assembling entries in jars on a seven-tiered rack.

Around this nucleus belong *Lóngjīn fèngsuǐ pàn* 龍筋鳳髓判 [KR3k0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0005) — Zhāng Zhuó's 張鷟 model-*pàn* 判 anthology for the Táng *shēnyánshūpàn* 身言書判 examination — and the surviving fragments of two specifically examination-oriented texts recovered from Dùnhuáng and Dazaifu, *Tùyuán cèfǔ* 兔園策府 [KR3k0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0069) and *Hànyuàn* 翰苑 [KR3k0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0070). These fragmentary witnesses are textually marginal but historically central as the only direct evidence for early-Táng *cèwén* pedagogy.

#### The "four great books of the Sòng" (Sòng sì dà shū 宋四大書) — the three in KR3k

Of the four court-commissioned mega-compendia of early Northern Sòng (the fourth being *Tàipíng guǎngjì* 太平廣記, classified under *xiǎoshuō* and not in KR3k), three are here:

- *Tàipíng yùlǎn* 太平御覽 [KR3k0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0012) — Lǐ Fǎng 李昉 et al., 977–983, in 1000 *juan*; arranged in 55 *bù* / 5,363 *lèi*; quotes from over 2,000 sources, ~70–80 % otherwise lost (Wilkinson §72.1.2.2).
- *Cèfǔ yuánguī* 册府元龜 [KR3k0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0013) — Wáng Qīnruò 王欽若, Yáng Yì 楊億 et al., completed 1013, in 1000 *juan*; restricted to *zhèngshǐ* extracts; the principal Northern-Sòng compendium of imperial and bureaucratic precedent.
- *Yùhǎi* 玉海 [KR3k0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0032) — Wáng Yīnglín 王應麟, late 13th c., in 200 *juan*; technically the latest of this group but functionally the most intellectually rigorous, and the most reliable Sòng *lèishū* for source-citation (compiled as preparation for the *Bóxué hóngcí* 博學宏詞 examination, which Wáng passed in 1255).

#### The Wáng Yīnglín cluster

Wáng Yīnglín alone accounts for four KR3k titles: the *Yùhǎi* [KR3k0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0032), the numerical-categories primer *Xiǎoxué gànzhū* 小學紺珠 [KR3k0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0033), the surname mnemonic *Xìngshì jíjiù piān* 姓氏急就篇 [KR3k0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0034), and (associated) the *Liùtiē bǔ* 六帖補 [KR3k0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0037) supplement of his student Yáng Bóyán 楊伯喦. This cluster is the high-water mark of late-Sòng *kǎojù*-style *lèishū* scholarship: every excerpt in *Yùhǎi* is source-tagged, an editorial standard not matched again until the *Sìkù*.

#### Southern-Sòng statecraft / examination-crammer cluster

Driven by the late-12th- and 13th-century *cèyì* 策議 and *cèlùn* 策論 examination format, a recognisable cluster of policy-essay reference works was produced largely from the Yǒngjiā 永嘉 and Wùxué 婺學 milieu:

- *Lìdài zhìdù xiángshuō* 歷代制度詳說 [KR3k0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0021) — Lǚ Zǔqiān 呂祖謙, the Wùxué patriarch.
- *Bāmiàn fēng* 八面鋒 [KR3k0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0022) — Chén Fùliáng 陳傅良, in 93 aphoristic *gāng* 綱.
- *Qúnshū kǎosuǒ* 羣書考索 [KR3k0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0029) — Zhāng Rúyú 章如愚, in 4 *jí* and 212 *juan*, the largest of the cluster; central to Tillman 1990–92 (cited in Wilkinson §72.1.2.2) on Sòng polymath encyclopaedism.
- *Gǔjīn yuánliú zhìlùn* 古今源流至論 [KR3k0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0031) — Lín Jiōng 林駉 and Huáng Lǚwēng 黃履翁.
- *Qúnshū huìyuán jiéjiāng wǎng* 羣書會元截江網 [KR3k0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0027) — anonymous, a representative *fāngběn* 坊本 commercial crammer for Tàixué 太學 students.

#### Surname-and-pedigree (*xìngshì*) tradition

A distinct *lèishū* sub-genre indexing the historical *jùnwàng* 郡望 (territorial branches of surname-lineages):

- *Yuánhé xìngzuǎn* 元和姓纂 [KR3k0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0007) — Lín Bǎo 林寶, 812; foundational Táng manual originally for fief-bestowal.
- *Gǔjīn xìngshì shū biànzhèng* 古今姓氏書辯證 [KR3k0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0018) — Dèng Míngshì 鄧名世, Southern Sòng critical revision of the *Yuánhé xìngzuǎn*.
- *Míngxián shìzú yánxíng lèigǎo* 名賢氏族言行類稿 [KR3k0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0026) — Zhāng Dìng 章定, hybrid of surname-pedigree and biographical-anecdote anthology, covering 1,189 surnames.
- *Shìzú dàquán* 氏族大全 [KR3k0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0041) — anonymous Yuán Máshā 麻沙 commercial expansion.
- *Wànxìng tǒngpǔ* 萬姓統譜 [KR3k0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0044) — Líng Dízhī 凌迪知, the bulk culmination of the Míng tradition (140 *juan*).

#### Homonymic / sobriquet / childhood-name prosopography

The line founded by [KR3k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0001) (above) continues with *Xiǎomíng lù* 小名錄 [KR3k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0009) (Lù Guīméng 陸龜蒙, late Táng); *Xiǎozì lù* 小字錄 [KR3k0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0035) (Chén Sī 陳思, late Sòng); *Míngyí* 名疑 [KR3k0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0042) (Chén Shìyuán 陳士元, Míng); *Tóngxìngmíng lù* 同姓名錄 [KR3k0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0047) (Yú Yín 余寅, late Míng, the 12-*juan* expansion explicitly named in the *Sìkù tíyào* to [KR3k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0001) as the 21-*juan* descendant); and the rhyme-organised *Bié hào lù* 別號錄 [KR3k0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0064) (Gě Wànlǐ 葛萬里, Qīng), which inverts the relationship and indexes from sobriquet back to personal name.

#### Phraseological and rhyme-treasury *lèishū* (the Qīng imperial trilogy)

The Kāngxī–Yōngzhèng court produced an unparalleled cluster of phraseological reference works, all sponsored by the throne and printed at the Wǔyīngdiàn 武英殿:

- *Yùnfǔ qúnyù* 韻府群玉 [KR3k0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0039) — Yīn Jìnxián 陰勁弦 et al., late Yuán; the founding *yùnfǔ* 韻府 to which the entire Qīng imperial cluster responds. Cited by the Yǒnglè emperor in his commission of the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* (Wilkinson §72.1.2.3) as one of his two model works.
- *Yùdìng Pèiwén yùnfǔ* 御定佩文韻府 [KR3k0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0059) — Zhāng Yùshū 張玉書, Chén Tíngjìng 陳廷敬 et al., Kāngxī commission, 444 *juan*; "still has no equal among modern dictionaries for amount of lexical data" (Wilkinson §72.1.1).
- *Yùdìng Yùnfǔ shíyí* 御定韻府拾遺 [KR3k0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0060) — Kāngxī's own supplement to the *Pèiwén yùnfǔ*.
- *Yùdìng Piánzì lèibiān* 御定駢字類編 [KR3k0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0056) — Wú Shìyù 吳士玉, Shěn Zōngjìng 沈宗敬, 240 *juan*; complementary indexing-by-head-character to the *Pèiwén yùnfǔ*'s indexing-by-tail-rhyme.
- *Yùdìng Fēnlèi zìjǐn* 御定分類字錦 [KR3k0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0057) — Hé Chuò 何焯, Chén Péngnián 陳鵬年; Kāngxī matched-pair *duìǒu* 對偶 phraseological compendium.
- *Yùdìng Zǐshǐ jīnghuá* 御定子史精華 [KR3k0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0058) — Wú Shìyù, Wú Xiāng 吳襄; Yōngzhèng-period topical anthology of extracts from the 子 and 史 branches.

#### General Qīng imperial *lèishū*

- *Yùdìng Yuānjiàn lèihán* 御定淵鑑類函 [KR3k0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0055) — Zhāng Yīng 張英, Wáng Shìzhēn 王士禛, completed 1702, printed 1710, 450 *juan*; a Kāngxī rework of the late-Míng *Táng lèihán* 唐類函 with later citations marked *zēng* 增 (Wilkinson §72.1.2.4); the principal Qīng general *lèishū* in KR3k. (The much larger *Gǔjīn túshū jíchéng* 古今圖書集成, 1726–28, was not included in the *Sìkù* and is therefore absent from KR3k.)

#### Material-culture and *géwù* (*qǐyuán*) line

- *Shìwù jìyuán* 事物紀原 [KR3k0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0014) — Gāo Chéng 高承, Northern Sòng; the founding "origins-of-things" *lèishū*.
- *Gézhì jìngyuán* 格致鏡原 [KR3k0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0061) — Chén Yuánlóng 陳元龍, Qīng; the genre's mature *géwù* synthesis (cited in Wilkinson §72.1.2.4).
- *Huā mù niǎo shòu jí lèi* 花木鳥獸集類 [KR3k0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0063) — Wú Bǎozhī 吳寶芝, small Qīng natural-world allusion compendium.

#### Late-Míng general / private / botanical

- *Tiānzhōng jì* 天中記 [KR3k0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0049) — Chén Yàowén 陳耀文, mid-Míng general *lèishū* with proto-*kǎojù* source citation.
- *Shāntáng sìkǎo* 山堂肆考 [KR3k0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0052) — Péng Dàyì 彭大翼, large late-Míng general *lèishū* by a private *zhūshēng* 諸生 compiler.
- *Túshū biān* 圖書編 [KR3k0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0050) — Zhāng Huáng 章潢, massive 127-*juan* late-Míng *túpǔ* 圖譜 (charts-and-tables) encyclopedia from the Báilùdòng 白鹿洞 milieu.
- *Quánfāng bèizǔ jí* 全芳備祖集 [KR3k0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0028) — Chén Jǐngyí 陳景沂, late-Sòng botanical *lèishū* of plants, flowers, fruits, vegetables, and herbs.

#### *Méngqiú* primers

- *Méngqiú jízhù* 蒙求集註 [KR3k0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0010) — Sòng commentary by Xú Zǐguāng 徐子光 on Lǐ Hàn 李瀚's Táng *Méngqiú* (rhymed historical-anecdote primer for children).
- *Chúnzhèng méngqiú* 純正蒙求 [KR3k0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0040) — Hú Bǐngwén 胡炳文, Yuán Zhū Xī school orthodox primer.

### Topics

- **The *lèishū* as conduit for lost books.** From the Táng *Yìwén lèijù* through the *Tàipíng yùlǎn* to the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* — itself the source-base for the *Sìkù* recovery of [KR3k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0001) — KR3k is the single largest collection of pre-Táng citations preserved by quotation. The methodological caution (Wilkinson §72.1.1; Gù Yánwǔ's *gāotán ér bù gēn* 高談而不根) is that *lèishū* almost always quote a previous *lèishū* rather than the original; verification against the surviving original — when one exists — is therefore mandatory.

- **Imperial sponsorship and dynastic legitimation.** Wilkinson §72.1.1 emphasises the timing of the major imperial commissions (Sòng Tàizōng's *Tàipíng yùlǎn*; Yǒnglè's *Dàdiǎn*; Kāngxī's *Yuānjiàn lèihán* and *Pèiwén yùnfǔ*) at the start of new dynasties or after disputed accessions: the *lèishū* simultaneously displayed the new throne's literary stature, kept restive scholar-officials usefully employed, and let the new regime decide what counted as transmissible knowledge.

- **Classification systems.** The genre's organising matrices — heaven / earth / man / events / things, with the deeper *bù* / *lèi* / *mù* / *shǔ* hierarchy — set the template for many *bǐjì* and reference works outside the *lèishū* genre proper (Wilkinson §72.1.1.2). Departures from this matrix — Wáng Yīnglín's numerical-set organisation in *Xiǎoxué gànzhū* [KR3k0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0033), the rhyme-organisation of the *yùnfǔ* line, the surname-as-key indexing of *xìngshì* compendia — are the genre's most consequential structural innovations.

- **The Sòng *cèyì* / *kǎojù* statecraft *lèishū*.** A distinct Southern-Sòng cluster (Yǒngjiā / Wùxué) used the *lèishū* form not as a literary aid but as a policy-essay crammer for the examinations and as a vehicle for institutional history. Tillman 1990–92 (Wilkinson §72.1.2.2) treats Zhèng Qiáo 鄭樵, Zhāng Rúyú [KR3k0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0029), and Wáng Yīnglín together as a Sòng polymath-encyclopaedist tradition.

- **Phraseological *lèishū* and the Qīng court.** From the Sòng *Shìlèi fù* [KR3k0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0011) through to the Kāngxī rhyme-treasuries, a steadily intensifying technical machinery for the manufacture of parallel-prose and regulated verse: indexed by rhyme (*Pèiwén yùnfǔ*, *Yùnfǔ shíyí*), by head-character (*Piánzì lèibiān*), by matched pair (*Fēnlèi zìjǐn*), by topic-and-allusion (*Yuānjiàn lèihán*). For the user, these compete and complement; for the Qīng court, the entire suite functioned as instruments of cultural standardisation.

- **The surname-and-prosopography line.** A historiographically distinct *lèishū* tradition concerned with disambiguating persons rather than topicalising knowledge: from the Liáng *tóngxìngmíng* compendium [KR3k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0001) through the Táng *Yuánhé xìngzuǎn* [KR3k0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0007) to the Qīng *Bié hào lù* [KR3k0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0064). This line bridges KR3k and the genealogical interests of KR2 (Histories) more than any other cluster in the division.

- **The boundary problem.** The *Sìkù* editors deliberately excluded both the Yǒnglè *Dàdiǎn* (lost in 1900 in the Hànlín fire) and the *Gǔjīn túshū jíchéng* (printed by Yōngzhèng but not yet in the *Sìkù* canon when KR3k was constituted) from the category. Conversely, they extracted [KR3k0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3k/KR3k0001) from the *Dàdiǎn* and re-issued it. The category as we receive it through KR3k is therefore a *Sìkù*-mediated and *Sìkù*-curated selection — not an exhaustive *lèishū* archive.
