# 小說家類 (KR3l)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR3l 小說家類 *Xiǎoshuō jiā lèi* — Masters — School of Minor Discourses (anecdotal miscellanies, *biji*, *zhì-guài*)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR3l 小說家類 is the *Sìkù* Masters Branch (子部) subdivision that gathers what later editors called *xiǎoshuō* 小說 in the pre-modern sense — anecdotal miscellanies (*bǐjì* 筆記), accounts of the strange (*zhìguài* 志怪), records of urban and court anecdote (*yìshì* 逸事, *suǒyán* 瑣言, *wénjiàn lù* 聞見錄), and the Tang-Sòng narrative experiments that modern literary history calls *chuánqí* 傳奇. The category descends from the *Hànshū yìwén zhì* "ten Schools" rubric — *xiǎoshuō jiā zhě liú, gài chū yú bàiguān* 小說家者流, 蓋出於稗官 ("the School of Minor Discourses derives from the petty officers") — and was re-anchored under the *Sìkù* as the trailing subdivision of the Masters Branch on the strength of an editorial decision the Qing reviewers themselves call grudging: *xiǎoshuō* sits at the bottom of *zǐbù* because, by the eighteenth century, neither the bureaucratic-realist *jìshì* register nor the *zhìguài* / *chuánqí* register fitted the orthodox classification cleanly, yet too much of the medieval and Sòng documentary record was preserved only here to permit exclusion. Wilkinson §53 ("*Biji*"), §53.3 ("*Biji xiaoshuo*"), and §60.3 (under *Shishuo xinyu*) together provide the standard English-language framing: the genre's pre-Han origins in *jiētán xiàngyǔ* 街談巷語 street-corner talk; Liú Zhījī's eighth-century re-classification of *záshù* 雜述 into ten sub-types (*piānjì*, *xiǎolù*, *yìshì*, *suǒyán*, *jùnshū*, *jiāshǐ*, *biézhuàn*, *zájì*, *dìlǐ*, *dūyì bù*; *Shǐtōng* 史通, Nèi 34, [Wilkinson Box 264]); the persistent failure of pre-modern Chinese taxonomy to distinguish "fiction" from "factual notes," because the same *bǐjì* routinely mixes both; and the modern May-Fourth re-purposing of *xiǎoshuō* to mean prose fiction in the European sense, an equation that maps poorly onto everything classified here.

The chronological span of the division runs from the *Shānhǎi jīng* 山海經 [KR3l0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0090) (a composite Warring-States-to-Hàn cosmographic-cum-marvel anthology) to *Liáozhāi zhìyì* 聊齋誌異 [KR3l0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0130) (Pú Sōnglíng, c. 1670–1715) — effectively, the whole arc of premodern Chinese anecdotal and *zhìguài* writing in literary Chinese. Three transmissional traditions a reader must keep in mind are: (1) the pre-Táng *zhìguài* corpus, much of which survives only as quotation-fragments in *lèishū* (*Yìwén lèijù*, *Tàipíng yùlǎn*, *Tàipíng guǎngjì*) and which the modern Lǔ Xùn 魯迅 *Gǔ xiǎoshuō gōu chén* 古小說鉤沈 reconstruction project brought back into circulation — the entries `[KR3l0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0131)`–`[KR3l0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0169)` are *jíyì* reconstructions of this kind; (2) the Sòng-Yuán-Míng *bǐjì* mainstream, the principal supplementary source for everything the Standard Histories chose not to record (cf. Wilkinson §62.3.11 on Sòng *bǐjì*); and (3) the late-imperial *zhìguài* literary revival that culminates in *Liáozhāi zhìyì* and is anticipated by *Yǒuyáng zázǔ* 酉陽雜俎 [KR3l0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0125) in the ninth century.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The *Shìshuō xīnyǔ* and the *shìshuō tǐ* tradition.** *Shìshuō xīnyǔ* 世說新語 [KR3l0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0002) (c. 430–444, compiled under [劉義慶](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E7%BE%A9%E6%85%B6) Liú Yìqìng; commentary by [劉孝標](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AD%9D%E6%A8%99) Liú Xiàobiāo, 462–521) is the foundational anecdotal compilation of medieval China and the genre-prototype of the *shìshuō tǐ* 世說體 — some 1,130 short anecdotes on c. 600 persons of the late Hàn and Wèi-Jìn organised into thirty-six character-appraisal categories from *Déxíng* 德行 to *Chóuxì* 仇隟. Liú Xiàobiāo's commentary, citing some 400 lost works, is itself one of the great survival-vectors for Six Dynasties biography. The division registers the *shìshuō tǐ* afterlife directly in *Yǔlín* 語林 [KR3l0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0089) (Hé Liángjùn 何良俊, Míng), *Táng yǔlín* 唐語林 [KR3l0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0055) (Wáng Dǎng 王讜, Sòng — a *shìshuō*-style re-categorisation of Táng anecdote), and the lost *Péizǐ yǔlín* 裴子語林 [KR3l0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0135) (Péi Qǐ 裴啟, fl. c. 362), the work whose forgery scandal Liú Yìqìng's commission was designed in part to displace.

**Pre-Táng *zhìguài* core.** *Sōushén jì* 搜神記 [KR3l0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0099) (Gān Bǎo 干寶, c. 317–336) is the canonical *zhìguài* anthology and the principal source of the genre's iconography of ghosts, foxes, dragons, and karmic retribution. The companion *Sōushén hòujì* 搜神後記 [KR3l0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0100) is conventionally ascribed to Táo Qián 陶潛 (365–427) but is almost certainly Liú-Sòng. *Yìyuàn* 異苑 [KR3l0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0101) (Liú Jìngshū 劉敬叔, Liú-Sòng), *Shíyí jì* 拾遺記 [KR3l0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0098) (Wáng Jiā 王嘉, late-fourth-century; supplemented by Xiāo Qǐ 蕭綺, Liáng), *Xù Qíxié jì* 續齊諧記 [KR3l0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0102) (Wú Jūn 吳均, Liáng), and *Huányuān jì* 還冤記 [KR3l0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0103) (Yán Zhītuī 顏之推, Suí) round out the surviving core. The pseudepigraphic Hàn cluster — *Shényì jīng* 神異經 [KR3l0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0093) (attributed to Dōngfāng Shuò 東方朔), *Hǎinèi shízhōu jì* 海內十洲記 [KR3l0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0094) (id.), *Hàn Wǔ gùshì* 漢武故事 [KR3l0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0095) and *Hàn Wǔdì nèizhuàn* 漢武帝內傳 [KR3l0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0096) (both attributed to Bān Gù 班固), and *Dòngmíng jì* 洞冥記 [KR3l0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0097) (attributed to Guō Xiàn 郭憲) — are uniformly Six-Dynasties or later pseudepigrapha that present a Hàn world reimagined through *fāngshì* and early Daoist mythography.

**The cosmographic and *bówù* tradition.** *Shānhǎi jīng* 山海經 [KR3l0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0090) (with Guō Pú's 郭璞 [276–324] standard commentary) and *Mù Tiānzǐ zhuàn* 穆天子傳 [KR3l0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0092) (id.) are the two Warring-States-to-Hàn cosmographic-cum-marvel survivors that the Sìkù editors placed in this division rather than under geography or history. *Bówù zhì* 博物志 [KR3l0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0123) (Zhāng Huá 張華, 232–300) and its Sòng continuation *Xù bówù zhì* 續博物志 [KR3l0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0128) (Lǐ Shí 李石, twelfth century) define the *bówù* "treatise on universal things" sub-genre. *Wú Rènchén's* 吳任臣 *Shānhǎi jīng guǎngzhù* 山海經廣注 [KR3l0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0091) is the standard early-Qīng (1667) re-annotation. *Xuánzhōng jì* 玄中記 [KR3l0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0160), attributed in part to Guō Pú, survives only in fragments.

**The Táng anecdotal *bǐjì*.** *Cháoyě qiānzài* 朝野僉載 [KR3l0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0003) (Zhāng Zhuó 張鷟, c. 700–730) is the earliest Táng court-and-country miscellany in the division; *Táng xīnyǔ* 唐新語 [KR3l0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0004) (Liú Sù 劉肅, 807) is its *shìshuō*-modelled re-organisation. *Táng guóshǐ bǔ* 唐國史補 [KR3l0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0006) (Lǐ Zhào 李肇, c. 813–825) is the most-cited Mid-Táng anecdotal supplement to the dynastic record. *Cì Liǔshì jiùwén* 次柳氏舊聞 [KR3l0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0005) (Lǐ Déyù 李德裕, 834), *Liú Bīnkè jiāhuà lù* 劉賓客嘉話錄 [KR3l0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0007) (Wéi Xuàn 韋絢, 856 — a record of Liú Yǔxī's 劉禹錫 conversation), *Yīnhuà lù* 因話錄 [KR3l0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0008) (Zhào Lín 趙璘), *Mínghuáng záilù* 明皇雜錄 [KR3l0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0009) (Zhèng Chǔhuì 鄭處誨, 855), *Dà Táng chuánzài* 大唐傳載 [KR3l0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0010), and *Jiàofāng jì* 教坊記 [KR3l0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0011) (Cuī Lìngqīn 崔令欽, on the imperial Music Bureau under Xuánzōng) define the High-Táng / Mid-Táng register. *Sōngchuāng záilù* 松窗雜錄 [KR3l0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0013), *Yúnxī yǒuyì* 雲谿友議* [KR3l0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0014), *Yùquán zǐ* 玉泉子 [KR3l0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0015), and *Yúnxiān záilù* 雲仙雜記 [KR3l0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0016) (a Sòng forgery placed under the name of Féng Zhì 馮贄) carry the genre into the Late Táng and across the early-Sòng forgery boundary. The Five Dynasties — *Táng zhāiyán* 唐摭言 [KR3l0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0017) (Wáng Dìngbǎo 王定保, c. 954, on the Táng examination system), *Zhōngcháo gùshì* 中朝故事 [KR3l0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0018), *Jīnhuá zǐ záibiān* 金華子雜編 [KR3l0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0019), *Kāiyuán Tiānbǎo yíshì* 開元天寶遺事 [KR3l0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0020) (Wáng Rényù 王仁裕, c. 940–956), and *Jiànjiè lù* 鑑誡錄 [KR3l0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0021) (Hé Guāngyuǎn 何光遠, Later Shǔ) — preserve the trauma of the Táng collapse from the perspective of officials who had served under both dynasties.

**The Táng *zhìguài* / *chuánqí* line.** *Jíyì jì* 集異記 [KR3l0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0104) (Xuē Yòngruò 薛用弱, c. 821–824), *Bóyì jì* 博異記 [KR3l0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0105) (Gǔ Shénzǐ 谷神子), *Qiándìng lù* 前定錄 [KR3l0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0107) (Zhōng Lù 鍾輅, 827–835), *Xuānshì zhì* 宣室志 [KR3l0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0110) (Zhāng Dú 張讀), *Jùtán lù* 劇談錄 [KR3l0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0109) (Kāng Pián 康駢, 877–895), *Dùyáng zábiān* 杜陽雜編 [KR3l0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0106) (Sū È 蘇鶚, 886), *Guìyuàn cóngtán* 桂苑叢談 [KR3l0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0108), *Táng quē shǐ* 唐闕史 [KR3l0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0111) (Gāo Yànxiū 高彥休), *Gānzé yáo* 甘澤謠 [KR3l0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0112) (Yuán Jiāo 袁郊), *Kāitiān chuánxìn jì* 開天傳信記 [KR3l0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0113), and *Xù yōuguài lù* 續幽怪錄 [KR3l0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0126) (Lǐ Fùyán 李復言, Bùyǔ 補語 to Niú Sēngrú's 牛僧孺 lost *Xuánguài lù*) constitute the corpus most directly continuous with what modern literary history calls Táng *chuánqí*. *Yǒuyáng zázǔ* 酉陽雜俎 [KR3l0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0125) (Duàn Chéngshì 段成式, c. 853–863) stands apart in scale and erudition — Wilkinson §61.3.11 notes that it would "well be taken for *xiǎoshuō*, although today it is classified as a *biji*" — and is the most-cited Táng miscellany of the entire post-Táng tradition.

**The Northern Sòng *bǐjì* mainstream.** This is the largest cluster in the division. *Sùshuǐ jìwén* 涑水記聞 [KR3l0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0030) (Sīmǎ Guāng 司馬光, c. 1070–1086) records the political-historical anecdotes Sīmǎ collected during *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* compilation but excluded as too informal for the *tōngjiàn* proper. *Guītián lù* 歸田錄 [KR3l0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0032) (Ōuyáng Xiū 歐陽修, 1067) is the canonical retirement-*bǐjì*. *Shéngshuǐ yàntán lù* 澠水燕談錄 [KR3l0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0031) (Wáng Pìzhī 王闢之, c. 1095), *Dōngzhāi jìshì* 東齋記事 [KR3l0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0034) (Fàn Zhèn 范鎮), *Qīngxiāng zájì* 青箱雜記 [KR3l0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0035) (Wú Chǔhòu 吳處厚), *Lóngchuān lüèzhì* 龍川畧志 [KR3l0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0037) (Sū Zhé 蘇轍, 1099), *Hòushān táncóng* 後山談叢 [KR3l0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0038) (Chén Shīdào 陳師道), *Sūngōng tánpǔ* 孫公談圃 [KR3l0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0039) (Sūn Shēng 孫升 / Liú Yánshì 劉延世), *Tányuàn* 談苑 [KR3l0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0040) (Kǒng Píngzhòng 孔平仲), and *Dōngxuān bǐlù* 東軒筆錄 [KR3l0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0048) (Wèi Tài 魏泰, c. 1086–1110, the principal hostile source on Wáng Ānshí's reforms) collectively cover political and personal anecdote across the late eleventh and early twelfth centuries. *Wáng Gǒng's* 王鞏 (fl. 1075–1104) three works — *Jiǎshēn zájì* 甲申雜記 [KR3l0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0042), *Wénjiàn jìnlù* 聞見近錄 [KR3l0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0043), *Suíshǒu zálù* 隨手雜錄 [KR3l0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0044) — form a single Sū Shì-circle trilogy of personal recollection. The Buddhist-monastic register is represented by *Shì Wényíng's* 釋文瑩 two works *Xiāngshān yělù* 湘山野錄 [KR3l0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0045) and *Yùhú yěshǐ* 玉壺野史 [KR3l0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0046). *Hóuqīng lù* 侯鯖錄 [KR3l0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0047) (Zhào Lìngzhì 趙令畤), *Bózhái biān* 泊宅編 [KR3l0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0049) (Fāng Sháo 方勺), *Tiěwéishān cóngtán* 鐵圍山叢談 [KR3l0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0051) (Cài Tāo 蔡絛, son of Cài Jīng 蔡京, written during exile after the Northern-Sòng collapse), and *Mòkè huīxī* 墨客揮犀 [KR3l0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0054) complete the Northern-Sòng corpus.

**The Northern–Southern Sòng transition cluster.** *Wénjiàn lù* 聞見錄 [KR3l0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0066) (Shào Bówēn 邵伯溫, 1132–1134) and its continuation *Wénjiàn hòu lù* 聞見後錄 [KR3l0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0069) (Shào Bó 邵博, fl. 1138) preserve the founding *Lǐxué* circle of Shào Yōng 邵雍 alongside the political record of the late Běi-Sòng. *Qīngbō zázhì* 清波雜志 [KR3l0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0067) (Zhōu Huī 周煇, c. 1192–1194), *Jīlèi biān* 雞肋編 [KR3l0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0068) (Zhuāng Chuò 莊綽, c. 1133–1139), *Mòjì* 默記 [KR3l0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0061) (Wáng Zhì 王銍), *Guòtíng lù* 過庭錄 [KR3l0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0058) (Fàn Gōngchēng 范公偁), *Gāozhāi mànlù* 高齋漫錄 [KR3l0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0060) (Zēng Zào 曾慥), *Bùlǐ kètán* 步里客談 [KR3l0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0071) (Chén Chángfāng 陳長方), and *Běichuāng zhìguǒ lù* 北牕炙輠錄 [KR3l0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0070) (Shī Décāo 施德操) collectively document the trauma of the *Jìngkāng* 靖康 catastrophe and the southern reconstitution.

**The Southern Sòng anecdotal masters.** *Wáng Míngqīng's* 王明清 (b. 1127) trilogy — *Huīchén lù* 揮塵錄 [KR3l0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0062), *Yùzhào xīnzhì* 玉照新志 [KR3l0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0063), *Tóuxiá lù* 投轄錄 [KR3l0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0064) — is the most comprehensive single private record of the Southern Sòng court and is heavily mined by the *Sòngshǐ* compilers. *Tīngshǐ* 桯史 [KR3l0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0072) (Yuè Kē 岳珂, c. 1200–1214), grandson of Yuè Fēi 岳飛, supplies the family-perspective record of the Shàoxīng peace and after. *Dúxǐng zázhì* 獨醒雜志 [KR3l0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0073) (Zēng Mǐnxíng 曾敏行), *Sìcháo wénjiàn lù* 四朝聞見錄 [KR3l0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0075) (Yè Shàowēng 葉紹翁, c. 1225–1235, a key source on the Qìngyuán *dǎngjìn* against Zhū Xī), and *Qíjiù xùwén* 耆舊續聞 [KR3l0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0074) (Chén Hú 陳鵠) round out the High and Late Southern Sòng. *Guǐxīn zázhì* 癸辛雜識 [KR3l0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0076) (Zhōu Mì 周密, c. 1280–1298) and *Suíyǐn mànlù* 隨隱漫錄 [KR3l0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0077) (Chén Shìchóng 陳世崇) are the major Sòng-loyalist records of the Yuán transition. The two great Southern-Sòng *zhìguài* collections — *Hóng Mài's* 洪邁 *Yíjiān zhì jiǎ* 夷堅志甲 [KR3l0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0122) (the surviving *jiǎ* portion of an originally encyclopaedic project) and *Kuíchē zhì* 睽車志 [KR3l0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0121) (Guō Tuàn 郭彖) — extend the Tang *zhìguài* line into the twelfth century, with *Yíjiān zhì* in particular providing some of the richest material on vernacular language change for the period (Wilkinson §6.7, citing *HD* corrections).

**The Yuán cluster.** *Guīqián zhì* 歸潛志 [KR3l0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0079) (Liú Qí 劉祁, 1235–1241) is the canonical record of the Jīn-Yuán transition by an ex-Jīn official; it is widely cited in *Jīnshǐ* compilation. *Shānjū xīnhuà* 山居新話 [KR3l0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0081) (Yáng Yú 楊瑀), *Suìchāng zálù* 遂昌雜錄 [KR3l0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0082) (Zhèng Yuányòu 鄭元祐), *Lèjiāo sīyǔ* 樂郊私語 [KR3l0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0083), *Shānfáng suíbǐ* 山房隨筆 [KR3l0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0080), and *Dōngnán jìwén* 東南紀聞 [KR3l0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0078) survey late-Yuán southern society. *Chuògēng lù* 輟耕錄 [KR3l0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0084) (Táo Zōngyí 陶宗儀, c. 1366–1368, 30 *juǎn*) is the single most influential late-Yuán *bǐjì* and Wilkinson's main example (§53.1, Box 265) of the irreducibly mixed character of the genre: nine subject categories ranging from history (247 entries) and biography (157) to folklore (42) and the supernatural (97).

**The Míng cluster.** *Shuǐdōng rìjì* 水東日記 [KR3l0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0085) (Yè Shèng 葉盛, 1460–1474), *Shūyuán zájì* 菽園雜記 [KR3l0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0086) (Lù Róng 陸容, 1480–1494), *Xiānjìn yífēng* 先進遺風 [KR3l0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0087) (Gěng Dìngxiàng 耿定向 / Máo Zài 毛在), *Gū bù gū lù* 觚不觚錄 [KR3l0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0088) (Wáng Shìzhēn 王世貞, 1580–1590, on the breakdown of Míng institutional culture under Wànlì), and *Yǔlín* 語林 [KR3l0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0089) (Hé Liángjùn 何良俊, 1540–1551, the Míng *shìshuō tǐ* anchor) carry the genre through the dynasty.

**Imperially commissioned *biji xiǎoshuō* and *lèishū*-aligned *zhìguài*.** *Tàipíng guǎngjì* 太平廣記 [KR3l0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0118) (Lǐ Fǎng 李昉 et al., 977–978, 500 *juǎn*) is the foundational imperial compendium of Six-Dynasties-and-Táng *xiǎoshuō*, classified here rather than as a *lèishū* despite its 150-plus subject categories; it preserves c. 7,000 stories drawn from over 500 source-titles, c. 250 of which survive nowhere else (Wilkinson §53.3.1). *Fēnmén gǔjīn lèishì* 分門古今類事 [KR3l0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0119) is its modest twelfth-century successor on a *Tàipíng guǎngjì* topical model.

**The early-Sòng *zhìguài* / *yìrén* corpus.** *Jīshén lù* 稽神錄 [KR3l0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0114) (Xú Xuàn 徐鉉, 916–991, written before he came over to the Sòng from the Southern Táng), *Jiānghuái yìrén lù* 江淮異人錄 [KR3l0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0115) (Wú Shū 吳淑, 947–1002), *Máotíng kèhuà* 茅亭客話 [KR3l0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0116) (Huáng Xiūfù 黃休復), *Kuòyì zhì* 括異志 [KR3l0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0117) (Zhāng Shīzhèng 張師正), *Qīngyì lù* 清異錄 [KR3l0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0127) (Táo Gǔ 陶穀), *Tao-zhū xīnlù* 陶朱新錄 [KR3l0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0120) (Mǎ Chún 馬純), and *Nán Táng jìnshì* 南唐近事 [KR3l0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0022) (Zhèng Wénbǎo 鄭文寶, 977) extend the Táng *zhìguài* line directly into the early Sòng. *Běimèng suǒyán* 北夢瑣言 [KR3l0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0023) (Sūn Guāngxiàn 孫光憲, d. 968) and *Nánbù xīnshū* 南部新書* [KR3l0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0026) (Qián Yì 錢易, 1008–1016) preserve substantial Late-Táng and Five-Dynasties anecdote from a tenth-century perspective.

**The Lǔ Xùn *jíyì* recovery cluster.** Entries [KR3l0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0131)–[KR3l0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0169) (the second layer beyond the WYG *Sìkù*) are fragment-reconstructions, mostly drawn from Lǔ Xùn's *Gǔ xiǎoshuō gōu chén* 古小說鉤沈 (1909–11) and continued in modern compilations: *Yān Dānzǐ* 燕丹子 [KR3l0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0131) (reconstructed from *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* by Sūn Xīngyǎn 孫星衍, 1788); *Míngxiáng jì* 冥祥記 [KR3l0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0132) (Wáng Yǎn 王琰, late-fifth-century Buddhist *zhìguài*); *Gǔjīn shànyán* 古今善言 [KR3l0133](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0133) (Fàn Tài 范泰); *Lièyì zhuàn* 列異傳 [KR3l0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0137) (attributed to Cáo Pī 曹丕 or Zhāng Huá); *Péizǐ yǔlín* 裴子語林 [KR3l0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0135); *Guō zǐ* 郭子 [KR3l0155](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0155) (Guō Chéngzhī 郭澄之); *Sú shuō* 俗說 [KR3l0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0157) (Shěn Yuē 沈約); *Xiǎoshuō* 小說 [KR3l0158](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0158) (Yīn Yún 殷芸, c. 519–529, the first Chinese work explicitly titled "*xiǎoshuō*"); *Qíxié jì* 齊諧記 [KR3l0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0168) (Dōngyáng Wúyí 東陽無疑, Liú-Sòng); *Yōumíng lù* 幽明錄 [KR3l0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0169) (Liú Yìqìng — the second of his three works in this division); *Xuānyàn jì* 宣驗記 [KR3l0151](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0151) (also Liú Yìqìng); *Jí líng jì* 集靈記 [KR3l0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0167) (Yán Zhītuī, paired with his *Huányuān jì*); and a long tail of single-fragment *zhìguài* reconstructions ([KR3l0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0136)–[KR3l0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0166)). These entries are *not* WYG-derived and should be read with the understanding that the surviving fragments are typically a few dozen to a few hundred lines, not full books.

**The *Shìér xiǎomíng lù* trilogy.** [KR3l0170](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0170)–[KR3l0172](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0172) — *Shìér xiǎomíng lù* (Hóng Shì 洪适 / Wáng Zhì 王銍, attribution disputed), *Shìér xiǎomíng lù shíyí* 侍兒小名錄拾遺 (Zhāng Bāngjī 張邦基), and *Xù bǔ Shìér xiǎomíng lù* 續補侍兒小名錄 (Wáng Zhì) — are a Sòng-period micro-genre of records of the personal names of palace-women and serving-maids, an unusual onomastic supplement to the conventional historical record.

**The terminal point: *Liáozhāi zhìyì*.** *Liáozhāi zhìyì* 聊齋誌異 [KR3l0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0130) (Pú Sōnglíng 蒲松齡, c. 1670–1715) is the great *Qīng* literary-Chinese *zhìguài* / *chuánqí* collection, the work that retrospectively recasts the entire pre-modern *zhìguài* tradition into a single literary genealogy. It sits at the chronological terminus of the division and is the most translated of all KR3l texts.

### Important persons

- [劉義慶](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E7%BE%A9%E6%85%B6) — Liú-Sòng prince and patron-compiler of *Shìshuō xīnyǔ* [KR3l0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0002); also credited (probably as patron) with *Yōumíng lù* [KR3l0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0169) and *Xuānyàn jì* [KR3l0151](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0151). The single most consequential figure in the early-medieval anecdotal tradition.
- [劉孝標](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AD%9D%E6%A8%99) — Liáng commentator (462–521) on *Shìshuō xīnyǔ*; his citations preserve a substantial portion of the lost Six-Dynasties biographical corpus.
- [干寶](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B9%B2%E5%AF%B6) — Eastern Jìn *Sōushén jì* [KR3l0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0099) compiler; the canonical *zhìguài* anchor.
- [張華](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E8%8F%AF) — Jìn polymath (232–300), author of *Bówù zhì* [KR3l0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0123); commentator on *Shényì jīng* [KR3l0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0093); attributed (jointly with Cáo Pī) as compiler of *Lièyì zhuàn* [KR3l0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0137).
- [郭璞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E7%92%9E) — Jìn (276–324) commentator on the two foundational cosmographic-marvel works *Shānhǎi jīng* [KR3l0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0090) and *Mù Tiānzǐ zhuàn* [KR3l0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0092); also attributed compilation of *Xuánzhōng jì* [KR3l0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0160).
- [顏之推](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E4%B9%8B%E6%8E%A8) — Suí scholar-official (531–591) and author of *Huányuān jì* [KR3l0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0103) and (in fragments) *Jí líng jì* [KR3l0167](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0167); both are major sources for sixth-century Buddhist *zhìguài*.
- [段成式](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AE%B5%E6%88%90%E5%BC%8F) — Late-Táng (fl. 853–863) author of *Yǒuyáng zázǔ* [KR3l0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0125), the most-cited Táng miscellany of the post-Táng tradition.
- [李昉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%98%89) — Northern-Sòng compiler (925–996) of *Tàipíng guǎngjì* [KR3l0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0118); the principal vector for the survival of Six-Dynasties and Táng *xiǎoshuō*.
- [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) — *Sùshuǐ jìwén* [KR3l0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0030) author; his *bǐjì* preserves the political-historical material his *Zīzhì tōngjiàn* method excluded.
- [歐陽修](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%90%E9%99%BD%E4%BF%AE) — *Guītián lù* [KR3l0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0032) author; the canonical post-retirement *bǐjì*.
- [蘇轍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BD%8D) — Sū-clan member, author of *Lóngchuān lüèzhì* [KR3l0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0037); classed here rather than in his collected works.
- [釋文瑩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E6%96%87%E7%91%A9) — Northern-Sòng monk and author of the paired *Xiāngshān yělù* [KR3l0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0045) and *Yùhú yěshǐ* [KR3l0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0046); the principal monastic-perspective *bǐjì* of the eleventh century.
- [王鞏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%9E%8F) — Sū Shì-circle figure with three works in the division — *Jiǎshēn zájì* [KR3l0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0042), *Wénjiàn jìnlù* [KR3l0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0043), *Suíshǒu zálù* [KR3l0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0044).
- [邵伯溫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E4%BC%AF%E6%BA%AB) and [邵博](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E5%8D%9A) — father and son, authors of *Wénjiàn lù* [KR3l0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0066) and *Wénjiàn hòu lù* [KR3l0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0069) respectively; the standard family-record of the founding *Lǐxué* circle.
- [洪邁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E9%82%81) — Southern-Sòng (1123–1202) compiler of *Yíjiān zhì jiǎ* [KR3l0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0122); the great Sòng *zhìguài* collection and one of the most-cited single sources for twelfth-century vernacular and material culture.
- [周密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E5%AF%86) — Sòng-loyalist compiler of *Guǐxīn zázhì* [KR3l0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0076); the principal Sòng-to-Yuán transition source.
- [岳珂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B2%B3%E7%8F%82) — Yuè Fēi's grandson; author of *Tīngshǐ* [KR3l0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0072).
- [王明清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%98%8E%E6%B8%85) — Author of three Southern-Sòng works *Huīchén lù* [KR3l0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0062), *Yùzhào xīnzhì* [KR3l0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0063), *Tóuxiá lù* [KR3l0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0064) — the most comprehensive single private record of the Southern Sòng court.
- [劉祁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E7%A5%81) — Jīn-Yuán transition author of *Guīqián zhì* [KR3l0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0079); the principal *Jīnshǐ* supplementary source.
- [陶宗儀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%AE%97%E5%84%80) — Late-Yuán (fl. 1360–1368) author of *Chuògēng lù* [KR3l0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0084); Wilkinson's main example (§53.1, Box 265) of the mixed *bǐjì* genre.

### Topics

1. **The instability of *xiǎoshuō* as a category.** The division is the bibliographical residue of a classification problem that pre-modern Chinese taxonomy never solved: a single *bǐjì* routinely mixes anecdote, scholarly note, geographic observation, biographical sketch, and *zhìguài*. Wilkinson §53 frames this as the principal *interpretive* challenge for the reader of any work here. *Chuògēng lù* [KR3l0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0084) is the standard example.

2. **The factual / fictional boundary.** Until the May-Fourth re-purposing of *xiǎoshuō* to mean "fiction" in the European sense, no Chinese editorial tradition required the distinction. The division therefore includes works that are now read as fiction (*Liáozhāi zhìyì* [KR3l0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0130)), works that are now read as history (*Sùshuǐ jìwén* [KR3l0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0030), the Wáng Míngqīng trilogy [KR3l0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0062)–[KR3l0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0064)), and works that resist either reading (the great majority).

3. **The pseudepigraphic Hàn cluster.** *Shényì jīng* [KR3l0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0093), *Hǎinèi shízhōu jì* [KR3l0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0094), *Hàn Wǔ gùshì* [KR3l0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0095), *Hàn Wǔdì nèizhuàn* [KR3l0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0096), *Dòngmíng jì* [KR3l0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0097), and the disputed *Xījīng zájì* [KR3l0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0001) (ascribed to Liú Xīn 劉歆, transmitted by Gě Hóng 葛洪, but a post-Liáng compilation by the criterion of internal evidence) constitute a coherent body of Six-Dynasties pseudepigraphic reimaginings of the Western Hàn world, structured around the *fāngshì* and early Daoist mythography that took shape between the second and the sixth centuries.

4. **The *zhìguài* / *chuánqí* relationship.** The division flattens the modern literary-historical distinction: many Táng works classed as *xiǎoshuō* by the *Sìkù* (the *Jíyì jì* line, [KR3l0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0104)–[KR3l0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0114)) are read in modern literary history as the founding documents of the *chuánqí* genre.

5. **The *shìshuō tǐ* persistence.** The character-appraisal anecdotal mode initiated by *Shìshuō xīnyǔ* [KR3l0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0002) continues to generate works for more than a millennium — *Táng yǔlín* [KR3l0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0055), *Yǔlín* [KR3l0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0089), the lost *Péizǐ yǔlín* [KR3l0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0135) — and Wilkinson (§60.3, citing Qián Nánxiù 2001) counts c. thirty *Shìshuō*-style works between the Táng and the early twentieth century, including two Qīng works titled *Nǚ shìshuō* 女世說.

6. **The *lèishū*-mediated survival of the pre-Táng corpus.** A very large share of the works that would otherwise belong in this division survive only as quotation-fragments in *Tàipíng guǎngjì* [KR3l0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0118), *Yìwén lèijù*, *Tàipíng yùlǎn*, and *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn*. The Lǔ Xùn *jíyì* recovery cluster ([KR3l0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0131)–[KR3l0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0169)) makes this survival mechanism explicit.

7. **The *bǐjì* as a corrective to the Standard Histories.** Wilkinson §53 makes the historiographic case explicitly: "*Biji* often relate anecdotes, gossip, and rumor, all subjects considered unfit for more formal works, but not infrequently essential for social history. They are therefore a useful corrective to the *Histories* and other works of Confucian historiography." The Táng anecdotal cluster ([KR3l0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0003)–[KR3l0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0017)) and the entire Sòng *bǐjì* mainstream are mined heavily by modern social, economic, and institutional historians for precisely this reason.

8. **Vernacular language change.** Several works in the division — *Shìshuō xīnyǔ* [KR3l0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0002) (Six-Dynasties spoken language), *Yǒuyáng zázǔ* [KR3l0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0125) (Mid-Táng colloquial), *Yíjiān zhì jiǎ* [KR3l0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3l/KR3l0122) (Southern-Sòng vernacular) — are principal sources for the diachronic study of spoken Chinese, far in excess of what their classification under *xiǎoshuō* would suggest.

# 楚辭類 (KR4a)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4a 楚辭類 *Chǔ cí lèi* — Collected Works — Songs of Chu](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

`KR4a` is the *Chǔcí* 楚辭 (*Songs of Chu* / *Songs of the South*) subcategory of the Sìkù 集部 (Literature) branch. It is by far the smallest of the *jíbù* subcategories, comprising the anthology itself plus the commentaries and pictorial editions that grew around it. The Sìkù compilers placed *Chǔcí* at the very head of the Literature branch (Wilkinson, *Chinese History: A New Manual*, §30.1, Table 37), reflecting its status as the second great anthology of ancient Chinese verse after the *Shī* 詩 ([KR1h](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/)) and the founding text of the *cífù* 辭賦 tradition. The poems collected — *Lí sāo* 離騷, *Jiǔ gē* 九歌, *Tiān wèn* 天問, *Jiǔ zhāng* 九章, *Yuǎn yóu* 遠遊, *Jiǔ biàn* 九辯, *Zhāo hún* 招魂, *Dà zhāo* 大招, and the rest — emerged from the late Warring-States and Hàn south, took their received seventeen-section shape under [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8) in the second century CE, and have been continuously annotated since.

The chronological span of the division is exceptional. The earliest dateable layer is the late-fourth-century BCE work conventionally ascribed to [屈原](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B1%88%E5%8E%9F); the latest piece is the 1782–1784 imperial illustrated edition [KR4a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0006). Two commentarial currents structure the tradition: the Hàn-Sòng philological line of [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8)'s *Zhāng jù* ([KR4a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0002)) and [洪興祖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E8%88%88%E7%A5%96)'s *Bǔ zhù* ([KR4a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0003)), which preserves and extends the loyal-minister-in-exile reading inherited from Sīmǎ Qiān; and the Southern Sòng Neo-Confucian re-reading of [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) ([KR4a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0004), [KR4a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0008), [KR4a0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0009)), which restructured the canon, applied the *xìng / bǐ / fù* 興比賦 categories of the *Máo shī* commentary, and severely pruned what it judged shallow. Qīng *kǎozhèng* 考證 work — best represented in this division by [蔣驥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E9%A9%A5)'s topographic-biographical commentary ([KR4a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0007)) — and Qián-lóng-court pictorial scholarship ([KR4a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0006)) round out the inherited tradition. Wú Rénjié's *Lí sāo cǎo mù shū* ([KR4a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0005)) opens a third, *bówù* 博物 (broad-learning-of-things) strand parallel to the line of Lù Jī 陸璣 on the *Shī*.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The base text.** *Chǔ cí* 楚辭 [KR4a0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0001) — the seventeen-section anthology in TLS base, the textual ground on which everything else in the division builds.
- **Hàn-Sòng commentarial cluster.** *Chǔ cí zhāng jù* 楚辭章句 [KR4a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0002) by [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8) is the earliest surviving complete commentary and the source of the seventeen-section canon; *Chǔ cí bǔ zhù* 楚詞補注 [KR4a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0003) by [洪興祖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E8%88%88%E7%A5%96) is the principal medium of its transmission, reproducing Wáng Yì's commentary in full and adding *bǔyuē* 補曰 notes from a long collation history. Read together, these two works are the platform of the philological tradition; modern critical editions still take Hóng's recension as their base.
- **The Zhū Xī trilogy.** *Chǔ cí jí zhù* 楚辭集注 [KR4a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0004), *Chǔ cí biàn zhèng* 楚辭辯證 [KR4a0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0009), and *Chǔ cí hòu yǔ* 楚辭後語 [KR4a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0008) — the *Jí zhù* fixes a new eight-juan canon (twenty-five Qū-Yuán pieces as *Lí sāo* core + sixteen later pieces as *Xù lí sāo*), the *Biàn zhèng* is its passage-by-passage polemic against Wáng Yì and Hóng Xīngzǔ, and the *Hòu yǔ* extends the *sāo* lineage forward through Hàn, Wèi-Jìn, Táng, and Northern Sòng. Written in [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9)'s last decade, partly under the 1196 *dàoxué* 道學 ban, the trilogy became the orthodox interpretive vocabulary of the *Chǔ cí* in Yuán, Míng, Korean, and Japanese reception.
- **Natural history.** *Lí sāo cǎo mù shū* 離騷草木疏 [KR4a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0005) by [吳仁傑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E4%BB%81%E5%82%91) is the principal botanical commentary, modeled on Lù Jī's *Máo shī cǎo mù niǎo shòu chóng yú shū* but methodologically distinctive in taking the *Shān hǎi jīng* 山海經 as its decisive authority for *Lí sāo* flora.
- **Qīng commentary.** *Shāndàigé zhù Chǔ cí* 山帶閣註楚辭 [KR4a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0007) by [蔣驥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E9%A9%A5) integrates biography and topography into the gloss, anchoring every section to a five-map reconstruction of Qū Yuán's exile route; the appended *Yú lùn* 餘論 and *Shuō yùn* 說韻 carry his rhyme-and-disputation work. The Sìkù tíyào treats it as transitional from late-Kāng-xī commentary to mature Qián-Jiā *kǎojù* 考據.
- **Pictorial.** *Qīndìng bǔhuì Xiāo Yúncóng Lísāo quántú* 欽定補繪蕭雲從離騷全圖 [KR4a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0006) — the surviving sixty-four illustrations of [蕭雲從](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%95%AD%E9%9B%B2%E5%BE%9E)'s 1645 *yímín* 遺民 *Lí sāo tú*, supplemented by ninety-one new images executed by Mén Yìngzhào 門應兆 and the court painters in 1782–1784 in conscious imitation of Lǐ Gōnglín 李公麟's *Jiǔ gē tú* — is the unique pictorial entry in the Sìkù *Chǔcí* subsection.

### Important persons

- [屈原](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B1%88%E5%8E%9F) (Qū Yuán, conventionally ca. 343–278 BCE; attributed author): the figure around whom the anthology coalesced and to whom orthodox tradition since Sīmǎ Qiān (*Shǐ jì* 84) ascribes *Lí sāo*, *Tiān wèn*, the *Jiǔ zhāng* group, and most of *Jiǔ gē*. Modern scholarship treats this attribution as a Hàn editorial construction; for the present division he is the canonical authorial reference point.
- [宋玉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E7%8E%89) (Sòng Yù, 3rd c. BCE; attributed author): the canonical second voice, to whom [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8) assigned *Jiǔ biàn* and *Zhāo hún*.
- [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8) (Wáng Yì, fl. 89–158): the foundational figure of the division. His *Chǔ cí zhāng jù* ([KR4a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0002)) fixed the seventeen-section canon, supplied the first complete commentary, and stabilized the loyal-minister-in-exile reading.
- [洪興祖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E8%88%88%E7%A5%96) (Hóng Xīngzǔ, 1090–1155): the Sòng commentator whose *Bǔ zhù* ([KR4a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0003)) is the principal medium through which [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8)'s text has been transmitted from the twelfth century onward. Officially suppressed by Qín Huì's 秦檜 faction but circulated privately.
- [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) (Zhū Xī, 1130–1200): the dominant Sòng Neo-Confucian re-reader of the corpus, author of the trilogy [KR4a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0004) / [KR4a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0008) / [KR4a0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0009) that restructured the canon along *xìng / bǐ / fù* lines.
- [吳仁傑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E4%BB%81%E5%82%91) (Wú Rénjié, b. 1137): Sòng natural historian whose *Lí sāo cǎo mù shū* ([KR4a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0005)) is the standard botanical commentary; also the author of *Yì*-classics work in [KR1a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/).
- [蕭雲從](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%95%AD%E9%9B%B2%E5%BE%9E) (Xiāo Yúncóng, 1596–1673): *yímín* painter whose 1645 *Lí sāo tú* survives partially in [KR4a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0006).
- [蔣驥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E9%A9%A5) (Jiǎng Jì, fl. 1707–1727): Qīng author of [KR4a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0007), whose itinerary-and-topography method is still cited as a reference point in modern *Chǔcí* studies. (Date discrepancy: catalog meta gives the *fl.* window, CBDB suggests b. 1714; see person note.)

### Topics

- **Political allegory vs. ritual/shamanic reading.** The dominant interpretive dichotomy of the entire commentarial tradition. The orthodox reading — Qū Yuán as the loyal slandered minister, the *Lí sāo* as veiled political protest — runs from Sīmǎ Qiān through [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8), [洪興祖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E8%88%88%E7%A5%96), and [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) and was elaborated through every Yuán-Míng-Qīng commentary. Twentieth-century scholarship, building on the figure of the *wū* 巫, has read *Jiǔ gē* and *Zhāo hún* as séance liturgies; Wilkinson §58.6.3.2 notes the absence of any agreement on the form Chǔ shamanism actually took.
- **The construction of "Qū Yuán."** Modern scholarship (Du 2019, Schneider 2020) treats [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8)'s *Zhāng jù* ([KR4a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0002)) as the principal site at which the figure of Qū Yuán was constructed: Wáng's sectional prefaces did the editorial work that grounded the anthology around a single biographical hero. The *Chǔcí* tradition is therefore inseparable from a long Chinese myth of loyalty and dissent.
- **The *xìng / bǐ / fù* classification.** [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9)'s decision in [KR4a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0004) to label every *zhāng* 章 as *xìng* 興, *bǐ* 比, or *fù* 賦 — categories borrowed from the *Máo shī zhuàn* 毛詩傳 ([KR1h](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/)) — projects a unified Confucian poetics across the *Shī* and the *Chǔ cí*. The move was polemic: by deleting *Qī jiàn*, *Jiǔ huái*, *Jiǔ tàn*, and *Jiǔ sī* from the seventeen-section canon and admitting Jiǎ Yì's 賈誼 *fù* and Yáng Xióng's 揚雄 *Fǎn sāo* 反騷 (the last as a polemic foil), Zhū tilted the anthology decisively toward the loyalist-allegorical reading.
- **Section-order and the placement of prefaces.** The transmitted *Zhāng jù* is not [王逸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%80%B8)'s autograph: as the Sìkù tíyào to [KR4a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0002) notes, both the section order and the placement of the *xù* 序 prefaces were rearranged in the Sòng, partly by Chén Shuōzhī 陳說之 in 1032 and partly by unknown later hands. The *Gǔwén Chǔcí Shìwén* 古文楚辭釋文 preserved by Lù Démíng 陸德明 attests an alternative order beginning with *Jiǔ biàn*. This Hóng Xīngzǔ–era debate is recovered in the front matter of [KR4a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0002) and in [KR4a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0003).
- **Natural-historical commentary.** The *Cǎo mù shū* ([KR4a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0005)) inaugurates a *bówù* strand within *Chǔcí* scholarship — close in method to Lù Jī's *Máo shī cǎo mù shū* and Luó Yuàn's *Ěr yǎ yì*, controversial for grounding the botanical glosses in the *Shān hǎi jīng*, and prefiguring Qīng natural-historical philology. The *xiāng cǎo* 香草 (fragrant-plant) catalog of the imperial pictorial edition ([KR4a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0006)) is the visual counterpart.
- **Topography and biographical reconstruction.** [蔣驥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E9%A9%A5)'s *Shāndàigé zhù* ([KR4a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0007)) introduces a systematic itinerary reconstruction: every section is dated and located by reference to a five-map model of Qū Yuán's exile. Even where modern *Chǔcí* scholarship rejects individual datings, the maps are still cited.
- **Ancient rhyme.** The *Zhāng jù* preserves rhymed sequences in its own commentary (the Sìkù tíyào to [KR4a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0002) singles them out: e.g. *哀憤結縎, 慮煩冤也*); these are useful Eastern-Hàn rhyme evidence that the *gǔyùn* 古韻 tradition from Wú Yù 吳棫 onward never exploited. [蔣驥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E9%A9%A5)'s *Shuō yùn* 說韻 ([KR4a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0007)) is the division's standalone treatise on *Chǔcí* rhyme; its conflation of *zìmǔ* 字母 (Indic-derived initials) with native *shēngyùn* 聲韻 (ancient rhymes) was already a fair Qián-Jiā philological complaint by the time of the Sìkù tíyào.
- **Pictorial *Chǔcí*.** [蕭雲從](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%95%AD%E9%9B%B2%E5%BE%9E)'s 1645 *Lí sāo tú*, taken up by the Qiánlóng court as [KR4a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4a/KR4a0006), is one of the division's most political objects: an *yímín* lament for the fallen Míng, "completed" by court painters in 1782–84 and reframed as an imperially-validated reading.

# 別集類漢六朝 (KR4b)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4b 別集類一 *Bié-jí lèi yī* — Collected Writings — Individual Collections, Hàn through Suí](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR4b sits inside `KR4` 集部 (*jíbù*, Collected Writings) as the first of the four chronological bands into which the *Sìkù quánshū* sub-divides the *biéjí lèi* 別集類 — the collected writings of named individuals, as distinct from anthologies (*zǒngjí* 總集), *cí*-and-*qǔ* (*cíqǔ lèi* 詞曲類), and the *Chǔcí* group. The nineteen works gathered here run from the Western Hàn polymath Yáng Xióng 揚雄 (53 BCE – 18 CE) to the Liáng-Chén stylist Xú Líng 徐陵 (507–583), spanning roughly six centuries and the entire arc the *Sìkù* compilers designated as the formative period of the Chinese authorial *jí*: late-Hàn classicists, the *Jiànān* 建安 generation, the *Zhúlín qī xián* 竹林七賢 / *Wèi-Jìn* counterculture, the southern *Èr Lù* 二陸, the Eastern-Jìn / Liú-Sòng eremitic and *yuèfǔ* lines, the *Yǒngmíng* / *gōngtǐ* 永明–宮體 prosodists of the Southern Qí and Liáng, and the great Liáng / Northern-Zhōu *parallel-prose* (*piántǐ* 駢體) masters who fed directly into the Táng. The Suí is represented only by Yǔ Xìn's 庾信 final year (the *Xīn Chéng bēi wén* 辛成碑文 reburial of 581 places his last attested composition in the new dynasty); no native Suí *jí* appears in the division.

The defining textual fact for this band — flagged in almost every per-text *tíyào* — is that **scarcely any of the early collections survives in anything like its Hàn-to-Liáng form**. Wilkinson §61.3.10 records that even by the Suí the early *biéjí* corpus had been reduced to about 34 securely attested collections, against just under 1,000 known by title for the Táng (Tāo and Lǐ 2001); for the Sòng *Wén xiàn tōng kǎo* and the *Sìkù*, the situation upstream of the Sòng is more attrition than transmission. The *juǎn*-counts in *Suíshū jīngjí zhì*, the two *Tángshū yìwén zhì*, *Chóng wén zǒng mù*, and Chén Zhènsūn's *Shū lù jiě tí* document a near-continuous loss curve: Yáng Xióng's 5-*juǎn* original disappears in the Sòng and is replaced by a Wànlì re-aggregation (1595) of forty-some pieces gleaned from the *Hànshū*, *Gǔwén yuàn*, and *lèishū*; Kǒng Róng's 9–10 *juǎn* perish in the Sòng, leaving a Míng patchwork of 44 substantive fragments; Cài Yōng's Liáng 20-*juǎn* drops to a 10-*juǎn* Sòng version and finally a Yōngzhèng-era Chénliú-cut 6-*juǎn* recension; Cáo Zhí's 30-*juǎn* Suí text is the ancestor of a 1213 Sòng print whose 210 pieces in fact *over-shoot* the Wèi-court enumeration of "over a hundred" by absorbing *lèishū* fragments and music-bureau adjustments. The reader of KR4b is therefore never handling a Hàn or Wèi book directly — every text in the division is a Sòng-Míng-Qīng *reconstruction*, and the *tíyào* tradition (carried in this division almost exclusively by Jì Yún 紀昀, Lù Xīxióng 陸錫熊, Sūn Shìyì 孫士毅, and Lù Fèichí 陸費墀 between 1778 and 1781) does its most consequential work by tracking which layer of the editorial palimpsest each piece belongs to. Wilkinson §27.6 frames the same point from the other side: the late-Sòng / Míng *Bǎi sān jiā jí* 百三家集 of Zhāng Pǔ 張溥 and the parallel Wànlì *cǎijìn* prints are the principal recoverable filter through which Hàn-Wèi-Six-Dynasties writing reaches the modern reader.

### Important texts and text clusters

The division resolves into a small number of recognizable clusters, each of which crystallizes a moment in the long arc from Hàn classicism to Táng prosody.

- **Hàn classicists.** *Yáng Zǐyún jí* 揚子雲集 [KR4b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0001) — the Wànlì Zhèng Pǔ 鄭樸 re-aggregation of Yáng Xióng's prose, *fù*, and three philosophical treatises, also the locus of the *Sìkù*'s major editorial defense of the *Hànshū* "*Mǎng dàfū* 莽大夫" verdict against Jiāo Hóng's 焦竑 chronological rehabilitation. *Cài Zhōngláng jí* 蔡中郎集 [KR4b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0002) — the surviving signature of the supervisor of the *Xīpíng shí jīng* 熹平石經, transmitted in a Yōngzhèng Chénliú re-edition partial to its native son. *Kǒng Běihǎi jí* 孔北海集 [KR4b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0003) — a one-*juǎn* Míng reconstruction preserving the satirical voice that cost Kǒng Róng his life under Cáo Cāo.
- **Jiànān 建安 and Wèi.** *Cáo Zǐjiàn jí* 曹子建集 [KR4b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0004) — Sòng Jiādìng 6 (1213) print, the cornerstone of the *Jiànān* canon and the principal source for the *Luò shén fù* 洛神賦, *Qī āi* 七哀, *Zèng Bái Mǎ Wáng Biāo* 贈白馬王彪, and the seven *Zá shī* 雜詩. *Xí Zhōngsǎn jí* 嵇中散集 [KR4b0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0005) — the foundational corpus of *mínglǐ* 名理 argument (*Shēng wú āi lè lùn* 聲無哀樂論, *Yǎng shēng lùn* 養生論, *Shì sī lùn* 釋私論) and the two *jué jiāo shū* 絕交書 that secured Xí Kāng's iconic refusal of Wèi-Jìn court compromise.
- **Western Jìn — the *Èr Lù* 二陸.** *Lù Shìhéng wén jí* 陸士衡文集 [KR4b0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0006) and *Lù Shìlóng wén jí* 陸士龍文集 [KR4b0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0007) — Xú Mínzhān's 徐民瞻 joint Sòng Qìngyuán 6 (1200) *Jìn èr jùn wén jí* 晉二俊文集, anchoring the *Wén fù* 文賦 (the first systematic *fù* on the writing process) and Lù Yún's extraordinary correspondence with his brother on the drafting of that very text — the most intimate compositional document in early-medieval Chinese letters.
- **Eastern Jìn — Táo Qián 陶潛.** *Táo Yuānmíng jí* 陶淵明集 [KR4b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0008) — the Qiánlóng *Sìkù* eight-*juǎn* re-edition that, on explicit imperial endorsement, strips the *Wǔ xiào zhuàn* 五孝傳 and *Sìbā mù* 四八目 as Northern-Qí forgeries planted by Yáng Xiūzhī 陽休之 and restores a putatively Xiāo-Tǒng-original division. *Jiānzhù Táo Yuānmíng jí* 箋註陶淵明集 [KR4b0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0009) — the late-Sòng / Yuán Lǐ Gōnghuàn 李公煥 *jiānzhù* preserved in the SBCK as the Yuán *Cuìyánjīngshè* 翠巖精舍 cut, retaining the disputed paratexts and serving as the principal source for the Sòng-Yuán reception (Sū Shì, Huáng Tíngjiān) that canonized the *Guī qù lái cí* 歸去來辭 and *Táo huā yuán jì* 桃花源記. The pairing of these two volumes is the single most instructive editorial dossier in the division.
- **Wǔgōng curiosity.** *Xuánjī tú shī dú fǎ* 璇璣圖詩讀法 [KR4b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0010) — Kāng Wànmín 康萬民's late-Wànlì exegesis of the Former-Qín *huíwén* 回文 brocade-poem attributed to Sū Huì 蘇蕙, the canonical exemplar of constraint-based composition in the Chinese tradition; classed in *biéjí* on the strength of Sū Huì's putative authorship.
- **Liú-Sòng / Yuán-Jiā 元嘉.** *Bào Míngyuǎn jí* 鮑明遠集 [KR4b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0011) — the Yú Yán 虞炎 Southern-Qí recension preserved in a Míng *Zhèngdé* 5 (1510) Zhū Yìngdēng 朱應登 print, foundational for the seven-syllable *yuèfǔ* line (*Nǐ Xíng lù nán* 擬行路難) and the great ruins-*fù* *Wú chéng fù* 蕪城賦.
- **Southern Qí *Yǒngmíng tǐ* 永明體.** *Xiè Xuānchéng jí* 謝宣城集 [KR4b0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0012) — Lóu Zhào's 樓炤 Shàoxīng 28 (1158) cut, the five *fù*-and-*shī juǎn* surviving from the original ten (the prose half having been editorially discarded as "matters of a declining age"); the principal witness to the prosodic experiments that prepared Táng *jìntǐ shī* 近體詩.
- **Liáng court literature.** *Zhāomíng tàizǐ jí* 昭明太子集 [KR4b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0013) — Xiāo Tǒng's 蕭統 own collection, a Míng aggregation whose textual integrity the *Sìkù tíyào* damages by identifying five poems as in fact by *Liáng Jiǎnwéndì* 簡文帝 (Xiāo Gāng) misattributed under the homonymous "*tàizǐ*" title. *Hé Shuǐbù jí* 何水部集 [KR4b0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0014) — the spare one-*juǎn* survival of the *Yǒngmíng* second-wave miniaturist whom Dù Fǔ 杜甫 invoked at every opportunity as a stylistic forebear. *Jiāng Wéntōng jí* 江文通集 [KR4b0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0015) and *Liáng Jiāng Wéntōng wén jí* 梁江文通文集 [KR4b0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0016) — twin recensions (a *Sìkù*-WYG four-*juǎn* Liáng Bīn 梁賓 collation of 1758 against an SBCK ten-*juǎn* Yè Shùlián 葉樹廉 conservative edition) of Jiāng Yān's writings, source of *Hèn fù* 恨賦, *Bié fù* 別賦, and the *Zá tǐ shī* 雜體詩 imitations.
- **Liáng–Northern-Zhōu *parallel-prose* masters.** *Yǔ Kāifǔ jí jiānzhù* 庾開府集箋註 [KR4b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0017) and *Yǔ Zǐshān jí* 庾子山集 [KR4b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0018) — the paired Kāngxī commentaries on Yǔ Xìn 庾信 (Wú Zhàoyí 吳兆宜's pioneering effort, and Ní Fán's 倪璠 1689 redo with the first systematic *niánpǔ* 年譜 and the *Wén yuàn yīng huá*–based transfer of two stelae to Yáng Jiōng 楊炯), centered on the *Āi Jiāngnán fù* 哀江南賢. *Xú Xiàomù jí jiānzhù* 徐孝穆集箋注 [KR4b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0019) — Wú Zhàoyí's *jiānzhù* (completed by Xú Wénbǐng 徐文炳) on Yǔ Xìn's literary twin Xú Líng 徐陵, including the *Yùtái xīnyǒng xù* 玉臺新詠序 — the foundational document of the *gōngtǐ* 宮體 aesthetic. Together with the *Yǔ Xìn* pair, this volume closes the division on the threshold of the Táng *sìliù* 四六 tradition.

### Topics

- **Reconstructed vs. transmitted text.** Every Hàn and early-Wèi collection in the division is a Sòng-Míng-Qīng reconstruction; the *biéjí* category here is therefore as much about *editorial archaeology* as about authorship. The signature philological move — exposing a re-editing layer via tell-tale graphic substitutions (e.g., *zhào* 照 / *zhāo* 昭 in [KR4b0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0011), the Wǔ Zétiān taboo), citation-introduction "*yuē* 曰" wrongly absorbed into the text (the Cáo Zhí *Yáo què fù* and *Biān fú fù*), or *jí zuò …* 集作 cross-reference glosses that betray a derivative recension — is the *Sìkù tíyào*'s recurring contribution.
- **Forgery, attribution, and the limits of canon.** The *Wǔ xiào zhuàn* / *Sìbā mù* deletion in [KR4b0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0008), the *Jǐn dài shū* and *yīng chū gǔ* anachronism in [KR4b0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0013), the *Xuánjī tú* Wǔ-Zétiān preface in [KR4b0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0010), the three Cáo-Cāo-praising six-syllable poems attributed to Kǒng Róng in [KR4b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0003), and the transfer of two *mùzhì* from Yǔ Xìn to Yáng Jiōng in [KR4b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0018) — all these establish a connected dossier on how the *Sìkù* compilers handled forgery, dating-by-anachronism, and homonym-driven misattribution.
- **From four-character verse to seven-character *yuèfǔ* to *gōngtǐ* / *Yǒngmíng* prosody.** The diachronic backbone of the division traces the development of poetic line: Yáng Xióng's *fù* and *zhēn* → the *Jiànān* four-and-five-character poets ([KR4b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0003), [KR4b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0004), [KR4b0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0005)) → Cáo Zhí's transitional five-character lyric → Lù Jī's *Wén fù*-anchored five-character imitations → Táo Qián's four-and-five-character pastoral → Bào Zhào's *Nǐ Xíng lù nán* seven-character *yuèfǔ* → Xiè Tiǎo's and Hé Xùn's tonal-rule poems → the *gōngtǐ* of Xú Líng and the late Yǔ Xìn's *Āi Jiāngnán fù*. Almost every signal innovation in pre-Táng prosody can be located on a single *jí* in this division.
- **Parallel prose (*piántǐ wén* 駢體文 / *sìliù wén* 四六文).** The other diachronic axis runs from Cài Yōng's stelae through Lù Jī's *fù* to Jiāng Yān's *Hèn-Bié* tradition and culminates in the *Xú-Yǔ tǐ* 徐庾體 of [KR4b0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0017) / [KR4b0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0018) / [KR4b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0019) — the immediate ancestor of the Táng *Sì jié* 四傑 and the canonical Táng *sìliù*.
- **Southern and northern voices.** The division registers the long migration of southern (Wú, Qí, Liáng, Chén) literary prestige into the unified northern court order — the *Èr Lù* 's move to Luòyáng, Yǔ Xìn's and Xú Líng's diplomatic captures by the Wèi and the Qí. Wilkinson §27 notes this as the formative period for the long-term southern colonization of court literary aesthetics, an arc this division documents in editorial detail.
- **Reception and the formation of authorial personae.** The Sòng-Yuán reception layers (Sū Shì and Huáng Tíngjiān on Táo Qián; Lǐ Bái on Xiè Tiǎo; Dù Fǔ on Hé Xùn and Yǔ Xìn) are repeatedly carried forward by the editorial apparatus itself — preserved as *zǒng lùn* 總論 prefatory matter or worked into the *jiānzhù* — so that the persona of each author is in part the deposit of his later canonization. The division is therefore also a small archive of medieval-into-Sòng *reception* history.

### Timeline

- **c. 18 CE — *Yáng Zǐyún jí* 揚子雲集 [KR4b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0001)** — the Hàn writings of [揚雄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%9A%E9%9B%84); collection itself is the Wànlì 1595 Zhèng Pǔ re-aggregation, dated bracket of the recension, but the contents anchor the division's Western-Hàn floor.
- **c. 192 — *Cài Zhōngláng jí* 蔡中郎集 [KR4b0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0002)** — at the death of [蔡邕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E9%82%95); transmitted via successive recensions down to the Yōngzhèng-era (1723–1735) Chénliú cut.
- **c. 208 — *Kǒng Běihǎi jí* 孔北海集 [KR4b0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0003)** — at the death of [孔融](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E8%9E%8D); surviving 44-piece Míng aggregation (compiled c. 1500–1644).
- **c. 232 — *Cáo Zǐjiàn jí* 曹子建集 [KR4b0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4b/KR4b0004)** — at the death of [曹植](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%B9%E6%A4%8D); received form is the Sòng Jiādìng 6 (1213) print, with 210 Sòng-aggregated pieces.

# 別集類唐 (KR4c)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4c 別集類·唐五代 *Biéjí lèi · Táng Wǔdài* — Collected Works — Individual Writers of the Tang and Five Dynasties](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR4c sits inside the Sìkù *jíbù* 集部 *biéjí lèi* 別集類 (Collections → individual collected works), which the *Sìkù quánshū zǒngmù* arranges chronologically. KR4c is the **Tang and Five Dynasties** segment — the *biéjí* of named individual writers active between the early seventh century (Wáng Jì 王績, d. 644) and the close of the *Wǔdài* tenth century (Shì Qíjǐ 釋齊己's *Báilián jí*, prefaced 938; Dù Guāngtíng 杜光庭's *Guǎngchéng jí*, *fl.* 901–933). It is the largest single dynastic block of *biéjí* in the entire Kanripo corpus, reflecting the Sìkù compilers' inheritance of just under a thousand recorded Tang *biéjí* titles (of which roughly a quarter survived to the eighteenth century) — see Wilkinson, *Chinese History: A New Manual*, §61.3.10 for the survival figures, and §30.4 for the *biéjí* form generally.

The division reads in two registers at once. Its primary axis is the conventional periodization of Tang poetry into 初唐 (early), 盛唐 (high), 中唐 (mid), and 晚唐 (late) — the four-stage canon codified in Yán Yǔ's 嚴羽 *Cānglàng shīhuà* and naturalized into every late-imperial anthology — together with the *Wǔdài* tail. Its secondary axis is the Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng *commentary apparatus* on the canonical Tang masters: roughly thirty of the 113 KR4c entries are not Tang autographs at all but later philological / annotated editions, especially the Sòng *jízhù* and Qīng *xiángzhù* productions on Dù Fǔ, Lǐ Bái, Hán Yù, Liǔ Zōngyuán, Wáng Wéi, Lǐ Shāngyǐn, Wēn Tíngyún, and Lǐ Hè. The division is therefore as much a record of how the Tang was *read* by the Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng tradition as it is a record of Tang writing itself. For the Wilkinson framing of the literary corpus see §54 (Tang literature), which identifies Wáng Wéi, Dù Fǔ, Lǐ Bái, and Bái Jūyì as the High-Tang core and frames Hán Yù-Liǔ Zōngyuán as the *gǔwén* anchor.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The Four Outstanding Ones of the early Tang (初唐四傑)** — [KR4c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0003) *Wáng Zǐān jí* (Wáng Bó), [KR4c0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0004) *Yíngchuān jí* (Yáng Jiǒng), [KR4c0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0005) *Lú Shēngzhī jí* (Lú Zhàolín), and [KR4c0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0006)–[KR4c0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0007) (Luò Bīnwáng). With [KR4c0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0001) *Dōnggāo zǐ jí* (Wáng Jì), [KR4c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0008) *Chén Shíyí jí* (Chén Zǐáng), [KR4c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0009) *Zhāng Yāngōng jí* (Zhāng Shuō), [KR4c0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0010) *Lǐ Běihǎi jí* (Lǐ Yōng), and [KR4c0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0093) *Sòng Zhīwèn jí*, these form the early-Tang cluster whose stylistic transition from *liùcháo* ornament to mature regulated verse is the conventional point of departure for the High Tang.
- **The High-Tang core (盛唐)** — [KR4c0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0011) *Qǔjiāng jí* (Zhāng Jiǔlíng), [KR4c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0012) *Lǐ Tàibái wén jí* (Lǐ Bái), [KR4c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0015) / [KR4c0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0017) / [KR4c0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0018) / [KR4c0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0020) (the principal annotated editions of Dù Fǔ), [KR4c0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0021) / [KR4c0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0022) (annotated Wáng Wéi), [KR4c0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0023) *Gāo Chángshì jí* (Gāo Shì), [KR4c0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0024) *Cháng Jiàn shī*, [KR4c0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0025) *Mèng Hàorán jí*, [KR4c0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0026) *Chǔ Guāngxī shī jí*, [KR4c0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0029) *Cén Jiāzhōu shī* (Cén Shēn). The four named pillars of High-Tang verse — Wáng Wéi, Mèng Hàorán, Lǐ Bái, Dù Fǔ — are the canonical anchor; Gāo Shì and Cén Shēn carry the *biānsài* 邊塞 (frontier) sub-style.

- **The Korean Tang-resident** — [KR4c0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0100) *Guìyuàn bǐgēng jí* (Chǒe Ch'iwǒn 崔致遠), the Silla aristocrat-turned-Tang *jìnshì* whose collected *Yángzhōu* staff correspondence is the most important Tang-period East Asian diplomatic literary corpus.

### Important persons

- [李白](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E7%99%BD) — the supreme High-Tang lyricist; the *Lǐ-Dù* pairing with [杜甫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E7%94%AB) anchors the High-Tang canon.
- [杜甫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E7%94%AB) — the *shī shèng* 詩聖, the dense-textured High-Tang corpus that absorbed the entire later commentary tradition.
- [王維](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%B6%AD) — the *shānshuǐ tiányuán* master, the *Wáng-Mèng* pair with [孟浩然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E6%B5%A9%E7%84%B6).
- [白居易](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%99%BD%E5%B1%85%E6%98%93) — the *Yuán Bái* social-realist core; the most widely circulated Tang poet during his own lifetime, and the East Asian (Japanese Heian, Koryŏ) canonical Tang voice.
- [元稹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E7%A8%B9) — Bái's lifelong literary partner; author of the *Yīngyīng zhuàn* 鶯鶯傳 and the 1812 *xīn yuèfǔ* manifesto.
- [韓愈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%93%E6%84%88) — leader of the Tang *gǔwén* movement; the most heavily-commentated Tang prose corpus.
- [柳宗元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%B3%E5%AE%97%E5%85%83) — Hán Yù's *gǔwén* partner and equally heavily-commentated.
- [陳子昂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%AD%90%E6%98%82) — author of the *Gǎn yù* cycle, the conventional founder of the High-Tang *fùgǔ* program.
- [張九齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E4%B9%9D%E9%BD%A1) — the *Kāiyuán* *zǎixiàng* whose *Gǎn yù* cycle continues Chén Zǐáng's lineage and feeds directly into Lǐ Bái's *Gǔ fēng*.
- [孟浩然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E6%B5%A9%E7%84%B6) — the *Xiāngyáng* hermit-poet, the *Wáng-Mèng* counterpart to Wáng Wéi.
- [韋應物](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%8B%E6%87%89%E7%89%A9) — *Wéi Sūzhōu*, the *Táo-Wéi* pair with Táo Qián, principal post-rebellion contemplative-landscape voice.
- [杜牧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E7%89%A7) — the *Wǎn Táng* prose-and-verse master; the *Zuì yán* on the *fānzhèn* crisis.
- [李商隱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%95%86%E9%9A%B1) — Dù Mù's *Wǎn Táng* counterpart, the *wútí* lyricist, principal model of the Northern-Sòng *Xīkūn tǐ*.
- [孟郊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E9%83%8A) / [賈島](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B3%88%E5%B3%B6) / [李賀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E8%B3%80) / [盧仝](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9B%A7%E4%BB%9D) — the *Hán-Mèng* difficult-bitter school of late-mid-Tang verse.
- [釋皎然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E7%9A%8E%E7%84%B6) — *Dàlì* poet-monk and theorist (*Shī shì* 詩式); the bridge between High-Tang practice and late-Tang critical theory.
- [釋寒山](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E5%AF%92%E5%B1%B1) / [釋貫休](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E8%B2%AB%E4%BC%91) / [釋齊己](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E9%BD%8A%E5%B7%B1) — the three canonical Tang monk-poets, foundational for the Sòng *Chán* poetic tradition and (for Hánshān) for twentieth-century Anglophone reception.
- [陸贄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E8%B4%84) — the supreme *Hànlínyuàn* drafter, the model for all Sòng official-document prose.
- [司空圖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E7%A9%BA%E5%9C%96) — late-Tang martyr-recluse and (traditionally) author of the *Èrshísì shīpǐn*.
- [羅隱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%85%E9%9A%B1) / [皮日休](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9A%AE%E6%97%A5%E4%BC%91) / [陸龜蒙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E9%BE%9C%E8%92%99) / [韋莊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%8B%E8%8E%8A) — the Wǎn Táng to Wǔdài tail of socially-engaged verse.
- [杜光庭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E5%85%89%E5%BA%AD) — the foundational late-Tang / 後蜀 Daoist literary voice.
- [崔致遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B4%94%E8%87%B4%E9%81%A0) — Silla diplomat-literatus, the principal East Asian Tang-correspondence corpus.
- [宋敏求](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E6%95%8F%E6%B1%82) — Sòng compiler whose recensional work on Lǐ Bái ([KR4c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0012)), Liú Yǔxī ([KR4c0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0051)), Mèng Jiāo ([KR4c0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0058)), and Yán Zhēnqīng ([KR4c0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0028)) underlies the standard Sòng-Yuán text of half the Tang canon.

### Topics

- **The four-stage canon: 初/盛/中/晚 Tang.** The chronological periodization codified in Yán Yǔ's *Cānglàng shīhuà* and naturalized into every Míng-Qīng anthology runs as the unspoken organizational principle of the division. Each phase has its emblematic figures (the *Sì jié* and Chén Zǐáng in the early; Wáng-Mèng-Lǐ-Dù in the high; Hán-Liǔ-Yuán-Bái in the mid; Lǐ-Dù-Wēn in the late) and its emblematic stylistic register.
- **The 古文運動 (Hán Yù-Liǔ Zōngyuán *gǔwén* movement).** The mid-Tang programmatic return to "ancient prose" — *Hàn-Wèi*-style direct argument-and-narrative against the *liùcháo* parallel-prose tradition — anchored in [韓愈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%93%E6%84%88) and [柳宗元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%B3%E5%AE%97%E5%85%83) and theorized in their letters. The downstream Sòng commentary apparatus (the Fāng Sōngqīng / Zhū Xī / Wáng Bódà / Wèi Zhòngjǔ / Liào Yíngzhōng / Chén Jǐngyún chain) is the densest critical-edition genealogy of any Tang prose corpus.
- **新樂府 vs. 苦吟 vs. 古體**. The mid-Tang split between [白居易](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%99%BD%E5%B1%85%E6%98%93) and [元稹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E7%A8%B9)'s social-realist *xīn yuèfǔ* program (with its accessible diction and political-didactic aim), the *Hán-Mèng* difficult-bitter school of [孟郊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E9%83%8A), [賈島](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B3%88%E5%B3%B6), [李賀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E8%B3%80), and [盧仝](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9B%A7%E4%BB%9D) (recondite vocabulary and bizarre image), and the [李白](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E7%99%BD)-Chén Zǐáng *fùgǔ* line of archaic *gǔfēng* — three competing visions of what mid-Tang verse should be doing.
- **山水田園 (landscape-and-farmstead) and the *Táo-Wéi-Wáng-Mèng* lineage.** The post-Táo Qián 陶潛 contemplative landscape mode, anchored in [王維](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%B6%AD) and [孟浩然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E6%B5%A9%E7%84%B6) in the High Tang and in [韋應物](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%8B%E6%87%89%E7%89%A9) and [柳宗元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%B3%E5%AE%97%E5%85%83) in the mid Tang; Sū Shì's Sòng-period codification of the *Táo-Wéi* pair defined the Sòng-Yuán-Míng reading.
- **邊塞 (frontier) verse.** [高適](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E9%81%A9) and [岑參](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B2%91%E5%8F%83) (with 王昌齡) as the principal voices of the High-Tang frontier-campaign genre — a register that thins out almost completely after the *An Lùshān* rebellion.
- **The *Wǎn Táng* dense-allusive style and its Northern Sòng inheritance.** [李商隱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%95%86%E9%9A%B1)'s *wútí* poems and [杜牧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E7%89%A7)'s allusive *juéjù* became the model for the early-Sòng *Xīkūn tǐ* 西崑體 of Yáng Yì, Liú Zǐyí, and Qián Wéiyǎn; the Sòng *Yuányòu* generation's reaction against this style is one of the principal storylines of the *Wényuán yīnghuá* / *Tángshī* anthology selection process.
- **Buddhist and Daoist literary participation.** The monks ([釋皎然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E7%9A%8E%E7%84%B6), [釋寒山](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E5%AF%92%E5%B1%B1), [釋貫休](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E8%B2%AB%E4%BC%91), [釋齊己](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E9%BD%8A%E5%B7%B1)) and the Daoist priest-writers ([吳筠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E7%AD%A0), [杜光庭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E5%85%89%E5%BA%AD)) hold a distinct register: half *shī*, half *jì* (gāthā) / Daoist ritual hymn, with circulation through monastic-archive transmission rather than the official *biéjí* network.
- **The Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng commentary enterprise.** A third of the KR4c entries are not Tang-period autographs but later annotated, collated, or anthologized editions. The Sòng commentary on Dù Fǔ alone runs to five major recensions in this division; Hán Yù has six; Liǔ Zōngyuán three. The KR4c material is therefore as much a record of Tang reception-history as of Tang composition.
- **Recension and textual problem.** The transmission of every major Tang collection is bibliographically distinctive. Bái Jūyì curated his own corpus by depositing manuscript copies at *Dōnglín sì*, *Shèngshàn sì*, *Sūzhōu Nánchán yuàn*, and *Xiāngshān sì* ([KR4c0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0069)); Lǐ Bái's collection was assembled by his cousin Lǐ Yángbīng at his deathbed and lay almost lost until the *Xiánpíng* (998–1003) recovery ([KR4c0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0012)); Wáng Bó's corpus is partly recovered from a *Shōsō-in* Tang MS ([KR4c0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0003)); the Chén Zǐáng *juǎn* 7 lacunae are filled from the *Wén yuàn yīng huá* ([KR4c0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4c/KR4c0008)). The transmission stories are themselves a major chapter in Tang literary history.
- **The dynastic boundary.** The *Wǔdài* Five-Dynasties holdovers — [釋齊己](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E9%BD%8A%E5%B7%B1) under *Jīngnán Nánpíng*, [釋貫休](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%8B%E8%B2%AB%E4%BC%91) under *Former Shǔ*, [韋莊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9F%8B%E8%8E%8A) under *Former Shǔ*, [李建勳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%BB%BA%E5%8B%B3) under *Nán Táng*, [杜光庭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E5%85%89%E5%BA%AD) under *後蜀* — are filed in KR4c rather than in the Sòng division, on the principle that Tang training rather than Tang reign-date governs categorization.
