# 別集類宋 (KR4d)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4d 別集類·宋金元 *Biéjí lèi · Sòng Jīn Yuán* — Collected Works — Individual Writers of the Sòng, Jīn, and Yuán](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR4d sits inside the *Sìkù quánshū jíbù* 集部 *biéjí lèi* 別集類 (Collections → individual collected works), the Sìkù compilers' chronological *biéjí* sequence, immediately after KR4c (Tang and Five Dynasties) and before KR4e (Ming) and KR4f (Qing). It is the **Sòng-Jīn-Yuán segment**: 415 Sòng, 5 Jīn, and 175 Yuán biéjí, 595 entries in all — the second-largest dynastic block in KR4 after KR4f, and the largest dynastic block in KR4 if Yuán-into-early-Míng cataloging conventions are taken into account. The opening is Xú Xuàn's *Qíshěng jí* 騎省集 ([KR4d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0001), 991 — a Five-Dynasties → Sòng transition figure whose Sòng dating places him in this division rather than KR4c) and the closing tail is the late-Yuán *Tiěyá* circle and the painter-poet Ní Zàn 倪瓚 ([KR4d0575](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0575), [KR4d0576](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0576), death 1374) on the cusp of the Míng.

The division is the **first dynastic *biéjí* block where collected works survive in critical mass**. Wilkinson, *Chinese History: A New Manual* §30.4.3, gives the survival figures: of pre-Táng *biéjí* only nineteen reach the Sìkù; of perhaps a thousand recorded Táng *biéjí* roughly three hundred survive; but for the Sòng about **800 individuals' biéjí survive** (≈ 20–30 % of those printed), and for Liáo / Jīn / Yuán together more than 250 survive. The reason is the printing revolution: from the Northern Sòng forward, *biéjí* are printed during or shortly after their authors' lifetimes by family, disciples, and provincial offices, and are no longer dependent on a single manuscript line. Wilkinson §62.3.10 gives the headline figure that the Sìkù itself contains 355 Sòng *biéjí*; the Kanripo extends slightly past that selection (415 Sòng entries) by including a handful of *Sìkù cúnmù* and post-Sìkù collections. For Yuán, Wilkinson §64.3.8 records about 250 extant *biéjí*, of which 175 are catalogued here. The standard modern reference catalogues are Zhū Shàngshū 祝尚書 *Sòngrén biéjí xùlù* 宋人別集敘錄 (rev. 2020) and Lù Jùnlíng 陸峻嶺 *Yuánrén wénjí piānmù fēnlèi suǒyǐn* 元人文集篇目分類索引 (1979).

Two structural points govern reading the division. First, the *biéjí* form itself is functionally biographical: a Sòng or Yuán *biéjí* contains both the literary output (*shī*, *fù*, *cí*, *jì*, *xù*, *bēi*) and the official documentary residue (*zòuyì*, *gōngdú*, *qǐ*, *zhuàng*, *zhì*, *biǎo*, *jiàoshū*) of a single life — making KR4d simultaneously the documentary archive of the Sòng-Yuán bureaucracy and the literary corpus of the same period (cf. §19.7: ~55 % of Táng-through-Qīng *biéjí* are by *jìnshì* holders). Second, the Sòng innovated the now-standard arrangement of *biéjí* contents — by genre at the top level, then chronologically within each genre — explicitly tied to the parallel Sòng establishment of the *niánpǔ* 年譜 (Wilkinson §30.4.1). This means KR4d collections can be read as ordered biographical sources in a way Táng *biéjí* often cannot. A high proportion of KR4d entries — at least two dozen — survive only through *Sìkù* editorial reconstruction from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* 永樂大典, the most aggressive imperial recovery program of the eighteenth century.

For the period-level periodization Wilkinson is silent on the school-level subdivisions of Sòng poetry (*Xīkūn tǐ* 西崑體, *Jiāngxī shīpài* 江西詩派, *Yǒngjiā sìlíng* 永嘉四靈, *Jiānghúpài* 江湖派), all of which are nevertheless basic to reading the division and for which the supplementary reference is Denecke et al., *Oxford Handbook of Classical Chinese Literature*.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **Early Northern Sòng *gǔwén* and reform-poetry pioneers (c. 990–1060).** [KR4d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0001) *Qíshěng jí* 騎省集 (Xú Xuàn 徐鉉), [KR4d0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0009) *Xiǎoxù jí* 小畜集 (Wáng Yǔchèn 王禹偁), [KR4d0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0012) *Wǔyí xīnjí* 武夷新集 (Yáng Yì 楊億, the *Xīkūn tǐ* anchor), [KR4d0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0013) *Lín Héjìng jí* 林和靖集 (Lín Bū 林逋), [KR4d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0014) / [KR4d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0015) *Mù cānjūn jí* / *Hénán Mùgōng jí* (Mù Xiū 穆修), [KR4d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0025) *Fàn Wénzhèng jí* 范文正集 (Fàn Zhòngyān), [KR4d0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0028) *Cúlái jí* 徂徠集 (Shí Jiè 石介), [KR4d0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0034) *Sū xuéshì jí* 蘇學士集 (Sū Shùnqīn 蘇舜欽), [KR4d0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0056) *Wǎnlíng jí* 宛陵集 (Méi Yáochén 梅堯臣). Together these document the decisive break from late-Táng / *Xīkūn* aestheticism towards the *Qìnglì* (1041–48) reform-period prose-and-verse program.
- **The Northern Sòng *bā dàjiā* and the Sū circle.** Five of the six Sòng *Táng-Sòng bā dàjiā* are present: Ōuyáng Xiū's principal *biéjí* [KR4d0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0068) *Wénzhōng jí* 文忠集 (153 *juǎn*, edited by Zhōu Bìdà 周必大, with a digest at [KR4d0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0069) *Ōuyáng wéncuì*); [KR4d0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0073) *Línchuān wénjí* 臨川文集 + [KR4d0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0074) *Wáng Jīnggōng shīzhù* (Wáng Ānshí 王安石, with Lǐ Bì 李壁's 1207 commentary); [KR4d0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0054) *Yuánfēng lèigǎo* 元豐類藁 (Zēng Gǒng 曾鞏); [KR4d0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0072) *Jiāyòu jí* 嘉祐集 (Sū Xún 蘇洵); [KR4d0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0076) *Dōngpō quánjí* 東坡全集 (Sū Shì 蘇軾, the post-loss reconstruction by Cài Shìyīng 蔡士英 in 115 *juǎn* under the Kāngxī court) with its four-text Sòng / Yuán / Qīng commentary apparatus [KR4d0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0077)–[KR4d0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0080) and Zhā Shènxíng 查慎行's [KR4d0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0081) *Sūshī bǔzhù* (1702 — the only Qīng entry in the division, retained because it is part of the Sūshī commentarial ecology); [KR4d0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0082) / [KR4d0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0083) *Luánchéng jí* / *Yìngzhào jí* (Sū Zhé 蘇轍).
- **The *Sūmén sì xuéshì* 蘇門四學士 and the *Jiāngxī shīpài*.** [KR4d0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0085) / [KR4d0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0086) *Shāngǔ nèijí shīzhù* / *wàijí shīzhù* (Huáng Tíngjiān 黃庭堅, with Rèn Yuān 任淵 / Shǐ Róng 史容's annotated editions, the founding text of the *Jiāngxī shīpài*); [KR4d0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0087) / [KR4d0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0088) *Hòushān jí* / *Hòushān shīzhù* (Chén Shīdào 陳師道, with Rèn Yuān again); [KR4d0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0090) *Zhāng yòushǐ wénjí* (Zhāng Lěi 張耒); [KR4d0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0091) *Huáihǎi jí* 淮海集 (Qín Guān 秦觀); [KR4d0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0105) *Jīlèi jí* 雞肋集 (Cháo Bǔzhī 晁補之). [KR4d0195](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0195) *Dōnglái shī jí* (Lǚ Běnzhōng 呂本中) carries the *Jiāngxī shīpài tú* 江西詩派圖 — the canon-list that constituted the school as a literary identity. The principal Northern-Sòng → Southern-Sòng poet-bridge is [KR4d0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0153) *Jiǎnzhāi jí* 簡齋集 (Chén Yǔyì 陳與義).
- **The conservative pole and the great Northern-Sòng official corpora.** [KR4d0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0040) *Chuánjiā jí* 傳家集 (Sīmǎ Guāng 司馬光); [KR4d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0024) *Ānyáng jí* 安陽集 (Hán Qí 韓琦); [KR4d0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0029) *Duānmíng jí* 端明集 (Cài Xiāng 蔡襄); [KR4d0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0035) *Sū Wèigōng wénjí* (Sū Sòng 蘇頌, the future *Xīnyí xiàng* astronomer); [KR4d0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0061) *Lùgōng wénjí* (Wén Yànbó 文彥博); [KR4d0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0044) *Gōngshì jí* + [KR4d0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0045) *Péngchéng jí* (the Liú 劉敞 / 劉攽 brothers).
- **The early *Dàoxué* and *Lǐxué* literary corpora.** Although the *yǔlù* and treatises live in KR3a / KR3c, the literary collections of the founding cohort are filed here: [KR4d0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0062) *Jīrǎng jí* 擊壤集 (Shào Yōng 邵雍, with its distinctive *xiàngshù*-inflected *yǒngshǐ shī*); [KR4d0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0065) *Zhōu Yuángōng jí* (Zhōu Dūnyí 周敦頤); [KR4d0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0136) / [KR4d0137](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0137) *Guīshān jí* / *xiānshēng yǔlù* (Yáng Shí 楊時); [KR4d0182](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0182) *Yùzhāng wénjí* (Luó Cóngyàn 羅從彥, of the *Yánpíng sān xiānshēng*); [KR4d0177](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0177) *Píngshān jí* (Liú Zǐhuī 劉子翬, one of Zhū Xī's teachers); and the central [KR4d0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0226) *Huìān jí* 晦菴集 (Zhū Xī 朱熹, 1265 Hú Bīngwén edition), which Wilkinson §30.4.1 takes as the paradigmatic late-imperial *biéjí*. The opposing *Xīnxué* pole is [KR4d0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0253) *Xiàngshān jí* 象山集 (Lù Jiǔyuān 陸九淵). The senior late-Sòng *Lǐxué* officialdom: [KR4d0306](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0306) *Xīshān wénjí* 西山文集 (Zhēn Déxiù 真德秀) and [KR4d0305](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0305) *Hèshān jí* 鶴山集 (Wèi Liǎowēng 魏了翁).
- **The *Jìngkāng* trauma and Sòng patriotic literature.** A distinctive cluster running from the Jīn invasion through the early Southern-Sòng: [KR4d0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0188) *Shǎoyáng jí* 少陽集 (Chén Dōng 陳東, executed 1127); [KR4d0135](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0135) *Zōng zhōngjiǎn jí* 宗忠簡集 (Zōng Zé 宗澤); [KR4d0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0138) *Liángxī jí* 梁谿集 (Lǐ Gāng 李綱); [KR4d0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0148) *Zhōngzhèng déwén jí* (Zhào Dǐng 趙鼎); [KR4d0191](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0191) *Yuè Wǔmù yíwén* 岳武穆遺文 (the surviving prose of Yuè Fēi 岳飛, edited by Xú Jiē 徐階 in the Míng); [KR4d0196](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0196) *Dànān wénjí* 澹菴文集 (Hú Quán 胡銓, of the famous 1138 anti-peace memorial). These collections are continuous in spirit with the late-Sòng loyalist cluster below and constitute the principal documentary basis for the historiography of the *Jìngkāng* and *Shàoxīng* (1127–1162) reconstitution.
- **The *Zhōngxīng sì dà shīrén* 中興四大詩人.** The four canonical High Southern-Sòng poets: [KR4d0265](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0265) *Shíhú shījí* (Fàn Chéngdà 范成大), [KR4d0266](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0266) *Chéngzhāi jí* 誠齋集 (Yáng Wànlǐ 楊萬里), [KR4d0229](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0229) *Liángxī yígǎo* (Yóu Mào 尤袤), and the largest single-author cluster of the division at [KR4d0267](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0267)–[KR4d0270](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0270) (Lù Yóu 陸游's *Jiànnán shīgǎo* 劎南詩槀, *Wèinán wénjí* 渭南文集, *Fàngwēng shīxuǎn*, and *Jiàngǔ jīngxuǎn Lù Fàngwēng*).
- **The *Yǒngjiā* and *Yǒngkāng* utilitarian schools and their Daoxue counterparts.** [KR4d0264](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0264) *Làngyǔ jí* 浪語集 (Xuē Jìxuān 薛季宣, founder), [KR4d0233](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0233) *Zhǐzhāi jí* 止齋集 (Chén Fùliáng 陳傅良), [KR4d0273](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0273) *Shuǐxīn jí* 水心集 (Yè Shì 葉適, the mature *Yǒngjiā gōnglìxué* synthesis), [KR4d0303](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0303) *Lóngchuān jí* 龍川集 (Chén Liàng 陳亮, the *Yǒngkāng* utilitarian and Zhū Xī's interlocutor in the famous *wángbà* exchange). Their constitutional-historical counterpart is [KR4d0232](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0232) *Dōnglái jí* (Lǚ Zǔqiān 呂祖謙) and [KR4d0284](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0284) *Nánxuān jí* (Zhāng Shì 張栻, edited by Zhū Xī).
- **The *Yǒngjiā sìlíng* 永嘉四靈 and the *Jiānghúpài* 江湖派.** The reaction against *Jiāngxī*-school recondite verse: [KR4d0297](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0297) *Fānglánxuān jí* (Xú Zhào 徐照) and [KR4d0298](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0298) *Èrwēitíng shījí* (Xú Jǐ 徐璣), two of the four *Sìlíng* (the others — Zhào Shīxiù 趙師秀 and Wēng Juǎn 翁卷 — survive only outside KR4d). The *Jiānghúpài* anchors are [KR4d0278](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0278) *Shípíng shījí* 石屏詩集 (Dài Fùgǔ 戴復古) and [KR4d0340](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0340) *Hòucūn jí* 後村集 (Liú Kèzhuāng 劉克莊, also the principal *Jiānghú* anthologist).
- **The Sòng loyalist (*yímín* 遺民) corpus.** [KR4d0365](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0365) *Wénshān jí* 文山集 + [KR4d0366](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0366) *Wén Xìnguó jí Dù shī* (Wén Tiānxiáng 文天祥, including the *Yuándū* prison-cell *Jí Dù shī* assembled wholly from Dù Fǔ couplets); [KR4d0367](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0367) *Diéshān jí* 叠山集 (Xiè Fāngdé 謝枋得); [KR4d0395](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0395) *Jìshān wénjí* (Lín Jǐngxī 林景熙, of the famous *Mèngmò shī* on the desecration of the Six Sòng tombs); [KR4d0331](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0331) *Sānshān Zhèng Júshān xiānshēng qīngjùn jí* (attributed to Zhèng Sīxiào 鄭思肖); [KR4d0382](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0382) *Sìmíng wénxiàn jí* (Wáng Yìnglín 王應麟); [KR4d0406](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0406) *Bóyá qín* 伯牙琴 (Dèng Mù 鄧牧, anti-totalitarian remnant prose); [KR4d0407](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0407) *Cúnyǎtáng yígǎo* (Fāng Fèng 方鳳); [KR4d0374](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0374) *Xūxī jí* 須溪集 (Liú Chénwēng 劉辰翁, also the principal late-Sòng anthologist and commentator on Tang poetry).
- **The Jīn dynasty (5 entries).** [KR4d0416](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0416) *Zhuōxuān jí* (Wáng Jì 王寂); [KR4d0417](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0417) *Fǔshuǐ jí* 滏水集 (Zhào Bǐngwén 趙秉文, the head of the late-Jīn *wénrén*); [KR4d0418](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0418) *Hūnán jí* 滹南集 (Wáng Ruòxū 王若虛); [KR4d0419](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0419) *Zhuāngjìng jí* (Lǐ Jùnmín 李俊民); and the pivotal Jīn → Yuán figure [KR4d0420](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0420) *Yíshān jí* 遺山集 (Yuán Hàowèn 元好問, the supreme Jīn poet whose *Zhōngzhōu jí* preserves the rest of Jīn verse).

- **The Sòng → Yuán literary bridge and the southern *Lǐxué*.** [KR4d0431](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0431) *Shànyuán wénjí* (Dài Biǎoyuán 戴表元, the principal stylistic bridge); [KR4d0428](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0428) *Tóngjiāng xùjí* (Fāng Huí 方回, surrendered Sòng prefect, compiler of the *Yíngkuí lǜsuǐ* 瀛奎律髓 and the principal Yuán theorist of the *Jiāngxī* tradition); [KR4d0445](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0445) *Sōngxuězhāi jí* 松雪齋集 (Zhào Mèngfǔ 趙孟頫, calligrapher–painter–poet, the most consequential collaborating Hànrén of the early Yuán); [KR4d0446](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0446) *Wú Wénzhèng jí* (Wú Chéng 吳澄, the southern *Lǐxué* master).
- **The *Yányòu* generation: the *Yuán shī sì dà jiā* 元詩四大家 and the *Rúlín sìjié* 儒林四傑.** The mature mid-Yuán imperial-academy literary establishment, crystallized after the 1313 restoration of the examinations: [KR4d0493](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0493) *Dàoyuán xuégǔ lù* + [KR4d0494](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0494) *Dàoyuán yígǎo* (Yú Jí 虞集), [KR4d0495](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0495) *Yáng Zhònghóng jí* (Yáng Zǎi 楊載), [KR4d0496](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0496) *Fàn Déjī shījí* (Fàn Pēng 范梈), [KR4d0497](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0497) *Wénān jí* (Jiē Xīsī 揭傒斯) — the four together = *Yuán shī sì dà jiā*. Add [KR4d0502](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0502) / [KR4d0503](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0503) *Wénxiàn jí* / *Jīnhuá Huáng xiānshēng wénjí* (Huáng Jǐn 黃溍), [KR4d0504](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0504) *Guīzhāi wénjí* (Ōuyáng Xuán 歐陽玄, chief compiler of the *Sòng-Liáo-Jīn shǐ*), [KR4d0505](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0505) *Dàizhì jí* (Liǔ Guàn 柳貫), [KR4d0473](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0473) *Qīngróng jūshì jí* (Yuán Juè 袁桷); the four (Yú / Huáng / Liǔ / Ōu) = *Rúlín sìjié*. This is the documentary residue of the Tuōtuō *guóshǐyuàn* compilation enterprise.
- **The *sèmù* literati operating in Chinese.** A genuine Yuán novelty: Khitan, Tangut, Uyghur, and Mongol authors with full *biéjí*. [KR4d0421](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0421) (Yēlǜ Chǔcái, Khitan Buddhist); [KR4d0491](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0491) *Shítián wénjí* 石田文集 (Mǎ Zǔcháng 馬祖常, of Önggüd Christian descent, the most distinguished *sèmù* poet of the *Sì dà jiā* generation); [KR4d0514](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0514) *Yànmén jí* 雁門集 + [KR4d0519](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0519) *Sà Tiānxī shījí* (Sà Dūlā 薩都拉, of Türkic / Tangut origin, the leading mid-late Yuán *sèmù* poet).

### Topics

- **The Sòng *gǔwén* continuation and the *Táng-Sòng bā dàjiā* canon.** The Sòng leg of the *Táng-Sòng bā dàjiā* — Ōuyáng Xiū, Zēng Gǒng, Wáng Ānshí, the three Sū — anchors the Sìkù conception of mature classical prose. The post-Sū Northern-Sòng *gǔwén* legacy then bifurcates into the Sòng *Dàoxué* prose tradition (Zhū Xī's letters and disquisitions) and the Yǒngjiā / Yǒngkāng utilitarian prose (Yè Shì, Chén Liàng); the trajectory continues through the Yuán in the Yú Jí / Huáng Jǐn / Liǔ Guàn / Ōuyáng Xuán generation as the model for state-document prose. KR4d is the principal documentary archive of this arc.
- **The *Xīkūn* → reform-poetry → *Jiāngxī* → *Sìlíng* / *Jiānghú* axis of Sòng poetry.** The early-Sòng Yáng Yì–Liú Yún ornamental *Xīkūn tǐ* is displaced in the 1040s by the Méi Yáochén / Sū Shùnqīn reform program; this matures into the Sū-Huáng *Dōngpō* / *Shāngǔ* style; the *Jiāngxī shīpài* (Lǚ Běnzhōng's canonical list) carries it through the Northern-Southern Sòng transition; the *Yǒngjiā sìlíng* and the *Jiānghúpài* mount a late-twelfth-century reaction recovering late-Tang plain-style verse; Yán Yǔ's *Cānglàng shīhuà* codifies the resulting periodization. Almost every major *biéjí* in KR4d either belongs to or argues against one of these positions.
- **Cí 詞 versus shī 詩 inside the *biéjí*.** Many KR4d collections contain *cí* alongside their *shī* and *wén* (Sū Shì, Lù Yóu, Yáng Wànlǐ, Yè Mèngdé, Chén Liàng, etc.), and many of the canonical *cí* poets are present here only by their secondary genres ([KR4d0216](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0216) Zhāng Xiàoxiáng's *Yúhú jí*; cf. *cí*-only collections in adjacent divisions). The *biéjí* form thus preserves *cí* as a part of integrated authorial output rather than as a separate genre — important for the editorial history of the Sòng *cí* canon.
- **Dàoxué and Lǐxué literary practice.** A thread through the entire division: the founding Northern-Sòng cohort (Zhōu Dūnyí, Shào Yōng), the *Yánpíng* line (Yáng Shí, Luó Cóngyàn, Lǐ Tóng), Zhū Xī's massive *biéjí*, the Sì-Lú-Wèi-Zhēn senior-officialdom set, and the southern / northern Yuán transmitters (Wú Chéng, Xǔ Héng). The *xīnxué* counter-pole (Lù Jiǔyuān) and the utilitarian *Yǒngjiā* / *Yǒngkāng* alternatives are equally present. KR4d documents what *Dàoxué* looked like as a literary practice, not only as a philosophical school.
- **The *Jìngkāng* trauma and the loyalist tradition.** Two parallel loyalist clusters: the high-Northern-Sòng-into-Southern-Sòng (Chén Dōng → Zōng Zé → Lǐ Gāng → Yuè Fēi → Hú Quán → Lù Yóu), and the late-Sòng-into-early-Yuán (Wén Tiānxiáng → Xiè Fāngdé → Lín Jǐngxī → Zhèng Sīxiào → Dèng Mù → Liú Chénwēng). Each is editorially distinctive: the first largely transmitted by family and by Sòng official offices; the second often surviving only in late-Míng or early-Qīng *jíběn* recovery and in Sìkù *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* extraction. The pair frames KR4d as the principal documentary archive of pre-modern Chinese loyalist literary identity.
- **The Mongol-court Hànrén establishment and the *sèmù* literati.** The integration of Khitan, Jurchen, Tangut, Uyghur, Önggüd, and Mongol authors into the Sòng-Yuán literary canon is a feature unique to KR4d in the entire Kanripo corpus. The Hànrén collaborators (Yēlǜ Chǔcái, Xǔ Héng, Yú Jí, Zhào Mèngfǔ) and the *sèmù* poets (Mǎ Zǔcháng, Sà Dūlā) collectively redefine what a "Chinese" *biéjí* can be: Christian-descent, Tangut-Uyghur, and Mongol authors writing in Chinese on classical themes for a multi-ethnic court audience.
- **The *Yányòu* (1313) restoration of the examinations and the maturation of Yuán prose.** Most of the principal Yuán-period *biéjí* date from after the 1313 *kējǔ* restoration, which produced the *Yuán shī sì dà jiā* and the *Rúlín sìjié*; their collections double as the documentary residue of the Tuōtuō *guóshǐyuàn* compilation effort that produced the *Sòng*, *Liáo*, and *Jīn shǐ*. The corpus is therefore not just a literary archive but a state-historiographical archive.
- **Editorial reconstruction and the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* recovery.** A high proportion of KR4d entries — including [KR4d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0004) Pān Láng, [KR4d0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0308) Gě Shàotǐ, [KR4d0322](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0322), [KR4d0332](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0332), [KR4d0342](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0342) Hán Hù, [KR4d0347](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0347), [KR4d0351](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0351), [KR4d0364](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0364), [KR4d0374](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0374) Liú Chénwēng, [KR4d0518](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0518), [KR4d0565](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0565), [KR4d0581](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0581), [KR4d0591](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0591) — survive only because the eighteenth-century *Sìkù* editors extracted them from the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn*. KR4d is therefore also a record of what the Qīng imperial editorial enterprise judged worth recovering. The complementary editorial axis is the dense Sòng / Yuán / Míng / Qīng commentary apparatus around the canonical poets ([KR4d0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0076)–[KR4d0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0081) for Sū Shì, [KR4d0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0085)–[KR4d0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0088) for Huáng-Chén, [KR4d0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0073)–[KR4d0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4d/KR4d0074) for Wáng Ānshí), structurally parallel to the KR4c Hán-Liǔ-Dù-Lǐ commentarial clusters.

# 別集類明 (KR4e)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4e 別集類·明 *Biéjí lèi · Míng* — Collected Works — Individual Writers of the Míng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR4e sits inside the *Sìkù quánshū jíbù* 集部 *biéjí lèi* 別集類 (Collections → individual collected works), the *Sìkù* compilers' chronological *biéjí* sequence, immediately after KR4d (Sòng, Jīn, Yuán) and before KR4f (Qīng). It is the **Míng segment**: 228 entries running from the founder Zhū Yuánzhāng 朱元璋's *Míng Tàizǔ wénjí* 明太祖文集 ([KR4e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0001), composed 1368–1398) through the writings of the Chóngzhēn 崇禎 martyrs of 1644 ([KR4e0240](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0240), [KR4e0241](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0241), [KR4e0242](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0242)) and the early-Qīng survivors who finished their *jí* in the aftermath of the dynastic collapse ([KR4e0230](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0230), [KR4e0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0244), [KR4e0245](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0245)). Posthumous editorial work on Hóngwǔ-period collections (e.g. [KR4e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0003), printed 1655) extends the publication tail another decade. KR4e is the third-largest dynastic block in KR4 and represents the *Sìkù* compilers' canonical filter on the Míng *biéjí* tradition — out of "at least 1,500 extant collected works of individual Ming authors" attested by the modern catalogs (Wilkinson, *Chinese History: A New Manual*, §65.3.9, citing the HYZ database and Cuī Jiànyīng's *Míng biéjí bǎnběn zhì* 明别集版本志, which lists more than 3,600 separate editions), the *Sìkù* admitted only a curated fraction.

That filter is itself a major intellectual statement. The 228 collections gathered here are the Qiánlóng-era court's official Míng literary canon: the *táigé tǐ* 臺閣體 cabinet stylists of the Yǒnglè–Xuāndé courts, the *Chálíng pài* 茶陵派 of Lǐ Dōngyáng 李東陽, the Hóngzhì–Zhèngdé archaist *Qián qī zǐ* 前七子, the mid-Jiājìng *Táng-Sòng pài* 唐宋派 prose revivalists, the Jiājìng–Wànlì *Hòu qī zǐ* 後七子, the *Yángmíng* 陽明 inheritors thought safe enough to print, and the Chóngzhēn-era loyalist martyrs whose deaths in 1644–45 served the Qīng narrative of legitimate succession. The figures the *Sìkù* deliberately suppressed — Lǐ Zhì 李贄, the Yuán brothers and the *Gōngān pài* 公安派, the *Jìnglíng pài* 竟陵派, the *Fùshè* 復社 partisans Chén Zǐlóng 陳子龍 and Zhāng Pǔ 張溥, and the most outspoken Yángmíng "wild *chán*" (狂禪) thinkers Wáng Jī 王畿, Wáng Gěn 王艮, Jiāo Hóng 焦竑 — are not in KR4e, and their absence is at least as informative for the historian as the names that are present. For those exclusions, KR4f and the supplementary *cóngshū* of the late Qīng and Republican periods are the necessary supplement; KR4e on its own gives the orthodox Sìkù view of three centuries of Míng letters.

### Important texts and text clusters

The 228 *jí* group themselves into recognizable clusters, presented here in roughly chronological order. The per-text Abstracts give the evidence; this section is the navigational map.

**Late-Yuán to early-Míng transition.** The earliest *notBefore* dates in the division (1330s) belong to figures whose lives straddled the Yuán collapse: *Shuōxué zhāi gǎo* 說學齋稿 ([KR4e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0012)) of Wēi Sù 危素, the Yuán *jìnshì* who surrendered to the Míng; *Gēngxué zhāi shījí* 耕學齋詩集 ([KR4e0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0056)) of Yuán Huá 袁華, transmitted via the editing of the Yuán-loyalist *Tiěyá* 鐵崖 poet Yáng Wéizhēn 楊維楨; and the works of Sòng Lián 宋濂 ([KR4e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0002), [KR4e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0003), [KR4e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0004)) and Liú Jī 劉基 ([KR4e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0005), [KR4e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0006)), the two architects of Hóngwǔ legitimacy whose *jí* form the literary spine of the new dynasty.

**Hóngwǔ founding court.** The imperial-author convention places the *Míng Tàizǔ wénjí* ([KR4e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0001)) at the head of the division. Around it stand the *jí* of the four "Hóngwǔ Three" — Sòng Lián 宋濂, Liú Jī 劉基, Wáng Yī 王禕 ([KR4e0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0010)) — plus Wāng Guǎngyáng 汪廣洋 ([KR4e0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0007)), Táo Ān 陶安 ([KR4e0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0008)), Sòng Nè 宋訥 ([KR4e0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0009)), and Sū Bóhéng 蘇伯衡 ([KR4e0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0024)). These collections double as primary sources for the institutional history of the founding reign.

**Wúzhōng (Sūzhōu) poets and the early-Hóngwǔ purges.** The *Wúzhōng sì jié* 吳中四傑 generation, decimated by Tàizǔ's political violence, is well represented: Gāo Qǐ 高啓 in *Dàquán jí* 大全集 ([KR4e0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0039)) and *Fúzǎo jí* 鳧藻集 ([KR4e0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0040)), and the cluster of *jí* by Zhāng Yǔ 張羽, Xú Bēn, Wáng Yí 王彝, Sūn Zuò 孫作 ([KR4e0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0023) vicinity), and Bèi Qióng 貝瓊 ([KR4e0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0023)) in the early KR4e numbering.

**Yǒnglè cabinet — *táigé tǐ* 臺閣體.** The smoothed-out, decorous prose of the Yǒnglè–Xuāndé Hànlín cabinet is the next major formation: *Dōnglǐ jí* 東里集 ([KR4e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0090)) of Yáng Shìqí 楊士奇, *Wénmǐn jí* 文敏集 ([KR4e0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0091)) of Yáng Róng 楊榮, *Wényì jí* 文毅集 ([KR4e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0083)) of Xiè Jìn 解縉, *Shěngqiān jí* 省愆集 ([KR4e0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0092)) of Huáng Huái 黃淮, *Jīn Wénjìng jí* 金文靖集 ([KR4e0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0094)) of Jīn Yòuzī 金幼孜, and *Yíān wénxuǎn* 頤庵文選 ([KR4e0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0088)) of Hú Yǎn 胡儼. These are the literary face of the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* 永樂大典 generation.

**Chéng-Huà / Hóngzhì Confucian and *Chálíng* 茶陵 turn.** The mid-fifteenth century shift away from cabinet decorum is anchored by Xuē Xuān 薛瑄's *Jìngxuān wénjí* 敬軒文集 ([KR4e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0100)) on the Lǐxué side and Lǐ Dōngyáng 李東陽's *Huáilùtáng jí* 懷麓堂集 ([KR4e0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0120)) on the literary side. The *Chálíng pài* gathered around Lǐ; Chéng Mǐnzhèng 程敏政's *Huángdūn wénjí* 篁墩文集 ([KR4e0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0125)) is the principal subsidiary collection. Qiū Jùn 丘濬's *Chóngbiān Qióngtái gǎo* 重編瓊臺藁 ([KR4e0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0115)) represents the imperial-tutor lineage at the same court.

**Chán-Confucian / Yángmíng filiation.** Chén Xiànzhāng 陳獻章's *Chén Báishā jí* 陳白沙集 ([KR4e0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0108)) is the immediate forerunner; Wáng Shǒurén 王守仁 himself enters via the comprehensive *Wáng Wénchéng quánshū* 王文成全書 ([KR4e0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0157)) and the topical *Yángmíng xiānsheng jíyào* 陽明先生集要 ([KR4e0245](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0245)). The Jiāngyòu *Yángmíng* heir Luó Hóngxiān 羅洪先's *Niànān wénjí* 念菴文集 ([KR4e0187](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0187)) is the principal mid-century continuation.

**前七子 — Hóngzhì–Zhèngdé archaists.** The classic seven: Lǐ Mèngyáng 李夢陽 *Kōngtóng jí* 空同集 ([KR4e0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0150)), Hé Jǐngmíng 何景明 *Dàfù jí* 大復集 ([KR4e0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0162)), Biān Gòng 邊貢 *Huáquán jí* 華泉集 ([KR4e0153](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0153)), Xú Zhēnqīng 徐禎卿 *Dígōng jí* 迪功集 ([KR4e0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0166)), Kāng Hǎi 康海 *Duìshān jí* 對山集 ([KR4e0159](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0159)); Gù Lín 顧璘 *Gù Huáyù jí* 顧華玉集 ([KR4e0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0152)) stands as a close associate. Their slogan — *wén bì Qín-Hàn, shī bì Shèng Táng* 文必秦漢, 詩必盛唐 ("prose must be Qín-Hàn, poetry must be High Táng") — defines the early-sixteenth-century literary controversy.

**Tāng-Sòng prose revival (*Táng-Sòng pài* 唐宋派).** Against archaist constriction came Wáng Shènzhōng 王愼中 *Zūnyán jí* 遵巖集 ([KR4e0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0185)), Táng Shùnzhī 唐順之 *Jīngchuān jí* 荊川集 ([KR4e0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0190)), and the towering Guī Yǒuguāng 歸有光 *Zhènchuān jí* 震川集 ([KR4e0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0215)) — the latter the principal Míng exhibit in the *Sìkù* compilers' Qīng-era Tāng-Sòng-prose canon, and the model later claimed by the *Tóngchéng* 桐城 school. Gāo Shūsì 高叔嗣's *Sūmén jí* 蘇門集 ([KR4e0183](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0183)) sits adjacent, a poetic counterpart that resisted full archaist conformity.

**後七子 — Jiājìng–Wànlì archaist revival.** Led by Lǐ Pānlóng 李攀龍 *Cāngmíng jí* 滄溟集 ([KR4e0198](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0198)) and Wáng Shìzhēn 王世貞 *Yǎnzhōu sìbù gǎo* 弇州四部稿 ([KR4e0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0201)) and its sequel *Dúshū hòu* 讀書後 ([KR4e0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0202)). Wáng's *Yǎnzhōu sìbù gǎo* — at 174 *juǎn* one of the largest individual *jí* in the entire Kanripo corpus — was the encyclopedic standard against which late-Míng literary judgment defined itself. Yú Shènxíng 于愼行 *Gǔchéng shānguǎn shījí* 穀城山館詩集 ([KR4e0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0219)) extends the Wànlì-era continuation.

**Wànlì–Tiānqǐ administrators and stylists.** A long tail of Wànlì-era court officials and provincial literati fills [KR4e0210](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0210)–[KR4e0239](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0239), including Shěn Lǐ 沈鯉 *Yìyùtáng gǎo* 亦玉堂稿 ([KR4e0213](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0213)), and a wide spread of secondary *jí* often surviving only because they entered an imperially-commissioned project.

**Chóngzhēn martyrs and loyalist-era closings.** The division closes with the writings of those who died for the dynasty in 1644–45 or shortly after, a Qīng-curated framing that gives the Míng a literary martyr's exit: Ní Yuánlù 倪元璐 *Ní Wénzhēn jí* 倪文貞集 ([KR4e0240](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0240), suicide at the fall of Beijing, 1644), Líng Yìqú 凌義渠 *Líng Zhōngjiègōng jí* 凌忠介公集 ([KR4e0241](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0241), suicide 1644), Shēn Jiāyìn 申佳胤 *Shēn Zhōngmǐn shījí* 申忠愍詩集 ([KR4e0242](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0242), suicide 1644), Huáng Chúnyào 黃淳耀 *Táoān quánjí* 陶菴全集 ([KR4e0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0244), suicide at the fall of Jiādìng 1645), and Liú Zōngzhōu 劉宗周 *Liú Jíshān jí* ([KR4e0230](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0230), starved himself 1645). The single posthumously-printed Sòng Lián *yíjí* of 1655 ([KR4e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0003)) is the chronological tail.

### Important persons

- [朱元璋](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%85%83%E7%92%8B) — founding emperor (r. 1368–1398) and *de facto* literary patron; his own *wénjí* opens the division and his court framed the Hóngwǔ literary culture from which the early Míng *biéjí* tradition emerged.
- [宋濂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E6%BF%82) — chief Hóngwǔ court literatus, principal compiler of the *Yuán shǐ* 元史 and the dominant prose stylist of the founding generation; three separate *jí* of his work survive in KR4e ([KR4e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0002), [KR4e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0003), [KR4e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0004)).
- [劉基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%9F%BA) — Hóngwǔ strategist-statesman and poet, posthumously *Chéngyìbó* 誠意伯; the two recensions of his *jí* ([KR4e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0005), [KR4e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0006)) preserve both his prose memorials and his political-allegorical *fù*.
- [高啟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AB%98%E5%95%9F) — leader of the Wúzhōng poets, executed by Tàizǔ in 1374; widely regarded as the finest Míng *shī* poet, and the principal model invoked by later anti-archaists.
- [楊士奇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E5%A3%AB%E5%A5%87) — head of the Yǒnglè–Xuāndé Hànlín cabinet and the defining stylist of the *táigé tǐ* prose [KR4e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0090).
- [李東陽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%9D%B1%E9%99%BD) — leader of the *Chálíng pài*, prime minister under the Hóngzhì emperor, and the bridge from cabinet decorum to the archaist generation that reacted against him [KR4e0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0120).
- [王守仁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%AE%88%E4%BB%81) — *xīnxué* 心學 founder; his complete works [KR4e0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0157) are the Míng literary canon's primary admission of the Yángmíng school.
- [李夢陽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%A4%A2%E9%99%BD), [何景明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E6%99%AF%E6%98%8E) — co-leaders of the *Qián qī zǐ* and architects of the *fùgǔ* 復古 archaist programme [KR4e0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0150), [KR4e0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0162).
- [唐順之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%94%90%E9%A0%86%E4%B9%8B), [歸有光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%B8%E6%9C%89%E5%85%89) — twin pillars of the *Táng-Sòng pài* prose revival [KR4e0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0190), [KR4e0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0215), the model later canonized by *Tóngchéng*.
- [王世貞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E4%B8%96%E8%B2%9E) — magnate of the *Hòu qī zǐ*, encyclopaedic critic of late-Míng letters; his *Yǎnzhōu sìbù gǎo* [KR4e0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0201) is the single largest individual *jí* in KR4e.
- [羅洪先](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%85%E6%B4%AA%E5%85%88) — Jiāngyòu Yángmíng heir whose *Niànān wénjí* [KR4e0187](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0187) is the principal mid-century vehicle for orthodox-leaning *xīnxué* expression admitted to the Sìkù.
- [劉宗周](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%AE%97%E5%91%A8) — last great Míng Confucian, *Dōnglín / Jíshān* lineage, starved himself after the 1645 fall of Hángzhōu [KR4e0230](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0230).
- [倪元璐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%80%AA%E5%85%83%E7%92%90) — Chóngzhēn-era Hànlín official, suicide at the 1644 fall of Beijing, exemplary martyr-writer [KR4e0240](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0240).

### Topics

- **Archaism vs. its discontents (復古 *fùgǔ*).** The defining literary-historical thread of the Míng *biéjí* tradition. The *Qián qī zǐ* slogan *wén bì Qín-Hàn, shī bì Shèng Táng* triggered nearly a century of reaction: the *Táng-Sòng pài*'s rehabilitation of Hán Yù 韓愈 and Ōuyáng Xiū 歐陽修 as prose models, the *Hòu qī zǐ*'s re-articulation of the archaist programme, and ultimately the *Gōngān* 公安 *xìnglíng* 性靈 reaction (whose practitioners the *Sìkù* refused to admit). KR4e is the primary site where this controversy is documented through the writers themselves rather than through later anthologies or *shīhuà* 詩話.
- ***Táigé tǐ* and the literature of imperial service.** The Yǒnglè–Xuāndé cabinet style of [KR4e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0090) [KR4e0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0091) [KR4e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0083) is the orthodox starting point against which everything from the *Chálíng pài* onward defined itself; reading KR4e from beginning to end exposes the long arc of literati discomfort with state-orthodox decorum.
- **Heart-mind learning in literary form.** The admission of [陳獻章](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E7%8D%BB%E7%AB%A0)'s *Chén Báishā jí* [KR4e0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0108) and the Yángmíng line ([KR4e0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0157), [KR4e0187](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0187), [KR4e0245](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0245)) reflects a careful Qīng compromise: the Sìkù editors admitted the Yángmíng *biéjí* but excluded the most heterodox of the Tàizhōu and "wild Chán" inheritors (Wáng Jī, Wáng Gěn, Lǐ Zhì, Jiāo Hóng). Readers of the division need to bring these absences with them.
- **The Sìkù's curated late Míng.** The genuine late-Míng literary moment — *Gōngān*, *Jìnglíng*, *xiǎopǐn* 小品 essayism, Lǐ Zhì's iconoclasm, the *Fùshè* and Jǐshè 幾社 partisans — is structurally absent from KR4e. The division's late-Míng "voice" is instead loyalist, martyr-coloured, and Confucian-orthodox: the writings of the men who died in 1644–45 ([KR4e0240](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0240) [KR4e0241](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0241) [KR4e0242](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0242) [KR4e0230](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0230) [KR4e0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0244)). This is the dynasty's officially-licensed epitaph.
- **The Wúzhōng question.** A persistent sub-theme is the relationship between the Sūzhōu literary milieu (Gāo Qǐ, Yáng Jī, Zhāng Yǔ, Xú Bēn, Wáng Yí, Sūn Zuò) and the Hóngwǔ throne. Tàizǔ executed or persecuted most of the Wúzhōng poets; their *jí* survive in KR4e because the *Sìkù* compilers respected their literary stature, but the political backstory is integral to reading the early-Míng portion of the division.
- **The imperial author at the head.** A Sìkù *biéjí lèi* convention places the dynastic founder's *wénjí* first ([KR4e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0001)) — a paratextual editorial choice that frames the division as the literary history of an institution, not a free-standing literary survey.

### Timeline

The Míng *biéjí* timeline is densest in three phases: the Hóngwǔ founding generation (works completed 1340s–1380s), the Jiājìng–Wànlì literary debates (works completed roughly 1500–1610), and the Chóngzhēn-collapse martyrs (1640s). The list below picks the best-dated landmark in each cluster.

- 1330–1368 — *Shuōxué zhāi gǎo* 說學齋稿 [KR4e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0012) — Wēi Sù 危素's Yuán-period writings, the earliest *biéjí* admitted into the Míng division on the basis of the author's post-1368 Míng service.
- 1336–1375 — *Chéngyìbó wénjí* 誠意伯文集 [KR4e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0005) — Liú Jī, founding-court strategist and poet.
- 1340–1381 — *Wénxiàn jí* 文憲集 [KR4e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0002) — Sòng Lián, the defining prose stylist of the founding generation.
- 1353–1374 — *Gāo Tàishǐ dàquán jí* 高太史大全集 [KR4e0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0039) — Gāo Qǐ, the leading Wúzhōng poet, executed 1374.
- 1368–1398 — *Míng Tàizǔ wénjí* 明太祖文集 [KR4e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0001) — Zhū Yuánzhāng's writings, opening the division by *Sìkù* convention.
- c. 1380–1430 — *Wényì jí* 文毅集 [KR4e0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0083) — Xiè Jìn, *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* general editor, opening the cabinet-style cluster.
- c. 1390–1444 — *Dōnglǐ jí* 東里集 [KR4e0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0090) — Yáng Shìqí, the defining *táigé tǐ* prose stylist.
- c. 1430–1464 — *Jìngxuān wénjí* 敬軒文集 [KR4e0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0100) — Xuē Xuān, the mid-Míng Lǐxué pivot.
- c. 1450–1500 — *Chén Báishā jí* 陳白沙集 [KR4e0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0108) — the immediate Yángmíng forerunner.
- c. 1480–1516 — *Huáilùtáng jí* 懷麓堂集 [KR4e0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0120) — Lǐ Dōngyáng, *Chálíng pài* anchor.
- c. 1490–1529 — *Kōngtóng jí* 空同集 [KR4e0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0150) — Lǐ Mèngyáng, *Qián qī zǐ* manifesto-collection.
- c. 1505–1528 — *Wáng Wénchéng quánshū* 王文成全書 [KR4e0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0157) — Wáng Shǒurén, the canonical Yángmíng *biéjí* admitted into the Sìkù.
- c. 1530–1560 — *Jīngchuān jí* 荊川集 [KR4e0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0190) — Táng Shùnzhī, *Táng-Sòng pài*.
- c. 1540–1571 — *Zhènchuān jí* 震川集 [KR4e0215](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0215) — Guī Yǒuguāng, the Míng prose model later canonized by *Tóngchéng*.
- c. 1555–1590 — *Yǎnzhōu sìbù gǎo* 弇州四部稿 [KR4e0201](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0201) — Wáng Shìzhēn, the encyclopedic *Hòu qī zǐ* compendium and the largest *jí* in the division.
- c. 1570–1610 — *Gǔchéng shānguǎn shījí* 穀城山館詩集 [KR4e0219](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0219) — Yú Shènxíng, late-Wànlì continuation of the archaist line.
- c. 1601–1645 — *Liú Jíshān jí* 劉蕺山集 [KR4e0230](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0230) — Liú Zōngzhōu, last great Míng Confucian, *Dōnglín / Jíshān* lineage.
- 1622–1644 — *Ní Wénzhēn jí* 倪文貞集 [KR4e0240](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4e/KR4e0240) — Ní Yuánlù, Chóngzhēn-court martyr, suicide at the fall of Beijing 1644.

# 別集類清 (KR4f)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4f 別集類(清) *Biéjí lèi (Qīng)* — Belles-Lettres — Individual Collections of the Qīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/)

*Belles-Lettres — Individual Literary Collections of the Qīng Dynasty*

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR4f sits within KR4 集部 *Jíbù* (the fourth of the four 四部 divisions of the SKQS classification — *Jīng, Shǐ, Zǐ, Jí*) and gathers individual literary collections (*biéjí* 別集 — a single author's collected prose, poetry, and lyric, as distinct from the *zǒngjí* 總集 anthologies of multiple authors) of the Qīng dynasty (清, 1644–1911). All 69 catalog entries in KR4f are Qīng works, including a handful of Míng-Qīng-transition *yímín* 遺民 (Ming-loyalist) figures conventionally classified under their Qīng-dynasty productive years. The Qīng *biéjí* corpus is the largest in Chinese bibliographic history: Wilkinson §66.4.9 records that Ke Yuchun's 2002 *Qīngrén shīwénjí zǒngmù tíyào* lists some 40,000 collected works of over 19,700 Qīng literati, of which only a fraction were printed and a still smaller fraction transmitted to modern collections. The 69 works in KR4f therefore represent a doubly-filtered canon.

Two distinct curatorial filters shape the selection. The *Sìkù quánshū* 文淵閣 selection (1773–1782) admitted Qīng authors approved by the imperial editorial board — Hānlín officials, high-provincial figures, Cheng-Zhu orthodox writers, plus the Kāngxī-Yōngzhèng-Qiánlóng imperial *yùzhì* 御製 collections — and systematically excluded Ming-loyalist authors on political grounds, so that [顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6), [黃宗羲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%AE%97%E7%BE%B2), [王夫之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A4%AB%E4%B9%8B), and [錢謙益](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%8C%A2%E8%AC%99%E7%9B%8A) are absent from WYG. The *Sìbù cóngkān* 四部叢刊 selection (1919–1936) restored these *yímín* collections and added important later figures — [姚鼐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E9%BC%90), [全祖望](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%A8%E7%A5%96%E6%9C%9B), [戴震](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%B4%E9%9C%87), [錢大昕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%8C%A2%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%95), [阮元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%98%AE%E5%85%83), [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80), [龔自珍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BE%94%E8%87%AA%E7%8F%8D), [曾國藩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%BE%E5%9C%8B%E8%97%A9) — whose *biéjí* circulated in the Qīng only in family imprints or Tóng-zhì-era post-Tài-píng restoration reprints. Together the two filters preserve roughly complementary canons of Qīng literature.

Three principal Qīng literary-theoretical traditions structure the division: the *Shényùn* 神韻 school of poetic indirection centered on [王士禛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A3%AB%E7%A6%9B); the Tóngchéng 桐城 school of *gǔwén* 古文 prose, descending from [方苞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%B9%E8%8B%9E) through 劉大櫆 to [姚鼐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E9%BC%90) (the Yánghú 陽湖 offshoot of [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80) and [惲敬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%B2%E6%95%AC) partly broke with this synthesis — Wilkinson, Box 173); and the *Chángzhōu* 常州 and *Zhèxī* 浙西 *cí* 詞 schools of allusive lyric, descending from [陳維崧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E7%B6%AD%E5%B4%A7) and [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) in the early Qīng through [厲鶚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8E%B2%E9%B6%9A) to [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80)'s late-imperial *Cí xuǎn* 詞選 program. Cross-cutting these is the great *kǎozhèng* 考證 (evidential research) movement of the late Qiánlóng / early Jiāqìng generation — [戴震](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%B4%E9%9C%87), [錢大昕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%8C%A2%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%95), [盧文弨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9B%A7%E6%96%87%E5%BC%A8), [孫星衍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%98%9F%E8%A1%8D), [洪亮吉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E4%BA%AE%E5%90%89), [汪中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%AA%E4%B8%AD), [阮元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%98%AE%E5%85%83) — whose *biéjí* preserve the polemical, biographical, and methodological apparatus surrounding the technical monographs catalogued elsewhere in KR1–KR3. The late-Qīng *Gōngyáng* 公羊 New-Text Confucian tradition that runs from [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80) through [龔自珍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BE%94%E8%87%AA%E7%8F%8D) to the Hundred-Days Reform generation supplies the diagnostic vocabulary of dynastic decline that closes the division.

### Important texts and text clusters

**Early-Qīng *yímín* prose and verse.** The three great early-Qīng Confucians — [顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6) in [KR4f0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0006) *Tínglín shījí* 亭林詩集 and [KR4f0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0007) *Tínglín yújí* 亭林餘集; [黃宗羲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%AE%97%E7%BE%B2) in [KR4f0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0008) *Nánléi wénàn* 南雷文案; [王夫之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A4%AB%E4%B9%8B) in [KR4f0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0009) *Jiāngzhāi shīwénjí* 薑齋詩文集 — were excluded by the *Sìkù* as politically inadmissible and survive in pre-modern print only via the SBCK. To these belong [KR4f0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0010) / [KR4f0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0011) *Mùzhāi chūxué jí* / *Yǒuxué jí* 牧齋初學集 / 牧齋有學集 of [錢謙益](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%8C%A2%E8%AC%99%E7%9B%8A) (the surrendered late-Míng grand secretary whose poetics shaped the *Yúshān* 虞山 tradition); [KR4f0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0021) *Jūyìtáng jí* 居易堂集 of [徐枋](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E6%9E%8B) (a recluse who refused all Qīng patronage); and [KR4f0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0069) *Míngzhāi jí* 茗齋集 of [彭孫貽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E5%AD%AB%E8%B2%BD).

**Imperial *yùzhì* collections.** [KR4f0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0001) *Shèngzǔ rén huángdì yùzhì wénjí* 聖祖仁皇帝御製文集 (the Kāngxī emperor, 176 juan); [KR4f0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0002) *Shìzōng xiàn huángdì yùzhì wénjí* 世宗憲皇帝御製文集 (the Yōngzhèng emperor, 30 juan); [KR4f0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0003) *Yùzhì lèshàntáng quánjí dìngběn* 御製樂善堂全集定本 (the Qiánlóng emperor's prince-period writings, re-edited under his reign); [KR4f0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0004) *Yùzhì wénjí* 御製文集 and [KR4f0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0005) *Yùzhì shījí* 御製詩集 (Qiánlóng's reign-era prose and 454-juan poetry — the single largest text in KR4f). These four imperial corpora are the principal documentary record of high-Qīng court intellectual culture and of the imperial editorial program that produced the *Sìkù quánshū* itself.

**Early-Qīng Hànlín literary circle.** [KR4f0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0012) / [KR4f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0013) *Méicūn jí* / *Méicūn jiāzànggǎo* 梅村集 / 梅村家藏藁 of [吳偉業](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E5%81%89%E6%A5%AD) Wú Wěiyè (Ming-loyalist who later took Qīng office); [KR4f0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0019) *Jīng huá lù* 精華錄 of [王士禛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A3%AB%E7%A6%9B) Wáng Shìzhēn (founder of *Shényùn*); [KR4f0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0020) *Yáofēng wénchāo* 堯峯文鈔 of [汪琬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%AA%E7%90%AC); [KR4f0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0022) *Wǔtíng wénbiān* 午亭文編 of [陳廷敬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E5%BB%B7%E6%95%AC); [KR4f0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0025) *Pùshūtíng jí* 曝書亭集 of [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) Zhū Yízūn (founder of the *Zhèxī* *cí* school); [KR4f0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0029) *Wénduān jí* 文端集 of [張英](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E8%8B%B1); [KR4f0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0030) *Xīhé jí* 西河集 of [毛奇齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E5%A5%87%E9%BD%A1) Máo Qílíng (the most prolific early-Qīng polemicist, 189 juan — the largest single-author *biéjí* in the division); [KR4f0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0031) *Chén Jiǎntǎo sìliù* 陳檢討四六 and [KR4f0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0032) *Chén Jiālíng wénjí* 陳迦陵文集 of [陳維崧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E7%B6%AD%E5%B4%A7) (founder of the *Yángxiàn* *cí* school).

**Cheng-Zhu Lǐxué officials.** [KR4f0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0014) *Tāngzǐ yíshū* 湯子遺書 of [湯斌](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%AF%E6%96%8C); [KR4f0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0015) *Jiānjìtáng wénjí* 兼濟堂文集 of [魏裔介](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E8%A3%94%E4%BB%8B); [KR4f0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0039) *Róngcūn jí* 榕村集 of [李光地](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%85%89%E5%9C%B0) (Kāngxī's principal Sòng-school adviser); [KR4f0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0040) *Sānyútáng wénjí* 三魚堂文集 of [陸隴其](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E9%9A%B4%E5%85%B6); [KR4f0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0043) *Èrxītáng wénjí* 二希堂文集 of [蔡世遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E4%B8%96%E9%81%A0). The documentary record of the Qīng *Lǐxué* establishment that anchored the dynasty's Confucian-orthodox ideological program.

**Tóngchéng prose tradition.** [KR4f0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0045) *Wàngxī jí* 望溪集 of [方苞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%B9%E8%8B%9E) Fāng Bāo (the founder) and [KR4f0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0052) *Xībàoxuān wénjí* 惜抱軒文集 of [姚鼐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E9%BC%90) Yáo Nài (the second-generation synthesizer of *yìlǐ*, *kǎojù*, *cízhāng*) together define Tóngchéng doctrine. Yáo's parallel anthology *Gǔwéncí lèizuǎn* 古文辭類纂 — not in KR4f — became the standard composition textbook of late-imperial China and the Republican period.

**Mid-Qīng *Zhèxī* lyric and Sòng-poetic line.** [KR4f0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0044) *Jìngyètáng shījí* 敬業堂詩集 of [查慎行](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%A5%E6%85%8E%E8%A1%8C) (the leading early-Qīng Sòng / Lù Yóu line poet); [KR4f0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0049) *Fánxiè shānfáng jí* 樊榭山房集 of [厲鶚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8E%B2%E9%B6%9A) (third in the canonical *Zhèxī* *cí* line after Zhū Yízūn, also the foundational mid-Qīng Sòng-poetry historian via his *Sòng shī jì shì* 宋詩紀事).

**The *kǎozhèng* generation.** [KR4f0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0053) *Dài Dōngyuán jí* 戴東原集 of [戴震](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%B4%E9%9C%87) (the central Qián-Jiā intellectual figure); [KR4f0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0054) *Jíqítíng jí* 鮚埼亭集 and [KR4f0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0055) *Jíqítíng shījí* 鮚埼亭詩集 of [全祖望](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%A8%E7%A5%96%E6%9C%9B) (the *Zhèdōng* historiographer who continued Huáng Zōngxī's *Sòng-Yuán xuéàn*); [KR4f0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0058) *Bàojīngtáng wénjí* 抱經堂文集 of [盧文弨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9B%A7%E6%96%87%E5%BC%A8); [KR4f0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0059) *Qiányántáng wénjí* 潛研堂文集 of [錢大昕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%8C%A2%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%95) (foremost historical philologist of the generation); [KR4f0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0056) *Hóng Běijiāng shīwénjí* 洪北江詩文集 of [洪亮吉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E4%BA%AE%E5%90%89); [KR4f0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0057) *Sūn Yuānrú shīwénjí* 孫淵如詩文集 of [孫星衍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%98%9F%E8%A1%8D); [KR4f0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0060) / [KR4f0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0061) *Shùxué nèipiān* 述學內篇 / *Róngfǔ xiānshēng yíshī* 容甫先生遺詩 of [汪中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%AA%E4%B8%AD); [KR4f0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0050) *Guǒtáng jí* 果堂集 of [沈彤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B2%88%E5%BD%A4); [KR4f0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0062) *Yánjīngshì yījí* 揅經室一集 of [阮元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%98%AE%E5%85%83) (the institutional architect of late-Qiánlóng *kǎozhèng*, founder of the Gūshān 詁經精舍 and Xuéhǎitáng 學海堂 academies). This is the largest single cluster in the division and supplies the literary-personal complement to the technical *kǎozhèng* monographs scattered through KR1, KR2, and KR3.

**Chángzhōu / Yánghú school and late-Qīng *Gōngyáng*.** [KR4f0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0063) *Dàyún shānfáng wéngǎo* 大雲山房文稿 of [惲敬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%B2%E6%95%AC) (Yánghú co-founder); [KR4f0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0066) *Míngkē wén chūbiān* 茗柯文初編 and [KR4f0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0067) *Míngkē wén bǔbiān* 茗柯文補編 of [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80) (Yánghú co-founder, *Yúshì Yì* 虞氏易 specialist, founder of the Chángzhōu *cí* school via the *Cí xuǎn xù* 詞選序); [KR4f0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0064) *Dìngān wénjí* 定盦文集 and [KR4f0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0065) *Dìngān wénjí bǔbiān* 定盦文集補編 of [龔自珍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BE%94%E8%87%AA%E7%8F%8D) (the late-Cháng-zhōu *Gōngyáng* prophet of Qīng decline; maternal grandson of [段玉裁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AE%B5%E7%8E%89%E8%A3%81), student of Liú Fénglù 劉逢祿).

**Late-Qīng restoration.** [KR4f0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0068) *Zēng Wénzhènggōng shījí* 曾文正公詩集 of [曾國藩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%BE%E5%9C%8B%E8%97%A9) (Tóngzhì restoration statesman, suppressor of the Tàipíng, principal Self-Strengthening leader, posthumously honored *Wénzhèng* 文正).

### Important persons

- [聖祖玄燁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%81%96%E7%A5%96%E7%8E%84%E7%87%81) (1654–1722) — the Kāngxī emperor; his *yùzhì wénjí* is the documentary heart of early-high-Qīng imperial-literary culture and supplies the imperial side of debates carried elsewhere by his senior officials.
- [顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6) (1613–1682) — founder of Qīng *kǎozhèng*; his poetry in KR4f supplies the early-Qīng *yímín* lyric tradition.
- [黃宗羲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%AE%97%E7%BE%B2) (1610–1695) — founder of the *Zhèdōng* historical school; his prose carries the political-philosophical kernels later elaborated in the *Míng yí dài fǎng lù*.
- [王夫之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A4%AB%E4%B9%8B) (1619–1692) — third of the three great early-Qīng Confucians; *yímín* poet-philosopher of Héngyáng.

### Topics

- **The *Sìkù* / SBCK divide.** The Qīng *biéjí* corpus is uniquely shaped by two successive curatorial filters separated by 130 years. The *Sìkù quánshū* (1773–1782) excluded Ming-loyalist authors on political grounds; the *Sìbù cóngkān* (1919–1936) restored these and added important later figures whose collections circulated only in family imprints. The textual provenance of each KR4f entry (WYG vs. SBCK) is therefore the key bibliographic signal of its political-and-canonical status.

- **The *Shényùn* / Sòng-poetic divide.** [王士禛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A3%AB%E7%A6%9B)'s *Shényùn* school of poetic indirection — derived from Wáng Wéi and Yán Yǔ's *Cānglàng shīhuà* — dominated Kāngxī Yōngzhèng critical taste; the principal counter-tradition was the Sòng-poetic line (Lù Yóu, Yuán Hàowèn, Chén Shīdào), represented by [查慎行](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%A5%E6%85%8E%E8%A1%8C) and by the *Zhèxī* *cí*-and-Sòng-poetics school of [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) and [厲鶚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8E%B2%E9%B6%9A). The *Sìkù* programmatic preference for *Shényùn* shaped the inclusion-and-evaluation language of many tíyào.

- **The Tóngchéng / Yánghú dispute.** The Tóngchéng program of [方苞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%B9%E8%8B%9E) and [姚鼐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E9%BC%90) sought to unite *yìlǐ* (Sòng moral metaphysics), *kǎojù* (Hàn-Qīng evidential philology), and *cízhāng* (literary craft) under a single *gǔwén* method. The Yánghú offshoot of [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80) and [惲敬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%B2%E6%95%AC) broke partly with this synthesis, accommodating *pián* parallel-prose and Chángzhōu *kǎozhèng* in a more eclectic mode (Wilkinson, Box 173). The dispute structures the entire second half of the division.

- **The *Chángzhōu cí* / *Zhèxī cí* succession.** The early-Qīng *cí* revival had two principal regional traditions: the *Yángxiàn* of [陳維崧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E7%B6%AD%E5%B4%A7) and the *Zhèxī* of [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A). The *Zhèxī* tradition descended through [厲鶚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8E%B2%E9%B6%9A) to the early-Jiāqìng generation, where [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80)'s *Cí xuǎn xù* (preserved in [KR4f0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0066) *Míngkē wén chūbiān*) inaugurated a new *Chángzhōu* program emphasizing allegorical depth — the dominant late-imperial *cí* doctrine through 1900.

- **The Qián-Jiā *kǎozhèng* personal record.** The mid- to late-Qīng *biéjí* serve as the personal-biographical apparatus of the evidential-research movement. Prefaces, friendship-letters, *bēizhì* 碑誌 epitaphs, *zhuàn* 傳 biographies, and *jì* 記 records here document the social networks among [戴震](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%88%B4%E9%9C%87), [錢大昕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%8C%A2%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%95), [盧文弨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9B%A7%E6%96%87%E5%BC%A8), [孫星衍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%98%9F%E8%A1%8D), [洪亮吉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B4%AA%E4%BA%AE%E5%90%89), [汪中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%AA%E4%B8%AD), [段玉裁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AE%B5%E7%8E%89%E8%A3%81), and [阮元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%98%AE%E5%85%83) — while their technical *kǎozhèng* monographs are catalogued separately across KR1, KR2, and KR3.

- **The late-Qīng *Gōngyáng* and dynastic-decline diagnosis.** From Liú Fénglù through [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80) to [龔自珍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BE%94%E8%87%AA%E7%8F%8D), the Chángzhōu *Gōngyáng* New-Text Confucian tradition supplied late-Qīng intellectuals with a critical idiom for diagnosing dynastic decline — the *sān shì* 三世 (three-age) and *yī tǒng* 一統 (unified-rule) doctrines, recast as periodization of Qīng crisis. The vocabulary descends to Kāng Yǒuwéi's *Dàtóng shū* and Liáng Qǐchāo's late-Qīng historiography. [KR4f0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0064) *Dìngān wénjí* is the principal documentary node for this transition.

- **The Tàipíng / Tóngzhì restoration filter.** Many late-Qīng *biéjí* in KR4f (the 1869 reprint of [KR4f0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0066) *Míngkē wén* with [曾國藩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%BE%E5%9C%8B%E8%97%A9)'s preface; the 1860s Wú Xù imprint of [KR4f0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4f/KR4f0064) *Dìngān wénjí*) are explicitly products of the post-Tài-píng restoration program — the Tóng-zhì-era project to recover the Jiāngnán literary record after the destruction of 1850–1864. The prefaces of these editions are themselves a documentary record of the restoration.

# 總集類 (KR4h)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4h 總集類 *Zǒngjí lèi* — Collected Works — General Anthologies](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR4h is the **總集類** (*Zǒngjí lèi*, "general anthologies") of the **集部** (*Jíbù*, Literature branch) — the third of the five *Sìkù* sub-categories of belles-lettres, sitting alongside *Chǔcí* 楚辭, *biéjí* 别集 (collected works of individuals), *shīwén píng* 詩文評 (literary criticism), and *cí/qǔ* 詞曲. As Wilkinson notes in §30.3 (General Anthologies), the *Sìkù* editors used *zǒngjí* in contrast to *biéjí* — *biéjí* gathers the writings of one author, *zǒngjí* the writings of many. Together, these two categories carry the bulk of the *Jíbù*, which by the eighteenth century constituted thirty-seven percent of the *Sìkù quánshū* — far the largest of the four branches (Wilkinson §30.1, Table 37). Although poetry (*shī* 詩) is never given a *Sìkù* category of its own, it is in practice the first and most prestigious genre within both *biéjí* and *zǒngjí*; rhapsodies (*fù* 賦), parallel prose (*piánwén* 駢文), ancient-style prose (*gǔwén* 古文), examination essays, *yuèfǔ* 樂府 songs, regulated verse (*lǜshī* 律詩), quatrains (*juéjù* 絕句), and palace verse (*gōngcí* 宮詞) all follow.

The division's chronological span runs from the early-sixth-century *Wén xuǎn* 文選 [KR4h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0001) of Xiāo Tǒng 蕭統, Crown Prince Zhāomíng of the Liáng, down to the great Qiánlóng-era imperially-sponsored anthologies (*Yùxuǎn Táng-Sòng wén chún* [KR4h0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0147), *Sì shū wén* [KR4h0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0150) etc.) and on to twentieth-century critical compilations (*Quán Táng wén* [KR4h0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0168), *Táng shī sānbǎi shǒu* [KR4h0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0169), *Quán Sòng cí* [KR4h0170](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0170), *Dūnhuáng biànwén xuǎnzhù* [KR4h0171](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0171)). Two transmissional axes run through the whole. The first is the **canon-defining axis**: the *Wén xuǎn* establishes a genre-based literary canon in the early Liáng, the *Wényuàn yīnghuá* 文苑英華 [KR4h0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0022) of 982–987 extends it through the Táng under the *Wén xuǎn*'s own genre grid, the *Sòng wénjiàn* 宋文鑑 [KR4h0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0040) of Lǚ Zǔqiān (1177–1179) does the same for the Northern Sòng, the *Yuán wénlèi* 元文類 [KR4h0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0081) of Sū Tiānjué for the Yuán, the *Míng wénhéng* 明文衡 [KR4h0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0102) and *Míng wén hǎi* 明文海 [KR4h0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0152) for the Míng, and the Kāngxī-era *Quán Táng shī* 全唐詩 [KR4h0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0140) and its parallels close the loop with imperially-determined comprehensive recensions of period-defining corpora. The second is the **pedagogical-canonical axis**: the *gǔwén* 古文 line that runs from Lǚ Zǔqiān's *Gǔwén guānjiàn* 古文關鍵 [KR4h0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0041) through Lóu Fǎng's *Chónggǔ wénjué* [KR4h0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0044), Zhēn Déxiù's *Wénzhāng zhèngzōng* [KR4h0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0046), Xiè Fāngdé's *Wénzhāng guǐfàn* [KR4h0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0059), and Máo Kūn's *Táng-Sòng bā dà jiā wén chāo* [KR4h0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0115) — the textbook tradition that supplied the civil-service examination its prose models and that culminates, beyond the borders of this division, in Yáo Nài's *Gǔwénci lèizuǎn* and Wú Chǔcái's *Gǔwén guānzhǐ* (Wilkinson §30.3.1, Box 174–175).

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Wén xuǎn* 文選 [KR4h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0001) — Xiāo Tǒng's c. 526–531 anthology of pre-Liáng literature in 37(–39) genres is the genre-defining ancestor of every later *zǒngjí*; from the Táng onward "the *Wén xuǎn* thoroughly done, half a *xiùcái* won" (Wilkinson §30.3.1). The Tang annotators recast it as the Lǐ Shàn 李善 commentary [KR4h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0002) and the *Liù chén zhù* [KR4h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0003) (Lǐ Shàn plus the Five Officials), and a separate Yuán-period critical study of its principal poets [KR4h0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0004) survives.
- *Yùtái xīnyǒng* 玉臺新詠 [KR4h0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0005) — Xú Líng's mid-sixth-century anthology of love poetry, the principal Liáng counter-tradition to the *Wén xuǎn*'s ethical-aesthetic balance (Wilkinson §30.1, view (2)); read in the Qīng through Jì Róngshū's textual study [KR4h0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0006).
- The **Táng small-anthology cluster** ([KR4h0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0008)–[KR4h0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0020)) — *Héyuè yīnglíng jí* [KR4h0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0009) (Yīn Fán, 753), *Guóxiù jí* [KR4h0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0010), *Zhōngxìng jiānqì jí* [KR4h0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0012), *Jíxuán jí* [KR4h0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0013), *Sōnglíng jí* [KR4h0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0014), *Cáidiào jí* [KR4h0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0019), et al. — together preserve the bulk of what survives from middle and late Táng poetry outside the *Quán Táng shī*'s later recovery efforts; they are the principal pre-Sòng source for Táng poetic taste and circle-formation.
- *Wényuàn yīnghuá* 文苑英華 [KR4h0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0022) — Lǐ Fǎng's 982 imperial committee work in 1,000 *juàn*, conceived as the continuation of the *Wén xuǎn* and the chief Northern-Sòng vessel for Táng and Five-Dynasties prose and poetry; Péng Shūxià's *Biànzhèng* [KR4h0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0023) is its textual companion.
- *Táng wéncuì* 唐文粹 [KR4h0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0024) — Yáo Xuàn's 1011 hundred-*juàn* distillation of *Wényuàn yīnghuá* into *gǔwén* canon, retroactively defining the prose canon of the Táng for later generations.
- *Yuèfǔ shījí* 樂府詩集 [KR4h0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0034) — Guō Màoqiàn's late-Northern-Sòng compilation in 100 *juàn* is the indispensable anthology of *yuèfǔ* from Hàn through Táng and the principal source for early Chinese musical-literary history; later supplemented by Méi Dǐngzuò's *Gǔ yuèyuàn* 古樂苑 [KR4h0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0119).
- *Sòng wénjiàn* 宋文鑑 [KR4h0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0040) — Lǚ Zǔqiān's 1177–1179 imperially-commissioned anthology of Northern Sòng prose; the foundational *zǒngjí* for the period, paralleling for the Sòng what the *Wényuàn yīnghuá* had been for the Táng.
- **Gǔwén pedagogical cluster** — *Gǔwén guānjiàn* [KR4h0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0041) (Lǚ Zǔqiān), *Chónggǔ wénjué* [KR4h0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0044) (Lóu Fǎng), *Wénzhāng zhèngzōng* [KR4h0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0046) and *Xù Wénzhāng zhèngzōng* [KR4h0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0047) (Zhēn Déxiù), *Wénzhāng guǐfàn* [KR4h0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0059) (Xiè Fāngdé), and *Táng-Sòng bā dà jiā wén chāo* [KR4h0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0115) (Máo Kūn). Between them they domesticated the prose of Hán Yù 韓愈, Liǔ Zōngyuán 柳宗元, Ōuyáng Xiū 歐陽修, Sū Shì 蘇軾 and the rest of the Eight Masters into the staple curriculum of Sòng-through-Qīng civil-service candidates.
- *Jiānghú xiǎojí* / *Jiānghú hòují* [KR4h0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0053)–[KR4h0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0054) — Chén Qǐ's Hángzhōu-publisher anthologies of Southern Sòng *jiānghú* poets, the principal vehicle for the Yǒngjiā Four Spirits 永嘉四靈 and the *jiānghú* poetic movement.
- *Zhōngzhōu jí* 中州集 [KR4h0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0069) — Yuán Hàowèn's anthology with poet-biographies of the Jīn dynasty, the single most important source for Jīn-dynasty literary history and the model later extended in Wáng Shìzhēn's *Yùdìng Zhōngzhōu jí zēngbǔ* [KR4h0144](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0144).
- *Yíngkuí lǜsuǐ* 瀛奎律髓 [KR4h0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0074) — Fāng Huí's late-Sòng / early-Yuán anthology of *lǜshī* organised by theme, foundational to subsequent reading of Táng and Sòng regulated verse and the textual fount for the Jiāng-xī-school 江西派 reception of Dù Fǔ 杜甫.
- *Yuán wénlèi* 元文類 [KR4h0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0081) — Sū Tiānjué's mid-fourteenth-century anthology of Yuán-dynasty prose, the parallel to *Sòng wénjiàn* for the Yuán.
- *Táng shī pǐnhuì* 唐詩品彙 [KR4h0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0095) — Gāo Bǐng's 1393 ninety-juàn anthology and its later *Shíyí*, the work that codified the four-period periodisation of Táng poetry (*chūshèngzhōngwǎn* 初盛中晚) that would dominate critical reception for half a millennium.
- **Méi Dǐngzuò 梅鼎祚 *Wénjì* series** — *Pángà wénjì* [KR4h0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0120), *Xī Hàn wénjì* [KR4h0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0121), *Dōng Hàn wénjì* [KR4h0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0122), *Xī-Jìn wénjì* [KR4h0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0123), *Sòng wénjì* [KR4h0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0124), *Nán Qí wénjì* [KR4h0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0125), *Liáng wénjì* [KR4h0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0126), *Chén wénjì* [KR4h0127](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0127), *Běi-Qí wénjì* [KR4h0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0128), *Hòu Zhōu wénjì* [KR4h0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0129), *Suí wénjì* [KR4h0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0130), *Shì wénjì* [KR4h0131](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0131) — the late-Míng dynasty-by-dynasty prose project that compiled, in twelve linked volumes, the surviving prose of every dynasty from high antiquity through the Suí. This was the principal pre-modern attempt at a "complete prose" of the early empire, and Yán Kějūn 嚴可均's *Quán shànggǔ Sāndài Qín Hàn Sānguó Liùcháo wén* in the nineteenth century built directly on it (Wilkinson §30.3.2).
- *Yùdìng Quán Táng shī* 御定全唐詩 [KR4h0140](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0140) — Péng Dìngqiú's 1705–1707 Kāngxī-commissioned compilation in 900 *juàn*, with c. 48,900 poems by c. 2,200 authors, the most authoritative pre-modern corpus of any single dynasty's poetry; supplemented by *Yùdìng Quán Táng shī lù* [KR4h0161](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0161).
- **Kāngxī imperially-sponsored anthology cluster** — *Yùxuǎn gǔwén yuānjiàn* [KR4h0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0138), *Yùdìng lìdài fùhuì* [KR4h0139](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0139), *Yùdìng Pèiwénzhāi yǒngwù shīxuǎn* [KR4h0141](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0141), *Yùdìng lìdài tíhuà shīlèi* [KR4h0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0142), *Yùxuǎn Sòng Jīn Yuán Míng sìcháo shī* [KR4h0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0143), *Yùxuǎn Táng shī* [KR4h0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0145); later, in the Qiánlóng reign, *Yùxuǎn Táng-Sòng wén chún* [KR4h0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0147) and *Yùxuǎn Táng-Sòng shī chún* [KR4h0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0148). Together they constitute the most ambitious imperial-anthology programme in Chinese history and the basis for nearly every subsequent claim about the corpus of Táng-Sòng-Yuán-Míng literature.
- *Míng shī zōng* 明詩綜 [KR4h0156](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0156), *Sòng shī chāo* [KR4h0157](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0157), *Yuán shī xuǎn* [KR4h0160](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0160) — Zhū Yízūn 朱彝尊 and the *Sòng shī chāo* compilers under Wú Zhīzhèn, the Qīng dynasty-by-dynasty poetry compilations that brought the *Wénjì* programme into the late-imperial period for poetry.
- *Quán Táng wén* 全唐文 [KR4h0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0168), *Táng shī sānbǎi shǒu* 唐詩三百首 [KR4h0169](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0169), *Quán Sòng cí* 全宋詞 [KR4h0170](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0170), *Dūnhuáng biànwén xuǎnzhù* [KR4h0171](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0171) — the late-imperial and twentieth-century closures of the anthology tradition: the *Quán Táng wén* of 1814 as the prose counterpart of the *Quán Táng shī*, Sūn Zhū's *Tángshī sānbǎi shǒu* of 1763 as the most influential late-imperial pedagogical canon, Táng Guīzhāng's *Quán Sòng cí* (1940/65) as the modern-philological completion of the Sòng *cí* corpus, and the *Dūnhuáng biànwén xuǎnzhù* as the manuscript-recovery supplement.

- [蕭統](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%95%AD%E7%B5%B1) (Xiāo Tǒng, 501–531) — Crown Prince Zhāomíng of the Liáng, patron-editor of [KR4h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0001) and the figurehead of the court editorial circle that produced the foundational Chinese literary anthology.

- [郭茂倩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E8%8C%82%E5%80%A9) (Guō Màoqiàn, fl. 1085–1099) — compiler of [KR4h0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0034) and the single most important pre-modern editor of the *yuèfǔ* tradition.
