### Topics

- **The *Wén xuǎn* genre grid.** Wilkinson §30.3.1, Box 174, lists the thirty-seven-to-thirty-nine genres recognised by Xiāo Tǒng's editorial circle — *fù* 賦, *shī* 詩, *sāo* 騷, *qī* 七, *zhào* 詔, *cè* 策, *biǎo* 表, *shàngshū* 上書, *qǐ* 啟, *jiān* 牋, *zòujì* 奏記, *shū* 書, *xí* 檄, *duìwèn* 對問, *shèlùn* 設論, *cí* 辭, *xù* 序, *sòng* 頌, *zàn* 贊, *fúmìng* 符命, *shǐlùn* 史論, *shǐshùzàn* 史述贊, *lùn* 論, *liánzhū* 連珠, *zhēn* 箴, *míng* 銘, *lěi* 誄, *āi* 哀, *bēiwén* 碑文, *mùzhì* 墓誌, *xíngzhuàng* 行狀, *diàowén* 弔文, *jìwén* 祭文, and others. This grid was reproduced (with minor adjustments) by *Wényuàn yīnghuá*, *Sòng wénjiàn*, *Yuán wénlèi*, *Míng wénhéng*, and Méi Dǐngzuò's *Wénjì* series; the rival grid (Yáo Nài's *Gǔwénci lèizuǎn*, Box 175, with thirteen classes) belongs largely to the eighteenth-century *gǔwén* tradition outside this division.
- **The 古文 (*gǔwén*) movement and the examination canon.** From Lǚ Zǔqiān's *Gǔwén guānjiàn* through Lóu Fǎng, Zhēn Déxiù, Xiè Fāngdé, and Máo Kūn to the eighteenth-century Tóngchéng school, *zǒngjí* compilation tracked — and shaped — the prose curriculum of the civil-service examination. The "Eight Great Masters of Táng and Sòng" canon (Hán Yù, Liǔ Zōngyuán, Ōuyáng Xiū, Sū Xún, Sū Shì, Sū Zhé, Wáng Ānshí, Zēng Gǒng) is a product of this anthologising tradition, not a fact about Chinese literary history independent of it.
- **Periodisation of Táng poetry.** Gāo Bǐng's *Táng shī pǐnhuì* [KR4h0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0095) formalises the *chūshèngzhōngwǎn* four-period model, which structures the *Yùdìng Quán Táng shī* and almost every Míng-Qīng Táng-poetry anthology — even when, as in the Kāngxī Emperor's preface to *Quán Táng shī*, the imposed periodisation is itself overtly rejected.
- **The *yuèfǔ* tradition.** Guō Màoqiàn's [KR4h0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0034) organises *yuèfǔ* into the twelve canonical sub-genres (*jiāomiào gēcí* 郊廟歌辭, *yānshè gēcí* 燕射歌辭, *gǔchuī qūcí* 鼓吹曲辭, *héngchuī qūcí* 橫吹曲辭, *xiānghé gēcí* 相和歌辭, *qīngshāng qūcí* 清商曲辭, *wǔqū gēcí* 舞曲歌辭, *qínqū gēcí* 琴曲歌辭, *zámiào gēcí* 雜謠歌辭, *jìndài qūcí* 近代曲辭, *zágē yáocí* 雜歌謠辭, *xīn yuèfǔ cí* 新樂府辭), a classification taken up by Méi Dǐngzuò's [KR4h0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0119) and still followed by modern editions.
- **Imperial sponsorship.** Three peaks: Sòng Tàizōng's *Wényuàn yīnghuá* programme (980s), Lǚ Zǔqiān's *fèngchì* compilation of *Sòng wénjiàn* (1170s), and the Kāngxī–Qiánlóng programme that runs from *Yùxuǎn gǔwén yuānjiàn* (1685) through *Yùdìng Quán Táng shī* (1707) to *Yùxuǎn Táng-Sòng shī chún* (1750). All three were politically motivated as much as scholarly — anthology as imperial legitimation through cultural inheritance.
- **The local and regional anthology.** *Huìjī duōyīng zǒngjí* [KR4h0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0028), *Yánlíng jí* [KR4h0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0036), *Wúdū wéncuì* [KR4h0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0057) / *xùjí* [KR4h0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0116), *Tiāntái qiánjí* [KR4h0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0048), *Chìchéng jí* [KR4h0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0049), *Wǎnlíng qúnyīng jí* [KR4h0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0080), *Guǎngzhōu sì xiānshēng shī* [KR4h0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0096), *Mǐnzhōng shízǐ shī* [KR4h0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0098), *Quán-Shǔ yìwén zhì* [KR4h0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0109), *Yǒngshàng qíjiù shī* [KR4h0162](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0162), *Zuìlǐ shī xì* [KR4h0163](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0163), *Póyáng wǔjiā jí* [KR4h0165](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0165) — Wilkinson §30.3.3 treats these "Anthologies of Specific Places" as a distinct sub-type, important sources for local literary culture.
- **The dynastic-complete anthology programme.** Méi Dǐngzuò's *Wénjì* series in the late Míng, then Yán Kějūn's *Quán shànggǔ Sāndài Qín Hàn Sānguó Liùcháo wén* (in the wake of and partly outside this division), then the Kāngxī *Quán Táng shī* and Qiánlóng-era successors, then the twentieth-century *Quán Sòng wén*, *Quán Yuán wén*, *Quán Sòng cí*, *Quán Yuán shī* — a continuous ambition, from the sixteenth century forward, to compile the "complete" surviving literature of each dynasty.
- **Examination-essay anthologies.** *Lùnxué shéngchǐ* [KR4h0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0056), *Wénzhāng guǐfàn* [KR4h0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0059), *Zēngzhù Tángcè* [KR4h0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0064), *Shí xiānshēng àolùn zhù* [KR4h0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0066), *Wén biān* [KR4h0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0106), *Jīngyì mófàn* [KR4h0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0105), and ultimately the Qiánlóng-imperial *Sì shū wén* [KR4h0150](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0150) — anthologies that targeted the *bāgǔ wén* 八股文 and decree-essay sub-genres of the examination system, a sub-corpus that the *Sìkù* editors largely tolerated rather than celebrated.
- **Recovery of lost early poetry.** A tradition of *jì* 紀 and *xuǎn* 選 that aimed to reconstruct early corpora — *Gǔshī jì* [KR4h0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0107) of Féng Wéinè, with Féng Shù's *Shījì kuāngmiù* [KR4h0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0108) as its critical companion, and Méi Dǐngzuò's *Hàn-Wèi Liùcháo bǎisānjiā jí* [KR4h0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4h/KR4h0134) — paving the way for nineteenth-century philological projects.

# 詩文評類 (KR4i)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4i 詩文評類 *Shī wén píng lèi* — Belles-Lettres — Literary Criticism](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR4i 詩文評類 (*Shī wén píng lèi*, "Critiques of Poetry and Prose") is the last of the nine sub-categories of *Jíbù* 集部 (KR4, Belles-Lettres) in the *Sìkù quánshū* 四庫全書 taxonomy. It collects the canon of pre-modern Chinese literary criticism: works that *judge* writing rather than *contain* it. The tradition begins with two Liáng-dynasty 梁 (early 6th c.) monuments — Liú Xié's 劉勰 *Wénxīn diāolóng* 文心雕龍 and Zhōng Róng's 鍾嶸 *Shīpǐn* 詩品 — whose ambition to provide a comprehensive theory of writing was not matched again until the late Míng and Qīng. From the eleventh century onward, criticism became overwhelmingly informal and pointillistic: Ōuyáng Xiū 歐陽修 founded the *shīhuà* 詩話 ("remarks on poetry") in 1071–72, a loose, anecdotal form that Wilkinson (§30.5) describes as "a specialized subgenre of *biji*" 筆記. Some forty Sòng-Yuán-Míng-Qīng *shīhuà*, together with parallel-prose criticism (*sìliù huà* 四六話), epitaph-and-inscription manuals (*jīnshí lì* 金石例 etc.), and examination-essay primers (*zuò yì yào jué* 作義要訣), make up the rest of the division.

The works span roughly thirteen centuries — c. 496 to c. 1778 — and divide cleanly along genre lines: lyric poetry (*shī* 詩), parallel and ornamental prose (*pián* 駢, *sìliù* 四六), examination and stelae prose, and broad surveys of "literature" (*wén* 文) as such. The chronological centre of gravity sits squarely in the Sòng 宋, when the new examination culture and printed-book economy produced the dense network of *shīhuà* whose internal cross-quotation effectively constitutes the canon of Táng and Sòng poetic taste. Cross-references between texts in this division are exceptionally dense: nearly every Southern Sòng *shīhuà* engages with the Jiāngxī 江西 school of Huáng Tíngjiān 黃庭堅 (KR4d), with the *Sūshì* 蘇軾 tradition, and ultimately with the Late-Sòng synthesis of Yán Yǔ's 嚴羽 *Cānglàng shīhuà* 滄浪詩話. Wilkinson's chronological list of literary-critical landmarks (§30.5) overlaps with the KR4i contents but omits the bulk of the Southern Sòng *shīhuà* preserved here.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The two Liáng foundations.** *Wénxīn diāolóng* 文心雕龍 [KR4i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0001) (Liú Xié 劉勰, c. 496–502) is the first comprehensive Chinese treatise on literature, surveying over thirty genres and laying out a theory of style and composition. *Shīpǐn* 詩品 [KR4i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0003) (Zhōng Róng 鍾嶸, c. 513–517) grades 122 poets from the Hàn through the Liáng into three classes, traces their stylistic genealogies, and is the earliest comprehensive history of *shī* 詩. *Wénzhāng yuánqǐ* 文章緣起 [KR4i0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0004) (attributed to Rén Fǎng 任昉; received recension Táng–Qīng), traces the origins of every literary genre to a "first" exemplar.

**The Táng anecdote-criticism precursor.** *Běnshì shī* 本事詩 [KR4i0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0005) (Mèng Qǐ 孟棨, 886) records the biographical occasions for famous Táng poems and is the immediate generic ancestor of the Sòng *shīhuà*.

**The Northern Sòng founding of *shīhuà*.** Ōuyáng Xiū's *Liùyī shīhuà* 六一詩話 [KR4i0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0006) (1071–72) is the earliest work to bear the term *shīhuà* in its title; its sequels and imitators form a tight cluster: *Xù shīhuà* 續詩話 [KR4i0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0007) (Sīmǎ Guāng 司馬光), *Zhōngshān shīhuà* 中山詩話 [KR4i0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0008) (Liú Bān 劉攽), *Hòushān shīhuà* 後山詩話 [KR4i0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0009) (attributed to Chén Shīdào 陳師道), *Línhàn yǐnjū shīhuà* 臨漢隱居詩話 [KR4i0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0010) (Wèi Tài 魏泰), *Yōugǔtáng shīhuà* 優古堂詩話 [KR4i0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0011) (Wú Jiān 吳幵), and *Shílín shīhuà* 石林詩話 [KR4i0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0018) (Yè Mèngdé 葉夢得).

**The Southern Sòng compendia.** Three large works gather and organize the proliferating shorter *shīhuà*: *Shīhuà zǒngguī* 詩話總龜 [KR4i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0012) (Ruǎn Yuè 阮閱, c. 1123), *Tiáoxī yúyǐn cónghuà* 漁隱叢話 [KR4i0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0029) (Hú Zǐ 胡仔, c. 1148–67), and *Shīrén yùxiè* 詩人玉屑 [KR4i0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0036) (Wèi Qìngzhī 魏慶之, c. 1240–44). Together they preserve the bulk of the lost Northern Sòng critical literature.

**Anecdote-criticism on poetry as historical record.** *Táng shī jì shì* 唐詩紀事 [KR4i0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0025) (Jì Yǒugōng 計有功, c. 1145) and its Qīng successor *Sòng shī jìshì* 宋詩紀事 [KR4i0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0062) (Lì È 厲鶚, c. 1740) extend Mèng Qǐ's *běnshì* model into vast period-anthologies built around historical context.

**Late-Sòng theoretical synthesis.** *Cānglàng shīhuà* 滄浪詩話 [KR4i0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0035) (Yán Yǔ 嚴羽, c. 1230–45) periodizes Táng poetry, canonizes the High Táng of Dù Fǔ 杜甫 and Lǐ Bái 李白 as the model, and attacks the Jiāngxī school via the famous Chán-inflected metaphor of "marvellous awakening" (*miào wù* 妙悟). It is the single most influential work of pre-modern Chinese poetic theory and shapes every later orthodoxy down to Wáng Shìzhēn 王士禎.

**Parallel-prose criticism.** *Sìliù huà* 四六話 [KR4i0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0016) (Wáng Zhì 王銍) and *Sìliù tán zhǔ* 四六談麈 [KR4i0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0027) (Xiè Jí 謝伋) are the only sustained Sòng treatises on the parallel-prose (*sìliù*) tradition that dominated official documentary writing.

**Prose-theory manuals.** *Wén zé* 文則 [KR4i0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0031) (Chén Kuí 陳騤, c. 1170s–80s) is the first systematic Chinese rhetoric of prose. *Wén shuō* 文說 [KR4i0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0046) (Chén Yìzēng 陳繹曾) and *Xiūcí jiàn héng* 修辭鑑衡 [KR4i0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0047) (Wáng Gòu 王構) extend the project into the Yuán.

**Inscription and examination manuals.** *Jīnshí lì* 金石例 [KR4i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0048) (Pān Mǎoxiāo 潘昴霄), *Mùmíng jǔlì* 墓銘舉例 [KR4i0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0050) (Wáng Xíng 王行), and *Jīnshí yàolì* 金石要例 [KR4i0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0057) (Huáng Zōngxī 黃宗羲) form a self-contained cluster of technical works on epitaph and stele composition. *Zuò yì yào jué* 作義要訣 [KR4i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0049) (Ní Shìyì 倪士毅) is a Yuán manual for the examination essay.

**Míng–Qīng *shīhuà* and the *Wénxīn diāolóng* revival.** *Huáilùtáng shīhuà* 懷麓堂詩話 [KR4i0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0051) (Lǐ Dōngyáng 李東陽), *Tángyīn guǐ qiān* 唐音癸籤 [KR4i0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0055) (Hú Zhènhēng 胡震亨), and Wáng Shìzhēn's *Shīyǒu shīzhuàn lù* 師友詩傳錄 [KR4i0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0059) anchor the post-Yán-Yǔ orthodoxies; Zhào Zhíxìn's 趙執信 paired *Shēngdiào pǔ* 聲調譜 [KR4i0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0060) and *Tánlóng lù* 談龍錄 [KR4i0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0061) are the principal critique of Wáng Shìzhēn's *shényùn* 神韻 aesthetic. Huáng Shūlín's 黃叔琳 *Wénxīn diāolóng jí zhù* 文心雕龍輯註 [KR4i0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0002) (1738) is the foundational Qīng critical edition that opened the modern field of *Lóngxué* 龍學.

**An outlier: the earliest extant *cí* anthology.** *Huājiān jí* 花閒集 [KR4i0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4i/KR4i0013) (Zhào Chóngzuò 趙崇祚, 940) is anomalous in this division — it is not literary criticism but the founding *cí* 詞 anthology of the Five Dynasties; the SKQS editors classified it here for the absence of a *cí* category.

### Important persons

- [劉勰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%8B%B0) — author of *Wénxīn diāolóng*, the inaugural and unsurpassed Chinese theoretical treatise on writing.
- [鍾嶸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%8D%BE%E5%B6%B8) — author of *Shīpǐn*, the first ranked-history of poets, whose three-class taxonomy shaped a millennium of poetic evaluation.
- [歐陽修](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%90%E9%99%BD%E4%BF%AE) — Northern Sòng eminence who founded the *shīhuà* genre with *Liùyī shīhuà*.
- [司馬光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E5%85%89) — historian (*Zīzhì tōngjiàn*) whose *Xù shīhuà* sealed the genre's legitimacy among the highest tier of Sòng officials.
- [葉夢得](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%89%E5%A4%A2%E5%BE%97) — Northern–Southern Sòng official whose *Shílín shīhuà* is the most analytically sophisticated of the early *shīhuà*.
- [胡仔](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E4%BB%94) — compiler of *Tiáoxī yúyǐn cónghuà*, the principal preserver of lost Northern Sòng *shīhuà*.
- [計有功](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%88%E6%9C%89%E5%8A%9F) — compiler of *Táng shī jì shì*, the indispensable Sòng repository of Táng poetic anecdote.
- [嚴羽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9A%B4%E7%BE%BD) — author of *Cānglàng shīhuà*, the doctrinal pivot of pre-modern Chinese poetic theory.
- [魏慶之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E6%85%B6%E4%B9%8B) — compiler of *Shīrén yùxiè*, the most systematic Sòng topical organization of *shīhuà* material.
- [楊萬里](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E8%90%AC%E9%87%8C) — Southern Sòng poet whose *Chéngzhāi shīhuà* is the only major *shīhuà* by a first-rank practising poet.
- [劉克莊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%85%8B%E8%8E%8A) — late-Sòng *Hòucūn shīhuà* author, important for the canonization of late Táng and Sòng poets.
- [陳騤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%A8%A4) — author of *Wén zé*, the first systematic rhetoric of Chinese prose.
- [黃宗羲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%AE%97%E7%BE%B2) — Qīng polymath whose *Jīnshí yàolì* completes the epitaph-manual tradition.
- [李東陽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%9D%B1%E9%99%BD) — leading Míng official-poet whose *Huáilùtáng shīhuà* set the agenda for early Míng poetic orthodoxy.
- [楊愼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E6%84%BC) — Míng polymath whose *Shīhuà bǔyí* supplements his lost *Shēng'ān shīhuà*.
- [胡震亨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E9%9C%87%E4%BA%A8) — Míng compiler of *Tángyīn guǐqiān*, the most ambitious pre-Qīng study of Táng poetry.
- [王士禎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A3%AB%E7%A6%8E) — Qīng arbiter of taste whose *shényùn* doctrine, represented here by *Shīyǒu shīzhuàn lù* and (uncatalogued) *Yúyáng shīhuà*, dominated early-Qīng poetic theory.
- [趙執信](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E5%9F%B7%E4%BF%A1) — author of *Shēngdiào pǔ* and *Tánlóng lù*, the most articulate Qīng dissenter from *shényùn* orthodoxy.
- [厲鶚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8E%B2%E9%B6%9A) — Qīng compiler of *Sòng shī jì shì*, the standard premodern compendium of Sòng-dynasty poetic anecdote.
- [黃叔琳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%8F%94%E7%90%B3) — Qīng editor whose *Wénxīn diāolóng jí zhù* founded the modern philology of Liú Xié's text.

### Topics

- **The birth of the *shīhuà* genre.** Ōuyáng Xiū's 1071–72 experiment with informal, anecdotal poetic commentary became, within a generation, the dominant form of Chinese literary criticism, organizing thirty-plus Sòng texts in this division.
- **Genre theory.** From Liú Xié's thirty-genre taxonomy through Rén Fǎng's *yuánqǐ* etymologies, the question of how to classify writing is the persistent theoretical question of the division.
- **Periodization and the canonization of the High Táng.** Yán Yǔ's argument that the High Táng (Dù Fǔ, Lǐ Bái, Wáng Wéi) is the unsurpassable model creates the dominant orthodoxy of late-Sòng through Qīng poetics, against which every later school (Jiāngxī, *shényùn*, Tóngchéng) defines itself.
- **The Jiāngxī school polemic.** Late Northern and Southern Sòng *shīhuà* are dominated by attacks on or defenses of Huáng Tíngjiān's compositional rules — the central inner-Sòng critical fault-line.
- **Ranking and grading.** From Zhōng Róng's three-class *Shīpǐn* through Sòng *shīhuà* assessments to Qīng *zhèngzōng* 正宗 lists, the impulse to rank poets is one of the division's structural habits.
- **Anecdote vs. theory.** The division contains two distinct modes: comprehensive treatises (Liú Xié, Yán Yǔ, Hú Zhènhēng) and *běnshì* / *jìshì* / *cónghuà* anecdote-anthologies. The relation between the two — whether anecdote *grounds* theory or merely *illustrates* it — is the implicit methodological question of the genre.
- **Parallel-prose criticism.** A small but distinct cluster (*Sìliù huà*, *Sìliù tán zhǔ*) preserves theoretical reflection on the *sìliù* style that dominated Sòng official prose.
- **Technical manuals for stelae and examinations.** The division includes a separate stream of utilitarian compositional manuals (*Jīnshí lì*, *Mùmíng jǔlì*, *Jīnshí yàolì*, *Zuò yì yào jué*) bridging literary criticism and the world of official writing.
- **Tonal prosody and *shényùn*.** Zhào Zhíxìn's *Shēngdiào pǔ* and *Tánlóng lù* together constitute the principal Qīng challenge to Wáng Shìzhēn's *shényùn* aesthetic and a sustained empirical study of regulated verse prosody.
- **Editorial recovery of *Wénxīn diāolóng*.** Huáng Shūlín's 1738 critical edition begins the modern recovery of Liú Xié's text, prefiguring the twentieth-century rise of *Lóngxué*.

# 詞曲類 (KR4j)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR4j 詞曲類 *Cí-qǔ lèi* — Collected Works — Lyric Poetry and Songbooks](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

The *Cíqǔ lèi* 詞曲類 is the smallest of the five subdivisions of *Jíbù* 集部 (Collected Works) in the *Sìkù quánshū* arrangement, but bibliographically the most contested. It is the standing imperial admission that *cí* 詞 ("lyrics of unequal lines set to a tune") and *qǔ* 曲 ("aria") — genres that Sòng and Yuán catalogers had often hesitated to admit at all, on the grounds that they were *zhèngtǒng* 正統 *shī*-poetry's vernacular and "music-hall" descendants — deserve a legitimate place in the imperial library. Wilkinson (§30.2.1, Box 172) places *cí* and *qǔ* in the same dynastic-genre sequence as *shī* and *fù*, with *cí* "Tang developed; Song perfected, but lost the connection with songs," dated from the *Huājiān jí* 花間集 (940), and *qǔ* "reaching its height in the Yuan." The KR4j division covers exactly this arc: from the late-Táng / Five-Dynasties *Huājiān* corpus through the Sòng *cí* canon, the late-Sòng loyalist *yǒngwù* anthologies, the Yuán transition into *sǎnqǔ* 散曲, the Míng *cíhuà* 詞話 tradition, and the *Kāngxī*–*Qiánlóng* imperial canonization project that produced the *Yùxuǎn lìdài shīyú* [KR4j0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0074), the *Yùdìng cípǔ* [KR4j0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0086), and the *Yùdìng qǔpǔ* [KR4j0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0089).

The division is internally heterogeneous in three ways. First, by genre: it bundles *cí* (personal collections + anthologies + *cíhuà* + *cípǔ*), *sǎnqǔ* + *xìqǔ*-prosody (*Zhōngyuán yīnyùn* [KR4j0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0090), *qǔpǔ*, *qǔhuà*), and the *Kāngxī*-imperial canon-formation works under a single roof. Second, by chronology: it runs from 940 (*Huājiān jí*) to the late-Qián-lóng *Sìkù* apparatus (the 1782–1786 *Kǎozhèng* [KR4j0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0091) is bound at the division's tail). Third, by aesthetic axis: it crosses the two great stylistic poles of the *cí* — the *wǎnyuē* 婉約 (restrained, lyrical) line that runs from the *Huājiān* through Yàn Shū [晏殊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%8F%E6%AE%8A), Zhōu Bāngyàn [周邦彥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E9%82%A6%E5%BD%A5), Lǐ Qīngzhào [李清照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%B8%85%E7%85%A7), Jiāng Kuí [姜夔](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9C%E5%A4%94), and Wú Wényīng [吳文英](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%96%87%E8%8B%B1); and the *háofàng* 豪放 (bold, expansive) line opened by Sū Shì [蘇軾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE) and brought to its supreme statement by Xīn Qìjí [辛棄疾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%BE%9B%E6%A3%84%E7%96%BE). The *Sìkù tíyào* to the *Dōngpō cí* [KR4j0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0005) codifies the canonical historiography of this split: Liǔ Yǒng [柳永](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%B3%E6%B0%B8) was the Bái Jūyì of the *cí* form, Sū Shì its Hán Yù — opening the road for the entire Xīn Qìjí line that defines half the post-Sòng *cí* canon.

### Important texts and text clusters

- *Huājiān jí* 花間集 [KR4j0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0062) — the founding anthology of the *cí* (940, Hòu-Shǔ court of Mèng Chǎng), edited by Zhào Chóngzuò [趙崇祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E5%B4%87%E7%A5%9A); 500 *cí* by 18 late-Táng / Five-Dynasties poets and the textual source of the early *cí* repertoire.
- The Northern-Sòng *xiǎolìng* core — *Zhūyù cí* 珠玉詞 of Yàn Shū [KR4j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0001), *Liùyī cí* 六一詞 of Ōuyáng Xiū [KR4j0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0002), *Ānlù jí* 安陸集 of Zhāng Xiān [KR4j0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0004), *Xiǎoshān cí* 小山詞 of Yàn Jǐdào [KR4j0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0010) — the canonical entry-point to the polite *xiǎolìng* in the Féng Yánsì manner.
- *Yuèzhāng jí* 樂章集 [KR4j0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0003) — Liǔ Yǒng's lyric corpus; the foundational corpus of the *màncí* 慢詞 ("long-tune") form and the demotic urban *cí* register.
- *Dōngpō cí* 東坡詞 [KR4j0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0005) — Sū Shì's *cí*; the *biàngé* 變格 ("variant register") that opened the *háofàng* line and the locus classicus of *Niànnú jiāo · Chìbì huáigǔ*.
- *Piànyù cí* 片玉詞 [KR4j0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0015) — Zhōu Bāngyàn's prosodically supreme *cí*; head of the *Dàshèng yuèfǔ* 大晟樂府 reform and the model for the entire Southern-Sòng *gélǜ* 格律 school, with three matching-*cí* collections (Fāng Qiānlǐ [KR4j0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0019), Yáng Zémín, Chén Yǔnpìng) preserved alongside.
- *Shùyù cí* 漱玉詞 [KR4j0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0027) — Lǐ Qīngzhào's slim seventeen-piece collection, the most exalted single voice in the Chinese *cí* and the canonical *Yìān tǐ* 易安體.
- *Jiàxuān cí* 稼軒詞 [KR4j0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0040) — Xīn Qìjí's vast corpus (c. 626 *cí*), supreme *háofàng* monument and the canonical patriotic-loyalist *cí*-collection.
- *Báishí dàorén gēqǔ* 白石道人歌曲 [KR4j0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0047) — Jiāng Kuí's *cí* including 13 *zìzhìqǔ* 自製曲 (self-composed tunes) with the only surviving Sòng *cí* notation (*pángpǔ* 旁譜) — the single most musicologically important *cí* text.
- *Mèngchuāng gǎo* 夢窗稿 [KR4j0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0048) — Wú Wényīng's dense, opaque late-Southern-Sòng *cí*; the Lǐ Shāngyǐn 李商隱 of the *cí*-form, read against Jiāng Kuí as the prosodic-school co-pole.
- The late-Sòng anthology cluster — *Yuèfǔ yǎcí* 樂府雅詞 [KR4j0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0065) of Zēng Zào [曾慥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%BE%E6%85%A5), *Huāān cíxuǎn* 花菴詞選 [KR4j0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0066) and *Zhōngxīng yǐlái juémiào cíxuǎn* [KR4j0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0067) of Huáng Shēng [黃昇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E6%98%87), *Juémiào hǎocí jiān* 絕妙好詞箋 [KR4j0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0071) of Zhōu Mì [周密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E5%AF%86) (annotated by the Qīng commentators Chá Wéirén [查爲仁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%A5%E7%88%B2%E4%BB%81) and Lì È [厲鶚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8E%B2%E9%B6%9A)) — the principal Sòng-Yuán selections that constituted the *cí*-canon for late-imperial reading.
- *Yuèfǔ bǔtí* 樂府補題 [KR4j0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0072) — the politically supreme *yǒngwù* 詠物 anthology: 37 exchange-*cí* by 14 Sòng-loyalist *yímín* poets at five gatherings, 1278–1290; read since Wáng Guówéi as allegorical elegy for the desecrated Sòng imperial tombs at Shàoxīng.
- *Bìjī mànzhì* 碧鷄漫志 [KR4j0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0078) and *Yuèfǔ zhǐmí* 樂府指迷 [KR4j0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0080) — the two founding Sòng *cí*-treatises: Wáng Zhuó's historical-prosodic survey of the *cí* as song-form (1145–1149) and Shěn Yìfǔ's practical compositional handbook in the Wú Wényīng manner (1242–1250). The textual basis of all subsequent *cíhuà*.
- *Zhōngyuán yīnyùn* 中原音韻 [KR4j0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0090) — Zhōu Déqīng's 1324 phonological manual; the founding statement of modern *Mandarin* phonology (19 rhyme-groups; *yīn / yángpíng* division; *rù*-redistribution) and the indispensable reference for reading Yuán *běiqǔ*.
- The Yuán *sǎnqǔ* anthology pair — *Tàipíng yuèfǔ* 太平樂府 [KR4j0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0081) of Yáng Cháoyīng [楊朝英](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E6%9C%9D%E8%8B%B1) (1351) and the *Líyuán ànshì yuèfǔ xīnshēng* 梨園按試樂府新聲 [KR4j0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0082) — the principal documentary sources for Yuán *sǎnqǔ*.
- The Qīng anthology and prosody triad — *Cízōng* 詞綜 [KR4j0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0075) of Zhū Yízūn [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) (1678; founding charter of the *Zhèxīpài* 浙西派), *Shíwǔ jiā cí* 十五家詞 [KR4j0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0076) of Sūn Mò [孫默](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E9%BB%98) (1670s, *Yángxiànpài* 陽羨派 representative), and *Cílǜ* 詞律 [KR4j0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0087) of Wàn Shù [萬樹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%90%AC%E6%A8%B9) (1687) — together establishing the Qīng *cí* revival.
- The *Kāngxī* imperial canon — *Yùxuǎn lìdài shīyú* 御選歷代詩餘 [KR4j0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0074) (1707, c. 9,000 *cí* by c. 1,540 poets in 120 *juǎn*), *Yùdìng cípǔ* 御定詞譜 [KR4j0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0086) (1715, 826 tunes), *Yùdìng qǔpǔ* 御定曲譜 [KR4j0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0089) (1715, Northern + Southern *qǔ*). The three together constitute the institutionalized Qīng *cíqǔ* prosody.
- *Cíyuàn cóngtán* 詞苑叢談 [KR4j0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0085) of Xú Qiú [徐釚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E9%87%9A) — the most comprehensive of all Qīng *cíhuà*, organized into seven thematic *mén* (form, sound, criticism, anecdote, textual verification, jest, miscellany); the Qīng analytical encyclopedia of *cí*.
- *Kēxuě cí* 珂雪詞 [KR4j0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0061) of Cáo Zhēnjí [曹貞吉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%B9%E8%B2%9E%E5%90%89) — the only Qīng-period *cí* collection admitted to the *Sìkù* on its author's own merit, standing between *Yángxiàn* and *Zhèxī* aesthetic poles.

### Important persons

- [趙崇祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E5%B4%87%E7%A5%9A) — Hòu-Shǔ courtier; editor of the *Huājiān jí*, the founding *cí*-anthology of the tradition.
- [晏殊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%8F%E6%AE%8A) — Northern-Sòng councillor; foundational *xiǎolìng* master in the Féng Yánsì line.
- [柳永](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%B3%E6%B0%B8) — first great expander of the *cí* into the *màn* (long-tune) form; demotic Northern-Sòng urban *cí* and the songs of the courtesan-quarters.
- [蘇軾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE) — supreme *biàngé* poet; opened the *háofàng* line and made the *cí* a fully literary form.
- [周邦彥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E9%82%A6%E5%BD%A5) — head of the *Dàshèng yuèfǔ* Imperial Music Bureau under Huīzōng; the supreme musical theorist of the *cí* and parent of the Southern-Sòng *gélǜ* school.
- [李清照](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%B8%85%E7%85%A7) — supreme woman *cí*-poet; survivor of the Sòng-Jīn rupture and author of the *Jīnshí lù hòu xù*; canonical *Yìāntǐ*.
- [辛棄疾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%BE%9B%E6%A3%84%E7%96%BE) — supreme *háofàng* master; ex-Jīn-resistance fighter, sometime official, and the largest single *cí*-corpus of the Sòng.
- [陸游](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E6%B8%B8) — the great patriot poet, also represented by his *cí* [KR4j0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0043).
- [姜夔](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9C%E5%A4%94) — supreme prosodic-school master; only Sòng *cí*-writer whose own musical notation survives; ancestor of all subsequent musicological recovery of the Sòng *cí*.
- [吳文英](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%96%87%E8%8B%B1) — supreme late-Southern-Sòng prosodist; the "Lǐ Shāngyǐn of the *cí*"; co-pole of the *gélǜ* line with Jiāng Kuí.
- [蔣捷](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E6%8D%B7) — *Sòng* loyalist *cí*-writer of the *Zhúshān cí* [KR4j0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0053); canonized in the *Cízōng* as a *Zhèxī* auxiliary.
- [周密](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E5%AF%86) — late-Sòng loyalist and connoisseur; compiler of the *Juémiào hǎocí* and a contributor to the *Yuèfǔ bǔtí*.
- [黃昇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E6%98%87) — Southern-Sòng anthologist whose *Huāān cíxuǎn* preserved the basic life-data and corpus of 88 Southern-Sòng poets.
- [王灼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%81%BC) — Southern-Sòng theorist; author of the founding *cí*-treatise *Bìjī mànzhì*.

### Topics

- **Wǎnyuē 婉約 vs. háofàng 豪放.** The single most consequential interpretive axis of the *cí*-tradition. The *Huājiān*-line poets and Northern-Sòng *xiǎolìng* masters (Yàn Shū [晏殊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%8F%E6%AE%8A), Zhāng Xiān [張先](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%85%88)) established the restrained-lyrical mode; Liǔ Yǒng [柳永](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%B3%E6%B0%B8) opened the demotic line; Sū Shì [蘇軾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%98%87%E8%BB%BE) then opened the *háofàng* line, brought to its supreme statement by Xīn Qìjí [辛棄疾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%BE%9B%E6%A3%84%E7%96%BE) in the Southern Sòng. The *Sìkù tíyào* to *Dōngpō cí* [KR4j0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0005) is the canonical Qīng formulation: Liǔ as the Bái Jūyì of the *cí*, Sū as its Hán Yù. The Qīng *Zhèxīpài* of [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) explicitly canonized the *wǎnyuē* line through Jiāng Kuí [姜夔](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9C%E5%A4%94); the *Chángzhōupài* of Zhāng Huìyán in the early 19th century positioned itself in opposition. Every comprehensive anthology in the division — *Huāān cíxuǎn* [KR4j0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0066), *Cízōng* [KR4j0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0075), *Yùxuǎn lìdài shīyú* [KR4j0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0074) — takes a definite editorial position on this axis.

- **Cí as song-form vs. cí as literary form.** Whether the *cí* should be conceived primarily as a singable musical form or as a written literary form is the founding theoretical question of the genre, opened by Wáng Zhuó's *Bìjī mànzhì* [KR4j0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0078) (which mourns the loss of the Táng *gēfǎ* and treats the Sòng *cí* as a residual song-tradition) and by Shěn Yìfǔ's *Yuèfǔ zhǐmí* [KR4j0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0080) (which formalizes the *qùshēng* / *píngshǎngrù* substitution rule). The question becomes acute with the loss of Sòng *qǔpǔ* by the Yuán, after which *cí* could only be a literary form. Jiāng Kuí's *zìzhìqǔ* in [KR4j0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0047) — with surviving notation — remains the principal documentary anchor of the song-form reading. Wàn Shù's *Cílǜ* [KR4j0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0087) takes the literary form to its logical end with a *qūpǔ*-based prosody recovered by collation.

- **Yǎzhèng 雅正 as anthology principle.** The classifying principle that runs from Zēng Zào's *Yuèfǔ yǎcí* [KR4j0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0065) through Zhōu Mì's *Juémiào hǎocí* to Zhū Yízūn's *Cízōng* [KR4j0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0075) — *cí* must conform to *yǎzhèng* (the canonically refined and orthodox) and not to the *Huājiān* / *Cǎotáng* line of decorative pretty pieces. The *Yùxuǎn lìdài shīyú* [KR4j0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0074) institutionalizes the *yǎzhèng* preference as imperial taste.

- **Yǒngwù 詠物 as political allegory.** The Southern-Sòng *yǒngwù* mode — descriptive lyrics on objects — became, in the loyalist generation after 1276, a vehicle for political allegory. The *Yuèfǔ bǔtí* [KR4j0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0072) is the supreme example: five sets of exchange-*cí* on dragon-spittle perfume, white lotus, water-shield, cicada, and crab — read by Wáng Guówéi and modern scholars as figures for the desecrated Sòng imperial tombs. The *yǒngwù* mode shapes the late Wú Wényīng [吳文英](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%96%87%E8%8B%B1) [KR4j0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0048) and the entire late-Southern-Sòng tail.

- **The Sòng-Yuán transition: cí into sǎnqǔ.** As Wilkinson's Box 172 sets out, *qǔ* reached its height in the Yuán as a successor genre to *cí*: the same musical-lyric impulse moving to a new prestige form. The transition is documented within the division by the late-Sòng-into-Yuán *cí*-writers Zhāng Yán, Bái Pǔ [KR4j0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0059), Zhāng Hùi [KR4j0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0060), and by the founding Yuán phonological and anthology works ([KR4j0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0090), [KR4j0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0081), [KR4j0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0082)). The *Yùdìng qǔpǔ* [KR4j0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0089) then institutionalizes the unified *cíqǔ* prosodic tradition.

- **North vs. South in qǔ.** The Yuán *běiqǔ* tradition (rooted in *Zhōngyuán yīnyùn* phonology [KR4j0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0090) and the *Tàipíng yuèfǔ* anthology [KR4j0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0081)) and the Míng *nánqǔ* tradition (running through the *Yōngxī yuèfǔ* [KR4j0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0068) and the *Wúsāo hébiān* [KR4j0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0069)) form the two great regional song-traditions of the Yuán-Míng period. The *Yùdìng qǔpǔ* [KR4j0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0089) codifies both in parallel registers.

- **Cí by women.** The *Cíqǔ lèi* admits two single-author collections by Sòng women: the *Shùyù cí* of Lǐ Qīngzhào [KR4j0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0027) and the *Duàncháng cí* 斷腸詞 of Zhū Shūzhēn [KR4j0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0058) — together the principal documentary basis of the Sòng-era *guīyīn* 閨音 ("women's voice") tradition. Chén Tíng's *Zhūshāntáng cíhuà* [KR4j0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0083) preserves Wáng Zhāoyí's *Mǎnjiānghóng*, the most-anthologized late-Sòng court-lady's *cí*.

- **Cípǔ and qǔpǔ as scholarly enterprise.** The Qīng *kǎojù*-era *cípǔ* / *qǔpǔ* project — Wàn Shù's *Cílǜ* [KR4j0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0087) privately and the imperial *Cípǔ* [KR4j0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0086) / *Qǔpǔ* [KR4j0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR4/KR4j/KR4j0089) institutionally — is the longest-running scholarly enterprise within the division. It reflects the wider *kǎojù*-era ambition to recover by philological-prosodic means what the loss of the Sòng *qǔpǔ* had taken away.

# 洞真部 (KR5a)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR5a 洞真部 *Dòngzhēn bù* — Daoist Canon — Cavern of Perfection](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR5a 洞真部 (*Dòngzhēn bù*, "Cavern of Perfection") collects 328 works (DZ 0001 – DZ 0316 in the Schipper / Verellen *Concordance du Tao-tsang* numbering) — the first of the *Sāndòng* 三洞 ("Three Caverns") under which the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (1445) is arranged. Wilkinson describes the *sāndòng* scheme as inherited from the Southern Dynasties: the three Caverns are notionally *schools* — 洞真 with the Shàngqīng 上清 revelations, 洞玄 with the Língbǎo 靈寶 corpus, 洞神 with the Sānhuáng 三皇 tradition — while the further subdivision of each Cavern into 十二類 ("twelve sections": 本文, 神符, 玉訣, 靈圖, 譜錄, 戒律, 威儀, 方法, 衆術, 記傳, 讚頌, 表奏) supplies a *genre* axis cutting across them (Wilkinson §29.4.3, §29.4.4). In practice, by the time the canon was fixed in the Ming the school boundaries had long collapsed: the *Dòngzhēn bù* opens not with a Shàngqīng text but with the Língbǎo *Dùrén jīng* 度人經 [KR5a0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0001), placed at DZ 0001 because the Northern Sòng court under Huīzōng 徽宗 (r. 1100–1126) had elevated it to canonical primacy, and runs on through Táng pseudepigrapha, Sòng-Yuán internal-alchemy commentaries, Yuán hagiographies, and Ming ritual liturgy.

The chronological span of the collected works runs from the pre-Qin *Mù tiānzǐ zhuàn* 穆天子傳 [KR5a0303](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0303) (c. 300 BCE), included for its mythography and for Guō Pú's 郭璞 Jìn-era commentary; through the *Liè xiān zhuàn* 列仙傳 [KR5a0306](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0306), the earliest extant collection of immortal-biographies; through the foundational Six-Dynasties strata of *Old Shàngqīng* (~317–420) and *Old Língbǎo* (~395–402) revelation-scriptures; an extensive Táng layer of court-sponsored and pseudo-revealed scriptures; the great Northern Sòng / Huīzōng-era reorganization driven by the Shénxiāo 神霄 movement around Lín Língsù 林靈素 (1076–1120); the Southern Sòng explosion of internal-alchemy (內丹 *nèidān*) commentary on Zhāng Bóduān's *Wùzhēn piān* 悟真篇 and the Southern-Lineage (南宗) writings of Bái Yùchán; the Yuán hagiographic synthesis in Zhào Dàoyī's *Lìshì zhēnxiān tǐdào tōngjiàn* 歷世真仙體道通鑑 [KR5a0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0308); and a late stratum of Ming liturgy, with works compiled or revised under the forty-third Tiānshī Zhāng Yǔchū 張宇初 (1361–1410) reaching down to the 1410s. Date distribution by composition midpoint is sharply trimodal: a Six-Dynasties stratum (4th–6th c., ~40 works), a major Táng layer (7th–8th c., ~65 works), and a dominant Sòng-Yuán mass (11th–14th c., ~200 works); the late-imperial liturgy is comparatively thin.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The opening *Dùrén jīng* corpus.**
- *Língbǎo wúliàng dùrén shàngpǐn miàojīng* 靈寶無量度人上品妙經 [KR5a0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0001) — *the* opening text of the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* (DZ 0001), the flagship scripture of the Língbǎo tradition. Juan 1 is the late-fourth-century core, juan 2–61 a Northern-Sòng expansion produced under Huīzōng in the Shénxiāo circle around Lín Língsù.
- *Yuánshǐ wúliàng dùrén shàngpǐn miàojīng zhíyīn* 元始無量度人上品妙經直音 [KR5a0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0002) — Sòng-Yuán phonetic guide to the same text.
- The Sòng-Yuán *Dùrén jīng* commentary cluster: *Sìzhù* 四註 [KR5a0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0087), *Zhù* 註 [KR5a0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0088), *Tōngyì* 通義 [KR5a0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0089), *Nèiyì* 內義 [KR5a0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0090), *Zhùjiě* 註解 ([KR5a0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0092), [KR5a0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0093)), *Jīngfǎ* 經法 [KR5a0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0094), *Dàfàn yǐnyǔ shūyì* 大梵隱語疏義 [KR5a0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0095), *Jué yīnyì* 訣音義 [KR5a0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0096) — the densest exegetical layer attached to any single Daoist scripture, plus the diagrammatic *Fútú* 符圖 [KR5a0148](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0148) and *Pángtōng tú* 旁通圖 [KR5a0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0149) and the *Dàfǎ* 大法 ritual codification [KR5a0220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0220).

**Old Shàngqīng revelations (~317–420).** Originating in the visionary séances of Yáng Xī 楊羲 and the Xǔ family at Mount Máo 茅山 and codified two centuries later by Táo Hóngjǐng [陶弘景](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%BC%98%E6%99%AF):
- *Shàngqīng huángqì yángjīng sāndào shùnxíng jīng* 上清黃氣陽精三道順行經 [KR5a0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0033), *Dòngzhēn tàijí Běidì Zǐwēi shénzhòu miàojīng* 洞真太極北帝紫微神咒妙經 [KR5a0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0049), *Shàngqīng qiónggōng língfēi liùjiǎ zuǒyòu shàngfú* 上清瓊宮靈飛六甲左右上符 [KR5a0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0084), *Tàiwéi língshū zǐwén xiānjì zhēnjì shàngjīng* 太微靈書紫文仙忌真記上經 [KR5a0180](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0180), *Tàiwéi língshū zǐwén lánggān huádān shénzhēn shàngjīng* 太微靈書紫文琅玕華丹神真上經 [KR5a0256](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0256), *Tàishàng yùpèi jīndāng tàijí jīnshū shàngjīng* 太上玉珮金璫太極金書上經 [KR5a0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0056), *Báiyǔ hēihé língfēi yùfú* 白羽黑翮靈飛玉符 [KR5a0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0083) — together the densest concentration of fourth-century Shàngqīng material in the canon.

**Old Língbǎo revelations (~395–402).** The "ancient Língbǎo scriptures" (*gǔ Língbǎo jīng* 古靈寶經) ascribed to Gě Cháofǔ 葛巢甫 and canonized in Lù Xiūjìng's 陸修靜 *Língbǎo jīngmù* 靈寶經目 (437):
- *Yuánshǐ wǔlǎo chìshū yùpiān zhēnwén tiānshū jīng* 元始五老赤書玉篇真文天書經 [KR5a0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0022) — the *Wǔpiān zhēnwén* 五篇真文, number 1 in Lù Xiūjìng's catalogue.
- *Tàishàng zhūtiān língshū dùmìng miàojīng* 太上諸天靈書度命妙經 [KR5a0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0023), *Tàishàng língbǎo zhūtiān nèiyīn zìrán yùzì* 太上靈寶諸天內音自然玉字 [KR5a0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0098), *Língbǎo zìrán jiǔtiān shēngshén sānbǎo dàyǒu jīnshū* 靈寶自然九天生神三寶大有金書 [KR5a0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0166) — the cosmogonic core of the early Língbǎo system.

**The *Shàngqīng dàdòng zhēnjīng* tradition.**
- *Shàngqīng dàdòng zhēnjīng* 上清大洞真經 [KR5a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0006) — the central scripture of Shàngqīng inner practice, transmitted as a 31-chapter recitation cycle; the received recension descends through Zhū Zìyīng's 朱自英 1024 Máoshān preface, Jiǎng Zōngyíng's 蔣宗瑛 Sòng-Yuán editorial work, and Zhāng Yǔchū's early-Ming colophon.
- *Dàdòng yùjīng* 大洞玉經 [KR5a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0007) — Ming reworking by Gōng Détóng 龔德同.
- *Tàishàng wújí zǒngzhēn Wénchāng dàdòng xiānjīng* 太上無極總真文昌大洞仙經 [KR5a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0005) and its commentary *Yùqīng wújí zǒngzhēn Wénchāng dàdòng xiānjīng zhù* 玉清無極總真文昌大洞仙經註 [KR5a0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0104) — the Wénchāng-cult retake on the *Dàdòng* genre.
- *Shàngqīng dàdòng zhēnjīng yùjué yīnyì* 上清大洞真經玉訣音義 [KR5a0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0105) — phonetic-and-glossary aid.

**The *Yùhuáng* (Jade Emperor) scriptures.** Late-Northern-Sòng to early-Yuán composite, framed as the speech of the *Yùhuáng dàdì* 玉皇大帝:
- *Gāoshàng Yùhuáng běnxíng jíjīng* 高上玉皇本行集經 [KR5a0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0010) [KR5a0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0011) — the long *vita* of the Jade Emperor.
- *Gāoshàng Yùhuáng běnxíng jīngsuǐ* 高上玉皇本行經髓 [KR5a0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0012) (Liú Chùyuán's 劉處源 distillation), *Gāoshàng Yùhuáng xīnyìn jīng* 高上玉皇心印經 [KR5a0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0013), *Gāoshàng Yùhuáng tāixí jīng* 高上玉皇胎息經 [KR5a0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0014) — the inner-cultivation short scriptures of the Yùhuáng cycle.

**The 雷霆 *Léitíng* / Shénxiāo storm-magic corpus.** Composed under and around the Shénxiāo movement of the Huīzōng court:
- *Wúshàng jiǔxiāo Yùqīng Dàfàn Zǐwēi xuándū léitíng yùjīng* 無上九霄玉清大梵紫微玄都雷霆玉經 [KR5a0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0015), *Jiǔtiān yìngyuán léishēng pǔhuà tiānzūn yùshū bǎojīng* 九天應元雷聲普化天尊玉樞寶經 [KR5a0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0016) and its *Jízhù* 集註 [KR5a0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0100), *Tàishàng shuō cháotiān xièléi zhēnjīng* 太上說朝天謝雷真經 [KR5a0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0017) — together the doctrinal scaffolding of the Sòng-Yuán thunder-rite (*léifǎ* 雷法) tradition.

**The *Wùzhēn piān* 悟真篇 commentary cluster.** Zhāng Bóduān's [張伯端](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E4%BC%AF%E7%AB%AF) (c. 987–1082) verse-treatise on internal alchemy, canonized in the Sòng-Yuán Southern Lineage (南宗) and surrounded in the *Dòngzhēn bù* by the densest concentration of *nèidān* exegesis in the canon:
- *Zǐyáng zhēnrén Wùzhēn piān zhùshū* 紫陽真人悟真篇註疏 [KR5a0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0142) — Wēng Bǎoguāng's 翁葆光 (fl. 1173) commentary as re-edited by Dài Qǐzōng 戴起宗 (c. 1335–1340).
- *Wùzhēn piān sānzhù* 悟真篇三註 [KR5a0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0143), *Zhíxiǎng xiángshuō sānchéng mìyào* 直指詳說三乘秘要 [KR5a0144](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0144), *Shíyí* 拾遺 [KR5a0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0145), *Zhùshì* 註釋 [KR5a0146](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0146), *Jiǎngyì* 講義 [KR5a0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0147) — five further received commentaries, plus the *Xiūzhēn shíshū* recension [KR5a0268](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0268).

**The *Xiūzhēn shíshū* 修真十書 collection.** A ten-text Sòng-Yuán anthology of Southern-Lineage and proto-Quánzhēn material, gathered into a single ten-juan collection in the Yuán:
- [KR5a0265](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0265) *Jīndān dàchéng jí* 金丹大成集 (Xiāo Tíngzhī 蕭廷芝), [KR5a0266](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0266) *Zhōng Lǚ chuándào jí* 鍾呂傳道集 (the foundational Zhōnglí Quán 鍾離權 / Lǚ Dòngbīn 呂洞賓 dialogues), [KR5a0267](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0267) *Zázhù jiéjìng* 雜著捷徑, [KR5a0268](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0268) *Wùzhēn piān*, [KR5a0269](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0269) *Yùlóng jí* 玉隆集 and [KR5a0270](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0270) *Shàngqīng jí* 上清集 and [KR5a0271](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0271) *Wǔyí jí* 武夷集 (the three Bái Yùchán 白玉蟾 collected-writings volumes), [KR5a0272](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0272) *Pánshān yǔlù* 盤山語錄 (Wáng Zhìjǐn 王志謹's Quánzhēn discourses), [KR5a0273](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0273) *Huángtíng nèijǐng wǔzàng liùfǔ tú* 黃庭內景五藏六府圖, [KR5a0274](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0274) *Huángtíng nèijǐng yùjīng zhù* 黃庭內景玉經注 — together one of the great preserved compendia of Sòng-Yuán inner-alchemical practice.

**Hagiography and biography (記傳類).**
- *Mù tiānzǐ zhuàn* 穆天子傳 [KR5a0303](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0303) — the late-Warring-States travel romance of King Mù's encounter with the Queen Mother of the West, with Guō Pú's Jìn commentary; chronologically the oldest text in the division.
- *Liè xiān zhuàn* 列仙傳 [KR5a0306](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0306) — earliest extant Daoist hagiography, pseudepigraphically ascribed to Liú Xiàng 劉向 (77 – 6 BCE).
- *Hàn Wǔdì nèizhuàn* 漢武帝內傳 [KR5a0304](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0304) — Six-Dynasties Shàngqīng-flavoured fiction on the Hàn emperor's reception of the Queen Mother.
- *Zǐyáng zhēnrén nèizhuàn* 紫陽真人內傳 [KR5a0315](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0315) — Eastern-Jìn Shàngqīng *vita* of Zhōu Yìshān 周義山.
- *Zhōu shì míngtōng jì* 周氏冥通記 [KR5a0314](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0314) — Táo Hóngjǐng's 515–516 record of his disciple Zhōu Zǐliáng's 周子良 night-time encounters with the Perfected; the single best-preserved document of fifth-century Shàngqīng séance practice.
- *Lìshì zhēnxiān tǐdào tōngjiàn* 歷世真仙體道通鑑 [KR5a0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0308) (Zhào Dàoyī 趙道一, 53 juan, c. 1294), with continuation [KR5a0309](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0309) and *Hòují* 後集 [KR5a0310](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0310) — the great Yuán Daoist hagiographical synthesis, more than 900 biographies; long the principal Daoist counterpart to the Buddhist *Gāosēng zhuàn* 高僧傳.
- *Máoshān zhì* 茅山誌 [KR5a0316](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0316) (Liú Dàbīn 劉大彬, 1328) — the standard Yuán gazetteer of the central Shàngqīng mountain.

**Genealogies and ranking (譜錄類).**
- *Dòngxuán língbǎo zhēnlíng wèiyè tú* 洞玄靈寶真靈位業圖 [KR5a0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0168) — Táo Hóngjǐng's ranked diagram of the entire Daoist pantheon across seven celestial levels; foundational for later Daoist liturgy and the principal source for the Six-Dynasties imagination of the heavens.

**The Lǐ Dàochún 李道純 syncretic *nèidān* corpus.** A late-Yuán cluster gathering the writings of the Quánzhēn-Southern-Lineage syncretist (fl. 1290) — six titles in the division, the densest single-author concentration after the *Dùrén* and *Wùzhēn* commentary clusters.

### Important persons

- [陶弘景](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%BC%98%E6%99%AF) (Táo Hóngjǐng, 456–536) — patriarch of the Máoshān Shàngqīng tradition; compiler of the *Zhēnlíng wèiyè tú* [KR5a0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0168) and editor of the *Zhōu shì míngtōng jì* [KR5a0314](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0314); the indispensable transmitter of Yáng Xī's fourth-century revelations.
- [陸修靜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E4%BF%AE%E9%9D%9C) (Lù Xiūjìng, 406–477) — Liú-Sòng codifier of the Língbǎo corpus, whose 437 *Língbǎo jīngmù* fixed the canonical sequence of the *Yuánshǐ wǔlǎo chìshū* [KR5a0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0022) and its companion scriptures, and whose *Sāndòng* classification became the architecture of every subsequent Daoist canon — including the one this division opens.
- [郭璞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E7%92%9E) (Guō Pú, 276–324) — Jìn polymath whose commentary on the *Mù tiānzǐ zhuàn* [KR5a0303](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0303) is co-transmitted with the text and is its principal reading aid.
- [劉向](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E5%90%91) (Liú Xiàng, 77 – 6 BCE, attributed) — pseudepigraphic compiler of the *Liè xiān zhuàn* [KR5a0306](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0306), the prototype of the immortal-biography genre.
- [寇謙之](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%87%E8%AC%99%E4%B9%8B) (Kòu Qiānzhī, 365–448) — Northern-Wèi Tiānshī reformer whose Old-Tiānshī materials underlie several pseudo-archaic ritual texts in the division.
- [朱自英](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E8%87%AA%E8%8B%B1) (Zhū Zìyīng, 976–1029) — 23rd Máoshān patriarch; his 1024 preface anchors the received [KR5a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0006) *Shàngqīng dàdòng zhēnjīng*.
- [閭丘方遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%96%AD%E4%B8%98%E6%96%B9%E9%81%A0) (Lǘqiū Fāngyuǎn, d. 902) — late-Táng Shàngqīng master whose editorial work fixed the received text of the *Zhēnlíng wèiyè tú* [KR5a0168](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0168).
- [陳景元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%99%AF%E5%85%83) (Chén Jǐngyuán, 1024–1094) — Northern-Sòng Shàngqīng exegete; commentator on the *Dùrén jīng* and contributor to the early *Dòngzhēn* commentarial stream.
- [張伯端](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E4%BC%AF%E7%AB%AF) (Zhāng Bóduān, c. 987–1082) — author of the *Wùzhēn piān*, founder of the Southern Lineage (南宗) of *nèidān*; his work generates the seven *Wùzhēn piān* texts [KR5a0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0142)–[KR5a0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0147) and [KR5a0268](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0268) and is, by sheer volume of derivative commentary, the single most influential text in the division.
- [翁葆光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BF%81%E8%91%86%E5%85%89) (Wēng Bǎoguāng, fl. 1173) — principal early commentator on the *Wùzhēn piān* [KR5a0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0142) [KR5a0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0143) [KR5a0144](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0144) [KR5a0145](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0145).
- [白玉蟾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%99%BD%E7%8E%89%E8%9F%BE) (Bái Yùchán, c. 1194–1229) — fourth Patriarch of the Southern Lineage; the *Yùlóng* [KR5a0269](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0269), *Shàngqīng* [KR5a0270](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0270), and *Wǔyí* [KR5a0271](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0271) collections in the *Xiūzhēn shíshū* are his collected writings, and many of the late-Sòng thunder-rite and *Léitíng* texts in the division pass through his school.
- [李道純](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%81%93%E7%B4%94) (Lǐ Dàochún, fl. 1290) — Yuán syncretist who fused Quánzhēn and Southern-Lineage *nèidān*; the most prolific single late-Yuán author in the division.
- [趙道一](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E9%81%93%E4%B8%80) (Zhào Dàoyī, late 13th c.) — compiler of the *Lìshì zhēnxiān tǐdào tōngjiàn* [KR5a0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0308)–[KR5a0310](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0310), the principal Yuán hagiographical synthesis.
- [蔣宗瑛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E5%AE%97%E7%91%9B) (Jiǎng Zōngyíng, fl. 1250) — Sòng-Yuán transitional editor of the *Shàngqīng dàdòng zhēnjīng* [KR5a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0006).
- [苗善時](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8B%97%E5%96%84%E6%99%82) (Miáo Shànshí, fl. 1310) — Yuán hagiographer of the Lǚ Dòngbīn cult; author of [KR5a0317](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0317) *Chúnyáng dìjūn shénhuà miàotōng jì* 純陽帝君神化妙通紀.
- [張宇初](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%AE%87%E5%88%9D) (Zhāng Yǔchū, 1361–1410) — 43rd Celestial Master; editorial overseer of the early-Ming preparations for the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* whose colophons are visible on [KR5a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0006) and elsewhere in the division.
- [路時中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B7%AF%E6%99%82%E4%B8%AD) (Lù Shízhōng, fl. 1120) — Northern-Sòng Tiānxīn 天心 ritual codifier whose materials filter into the *Dòngzhēn* ritual texts.
- [王玠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%8E%A0) (Wáng Jiè, fl. 1330) — late-Yuán commentator on the *Dùrén jīng* and *Wùzhēn piān*; one of the principal voices of post-Bái-Yùchán Southern-Lineage exegesis.
- [陳致虛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E8%87%B4%E8%99%9B) (Chén Zhìxū, c. 1289 – after 1335) — Yuán syncretic *nèidān* author and *Wùzhēn piān* commentator [KR5a0143](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0143).
- [夏元鼎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%8F%E5%85%83%E9%BC%8E) (Xià Yuándǐng, fl. 1225) — Southern Sòng *Wùzhēn piān* commentator.
- [元陽子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E9%99%BD%E5%AD%90) (Yuánzǐ, Táng) — pseudonymous Táng alchemical author whose *Yīnfú jīng* hymn-commentary [KR5a0323](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0323) enters the division's *zànsòng* 讚頌 layer.
- [文昌帝君](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%87%E6%98%8C%E5%B8%9D%E5%90%9B) (Wénchāng dìjūn) — divine "author" of the Wénchāng-cult scriptures including [KR5a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0005) and [KR5a0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0029), reflecting the absorption of regional cult literature into the Daoist canon from the late Sòng onward.

Lín Língsù 林靈素 (1076–1120), founder of the Shénxiāo school under Huīzōng and chief architect of the 60-juan expansion of [KR5a0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0001), and Gě Cháofǔ 葛巢甫 (fl. c. 400), to whom the *Old Língbǎo* revelation cycle of [KR5a0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0022) [KR5a0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0023) [KR5a0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0098) [KR5a0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0166) is ascribed, would belong on this list; person notes for both remain to be created.

### Topics

- **The *sāndòng* 三洞 scheme and the school / genre cross-classification.** The notional division of the canon by school (Shàngqīng / Língbǎo / Sānhuáng) cuts against the genre subdivision into 十二類 — and by the time of the Ming compilation the two axes have ceased to cohere: in *Dòngzhēn bù* the opening text is Língbǎo, the largest cluster (the *Yùhuáng* and Léitíng scriptures) is post-revelation Sòng material, and many texts placed in 本文 are Sòng or Yuán pseudo-revelations rather than ancient scripture. Wilkinson (§29.4.4) notes the same drift across the canon as a whole.

- **Old Shàngqīng vs. Old Língbǎo.** The two principal Six-Dynasties revelation cycles preserve sharply different theological tones — Shàngqīng inner visualization and astral travel ([KR5a0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0033) [KR5a0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0049) [KR5a0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0084) [KR5a0180](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0180) [KR5a0256](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0256)) versus the Mahāyāna-influenced Língbǎo soteriology of universal salvation in the *Yuánshǐ wǔlǎo chìshū* [KR5a0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0022) and *Zhūtiān língshū dùmìng* [KR5a0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0023). The two traditions are interleaved without comment in the *Dòngzhēn* 本文 layer.

- **The *Dùrén jīng* and the Huīzōng-Shénxiāo expansion.** A 4th–5th-century Língbǎo scripture of about one juan is grown in the early twelfth century into a sixty-one-juan compendium — the founding intervention of the Shénxiāo movement, and the editorial reason the Ming canon places this text at DZ 0001. The commentary cluster [KR5a0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0087)–[KR5a0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0096) is the single densest exegetical archipelago around any scripture in the canon.

- **Internal alchemy (*nèidān* 內丹) and the Southern Lineage.** The arrival of Zhāng Bóduān's *Wùzhēn piān* in the late eleventh century reorganizes Daoist soteriology around the symbolic alchemical refinement of *jīng* 精 — *qì* 氣 — *shén* 神. The *Dòngzhēn bù* preserves the densest commentary cluster on the *Wùzhēn piān* in any surviving collection ([KR5a0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0142)–[KR5a0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0147), [KR5a0268](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0268)) and the three-volume Bái Yùchán corpus inside [KR5a0269](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0269)–[KR5a0271](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0271), together with the *Zhōng Lǚ chuándào jí* [KR5a0266](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0266) that fixes the eponymous teacher-student dialogue framing of the entire Southern Lineage.

- **Thunder-rites and Shénxiāo / Léitíng theology.** A distinctive Northern-Sòng strand of Daoist ritual centred on the *Léishēng pǔhuà tiānzūn* 雷聲普化天尊 (the Heavenly Worthy of the Universal Transformation of Thunder), institutionally crystallizing in the Shénxiāo school. The principal scriptural texts [KR5a0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0015) [KR5a0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0016) [KR5a0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0017) and the *Jízhù* [KR5a0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0100) are flanked in the canon by the matching *Léitíng* repentance liturgies [KR5a0196](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0196) [KR5a0197](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0197).

- **Cult-literature absorption: Wénchāng, Yùhuáng, Zhēnwǔ.** Three regional cults — the Sichuan god of literature Wénchāng (texts [KR5a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0005) [KR5a0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0028) [KR5a0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0029) [KR5a0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0104)), the Jade Emperor (the *Yùhuáng* group [KR5a0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0010)–[KR5a0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0014)), and the northern martial god Zhēnwǔ ([KR5a0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0027)) — enter the Daoist canon in the Sòng-Yuán-Ming centuries through scriptures framed as the speech of these gods themselves. The pattern is characteristic of the late imperial canon's openness to non-revelation-school literature.

- **Hagiographical synthesis.** A continuous tradition from the *Liè xiān zhuàn* [KR5a0306](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0306) through the *Hàn Wǔdì* romances [KR5a0304](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0304) [KR5a0305](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0305), the targeted single-figure biographies ([KR5a0312](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0312) *Huáyáng Táo yǐnjū nèizhuàn* on Táo Hóngjǐng; [KR5a0315](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0315) *Zǐyáng zhēnrén nèizhuàn*), and finally the great Yuán synthesis of Zhào Dàoyī ([KR5a0308](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0308) [KR5a0309](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0309) [KR5a0310](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0310)), to which the gazetteers ([KR5a0316](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0316) *Máoshān zhì*; [KR5a0318](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0318) *Tàihuá xīyí zhì*; [KR5a0319](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0319) *Xīyuè Huáshān zhì*) attach.
