# 太玄部 (KR5d)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR5d 太玄部 *Tàixuán bù* — Daoist Canon — Great Mystery](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR5d 太玄部 (*Tàixuán bù*, "Great Mystery") collects 123 works (DZ 984 – DZ 1100 in the Schipper / Verellen *Concordance du Tao-tsang* numbering) — the first of the *sì fǔ* 四輔 ("Four Supplements") of the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (1445), which sit after the *sāndòng* 三洞 ("Three Caverns" — [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) 洞真, [KR5b](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/) 洞玄, [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/) 洞神). In the classical *sì fǔ* scheme, *Tàixuán* is the supplement attached to the *Dòngzhēn bù* and to the Shàngqīng 上清 tradition: it was originally the textual home of the Lǎozǐ-and-its-commentaries — that being the senior pre-revelation classical layer Shàngqīng claimed as its philosophical ancestry. Wilkinson §29.4.3–4 notes that the *sāndòng* are *schools* and the cross-cutting *shí'èr lèi* 十二類 are *genres*, with the four supplements wedged in between — and that by the Míng compilation the school-axis had ceased to cohere with the actual contents of each section. Nowhere is the dislocation sharper than here: the Lǎozǐ corpus that *Tàixuán* was theoretically built around was in the event placed in [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/) *Dòngshén bù* during the Sòng-era catalog merger Schipper & Verellen reconstruct (*Taoist Canon* 1: 30–40), and what fills the surviving *Tàixuán bù* of the Míng canon is what the editors had left over once the three Caverns and the Lǎozǐ block had been fixed: a heterogeneous archive of (i) a tail of supplementary Shàngqīng / Língbǎo scriptures the *Dòngzhēn* and *Dòngxuán* blocks did not absorb, (ii) the entire ***Zhōuyì cāntóngqì*** 周易參同契 commentary tradition — the foundational scripture of Chinese alchemy, structurally tied to the *Yì jīng* and to the Lǎozǐ but not at home in either, (iii) the great Daoist anthologies *Yún jí qī qiān* 雲笈七籤 [KR5d0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0055) and *Dào shū* 道樞 [KR5d0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0039), (iv) the Daoist-affiliated medical classics *Huáng dì nèi jīng* and *Nán jīng* with their canonical Táng-Sòng commentaries [KR5d0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0040)–[KR5d0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0047), (v) the Tao Hongjing flagship *Zhēn gào* 真誥 [KR5d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0036) — the foundational document of Shàngqīng, here because *Tàixuán* is technically the Shàngqīng supplement, (vi) a *zhūzǐ* 諸子 (masters) cluster of Lǎo-Zhuāng-orbit pseudepigraphic works — *Guǐ gǔ zǐ* [KR5d0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0048), *Kàng cāng zǐ* [KR5d0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0037) [KR5d0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0038), *Tiān yǐn zǐ* [KR5d0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0049), *Sù lǚ zǐ* [KR5d0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0050), *Wú néng zǐ* [KR5d0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0051), *Xuán zhēn zǐ* [KR5d0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0052), *Liú zǐ* [KR5d0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0053) — and the *Shān hǎi jīng* 山海經 [KR5d0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0054) with [郭璞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E7%92%9E)'s commentary, (vii) the Quánzhēn 全真 *yǔlù* 語錄 ("recorded sayings") corpus that documents the early Northern-Lineage patriarchs [KR5d0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0079)–[KR5d0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0083), and (viii) a dense Southern-Sòng / Jīn / Yuán *nèidān* 內丹 commentary archive culminating in [陳致虛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E8%87%B4%E8%99%9B)'s *Shàng yáng zǐ jīn dān dà yào* [KR5d0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0090)–[KR5d0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0093) and the Yuán Quánzhēn *cí*-anthology *Míng hè yú yīn* 鳴鶴餘音 [KR5d0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0123) that closes the section. The *Tàixuán bù* is therefore best read not as a coherent textual school but as the *Dàozàng*'s structural overflow basin for major Daoist literature that the three-Cavern scheme could not house.

The chronological span runs from the late-Warring-States *Shān hǎi jīng* core (c. 400 BCE, [KR5d0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0054)) and the *Guǐ gǔ zǐ* (Warring States – Hàn, [KR5d0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0048)) through to the early-Míng *Suí jī yìng huà lù* 隨機應化錄 of [何道全](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E9%81%93%E5%85%A8) (1401, [KR5d0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0099)). Date distribution by composition midpoint is sharply skewed to the Sòng-Yuán: a thin pre-Táng nucleus (5–6 titles: the *Shān hǎi jīng*, *Guǐ gǔ zǐ*, *Líng qí běn zhāng zhèng jīng* [KR5d0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0064), *Liú zǐ* [KR5d0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0053), *Zhēn gào* [KR5d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0036), *Huá yáng Táo yǐn jū jí* [KR5d0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0073)); a substantial Táng layer (~15 titles, anchored by [王冰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%86%B0)'s 762 *Sù wèn* recension [KR5d0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0040) and the [司馬承禎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E6%89%BF%E7%A6%8E) / [吳筠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E7%AD%A0) philosophical-Daoist cluster); a sharp Five-Dynasties peak with the 947 [彭曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E6%9B%89) *Cān tóng qì* commentary [KR5d0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0019) [KR5d0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0020) and [譚峭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%9A%E5%B3%AD)'s *Huà shū* [KR5d0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0067); a major Northern-Sòng wave driven by [張君房](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%90%9B%E6%88%BF)'s *Yún jí qī qiān* and [邵雍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E9%9B%8D)'s cosmological-historical corpus; the dominant **Southern-Sòng / Jīn / Yuán mass (~80 titles, c. 1100–1400)** that contains the entire *Cān tóng qì* commentary archipelago, the Quánzhēn *yǔlù* cluster, the [俞琰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BF%9E%E7%90%B0) and [雷思齊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9B%B7%E6%80%9D%E9%BD%8A) Yì-cosmology clusters, and the late-Yuán *nèidān* synthesis of [陳致虛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E8%87%B4%E8%99%9B) and his successors; and a sparse early-Míng tail terminating at [何道全](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E9%81%93%E5%85%A8) (1401) and [彭致中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E8%87%B4%E4%B8%AD) (1347). The section therefore reads in practice as the great Sòng-Yuán Daoist-syncretic archive — bracketed by a token classical residue at one end and a Quánzhēn-poetry coda at the other.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The opening Shàngqīng / Língbǎo residue (本文類, [KR5d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0001)–[KR5d0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0011)).** Eleven short scriptures that the *Dòngzhēn* and *Dòngxuán* compilers did not absorb, falling onto the *Tàixuán* supplement as overflow from the senior Shàngqīng tradition. The cluster includes [KR5d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0001) *Xuán jīng bì xiá Líng bǎo jù xuán jīng*, [KR5d0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0002) *Tài shàng Dòngxuán Líng bǎo sān yī wǔ qì zhēn jīng*, the *Shàng qīng* short scriptures [KR5d0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0005) [KR5d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0006) [KR5d0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0010) [KR5d0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0011), and the Líng bǎo / Dòngxuán short scriptures [KR5d0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0003) [KR5d0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0004) [KR5d0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0007) [KR5d0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0008) [KR5d0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0009). Most are Six-Dynasties – Táng in core date with substantial Sòng-era editorial layers; the cluster is the principal reason the section is *technically* still the Shàngqīng supplement.

**The *Zhēn gào* and the Shàngqīng documentary anchor.**
- *Zhēn gào* 真誥 [KR5d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0036) — [陶弘景](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%BC%98%E6%99%AF) (456–536), finished form 499. **The foundational compilation of the Shàngqīng revelation**, gathering the séance records of Yáng Xī 楊羲 and the Xǔ 許 family (364–370) with Táo's philological apparatus including the celebrated marginal notes on autograph-handwriting identification — at once the central document of fourth-century Shàngqīng visionary practice and a masterpiece of medieval textual criticism.
- *Huá yáng Táo yǐn jū jí* 華陽陶隱居集 [KR5d0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0073) — [陶弘景](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%BC%98%E6%99%AF)'s collected works in 2 *juàn*, edited by Fù Xiāo 傅霄 (d. 1159) and Chén Jué 陳桷 (fl. 1131–1162); the principal source for Táo's prose and verse outside the *Zhēn gào*.

**The *Zhōuyì cāntóngqì* 周易參同契 commentary archipelago — the densest single exegetical cluster in the section.** The foundational alchemical scripture, traditionally ascribed to the Eastern-Hàn [魏伯陽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E4%BC%AF%E9%99%BD) (Wèi Bóyáng) — the **Urtext of both *wài dān* 外丹 (external alchemy) and Sòng-Yuán *nèi dān* 內丹 (internal alchemy)**, structurally a synthesis of *Yì jīng* cosmology, Huáng Lǎo metaphysics, and alchemical practice. The *Tàixuán bù* preserves five distinct received recensions of the text plus its principal traditional commentaries:
- *Recension I*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì* (一) [KR5d0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0016) — Táng recension with commentary ascribed to the Hàn immortal [陰長生](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B0%E9%95%B7%E7%94%9F) (Yīn Chángshēng), pseudepigraphical.
- *Recension II*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì zhù* (二) [KR5d0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0017) — twelfth-century or later anonymous commentary.
- *Recension III*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì kǎo yì* 考異 [KR5d0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0018) — **[朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) (Zhū Xī, 1130–1200)**'s 1197 philological collation, the principal Neo-Confucian engagement with the alchemical classic and an unusual instance of a major Chéng-Zhū-school text entering the Daoist canon.
- *Recension IV*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì zhù* (四) [KR5d0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0021) — Five-Dynasties anonymous.
- *Recension V*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì zhù* (五) [KR5d0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0027) — Southern Sòng commentary by [儲華谷](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%84%B2%E8%8F%AF%E8%B0%B7).
- *Péng Xiǎo's commentary*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì fēn zhāng tōng zhēn yì* [KR5d0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0019) + *Dǐng qì gē míng jìng tú* [KR5d0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0020) — **[彭曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E6%9B%89) (Péng Xiǎo, d. 955)**, 947, **the single most influential traditional commentary on the *Cān tóng qì***; Péng's structural division into chapters and his coherent alchemical reading furnish the interpretive framework inherited by every later commentator, including Zhū Xī.
- *Yú Yǎn's commentary*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì fā huī* 發揮 [KR5d0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0022) (1284) + *Shì yí* 釋疑 [KR5d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0024) (1281) — [俞琰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BF%9E%E7%90%B0) (Yú Yǎn, 1258–1314), the principal Sòng-Yuán transition commentary.
- *Chén Xiǎnwēi's commentary*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì jiě* 解 [KR5d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0025) (1234) — [陳顯微](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%A1%AF%E5%BE%AE), Southern Sòng nèidān reading.
- *Chén Zhìxū's commentary*: *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì fēn zhāng zhù* 分章註 [KR5d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0023) (Yuán) — [陳致虛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E8%87%B4%E8%99%9B).
- *Jiǎng Yībiāo's collection*: *Gǔ wén Cān tóng qì jí jiě* [KR5d0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0026) (Míng) — [蔣一彪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E4%B8%80%E5%BD%AA) (fl. 1614)'s late-Míng compendium.

**The "Old-Text Dragon-Tiger Classic" satellite cluster.** A late-Hàn / Táng pseudepigraphic alchemical scripture treated by Sòng commentators as either a source-text of, or a parallel rewriting of, the *Cāntóng qì* itself:
- *Gǔ wén Lóng hǔ jīng zhù shū* 古文龍虎經註疏 [KR5d0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0013) — [王道](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%81%93) (Sòng).
- *Gǔ wén Lóng hǔ shàng jīng zhù* [KR5d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0014) and *Dú Lóng hǔ jīng* [KR5d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0015) — anonymous Sòng companion commentaries.
- *Lóng hǔ yuán zhǐ* 龍虎元旨 [KR5d0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0106) — [青霞子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9D%92%E9%9C%9E%E5%AD%90) (late Táng – Five Dynasties), the philosophical-cosmological reading.
- *Lóng hǔ huán dān jué sòng* [KR5d0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0105) ([林太古](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9E%97%E5%A4%AA%E5%8F%A4), N. Sòng) and *Lóng hǔ huán dān jué* [KR5d0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0107) ([李真人](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E7%9C%9F%E4%BA%BA), N. Sòng) — the operative-alchemy gloss tradition.

**The Yú Yǎn — Léi Sīqí Yì-cosmology cluster.** Two Sòng-Yuán figures who reread the *Yì jīng* through Daoist-cosmological lenses, jointly responsible for placing Yì-numerology inside the canon:
- [俞琰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BF%9E%E7%90%B0) (Yú Yǎn, 1258–1314): the *Cāntóng qì* commentaries above plus *Yì wài bié zhuàn* 易外別傳 [KR5d0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0028) (the Yìjīng-as-alchemical-key reading, c. 1284), *Xí shàng fǔ tán* 席上腐談 [KR5d0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0029) (philosophical miscellany), *Xuán pìn zhī mén fù* 玄牝之門賦 [KR5d0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0030) — Yú Yǎn alone accounts for **six titles** in the section, the most prolific single author in *Tàixuán bù*.
- [雷思齊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9B%B7%E6%80%9D%E9%BD%8A) (Léi Sīqí, 1223–1301, "Kōng shān xiān sheng" 空山先生): *Yì shì tōng biàn* 易筮通變 [KR5d0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0031), *Hé tú* 河圖 [KR5d0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0033), *Yì tú tōng biàn* 易圖通變 [KR5d0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0034) (1330); with prefatory piece [KR5d0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0032) (1300) — the principal Daoist *Yì*-diagrammatics tradition of the Yuán, parallel to the Confucian *Hé tú / Luò shū* speculation of [邵雍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E9%9B%8D).

**[邵雍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E9%9B%8D)'s cosmological-historical corpus.** The Sòng Yìxué master enters the Daoist canon through his two principal works:
- *Huáng jí jīng shì* 皇極經世 [KR5d0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0063) — [邵雍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E9%9B%8D) (Shào Yōng, 1011–1077), the great cosmological-historical treatise; the entire history of the cosmos and of human civilization charted on the 元 (yuán) – 會 (huì) – 運 (yùn) – 世 (shì) grid yielding world-cycles of 129,600 years. Together with the *Cān tóng qì*, the foundational reference of East Asian speculative numerology.
- *Yī chuān jī rǎng jí* 伊川擊壤集 [KR5d0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0065) — Shào's poetry collection in 20 *juàn*, the principal source for his philosophical *shī* and the textual record of his Luòyáng circle (Sī Mǎguāng, Chéng Yí, Zhāng Zǎi). The presence in *Tàixuán bù* of two major works by a figure conventionally listed as a Neo-Confucian *Yìxué* master is one of the section's striking editorial decisions.

**The great Northern Sòng / Southern Sòng Daoist anthologies.**
- *Yún jí qī qiān* 雲笈七籤 [KR5d0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0055) — [張君房](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%90%9B%E6%88%BF) (Zhāng Jūnfáng, fl. 1008–1025), c. 1028–1029, 122 *juàn*. **The single most important pre-modern Daoist encyclopedia**, distilled from the Northern-Sòng *Dà Sòng tiān gōng bǎo zàng* 大宋天宮寶藏 (1019) which Zhāng had supervised. Preserves substantial material — early hagiographies, Six-Dynasties Shàngqīng meditation texts, Táng alchemical and dietetic literature — not transmitted elsewhere, since the Northern Sòng canon Zhāng was excerpting was lost in the Jīn-Yuán destructions. The first reference consulted for any Táng or pre-Táng Daoist text.
- *Dào shū* 道樞 [KR5d0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0039) — [曾慥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%BE%E6%85%A5) (Zēng Zào, d. 1155), c. 1151, 42 *juàn*. The great Southern-Sòng topical anthology of Daoist meditative, alchemical, and *yǎngshēng* literature, organized under 100+ thematic headings; many cited passages derive from texts otherwise lost.
- *Zhì yán zǒng* 至言總 [KR5d0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0056) — [范翛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8C%83%E7%BF%9B%E7%84%B6) (late Táng), 5 *juàn*; smaller topical anthology of the same genre.

**The Daoist-medical cluster — the *Huáng dì nèi jīng* and *Nán jīng*.** A striking concentration of medical classics inside the Daoist canon, reflecting the Tang-Song understanding of medicine as a branch of Daoist cosmological practice:
- *Huáng dì nèi jīng Sù wèn bǔ zhù shì wén* 黃帝內經素問補註釋文 [KR5d0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0040) — [王冰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%86%B0) (Wáng Bīng, c. 710 – c. 805) commentary, 762, with the Sòng supplements of [林億](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9E%97%E5%84%84) (Lín Yì) and [孫兆](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E5%85%86) (Sūn Zhào) c. 1078. **The standard received recension of the *Sù wèn***, including Wáng Bīng's restoration of the lost "Seven Great Treatises" (七篇大論) on cosmological correspondences.
- *Huáng dì nèi jīng Líng shū lüè* 黃帝內經靈樞略 [KR5d0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0041) — short companion-text to the *Líng shū*.
- *Huáng dì Sù wèn Líng shū jí zhù* 黃帝素問靈樞集註 [KR5d0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0042) — [史崧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B2%E5%B4%A7) (Shǐ Sōng, fl. 1155), 23 *juàn*; the standard received *Líng shū*, transmitting Shǐ Sōng's 1155 collation of the previously lost text.
- *Huáng dì nèi jīng Sù wèn yí piān* [KR5d0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0043) — Sòng supplement.
- *Sù wèn rù shì yùn qì lùn ào* 素問入式運氣論奧 [KR5d0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0044) — [劉溫舒](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E6%BA%AB%E8%88%92) (1099); the Northern Sòng systematization of *Sù wèn* "yùnqì" 運氣 (climatic-cycle) cosmology.
- *Sù wèn liù qì xuán zhū mì yǔ* 素問六氣玄珠密語 [KR5d0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0045) — [王冰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%86%B0) attributed.
- *Huáng dì bā shí yī Nán jīng* commentary cluster: *zhù yì tú xù lùn* [KR5d0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0046) and *zuǎn tú jù jiě* [KR5d0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0047) (1269) — both by [李駉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%A7%89) (Lǐ Jiǒng), the Southern-Sòng received-text commentary on the *Eighty-One Difficulties Classic* 難經.

**The *zhūzǐ* 諸子 (masters) cluster.** Pre-Hàn–Táng pseudepigraphic master-texts in the Lǎo-Zhuāng orbit that the Sòng catalogers placed here rather than alongside the *Lǎozǐ* corpus in [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/) *Dòngshén bù*:
- *Guǐ gǔ zǐ* 鬼谷子 [KR5d0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0048) — attributed to the Warring-States teacher of Sū Qín 蘇秦 and Zhāng Yí 張儀; rhetorical-diplomatic treatise on persuasion-by-contextual-calibration.
- *Kàng cāng zǐ* 亢倉子 [KR5d0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0037) (text) + *zhù* [KR5d0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0038) (commentary) — fabricated 742 under [李隆基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%9A%86%E5%9F%BA) (Táng Xuánzōng)'s patronage to round out the canonical Daoist classics, ascribed to *Zhuāngzǐ* ch. 23 figure [庚桑楚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%9A%E6%A1%91%E6%A5%9A); the companion-fabrication to the *Dòng líng zhēn jīng* [KR5c0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0050).
- *Tiān yǐn zǐ* 天隱子 [KR5d0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0049) — [司馬承禎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E6%89%BF%E7%A6%8E) (Sī Mǎ Chéngzhēn, 647–735), 12th Máoshān patriarch; a foundational Táng meditation manual organized in eight stages (*qì shàn* 齋戒, *ān chù* 安處, *cún xiǎng* 存想, *zuò wàng* 坐忘, *shén jiě* 神解, etc.).
- *Sù lǚ zǐ* 素履子 [KR5d0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0050) — [張弧](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%BC%A7) (Zhāng Hú, Táng), philosophical miscellany.
- *Wú néng zǐ* 無能子 [KR5d0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0051) — anonymous, 887; a late-Táng political-Daoist treatise on the failure of social institutions, contemporaneous with the Huáng Cháo 黃巢 rebellion.
- *Xuán zhēn zǐ wài piān* 玄真子(外篇) [KR5d0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0052) — [張志和](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%BF%97%E5%92%8C) (Zhāng Zhìhé, fl. 757–762), the lyric-philosophical writings of the famous fisherman-poet.
- *Liú zǐ* 劉子 [KR5d0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0053) — with [袁孝政](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%81%E5%AD%9D%E6%94%BF)'s commentary; a Liáng – Táng compendium of moral-political maxims.
- *Shān hǎi jīng* 山海經 [KR5d0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0054) — with [郭璞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E7%92%9E) (Guō Pú, 276–324)'s Jìn commentary; the late-Warring-States mythical-geographical encyclopedia, here entering the Daoist canon as a source of *xiānjìng* 仙境 cosmography. Chronologically the oldest text in the section.

**The Sī Mǎ Chéngzhēn — Wú Yún Táng-Daoist philosophical cluster.**
- *Zuò wàng lùn* 坐忘論 [KR5d0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0059) — [司馬承禎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E6%89%BF%E7%A6%8E) (647–735), the classical Táng treatise on the practice of "sitting and forgetting" (*zuò wàng*) drawn from *Zhuāngzǐ* ch. 6; the foundational text of Táng Daoist meditation theory. Together with [KR5d0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0049) *Tiān yǐn zǐ*, anchors the 上清 / 茅山 meditation tradition.
- *Zōng xuán xiān sheng wén jí* 宗玄先生文集 [KR5d0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0074) — [吳筠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E7%AD%A0) (Wú Yún, d. 778)'s collected works in 3 *juàn*; one of the few Táng Daoist literary collections to survive intact.
- *Zōng xuán xiān sheng Xuán gāng lùn* 玄綱論 [KR5d0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0075) — Wú Yún's principal philosophical-Daoist treatise, a systematic exposition of the "Mystic Net" cosmology in 33 essays.
- *Wú zūn shī zhuàn* 吳尊師傳 [KR5d0076](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0076) — [權德輿](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AC%8A%E5%BE%B7%E8%BC%BF) (Quán Déyú, 759–818)'s biography of Wú Yún, the principal Táng-era source on his life.
- *Nán tǒng dà jūn nèi dān jiǔ zhāng jīng* [KR5d0077](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0077) — pseudepigraphic Five-Dynasties scripture ascribed to Wú Yún.

**The Quánzhēn 全真 *yǔlù* 語錄 ("recorded sayings") cluster.** The principal documentation of the first two generations of the Northern-Lineage Quánzhēn patriarchs — [王重陽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%87%8D%E9%99%BD) (Wáng Chóngyáng, 1113–1170) and his "Seven Perfected" (*qī zhēn* 七眞) disciples — recorded by their immediate followers:
- *Jìn zhēn rén yǔ lù* 晉真人語錄 [KR5d0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0079) — sayings of Jìn Zhīqī 晉志契 (Jin Zhenren), Jin-Yuan transition.
- *Dān yáng zhēn rén yǔ lù* 丹陽真人語錄 [KR5d0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0080) — compiled by [王頤中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%A0%A4%E4%B8%AD); the sayings of [馬鈺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%88%BA) (Mǎ Yù, 1123–1184, 丹陽子), the senior of Wáng Chóngyáng's seven disciples and chief patriarch of the Yùxiān 遇仙 branch.
- *Wú wéi qīng jìng cháng shēng zhēn rén zhì zhēn yǔ lù* 無為清靜長生真人至真語錄 [KR5d0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0081) — [劉處玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E8%99%95%E7%8E%84) (Liú Chùxuán, 1147–1203, *Chángshēng zǐ*); 1202 preface; the sayings of the third disciple, founder of the Suíshān 隨山 branch.
- *Pán shān Qī yún Wáng zhēn rén yǔ lù* 盤山棲雲王真人語錄 [KR5d0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0082) — compiled by [論志煥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AB%96%E5%BF%97%E7%85%A5) 1247; the sayings of [王志謹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BF%97%E8%AC%B9) (Wáng Zhìjǐn, 1178–1263), the great second-generation Quánzhēn teacher whose Pánshān 盤山 discourses are the most philosophically developed of the early-Quánzhēn *yǔlù* corpus (the same text appears as [KR5a0272](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0272) in the *Xiūzhēn shíshū*).
- *Qīng ān Yíng chán zǐ yǔ lù* 清庵瑩蟾子語錄 [KR5d0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0083) — 1288 preface, compiled by [柴元皋](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%B4%E5%85%83%E7%9A%8B); the sayings of [李道純](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%81%93%E7%B4%94) (Lǐ Dàochún, fl. 1290), the great late-Yuán Quánzhēn-Southern syncretist.

**The Lǚ Dòngbīn / Wáng Yù late-Sòng – Yuán syncretic cluster.**
- *Chún yáng zhēn rén hùn chéng jí* 純陽真人渾成集 [KR5d0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0078) — compiled by [何志淵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E5%BF%97%E6%B7%B5) 1251; verse and prose ascribed to [呂洞賓](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E6%B4%9E%E8%B3%93) (Lǚ Dòngbīn, Chúnyáng zhēnrén), the central figure of the Zhōng–Lǚ 鍾呂 nèidān lineage and the patron-saint of late-imperial Daoism.
- *Shàng qīng tài xuán jí* 上清太玄集 [KR5d0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0084) — [侯善淵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BE%AF%E5%96%84%E6%B7%B5) (Hóu Shànyuān, Jīn), the principal Quánzhēn-flavoured Jīn-era collected writings.
- *Xuán jiào dà gōng àn* 玄教大公案 [KR5d0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0088) — [苗善時](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8B%97%E5%96%84%E6%99%82) (1324); the Quánzhēn "great gōngàn" 公案 — Daoist appropriation of the Chán *kōan* form.
- *Xuán zōng zhí zhǐ wàn fǎ tóng guī* 玄宗直指萬法同歸 [KR5d0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0089) — [牧常晁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%89%A7%E5%B8%B8%E6%99%81) (fl. 1294–1320), the Yuán Quánzhēn syncretic synthesis under the slogan "the ten thousand methods all converge".
- *Dào chán jí* 道禪集 [KR5d0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0096) — [王志担](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BF%97%E6%8B%85) (1200–1272), explicit Daoist-Chán synthesis.

**[陳致虛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E8%87%B4%E8%99%9B)'s *Jīn dān dà yào* corpus.** The principal late-Yuán *nèidān* systematic synthesis, all dated c. 1331:
- *Shàng yáng zǐ jīn dān dà yào* 上陽子金丹大要 [KR5d0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0090) — 16 *juàn*; the systematic treatise integrating Southern-Lineage and Quánzhēn nèidān doctrine.
- *Jīn dān dà yào tú* [KR5d0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0091) — illustrated supplement.
- *Jīn dān dà yào liè xiān zhì* [KR5d0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0092) — companion hagiography.
- *Jīn dān dà yào xiān pài* [KR5d0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0093) — lineage tables documenting the genealogy of Chén Zhìxū's transmission from [張伯端](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E4%BC%AF%E7%AB%AF) forward.
- *Zhōu yì cān tóng qì fēn zhāng zhù* [KR5d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0023) — Chén Zhìxū's parallel *Cān tóng qì* commentary, intellectually continuous with the *Dà yào*.

**The *Wùzhēn piān* / Southern Lineage *nèidān* commentary tradition.** The *Wùzhēn piān* itself sits in [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) [KR5a0142](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0142)–[KR5a0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0147); the *Tàixuán bù* preserves the further satellite literature:
- *Jīn dān sì bǎi zì* 金丹四百字 [KR5d0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0104) — attributed to [張伯端](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E4%BC%AF%E7%AB%AF) (Zhāng Bóduān, 984–1082, founder of the Southern Lineage 南宗), the 400-character verse-summary of the *Wùzhēn piān* with 黃自如's 1241 commentary.
- *Huán dān fù mìng piān* 還丹復命篇 [KR5d0111](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0111) — [薛道光](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%96%9B%E9%81%93%E5%85%89) (Xuē Dàoguāng, 1078–1191), 1126 preface; the third patriarch of the Southern Lineage. Together with [KR5d0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0114) *Huán yuán piān* 還源篇 ([石泰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9F%B3%E6%B3%B0) Shí Tài, d. 1158, second patriarch) the section preserves the patriarchal succession-texts of the Southern Lineage.
- *Cuì xū piān* 翠虛篇 [KR5d0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0113) — [陳楠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%A5%A0) (Chén Nán, d. 1213, fourth patriarch); compiled by Wáng Sīchéng 1217.
- *Yuán qīng zǐ zhì mìng piān* 爰清子至命篇 [KR5d0112](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0112) — [王慶升](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%85%B6%E5%8D%87) (1249).
- *Yú zhuāng xiè hòu lù* 漁莊邂逅錄 [KR5d0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0109) — [吳悞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%82%9E) (Wú Wù, fl. 1187).
- *Jīn dān zhí zhǐ* 金丹直指 [KR5d0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0095) — [周無所住](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E7%84%A1%E6%89%80%E4%BD%8F) (1250).
- A constellation of shorter Sòng-Yuán *nèidān* essays and verse: *Zhèng dào gē* [KR5d0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0118), *Chén xiān sheng nèi dān jué* [KR5d0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0119), *Dòng yuán zǐ nèi dān jué* [KR5d0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0120), *Nèi dān huán yuán jué* [KR5d0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0121), *Cháng shēng zhǐ yào piān* [KR5d0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0122), *Jīn yè dà dān shī* [KR5d0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0117), *Huán dān zhì yào piān* [KR5d0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0115), *Dǎn jiǎ jí* [KR5d0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0116), *Nèi dān mì jué* [KR5d0108](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0108), *Jīn dān zhēng zōng* [KR5d0110](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0110), *Jīn dān zhēn yī lùn* [KR5d0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0103), *Zhēn rén Gāo Xiàngxiān jīn dān gē* [KR5d0102](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0102) (1014).

**[王玠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E7%8E%A0) (Wáng Jiè, fl. 1330s–1392) and the early-Ming Quánzhēn coda.**
- *Huán zhēn jí* 還真集 [KR5d0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0097) — Wáng Jiè, 1392 preface (with foreword by 43rd Celestial Master [張宇初](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%AE%87%E5%88%9D)); the late-Yuán Quánzhēn-Southern syncretic capstone.
- *Dào xuán piān* 道玄篇 [KR5d0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0098) — Wáng Jiè, parallel collection.
- *Yuán yáng zǐ fǎ yǔ* 原陽子法語 [KR5d0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0094) — [趙宜真](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E5%AE%9C%E7%9C%9F) (Zhào Yízhēn, d. 1382), edited by his disciple [劉淵然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E6%B7%B5%E7%84%B6) (1351–1432); the late-Yuán / early-Ming Pure Brightness 淨明 / Quánzhēn synthesis.
- *Suí jī yìng huà lù* 隨機應化錄 [KR5d0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0099) — [何道全](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E9%81%93%E5%85%A8) (Hé Dàoquán, d. 1399), 1401 preface; the closing testimony of the Yuán-Míng Quánzhēn transition.

**The closing Quánzhēn poetry anthology.** *Míng hè yú yīn* 鳴鶴餘音 [KR5d0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0123) — compiled by [彭致中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E8%87%B4%E4%B8%AD) in 1347, with preface by [虞集](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%99%9E%E9%9B%86) (Yú Jí, 1272–1348); 9 *juàn* of *cí* 詞 lyric poems by Quánzhēn patriarchs and disciples — the most important collection of *nèidān* poetic literature. **The final text of *Tàixuán bù* and of the entire DZ-numbered range 1001–1100.**

**Miscellaneous further titles.**
- *Yuān yuán dào miào dòng zhēn jì piān* [KR5d0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0012) — [李景元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%99%AF%E5%85%83) (N. Sòng), Shàngqīng-flavoured 3-juan supplement.
- *Jīn suǒ liú zhū yǐn* 金鎖流珠引 [KR5d0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0035) — pseudepigraphically attributed to [李淳風](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%B7%B3%E9%A2%A8) (Lǐ Chúnfēng, 602–670); 29 *juàn* on stellar-Daoist meditation and astral ritual.
- *Líng qí běn zhāng zhèng jīng* 靈棋本章正經 [KR5d0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0064) — with [顏幼明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E5%B9%BC%E6%98%8E) (E. Jìn) commentary; the canonical Daoist divinatory casting-the-lots scripture, formally cognate with the *Yì jīng* but operationally distinct.
- *Tài xuán bǎo diǎn* 太玄寶典 [KR5d0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0057), *Dào tǐ lùn* 道體論 [KR5d0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0058), *Dà dào lùn* 大道論 [KR5d0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0060), *Xīn mù lùn* 心目論 [KR5d0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0061), *Sān lùn yuán zhǐ* 三論元旨 [KR5d0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0062), *Xuán zhū lù* 玄珠錄 [KR5d0071](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0071) ([王暉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%9A%89), 626–697), *Tài shàng xiū zhēn xuán zhāng* [KR5d0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0066), *Yún gōng fǎ yǔ* [KR5d0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0072) (1298), *Hǎi kè lùn* [KR5d0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0068), *Wù xuán piān* [KR5d0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0069) (1229), *Tài xū xīn yuān piān* [KR5d0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0070), *Xiū liàn xū zhī* [KR5d0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0100), *Yù shì jīng* [KR5d0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0101), *Dòng yuān jí* [KR5d0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0086) ([李思聰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%80%9D%E8%81%B0), c. 1050), *Dòng yuān jí* (再) [KR5d0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0087) ([長筌子](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%95%B7%E7%AD%8C%E5%AD%90), Jīn-Yuán), *Jìn dòng tiān hǎi yuè biǎo* [KR5d0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0085) (1050) — together making up the discursive-essay and short-cosmological-treatise tail of the section.

### Important persons

- [陶弘景](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%BC%98%E6%99%AF) (Táo Hóngjǐng, 456–536) — Shàngqīng patriarch and editor of the *Zhēn gào* [KR5d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0036); his collected works [KR5d0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0073) also live here. The Six-Dynasties textual anchor of *Tàixuán bù* (his role across the canon as Shàngqīng codifier is more fully treated in [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/)).
- [魏伯陽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E4%BC%AF%E9%99%BD) (Wèi Bóyáng, attributed, Eastern Hàn) — pseudo-author of the *Zhōuyì cāntóng qì*; the foundational alchemical authority around whose text the central commentary archipelago [KR5d0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0016)–[KR5d0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0027) of the section is built.
- [彭曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E6%9B%89) (Péng Xiǎo, d. 955) — Later-Shǔ alchemist; author of the most influential traditional commentary on the *Cāntóng qì* [KR5d0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0019) + [KR5d0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0020) (947), the structural framework for every subsequent reading. The single most consequential author in the central alchemical cluster.
- [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) (Zhū Xī, 1130–1200) — Southern-Sòng Neo-Confucian patriarch; his *Cāntóng qì kǎo yì* [KR5d0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0018) (1197) is the principal Chéng-Zhū-school engagement with Daoist alchemy and an unusual instance of a major Confucian *Daoxué* figure entering the Daoist canon. (His role in [KR1a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/) *Yì lèi* and elsewhere in the *Jīng* division is more central.)
- [俞琰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BF%9E%E7%90%B0) (Yú Yǎn, 1258–1314) — Sòng-Yuán transitional polymath; author of six titles in the section ([KR5d0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0022) [KR5d0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0024) [KR5d0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0028) [KR5d0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0029) [KR5d0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0030) plus other commentary) including the principal Sòng-Yuán *Cāntóng qì* commentary and the *Yì wài bié zhuàn*. The most prolific single author in *Tàixuán bù*.
- [雷思齊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9B%B7%E6%80%9D%E9%BD%8A) (Léi Sīqí, 1223–1301) — Yuán Daoist *Yìxué* master; author of the *Yì shì tōng biàn* / *Hé tú* / *Yì tú tōng biàn* cluster [KR5d0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0031)–[KR5d0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0034), the principal Daoist counterpart to the Confucian *Hé tú / Luò shū* speculation of [邵雍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E9%9B%8D).
- [陳致虛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E8%87%B4%E8%99%9B) (Chén Zhìxū, 1290–1343) — late-Yuán Quánzhēn-Southern syncretist; author of the *Shàng yáng zǐ jīn dān dà yào* cluster [KR5d0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0090)–[KR5d0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0093) (c. 1331) and a parallel *Cāntóng qì fēn zhāng zhù* [KR5d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0023). The principal systematic *nèidān* author in the section.
- [張君房](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%90%9B%E6%88%BF) (Zhāng Jūnfáng, fl. 1008–1025) — Northern-Sòng Daoist editor; compiler of the *Yún jí qī qiān* [KR5d0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0055), the foundational pre-modern Daoist encyclopedia. His earlier supervision of the Northern-Sòng *Dà Sòng tiān gōng bǎo zàng* (1019) makes him the single most consequential Daoist bibliographer of the Sòng.
- [曾慥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%BE%E6%85%A5) (Zēng Zào, d. 1155) — Southern-Sòng literatus; compiler of the *Dào shū* [KR5d0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0039) anthology, the principal Southern-Sòng counterpart to the *Yún jí qī qiān*.
- [邵雍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E9%9B%8D) (Shào Yōng, 1011–1077) — Northern-Sòng cosmologist; author of *Huáng jí jīng shì* [KR5d0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0063) and *Yī chuān jī rǎng jí* [KR5d0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0065). His placement in the Daoist canon, despite his Neo-Confucian standing, registers the Sòng catalogers' read of his numerological *Yìxué* as continuous with the Daoist cosmological tradition.
- [司馬承禎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E6%89%BF%E7%A6%8E) (Sī Mǎ Chéngzhēn, 647–735) — 12th Máoshān Shàngqīng patriarch; author of *Tiān yǐn zǐ* [KR5d0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0049) and *Zuò wàng lùn* [KR5d0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0059), the two foundational Táng treatises on Shàngqīng meditation. The principal Táng-era theoretician of *zuò wàng* sitting-and-forgetting practice.
- [吳筠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E7%AD%A0) (Wú Yún, d. 778) — Táng court Daoist; author of *Wén jí* [KR5d0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0074) and *Xuán gāng lùn* [KR5d0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0075); the principal Táng literary-philosophical Daoist after Sī Mǎ Chéngzhēn.
- [王冰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%86%B0) (Wáng Bīng, c. 710 – c. 805) — mid-Táng physician; author of the 762 *Huáng dì nèi jīng Sù wèn* recension [KR5d0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0040) including the restored "Seven Great Treatises" on cosmological-medical correspondences. The single most important commentator on the Chinese medical classic and the principal bridge between Táng Daoism and classical medicine.
- [譚峭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%9A%E5%B3%AD) (Tán Qiào, fl. 940s) — Five-Dynasties Daoist philosopher; author of *Huà shū* 化書 [KR5d0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0067), a foundational work of speculative philosophy whose meditation on cosmic and social transformation cuts across Daoist metaphysics and political critique.
- [馬鈺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%88%BA) (Mǎ Yù, 1123–1184) — Quánzhēn first-generation patriarch; chief disciple of [王重陽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%87%8D%E9%99%BD); subject of the *Dān yáng zhēn rén yǔ lù* [KR5d0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0080) (compiled by his disciple [王頤中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E9%A0%A4%E4%B8%AD)). The principal documented voice of the founding generation of Quánzhēn.
- [劉處玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E8%99%95%E7%8E%84) (Liú Chùxuán, 1147–1203) — Quánzhēn first-generation patriarch; subject of [KR5d0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0081); founder of the Suíshān 隨山 branch.
- [王志謹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BF%97%E8%AC%B9) (Wáng Zhìjǐn, 1178–1263) — Quánzhēn second-generation patriarch; subject of *Pán shān Qī yún Wáng zhēn rén yǔ lù* [KR5d0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0082) (also [KR5a0272](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0272) in the *Xiūzhēn shíshū* recension); the most philosophically developed Quánzhēn teacher of the Jīn-Yuán transition.
- [李道純](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%81%93%E7%B4%94) (Lǐ Dàochún, fl. 1290) — Yuán Quánzhēn-Southern syncretist; subject of *Qīng ān Yíng chán zǐ yǔ lù* [KR5d0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0083) (1288). His commentarial and doctrinal corpus is principally housed in [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) and [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/); *Tàixuán bù* preserves the *yǔlù* witness.
- [呂洞賓](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E6%B4%9E%E8%B3%93) (Lǚ Dòngbīn, attributed) — the principal patron-saint of late-imperial Daoism; the central figure of the *Zhōng Lǚ* 鍾呂 nèidān lineage; his Chúnyáng-zhēnrén-attributed verse corpus is preserved here as [KR5d0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0078).

### Topics

- **The *sì fǔ* 四輔 (Four Supplements) and the *Tàixuán* paradox.** The notional scheme of the *Dàozàng* pairs each of the *sāndòng* with a textual supplement: *Tàixuán* with *Dòngzhēn* (Shàngqīng), *Tàipíng* with *Dòngxuán* (Língbǎo), *Tàiqīng* with *Dòngshén* (Sānhuáng), plus *Zhèngyī* spanning all three. Wilkinson §29.4.4 notes that this scheme cuts against the *shí'èr lèi* 十二類 genre axis and that by the Míng compilation the school/genre cross-classification had collapsed. *Tàixuán bù* registers the collapse: the Lǎozǐ corpus that the section was originally built around lives in [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/) (the Schipper-Verellen reconstruction is that the *Tàixuán* and *Dòngshén* sections merged in a Sòng-era catalog reform), and what fills *Tàixuán bù* in 1445 is the *Dàozàng*'s editorial overflow basin: alchemical, Yì-cosmological, medical, anthological, and Quánzhēn material that did not fit cleanly inside any Cavern.

- **The *Cāntóng qì* commentary tradition and the Sòng-Yuán nèidān synthesis.** Twelve of the section's titles ([KR5d0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0016)–[KR5d0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0027)) are commentaries on or recensions of the *Zhōuyì cāntóng qì* — the densest single exegetical archipelago in *Tàixuán bù* and one of the densest in the whole canon. The cluster includes the foundational [彭曉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BD%AD%E6%9B%89) commentary (947), the Neo-Confucian [朱熹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%86%B9) *kǎo yì* (1197), and the Sòng-Yuán nèidān readings of [陳顯微](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%A1%AF%E5%BE%AE), [儲華谷](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%84%B2%E8%8F%AF%E8%B0%B7), [俞琰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BF%9E%E7%90%B0), [陳致虛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E8%87%B4%E8%99%9B), and [蔣一彪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A3%E4%B8%80%E5%BD%AA). From the late twelfth century onward the *Cāntóng qì* is increasingly read through the lens of [張伯端](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E4%BC%AF%E7%AB%AF)'s *Wùzhēn piān* and the Southern Lineage's symbolic alchemy of *jīng* — *qì* — *shén*; this reading culminates in [陳致虛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E8%87%B4%E8%99%9B)'s *Jīn dān dà yào* corpus [KR5d0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0090)–[KR5d0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0093).

- **Daoist *Yìxué* 易學 and speculative numerology.** A distinctive strand of Daoist *Yì*-reading runs through the section: [邵雍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%B5%E9%9B%8D)'s *Huáng jí jīng shì* [KR5d0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0063) grids the cosmos and human history on a system of 元-會-運-世 cycles; [俞琰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BF%9E%E7%90%B0)'s *Yì wài bié zhuàn* [KR5d0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0028) reads the *Yì* as an alchemical key; [雷思齊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9B%B7%E6%80%9D%E9%BD%8A)'s *Yì tú tōng biàn* [KR5d0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0031)–[KR5d0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0034) develops the Daoist counterpart to the Confucian *Hé tú / Luò shū* diagrammatics. The presence of these works inside the Daoist canon — and the absence from [KR1a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/) *Yì lèi* of Shào Yōng's main treatise — registers the Sòng-Yuán understanding of numerology as a Daoist-cosmological domain rather than a Confucian-classical one.

- **The medical-Daoist cluster.** Eight titles ([KR5d0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0040)–[KR5d0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0047)) preserve the *Huáng dì nèi jīng* and *Nán jīng* in their canonical Táng-Sòng commentaries — the only major concentration of Chinese medical classics inside the Daoist canon. The cluster reflects the Táng understanding of medicine (especially the *yùnqì* 運氣 cosmological-medical doctrine [劉溫舒](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E6%BA%AB%E8%88%92) systematizes in [KR5d0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0044)) as a branch of Daoist cosmological practice. [王冰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%86%B0)'s 762 *Sù wèn* recension is the textual centre of all subsequent Chinese medicine; the *Tàixuán bù* is one of its two principal transmissional carriers (the other being the Sòng imperial editorial line of [林億](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9E%97%E5%84%84) and [孫兆](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E5%85%86)).

- **The *zhūzǐ* 諸子 supplementary classics.** The Sòng catalogers placed several Lǎo-Zhuāng-orbit pseudepigraphic master-texts here rather than alongside the *Lǎozǐ* corpus in [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/) *Dòngshén bù*: the *Guǐ gǔ zǐ* [KR5d0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0048), *Kàng cāng zǐ* [KR5d0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0037) [KR5d0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0038) (the Táng court fabrication that parallels the *Dòng líng zhēn jīng* [KR5c0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0050)), *Tiān yǐn zǐ* [KR5d0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0049), *Sù lǚ zǐ* [KR5d0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0050), *Wú néng zǐ* [KR5d0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0051), *Xuán zhēn zǐ* [KR5d0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0052), *Liú zǐ* [KR5d0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0053), plus the *Shān hǎi jīng* [KR5d0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0054) with [郭璞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E7%92%9E)'s commentary. The grouping registers a Sòng editorial distinction between the *Lǎozǐ-Zhuāngzǐ-Lièzǐ-Gēngsāngzǐ* canonical four (placed in *Dòngshén*) and a second tier of *zhūzǐ* placed here.

- **The Quánzhēn *yǔlù* genre.** Five of the section's titles ([KR5d0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0079)–[KR5d0083](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0083)) preserve the recorded sayings of the founding generation of the Northern-Lineage Quánzhēn movement — [馬鈺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%88%BA), [劉處玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E8%99%95%E7%8E%84), [王志謹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BF%97%E8%AC%B9), [李道純](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%81%93%E7%B4%94), plus a parallel *Jìn zhēn rén yǔ lù*. The *yǔlù* form, modelled on the Chán *yǔlù* tradition with which Quánzhēn was in intense conversation through the Jīn-Yuán period, becomes a principal genre of late-medieval Daoist literature. The closing *Míng hè yú yīn* [KR5d0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0123) (1347) anthology converts the lineage's prose teaching into *cí* lyric verse.

- **Daoist anthologies and the preservation of lost texts.** The *Yún jí qī qiān* [KR5d0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0055) and *Dào shū* [KR5d0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0039) — the two great pre-modern Daoist anthologies — between them preserve a great mass of Six-Dynasties, Táng, and Sòng material otherwise lost. The *Yún jí qī qiān* in particular, drawn from the now-lost Northern-Sòng *Dà Sòng tiān gōng bǎo zàng* (1019), is the single most consulted reference work for the early Daoist textual tradition.

- **The Six-Dynasties / Táng Shàngqīng inheritance.** Although the bulk of Shàngqīng material lives in [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/), *Tàixuán bù* preserves the foundational documentary anchor of the tradition — [陶弘景](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%BC%98%E6%99%AF)'s *Zhēn gào* [KR5d0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0036) — together with the Táng meditation-theory cluster of [司馬承禎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B8%E9%A6%AC%E6%89%BF%E7%A6%8E) ([KR5d0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0049) [KR5d0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0059)), the Wú Yún literary-philosophical corpus ([KR5d0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0074) [KR5d0075](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0075)), and the eleven-title opening cluster [KR5d0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0001)–[KR5d0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0011) of supplementary Shàngqīng / Língbǎo scriptures. Together these establish *Tàixuán* as the section's residual identity as the Shàngqīng supplement.

### Timeline

- **c. 400–250 BCE (late Warring States)** — *Shān hǎi jīng* 山海經 [KR5d0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0054) core composed; *Guǐ gǔ zǐ* 鬼谷子 [KR5d0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0048) core composed. The two pre-Hàn classics of the section.
- **c. 142 – 220 CE (Eastern Hàn, traditional attribution)** — *Zhōuyì cāntóng qì* 周易參同契 attributed to [魏伯陽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E4%BC%AF%E9%99%BD) takes shape; the textual core is contested and may be later (post-Hàn Wèi-Jìn), but the tradition's terminus ante quem is c. 4th c.
- **276–324 (Western Jìn)** — [郭璞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E7%92%9E) composes the surviving commentary on the *Shān hǎi jīng* [KR5d0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0054).
- **3rd–4th c.** — *Líng qí běn zhāng zhèng jīng* [KR5d0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0064) (with [顏幼明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E5%B9%BC%E6%98%8E) E. Jìn commentary) takes shape; the canonical Daoist casting-the-lots scripture.
- **364–370 (Eastern Jìn)** — Yáng Xī's Shàngqīng séance revelations to the Xǔ family at Máoshān — the documentary base of the *Zhēn gào*.

# 太平部 (KR5e)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR5e 太平部 *Tàipíng bù* — Daoist Canon — Great Peace](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR5e 太平部 (*Tàipíng bù*, "Great Peace") collects 68 works (DZ 1101 – DZ 1166 in the Schipper / Verellen *Concordance du Tao-tsang* numbering, with DZ 1101 split into the three subitems 1101a/b/c that yield [KR5e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0001) – [KR5e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0003)) — the second of the *sì fǔ* 四輔 ("Four Supplements") of the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (1445), which sit immediately after the *sāndòng* 三洞 ("Three Caverns" — [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) 洞真, [KR5b](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/) 洞玄, [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/) 洞神) and the first supplement [KR5d](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/) 太玄部. Wilkinson §29.4.4 records the canon's tripartite-with-supplements structure but flags the by-now familiar dislocation: the three Caverns are *schools*, the twelve sections 十二類 (本文, 神符, 玉訣, 靈圖, 譜錄, 戒律, 威儀, 方法, 衆術, 記傳, 讚頌, 表奏) are a cross-cutting *genre* axis, and the four supplements were classically meant to attach to one Cavern apiece — *Tàixuán* to 洞真 / Shàngqīng, *Tàipíng* to 洞玄 / Língbǎo, *Tàiqīng* to 洞神 / Sānhuáng-cum-Lǎozǐ, and *Zhèngyī* across all three (Schipper & Verellen, *Taoist Canon* 1: 14–22, 30–40). In the *Tàipíng bù* the school-supplement scheme is visible only in the surviving openings: the section is named after, and opens with, the *Tàipíng jīng* 太平經 [KR5e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0002) — the foundational scripture of the late-Hàn *Tài píng dào* 太平道 / Yellow Turban movement, traditionally taken as the "Língbǎo *ante litteram*" by the canon-editors — and what follows is *de facto* an archive of whatever the Sòng and Míng compilers could not house in [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) / [KR5b](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/) / [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/) / [KR5d](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/) but judged canonical.

The actual contents fall into six unequal strata: (i) the **Tàipíng jīng nucleus** that gives the section its name (4 titles, [KR5e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0001) – [KR5e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0004): the Táng epitome *Tàipíng jīng chāo*, the fragmentary main scripture, the preface *Fù wén xù*, and the Táng digest *Shèng jūn mì zhǐ*); (ii) the **Jìngmíng 淨明 revelation corpus** (8 titles, [KR5e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0005) – [KR5e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0012)) — the scriptural and ritual archive of the Sòng-Yuán *Jìngmíng zhōngxiào dào* 淨明忠孝道 movement centred on the cult of [許遜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E9%81%9C) Xǔ Xùn at Xīshān 西山 (Jiāngxī), culminating in [黃元吉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%85%83%E5%90%89)'s 1327 *Jìngmíng zhōngxiào quánshū* [KR5e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0012); (iii) a substantial **Six-Dynasties – Táng doctrinal and systematic-theology block** ([KR5e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0013) – [KR5e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0041)) that holds the major Táng *Chóngxuán* 重玄 ("Twofold Mystery") scripture *Běn jì jīng* 本際經 [KR5e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0013), the foundational Daoist apologetic / systematic manuals *Dàomén jīng fǎ xiāng chéng cì xù* [KR5e0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0030) by [潘師正](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BD%98%E5%B8%AB%E6%AD%A3) (Pān Shīzhèng), *Dàojiào yì shū* [KR5e0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0031) by [孟安排](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E5%AE%89%E6%8E%92) (Mèng Ānpái), and *Dòngxuán Língbǎo xuán mén dà yì* [KR5e0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0026), and the great early-medieval **Daoist encyclopedias** *Wúshàng bìyào* 無上祕要 [KR5e0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0040) (compiled under Běi-Zhōu imperial sponsorship c. 577–589) and *Sāndòng zhū náng* 三洞珠囊 [KR5e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0041) by [王懸河](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%B8%E6%B2%B3) (Wáng Xuánhé) — by far the densest concentration of pre-Quánzhēn systematic Daoist literature anywhere in the canon; (iv) [羅隱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%85%E9%9A%B1)'s late-Táng political-Daoist treatise *Tàipíng liǎng tóng shū* [KR5e0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0037), inserted into the section on the strength of its title alone; (v) the **Quánzhēn 全真 literary archive** (22 titles, [KR5e0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0042) – [KR5e0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0063)) — the largest single deposit of the Wáng Chóngyáng-Seven Patriarchs *yǔlù* 語錄 and *shī cí* 詩詞 corpus in the *Dàozàng*, holding the *Chóngyáng quánzhēn jí* [KR5e0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0055) and three further Wáng Chóngyáng anthologies, [馬鈺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%88%BA) (Mǎ Yù / Dānyángzǐ)'s *Jiànwù jí* [KR5e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0044) / *Dòngxuán jīnyù jí* [KR5e0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0051) / *Dānyáng shén guāng càn* [KR5e0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0052), and the collected works of [丘處機](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%98%E8%99%95%E6%A9%9F), [譚處端](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%9A%E8%99%95%E7%AB%AF), [王處一](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%99%95%E4%B8%80), [郝大通](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%9D%E5%A4%A7%E9%80%9A), [劉處玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E8%99%95%E7%8E%84), and [尹志平](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%B9%E5%BF%97%E5%B9%B3); (vi) a small but consequential **Daoist medical block** ([KR5e0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0064) – [KR5e0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0067)) anchored by [孫思邈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%80%9D%E9%82%88) (Sūn Sīmiǎo)'s *Bèijí qiānjīn yàofāng* 備急千金要方 [KR5e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0065); and (vii) the closing early-Míng Thunder-Rites ritual compendium *Fǎ hǎi yí zhū* 法海遺珠 [KR5e0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0068).

The chronological span runs from the Eastern-Hàn core of the *Tàipíng jīng* itself (c. 100–250, [KR5e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0002)) through to the early-Míng *Jíjiù xiān fāng* 急救仙方 [KR5e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0066) and *Fǎ hǎi yí zhū* [KR5e0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0068) (both c. 1444–1445, finished just before the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* itself was printed). Distribution by composition midpoint is sharply bimodal: a Hàn–Six-Dynasties nucleus dominated by the *Tàipíng jīng* and a cluster of Liùcháo Língbǎo scriptures ([KR5e0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0016) [KR5e0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0017) [KR5e0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0020) [KR5e0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0021) [KR5e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0022)) plus the *Wúshàng bìyào* (577–589); a dense Táng peak (c. 30 titles, c. 600–900) carrying the *Chóngxuán*-philosophical scriptures, the Táng systematic-theology manuals, the great encyclopedias, and the *Qiānjīn yàofāng*; a Sòng-Yuán surge (c. 30 titles, c. 1100–1330) dominated by two distinct currents — the **Jìngmíng** scriptures and the **Quánzhēn** *yǔlù*/poetry corpus that documents the founding generation and immediate successors of [王嚞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%9A%9E) Wáng Chóngyáng (Wáng Zhé, 1113–1170); and a sparse early-Míng tail terminating with the *Fǎ hǎi yí zhū*. The section is therefore best read not as a coherent textual school but as the *Dàozàng*'s **Yellow-Turban / Jìngmíng / Quánzhēn overflow basin** — bracketed at one end by the foundational late-Hàn revelatory text that gives the supplement its name, at the other by the early-Míng Thunder-Rites archive.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The *Tàipíng jīng* nucleus — the section's etymological anchor.**
- *Tài píng jīng* 太平經 [KR5e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0002) — anonymous, Eastern-Hàn core (2nd c.) with extensive Six-Dynasties expansion. **One of the foundational scriptures of Chinese Daoism**, the cornerstone text of the earliest organized Daoist movement, traditionally associated with the Yellow Turban / Five-Pecks-of-Rice context and extensively quoted in the *Hòu Hàn shū* as the doctrinal source of the *Tài píng dào* 太平道 of Zhāng Jué 張角 (184 CE rebellion). The received text is defective: 57 *juàn* survive of an original 170. Doctrinal core: *tàipíng* 太平 (a utopian millennial socio-cosmic order), *chéng fù* 承負 (inherited moral-cosmic burden across generations), *sān qì* 三氣 (the three cosmic pneumas), and a prototype of Daoist ritual confession.
- *Tài píng jīng chāo* 太平經鈔 [KR5e0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0001) — a Táng 10-*juàn* abridgement organized by the sexagenary 甲乙丙丁戊己庚辛壬癸 cycle, preserving in condensed form much of the scripture's content now lost in the main copy. Together with [KR5e0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0003) *Fù wén xù* (the preface) and [KR5e0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0004) *Shèng jūn mì zhǐ* (a Táng doctrinal digest), the three DZ 1101 a/b/c items and DZ 1102 constitute the **entire surviving transmission of the Tàipíng-corpus** in the *Dàozàng*.

**The Jìngmíng 淨明 revelation cluster.** Eight scriptures and one anthology ([KR5e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0005) – [KR5e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0012)) documenting the **Jìngmíng zhōngxiào dào** 淨明忠孝道 ("Way of Pure Illumination, Loyalty, and Filiality"), a Daoist movement centred on the cult of [許遜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E9%81%9C) Xǔ Xùn (the deified third-century Jìn official) at Xīshān 西山 (Jiāngxī), reaching mature form in the 12th–14th centuries. The cluster's distinctive theology is a **Confucian-Daoist synthesis** in which *zhōngxiào* 忠孝 (loyalty and filiality) is the path to *jìngmíng* 淨明 (pure illumination).
- *Tài shàng Língbǎo Jìngmíng dòngshén shàng pǐn jīng* [KR5e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0005) — the opening scripture of the cluster, defining its cosmological-doctrinal frame.
- The *Yùzhēn shū / Dào yuán zhèng yìn / Tiān zūn shuō yù wēn / Shǒu rù sì guī / Jiǔ xiān shuǐ / Zhōng huáng bā zhù* scriptures [KR5e0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0006) – [KR5e0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0011) — the supporting Sòng-Yuán Jìngmíng scriptural archive.
- *Jìngmíng zhōngxiào quánshū* 淨明忠孝全書 [KR5e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0012) — compiled by [黃元吉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%85%83%E5%90%89) Huáng Yuánjí (1270–1324) with an introduction dated 1327. **The foundational compilation of the Yuán-period Jìngmíng school**, the authoritative anthology of scripture, ritual, doctrine, and hagiography around the Xǔ Xùn cult.

**The *Běn jì jīng* and the Táng *Chóngxuán* 重玄 ("Twofold Mystery") current.**
- *Tài xuán zhēn yī běn jì miào jīng* 太玄真一本際妙經 [KR5e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0013) — anonymous, early Táng (c. 600–630), 10 *juàn*. **The single most influential Táng Daoist philosophical-soteriological scripture**, articulating the *Chóngxuán* metaphysics through dialogues between Tàishàng Lǎojūn 太上老君 and a celestial retinue. Extensively quoted in Táng canonical compilations; substantially recovered from Dūnhuáng 敦煌 manuscripts (parts of the original were lost from the *Dàozàng* copy).

**The Táng systematic-theology / apologetic manuals.** The densest concentration of Daoist *yìxué* 義學 outside [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) in the canon.
- *Lù xiānshēng dào mén kē lüè* 陸先生道門科略 [KR5e0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0029) — [陸修靜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E4%BF%AE%E9%9D%9C) Lù Xiūjìng (406–477). The earliest text in this cluster, by the great Liùcháo Daoist liturgist who first systematized the *Dàozàng* into the *sāndòng* scheme.
- *Dào mén jīng fǎ xiāng chéng cì xù* 道門經法相承次序 [KR5e0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0030) — [潘師正](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BD%98%E5%B8%AB%E6%AD%A3) Pān Shīzhèng (Táng, 680–684). Written for emperor Gāozōng 高宗.
- *Dào jiào yì shū* 道教義樞 [KR5e0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0031) — [孟安排](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E5%AE%89%E6%8E%92) Mèng Ānpái (Táng, c. 680–710). Systematic 10-*juàn* manual of Daoist doctrine; partly digests the earlier *Dòngxuán Língbǎo xuán mén dà yì* [KR5e0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0026).
- *Dòngxuán Língbǎo sāndòng fèngdào kē jiè yíng shǐ* 洞玄靈寶三洞奉道科戒營始 [KR5e0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0027) — attributed to [金明七真](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%91%E6%98%8E%E4%B8%83%E7%9C%9F) Jīnmíng-Qīzhēn (early Táng). **The foundational regulatory-liturgical compendium of Táng Daoist monasticism** (translated by Kohn, *The Daoist Monastic Manual*, OUP 2004).
- *Dào diǎn lùn* [KR5e0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0032), *Tài shàng miào fǎ běn xiāng jīng* [KR5e0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0033), *Shàng qīng dào lèi shì xiāng* [KR5e0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0034) by [王懸河](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%B8%E6%B2%B3) Wáng Xuánhé, *Dòngxuán Língbǎo zuǒ xuán lùn* [KR5e0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0038) — further Táng doctrinal treatises.
- *Yī qiè dào jīng yīn yì miào mén yóu qǐ* 一切道經音義妙門由起 [KR5e0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0025) — [史崇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B2%E5%B4%87) Shǐ Chóng et al., 712–713. Compiled at the order of Táng Ruìzōng 睿宗; the philological-bibliographic preface of an unrealized Táng *Dàozàng* compilation.

**The great early-medieval Daoist encyclopedias.** The two densest reference works in the section.
- *Wúshàng bìyào* 無上祕要 [KR5e0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0040) — anonymous, Běi-Zhōu, c. 577–589. **The earliest substantial Daoist encyclopedia**, compiled under imperial sponsorship in 100 *juàn* (about a third has survived); the principal source for reconstructing the state of pre-Táng Daoist scripture.
- *Sāndòng zhū náng* 三洞珠囊 [KR5e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0041) — [王懸河](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%B8%E6%B2%B3) Wáng Xuánhé, Táng (c. 680–710), 10 *juàn*. **The principal Táng-era topical anthology of Daoist scripture**, organized by doctrinal headings and quoting extensively from sources now lost.

**[羅隱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%85%E9%9A%B1)'s political-Daoist treatise.** *Tài píng liǎng tóng shū* 太平兩同書 [KR5e0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0037) — Luó Yǐn (833–909), late Táng. A two-*juàn* political treatise on the unification of Confucian and Daoist statecraft, included in the section on the strength of its *tàipíng* title and its placement in the *zhūzǐ* 諸子 (masters) tradition Luó Yǐn worked within.

**The Quánzhēn 全真 literary archive — the largest single Wáng Chóngyáng-and-disciples deposit in the *Dàozàng*.** Twenty-two collections spanning four generations of Northern-Lineage Quánzhēn 全真 Daoism.
- *Founding patriarch — [王嚞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%9A%9E) Wáng Zhé (Wáng Chóngyáng, 1113–1170)*: *Chóng yáng quánzhēn jí* 重陽全真集 [KR5e0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0055) (his principal *shī cí* anthology), *Chóng yáng jiào huà jí* 重陽教化集 [KR5e0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0056), *Chóng yáng fēn lí shí huà jí* 重陽分梨十化集 [KR5e0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0057) (recording the ten allegorical "pear-dividing" exchanges with Mǎ Yù), and *Chóng yáng zhēn rén jīn guān yù suǒ jué* 重陽真人金關玉鎖訣 [KR5e0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0058) (a practical *neidān* instruction set). [KR5e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0060) *Chóng yáng zhēn rén shòu Dān yáng èr shí sì jué* preserves twenty-four instructions Wáng Chóngyáng transmitted to Mǎ Dānyáng.
- *The Seven Patriarchs (七真) — first generation of disciples*: [馬鈺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%88%BA) Mǎ Yù (Mǎ Dānyáng, 1123–1184) — *Jiànwù jí* 漸悟集 [KR5e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0044), *Dòngxuán jīn yù jí* 洞玄金玉集 [KR5e0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0051), *Dānyáng shén guāng càn* 丹陽神光燦 [KR5e0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0052) (1175). [譚處端](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%9A%E8%99%95%E7%AB%AF) Tán Chùduān (1123–1185) — *Shuǐ yún jí* 水雲集 [KR5e0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0062). [劉處玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E8%99%95%E7%8E%84) Liú Chùxuán (1147–1203) — *Xiān lè jí* 仙樂集 [KR5e0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0043). [丘處機](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%98%E8%99%95%E6%A9%9F) Qiū Chùjī (1148–1227) — *Pán xī jí* 磻溪集 [KR5e0061](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0061) (his major collection from the years before the audience with Činggis Qaγan). [王處一](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%99%95%E4%B8%80) Wáng Chùyī (1142–1217) — *Yún guāng jí* 雲光集 [KR5e0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0054). [郝大通](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%9D%E5%A4%A7%E9%80%9A) Hǎo Dàtōng (1140–1212) — *Tài gǔ jí* 太古集 [KR5e0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0063).
- *Second and third generations*: [尹志平](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%B9%E5%BF%97%E5%B9%B3) Yǐn Zhìpíng (1169–1251) — *Bǎo guāng jí* 葆光集 [KR5e0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0048). [姬志真](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%AC%E5%BF%97%E7%9C%9F) Jī Zhìzhēn (Yuán) — *Yún shān jí* 雲山集 [KR5e0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0042) (1265). [郭志誠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%AD%E5%BF%97%E8%AA%A0) Guō Zhìchéng (Yuán) — *Xī yún jí* 西雲集 [KR5e0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0049). Plus the further Quánzhēn-affiliated collections *Cǎo táng jí* by [王丹桂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E4%B8%B9%E6%A1%82) [KR5e0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0045), *Xuán xū zǐ míng zhēn jí* by [玄沖師](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E6%B2%96%E5%B8%AB) [KR5e0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0047), *Zì rán jí* [KR5e0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0046), *Wù zhēn jí* [KR5e0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0053), and the Southern-Sòng *Wù zhāi xiān sheng wén jí* of [楊至質](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%A5%8A%E8%87%B3%E8%B3%AA) [KR5e0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0050).
- *Pre-Quánzhēn alchemical instruction*: *Mǎ Zì rán jīn dān kǒu jué* 馬自然金丹口訣 [KR5e0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0059) — [馬自然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E8%87%AA%E7%84%B6) (Northern Sòng).

**The Daoist-affiliated medical block.**
- *Sūn zhēnrén bèijí qiānjīn yàofāng* 孫真人備急千金要方 [KR5e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0065) — [孫思邈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%80%9D%E9%82%88) Sūn Sīmiǎo (early-Táng), composed c. 650, revised by Sòng editors in the 11th century (the *Dàozàng* copy follows the Sòng recension in 93 *juàn*). **The foundational clinical encyclopedia of the Táng**: diagnostics, obstetrics-paediatrics, internal medicine, acupuncture, materia medica, and emergency treatment, anchored by Sūn's dictum that human life is worth more than a thousand pieces of gold. The matching index [KR5e0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0064) is a Sòng-era *mùlù* to the same work.
- *Xiān chuán wài kē mì fāng* 仙傳外科祕方 [KR5e0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0067) — [趙宜真](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E5%AE%9C%E7%9C%9F) Zhào Yízhēn (Yuán–early Míng, d. 1382). A Daoist-affiliated surgical and external-medicine manual.
- *Jí jiù xiān fāng* 急救仙方 [KR5e0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0066) — anonymous early Míng (c. 1444–1445), an emergency-prescription manual.

**The closing Thunder-Rites compendium.** *Fǎ hǎi yí zhū* 法海遺珠 [KR5e0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0068) — anonymous, early Míng (by 1445), 46 *juàn*. **The concluding text of the *Tàipíng bù***: a major ritual compendium collecting Daoist practices of the *léi fǎ* 雷法 (Thunder Rites) tradition and allied currents (the Tiānxīn 天心, Shénxiāo 神霄, and Qīngwéi 清微 ritual lineages).

### Important persons

- [陸修靜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E4%BF%AE%E9%9D%9C) (Lù Xiūjìng, 406–477) — the Liùcháo Daoist liturgist whose codification of the *sāndòng* scheme is the structural ancestor of the entire *Dàozàng*; here for *Lù xiānshēng dào mén kē lüè* [KR5e0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0029).
- [孫思邈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%80%9D%E9%82%88) (Sūn Sīmiǎo, early Táng) — the *yào wáng* 藥王 ("King of Medicine"), author of *Bèijí qiānjīn yàofāng* [KR5e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0065); canonized into the *Dàozàng* as a Daoist *zhēnrén* on the strength of his self-cultivation profile.
- [潘師正](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BD%98%E5%B8%AB%E6%AD%A3) (Pān Shīzhèng, 583–682) — Shàngqīng patriarch and tutor to Táng Gāozōng 高宗; author of *Dàomén jīng fǎ xiāng chéng cì xù* [KR5e0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0030).
- [孟安排](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E5%AE%89%E6%8E%92) (Mèng Ānpái, fl. c. 700) — compiler of the foundational Daoist systematic-theology manual *Dào jiào yì shū* [KR5e0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0031).
- [王懸河](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%B8%E6%B2%B3) (Wáng Xuánhé, late 7th – early 8th c.) — Táng Daoist priest at Chéngdū 成都; compiler of two of the section's principal reference works, the topical encyclopedia *Sāndòng zhū náng* [KR5e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0041) and the doctrinal repertory *Shàng qīng dào lèi shì xiāng* [KR5e0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0034).
- [史崇](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B2%E5%B4%87) (Shǐ Chóng, fl. 712–713) — editor of *Yī qiè dào jīng yīn yì miào mén yóu qǐ* [KR5e0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0025), commissioned by Táng Ruìzōng.
- [羅隱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%85%E9%9A%B1) (Luó Yǐn, 833–909) — late-Táng Hángzhōu literatus, author of *Tài píng liǎng tóng shū* [KR5e0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0037) — the single literati-political text in the section.
- [許遜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E9%81%9C) (Xǔ Xùn) — the deified Jìn-period (3rd–4th c.) administrator at the cultic centre of the Sòng-Yuán Jìngmíng movement; not the author of anything in this section, but the iconographic and ritual anchor of the entire Jìngmíng cluster [KR5e0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0005) – [KR5e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0012).
- [黃元吉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E5%85%83%E5%90%89) (Huáng Yuánjí, 1270–1324) — Yuán Jìngmíng patriarch and compiler of the school's foundational anthology *Jìngmíng zhōngxiào quánshū* [KR5e0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0012).
- [王嚞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%9A%9E) (Wáng Zhé, Wáng Chóngyáng, 1113–1170) — founder of Quánzhēn 全真 Daoism, the dominant Daoist movement of the post-Sòng period; four of his anthologies are preserved here ([KR5e0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0055) – [KR5e0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0058)) plus a fifth disciple-transmission record [KR5e0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0060).
- [馬鈺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%88%BA) (Mǎ Yù / Mǎ Dānyáng, 1123–1184) — senior of the Quánzhēn Seven Patriarchs, husband of Sūn Bù'èr 孫不二; three substantial collections [KR5e0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0044) [KR5e0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0051) [KR5e0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0052) — the largest single-author Quánzhēn deposit in the section.
