- [王處一](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%99%95%E4%B8%80) (Wáng Chùyī, 1142–1217), [譚處端](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AD%9A%E8%99%95%E7%AB%AF) (Tán Chùduān, 1123–1185), [郝大通](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%83%9D%E5%A4%A7%E9%80%9A) (Hǎo Dàtōng, 1140–1212), [劉處玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8A%89%E8%99%95%E7%8E%84) (Liú Chùxuán, 1147–1203) — further Seven-Patriarch Quánzhēn masters, each represented by one or two collections.
- [尹志平](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%B9%E5%BF%97%E5%B9%B3) (Yǐn Zhìpíng, 1169–1251) — Quánzhēn third-generation patriarch and Qiū Chùjī's principal successor; author of *Bǎo guāng jí* [KR5e0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0048).
- [趙宜真](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%B6%99%E5%AE%9C%E7%9C%9F) (Zhào Yízhēn, d. 1382) — Yuán–Míng Jìngmíng-affiliated Daoist physician; author of *Xiān chuán wài kē mì fāng* [KR5e0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0067).
- [侯善淵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BE%AF%E5%96%84%E6%B7%B5) (Hóu Shànyuān, Jīn) — Northern-school Daoist commentator and exegete; author of *Shàng qīng tài xuán jiàn jiè lùn* [KR5e0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0039).

### Topics

- **The *Tàipíng* utopia and its afterlife.** *Tàipíng* 太平 (Great Peace) as the foundational Daoist conception of a millennial socio-cosmic order under a sage-ruler, registered in the *Tàipíng jīng* cluster and replayed in muted form in [羅隱](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%85%E9%9A%B1)'s *Tàipíng liǎng tóng shū* [KR5e0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0037) (a Confucian-Daoist political treatise) and in the *Shàng fāng Língbǎo wú jí zhì dào kāi huà zhēn jīng* [KR5e0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0035) / *Shàng fāng jūn tiān yǎn fàn zhēn jīng* [KR5e0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0036) pair. The *Tàipíng* concept is the section's nominal organizing principle, even where the actual contents have drifted far away from it.
- **The *Tàipíng jīng* and the origins of organized Daoism.** The text's role as the doctrinal source of the late-Hàn *Tài píng dào* 太平道 of Zhāng Jué 張角 and its 184 CE Yellow Turban rebellion remains the principal question driving modern study of the scripture (Hendrischke 2006). The Hàn core / Six-Dynasties expansion / Táng epitome layering is the textual problem.
- **Chóngxuán 重玄 ("Twofold Mystery") Daoist philosophy.** A Táng metaphysical-soteriological current that re-reads the *Lǎozǐ* through *Mádhyamaka*-influenced double-negation logic; the *Běn jì jīng* [KR5e0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0013) is the *Tàipíng bù*'s principal scripture in this current, complemented by the systematic-theology manuals of [孟安排](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E5%AE%89%E6%8E%92) and [潘師正](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BD%98%E5%B8%AB%E6%AD%A3) (Assandri 2009).
- **Daoist systematic theology and the codification of *yìxué* 義學.** The *Dào jiào yì shū* [KR5e0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0031), *Dòngxuán Língbǎo xuán mén dà yì* [KR5e0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0026), and *Dào diǎn lùn* [KR5e0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0032) together constitute the Táng project of building a Daoist counterpart to Buddhist *abhidharma*-style systematic doctrine, in conscious response to the structural sophistication of Táng Buddhist scholasticism.
- **Daoist monasticism in the Táng.** The *Fèng dào kē jiè yíng shǐ* [KR5e0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0027) and *Dào xué kē yí* [KR5e0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0028) are the principal sources for reconstructing the institutional shape of Táng Daoist monasteries — refectory rules, ordination steps, the ritual day, the textual curriculum (Kohn 2003, 2004).
- **The early Daoist encyclopedic tradition.** *Wúshàng bìyào* (Běi Zhōu) [KR5e0040](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0040) and *Sāndòng zhū náng* (Táng) [KR5e0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0041) together hold the bulk of the *Dàozàng*'s pre-Song reference-encyclopedic literature; both quote extensively from scriptures since lost, and are therefore indispensable for any reconstruction of pre-Táng Daoism.
- **The Jìngmíng 淨明 Confucian-Daoist synthesis.** The Sòng-Yuán Jìngmíng movement's distinctive blending of Confucian *zhōngxiào* 忠孝 (loyalty, filiality) with Daoist *jìngmíng* 淨明 (pure illumination), in the cultic frame of the [許遜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A8%B1%E9%81%9C) Xīshān tradition (Akizuki 1978; Boltz 1987).
- **The Quánzhēn 全真 literary self-documentation.** The single largest topic in the section by volume. The Wáng Chóngyáng / Seven Patriarchs *shī cí* anthologies and *yǔlù* records are the principal primary sources for the rise of Quánzhēn Daoism in Jīn-period northern China and its consolidation under Mongol patronage; they document the *neidān* 內丹 (internal alchemy) practice tradition, the eremitic-yet-evangelical social style, and the lyric-poetry idiom Quánzhēn adopted for popular preaching (Marsone 2010; Goossaert 2001).
- **Daoism and medicine.** The *Bèijí qiānjīn yàofāng* [KR5e0065](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0065) and the *Xiān chuán wài kē mì fāng* [KR5e0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0067) register the long-running convergence of Daoist self-cultivation, alchemy, and clinical medicine — a convergence already visible in [孫思邈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%80%9D%E9%82%88)'s reputation as both *yào wáng* and Daoist *zhēnrén* (Sivin 1968, 1995; Unschuld 1986).
- ***Léi fǎ* 雷法 Thunder Rites.** The closing *Fǎ hǎi yí zhū* [KR5e0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0068) documents the synthesis of the major Sòng-Yuán new-ritual lineages (Tiānxīn 天心, Shénxiāo 神霄, Qīngwéi 清微) into the early-Míng exorcistic-thunder repertoire that defined late-imperial Daoist ritual practice (Skar 2000; Boltz 1987).

### Timeline

- c. 100–250 — *Tài píng jīng* 太平經 [KR5e0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0002) — the Eastern-Hàn revelatory core (with substantial Six-Dynasties expansion); the foundational scripture of the *Tài píng dào* and the textual anchor of the entire section.
- 317–589 — *Dòng xuán Líng bǎo běn xíng sù yuán jīng* [KR5e0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0016), *Běn xíng yīn yuán jīng* [KR5e0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0017), *Fēi xíng sān jiè tōng wēi nèi sī miào jīng* [KR5e0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0020), *Xuán yī zhēn rén shuō shēng sǐ lún zhuǎn yīn yuán jīng* [KR5e0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0021), *Zhōng hé jīng* [KR5e0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0022), *Shēng xuán nèi jiào jīng zhōng hé pǐn shù yì shū* [KR5e0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0024) — a cluster of Liùcháo Língbǎo scriptures.
- 406–477 — *Lù xiān shēng dào mén kē lüè* 陸先生道門科略 [KR5e0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/KR5e0029) — [陸修靜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E4%BF%AE%E9%9D%9C) Lù Xiūjìng; the earliest dated text in the section after the *Tàipíng jīng*.

# 太清部 (KR5f)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR5f 太清部 *Tài qīng bù* — Daoist Canon — Great Clarity Section (Third Supplement)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR5f corresponds to the **Tài qīng bù** 太清部, the third of the **Four Supplements** (*sì fǔ* 四輔) that complete the **Three Caverns** (*sān dòng* 三洞) bibliographic frame of the *Zhèng tǒng Dào zàng* 正統道藏 (1445). Within the canon's textile of *Dòng zhēn* 洞真, *Dòng xuán* 洞玄, *Dòng shén* 洞神 — *Tài xuán* 太玄, *Tài píng* 太平, *Tài qīng* 太清, *Zhèng yī* 正一, the Tài qīng bù was originally intended as the supplement to the *Dòng shén* cavern, providing the **alchemical-scriptural corpus** of the Highest Clarity (*Tài qīng*) revelations of the third/fourth century — the foundational tradition of operative alchemy (*wài dān* 外丹) systematized in Gě Hóng's *Bào pǔ zǐ*. By the Míng compilation, however, the section had drifted into a **catch-all collection** for philosophical, military, technical, and ethical works that did not fit elsewhere in the canon's classificatory scheme — most notably a remarkable cluster of pre-Qín and Hàn masters whose principal manuscript witnesses were preserved here precisely because mainstream Confucian transmission lapsed. The 25 texts of KR5f (DZ 1167–1191) span roughly fifteen centuries, from late-Warring-States philosophical writings to late-Yuán neo-Confucian cosmology.

The classification reflects the long Daoist self-understanding as the canonical home of *all* indigenous Chinese learning marginalized by the Confucian curriculum: the canonical Mòhist text, the principal text of the School of Names, the major Legalist compendium, the chief Hàn syncretic encyclopaedia, the standard Hàn imitation of the *Yì*, the central Eastern-Jìn alchemical treatise, and the foundational *nèi dān* manual of the Zhōng Lǚ lineage are all here, jostling with brief Táng-Sòng meditation scriptures and Sòng pseudepigraphical military classics. The section thus functions less as a doctrinally coherent grouping than as a **bibliographic reservoir** — and for several of the works housed here (the *Mò zǐ* especially) the Daozang witness is the most important single textual source for the modern critical tradition.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The popular-morality founder.**

- *Tài shàng gǎn yìng piān* 太上感應篇 [KR5f0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0001) — the single most influential Chinese morality tract, opening the section as DZ 1167 and seeding the entire late-imperial **morality-ledger** (*gōng guò gé* 功過格) tradition.

**Pre-Qín and Hàn philosophical masters preserved here (a remarkable cluster).**

- *Mò zǐ* 墨子 [KR5f0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0010) — the foundational text of Mòhism, whose Daozang witness is the most important manuscript witness of the work for the modern critical tradition.
- *Hán fēi zǐ* 韓非子 [KR5f0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0011) — the great Warring-States Legalist synthesis.
- *Gōng sūn Lóng zǐ* 公孫龍子 [KR5f0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0006) — the foundational text of the *Míng jiā* 名家 (School of Names), source of the "white horse is not horse" paradox.
- *Yǐn wén zǐ* 尹文子 [KR5f0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0007) — companion text of the *Míng jiā* / Huáng Lǎo current.
- *Hé guān zǐ* 鶡冠子 [KR5f0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0009) — Warring-States / early-Hàn Huáng Lǎo political-strategic text, transmitted here with **Lù Diàn 陸佃's Northern-Sòng commentary**; the Mǎ wáng duī finds vindicated its authenticity against long-standing forgery charges.
- *Yù zǐ* 鬻子 [KR5f0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0005) — short pseudepigraphical text ascribed to the Zhōu counselor Yù Xióng; received recension Hàn–Six Dynasties.
- *Huái nán hóng liè jiě* 淮南鴻烈解 [KR5f0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0018) — the *Huái nán zǐ*, Liú Ān's great Hàn syncretic-encyclopaedic compendium, with the composite "Xǔ Shèn" commentary.
- *Jí zhù Tài xuán jīng* 集註太玄經 [KR5f0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0017) — Yáng Xióng's 81-tetragram Hàn imitation of the *Yì jīng*, with accumulated Hàn–Sòng commentaries.

**The Gě Hóng / Bào pǔ zǐ corpus** — the alchemical heart of the section.

- *Bào pǔ zǐ nèi piān* 抱朴子內篇 [KR5f0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0019) — Gě Hóng's foundational defence of operative alchemy, *shén xiān* 神仙, and esoteric practice; one of the most important works in the entire Daoist canon.
- *Bào pǔ zǐ wài piān* 抱朴子外篇 [KR5f0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0021) — the same author's 50-*juàn* Confucian-social complement.
- *Bào pǔ zǐ bié zhǐ* 抱朴子別旨 [KR5f0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0020) — a Táng supplementary text attached to the corpus.

**Inner alchemy** (*nèi dān*) **and esoterica.**

- *Mì chuán Zhèng yáng zhēn rén Líng bǎo bì fǎ* 祕傳正陽真人靈寶畢法 [KR5f0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0025) — the foundational Northern-Sòng *nèi dān* text of the Zhōng Lǚ 鍾呂 transmission (Zhōnglí Quán → Lǚ Dòng bīn), and the concluding text of the entire Tài qīng bù (DZ 1191) — and thus of the Four Supplements.

- *Tuó yuè zǐ* 橐籥子 [KR5f0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0022) — Sòng philosophical-cosmological treatise on the *Dào dé jīng*'s "bellows" image.

**Daoist devotional scriptures** (a small but doctrinally significant group).

### Topics

- **The Daoist canon as bibliographic refuge.** The Tài qīng bù is the principal site of the well-known phenomenon by which texts marginalized in the Confucian curriculum — Mòhism, the School of Names, Legalism, the Huáng Lǎo current — were preserved through Daoist transmission. The modern critical text of the *Mò zǐ* depends decisively on the Daozang witness, and several of the smaller masters (*Hé guān zǐ*, *Yǐn wén zǐ*, *Gōng sūn Lóng zǐ*) would be far more attenuated without it.
- **The Tài qīng alchemical lineage.** The section's nominal subject — the *Tài qīng* scriptural revelation of operative alchemy (third/fourth century) — is represented above all by the *Bào pǔ zǐ* trilogy. The deeper history is the trajectory from **operative alchemy** (*wài dān* 外丹, elixir-compounding) of the Six Dynasties to the **inner alchemy** (*nèi dān* 內丹) systematization of the Sòng, traced here from Gě Hóng [KR5f0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0019) through to the Zhōng Lǚ *Líng bǎo bì fǎ* [KR5f0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0025).
- **The morality-book revolution.** The opening text — *Tài shàng gǎn yìng piān* [KR5f0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/KR5f0001) — inaugurated a new genre of Daoist-flavoured popular ethics that would dominate late-imperial religious-moral practice through the morality-ledger (*gōng guò gé* 功過格) tradition and shape Míng-Qīng popular religion across denominational lines.
- **Pseudepigraphy in the section.** A striking proportion of the texts are pseudepigraphical attributions to figures of high antiquity — *Yù zǐ* to Yù Xióng of the Zhōu, *Zǐ huá zǐ* to Chéng Běn of the Spring-and-Autumn, *Huáng shí gōng sù shū* to the Hàn immortal Huáng shí gōng, *Líng bǎo bì fǎ* to Zhōnglí Quán of the Hàn — typically masking Sòng compilation. The dating policy in this division consistently follows the **received recension** rather than the legendary ascription.
- **Hàn syncretism and its Sòng inheritors.** *Huái nán zǐ*, *Tài xuán jīng*, and the Mòhist / Míngjiā / Huáng Lǎo texts represent the Hàn syncretic moment; the Sòng texts of the section (*Hé guān zǐ* commentary, *Sù shū*, *Sūn zǐ* commentaries, *Tiān yuán fā wēi*) represent successive re-readings of that inheritance from the standpoint of Sòng neo-Confucian and Daoist cosmology.

# 正一部 (KR5g)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR5g 正一部 *Zhèng yī bù* — Daoist Canon — Orthodox Unity (Fourth Supplement)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR5g 正一部 (*Zhèng yī bù*, "Orthodox Unity Section") is the **fourth and largest of the four supplements** (*sì fǔ* 四輔) of the *Zhèng tǒng Dào zàng* 正統道藏 (1445), spanning **DZ 1192 – DZ 1431b** in the Schipper / Verellen *Concordance du Tao-tsang* numbering — **244 titles** in the Kanripo enumeration [KR5g0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0001) – [KR5g0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0244). Within the four-supplements architecture explained by Wilkinson §29.4.4 — *Tàixuán* 太玄 (to [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) *Dòng zhēn*), *Tàipíng* 太平 (to [KR5b](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/) *Dòng xuán*), *Tàiqīng* 太清 (to [KR5c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/) *Dòng shén*), *Zhèng yī* 正一 to all three — Zhèng yī was originally conceived as the **canonical archive of the Celestial-Masters tradition** (*Tiān shī dào* 天師道) descending from 張陵 Zhāng Líng (Zhāng Dàolíng, 34–156 [or 178] CE; Wilkinson §29.4.2), and ought in principle to have housed the ordination registers, ritual codes, and doctrinal scriptures of the lineage that had become the dominant priestly institution of imperial Daoism by the Sòng. In practice, the section is more than twice the size of the other three supplements combined ([KR5d](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/), [KR5e](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/), [KR5f](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/)) and has absorbed every variety of canonical material that the editors of 1445 could not place in *sāndòng* 三洞 or in the first three *fǔ* — most consequentially the **Sòng "new ritual" lineages** (Shén xiāo 神霄, Qīng wēi 清微, Tóng chū 童初, Tiān xīn 天心 — the *léi fǎ* 雷法 thunder-rites movements), the **Quán zhēn 全真 doctrinal and disciplinary archive**, the **Sòng-Yuán Nánzōng 南宗 inner-alchemical corpus**, the **late-medieval hagiographical and oracle-slip literature**, and — perhaps most surprisingly — a **large Six-Dynasties Shàng qīng 上清 scriptural archive** of more than 80 titles ([KR5g0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0122) – [KR5g0211](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0211) ff.) that classification should have placed in [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) *Dòng zhēn* but which the canon-editors of the *Zhèng yī bù* received from independent transmission streams and lodged here.

The section closes the *Dào zàng* itself: **the final six items ([KR5g0239](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0239) – [KR5g0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0244))** are the **bibliographic apparatus of the canon as a whole** — Bái Yúnjì 白雲霽's annotated catalogue of 1626 *Dào zàng mù lù xiáng zhù* [KR5g0239](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0239), the 1445 catalogue of texts known but missing from the *Zhèng tǒng* compilation *Dào zàng quē jīng mù lù* [KR5g0240](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0240), the *Dào zàng zūn jīng lì dài gāng mù* [KR5g0241](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0241) and *Dào jiào zōng yuán* [KR5g0242](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0242), the official 1445 table of contents *Dà Míng Dào zàng jīng mù lù* [KR5g0243](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0243), and the 1607 catalogue of the *Wàn lì Xù Dào zàng* 萬曆續道藏 supplement [KR5g0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0244) — so that the canon ends with itself indexed. (The 1607 supplement texts themselves are in [KR5h](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/) and [KR5i](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/), not here.) The chronological span of the section's actual contents runs from a **Wèi-period philosophical core** ([王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì's *Lǎo zǐ wēi zhǐ lì lüè* 老子微旨例略 [KR5g0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0064), 226–249) through the **dense Six-Dynasties Shàng qīng stratum** (4th–6th centuries), a **Táng ritual-codification layer** ([杜光庭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E5%85%89%E5%BA%AD) Dù Guāngtíng's monumental rubric collection *Dào mén kē fàn dà quán jí* [KR5g0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0034), 901–933), the **Sòng-Yuán "great-method" liturgies and Thunder-Rites theoretical archive** (c. 1100–1370), an **early-Míng administrative-reform layer** under the 43rd Celestial Master [張宇初](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%AE%87%E5%88%9D) Zhāng Yǔchū (1359–1410), and the **1444–1445 bibliographic apparatus** of the canon itself. KR5g is therefore best read **not as a coherent textual school but as the Daozang's institutional reservoir of the operative priesthood** — bracketed at one end by the foundational Six-Dynasties Celestial-Masters self-narrative ([KR5g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0014) *Sān tiān nèi jiě jīng*) and at the other by the canon's own table of contents.

### Important texts and text clusters

**The Celestial-Masters self-history and ordination-register core.** The earliest substantive Zhèngyī material in the section.

- *Sān tiān nèi jiě jīng* 三天內解經 [KR5g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0014) — anonymous "Xúshì" 徐氏 (fl. c. 420–478), Liú-Sòng. The lineage's own version of the Three-Heavens revelation, 張陵 Zhāng Dàolíng's covenant with Tàishàng Lǎojūn, and the early Celestial-Masters pantheon — the foundational southern-dynasties self-narrative of the school.
- *Zhèng yī tiān shī gào Zhào Shēng kǒu jué* 正一天師告趙昇口訣 [KR5g0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0082) — anonymous Eastern Jìn (317–420). The orally-transmitted instructions of Zhāng Dàolíng to his disciple Zhào Shēng 趙昇; among the oldest surviving Celestial-Masters texts.
- *Zhèng yī fǎ wén jīng zhāng guān pǐn* 正一法文經章官品 [KR5g0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0027) — anonymous Six Dynasties. The liturgical inventory of the spirit-officials invoked in *zhāng* 章 memorials — the bureaucratic personnel-roster of classical Zhèngyī petition ritual.
- *Tài shàng sān wǔ Zhèng yī méng wēi lù* 太上三五正一盟威籙 [KR5g0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0017) — anonymous Táng-Sòng, 6 *juàn*. **The core ordination-register of the lineage** — the *Sān wǔ méng wēi lù* 三五盟威籙 (Register of Three-and-Five Covenant-Authority) whose transmission defined entry into the Celestial-Masters priesthood. The cluster [KR5g0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0018) – [KR5g0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0021) preserves the associated transmission-ritual codes; [KR5g0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0022) – [KR5g0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0026) hold the supplementary individual registers for the *Xuán tiān Zhēn wǔ* 玄天真武 and *Běi jí* 北極 cults.

**The Sòng-Yuán-Míng "great-method" and general-ritual compendia.** The institutional spine of the section.

- *Dào fǎ huì yuán* 道法會元 [KR5g0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0029) — anonymous, early Míng (c. 1368–1445), **268 *juàn***. **The single largest ritual compendium in the entire *Dào zàng***: the umbrella collection of the Thunder-Rites (Shén xiāo, Qīng wēi, Tóng chū, Tiān xīn) corpora that defined late-imperial Zhèngyī practice (Skar 2000; Reiter 2007).
- *Shàng qīng Líng bǎo dà fǎ* 上清靈寶大法 (yī) [KR5g0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0030) — [王契真](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%A5%91%E7%9C%9F) Wáng Qìzhēn, Southern Sòng. The first of the two Dàozàng *Shàngqīng / Língbǎo* "great-method" syntheses. The associated *Mù lù* 目錄 [KR5g0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0031) catalogues its contents.
- *Shàng qīng Líng bǎo dà fǎ* 上清靈寶大法 (èr) [KR5g0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0032) — [金允中](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%91%E5%85%81%E4%B8%AD) Jīn Yǔnzhōng, Southern Sòng. The polemically distinct 66-*juàn* recension that, together with Wáng Qìzhēn's, documents the principal **Southern-Sòng inter-school ritual debate**.
- *Dào mén kē fàn dà quán jí* 道門科範大全集 [KR5g0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0034) — [杜光庭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E5%85%89%E5%BA%AD) Dù Guāngtíng (850–933), 87 *juàn*. The monumental late-Táng / Five-Dynasties rubric collection that supplies the underlying templates rebuilt in all later Zhèngyī compendia in the section.
- *Dào mén dìng zhì* 道門定制 [KR5g0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0033) — [呂元素](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E5%85%83%E7%B4%A0) Lǚ Yuánsù, dated by preface to **1188**. The Southern-Sòng codification of Daoist monastic and ritual regulations.
- *Dào mén tōng jiào bì yòng jí* 道門通教必用集 [KR5g0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0035) — [呂太古](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E5%A4%AA%E5%8F%A4) Lǚ Tàigǔ, preface dated **1201**. The everyday-use Southern-Sòng liturgy handbook, the practical counterpart to the great compendia.
- *Tài shàng zhù guó jiù mín zǒng zhēn bì yào* 太上助國救民總真祕要 [KR5g0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0036) — [元妙宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%83%E5%A6%99%E5%AE%97) Yuán Miàozōng, dated **1116**. The Huī-zōng-court state-protection manual, emblematic of the Northern-Sòng imperial sponsorship of Zhèngyī liturgy.
- *Dào mén shí guī* 道門十規 [KR5g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0041) — [張宇初](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%AE%87%E5%88%9D) Zhāng Yǔchū (1359–1410), 43rd Celestial Master, c. 1400. **The programmatic early-Míng Tiānshī reform document** that reorganized ordination, discipline, and Daoist-Confucian relations after the founding of the Míng — the institutional charter of the family that supervised the *Zhèng tǒng Dào zàng*.

**The Thunder-Rites *léi fǎ* 雷法 doctrinal apparatus.** Paired with the *Dào fǎ huì yuán* practical corpus.

- *Chōng xū tōng miào shì chén Wáng xiān sheng jiā huà* 沖虛通妙侍宸王先生家話 [KR5g0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0059) — sayings of 王文卿 Wáng Wénqīng (1093–1153), compiled by Yuán Tíngzhí. The doctrinal anchor of the **Shén xiāo Thunder-Rites lineage** whose ritual corpus fills the *Dào fǎ huì yuán*.
- *Dào fǎ xīn chuán* 道法心傳 [KR5g0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0062) — Wáng Wéiyī 王惟一, Yuán. Yuán doctrinal-transmission text formalizing the "heart-transmission" theory behind the Thunder-Rites.
- *Léi fǎ yì xuán piān* 雷法議玄篇 [KR5g0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0063) — Wàn Zōngshī 萬宗師, Yuán. Companion Yuán theoretical tract on Thunder-Rites mysteries.
- *Dào fǎ zōng zhǐ tú yǎn yì* 道法宗旨圖衍義 [KR5g0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0086) — Dèng Nán 鄧柟, Yuán. Diagrammatic exegesis of Daoist ritual essentials.

**The Tiānshī-family self-representation.** The 30th and 43rd Celestial Masters writing inside the supplement.

- *Sān shí dài tiān shī Xū jìng zhēn jūn yǔ lù* 三十代天師虛靜真君語錄 [KR5g0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0058) — recorded sayings of [張繼先](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E7%B9%BC%E5%85%88) Zhāng Jìxiān (1092–1127), 30th Celestial Master; the leading Tiānshī figure of Huīzōng's court-Daoist synthesis.
- *Dào mén shí guī* [KR5g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0041) and *Xiàn quán jí* 峴泉集 [KR5g0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0120) — the reform charter and the 20-*juàn* collected literary writings of [張宇初](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%AE%87%E5%88%9D) Zhāng Yǔchū (1359–1410), 43rd Celestial Master — the literary self-portrait of the family that supervised the compilation of the *Dào zàng*.

**The Quán zhēn 全真 cluster embedded inside the rival division.** A consequential editorial inclusion: the foundational doctrinal and disciplinary charters of the northern Quánzhēn school within the Tiānshī-supervised canon.

- *Chóng yáng lì jiào shí wǔ lùn* 重陽立教十五論 [KR5g0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0042) — [王嚞](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%9A%9E) Wáng Chóngyáng (1113–1170). **The founding doctrinal manifesto of Quán zhēn** — fifteen short discourses establishing the programmatic teaching (precepts, austerities, meditation, mind-nature).
- *Dān yáng zhēn rén zhí yán* 丹陽真人直言 [KR5g0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0043) — [馬鈺](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E9%88%BA) Mǎ Dānyáng (1123–1184). Direct sayings of Wáng Chóngyáng's senior disciple and first-generation Quánzhēn patriarch.
- *Quán zhēn qīng guī* 全真清規 [KR5g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0044) — [陸道和](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E9%81%93%E5%92%8C) Lù Dàohé, Yuán. **The foundational Quánzhēn monastic code** (modelled on Buddhist 清規).
- *Quán zhēn zuò bō jié fǎ* 全真坐鉢捷法 [KR5g0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0038) — anonymous Yuán Quánzhēn meditation manual.
- *Qīng hé zhēn rén Běi yóu yǔ lù* 清和真人北遊語錄 [KR5g0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0119) — sayings of [尹志平](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%B9%E5%BF%97%E5%B9%B3) Yǐn Zhìpíng (1169–1251), Qiū Chùjī's successor as third-generation Quánzhēn patriarch on his northern travels.
- *Cháng chūn zhēn rén xī yóu jì* 長春真人西遊記 [KR5g0238](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0238) — [李志常](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%BF%97%E5%B8%B8) Lǐ Zhìcháng (1193–1256), composed **1228**. **The travel-narrative of [丘處機](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%98%E8%99%95%E6%A9%9F) Qiū Chùjī's 1219–1223 overland journey to meet Činggis Qaγan in the Hindu Kush** — a top-rank primary source for 13th-century Inner Asian history and the Mongol-Quán-zhēn alliance (Waley 1931).

**The Bái Yùchán / Hǎiqióng cluster — the Nánzōng 南宗 anchor.**

- *Hǎi qióng Bái zhēn rén yǔ lù* 海瓊白真人語錄 [KR5g0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0116), *Hǎi qióng wèn dào jí* 海瓊問道集 [KR5g0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0117), *Hǎi qióng chuán dào jí* 海瓊傳道集 [KR5g0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0118) — three-text dossier of recorded sayings, dialogues, and transmission writings of [白玉蟾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%99%BD%E7%8E%89%E8%9F%BE) Bái Yùchán (1194–1229), Fifth Patriarch of the Southern Lineage of Daoist **inner alchemy** (*nèi dān* 內丹).

**The Six Dynasties Shàngqīng scriptural archive.** A surprisingly large stratum (~85 titles, [KR5g0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0122) – [KR5g0211](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0211) ff.) that classification would have placed in [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) *Dòng zhēn* but which the canon-editors received here through independent transmission. Representative items:

- *Dòng zhēn tài shàng sù líng dòng yuán dà yǒu miào jīng* 洞真太上素靈洞元大有妙經 [KR5g0123](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0123) — Six Dynasties.
- The *Bā sù zhēn jīng* 八素真經 corpus [KR5g0129](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0129) – [KR5g0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0134) — Six Dynasties / Táng.
- *Dòng zhēn huáng shū* 洞真黃書 [KR5g0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0152) — Six Dynasties; a key witness of the early sexual-ritual stratum subsequently subject to repeated Daoist reform.
- *Shàng qīng tài shàng dì jūn jiǔ zhēn zhōng jīng* 上清太上帝君九真中經 [KR5g0185](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0185) — Six Dynasties; foundational Shàng qīng visualization scripture.
- *Shàng qīng qióng gōng líng fēi liù jiǎ lù* 上清瓊宮靈飛六甲籙 [KR5g0200](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0200) — Eastern Jìn.
- *Shì dì chén Dōng huá shàng zuǒ sī mìng Yáng jūn zhuàn jì* 侍帝晨東華上佐司命楊君傳記 [KR5g0237](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0237) — Sòng hagiography of 楊羲 Yáng Xī (330–386), the visionary medium of the original Shàng qīng revelations. A major late witness to Sòng memory of the Mao-shan 茅山 revelations.

**Hagiographies and the *líng qiān* 靈籤 oracle-slip cluster.** A distinctive group of cult-specific divination texts.

- *Sān dòng qún xiān lù* 三洞群仙錄 [KR5g0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0057) — Chén Bǎoguāng 陳葆光, Southern Sòng. A 20-*juàn* hagiographical encyclopedia of immortals drawn from the Three Caverns — the Sòng-era benchmark anthology of Daoist saints' lives.
- *Yì shèng bǎo dé zhuàn* 翊聖保德傳 [KR5g0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0094) — [王欽若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%AC%BD%E8%8B%A5) Wáng Qīnruò (962–1025). Imperially-sponsored hagiography of the Yìshèng bǎodé zhēnjūn 翊聖保德真君, instituted to legitimize Sòng Zhēnzōng's Daoist program.
- *Lú shān Tài píng xīng guó gōng cǎi fǎng zhēn jūn shì shí* 盧山太平興國宮採訪真君事實 [KR5g0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0095) — [葉義問](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%89%E7%BE%A9%E5%95%8F) Yè Yìwèn (1098–1170). Southern-Sòng local-Daoist record of the Cǎifǎng zhēnjūn cult at Mount Lú, Jiāngxī.
- The *líng qiān* 靈籤 oracle-slip block [KR5g0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0107) – [KR5g0114](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0114) — eight cult-specific oracle-slip collections (the Four Saints, the Mother of the Nine-Heaven Defended Chamber, the Hóngēn Língjì zhēnjūn, the Jiāngdōng Wáng) — the principal Daoist-canon witness to the medieval Chinese **temple-oracle divination tradition**.
- *Gàn zhōu Shèng jì miào líng jì lǐ* 贛州聖濟廟靈跡理 [KR5g0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0113) — [宋濂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E6%BF%82) Sòng Lián (1310–1381). A Daoist temple stele-record written by the early-Míng's most senior Confucian literatus — rare cross-disciplinary witness to Confucian patronage of Daoist sanctuaries.

**Other free-standing texts of consequence.**

- *Lǎo zǐ wēi zhǐ lì lüè* 老子微旨例略 [KR5g0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0064) — [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì (226–249). The *xuán xué* 玄學 master's systematic introduction to the *Lǎo zǐ*, companion to his *Dào dé jīng* commentary — **the only major Wèi-Jìn philosophical text inside the supplement**, and the earliest dateable item in KR5g (commenting on [KR5c0088](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0088)).
- *Gě xiān wēng zhǒu hòu bèi jí fāng* 葛仙翁肘後備急方 [KR5g0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0115) — [葛洪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%9B%E6%B4%AA) Gě Hóng (283–343), revised by [陶弘景](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B6%E5%BC%98%E6%99%AF) Táo Hóngjǐng. Gě's "behind-the-elbow" emergency-prescription manual, **a foundational Chinese clinical-medicine text** containing the earliest description of smallpox.
- *Tài píng yù lǎn* 太平御覽 [KR5g0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0039) — [李昉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%98%89) Lǐ Fǎng (925–996) and imperial committee, **finished 983**. A 10-*juàn* Daoist extract from the great Sòng *lèi shū*, included as a quotation-bank of Daoist learning at the back of the section.
- *Dòng xuán Líng bǎo wǔ gǎn wén* 洞玄靈寶五感文 [KR5g0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0087) — [陸修靜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E4%BF%AE%E9%9D%9C) Lù Xiūjìng (406–477). A foundational early Língbǎo treatise by the patriarch who first systematized the *sāndòng* scheme.
- *Táng Tài gǔ miào yìng Sūn zhēn rén fú shòu lùn* 唐太古妙應孫真人福壽論 [KR5g0235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0235) — attributed to [孫思邈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%80%9D%E9%82%88) Sūn Sīmiǎo (581–682). Ethical-religious "blessings and longevity" tract under the famous physician's name.

**The bibliographic apparatus closing the canon.** KR5g — and the *Dào zàng* itself — ends with the books that index the books.

- *Dào zàng mù lù xiáng zhù* 道藏目錄詳註 [KR5g0239](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0239) — Bái Yúnjì 白雲霽, **1626**. The standard pre-modern annotated catalogue of the *Dào zàng*, definitive until Schipper-Verellen 2004.
- *Dào zàng quē jīng mù lù* 道藏闕經目錄 [KR5g0240](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0240) — anonymous, 1444–1445. The list of scriptures known from earlier recensions but missing from the 1445 compilation — indispensable index of canonical loss.
- *Dào zàng zūn jīng lì dài gāng mù* [KR5g0241](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0241), *Dào jiào zōng yuán* [KR5g0242](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0242) — anonymous Míng outline-catalogues of the canon and the lineage-origins of the Daoist tradition.
- *Dà Míng Dào zàng jīng mù lù* 大明道藏經目錄 [KR5g0243](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0243) — anonymous Míng editorial board (under [張宇初](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%AE%87%E5%88%9D)'s early supervision), 1444–1445. **The official table of contents of the 1445 *Zhèng tǒng Dào zàng*** — the canon's own table of contents.
- *Xù Dào zàng jīng mù lù* 續道藏經目錄 [KR5g0244](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0244) — anonymous Míng editor, **1607**. The very last text of the *Dào zàng*: catalogue of the *Wàn lì Xù Dào zàng* (the 1607 supplement of 56 further texts; the supplement's actual scriptures sit in [KR5h](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/) and [KR5i](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/)). Closes 正一部 and the canon as a whole.

### Important persons

- 張陵 (Zhāng Líng / Zhāng Dàolíng, 34–156 [or 178] CE) — founder of the Celestial-Masters tradition (*Tiān shī dào*) and the iconographic anchor of the entire division, even where he is not the author of named texts; his transmission to disciple 趙昇 underwrites [KR5g0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0082) and the lineage-narrative of [KR5g0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0014).
- [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) (Wáng Bì, 226–249) — Wèi-period *xuán xué* philosopher; author of *Lǎo zǐ wēi zhǐ lì lüè* [KR5g0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0064), the earliest dated text in the section.
- [葛洪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%9B%E6%B4%AA) (Gě Hóng, 283–343) — author of the *Bào pǔ zǐ* corpus in [KR5f](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5f/); the *Zhǒu hòu bèi jí fāng* [KR5g0115](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0115) preserved here is Daoism's principal medical handbook.
- [陸修靜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E4%BF%AE%E9%9D%9C) (Lù Xiūjìng, 406–477) — Liú-Sòng Daoist liturgist who codified the *sāndòng* bibliographic scheme; author of *Dòng xuán Líng bǎo wǔ gǎn wén* [KR5g0087](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0087).
- [杜光庭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E5%85%89%E5%BA%AD) (Dù Guāngtíng, 850–933) — the great late-Táng / Five-Dynasties Daoist liturgist and historian; author of the monumental rubric compendium *Dào mén kē fàn dà quán jí* [KR5g0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0034) that supplied the underlying templates for the later Sòng-Míng compendia in the section.
- [李昉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%98%89) (Lǐ Fǎng, 925–996) — Northern-Sòng official; chief editor of the *Tài píng yù lǎn* [KR5g0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0039).
- [王欽若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%AC%BD%E8%8B%A5) (Wáng Qīnruò, 962–1025) — Northern-Sòng grand councillor under Zhēnzōng; author of the imperial Daoist hagiography *Yì shèng bǎo dé zhuàn* [KR5g0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0094) that legitimized Zhēnzōng's Daoist program.
- [張繼先](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E7%B9%BC%E5%85%88) (Zhāng Jìxiān, 1092–1127) — 30th Celestial Master and the leading Tiānshī figure at Huīzōng's court; recorded sayings in [KR5g0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0058).
- 王文卿 (Wáng Wénqīng, 1093–1153) — founding patriarch of the Shén xiāo Thunder-Rites lineage; recorded sayings in [KR5g0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0059).

- [丘處機](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%98%E8%99%95%E6%A9%9F) (Qiū Chùjī, 1148–1227) — Quánzhēn patriarch summoned in 1219 by Činggis Qaγan; subject of the travel narrative [KR5g0238](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0238).

- [張宇初](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%AE%87%E5%88%9D) (Zhāng Yǔchū, 1359–1410) — 43rd Celestial Master; author of the reform charter *Dào mén shí guī* [KR5g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0041) and the collected writings *Xiàn quán jí* [KR5g0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0120); supervised the early stages of the *Zhèng tǒng Dào zàng* compilation.

- [孫思邈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%AB%E6%80%9D%E9%82%88) (Sūn Sīmiǎo, 581–682) — Táng *yào wáng* 藥王 ("King of Medicine"); nominal author of *Fú shòu lùn* [KR5g0235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0235) (the *Qiān jīn yào fāng* itself is in [KR5e](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5e/)).
- 楊羲 (Yáng Xī, 330–386) — Eastern-Jìn visionary medium of the original Shàng qīng revelations; subject of the Sòng hagiography [KR5g0237](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0237).

### Topics

- **The institutional priesthood and its ordination registers.** The Zhèngyī tradition's defining feature is the **graded transmission of registers** (*lù* 籙) — taxonomies of invocable spirit-officials that the priest receives at successive stages of ordination. The cluster [KR5g0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0017) – [KR5g0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0026) preserves the *Sān wǔ méng wēi lù* and its successors, the principal canonical record of how a Celestial-Masters priest was constituted.
- **The *zhāng* 章 memorial as the central liturgical act.** The Zhèngyī priest's primary intervention in the cosmos is the submission of memorials to the celestial bureaucracy. [KR5g0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0027) *Zhèng yī fǎ wén jīng zhāng guān pǐn* preserves the canonical roster of spirit-officials to whom memorials are addressed, and the Sòng-Yuán "great-method" compendia ([KR5g0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0030), [KR5g0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0032)) elaborate the full memorial-petition machinery.
- ***Léi fǎ* 雷法 Thunder-Rites and the Sòng "new ritual" lineages.** The Sòng dynasties produced a sequence of new Daoist ritual lineages — Tiānxīn 天心 (Heart of Heaven), Shénxiāo 神霄 (Divine Empyrean), Qīngwēi 清微 (Pure Tenuity), Tóngchū 童初 — built around the priest's invocation of celestial thunder gods for exorcism, healing, and rain-making. The *Dào fǎ huì yuán* [KR5g0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0029) is the canonical archive of these traditions, anchored doctrinally by 王文卿's sayings [KR5g0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0059) and the Yuán theoretical apparatus [KR5g0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0062) [KR5g0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0063) [KR5g0086](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0086) (Skar 2000; Reiter 2007).
- **The Tiānshī family and the supervision of the canon.** The *Zhèng tǒng Dào zàng* of 1445 was compiled under successive Celestial Masters of the 43rd–46th generations, beginning with [張宇初](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%AE%87%E5%88%9D). The supplement they supervised contains their own self-representation — [KR5g0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0058) (30th Master), [KR5g0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0041), [KR5g0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0120) (43rd Master) — and the canon they produced terminates with their bibliography [KR5g0243](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0243).
- **The Quán zhēn 全真 cluster inside Zhèngyī.** Quánzhēn was institutionally distinct from and at times in tension with the Celestial-Masters lineage that supervised the canon, but its foundational charters were preserved by the 1445 editors inside this very supplement: [KR5g0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0042) – [KR5g0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0044), [KR5g0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0119), [KR5g0238](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0238). The supplement is therefore the principal Dàozàng witness to **the late-imperial co-existence and editorial accommodation of the two great Daoist priestly traditions**.
- **The Nánzōng 南宗 inner alchemy.** The three-text Hǎiqióng cluster [KR5g0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0116) – [KR5g0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0118) documents [白玉蟾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%99%BD%E7%8E%89%E8%9F%BE)'s consolidation of the Southern Lineage of *nèi dān*, the lineage of Zhāng Bódūan 張伯端 (whose *Wù zhēn piān* sits elsewhere in the canon).
- **The Six-Dynasties Shàng qīng survival.** The very large block of 4th-6th-century Shàngqīng scriptures lodged in [KR5g0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0122) – [KR5g0211](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/KR5g0211) ff. — including substantial *Bā sù zhēn jīng* 八素真經 and *Yù qīng yǐn shū* 玉清隱書 corpora — is the Zhèngyī Supplement's most striking case of editorial overflow: scriptures whose home in the *sāndòng* scheme would have been [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) *Dòng zhēn* were received through independent transmission and lodged here, making KR5g a major secondary Shàngqīng archive alongside [KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/) itself.

# 續道藏 (KR5h)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR5h 續道藏 *Xù Dàozàng* — Masters — Wànlì Supplement to the Daoist Canon (1607)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR5h collects the **Xù Dàozàng** 續道藏, the supplement to the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (1445) compiled by the 50th Celestial Master **Zhāng Guóxiáng** 張國祥 (*d.* 1611) and printed in 1607 under imperial sponsorship by the Wànlì 萬曆 emperor. The supplement adds 32 *hán* 函 (case-units) of further material, numbered **DZ 1432–1487** (CT 1432–1487) in Schipper's *Concordance du Tao-tsang*, and is preserved in modern reprints as the 三家本 (Sānjiā běn, 1988) and the *Zhōnghuá Dàozàng* 中華道藏 (ZHDZ, 2004) editions. All 57 works in this division carry both `SJB` and `ZHDZ` in their `editions` frontmatter — the supplement was never separately printed in WYG 文淵閣四庫全書 form, since the Sìkù compilers regarded the Daoist Canon as outside the orthodox 子部 categorization.

Although KR5h sits inside Kanripo's **KR5 Masters** tree, the division is materially a Daoist-canon block rather than a *zhūzǐ* 諸子 block. The works range from genuine early-medieval Shàngqīng 上清 and Língbǎo 靈寶 scriptures preserved long after their composition, through Sòng–Yuán liturgies of the Shénxiāo 神霄 / Qīngwēi 清微 thunder-rite (*léifǎ* 雷法) traditions, to a large body of Míng popular-cult scriptures (Wáng Língguān 王靈官, Bìxiá yuánjūn 碧霞元君, Lǚzǔ 呂祖, Zhēnwǔ 真武, Huáguāng 華光, the city-god *chénghuáng* 城隍), and finally to a set of late-Míng anthologies and *Classics* commentaries (Jiāo Hóng's 焦竤 *Lǎozǐ yì* and *Zhuāngzǐ yì*) that mark the formal close of the canon. The supplement is therefore not a doctrinal corpus but an editorial container — its principle of selection was what the Wànlì-era court and the 龍虎山 Lónghǔ shān Celestial-Masters compilers judged worth preserving outside the 1445 canon, including older material that had been overlooked, newer scriptures generated by the popular pantheon, and the institutional self-documentation of the Zhāng lineage itself ([KR5h0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0031), [KR5h0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0032)).

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The Daoist *Lotus Sūtra* and Peacock-King cluster** — *Tàishàng zhōngdào miàofǎ liánhuā jīng* 太上中道妙法蓮花經 [KR5h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0001) (the opening text of the supplement, a conscious Daoist re-modelling of the Buddhist *Saddharma-puṇḍarīka*), and the three-text Peacock-King block [KR5h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0002), [KR5h0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0003), [KR5h0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0004) (a Daoist appropriation of Buddhist *Mahāmāyūrī* 孔雀明王). These texts set the supplement's signature register of Buddhist-Daoist syncretism.
- **Early-medieval Shàngqīng and Língbǎo scriptures preserved through late inclusion** — *Shàngqīng yuánshǐ biànhuà bǎozhēn shàngjīng* 上清元始變化寶真上經 [KR5h0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0005) (六朝), *Tàishàng Lǎojūn kāitiān jīng* 太上老君開天經 [KR5h0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0006) (六朝 cosmogony attributed to 張泮), *Gāoshàng yùchén yōulè zhāng* 高上玉宸憂樂章 [KR5h0026](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0026) (東晉), and the Táng Shàngqīng block [KR5h0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0007), [KR5h0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0024), [KR5h0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0025), [KR5h0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0027), [KR5h0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0028), [KR5h0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0029) — pre-Sòng material the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* had not absorbed.
- **Wàn-lì-era popular-cult scriptures** — the Wánglíngguān *Tàishàng Yuányáng shàngdì… Huǒchē Wánglíngguān zhēnjīng* 王靈官真經 [KR5h0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0012), the Medicine-King *Yàowáng* [KR5h0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0013), the Tàishān fertility goddess *Bìxiá yuánjūn* [KR5h0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0014), the Guān-Yǔ-associated *Lǎnglíng shàngjiāng* [KR5h0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0015), the city-god scripture [KR5h0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0016), and the *Huáguāng dàdì* / Mǎzǔ scripture [KR5h0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0017). Together this cluster documents the late-imperial pantheon as the canon-compilers found it.
- **Liturgical *kē* and repentance texts** — *Zhōngtiān Zǐwēi xīngzhēn bǎochàn* 中天紫微星真寶懺 [KR5h0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0019), *Zǐhuáng liàndù xuánkē* 紫皇鍊度玄科 [KR5h0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0020), the Dǒumǔ / Marīcī liturgy *Xiāntiān Dǒumǔ zòugào xuánkē* 先天斗母奏告玄科 [KR5h0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0021) (the most fully analysed liturgical *kē* in the supplement, diagnostic of the Shénxiāo / Qīngwēi thunder-rite synthesis), *Cháozhēn fāyuàn chànhuǐ wén* [KR5h0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0022), and the Língbǎo *shīshí* hungry-ghost-feeding ritual [KR5h0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0023).
- **The Celestial-Masters institutional dossier** — *Huáng Míng ēnmìng shìlù* 皇明恩命世錄 [KR5h0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0031) (a generational record of imperial favours to Lónghǔ shān) and *Hàn tiānshī shìjiā* 漢天師世家 [KR5h0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0032) (Zhāng Guóxiáng's own genealogy of the Celestial-Masters lineage from Zhāng Dàolíng 張道陵 onward), both fundamental to the institutional history of Zhèngyī 正一 Daoism.
- **Hagiographies and *xiānzhuàn* compendia** — *Xúxiān hànzǎo* 徐仙翰藻 [KR5h0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0037) and *Xúxiān zhēnlù* 徐仙真錄 [KR5h0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0039) (both centred on the Sòng thaumaturge Xú Shénwēng 徐神翁), *Hóngdào lù* 弘道錄 [KR5h0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0033) (Shào Jīngbāng's 25-*juàn* Daoist *Lives*), the syncretic *Xiāoyáo xū jīng* 消搖墟經 [KR5h0034](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0034), and *Lǚzǔ zhì* 呂祖志 [KR5h0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0054) (the Lǚ-Dòngbīn cult compendium).
- **Princely synthesis and sacred-geography** — *Tiānhuáng zhìdào Tàiqīng yùcè* 天皇至道太清玉冊 [KR5h0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0053) by the Míng Prince Níng **Zhū Quán** 朱權 (1378–1448), a comprehensive 8-*juàn* mid-Míng *summa* of Daoist doctrine, ritual, history and practice, and *Dài shǐ* 岱史 [KR5h0041](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0041), the 1586 gazetteer of Tàishān 泰山 (the chief of the Five Sacred Peaks and centre of the Dōngyuè 東嶽 cult).
- **Divination and almanac handbooks** — *Xǔ zhēnjūn yùxiá jì* 許真君玉匣記 [KR5h0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0050) (attributed to Xǔ Xùn 許遜, with its own table of contents [KR5h0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0049)), *Fǎshī xuǎnzé jì* 法師選擇記 [KR5h0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0051), *Xuántiān shàngdì bǎizì shènghào* 玄天上帝百字聖號 [KR5h0052](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0052) (a Zhēnwǔ divination text), and *Zǐwēi dǒushù* 紫微斗數 [KR5h0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0055), the foundational handbook of the still-practised Purple-Pole star-astrology system traditionally ascribed to Chén Tuán 陳摶.
- **The terminal *Classics*-commentary block** — *Yìyīn shàngxià jīng* 易因上下經 [KR5h0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0042) by the iconoclast **Lǐ Zhì** 李贄 (1527–1602), the anonymous *Gǔyì kǎoyuán* 古易考原 [KR5h0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0043), the Western-Hàn *Jiāoshì Yìlín* 焦氏易林 [KR5h0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0044) (4 096 four-line divinatory verses for paired hexagrams), and **Jiāo Hóng's** 焦竤 (1540–1620) *Lǎozǐ yì* 老子翼 [KR5h0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0056) and *Zhuāngzǐ yì* 莊子翼 [KR5h0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0057) — the closing pair of the entire Zhèngtǒng + Xù canon, and the standard late-Míng collected commentaries on the two great *zǐ* texts.
- **Two narrative and philosophical inclusions** — the Eastern-Jìn *Sōushén jì* 搜神記 [KR5h0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0045) (the foundational *zhìguài* 志怪 collection of **Gān Bǎo** 干寶) and Tán Qiào's 譚峭 Five-Dynasties *Huàshū* 化書 [KR5h0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0047) (a second recension of the work better known from [KR5d0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5d/KR5d0067)), both included for their canonical status in the Daoist literary tradition.

### Topics

- **Buddhist–Daoist syncretism as constitutive register.** The supplement opens with an explicit Daoist *Lotus Sūtra* ([KR5h0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0001)) and continues through a Peacock-King block ([KR5h0002](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0002)–[KR5h0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0004)) and the Dǒumǔ / Marīcī liturgy ([KR5h0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0021)). The borrowing is not incidental but the editorial posture of the whole division: by 1607 the canon-compilers treat Buddhist deities and ritual forms as Daoist material when transposed into the appropriate idiom.
- **The pantheon of the late-imperial popular cult.** A substantial bloc of the supplement is dedicated to deities whose cults had matured between the Sòng and the Wànlì period — Wáng Língguān (the Míng court-promoted exorcist-general), Bìxiá yuánjūn (the Tàishān fertility goddess), Lǚ Dòngbīn (the *quánzhēn* 全真 patriarch turned popular saviour), Zhēnwǔ 真武 / Xuántiān shàngdì, Huáguāng dàdì, the city-god *chénghuáng*, and the Dōngyuè 東嶽 cult of Tàishān. The division is therefore a primary source for the religious culture of late-Míng China at large, well beyond the institutional Daoist priesthood.
- **Thunder-rite (*léifǎ* 雷法) and the Shénxiāo / Qīngwēi liturgical synthesis.** Several of the *kē* texts ([KR5h0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0019), [KR5h0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0020), [KR5h0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0021)) sit firmly inside the post-Sòng *léifǎ* tradition descended from Wáng Wénqīng 王文卿 and Bái Yùchán 白玉蟾, with the canonical Dèng–Xīn–Zhāng 鄧辛張 thunder-marshal triad and the lineage of Zhāng Xūjìng 張虛靖. The supplement preserves the most analytically tractable late-imperial witnesses to this ritual lineage.
- **The institutional history of the Celestial Masters at Lónghǔ shān.** The pairing of [KR5h0031](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0031) (imperial-edict record) and [KR5h0032](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0032) (Zhāng-family genealogy by the compiler himself) makes the supplement a deliberately self-documenting institutional dossier — the Zhāng lineage placing its own credentials inside the canon they were entrusted to expand.
- **Inner alchemy (*nèidān* 內丹) and life-prolongation (*yǎngshēng* 養生).** Smaller-scale but present throughout: [KR5h0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0035), [KR5h0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0036), [KR5h0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0046), plus the *Zǐwēi dǒushù* astrological corpus [KR5h0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0055) for cosmological body-cosmos correspondence.
- **The *Yì jīng* as Daoist-canonical scripture.** The terminal cluster ([KR5h0042](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0042), [KR5h0043](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0043), [KR5h0044](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0044)) reflects the Wànlì-era understanding that the *Yì* belongs as much to the Daoist as to the Confucian curriculum — culminating in the inclusion of Jiāo Hóng's anthological commentaries on the *Lǎozǐ* and *Zhuāngzǐ* ([KR5h0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0056), [KR5h0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/KR5h0057)) as the canon's closing word.
- **Editorial principle of the *Xù*.** Across the division, the supplement collects three kinds of material: (i) early-medieval texts the 1445 canon had missed (the Six-Dynasties and Táng block), (ii) late-imperial scriptures and liturgies generated since 1445, and (iii) late-Míng scholarly works the compilers wanted to canonize alongside earlier material. Distinguishing these three editorial layers is the principal interpretive task when working with KR5h.

# 清代道教文獻 (KR5i)

## Division note (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君): [KR5i 道藏輯要 *Dàozàng jíyào* — Masters — Essentials of the Daoist Canon (Qīng, 1806/1906)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/)

### Scope and scholarly tradition

KR5i collects the **Dàozàng jíyào** 道藏輯要, the principal Qīng-era abridgment-and-expansion of the Daoist Canon, in two superimposed strata: the **原版道藏輯要** (Yuánbǎn DZJY, base-edition tag `YPP`), compiled by **Jiǎng Yǔpǔ** 蔣予蒲 (= Jiǎng Yuántíng 蔣元庭, 1755–1819) and printed in Beijing in 1806/1809; and the **重刊道藏輯要** (Chóngkān DZJY, base-edition tag `CK-KZ`), the substantially enlarged re-engraving completed at the **Èrxiānān** 二仙菴 and **Qīngyánggōng** 青羊宮 of Chéngdū in 1906 under the abbacy of **Hé Lóngxiāng** 賀龍驤. The Kanripo recension preserves all 109 works in DZJY's final received state, with the YPP / CK-KZ stratification visible in each per-text frontmatter. The division has no WYG (Wényuàngé Sìkù) counterpart: the Sìkù compilers excluded the Daoist Canon and its supplements from the 子部, so DZJY's entry into Kanripo is via its own block-print line, not via any imperial bibliographic sanction (cf. the parallel situation for [KR5h](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/) *Xù Dàozàng*).

DZJY differs from the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* ([KR5a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/)–[KR5g](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5g/)) and its Wànlì supplement ([KR5h](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5h/)) in three editorial respects that shape the whole division. First, the selection is decisively **Lǚ-zǔ-centric and Quánzhēn / Lóngmén in orientation**: a large bloc of the texts are Lǚ Dòngbīn 呂洞賓 *fújī* 扶乩 (planchette) productions ([KR5i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0049), [KR5i0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0050), [KR5i0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0051), [KR5i0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0053), [KR5i0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0054), [KR5i0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0055), [KR5i0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0047), [KR5i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0048), [KR5i0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0045)), and the institutional precept and liturgy corpus ([KR5i0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0097)–[KR5i0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0099), [KR5i0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0090)–[KR5i0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0091)) anchors the collection on the post-1656 Wáng Chángyuè revival at the Báiyúnguàn 白雲觀. Second, **inner alchemy** (*nèidān* 內丹) is the dominant practice register — the *Cāntóngqì* and *Wùzhēnpiān* lineages, the Wǔ Liǔ pài 伍柳派 dossier, the women's-alchemy (*nǚdān*) corpus and the *Jīnhuá* / *Tàiyǐ jīnhuá zōngzhǐ* tradition are all present in their late-imperial received form. Third, DZJY enacts an explicit **Three-Teachings synthesis** by canonizing several non-Daoist works — Zhōu Dūnyí's 太極圖說 and 通書 with Zhū Xī's annotation ([KR5i0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0079)–[KR5i0080](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0080)), Shào Yōng's 皇極經世書 and 擊壤集 ([KR5i0081](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0081)–[KR5i0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0082)), and Zhūgě Liàng's collected works ([KR5i0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0078)) — alongside Buddhist-register expositions like Wǔ Shǒuyáng's *Xiān fó hé zōng* ([KR5i0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0066)). The geographic centre of gravity is **Sìchuān**: the texts emerge from, or were re-canonized through, the Chéngdū Lóngmén network around the Èrxiānān and the Sìchuān Lǚzǔ planchette altars, making DZJY the principal documentary witness to nineteenth-century West-China Daoist institutional life.

### Important texts and text clusters

- **The Lǚzǔ planchette dossier (*Chúnyáng* corpus).** The single largest cluster in the division: *Lǚzǔ běnzhuàn* 呂祖本傳 [KR5i0045](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0045), *Lǚdì wénjí* 呂帝文集 [KR5i0049](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0049), *Lǚdì shījí* 呂帝詩集 [KR5i0050](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0050), *Chúnyáng sānshū* 純陽三書 [KR5i0051](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0051), *Yǔlù dàguān* 語錄大觀 [KR5i0053](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0053), *Wēiyán zhāiyào* 微言摘要 [KR5i0054](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0054), *Lǚdì shèngjì jìyào* 呂帝聖蹟紀要 [KR5i0055](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0055), *Tóngcān jīng* 同參經 [KR5i0047](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0047), and *Wǔjīng hébiān* 五經合編 [KR5i0048](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0048). Together this bloc constitutes the **canonical anthology of the Lǚzǔ cult as it operated through Qīng planchette altars** — Liǔ Shǒuyuán 柳守元 is the recurring editorial hand, and the corpus defines DZJY's editorial centre of gravity.
- **The Wǔ Liǔ pài 伍柳派 inner-alchemy core.** *Tiānxiān zhènglǐ zhílùn* 天仙正理直論 [KR5i0067](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0067) and its *Qiǎnshuō* abridgement [KR5i0068](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0068), *Xiānfó hézōng yǔlù* 仙佛合宗語錄 [KR5i0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0066), *Wǔzhēnrén dāndào jiǔpiān* 伍真人丹道九篇 [KR5i0070](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0070), and *Jīndān yàojué* 金丹要訣 [KR5i0069](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0069) — the foundational dossier of the **Wǔ Shǒuyáng** 伍守陽 (c. 1574–1644) → Liǔ Huáyáng 柳華陽 inner-alchemical lineage, which became the most widely-printed and most-translated late-imperial *nèidān* tradition (Cleary's *Daoist Yoga* renders its derivative form).
- **The *Cāntóngqì* / *Wùzhēnpiān* commentarial tradition.** *Cāntóngqì chǎnyōu* 參同契闡幽 [KR5i0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0037) and *Wùzhēnpiān chǎnyōu* 悟真篇闡幽 [KR5i0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0059), the paired commentaries of **Zhū Yuányù** 朱元育 (Kāngxī era); *Cāntóngqì fēnzhāngzhù* 參同契分章註 [KR5i0038](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0038) by the Yuán master **Chén Zhìxū** 陳致虛; the foundational *Jīndān sìbǎizì* 金丹四百字 [KR5i0058](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0058) of **Zhāng Bóduān** 張伯端 (c. 1075–1085); *Wǔpiān língwén* 五篇靈文 [KR5i0062](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0062) (the Jīn-era short scripture of the Quánzhēn founders' alchemical insight); and the Sòng *Rùyàojìng* 入藥鏡 [KR5i0039](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0039) of [崔希範](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B4%94%E5%B8%8C%E7%AF%84) — collectively the classical inner-alchemical curriculum of late-imperial Daoism.
- **The *Jīnhuá* / *Golden Flower* and Qīnghuáshàngdì planchette compendia.** *Jīnhuá zōngzhǐ* 金華宗旨 [KR5i0046](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0046) (the DZJY recension of the work that reached Europe in 1929 as Richard Wilhelm's *Das Geheimnis der Goldenen Blüte*); *Tiānxiān jīndān xīnfǎ* 天仙金丹心法 [KR5i0056](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0056); *Chàngdào zhēnyán* 唱道真言 [KR5i0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0030) (the great Yōng-zhèng-era *Qīnghuáshàngdì* planchette compendium, datable to 3 May 1729); *Yǎngzhēn jí* 養真集 [KR5i0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0072), *Yùquán* 玉詮 [KR5i0073](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0073), and *Zhēnquán* 真詮 [KR5i0074](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0074) — the late-imperial cultivation digests.
- **The women's alchemy (*nǚdān* 女丹) corpus.** *Sūn Bùèr yuánjūn fǎyǔ* 孫不二元君法語 [KR5i0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0063), *Sūn Bùèr yuánjūn chuánshù dāndào mìshū* 孫不二元君傳述丹道祕書 [KR5i0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0064), and the late-Qīng *Nǚdān hébiān* 女丹合編 [KR5i0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0109) — the principal vehicle of female inner-alchemy in the post-1700 Daoist tradition.

- **The high-canonical scripture set.** *Yuánshǐ dàdòng yùjīng* 元始大洞玉經 [KR5i0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0001) and its 1709 expanded recension [KR5i0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0003) (Shàngqīng 大洞 tradition); *Gāoshàng yùhuáng běnxíng jíjīng* 高上玉皇本行集經 [KR5i0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0015) with its 1809 Jiǎng-circle commentary [KR5i0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0016) (Jade-Emperor scripture); the cluster of *Gāoshàng yùhuáng xīnyìn* recensions [KR5i0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0017)–[KR5i0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0020); the *Huángtíng* 黃庭 inner / outer scriptures [KR5i0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0010)–[KR5i0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0012); and the *Yùshū bǎojīng* 玉樞寶經 [KR5i0035](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0035) of the Sòng Shénxiāo 神霄 thunder-rite tradition.

### Topics

- **Spirit-writing (*fújī* 扶乩 / *fùluán* 扶鸞) as canonization mechanism.** A defining feature of DZJY: a large bloc of the "Qīng" texts are planchette-revealed scriptures whose attributed speakers are deified Táng-Sòng patriarchs (Lǚ Dòngbīn, Xǔ Xùn, Zhāng Sānfēng, Zhōnglí Quán) speaking centuries after their natural lives. The mechanism is not occasional but the principal mode by which new scripture entered the late-imperial Daoist canon. The Wén-chāng-cult bloc [KR5i0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0021) and the *Chàngdào zhēnyán* [KR5i0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0030) are paradigm cases; the dating policy across the division — *terminus a quo* = consolidation of the planchette cult (post-1700), *terminus ad quem* = inclusion in DZJY (1809 or 1906) — directly reflects this.
- **The Lǚzǔ cult as editorial centre.** No other figure even approaches Lǚ Dòngbīn's dominance across DZJY's frontmatter. The Lǚ-zǔ-circle planchette altars of late-imperial Sìchuān, Jiāngnán, and the capital are the editorial matrix of the entire division; reading DZJY without that frame collapses much of the editorial logic.
- **Inner alchemy (*nèidān* 內丹) as central practice.** Where the Míng *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* gave roughly equal weight to ritual / liturgy and to inner cultivation, DZJY tilts decisively toward inner alchemy. The *Cāntóngqì* / *Wùzhēnpiān* commentarial tradition, the Wǔ Liǔ corpus, the women's-alchemy materials, and the *Jīnhuá* / *Tàiyǐ jīnhuá zōngzhǐ* compendia together form the doctrinal core, and the standard late-imperial *nèidān* curriculum *is* the DZJY *nèidān* curriculum.
- **Three-Teachings synthesis (*sānjiào héyī* 三教合一).** The most-distinctive editorial commitment: the Sòng Neo-Confucian classics ([KR5i0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0079)–[KR5i0082](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0082)) are canonized *as Daoist material*, with Zhū Xī as their annotator; Wǔ Shǒuyáng's [KR5i0066](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0066) uses Chán Buddhist *yuánjué* as a paired absolute with Daoist *xiāntiān yīqì*; and Zhūgě Liàng's loyalty-and-martial corpus [KR5i0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0078) is incorporated as Daoist ancestry. This is not an accident of bricolage but a programmatic claim.
- **The Quánzhēn / Lóngmén institutional turn and the 1656 Báiyúnguàn revival.** The precept-and-liturgy bloc ([KR5i0090](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0090)–[KR5i0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0091), [KR5i0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0097)–[KR5i0099](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0099)) anchors the division to the post-Wáng-Cháng-yuè Lóngmén institutional revival. Sīchuān (Èrxiānān, Qīngyánggōng, Qīngchéngshān, Zǐyángdòng) is the geographic centre, and the local-stele texts [KR5i0100](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0100), [KR5i0101](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0101), [KR5i0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0103) make DZJY itself a documentary witness to its own institutional home.
- **The popular-cult pantheon at the doorstep of the literati.** Wénchāng, Guāndì, the Jade-Emperor / 玉皇 cult, Dòumǔ, and the *Tàishàng gǎnyìng piān* moral-merit tradition all appear in DZJY in their state-of-the-art Qīng forms. The division is therefore a primary source for the religious culture of late-imperial gentry life, not only for monastic Daoism.
- **Editorial layering: YPP (1806/1809) vs. CK-KZ (1906).** Every per-text frontmatter records the base-edition tag. Reading the division by edition reveals two editorial moments separated by a century: Jiǎng Yǔpǔ's Beijing-court-supported selection of 1806/1809, vs. Hé Lóngxiāng's Chéngdū institutional re-engraving of 1906 (which absorbs the supplement-track materials including [KR5i0104](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0104), [KR5i0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0107)–[KR5i0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0109)). Most analytic claims about DZJY must be relativised to which stratum a text belongs in.
- **Women's alchemy as a recognised sub-tradition.** The *Sūn Bùèr* materials [KR5i0063](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0063)–[KR5i0064](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0064) and the late-Qīng *Nǚdān hébiān* [KR5i0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0109) establish *nǚdān* as a self-aware, lineage-documented sub-tradition with its own boundary-policing against "*yīnyáng* schools" of sexual yoga ([KR5i0109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0109) *Pángmén lù* polemic).
- **The Sìchuān provenance of the received text.** The 1906 re-engraving was produced at Chéngdū institutions, and several DZJY-only items (the local-stele texts; the Sìchuān provincial-Daoist anthology [KR5i0094](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5i/KR5i0094)) point unambiguously to a Sìchuān editorial home. The Beijing 1806 stratum and the Chéngdū 1906 stratum jointly define the geography of late-imperial Daoist institutional Daoism in the period that immediately preceded the early-Republican Daoist reform.
